entry.summary: This paper connects speculative sampling for diffusion models to relative entropy coding, showing that lookahead drafts need not be a linear chain as in existing reflection maximal-coupling samplers. It introduces draft trees that consider richer candidate sets per round, lowering the number of expensive target evaluations while preserving the target distribution exactly.

entry.title: The Attention Within: Consensus Dynamics in Selective State Space Models

author.name: Jo\~ao Pedro Silvestre, \'Alvaro Rodr\'iguez Abella, Paulo Tabuada

entry.summary: This paper asks whether the recurrence in selective state space models drives hidden states toward consensus, as attention does in transformers. Using a control-theoretic lens, the authors analyze the token-mixing recurrence and its relationship to linear attention, characterizing whether SSM layers collapse representations to a single direction.

entry.title: Agora: Git as Shared Memory for Collective AutoResearch

author.name: Yifan Zhang, Yunheng Zou, Shaokun Zhang, Jian Hu, Hao Zhang, Binfeng Xu, Jan Kautz, Yi Dong

entry.summary: Agora is a shared-memory infrastructure for multiple autonomous research agents, recording claims, results, hypotheses, and verifications as immutable commits in a Git-backed DAG. A derived index exposes the research frontier, neglected branches, and verification status, while a diversity-aware selection rule prevents agents from converging on the same approaches. It addresses the redundancy problem when many AutoResearch loops run in parallel.

entry.title: Label-free steering: Compressing test-time reinforcement learning into bias-only subspaces

author.name: Naveen Vakada, Mingyuan Li, Shaoxiong Ji

entry.summary: This work asks whether test-time reinforcement learning can work when both the reward signal and the optimization space are severely restricted, using majority-vote pseudo-labels as rewards while training only about 100K bias parameters and freezing the pretrained backbone. On MATH-500 the approach reaches 76.67 percent accuracy, slightly exceeding the authors' own labeled bias-steering reproduction while updating roughly 76,000 times fewer parameters than full-parameter TTRL. It matters as evidence that test-time adaptation may live in a tiny, interpretable parameter subspace rather than requiring broad weight updates.

entry.title: Echo: Learning-based Matching Decompilation using Trusted Back Translation

author.name: Jun Bi, Xiangxin Fang, Aarsh Chaube, Jos\'e Wesley De Souza Magalh\~aes, Rodrigo C. O. Rocha, Michael O'Boyle

entry.summary: Echo performs matching decompilation by using compilation not only as verification but as trusted feedback that guides an iterative search for source code whose recompiled assembly exactly matches the target binary. A domain-specific model generates candidate programs and compilation configurations, which are then recompiled and compared to drive the search, which is otherwise hard for optimized binaries built with unknown compiler settings. It matters because exact-match evidence makes neural decompiler output far more trustworthy than raw model predictions.

entry.title: ASLEval: Measuring Privacy Exposure Displacement in LLM Agent Sessions

author.name: Guosen Wu, Huizhen Huang, Guoxiong Long, Tao Huang, Chen Hou

entry.summary: The paper introduces the notion of privacy exposure displacement, the mismatch between a local evaluation proxy such as a final response or attacker report and the true session-level exposure of protected data, and offers ASLEval, an authorization-aware framework that pre-registers a hidden target set and measures every declared visible exit. Across several enterprise-style environments and independently implemented runtimes, an expected-outlet-only view misses 46.9 percent of exposure recoveries. The work argues that privacy auditing of tool-using agents must be target-grounded and session-wide rather than proxy-based.

entry.title: Transcribe, Then Reason: Two-Pass Decomposition for Multimodal Review

author.name: Bojie Li, Noah Shi

entry.summary: The paper shows that asking a multimodal model to review a long recording or document in a single call quietly fails, with the model dropping roughly a third of content and embellishing the rest, and that this is not a perception failure since dropped content reappears when the model is asked merely to transcribe. The bottleneck is generation under load, where perceiving, reasoning, and writing a long faithful review compete for one output pass. The authors argue for a two-pass decomposition that separates transcription from reasoning, after ruling out modality and thinking-budget explanations.

entry.title: Double descent is the principle of least action

author.name: Congzhou M Sha

entry.summary: The paper explains the double descent phenomenon, where test error falls, peaks near the interpolation threshold, and falls again as parameter count grows, through statistical mechanics. It models the training trajectory of a stochastic gradient method as a particle diffusing over the training loss landscape at an induced temperature, so an equilibrated run visits parameter vectors of equal training loss with Boltzmann-distributed probability. Because training starts at an initialization and has only finite time to diffuse, it carries an effective weight decay, which the author uses to derive the observed curve.

entry.title: Objective vs. Search: Decomposing What Makes a Good Tokeniser

author.name: Ahmetcan Yavuz, Clara Meister, Tiago Pimentel

entry.summary: This work disentangles two orthogonal axes of tokenization algorithms: the optimization objective (compression versus log-likelihood) and the search procedure (bottom-up merging versus top-down pruning). The authors introduce two new tokenizers, BottomUpLL and TopDownComp, to complete the 2x2 design space, then train language models with each tokenizer while varying model size and other factors. The study clarifies which observed differences between BPE and UnigramLM stem from what is optimized versus how it is optimized.

entry.title: Exponential Hardness of Off-Policy Evaluation under History-Dependent Logging

author.name: Pranaya Jajoo

entry.summary: This theoretical paper constructs pairs of partially observable MDPs whose logged data covers all actions and beliefs with constants independent of the horizon, yet still requires exponentially many episodes to evaluate a known target policy to modest accuracy. The obstruction comes from a reset in the logger that erases information when the logging policy depends on history. It clarifies that common coverage assumptions are insufficient for off-policy evaluation in partially observed, history-dependent settings.

entry.title: METALICA: METAdynamics and repLICA exchange for enhanced diffusion sampling

author.name: Alireza Omidi, Jiajun He, J\"org Gsponer, Saifuddin Syed

entry.summary: METALICA combines metadynamics with replica exchange on a pretrained diffusion model to sample rare conformational states of proteins that equilibrium-trained models seldom visit. It accumulates a bias potential along a collective variable to repel new samples from previous ones, maintains one replica per diffusion level to form a Markov chain with inter-replica communication, and reweights samples back onto the unbiased distribution. The authors frame it as the dual of sequential control, where sequential Monte Carlo parallels the sampler.

entry.title: A Calibrated Instrument for Measuring How Inference Optimizations Affect Output Quality

author.name: Jerry Kaplan

entry.summary: Jerry Kaplan argues that inference optimization research, spanning quantization, early exit, and speculative decoding, relies on idiosyncratic benchmark scores that fall short of scientific measurement standards. The paper proposes a rigorous methodology using an LLM judge that is itself formally calibrated, by verifying no systematic preference between statistically equivalent outputs of the same model and measuring per-sample judge noise. It aims to make cross-system and cross-technique quality comparisons meaningful.

entry.title: Myovox: Reading Speech from the Muscles of the Face

author.name: Varshith Madishetty

entry.summary: Myovox decodes open-vocabulary English text from 31-channel surface EMG of facial muscles during vocalized speech, improving the emg2speech benchmark from 51.17% to 18.53% word error rate. The gain is decomposed into three measured steps: recovering missing open-vocabulary decode settings, replacing the causal encoder with a bidirectional Conformer trained via four-term cross-modal distillation, and further refinement. It is a substantial advance for silent-speech interfaces built on muscle signals.

entry.title: "If I Had to Buy Just ONE: Galaxy S26 Ultra": Auditing AI-Generated Product Recommendations

author.name: Lucas G. Uberti-Bona Marin, Thales Bertaglia, Giovanni Astante, Bram Rijsbosch, Gijs van Dijck, Anik\'o Hann\'ak, Gerasimos Spanakis, Konrad Kollnig

entry.summary: The study audits commercial advice from popular AI chatbots, curating 2,528 real product-advice queries (ConsumerQ) and evaluating 1,536 responses from ChatGPT, Google Gemini, and Google Search AI Overviews. It finds ChatGPT expresses a first-person product preference in 79% of recommending responses versus 7% for Gemini and 2% for AI Overviews, raising questions about bias and impartiality as AI advertising monetization grows.

entry.title: Racing in Volume with Flow Ensembles

author.name: Saswat Subhajyoti Mallick, Riu Cherdchusakulchai, Marc Ruiz Olle, Albert Mosella-Montoro, Jose Ribeiro-Gomes, Francisco Vicente Carrasco, Fernando De la Torre

entry.summary: The paper introduces FastFlowGS, a streaming 4D Gaussian Splatting method that reconstructs fast-moving subjects from a small set of fixed external cameras, and Monaco4D, a photorealistic Unreal Engine 5 benchmark for high-speed outdoor reconstruction. It targets a previously unaddressed setting: streaming capture of fast subjects from a sparse ring of allocentric cameras, where no prior method or benchmark existed. It matters for sports, broadcast and volumetric video applications.

entry.title: What Do Hallucinations Reveal About Multimodal Reasoning? Diagnosing Visual Grounding Failures via Contrastive Decoding Probes

author.name: Zhipeng Zhao, Wenxu Wang, Peishun Liu, Ruichun Tang

entry.summary: The paper introduces SAFE, a training-free decoding framework that contrasts visually grounded and vision-ablated generation paths to produce a token-level contrastive grounding score, identifying when a model favors linguistic priors over visual evidence. The signal serves both as a detector of visually ungrounded tokens and as the basis for decoding-time penalties. It matters because it uses models as instruments to study their own failure dynamics rather than only reporting benchmark scores.

entry.title: Multi-modal Knowledge Preserving Adapter for Embedding Backward Compatibility

author.name: Jaeseok Byun, Gukyeong Kwon, Han-Kai Hsu, Meher Gitika Karumuri, Zhikang Zhang, Hao Yang, Davide Modolo

entry.summary: Proposes MKP-Adapter, described as the first adapter-only backward-compatible training approach for multimodal large language model embeddings, so a new model can be deployed without re-indexing an existing vector database. The method avoids updating the backbone, sidestepping prohibitive training cost, regression risk, and lack of access to proprietary weights, while trying to preserve the new model's learned knowledge. It matters for practical, low-cost upgrades of production retrieval systems.

entry.title: Bi-FlowGS: Bridging Generative View Completion and Gaussian Geometry through Bidirectional Flow Co-Refinement

author.name: Yuetong Wang, Jinsheng Quan, Yi Yang, Yawei Luo

entry.summary: Tackles sparse-view 3D Gaussian Splatting, where plausible renderings can hide erroneous geometry, a failure mode the authors call Geometry Cheating. Bi-FlowGS uses optical flow to connect video-diffusion view completion with Gaussian geometry regularization through a plug-and-play video-to-geometry flow distillation, providing explicit geometry supervision rather than RGB pseudo-supervision alone. It matters for making sparse-view reconstruction geometrically trustworthy.

entry.title: SlotDiT: Object-Centric Representations for Diffusion Transformers

author.name: Gjergj Plepi, Sven Behnke

entry.summary: SlotDiT is a text-guided Diffusion Transformer that generates video in a slot-based object-centric latent space, decomposing scenes into object-level latents rather than pixel or VAE latents. Given a reference image and language instruction, it explores whether structured object-centric representations provide a better substrate for controllable generative modeling in robotics applications.

entry.title: RAF-VLA: Representation Alignment with the Future for End-to-End Autonomous Driving

author.name: Dogun Kim, Yongjae Lee, Joonhee Lim, Yeina Lee, Junhyeok Park, Moogeun Park, Dongsuk Kum

entry.summary: RAFT-VLA replaces explicit future-scene generation in world-modeling vision-language-action driving policies with direct guidance that shapes planning-relevant internal representations. This removes the extra training burden and inference latency of decoders that must generate future frames, while preserving the representational benefits of future prediction. It matters as a more efficient route to world-model-style driving policies.

entry.title: OmniRisk: Omnidirectional Trajectory-Risk Learning for Agile Quadrotor Dynamic Avoidance

author.name: Yifan He, Yang Liu, Wenhao Zhao, Hai Lin, Deping Zhang, Mingze Ma, Fei Gao, Huan Yu, Zipeng Dai, Ziming Ding

entry.summary: OmniRisk presents an omnidirectional planning framework that learns trajectory-level risk offline to allow efficient onboard evasion of fast-moving obstacles by agile quadrotors. A fixed-dimensional tensor combines LiDAR range panoramas, dynamic masks, and Cartesian surface velocities to represent geometry and motion jointly. The authors formulate an asymmetric risk field to support selecting feasible maneuvers within short reaction windows, targeting the failure modes of both sparse range observations and online trajectory optimizers in dense, high-speed encounters.

entry.title: GraphPoint: Semantic Entity Graphs and Point Trajectories for Compositional Robot Manipulation

author.name: Kang Luo, Hesheng Wang

entry.summary: GraphPoint investigates why manipulation policies fail to generalize beyond demonstrations when language and scenes are strongly correlated, causing fixed visual-action mappings instead of language-conditioned behavior. It studies compositional reuse both within subtasks (combining familiar entities, action types, and modifiers) and across subtasks (reusing learned subtasks in unseen long-horizon tasks). The authors introduce CoMani, a benchmark with controlled splits and matched initial scenes that change a single semantic factor at a time to discourage visual shortcuts, alongside semantic entity graphs and point trajectories.

entry.title: DeformSmith: Physics Harness-Guided Hierarchical Generation of Deformable Assets for Robot Manipulation

author.name: Can Li, Jie Gu, Zishun Deng, Jingmin Chen, Lei Sun

entry.summary: DeformSmith is a framework for automatically generating interactive, physically credible deformable assets for robot manipulation from text or a single image. It uses hierarchical agentic construction and a shared physics-grounded harness to progressively build and refine geometry, appearance, and physical properties that text and images alone cannot specify. This matters because deformable-object simulation assets are scarce and their contact behavior directly determines whether manipulation policies transfer.

entry.title: FIERCE: From Generalist Robot Policies to Fast Specialists via Progress-Failure Feedback

author.name: Runjia Tan, Yuang Tu, Yujie Yan, Lan Yu, Xuesong Tian, Chen Lv

entry.summary: FIERCE is a reinforcement learning framework that refines generalist robot policies into compact, fast specialists using a unified task-adaptive progress-failure evaluator. The evaluator shares an observation-language representation between a progress head and an action-conditioned latent predictor whose predictions feed a causal sequence model for failure estimation, trained with progress, preference, and terminal-outcome signals. Target-task rollouts then support adaptation and calibration.

entry.title: Calibrated Probabilistic Obstruction Reasoning with Vision-Language Models for Grasping in Clutter

author.name: Thanh-Tuan Tran, Ngoc-Chien Chu, Thanh Nguyen Canh, Nak Young Chong, Nguyen-Viet Ha, Xiem HoangVan

entry.summary: CPOR-Grasp is a calibrated probabilistic obstruction-reasoning framework that propagates uncertainty from pairwise VLM evidence into decisions about whether to grasp a target, remove a blocker, or defer. It calibrates and fuses vision-language model, depth, and amodal-mask cues, addressing the problems of miscalibrated VLM predictions, jointly inconsistent obstruction relations, and the absence of guarantees about discarded hypotheses. The goal is more reliable decision-making in cluttered grasping scenarios.

entry.title: AdaGeoVLN: Selective Geometry Across Representation Depth and Navigation Time for Vision-Language Navigation

author.name: Quan-Dung Pham, Anh Dao, Danh Vinh Le, Nguyen Viet Tri Pham, The-Anh Nguyen, Zhirui Dai, Yiyu Chen, Tuyen P. Le, Truong Nguyen, Quan Nguyen

entry.summary: AdaGeoVLN is a streaming vision-language navigation framework that examines how much geometry foundation model representation to use across two axes: representation depth and navigation time. It couples earlier, intermediate, and later GFM representations to successive policy stages instead of repeatedly injecting only a terminal feature, and retains historical global-attention KV states in a navigation-aware GFM memory. The work targets the unresolved question of how navigation policies should exploit hierarchical geometric features and retain historical spatial evidence.

entry.title: Who Audits Whom, on What Substrate, with What Evidence? An Independence-Graded Audit Protocol for Agentic AI

author.name: Mohamed Chahine Ghanem

entry.summary: The paper observes that agentic systems both undergo audits and increasingly act as auditors, yet independence, the foundation of assurance, is treated as binary. It argues independence must be graded along three orthogonal axes: principal independence (who controls the auditor), substrate independence (whether the auditor shares the auditee's model family, toolchain, or guardrails and thus fails with it), and evidence independence (whether evidence is attestable rather than self-reported), aggregating the axes by weakest link and applying the same rubric when the auditor is an agent. It matters as a governance and assurance contribution for a fast-growing class of autonomous systems.

entry.title: Beyond Routine Compliance: Cunning Data Cultivates Safety Vigilance in Large Language Models

author.name: Youjia Wang, Lin Xu, Yang Sun, Yuxiao Lu, Chengfang Fang, Jie Shi

entry.summary: The authors argue safety alignment should cultivate vigilance, the ability to detect unusual premises, misleading reasoning, and latent risks beneath benign surface semantics, not just recognise explicit harmful requests. They introduce cunning questions that are not necessarily safety-related but contain misleading premises, atypical reasoning, or subtle inconsistencies. Training on such data is hypothesised to improve the model's scrutiny of underlying intent and assumptions.

entry.title: Rethinking How We Evaluate Methodological Progress in Health AI

author.name: Florent Pollet, Matthew McDermott

entry.summary: The authors re-implement 12 historical and recent EHR algorithms in a shared evaluation framework and test them on MIMIC-IV and NWICU, comparing expert-authored clinically meaningful tasks with generated tasks built from randomly sampled event codes and horizons. They ask whether algorithm rankings transfer across task definitions. It matters because it probes how reproducibility and task design distort claims of methodological progress in clinical AI.

entry.title: QuanText: Protecting Dataset-Level Secrets in Textual Data Sharing

author.name: Shuaiqi Wang, Zinan Lin, Giulia Fanti

entry.summary: QuanText addresses a gap in privacy research: while differential privacy protects individual records, it offers weak protection for aggregate properties such as the proportion of records with a given diagnosis or political stance. The authors propose a training-free, LLM-agnostic release mechanism based on randomized quantization that protects these dataset-level secrets when sharing natural-language data. This matters as text datasets are increasingly released and property-inference attacks on global statistics become practical.

entry.title: No Usable Linear "Capitulation Direction" in Two Small LLMs: A Validation Protocol for Activation-Steering Claims, and a Cross-Family Behavioral Study of Sycophancy Under Pushback

author.name: Saad Aamir, Muhammad Awais Bin Adil

entry.summary: The authors challenge models with scripted forms of pushback on TriviaQA and measure how often initially correct answers flip, finding flip rates of about 42 and 43 percent in Qwen2.5-1.5B and Llama-3.2-1B. Which pushback style is most effective turns out to be model-specific, with a pre-registered paired comparison significant in opposite directions across the two families. The paper also reports a negative result for linear activation-steering claims and proposes a validation protocol for such claims.

entry.title: Beyond Random Couplings: Contrastive Noise Alignment in Generative Flows

author.name: Lennart Wittke, Vinicius Azevedo

entry.summary: The paper argues that independently sampled Gaussian noise creates arbitrary data-noise couplings that force networks to learn high-curvature transports, and proposes Contrastive Noise Alignment, which treats the noise batch as an interacting particle system optimized via a cross-modal InfoNCE objective. This dynamically reshapes the source noise distribution during training. It matters for diffusion and flow-matching efficiency and sample quality.

entry.title: Understanding AI Provider Recommendations in Local Service Markets

author.name: Hazem Ibrahim, Yasir Zaki

entry.summary: The authors audit AI provider recommendations across four registry-backed service domains in the 100 largest U.S. metropolitan areas, checking answers against official registries under three conditions: an open-weight model, a proprietary model without search, and the same proprietary model with search. Without search, both models largely fabricate recommendations, with only 4% of the open-weight model's recommended doctors and 11% of the proprietary model's matching a clinician in the queried city.

entry.title: FLAT: Resampling Image and Text into 1D Flexible-Length Aligned Transmodal Tokens for Retrieval and Generation

author.name: Guangyu Sun, Shlok Kumar Mishra, Wentao Bao, Robert Zhenheng Yang, Xiao Wang, Xiyuan Wang, Yujunrong Ma, Chen Yuan, Max Xiangjun Fan, Jun Xiao, Jianpeng Cheng

entry.summary: FLAT is a representation pretraining framework that jointly optimizes a shared multimodal encoder with text-to-image and image-to-text decoders, producing flexible-length aligned transmodal tokens that are directly consumable by generative decoders. It combines contrastive alignment with bidirectional cross-modal objectives, aiming to remove the bottleneck where generation is limited by frozen contrastive embeddings. It matters for unifying retrieval and generation in a single representation space.

entry.title: GeoLAM: Learning Geometry-Grounded Latent Actions from Unlabeled Human Videos

author.name: Yifan Xie, Hekun Tian, Jinkun Liu, YuAn Wang, Qiao Sun, Wenbo Ding

entry.summary: Proposes GeoLAM, which learns geometry-grounded latent actions from action-free human videos by combining future-frame reconstruction through a frozen geometric feature hierarchy with motion supervision from a training-only 4D geometry teacher. Targets include 3D displacement, residual image-plane motion, and surface-orientation change, pooled spatially, with visibility and confidence weighting. It matters because disentangling manipulation motion from appearance and camera movement is central to scaling robot learning from internet video.

entry.title: VLM-MPPI: Grounding Natural Language in Behaviorally Diverse Trajectories for Aerial Navigation

author.name: Hanbing Zhang, Fangguo Zhao, Zerui Li, Xin Guan, Peng Cheng, Shuo Li

entry.summary: VLM-MPPI presents a hierarchical UAV navigation framework connecting natural-language intent to dynamically feasible flight behaviors in cluttered indoor settings. It runs a parallelized ensemble of six behavior-conditioned Model Predictive Path Integral planners, using mode-specific guiding costs and sampling biases to induce intentionally diverse trajectory modes rather than stochastic variation. The 3D candidates are projected onto the onboard first-person RGB stream, turning language grounding into visual action selection handled by a pretrained vision-language model.

entry.title: CaSCo: Cascade-Aware Soft-Collision Motion Planning

author.name: Shivaram Kumar, Gaoyuan Liu, Yoonchang Sung

entry.summary: CaSCo is a cascade-aware soft-collision motion planning framework that treats contact as graded rather than binary, since brushing a cardboard box differs greatly in consequence from touching glass or an unstable object. A vision-language or language model assigns semantic risk to objects while a physics simulator predicts the consequences of candidate robot motions, including secondary object-object collisions triggered by direct contact. This makes motion risk depend on the physical evolution of the scene rather than only the robot's geometric path.

entry.title: NeMo Data Designer: An Extensible Framework for Multimodal Synthetic Data Generation

author.name: Johnny Greco, Nabin Mulepati, Andre Manoel, Eric Tramel, Kirit Thadaka, Mike Knepper, Dhruv Nathawani, Dane Corneil, Yev Meyer, Alex Watson, Maarten Van Segbroeck

entry.summary: NeMo Data Designer is an open-source framework for multimodal synthetic data generation with a declarative configuration where humans or agents define each dataset column across text, code, structured outputs, images, embeddings, and statistical samplers. Configurations are inspectable artifacts supporting sharing and reproducibility, and a plugin system plus preview-and-revision loop supports the iterative nature of SDG.

entry.title: A Four-Stage Decomposition of Word-Problem Solving and Mechanistic Fragility in LLM Math Reasoning

author.name: Zhongdi Qu, Carla P. Gomes

entry.summary: The paper shows that LLM math word-problem computation decomposes into four sequential stages: Schema Abstraction, Operation Planning, Operand Binding, and Computation, each with identifiable intermediate representations in specific layer bands. It localizes distractor-induced failures to Operation Planning by identifying attention heads whose causal role is validated bidirectionally.

entry.title: When Is Graph Structure Worth Its Cost? The Case for Structure Pricing in Retrieval-Augmented Generation

author.name: Yuzhong Zhang, Haoyang Ma, Chao Peng, Lionel Briand, Boxi Yu, Jialun Cao

entry.summary: This work asks whether the quality gains from graph-based retrieval-augmented generation justify the many language-model calls typically needed to construct the graph, and introduces EffiRAG, which uses the graph mainly to locate relevant passages while generating answers from the original source text. The design keeps graph construction and query processing lightweight and preserves source information. Evaluated on the UltraDomain set of 120 open-ended questions across four domains, EffiRAG was preferred over LightRAG-hybrid on the large majority of questions, supporting the idea of explicitly accounting for structure cost.

entry.title: REPAIR: Resolving Long-Tail Confusion in Scientific Retrievers via Fact-Verified Iterative Refinement

author.name: Yerim Oh, Gunhee Kim

entry.summary: The paper frames scientific retrieval as constrained by long-tailed concepts and high fact sensitivity, which limits dense retrievers and makes LLM augmentation prone to hallucination. REPAIR is a self-evolving data augmentation framework that iteratively synthesizes training data by cycling through diagnosis of long-tail concepts, API-guided evidence expansion, and hard negative mining to ground retrieval in verified facts. It matters because it targets fine-grained factual distinctions that general-purpose retrievers frequently confuse.

entry.title: Visual Compliance via Executable Safety Rule Entailment

author.name: Jisoo Kim (Sungkyunkwan University), TaeYoon Kwack (Sungkyunkwan University), Jinwoo Jang (Sungkyunkwan University), Honguk Woo (Sungkyunkwan University)

entry.summary: The paper argues that as risk patterns evolve and safety rules grow more complex, training-based end-to-end vision-language safeguards struggle with adaptability and with explaining reasoning over complex policies. It proposes GuardEn (Guarding by Safety Rule Entailment), an executable safeguard framework that decomposes safety policies into atomic propositions through safety-rule compilation, models their composition as executable code, and at test time instantiates those propositions with contextual visual information. It matters because it targets updateable, explainable compliance checking rather than fixed learned risk classifiers.

entry.title: Disentangling Long-Term Memory via Latent Neuro-Symbolic Reasoning

author.name: Cai Ke, Xinghao Chen, Xiaoyu Shen, Keyu Chen, Siyu An, Junnan Dong, Ruifeng Xu, Ruizhi Qiao, Xing Sun

entry.summary: LGM is a neuro-symbolic framework for long-term memory in personalised agents that shifts memory disentanglement into a continuous latent space rather than persisting fixed, query-agnostic graphs. It aims to capture context-dependent relations in noisy, entangled raw interaction histories for fine-grained cross-session personalisation. The approach addresses the computational cost and limited expressivity of flat retrieval and static structured memory baselines.

entry.title: CERA-MoA: Co-Evolving Routing Mechanisms with Continually Learning LLM Agents

author.name: Jiaxuan Jiang, Liyuan He, Zhixuan Fang

entry.summary: CERA-MoA is an iterative reinforcement learning framework in which a dynamic query router and independent agent policies co-evolve, rather than treating routing and agent fine-tuning as separate processes. It introduces a predictive familiarity estimator that uses mid-layer hidden states to assess which agents are semantically competent for a query, avoiding extra overhead. The design aims to let routing adapt as agent capabilities change and let agents specialise synergistically from data.

entry.title: Lost in Perception: Isolating Perceptual and Reasoning Failures in Multimodal Physics and Geometry Reasoning

author.name: Raj Jaiswal, Sree Krishna Uppalapati, Dhruvkumar Patel, Ria Khatoniar, Tanuja Ganu, Rajiv Ratn Shah

entry.summary: The authors introduce a five-task diagnostic experiment across physics and geometry benchmarks that separates failures into perceptual, reasoning, or mixed causes. They show that incorrect diagram interpretation degrades performance even on problems models solve correctly from text alone, and that accuracy generally rises from raw images to human-authored captions. Recovery under corrected captions is high for some models, distinguishing perception-blocked failures from genuine reasoning bottlenecks, with error type depending on domain (calculation errors in physics, conceptual errors in geometry).

entry.title: Pay Only for Disagreement: Certified No-Regression Verdicts for Model Updates with Matching Label-Complexity Bounds

author.name: Vishnu Bindu Balachandran

entry.summary: The paper formalizes model update promotion as certified paired risk-difference auditing, exploiting the identity that the risk difference between two models lives only on inputs where they disagree, which is observable without labels. The DISCERN protocol uses a zero-label tier to certify benign updates from unlabeled traffic and an audited tier that labels only sampled disagreements using an anytime-valid confidence sequence robust to adversarial label routing.

entry.title: Structure is not mechanism: high-gain gated-FFN rows across text and genomic foundation models

author.name: Alexandros Tzanakakis, Aris Karatzikos, Ilias Georgakopoulos-Soares

entry.summary: The authors analyze unusually high-gain rows in gated feed-forward networks across text and genomic foundation models, including a frozen 22-model causal census, computing the exact bilinear weight operator rather than a diagonal approximation. They find activation-derived candidates are functionally enriched relative to controls, yet spectral concentration and operator magnitude do not predict functional importance, indicating that structural extremeness is not a transferable mechanism.

entry.title: Confidence Comes from Experience: Experiential Confidence Estimation from Reasoning to Agents

author.name: Caiqi Zhang, Xiaochen Zhu, Chengzu Li, Yulong Chen, Dharshan Kumaran, Nigel Collier

entry.summary: XConf proposes estimating a language model's confidence using its accumulated graded past experience rather than only the current inference process, which existing estimators do by introspection, token probabilities or resampling. Experience is stored as records of prior episodes with task, model reflection and outcomes, and is used to inform calibrated confidence for deciding what to ship, escalate or retry.

entry.title: Whom Do AI Agents Work For? Role Assignment Induces Sponsorship Bias in LLM Recommenders

author.name: Davood Wadi, Yu Ma

entry.summary: This paper argues that LLM shopping assistants face a conflict of duty because they advise consumers but are deployed by platforms that benefit from sponsored listings. In controlled choice experiments, manipulating the agent's assigned role in the system prompt changes how it evaluates sponsored items, revealing role-induced sponsorship bias.

entry.title: ${M}^2$Tok: Multi-head Multi-codebook Discrete Action Tokenization for Vision-Language-Action Models

author.name: Chunpu Xu, Zhixuan Liang, Yuhao Zhang, Chi-Min Chan, Jessie Wang, Yang Xiao, Mengkang Hu, Xiaokang Yang, Yao Mu

entry.summary: M2Tok is a multi-head, multi-codebook action tokenizer that reduces reconstruction error when discretizing continuous robot actions for autoregressive vision-language-action models. It targets the discretization bottleneck that limits the fine-grained control achievable by existing single-codebook tokenizers. Better action tokenization could raise the performance ceiling of VLA policies.

entry.title: GYROval: A Robust Benchmark for Cultural Value Orientation in Large Language Models

author.name: Alexander Didenko, Anna Shabanova, Vladislav Zapylikhin, Alexander Antipov, Ruslana Raemgulova

entry.summary: GYROval is a new benchmark that measures cultural value orientation of LLMs along the two Inglehart-Welzel axes using binary contrastive scenarios with no correct answer, where both options are legitimate. Twenty models were evaluated, and eleven were also tested on a paired Russian translation and a second sampling temperature to probe robustness. It matters because it releases a bilingual, publicly available instrument for auditing how models encode cultural values and how stable those measurements are across language and sampling conditions.

entry.title: Taming the Agentic RAN: Stability-Guaranteed Arbitration of Autonomous AI Agents in O-RAN

author.name: Seyed Bagher Hashemi Natanzi, Bo Tang

entry.summary: The paper demonstrates on a live O-RAN testbed that independently deployed AI agents, implemented as rApps from different vendors, can jointly produce recurring opposing swings in a shared radio resource partition even when each agent is individually correct. Existing conflict mitigation assumes a statically known application population and cannot govern agents whose behavior emerges at runtime. The authors present AURA, a lightweight arbitration layer that admits agent actions only when they satisfy feasibility invariants, targeting stable multi-agent control of the RAN.

entry.title: MIRAGE: How Conversation State Shapes Historical Evidence Use in Multimodal Personal Agents

author.name: Yu Liu, Wenxiao Zhang, Cheng Hu, Cong Cao, Fangfang Yuan, Xinyu Wang, Jin B. Hong, Yanbing Liu

entry.summary: MIRAGE is a controlled study of how multimodal personal agents retrieve and use earlier evidence across dialogue, files, and workspace state, holding evidence objects, questions, and scoring fixed while varying only conversation state. It targets the problem that agents produce plausible answers even when access to history has degraded, so outcome-only evaluation overestimates true evidence use. The framework evaluates whether agents can determine and ground their answers in the correct historical evidence rather than merely matching final answers.

entry.title: rMuscle: Robotic Muscle Memory for Efficient Vision-Language-Action Model Inference

author.name: Kaijun Zhou, Zhiyang Li, Le Chen, Jinyu Gu

entry.summary: rMuscle targets inference latency in vision-language-action models used for repetitive factory robot tasks, arguing that existing VLA inference frameworks ignore the characteristics of embodied workloads and the differing bottlenecks across inference stages. The authors characterize these workloads and find substantial task similarity across repeated executions that can be exploited. The system, described as robotic muscle memory, reuses that similarity to speed up inference and improve responsiveness and motion smoothness.

entry.title: A Zeroth-Order Paradigm for LLM Preference Alignment

author.name: Peter Chen, Xi Chen, Wotao Yin, Tianyi Lin

entry.summary: The paper proposes Comparison-based Preference Optimization (ComPO), a zeroth-order alignment method that extracts directional information from preference pairs rather than directly optimizing a differentiable preference loss on them. The authors provide a convergence guarantee for the basic offline scheme under smoothness, gradient sparsity, and compatibility conditions between the oracle and a latent objective. It offers an alternative to standard direct-preference methods motivated by likelihood displacement issues with small likelihood margins.

entry.title: Revisiting the Objective of Echo Chamber Detection

author.name: Abylaikhan Bexeit, Kushani Perera, Shanika Karunasekera, Jean Honorio

entry.summary: This paper argues that detecting an echo chamber in a social network, meaning a set of nodes that agree with each other on a topic while disagreeing with everyone else, is a distinct problem from community detection, maximum graph cut, and maximum clique. The authors claim to be the first to formalize an objective function for echo chamber detection, deriving it from the theory of Fourier transforms of set functions, and then propose a scalable semidefinite relaxation solved with an interior point method plus sparse linear algebra. Experiments show the method recovers ground-truth echo chambers, suggesting the formalization gives a more principled target than generic graph-partitioning heuristics.

entry.title: WaveTLM: Reliable Time-Series Language Modeling through Task Compilation

author.name: Jiahui Chen, Bingke Zhu, Hongyu Pan, Yingying Chen

entry.summary: This paper distinguishes reliable task-object generation from predictive quality in time-series language models, arguing that plausible text can violate shape, scale, channel order, or label constraints. It introduces ExecTS-QA, a contract-grounded benchmark spanning forecasting, imputation, classification, anomaly detection, and waveform analysis, plus WaveTLM, a compiler-executor model that translates requests into executable task specifications. It matters for making time-series LLM outputs verifiable rather than merely fluent.

entry.title: MLLMs Hallucinate when Information Distribution Drifts in Synergy Heads

author.name: Meng'en Qin, Junye Chen, Jucheng Liu, Youlu Xing, Song Wang, Ruize Han

entry.summary: The paper proposes HEAL, a head-level method that first uses causal noise intervention to remove causally redundant attention heads and then disentangles the remaining heads with a counterfactual difference-in-differences procedure, sorting them into four categories tied to hallucination behavior. The claim is that hallucination in multimodal LLMs corresponds to information-distribution drift localized in specific synergy heads, which existing attention-weight heuristics fail to capture. It offers both a diagnostic account of hallucination and a targeted mitigation.

entry.title: Bracketing Uncertainty in Clustering Under the Manifold Hypothesis

author.name: Savik Kinger, Luciano Dyballa, Steven W. Zucker

entry.summary: Kinger, Dyballa, and Zucker formalize when two manifold components in data can actually be separated, combining intrinsic geometry (volume growth, reach) with sampling quantities (fill distance, density). This yields a threshold phenomenon for mutual-k-nearest-neighbor graphs governed by an offset-to-fill ratio, and implies that clustering algorithms often over-commit to a single partition when the data do not support one. The contribution is a principled way to bracket which cluster assignments are statistically defensible rather than asserting a unique answer.

entry.title: Matching Multi-Loop Complexities with a Single Loop: Optimal Optimization Stationarity and Best-Known Game Stationarity in Nonconvex--Concave Minimax Optimization

author.name: Minghao Zhang, Zi Xu

entry.summary: The authors present a single-loop projected damped extragradient method for smooth nonconvex-concave minimax optimization, combining projected extragradient updates, dual momentum, and a moving proximal center. Under both optimization-stationarity and game-stationarity criteria it achieves the best-known complexity among single-loop first-order methods, including a gradient complexity of order epsilon to the minus three. The result matters because single-loop methods are typically simpler and more practical than nested multi-loop schemes at comparable rates.

entry.title: Not All Layers Need Tuning: Diagnosing and Directing Adaptation in Vision-Language-Action Models

author.name: Shahram Najam Syed, Arthur Jakobsson, Prayuj Sachdev, Jeffrey Ichnowski

entry.summary: This paper challenges the assumption that every network region of a Vision-Language-Action model needs equal adaptation capacity, testing five architecturally diverse VLAs from 93M to 7B parameters. Measuring per-region adaptation cost as normalized parameter displacement under region-isolated fine-tuning reveals a consistent spectrum: appearance shifts concentrate in the vision encoder, instruction shifts in the language backbone, and novel-object shifts in the vision encoder plus the action head. The authors then use this structure to direct adaptation more efficiently.

entry.title: Acting in Meters: Learning Metric Interactions for Precise Robotic Manipulation

author.name: Lijie Wang, Zheng Lu, Yiming Wang, Heyang Yu, Kenghou Hoi, Bowen Hu, Di Cui, Tianyu Xin, Haoran Liao, Wanqi Zhong, Xingjie Fan, Yizhao Xu, Ziliang Wang, Fei Gao, Yiming Li

entry.summary: The paper introduces a metric interaction framework that models object-level and scene-level relations in physical Cartesian space at a shared metric scale for language-conditioned robotic manipulation. Interaction-Centric Tokens explicitly represent end-effector pose trajectories relative to manipulated objects and are jointly denoised with actions, supplying physically grounded interaction structure. The premise is that existing VLA and world-action models leave metric relations among actions, objects, and scene geometry implicit.

entry.title: Deep learning emergent spacetime from fermionic spectral functions in holography

author.name: Koji Hashimoto, Hyun-Sik Jeong, Keun-Young Kim, Daichi Takeda, Kwan Yun

entry.summary: Using Neural Ordinary Differential Equations with physics-informed hard constraints encoding UV asymptotics, horizon regularity, and extremality, the authors reconstruct the bulk spacetime and gauge field of a charged AdS black hole directly from boundary fermionic spectral functions. The framework recovers the extremal Reissner-Nordstrom AdS geometry across non-Fermi-liquid, marginal Fermi liquid, and Fermi-liquid regimes, and infers the probe charge to sub-percent accuracy. It demonstrates inverse-problem machine learning as a tool in holographic duality.

entry.title: Does Moral Reasoning Training Help or Hurt? Red-Teaming RL-Trained Ethical Agents with Persona Attacks

author.name: Arth Singh

entry.summary: The paper red-teams morally trained Gemma-2-27B/9B and Llama-3.1-8B agents with five persona attacks designed to inject competing role instructions. Moral reward cuts adversarial degradation by 5.2x at 27B but costs about 11 percentage points of ETHICS accuracy, and reasoning-level moral reward yields 5.8x robustness while matched random reward yields none. Noise-reward controls, adversarial PPO, representation analysis, steering, and head ablations probe the causality behind these effects.

entry.title: SEA-LION-v4.8: A Technical Report

author.name: Ahmed Mohammad Dabeer (David Wang Dawei), Ahn Jeongmi (David Wang Dawei), Anocha Sutaveephamochanon (David Wang Dawei), Antonyrex Sajeban (David Wang Dawei), Aulia Adila (David Wang Dawei), Chan Hok Teng (David Wang Dawei), Adwin (David Wang Dawei), Cheng Zi Yi (David Wang Dawei), Nicholas Zhuang Ziyi (David Wang Dawei), Choa Hsueh Mei Esther (David Wang Dawei), David Ong Tat-Wee (David Wang Dawei), Evelyn Tan Chor Phin (Li Chunren), Heng Cheng Peng (Li Chunren), Jonathan (Li Chunren), Lee Chwan Ren (Li Chunren), Leong Wai Yi (Huang Wenzong, Raymond), Leong Wei Qi (Huang Wenzong, Raymond), Leslie Teo Eng Sipp (Huang Wenzong, Raymond), Liew Rachel (Huang Wenzong, Raymond), Limkonchotiwat Peerat (Huang Wenzong, Raymond), Montalan Jann Railey Estrada (Huang Wenzong, Raymond), Muhammad Ridzuan Bin Mokhtar (Huang Wenzong, Raymond), Nagarajan Karthik (Huang Wenzong, Raymond), Ng Boon Cheong (Huang Wenzong, Raymond), Raymond (Huang Wenzong, Raymond), Ngui Jian Gang (Chen Xiaowei), Nguyen Thanh Ngan (Chen Xiaowei), Tasawong Panuthep (Chen Xiaowei), Pereira Mark Gregory (Chen Xiaowei), Phang Shi Wei Benjamin (Chen Xiaowei), Poon Yip Hung (Chen Xiaowei), Joseph (Chen Xiaowei), Rengarajan Hamsawardhini (Chen Xiaowei), Siow Wei Kang Bryan (Chen Xiaowei), Tai Ngee Chia (Chen Xiaowei), Tan Choon Meng (Chen Xiaowei), Tan Le Min (Chen Xiaowei), Sheryl (Chen Xiaowei), Tan Siao Wei (Chen Xiaowei), Tan Yi Xian, Tee Jun Yun, Teng Kok Wai, Tjhi William Chandra, Tuchinda Pume, Wu Donghang, Yong Xianbin, Yosephine, Zhang Zhou

entry.summary: This technical report introduces Nemotron-SEA-LION-v4.8, a family of Southeast Asian language models (30B-A3B and 120B-A12B) built on NVIDIA Nemotron 3. Using continued pretraining plus SFT and online on-policy distillation, the models improve SEA-HELM scores substantially, especially in instruction following, reasoning, and NLU across seven Southeast Asian languages.

entry.title: Planning or Improvisation? Stress-Testing the Poetry Planning Site on Open Models and Open Cross-Layer Transcoders

author.name: \'Eric Jacopin

entry.summary: This paper stress-tests the claim that language models plan rhymes at the newline before writing a line, testing it across seven model/transcoder cells using open models (0.6B to 2.6B) and open cross-layer transcoders on a single consumer GPU. It decomposes the claim into position specificity, newline site identity, and a newline-resident plan, finding partial generalization.

entry.title: Voice of Reason: Reinforcement Learning for Spoken Math

author.name: Timoth\'ee Weisselberger, Edouard Graves, Alexandre D\'efossez

entry.summary: This work applies reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards to the GLM-4-Voice speech model to close the gap between spoken and text mathematical reasoning. After supervised fine-tuning on synthesized spoken QA data, RL is shown to further improve spoken math performance, addressing hallucination and accuracy limitations of speech language models.

entry.title: PANORAMA: Panoptic Grounded Captioning via Mask Proposal Selection

author.name: Sara Pieri, Evangelos Kazakos, Shizhe Chen, Josef Sivic, Cordelia Schmid

entry.summary: The paper studies panoptic grounded captioning, a task requiring a vision-language model to describe both foreground objects and background regions while grounding each referring phrase with pixel-level masks. It contributes PanoCaps, a human-annotated benchmark built from panoptic data, and a method addressing the incompleteness of dense captions and the inaccuracy of segmentation masks in existing approaches.

entry.title: ProtoLIP: From Sentence-Level to Object-Level Evidence Disentanglement

author.name: Yan Zhu, Yongbo Chen, Zhengming Ding, Rebecca Faust

entry.summary: The paper shows that query-conditioned vision-language models often retain evidence from co-occurring objects and shared context when queried about a single object, and that an exposed evidence map does not necessarily reflect what drove the prediction. ProtoLIP addresses this with a lightweight prototype-mediated evidence layer that organizes reusable visual prototypes into text-derived semantic families and routes them based on the query. It matters for interpretability and for making fine-grained visual grounding more faithful.

entry.title: EgoPathBench: Evaluating Zero-Shot Egocentric Waypoint Decision-Making in Vision-Language Models

author.name: Yang Zhao, Zhuo Chen, Xubo Yang

entry.summary: EgoPathBench is a dataset and five-task benchmark for first-person waypoint decision-making, testing whether vision-language models can pick feasible sequences of spatial actions that reach a goal from an egocentric observation. It argues existing spatial-intelligence benchmarks measure isolated relation, direction or target judgments rather than the integrated ability combining target recognition, action-consequence assessment, distance estimation and path planning. It matters for assessing embodied and navigation readiness of foundation VLMs.

entry.title: VOR-Bench: A Human Perception-Driven Benchmark for Video Object Removal

author.name: Haonan Huang, Tianrui Qiu, Xianghao Zang, Yinan Du, Zhixiang He, Chi Zhang, Hao Sun, Zhongjiang He, Tianwei Cao, Xuchong Zhang, Hongbin Sun, Kongming Liang, Zhanyu Ma

entry.summary: Presents VOR-Bench, an evaluation suite for video object removal that pairs an edited-video dataset with graffiti masks covering model-generated, tool-rendered, and camera-captured data, plus a paired-video acquisition framework. The authors argue existing paradigms rely on questionable references and metrics misaligned with human preference. The benchmark matters because video editing quality is currently hard to measure reliably.

entry.title: Symmetry-Aware Likelihood-Orbit Aggregation for Selective Left-Right Claim Verification

author.name: Zhouzhi Xiong, Chuxi Zhang, Weizhen He, Yi Chen, Qi Li, Donglian Qi

entry.summary: Introduces Relation-Orbit, a closed-form contrast with no learned fusion parameters that assigns eight normalized likelihoods to roles determined by reflection, inverse relation, and entity exchange, to verify fine-grained left-right spatial claims in frozen vision-language models. Claims are asserted only when the signed contrast exceeds a threshold selected with pointwise Clopper-Pearson upper confidence bounds. It matters because frozen VLMs remain unreliable on spatial relations and need calibrated abstention.

entry.title: MUMINS: Metadata-conditioned Uncertainty-aware Medical Image Next-state Synthesis

author.name: Anna Oliveras, Roger Mar\'i, Rafael Redondo, Oriol Guardi\`a, Cynthia Ifeyinwa Ugwu, Ana Tost, Bhalaji Nagarajan, Carolina Migliorelli, Vicent Ribas, Petia Radeva

entry.summary: Proposes MUMINS, a diffusion framework that jointly diffuses a baseline scan and its follow-up residual, summing them to synthesize the follow-up scan while predicting a spatial uncertainty map in a single pass. This avoids the multi-pass sampling usually needed for uncertainty quantification in diffusion models, and conditions on patient metadata. It matters for forecasting stochastic, patient-specific anatomical change such as tumor growth or neurodegeneration.

entry.title: DecoGS: Adaptive Static-Dynamic Decoupling of 3D Gaussians for Free-Viewpoint Video Streaming

author.name: Idil Sulo, Alexey Supikov, Ilke Demir, Sainan Liu

entry.summary: DecoGS performs efficient online training of 3D Gaussian Splatting from streaming video by adaptively focusing optimization only on regions with motion or photometric change, avoiding redundant updates of static geometry. It adds region-aware Gaussian management through gradient gating, targeting reduced flicker and drift while enabling fast, high-fidelity scene updates for free-viewpoint streaming.

entry.title: PanoGS-SLAM: Panoramic 3D Gaussian Splatting SLAM

author.name: Yongqi Mao, Hao Shi, Yufan Zhang, Zhonghua Yi, Xiangfei Guo, Kaiwei Wang

entry.summary: PanoGS-SLAM is presented as the first dense SLAM system built on 3D Gaussian Splatting that operates directly in the spherical domain for panoramic cameras. By performing differentiable rendering and pose optimization with omnidirectional photometric constraints, it aims for more stable tracking than pinhole-camera 3DGS SLAM under rapid motion and large viewpoint changes.

entry.title: Efficient Reasoning Distillation: Small Video-Language Models via Synthetic CoT and Difficulty-Aware Fine-Tuning

author.name: Mantek Singh, Jeshwanth Challagundla, Siddharth Raina, Jasmin Jarsania

entry.summary: The authors distill reasoning into a compact 2B video-language model using roughly 900 uncertainty-selected examples augmented with synthetic chain-of-thought rationales from a 4B teacher, training in under two hours on one A100. The resulting model outperforms VLMs up to four times larger and generalizes across CinePile, ActivityNet-QA and MLVU, with the counterintuitive finding that placing rationales after the answer boosts reasoning.

entry.title: LEAP: Learning Emergent Active Perception for Quadruped Navigation

author.name: \"U. Bora G\"okbakan (WILLOW), St\'ephane Caron (ISIR), Philippe Sou\`eres (LAAS-GEPETTO)

entry.summary: LEAP trains quadruped navigation policies that decide where to look without adding hand-designed proxy rewards like coverage or curiosity bonuses; instead, active perception emerges from task pressure in a goal-oriented navigation setting over hazardous terrain with visually discovered goals. The authors propose a policy architecture for navigation with active perception and a terrain curriculum. It matters because it avoids the task-objective conflicts that plague reward-shaped perception learning.

entry.title: OpenDexGrasp: Open-vocabulary Task-Oriented Dexterous Grasping

author.name: Jiyao Zhang, Junhan Wang, Tianyu Wang, Zeyuan Chen, Anthony Bolten, Yitong Peng, Hao Dong

entry.summary: OpenDexGrasp targets open-vocabulary task-oriented dexterous grasping, where a robot must infer functional intent from free-form language, ground it in multi-view observations and object geometry, and output an executable high-DoF grasp. The framework pairs OpenDexVerse data with a Coverage-to-Alignment recipe: OpenDex-Scale supplies large-scale semantic and geometric coverage via automatic synthesis, with alignment supervision on top. It matters because stable grasps are not necessarily functionally useful grasps.

entry.title: Energy-Regularized Imitation Learning for Force- and Work-Aware Robotic Manipulation

author.name: Toshiki Otani, Hiromu Taketsugu, Norimichi Ukita

entry.summary: This paper frames energy-aware manipulation as a physically grounded learning problem, defining a joint-space mechanical-work proxy from joint torque and angular displacement and training a differentiable energy predictor to estimate that work from robot states and actions. The predictor turns a non-differentiable simulator-side physical quantity into a differentiable regularizer used to fine-tune a pretrained policy (RVT-2 on RLBench across 12 tasks). Reported fine-tuning cut average mechanical work modestly (208.8J to 204.4J, about 2.1%) while mean task success also improved.

entry.title: ForwardDLO: Model-Based Bimanual Shape Matching of Unconstrained Deformable Linear Objects

author.name: Tim Missal, Berk Guler, Lucas Domingues, Simon Manschitz, Jan Peters, Paula Dornhofer Paro Costa

entry.summary: ForwardDLO studies shape control of deformable linear objects such as ropes and cables in a general setting where the object lies unfixed on a surface and two arms may grasp it anywhere along its length. Because each arm chooses grasp point, direction, and magnitude, the joint action space is combinatorially large and per-prediction cost bounds planner search. The authors propose a recurrent latent dynamics model that predicts per-segment displacements grounded in the observed rope state at every step to support model-based bimanual shape matching.

entry.title: Benchmarking Visual-Inertial Odometry in Subterranean Environments Under Sensor Degradation, Miscalibration, and Dynamic Occlusion

author.name: Yueying Zhu, Xiang Li, Thien-Minh Nguyen, Xuehe Wang, Shenghai Yuan

entry.summary: This paper presents a failure-centric stress-test benchmark for visual-inertial odometry in GPS-denied subterranean settings, built on the CERBERUS dataset. It evaluates four representative VIO systems spanning filtering, optimization, and learning paradigms under nine perturbation conditions including IMU bias/noise variation, camera intrinsic and extrinsic drift, and dynamic occlusion. The contribution is diagnostic rather than a new estimator, aiming to reveal when real deployments break rather than just nominal accuracy.

entry.title: PESTO: Formally Correct Registration of LiDAR Point Clouds with Limited Overlap

author.name: Valen Yamamoto, Matteo Marchi, Paulo Tabuada

entry.summary: PESTO is a new LiDAR point-cloud registration algorithm that uses tetrahedra as environment-agnostic universal features, making it competitive especially in cluttered or occluded environments with limited overlap between scans. Beyond empirical results, the authors prove worst-case bounds on alignment error, giving formal correctness guarantees. This is notable because registration methods rarely come with certified error bounds.

entry.title: In-Context Robot Learning with VLM Agents

author.name: Dongzhou Cheng, Taoran Yi, Ye Fang, Xingwu Zhang, Fan Feng, Yixuan Li, Gengxiong Zhuang, Rongze Wang, Shuai Yang, Wei Song, Weizhi Xue, Minyan Wu, Jie Gui, Jiaqi Wang, Tong Wu

entry.summary: This work asks whether commercial vision-language models with strong agentic capabilities, such as GPT-6 Astra, can learn from demonstrations, examples, and interaction feedback and convert that into executable, verifiable robot behavior from a new initial state without gradient updates or persistent memory. It frames in-context learning as the key to generalization in embodied AI, since no finite demonstration set can cover every deployment situation. It matters because it tests whether general VLMs can serve as robot policies in a truly few-shot regime.

entry.title: Missing Bridges: Composition-Aware Active Imitation Learning

author.name: Maxwell J. Jacobson, Ahmed H Qureshi, Yexiang Xue

entry.summary: The paper observes that active imitation learning methods typically request demonstrations based on expected information gain about the expert policy, which ignores how reusable behaviors compose across combinatorially many start-goal tasks. The authors propose Adaptive Agents via Latent Topologies (AALT), which selects demonstrations that maximize expected gains in start-goal connectivity so a single demonstration can help solve many tasks at once. The framing matters for making interactive learning sample-efficient in structured multi-task domains such as robotics.

entry.title: Recursive Reasoning or Statistical Extrapolation? In-Context Learning in Multi-Agent Interdependent Decision-Making

author.name: Yu Liu, Wenwen Li, Yifan Dou, Guangnan Ye

entry.summary: The paper asks whether in-context learning improvements in LLM agents reflect genuine recursive belief reasoning or mere extrapolation of statistical patterns in the interaction history. Using a public goods game with controlled history statistics and a history-independent rational expectations equilibrium benchmark, the authors find that when historical statistical structure is disrupted, the benefits of longer context largely vanish. This suggests much apparent strategic sophistication is surface-level pattern matching.

entry.title: Reflect, Revise, Reuse: Training-Free Skill Evolution for GUI Agents

author.name: Bofan Chen, Boxuan Zhang, Fei Tang, Zhengxi Lu, Yong Du, Tongbo Chen, Weiming Lu, Jun Xiao, Yueting Zhuang, Yongliang Shen

entry.summary: EvoSkill-GUI argues that GUI agents need procedural skills that can be revised online from execution feedback rather than static artifacts authored before deployment. The training-free framework represents each skill as a structured, editable object that is reflected on, repaired and reused at deployment time to cope with pop-ups, delayed loads and relocated widgets that invalidate pre-computed plans in long-horizon GUI tasks.

entry.title: A Comprehensive Review of Generative Physical Artificial Intelligence

author.name: Satyam Gaba, Krutiksinh Rana, Siva Sai, Vinay Chamola, Dusit Niyato

entry.summary: This survey reviews Generative Physical AI, where foundation models are coupled with physical embodiments for autonomous perceive-reason-act loops. It proposes a five-part taxonomy spanning Robot Foundation Models, Vision-Language-Action models, Large Behavior Models, Diffusion Policy Models, and related approaches. It matters as a structuring reference for the fast-moving embodied AI and robotics literature.

entry.title: Beyond EER: Multi-Dimensional Evaluation of Information Leakage in Speaker De-Identification

author.name: Seungmin Seo, Oleg Aulov, P. Jonathon Phillips, Kevin Mangold, Jonathan Eskin

entry.summary: This paper argues that speaker de-identification is usually judged only by equal error rate, which ignores leakage channels such as soft biometric inference, embedding-level re-identification, and structural template similarity that threaten unlinkability and irreversibility of biometric references. The authors propose a holistic evaluation framework spanning five complementary metrics, including soft biometric leakage, cumulative match characteristic re-identification, and canonical correlation analysis. It matters because privacy claims for voice data rest on how thoroughly identity information is actually removed, not just on verification error.

entry.title: Reaching Every Position Without Searching: Rotating Sparse Wiring on the Hypercube as a Substitute for Attention

author.name: Yoshiaki Takashita

entry.summary: This paper asks how much can be achieved with fixed, sparse wiring that is simply rotated between layers instead of learned attention. Treating sequence positions as hypercube vertices and connecting each position to its neighbor along a rotating dimension, information reaches all positions in log2 n layers using 2n links per layer instead of n squared. On a synthetic task that requires universal reachability, the rotating scheme matches all-to-all wiring at one thirty-second of the links, while a static sparse pattern fails, underscoring that rotation rather than sparsity per se is what matters.

entry.title: Changepoint-Aware World Models: Detecting Dynamics Shifts and Recovering by Forgetting Stale Replay in Model-Based RL

author.name: Everest Yang

entry.summary: This paper presents Changepoint-Aware World Models, a DreamerV3-based agent that detects abrupt changes in its own dynamics using an online CUSUM test against a rolling prediction-error baseline, then flushes stale replay data while retaining learned representations. Evaluated on simulated locomotion under doubled gravity and halved actuator gain, it recovers performance faster than standard adaptation. It matters for robots whose dynamics drift due to wear, payload, or environmental change.

entry.title: Machine learning kinetics from molecular dynamics data

author.name: Jonathan Weare, Aaron R. Dinner

entry.summary: This review surveys modern methods for estimating the committor and related kinetic statistics from molecular simulations, emphasizing self-supervised approaches that learn solutions of the governing dynamical equations instead of relying on labeled shooting data. The authors develop a unifying operator viewpoint connecting generator-based partial differential equations, variational principles and related formulations. It matters as a synthesizing reference for the growing intersection of machine learning and molecular kinetics.

entry.title: Fast Learning Rates for Physics-Informed Kernel Methods

author.name: Luc Brogat-Motte, Joachim Bona-Pellissier, Giacomo Meanti, Lorenzo Rosasco

entry.summary: The paper analyzes a physics-informed kernel estimator that combines n noisy value observations with m noisy differential observations of a linear differential operator, proving finite-sample bounds that reveal a two-regime structure for prediction error. It answers how much differential information improves learning and how the improvement scales with n, m, and the operator D. This provides theory underpinning the increasingly popular physics-informed learning paradigm.

entry.title: High-Fidelity Video Quality Assessment with VQA-Specific Saliency

author.name: Hakan Emre Gedik, Shashank Gupta, Alan Bovik

entry.summary: Proposes HFVQA, a no-reference video quality assessment framework built on fixed-size spatio-temporal inputs and VQA-specific saliency, aimed at preserving original-resolution cues and dense temporal information without the distribution shift caused by fragmenting. The authors argue existing efficiency-driven preprocessing prevents effective reuse of video foundation models. It matters for accurate perceptual quality measurement at manageable compute.

entry.title: Beyond In-Distribution Metrics: A Systematic Out-of-Distribution Evaluation of Congenital Heart Disease Segmentation

author.name: Aniketh Vijesh, Shrisharanyan Vasu, Abhijit Ramesh, Clare Pomeroy-Ward, Harikrishnan Anil Maya, Sarin Xavier, Mahesh Kappanayil, Gilad Gressel

entry.summary: Presents what the authors describe as the first systematic out-of-distribution evaluation of congenital heart disease segmentation, using ImageCHD as a held-out target cohort. Representative architectures are compared under combined CT and CMR training, CT-only training, self-supervised pretraining, and limited target-domain adaptation. It matters because clinical deployment faces shifts in scanner, protocol, institution, population, and modality that in-distribution metrics hide.

entry.title: Probe-VAD: Ordinal Likelihood Probing for Training-Free Video Anomaly Detection

author.name: Jiawei Gu, Qilin Zhao, Tengkuo Guo, Zhiming Zhong, Shuangqing Zhang, Fan Lyu, Fang Zhao, Guo-Sen Xie, Caifeng Shan

entry.summary: Proposes Probe-VAD, a training-free video anomaly detection framework using ordinal binary probing of vision-language models, avoiding caption-based pipelines that compress visual evidence into text and direct numeric generation limited to predefined scores. The ordinal probing interface aims to preserve subtle differences in anomaly severity for better ranking resolution. It matters for leveraging VLM visual understanding in anomaly detection without task-specific training.

entry.title: Causal-History Test-Time Scaling for Failure Recovery in Autoregressive World-Action Models

author.name: Lin Li (Edwin), Long Chen (Edwin), Kwunhang (Edwin), Wong (Tim), Jiaming Lei (Tim), Song Jin (Tim), Shucheng Du (Tim), Chuhan Zhang (Tim), Songchen Ma (Tim), Weihao Zhang (Tim), Jun Xiao (Tim), Kwang-Ting (Tim), Cheng

entry.summary: This paper reframes failure recovery in autoregressive world-action models, which are trained mostly on successful trajectories, as test-time scaling over causal histories, deciding when to revise history, where to recover and how to act. The proposed framework is training-free and targets the compounding effect of execution errors that become part of the model's causal context. It matters because it makes world-action models more robust without retraining.

entry.title: RAFAIL: Relationship-Aware Failure Detection for Robotic Manipulation

author.name: Loris Schneider, Edgar Welte, Rania Rayyes

entry.summary: RAFAIL is a framework for detecting execution failures in robotic manipulation by monitoring anomalies in task-relevant relationships between entities, such as gripper-object or object-target relations. It argues VLMs give semantic outcome assessment but add runtime cost, while generic out-of-distribution detectors fire on harmless scene variation. By focusing OOD detection on relationship-relevant parts of an observation, RAFAIL reduces sensitivity to task-irrelevant variation, using offline VLM annotation of successful demonstrations with task predicates.

entry.title: PointZero: 3D Point Track Completion for Learning Transferable 3D Dynamics

author.name: Bardienus P. Duisterhof, Kaifeng Zhang, Adam Hung, Bowen Wen, Stan Birchfield, Yunzhu Li, Deva Ramanan, Jeffrey Ichnowski

entry.summary: PointZero studies 3D point track completion as a pre-training objective for learning transferable 3D dynamics without any robot action labels, predicting future 3D tracks of all observed points from a single RGB-D observation and sparse partial tracks. This unlocks web video data, which lacks action annotations, for training world models. The authors contribute a diverse dataset and show the objective yields a rich dynamics prior for downstream applications.

entry.title: Designing Agentic AI Workflow Portfolios under Imperfect Selection and Compute Cost

author.name: Mojtaba Abdolmaleki, Stefanus Jasin, Boyu Wang

entry.summary: The paper studies deployments that run several agentic workflows for the same task and then select among their outputs, noting that using only the highest-average-performing workflow is suboptimal because workflows succeed on different instances. It formulates a workflow portfolio problem in which the operator jointly chooses which workflows to run and how to select the final answer, trading extra executions that may surface correct answers against compute cost and the added difficulty of selecting among plausible distractors. It matters as a formal treatment of when running multiple agentic strategies pays off.

entry.title: The Missing "I Don't Know": Why Three Reasoning-Reliability Findings Converge on Calibrated Abstention

author.name: Srijith Ravikumar

entry.summary: This position-style paper argues that three seemingly unrelated reliability results, reasoning RL degrading tool-reliability representations, safety-constrained rewriting versus truncation behavior across model sizes, and a recursion-theoretic proof that consistent reasoners without an implicit I-dont-know function must hallucinate infinitely often, all converge on calibrated abstention as the missing capability. It frames the shared unavailability as arising from distinct capability, policy and theoretical gaps.

entry.title: Who Judges Matters: Measuring Family-Conditioned Preference in LLM-as-Judge Panels

author.name: David Ababio Awuni, Luke E. K. Achenie, Benjamin Tei Partey, Elvis Gyasi Owusu, Nii-Nai Derrick Sowah

entry.summary: This paper studies whether LLM judges favor outputs from their own model family, using a fully crossed pairwise design with 9,312 judgments across four open-weight families. After correcting for a confound between a naive per-family statistic and candidate quality, all four families show a positive same-family lift of roughly 3.4 to 8.4 percentage points.

entry.title: A Study of the Reliability of Agentic AI-Generated Programs

author.name: Ayesha Shafique, Barton P. MIller, Elisa R. Heymann

entry.summary: The authors apply a best-practices agentic AI workflow to re-implement ten well-known, release-quality Linux utility programs, then measure reliability using fuzz random testing, including generational and black-box variants. The human-written utilities serve as a concrete ground truth for comparison. It provides an objective test of claims that agentic coding improves speed, efficiency, and reliability.

entry.title: Look Less, Hear Better: Jointly Rewarded GRPO for Streaming ASR

author.name: Xiuwen Zheng

entry.summary: The paper argues that the structural delay parameter in delayed-streams modeling is a poor proxy for user-perceived latency and that alignment-based supervision wastes available latency budget. It introduces AWED, a word-level emission-delay metric measured against each word's acoustic end, and post-trains a streaming recognizer with GRPO on a reward jointly scoring transcription accuracy and emission timing. It matters for latency-sensitive streaming speech applications.

entry.title: Reliable Virtual Sensing: A Multi-Domain Benchmark for Robustness Under Sensor Failures

author.name: Jens U. Brandt, Noah C. Puetz, Alexander Windmann, Marc Hilbert, Elena Raponi, Thomas B\"ack, Thomas Bartz-Beielstein

entry.summary: MuViS-C is presented as the first multi-domain benchmark for robustness of learning-based virtual sensing under sensor failures, covering ten failure modes from subtle drift to catastrophic dropouts at multiple severities. The benchmark builds on an existing nominal-performance benchmark and established corruption taxonomies, and pairs corruptions with complementary robustness metrics. It matters because virtual sensing underpins control and monitoring in cyber-physical systems, where silent sensor failures can produce physically implausible estimates and system-level failures.

entry.title: Reporting Practice Matters: The Impact of Reference Choice on Chest X-ray Report Evaluation

author.name: Daniel P. Jeong, Charles Q. Li, Hossein Hosseiny, Nitya M. Bhalla, Fatma Uyar Morency, Pradeep Ravikumar, Zachary C. Lipton, Michael Oberst

entry.summary: The paper quantifies how heterogeneous radiologist reporting practices, differing in terminology, shorthand, formatting, and detail, affect the evaluation of AI radiology report generation models that are scored against human references. It shows the sensitivity of established metrics to these stylistic variations is large enough to change model rankings. The authors introduce a radiologist-informed taxonomy to characterize reporting practice variation and its consequences for evaluation.

entry.title: LIGE-GR: A Smooth Leap from Ranking to Generative Recommendation in the LLM Era

author.name: Venkat Srinivas, Chenzhang He, Sam Woodmansee, Shawn Lian, Wenjie Hu, Renjie Jiang, Ziheng Huang, Xinyuan Zhang, Zhihao Zheng, Zhuoran Yu, Rui Li, Lei Yuan, Ziwei Li, Jimmy Jia, Mert Terzihan, Ekrem Kocaguneli, Yiming Liao, Zhichen Zhao, Yue Yin, Yue Weng, Wanlin Ma, Xufeng Cai, Weimiao Wu, Yezhou Huang, Du Zhang, Yukun Ding, Aaron Johnston, Yueming Wang, Zhaojie Gong, Yuting Zhang, Serena Li, Adithya Ganesh, Boying Liu, Haichuan Yang, Xialu Li, Matt Ma, Qunshu Zhang, John Joshua Miller, Praveen Rathinavelu, Cheng Huang, Aadhar Sachdeva, Josh Karns, Andres Aaron Gutierrez, Neil Agarwal, Gustas Pladis, Vladimir Batygin, Gopal Ray, Aditya Priyadarshi, Shantanu Patil, Zhe Wang, Penny Pan, Yiping Han, Arun Singh, Guangdeng Liao, Bi Xue, Xinyao Hu, Yang Song, Yisong Song, Meihong Wang, Haotian Wu, Deepak Agarwal, Ji Liu

entry.summary: LIGE-GR describes an industrial route from conventional ranking-based recommendation to generative, LLM-style sequence modeling of the recommendation task. The authors frame two challenges: incorporating sequence-level generation and optimization from the LLM paradigm, and doing so inside mature production systems already tuned around business constraints and serving infrastructure. The very large author list and infrastructure framing indicate an applied, deployed recommendation system rather than a purely academic study.

entry.title: Every Fixed Metric Has a Blind Spot: A Learned Atmospheric Critic for Scoring Forecast Realism

author.name: Younes Elberkennou, Dmitri Demler, Thierry Meier, Luca Rispoli, Fanny Lehmann, Joel Oskarsson

entry.summary: The paper argues that ML weather forecasting models can score well on point-wise metrics while exhibiting blurring, periodic artifacts, and unphysical spatial structure, and that any fixed evaluation metric can only catch artifacts its chosen representation anticipates. The authors instead train a discriminator to separate reference analysis fields from model output and convert its logit into a divergence-like realism score. Because the critic learns whatever distinguishes a particular model's fields from real weather, it adapts to that model's specific failure mode.

entry.title: A Geometric Theory of Decision Boundaries in Structured Markov Decision Processes

author.name: Fredy Pokou (MRE, INOCS)

entry.summary: This theoretical paper develops a geometric account of optimal policies in structured Markov decision processes, treating the decision-boundary geometry induced by a fixed optimal policy as the primary object of analysis. Under structural regularity conditions, the author shows this geometry gives the minimal representation needed for policy reconstruction and determines statistical and computational complexity. It matters as a step toward understanding representation and sample complexity of policies beyond classical value-function perspectives.

entry.title: FedGuide: Diffusion Prior Alignment and Value Baseline Guidance for Heterogeneous Federated Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Zhilin He, Gauri Joshi

entry.summary: This paper proposes FedGuide, a federated reinforcement learning framework that uses diffusion priors as behavior models to supply personalized data-supported distributions for heterogeneous local policy learning. Rather than averaging local policies directly, it aggregates diffusion priors via optimal-transport mixture-of-experts and adds value baseline guidance. It matters for collaborative policy learning across agents facing distributional mismatch in their environments.

entry.title: GroupKV: Hierarchical KV Cache Management for Long-Context Diffusion LLM Inference

author.name: Jinhao Wang, Zhexin Hu, Kangjie Zhou, Xin Zhou, Fangfang Liu

entry.summary: GroupKV is a lightweight hierarchical KV cache management system aimed at diffusion large language models, where periodic full-sequence recomputation and localized token updates make the cache lifecycle much more dynamic than in autoregressive decoding. The design exploits block-wise structure to reduce cache bloat and offloading transfer overhead, and it deliberately avoids heavy token-level indexing or clustering that cannot be amortized in diffusion decoding. It matters as systems work for an emerging alternative to autoregressive generation.
