entry.title: QEMScore: How Much Does the Measurement Add to Learned Quantum Error Mitigation?

author.name: Yue Zhao, Huayue Gu, Yushun Dong, Xiyang Hu

entry.summary: The paper introduces QEMScore, an evaluation protocol for learned quantum error mitigation that compares a trained mitigator against a capacity-matched control which sees the circuit description but never the actual measurement outcomes. It accounts for measurement spend without forcing equalization, then applies the protocol in a controlled simulated campaign and reanalyzes two published learned mitigators, Q-LEAR and QRAFT, from released hardware data. The value is in exposing whether reported accuracy gains come from genuinely using measurements or merely from exploiting circuit structure.

entry.title: Preservation of Log-Concavity and Convergence of Wasserstein-Fisher-Rao Gradient Flows

author.name: Francesca Romana Crucinio, Sahani Pathiraja

entry.summary: Crucinio and Pathiraja analyze Wasserstein-Fisher-Rao gradient flows, which combine transport with Fisher-Rao birth-death dynamics, for sampling from distributions known only up to a normalizing constant. They show that for a class of strongly log-concave targets with extra curvature conditions, WFR flows preserve strong log-concavity, unlike Wasserstein flows which do so only in the Gaussian case. This yields explicit non-asymptotic convergence rates for a symmetrized Kullback-Leibler divergence.

entry.title: HiLNO: A Hierarchical Latent Neural Operator with Multi-Scale Supervision for PDEs on General Geometries

author.name: Zhicheng Hu, Jiacheng Li, Min Yang

entry.summary: HiLNO is a latent neural operator for PDEs that builds a fine-to-coarse-to-fine latent space to avoid losing multiscale spatial information during compression, adding multi-scale supervision and anisotropic Gaussian attention. It targets operator learning on general geometries where solutions have multiscale structure. This contributes to scientific machine learning by improving accuracy-efficiency tradeoffs in surrogate PDE solvers.

entry.title: Learning Lyapunov Operators for Nonlinear Systems

author.name: Amartya Mukherjee, Maxwell Fitzsimmons, David C. Del Rey Fern\'andez, Jun Liu

entry.summary: The paper studies the Lyapunov solution operator mapping a vector field to its Lyapunov function defined by a dissipation-based Lyapunov PDE, proving it is well-defined, unique, and continuous under exponential stability on compact subsets of the domain of attraction. This shifts the problem from solving for single systems to learning a reusable operator across systems. It matters for scalable stability certification in control and safety-critical learning.

entry.title: DANTINOX: A Unified Framework for Multi-Paradigm Language Modeling

author.name: Marco Simoni, Aleksandar Fontana, Giulio Rossolini, Andrea Saracino

entry.summary: DantinoX is an open-source JAX/Flax library in which one modular Transformer backbone supports autoregressive decoding, discrete masked diffusion, and continuous flow matching, switched purely by configuration. Because the backbone, tokenizer, initialization, and training stack stay fixed, differences measured across paradigms reflect the paradigms rather than implementation details. It provides the controlled comparison infrastructure the language-generation literature currently lacks.

entry.title: STRETCH the Boundaries: A Unified Self-Taught Framework for Progressive LLM Evolution

author.name: Yajie Yu, Mark Lee, Yue Feng

entry.summary: STRETCH is a self-improvement framework inspired by cognitive scaffolding that introduces a dynamic Stretch Zone aligning question difficulty with the model's evolving capability. Within one parameter space, the model alternates between a Scaffolder generating boundary-pushing challenges and a Learner optimizing solving trajectories via reinforcement learning, stabilizing dual-loop co-evolution.

entry.title: When Audit Quality Fails to Predict Downstream Utility: A Counterfactual Study of Synthetic-Data Selectors for Low-Resource African NLP

author.name: Son Ha Xuan, Phat T. Tran-Truong, Xuan-Bach Le

entry.summary: The study shows that using an LLM judge's quality ratings as a proxy for downstream usefulness breaks down in low-resource African-language classification. Across four languages, two tasks, and five matched-budget selectors, audit rankings barely correlate with downstream Macro-F1, and the authors propose a counterfactual audit framework that yields cleaner selected pools across multiple audit channels.

entry.title: Which Pretext Task Transfers? Self-Supervised Pretraining Objectives for Lung Ultrasound

author.name: Moein Heidari, Junbo Rao, Jai Choraria, Wenjin Chen, David J. Foran, Ilker Hacihaliloglu

entry.summary: This paper compares three self-supervised objective families, contrastive learning, masked reconstruction and joint-embedding predictive architectures, for lung ultrasound under a controlled setup with the same encoder, corpus, optimization schedule and frozen evaluation protocol. Encoders are pretrained on COVID-BLUeS videos and probed with linear, kNN and attentive readouts across several label budgets. It matters because it isolates which pretext task actually transfers in a medical imaging setting where prior comparisons were confounded.

entry.title: What Breaks Local Watermarks? A Robustness Benchmark for Local Invisible Image Watermarking

author.name: Kai Yao, Bence Szil\'agyi, Sebesty\'en Kamp, M\'at\'e Po\'or, M\'at\'e Szilveszter, Matyas K. Zsoldos, Marc Juarez

entry.summary: This paper presents the first systematic robustness benchmark for local invisible image watermarking, which embeds signals in selected image regions for payload recovery and localization. It spans 55 image transformations and unifies datasets and metrics that prior single-method studies chose inconsistently. The benchmark matters because it enables direct comparison across local watermarking methods and clarifies the overall robustness picture.

entry.title: MedPCFM-TED: One-Step Point Cloud Flow Matching for Implant Generation via Teacher-Guided Endpoint Distillation

author.name: Kamil Kwarciak, Marek Wodzinski

entry.summary: Proposes Teacher-guided Endpoint Distillation (TED), a one-step distillation framework for conditional cranial implant generation on point clouds. TED trains a one-step student using teacher-guided endpoint supervision and geometric matching losses without explicit path straightening, cutting the multiple neural function evaluations needed by standard flow matching. It matters because rapid generation of multiple plausible implant candidates is clinically useful.

entry.title: sensVLA: Spatially-Grounded Vision-Language-Action Model for Autonomous Wheel Loader

author.name: Gopi Krishna Erabati, Bjarne Johannsen, Angus Stewart, Vardeep Singh Sandhu

entry.summary: Presents sensVLA, a vision-language-action architecture pairing a Qwen3-2B VLM with a fully trainable transformer action expert trained by flow-matching velocity regression. Bird's-eye-view features from fused front and rear lidar go directly to the action expert via a dedicated cross-attention pathway, while the VLM consumes RGB views for task semantics, decoupling spatial grounding from linguistic reasoning. It matters as a real-world heavy-machinery autonomy demonstration.

entry.title: Predicting Human Disagreement for Calibrated Dynamic Facial Expression Recognition

author.name: Yiming Wang, Frederick W. B. Li, Jingyun Wang

entry.summary: Proposes a disagreement-aware dynamic facial expression recognition framework that trains directly on raw annotator count vectors using a Dirichlet-Multinomial likelihood, providing scale-sensitive supervision for the Dirichlet concentration while preserving the predictive mean. A separate ambiguity head predicts annotation entropy, and a monotone Chow-style reject rule combines ambiguity, vacuity, temporal instability, and input quality for selective prediction. It matters because facial expression labels are intrinsically ambiguous and majority-vote training discards that signal.

entry.title: From Foundation Embeddings to Cropland Maps: Label Efficiency, Temporal Transferability and Independent Human Validation

author.name: Mohammad Ammar Mughees, Giovanni Montefoschi, Zhongxin Chen, Maria Antonia Brovelli

entry.summary: Evaluates whether annual AlphaEarth geospatial foundation embeddings support binary cultivated versus non-cultivated mapping in Maine, USA, using 192 spatially separated patches with USDA Cropland Data Layer labels and no foundation-model fine-tuning. A lightweight classifier reaches 93.7 percent overall accuracy, with logistic regression within 0.3 points of a gradient-boosted ensemble and a parameter-free nearest-centroid rule at 90.2 percent. It matters as evidence about label efficiency and temporal transfer of geospatial foundation models with independent human validation.

entry.title: Cascaded Non-Line-of-Sight Imaging

author.name: Diego Royo, Mar\'ia Pe\~na, Forrest B. Peterson, Andreas Velten, Julio Marco, Diego Gutierrez

entry.summary: This paper argues that time-of-flight non-line-of-sight imaging has been unnecessarily restricted by the three-bounce assumption and shows that higher-order photon paths convey useful information for reconstructing hidden scenes. A cascaded approach combines ultrafast laser scanning with time-gated 2D sensor arrays to capture the relay wall impulse response, extending NLOS imaging to a broader range of single- and multi-corner scenarios.

entry.title: Anatomy-Change-Aware Bidirectional Selective State-Space Memory for Clinically Deployed Thoracic Radiotherapy Auto-Contouring

author.name: Galib Ahmed, Istiak Ahmed, Aritra Islam Saswato, Asib Mostakim Fony, Kazi Shahriar Sanjid, Md. Tanzim Hossain, Md. Anwarul Islam, Md. Nishan Khan, Md. Misbah Khan, Labiba Faiza Karim, Jobaer Rahman, S M Hasibul Hoque, Rahnuma Shahrin Rista, Kamruzzaman Rumman, Md Arifur Rahman, Syed Md. Akram Hussain, Mohammad Ashrafuzzaman Khan, M. Monir Uddin

entry.summary: DAMM-Net++ is a 2.5D thoracic organ-at-risk and target segmentation architecture whose core is an anatomy-change-aware bidirectional selective state-space memory that models through-plane anatomical change along the axial slice sequence. It also adds a boundary-aware decoder for sharper surface predictions and an uncertainty head providing calibrated per-voxel confidence for clinical triage, evaluated on 2,146 patients across four centers plus an independent external cohort.

entry.title: OPD-Aha: From Linguistic Momentum to Visual Reflection in Multimodal On-Policy Distillation

author.name: Chenhao Qiu, Dawei Li, Yechao Zhang, Lei Gong, Zhen Tan

entry.summary: OPD-Aha analyzes privileged on-policy distillation for multimodal reasoning, showing that when a student early misreads an image, the accumulating erroneous rationale can drag the teacher into the same hallucination and collapse supervision. The authors find the teacher's visual corrective preference is not lost, and exploit comparing teacher predictions with and without the real image to recover it.

entry.title: Timely Activation of Safety Filters via One-Step Reachability Expansion

author.name: Javier Borquez

entry.summary: This paper addresses the mismatch between continuous-time Hamilton-Jacobi reachability safety filters and discretely applied robot control, where a system can jump into the backward reachable tube between updates. It proposes a one-step expanded backward reachable tube that predicts all states able to reach the true unsafe set within one timestep, triggering the filter earlier. It matters for making least-restrictive safety filters actually safe under sampled control.

entry.title: Technical Report: One-Step Drifting Action Heads for GR00T N1.7

author.name: Xihe Shao

entry.summary: This technical report swaps the iterative diffusion-transformer action head of a GR00T N1.7 vision-language-action policy for a one-step drifting action head, plus an overlap-conditioned extension for asynchronous chunk replacement. On LIBERO the action-head forward time drops from roughly 45.3 ms to 5.0 ms and backbone-plus-head time from about 70.0 ms to 30.6 ms, while closed-loop task success is examined across multi-seed runs on two A800 GPUs. It matters for making VLA policies fast enough for real-time closed-loop control.

entry.title: Approximating High Dimensional Self-Motion Manifolds via Deep Generative Models

author.name: Haitao Gao, Yang Song, Liao Wu

entry.summary: The paper tackles self-motion manifolds (SMMs) of redundant manipulators, the geometric structure of the infinite set of inverse-kinematics solutions at a fixed end-effector pose. Existing null-space continuation and learning methods assume the SMM is a curve and fail for higher redundancy orders. The authors instead take a probabilistic view, treating the SMM as the support of the conditional posterior over configurations given a pose, recovering it by sampling from a learned distribution and separating disjoint components by clustering, with a formulation independent of manifold dimension.

entry.title: InterMASH: A Unified Geometric Representation for Grasp Synthesis

author.name: Xuanze Yang, Yumeng Liu, Haiyang Xin, Changhao Li, Haowei Shen, Kai Xu, Ligang Liu, Ruizhen Hu

entry.summary: InterMASH proposes a unified geometric representation for grasp synthesis that establishes cross-embodiment correspondence between human and robotic hands using sphere-fixed anchors. At each anchor, low-degree spherical harmonics compactly encode local hand geometry, avoiding the incompleteness of contact maps and the cost/redundancy of dense implicit descriptors. The goal is a shared representation supporting stable, physically plausible hand-object interaction generation across morphologies.

entry.title: DynoFluxBench: Benchmarking Kinodynamic Space-Time Planners in Dynamic Environments

author.name: Franz Quei{\ss}ner, Andreas Orthey, Wolfgang H\"onig

entry.summary: DynoFluxBench is a benchmark framework for comparing kinodynamic planners in known, dynamic environments with unbounded arrival time, filling a gap where no dedicated framework combined kinodynamic feasibility with moving obstacles. To demonstrate utility and establish baselines, the authors develop three planners: ST-Db-RRT (which expands with randomly selected discontinuity-bounded motion primitives using trajectory optimization), KIST, and ST-GBRRT, which maintain kinodynamic structure under a space-time formulation. The benchmark covers different kinodynamic search paradigms.

entry.title: TRACER: Adaptive Multi-Robot Social Navigation via Joint Human-Response Prediction and Interaction-Aware Replanning

author.name: Lan Hu, Minghui Liwang, Wenbo Zhu, Xinlei Yi, Wei Gong, Yiguang Hong, Seyyedali Hosseinalipour

entry.summary: TRACER is a bi-directional receding-horizon framework for multi-robot navigation in human-shared spaces that closes the loop between predicting human responses and adapting robot plans. It evaluates candidate team trajectories while jointly modeling robot-entity interactions and updating future decisions based on executed interaction outcomes. This unifies what prior work treated separately: action-conditioned prediction, multi-robot planning, and online adaptation.

entry.title: Obstacles to the scalable oversight of auto-alignment research

author.name: Sam Martin

entry.summary: This work studies obstacles to faithfully automating alignment research, framing the problem as one of scalable oversight: as models improve, humans' ability to notice failures in auto-alignment outputs will diminish because checks become too costly and models can tailor responses to their judges. Drawing on examples from Geoguessr and Arcadia's internal auto-alignment runs, the authors argue that debate shows promise on typical capability benchmarks but fails on judgment-call tasks resembling automated alignment research. It matters because auto-alignment is often proposed as a path to scaling safety work.

entry.title: New AI technique could make minimally invasive surgeries safer and more precise

author.name: Adam Zewe | MIT News

entry.summary: MIT researchers and clinicians developed an AI method that rapidly matches intraoperative X-rays to a patient's preoperative 3D CT or MRI scan, adapting to each patient in about five minutes. The approach aims to help surgeons localize catheters and endoscopes during minimally invasive procedures, where flat X-rays make tool position and orientation hard to judge.

entry.title: Learning Heterogeneous Preferences

author.name: Shiwali Mohan, Matt Hong, Dule Shu, Aniek Fransen, Shabnam Hakimi, Matt Klenk

entry.summary: The paper argues that standard RLHF-style utility models wrongly assume a universal utility shared across a population and treat annotator disagreement as noise. Drawing on rational choice theory, it introduces individuated utility functions to model subjective preference learning where choices arise from heterogeneous but internally consistent utilities.

entry.title: Where Should Agents Live? Energy-Memory Characterization of Agentic AI for the Edge-Cloud Continuum

author.name: Carolina Fortuna, Vid Han\v{z}el, Tim Strnad, Bla\v{z} Bertalani\v{c}

entry.summary: The paper examines agentic AI workflows, in which LLMs perform multi-step reasoning, call diagnostic tools, retrieve domain knowledge, and coordinate across agent teams, as they spread across the edge-cloud continuum in autonomous 5G-Advanced and 6G operations. It contrasts the roughly 20W metabolic budget of biological cognition with the energy and memory intensity of contemporary LLMs and argues existing lifecycle metrics evaluate only isolated single-model inferences or ignore multi-agent execution graphs entirely. The contribution is an energy-memory characterization intended to inform where agent workloads should be placed, supporting sustainable lifecycle orchestration.

entry.title: Beyond Truncation: Rethinking LLM Decoding as Ensemble Pruning

author.name: Dunyao Xue, Chengshuo Du, Zhengbo Wang, Wenlin Dai, Cheng Meng

entry.summary: ME-Decoding recasts LLM candidate token selection as an ensemble-pruning problem rather than simple truncation by scalar probability. It uses a Mahalanobis distance-driven subset optimisation to promote semantic diversity among selected candidates while preserving high-probability choices, dynamically discounting redundancy. The goal is to avoid the computational overhead and inference instability of existing geometry-aware reweighting methods.

entry.title: PrimeScientist: Strategic Allocation of Research Effort in Autonomous Research

author.name: Xinle Yu, Fan Bai, Kaiser Sun, Hengshuo Miao, Abhay Anand, Zhongyan Luo, Kun Zhou, Zhen Wang

entry.summary: PrimeScientist targets the problem that autonomous research agents propose more directions than they can pursue, so they must decide how to invest effort across attempts. It formulates strategic research effort allocation as a sequential decision problem that jointly determines research direction and resource investment over successive attempts.

entry.title: An Empirical Evaluation of Cost-Efficient Large Language Models on Algorithmic Programming Tasks

author.name: Chandimal Adikari, Nandika Herath

entry.summary: The study tests whether cheaper models (Gemini Flash 3, GPT-5.4 mini, Claude Haiku 4.5) can generate enterprise-grade Java Spring Boot service methods from written specs, running 992 problems across eight agent/prompt configurations for 7,593 total methods. Withheld problems probe behavior on missing inputs, and an eight-class taxonomy classifies outcomes. It provides practical evidence on the reliability limits of budget LLMs for production code generation.

entry.title: Trajectory Learnability for Offline On-Policy Distillation with Imperfect Teachers

author.name: Yihao Ai, Weilong Yan

entry.summary: This work asks what remains learnable from imperfect teacher supervision in offline on-policy distillation, where collected student trajectories and teacher labels are reused throughout optimization. Rather than repeatedly continuing trajectories to estimate teacher recoverability, the authors use teacher-successful problems as a cheap reference for what the student can absorb. It offers a practical criterion for filtering or weighting supervision without losing offline efficiency.

entry.title: Beyond Outcomes: Dual-View Relational Learning for Efficient Agent Benchmarking

author.name: Xinshuai Guo, Junjie Wu, Dolly Deng, Yinghui Li, Hai-Tao Zheng, Suncong Zheng, Maxm Pan

entry.summary: Because agent benchmarks are far costlier to run than standard LLM benchmarks, the authors study compression that goes beyond redundancy in final-score distributions. From large-scale trajectory analysis they identify six process signals systematically associated with final agent performance and propose DualViewEval, which jointly exploits outcome and process relations to learn a fixed-size miniset and predict full-benchmark scores. They validate across five agent benchmarks.

entry.title: Interpretable Multi-Instance Learning Enables Early Prediction of Key Molecular Alterations from Routine Flow Cytometry in Acute Myeloid Leukemia

author.name: Jonathan Legrand (IMB, MONC), Aguirre Mimoun (CHU Bordeaux), Baudouin Denis de Senneville (IMB, MONC), Audrey Bidet (CHU Bordeaux), Pierre-Yves Dumas (CHU Bordeaux, Inserm U1312 - BRIC), Christ\`ele Etchegaray (MONC, IMB)

entry.summary: This clinical machine learning study predicts NPM1 and FLT3-ITD mutations in acute myeloid leukemia from routine flow cytometry, using an interpretable multi-instance learning classifier that treats each patient sample as a bag of individual cells. The model is benchmarked against a clinical-variable random forest and a CNN adapted for the data. It matters because molecular results currently take weeks while treatment decisions cannot wait, so a fast, free, and interpretable surrogate could accelerate care.

entry.title: Derivative-Free Structured Updates for Muon

author.name: Pengcheng Xie

entry.summary: This paper develops a derivative-free framework that builds Muon-style updates, which normally orthogonalize a gradient-based momentum matrix, from structured finite differences instead of gradients. Four variants are studied: full entrywise recovery, random low-rank surrogates, basis-aligned rank-one probing and direct structured search, with the observation that exhaustive basis-aligned probing reduces to coordinate finite differences up to positive scaling. Matrix regression experiments show random rank-one probing can cut the number of function evaluations substantially at some cost in update accuracy.

entry.title: vidax: A Unified JAX Framework for Video Generative Models on Accelerator Meshes

author.name: Congyue Deng

entry.summary: vidax is an open-source JAX/Flax inference engine plus zero-copy PyTorch-to-JAX weight translator for modern video generative architectures, including Diffusion Transformers, omnimodal Mixture-of-Transformers, 3D VAEs, text encoders, and native samplers, with no PyTorch dependency at execution time. It unifies 1D tensor parallelism with DeepSpeed-Ulysses style sequence parallelism to make long-sequence spatiotemporal attention viable on Cloud TPU pods. The motivation is that open-source video models ship almost exclusively as PyTorch/CUDA implementations, leaving TPU memory pools without a production inference path.

entry.title: Gradient Descent with Stochastic Subspaces via Persistence of Memory

author.name: Subhroshekhar Ghosh, Clement Z. Q. Ng, Pierre-Louis Poirion, Akiko Takeda

entry.summary: The authors extend stochastic subspace gradient descent by introducing a weakly correlated guidance vector that persists across many iterations before being refreshed, structuring how random subspaces are generated. They provide guarantees linking refresh intervals to problem parameters and target large-scale and distributed optimization. This is relevant to scalable training and optimization theory where full-gradient steps are infeasible.

entry.title: SFT or RL for Tool-Calling Agents? A Controlled Study Across Data, Method, and Scale

author.name: Md Tahmid Rahman Laskar, Xue-Yong Fu, Shashi Bhushan TN

entry.summary: This controlled study compares LoRA supervised fine-tuning, GRPO reinforcement learning, and SFT followed by GRPO for tool calling across six Qwen3 models from 0.6B to 32B parameters, measuring both in-distribution performance and cross-dataset transfer. SFT with LoRA is strongest in-distribution across the whole range, winning 15 of 18 settings, while GRPO wins 29 of 54 transfer settings by a margin averaging under one point. The results temper the assumption that RL is uniformly superior for agentic tool use.

entry.title: Dependency-Aware Trajectory Refinement for Efficient Multi-Turn Agent Fine-Tuning

author.name: Zhuo Chen, Zhen Zhang, Xinyu Wang, Kewei Tu

entry.summary: This work models multi-turn agent trajectories as round-level dependency DAGs to identify which rounds are load-bearing for the final answer, then fine-tunes agents on refined trajectories with redundant rounds removed. Across four multimodal QA benchmarks, refined trajectories improve accuracy by up to 1.7 percentage points while lowering inference cost.

entry.title: A Probe Shift Is Not a Fairness Fix: The Limits of Representation Steering in Speech Models

author.name: Nicolas Bourrel, Abderrahmane Issam, Gerasimos Spanakis

entry.summary: This paper asks whether linearly decodable speaker attributes in ASR encoders provide useful directions for reducing group word-error-rate gaps. Testing Whisper-medium, HuBERT-large, and Wav2Vec2-large on Common Voice and the Speech Accent Archive, it finds that steering representations shifts probes without reliably improving fairness outcomes.

entry.title: ViD: Vision-Dominant Gender Bias Mitigation for Large Vision-Language Models

author.name: Zhipeng Zhao, Zhaoqiang Wei, Peishun Liu, Youwei Zhao, Ruichun Tang

entry.summary: ViD is a causally inspired framework for mitigating gender bias in large vision-language models, analyzing attention across five patterns to reveal confounding effects from strong language priors and showing that visual-to-language cross-attention suppresses bias. It targets limitations of training-phase adjustments and post-hoc calibration, which cannot capture real-time visual-textual incongruence or emergent bias patterns. It matters for fairness and trustworthiness of multimodal systems.

entry.title: MEgoVista: Multi-view Ego-aware Motion Estimation for Metric 4D Hands and Head in the Wild

author.name: Jiangong Xiao (Northwestern Polytechnical University), Zhihao Zhang (Xi'an Jiaotong University), Yifei Dong (Maniformer), Chao Ma (Maniformer), Zhouyi Jin (Maniformer), Zhiwen Hou (Maniformer), Li Liu (Maniformer), Weihuang Chen (Xi'an Jiaotong University), Hongbin Sun (Xi'an Jiaotong University), Maoqing Yao (Maniformer)

entry.summary: MEgoVista is an offline pipeline that converts a single unprepared egocentric head-worn recording into metric two-hand and head motion within one gravity-aligned world frame. It is designed to escape the constraints of studio rigs and instrumented headsets, which require prepared settings and independent reference checks. The result matters for learning manipulation from in-the-wild human video, where metric hand labels have been a bottleneck.

entry.title: Accelerated Decoding of Centroid Positional Encoding for Instance Segmentation

author.name: Carmelo Scribano, Filippo Muzzini, Nedyalko Prisadnikov, Mohammad Mahdi, Yuqian Fu, Giorgia Franchini, Danda Pani Paudel, Marko Bertogna, Luc Van Gool

entry.summary: Investigates the prediction-decoding stage of instance segmentation models that use sinusoidal centroid positional encoding, where each pixel regresses an embedding of its instance centroid. The authors show that converting dense centroid embeddings into instance masks dominates runtime and propose faster decoding to remove this bottleneck. The work matters because post-processing overhead is often ignored when reporting model efficiency gains.

entry.title: EventEgoHands++: Event-based Egocentric 3D Hand Mesh Reconstruction with Real Dataset

author.name: Ryosei Hara, Wataru Ikeda, Masashi Hatano, Mariko Isogawa

entry.summary: Extends egocentric event-based 3D hand mesh reconstruction, addressing the problem that the camera wearer's own motion produces dense background events that obscure hand signals, and that prior work relied only on a binary hand mask. The paper introduces a real dataset to support the task. It matters for AR/VR and human-robot interaction in low-light or high-motion conditions where frame cameras fail.

entry.title: Semantic-Spatial Agreement Verification for Mitigating Object Hallucination in Multimodal Large Language Models

author.name: Ziheng Ren, Qian Gao, Jun Fan, Guohui Ding, Zhenyu Yang, Yuteng Xiao

entry.summary: SSAV is a training-free method for verifying object claims made by multimodal LLMs by checking that a claim stays stable across semantically equivalent prompts and repeatedly localizes to the same image region. A query-induced regional verification component combines cross-query region persistence, spatial overlap, and relative candidate density, motivated by safety-critical uses such as medication assistance and accessible perception.

entry.title: Conditioning noise is a free regularizer for LoRA fine-tuning: no pathology encoder required for diffusion-based artifact detection in histopathology

author.name: Konstantinos Moutselos, Ilias Maglogiannis

entry.summary: The authors show that conditioning LoRA fine-tuning of a diffusion artifact detector on random Gaussian embeddings, resampled each step from a small set of precomputed embedding statistics, consistently widens clean-versus-artifact separation without any encoder, cache, or inference change. A four-step ablation chain shows the effect does not require content, provenance, tuned intensity, or per-patch identity, and a LoRA-dropout control attributes it specifically to the conditioning pathway rather than generic weight perturbation.

entry.title: Predictive Varanus: Combining CSP Conformance Monitoring with Predictive LTL Runtime Verification

author.name: Angelo Ferrando, Matt Luckcuck, Pedro Ribeiro

entry.summary: The authors extend the VARANUS runtime verifier, which checks observed event traces against CSP process-algebra models, with predictive LTL verification so that violations can be anticipated rather than only detected after a bad event. The pipeline first uses the CSP model as a conformance gate, then translates it for predictive monitoring. This matters for autonomous and robotic systems where reactive detection of failures comes too late to prevent harm.

entry.title: Map2Route: Benchmarking Compositional Language-Grounded Route Planning over Semantic Maps

author.name: Muyi Bao, Hang Xu, Jingfan Tang, Zihan Liu, Yuxin Cai, Chen Lv, Wenshan Wang, Ji Zhang

entry.summary: Map2Route introduces a human-curated benchmark of 1,000 episodes across 40 scenes for compositional language-grounded route planning over semantic maps, featuring relational, comparative and nested instructions plus must-pass, must-avoid and soft-preference constraints. The authors also present Grounding2Route, combining executable code-as-grounding, verification-guided repair and scope-aware planning, which outperforms seven adapted baselines. It matters for measuring real compositional instruction following in navigation.

entry.title: UAVs Meet Embodied Intelligence: Bridging Human Intents and Flying Dynamics Via Harnessing Physical-Digital AI Agents

author.name: Yonglin Tian, Weiyi Wang, Houhua Lu, Xinyi Li, Yihao Wu, Jingyang Chen, Jianli Sun, Chengxiang Li, Yinuo Chen, Fei Lin, Tengchao Zhang, Jing Yang, Deyi Ji, Jian Di, Naiqi Wu, Yisheng Lv

entry.summary: This survey-style paper characterizes UAV embodied intelligence (UAV EI), where perception, reasoning, embodiment, and action are tightly coupled through flight and environmental interaction in 3D space. It argues that foundation models, world models, and AI agents are shifting UAV autonomy from task-specific perception and control toward systems that interpret human intent, understand open environments, and reason about physical consequences under flight-dynamic constraints. The authors distinguish the paradigm of UAV EI from its system realization, the embodied-intelligent UAV, and aim to provide a unified view of the field.

entry.title: FIVE-VLA: Fast and EffectIVE Autonomous Driving with Recurrent Action Memory

author.name: Kemal Oksuz, Alexandru Buburuzan, Yuhan Yao, Puneet K. Dokania

entry.summary: FIVE-VLA tackles three common weaknesses of vision-language-action driving models: large parameter counts, inefficient high-resolution image processing, and a lack of temporal memory. It uses an efficient vision encoder that produces only 98 tokens from high-resolution images and skips text generation for single-pass trajectory prediction, plus Recurrent Action Memory, a lightweight module conditioning predictions on previous action tokens. The result is a faster, more temporally aware driving VLA.

entry.title: GraphEcho: Structural Redundancy and Evidence Provenance in LLM Graph Agents

author.name: Sikun Wang, Yixi Zhou, Lei Fan, Fan Zhang

entry.summary: GraphEcho tests whether LLM agents mistake repeated traversal of graph paths for additional corroborating evidence by varying path counts and evidential origins while holding evidence content fixed. It finds model-dependent judgment shifts, with redundant paths increasing repeated walks across frozen agents, and shows provenance-aware post-training reduces revisits while sometimes lowering accuracy on scientific claims.

entry.title: HPOQuest: A Rare-Disease Diagnostic Agent Using Active Phenotype Acquisition

author.name: Kamilia Zaripova, Nassir Navab, Azade Farshad, Annalisa Marsico

entry.summary: HPOQuest is a training-free framework that helps clinicians diagnose rare diseases by starting from a few observed phenotypes and actively choosing informative follow-up questions. It maintains a probabilistic disease ranking that is updated as phenotypes are confirmed or ruled out, while all responses refine the candidate question set. Across four benchmark cohorts it substantially improves diagnosis from sparse initial phenotypes.

entry.title: Cognitive Extensions for Dual-Process Language Agents: Memory and Self-Reflection in Interactive Environments

author.name: Jo\~ao Meneses dos Santos, Arlindo L. Oliveira

entry.summary: This work augments SwiftSage, a dual-process agent pairing a fast action proposer with a slower planner, with two modular cognitive extensions: an Adaptive Memory Module for salience-gated episodic storage and trigger-driven retrieval, and a Self-Reflection Module for bounded runtime validation and corrective intervention. Because both are feature-flagged over the same execution substrate, the authors run controlled ablations on ScienceWorld comparing baseline, each module alone, and the full system.

entry.title: Scaling Articulated Rationales for MLLM-based Recommendation

author.name: Haoke Xiao, Yueyang Liu, Yuhui Zhang, Xiang Chen, Yufei Liu, Jia Xu, Yalong Guan, Xiaolan Zhu, Xiaoyu Zhang, Shijun Wang, Shuang Yang, Zijie Meng, Zejian Zhang, Ruochen Yang, Xiangyu Wu, Tingting Gao, Han Li, Lantao Hu, Cheng Luo, Kun Gai

entry.summary: This industrial paper studies articulated user rationales, natural-language explanations of preferences, as polarity-aware and reason-level signals for recommendation that go beyond implicit clicks and watch time. It presents SARA, a framework that turns sparse, low-quality rationales into scalable recommendation signals by building and then leveraging MLLM-generated rationales across a large item space.

entry.title: Walking the Score Manifold: Continuous-time Generative Dynamics on Learned Data Manifolds

author.name: Jan Tauberschmidt, Brian B. Moser, Stanislav Frolov, Andreas Dengel, Andrew B. Duncan, Sebastian J. Vollmer

entry.summary: This work reframes time-dependent generation as continuous-time evolution on a learned data manifold, using pretrained score-based models as geometric priors. A vector field is trained simulation-free to evolve data along score-induced interpolation paths, enabling generation at arbitrary timestamps and temporal super-resolution beyond the training grid.

entry.title: EDCT-Bench: Uncovering Faithfulness Gaps in VLMs via Explanation-Driven Counterfactual Testing

author.name: Sihao Ding, Santosh Vasa, Aditi Ramadwar, Thomas Monninger

entry.summary: The authors propose Explanation-Driven Counterfactual Testing, which extracts visual concepts cited in a VLM's explanation, applies verified minimal edits, and checks whether answers and explanations stay consistent with the edited image. EDCT-Bench spans visual question answering, safety-critical driving, and 3D spatial reasoning, revealing substantial faithfulness gaps in evaluated VLMs.

entry.title: Autonomy in Check: Governor-Mediated Adaptive Security at the Edge

author.name: Ijaz Ahmad, Ijaz Ahmad, Flavio Esposito, Erkki Harjula

entry.summary: The paper treats the boundary between automated planner output and kernel enforcement as the primary security object, since rule-based controllers, learned policies, and LLM-assisted agents can now influence live policy state. It proposes a split-control architecture where an untrusted planner emits typed security intents and a deterministic governor validates each intent before enforcement. This addresses semantically wrong but syntactically valid actions arising from incomplete or manipulated observations.

entry.title: Probabilistic Linear Explanations

author.name: Frederic Koriche, Jean-Marie Lagniez, Chi Tran

entry.summary: This paper presents a unified framework for probabilistic explainability built on sparse, anchored linear models that applies to both binary classification and continuous regression. By mapping instances to the Boolean hypercube, the linear explanations generalize subset-based abductive approaches, capturing both the magnitude and direction of feature contributions under a prescribed sparsity budget k. The authors analyze minimization of relevance error within this formulation.

entry.title: On the Identifiability of Mixed Ordinal and Exponential Family Causal DAGs under Linear Parametric Models

author.name: Sambit Mishra, Urbashi Mitra

entry.summary: This paper studies when the direction of causal edges can be recovered from observational data alone in linear parametric models whose nodes follow either an ordered logit distribution or a general one-parameter exponential family. The main theorem shows every edge between an ordinal node and an exponential-family node is identifiable provided the ordinal node has at least three categories and the exponential-family node has at least three support points, and matching converses show both conditions are necessary. It extends classical structural equation identifiability to heterogeneous, non-Gaussian node families, which matters for causal discovery on mixed discrete-continuous data.

entry.title: FoundAna: A GNN-assisted Foundation Model for Graph Anomaly Detection

author.name: Suprim Nakarmi, Chahana Dahal, Yue Zhao, Junggab Son, Zuobin Xiong

entry.summary: FoundAna is presented as the first foundation-model framework for generalizable cross-graph anomaly detection, combining GNNs with transformers and an anomaly-detection head. It targets the one-model-per-dataset paradigm that limits transfer across domains with heterogeneous tasks, scarce labels, and varying data distributions. If the transfer claims hold, it would make graph anomaly detection deployable in fraud, spam, and intrusion settings without bespoke per-dataset training.

entry.title: Revisiting Distributed Sign-Based Variance Reduction

author.name: Wei Jiang, Zechao Li, Lijun Zhang

entry.summary: This paper revisits sign-based communication-efficient distributed optimization, showing that majority voting on local signs can be biased under heterogeneous data and can fail to reach stationary points even with exact local gradients. The authors propose tracking the global gradient at the server via unbiased compression of recursive gradient increments, obtaining optimal convergence rates for nonconvex stochastic and finite-sum settings. It matters for scaling distributed training under low communication budgets.

entry.title: VLA-ULAP: Interleaving Cloud VLA Calls with Ultra-Lightweight Local Action Prediction at the Edge

author.name: Deyu Cao, Ryuji Oi, Kosuke Matsushima, Yuxuan Pan, Ziheng Wang, Daichi Fujiki, Atsutake Kosuge

entry.summary: VLA-ULAP interleaves remote billion-parameter vision-language-action model calls with an ultra-lightweight local action predictor of roughly 7.4M parameters that uses current views, proprioception, and executed action history to predict action chunks in a single pass. On Jetson Orin Nano it runs in 19.9 ms at 0.183 J per inference versus 284.3 ms and 50.55 J for GR00T on a desktop GPU. This matters for making large VLA policies deployable on power-constrained robots with communication latency.

entry.title: Comprehensive reconstruction of collider events with hypergraph representation learning and graph-conditioned diffusion

author.name: Lining Mao, Yvonne Peters, Ethan Simpson, Zihan Zhang

entry.summary: The paper presents VyPER, a framework representing collider events as hypergraphs with physics-inspired topology, decomposing event reconstruction into assigning jets and leptons to parent particles and predicting neutrino kinematics. It combines supervised hyperedge classification with a graph-conditioned diffusion model for neutrinos, optimized through a joint loss. This matters for high-energy physics analysis pipelines where neutrino reconstruction is otherwise underconstrained.

entry.title: Efficient Text-to-Image Generation: An Adaptive Step Schedule Controller for Diffusion Models

author.name: Kuluhan Binici, Cihan Acar, Shivam Aggarwal, Siying Liu, Tulika Mitra

entry.summary: The paper proposes an adaptive controller that dynamically adjusts the number of denoising steps in text-to-image diffusion based on the complexity of the prompt, using a mixture of step schedules and an error-term discrepancy signal at each timestep. It requires no additional model training and is evaluated on COCO and DiffusionDB. It matters for reducing inference cost in diffusion pipelines while preserving image quality.

entry.title: MAETrack: Unleashing the Potential of Pretrained Geometric Priors for 3D Single Object Tracking

author.name: Sifan Zhou, Qiwei Wang, Linyue Tan, Ziyu Liu, Ziyu Zhao, Xiaobo Lu

entry.summary: MAETrack studies why self-supervised 3D masked autoencoders transfer poorly to 3D single object tracking and attributes it to a layer-wise mismatch, where shallow layers retain transferable geometric cues while deeper layers over-specialize to reconstruction. The paper then builds a tracking framework that exploits this diagnosis to make better use of pretrained geometric priors. It matters because pretraining transferability in 3D remains poorly understood relative to 2D vision.

entry.title: StackTok: Accelerating VLMs Inference with Budget-Adaptive Visual Token Selection

author.name: Zhenbin Wang, Lei Zhang, Lituan Wang, Wei Huang, Yan Wang, Zhenwei Zhang

entry.summary: StackTok is a training-free visual token selector for vision-language models that treats query relevance as the objective and visual coverage as budget-calibrated support. It builds a size-indexed coverage reference from a greedy coverage-only sequence and adjusts support per query and token budget, since localized questions favor relevance while holistic questions need broader coverage. The method matters for cutting the inference cost of high-resolution VLM inputs without retraining.

entry.title: PiPS: Post-Hoc Prototypical Explanations for Interpretable Semantic Segmentation

author.name: Mi{\l}osz Adamczyk, Tymoteusz Zapala, Piotr Borycki, Przemys{\l}aw Spurek

entry.summary: Introduces PiPS, a post-hoc method that brings prototype-based reasoning to dense prediction, explaining semantic segmentation decisions through visual similarity to learned prototypes. The authors note that prototype explanations are well studied for image classification but largely unexplored for segmentation, despite its importance for precise localization tasks. It matters for trust in high-stakes deployments such as medical diagnostics and autonomous driving.

entry.title: EMODY Flow: Emotion-Aware Audio-Driven Full-Body Motion Generation

author.name: Harsh Kumar Agarwal, Xavier Alameda-Pineda, Olivier Perrotin

entry.summary: EMODY Flow identifies that flow-matching motion generators given both rich audio embeddings and a discrete emotion label tend to suppress the emotion signal, producing nearly identical motion regardless of the requested emotion, analogous to under-used weak conditioning in other conditional generators. The authors propose a lightweight roughly 35M-parameter flow-matching framework attached to a frozen Qwen-3 Omni model to jointly generate body gestures and facial expressions aligned with speech and emotion.

entry.title: TEMPO: Learning Temporal Context for Dynamic Robot Manipulation

author.name: Zhenyang Feng, Jimin Heo, Erik B. Sudderth, Unnat Jain

entry.summary: TEMPO argues that vision-language-action models fail at dynamic manipulation because single-observation inference suffers from motion ambiguity and state aliasing, and that scale and low latency cannot fix this. It introduces explicit temporal context learning so VLA policies can anticipate moving objects and disambiguate visually similar task states.

entry.title: Vision-Language Grounded Task-Context-Aware Imitation Learning for Robotic Disassembly

author.name: Jeon Ho Kang, Igal Tamarkin, Ethan Niu, Ian Novales, Satyandra K. Gupta

entry.summary: This work tackles long-horizon robotic disassembly, where a robot must execute ordered manipulation skills across multiple parts and multiple valid task goals exist. The authors inject task context through language to structure skill selection and to link language-specified tasks with visual manipulation targets, combining a hierarchical task framework with imitation policies. It matters for extending imitation learning to realistic, combinatorially diverse assembly configurations.

entry.title: An Efficient Algorithm for Minimum-Pressure Growth Planning of Vine Robots

author.name: Andres C. Torres, Tobia Marcucci, Elliot W. Hawkes

entry.summary: This paper formulates growth planning for vine robots around polytopic obstacles as a minimum-pressure path problem, since excessive growth pressure can cause the robot to burst. The proposed algorithm is guaranteed globally optimal in 2D and approximate in 3D with vanishing error as discretization refines, and is derived from an analysis of growth mechanics. It matters because prior planners ignored the pressure cost of following a path.

entry.title: TacBPM: A Tactile-conditioned Behavior Prior Model for Dexterous Reorientation

author.name: Jie Yin, Wanli Xing, Zeyuan Zhao, Xuezhou Zhu, Zhijie Deng, Kaifeng Zhang

entry.summary: TacBPM proposes a tactile-conditioned behavior prior model for dexterous in-hand reorientation, where policies must coordinate many hand joints through intermittent contact-rich interaction. The method distills multi-scale sphere specialists into a latent controller and lets downstream policies reuse a fixed tactile prior through residual latent actions, reducing the need to re-explore from raw joint commands. The prior conditions on tactile-proprioceptive history so latent behavior reflects the current hand-object interaction state.

entry.title: DistAL: Distance-based Advantage Learning for VLA Fine-Tuning

author.name: Reece O'Mahoney, Ioannis Havoutis

entry.summary: DistAL improves advantage-conditioned fine-tuning of Vision-Language-Action models, which previously relied on sparse success/failure rewards that leave the value function unable to distinguish states of differing quality. Motivated by an exploration of out-of-distribution detection methods, the authors use an embedding-distance signal to produce richer advantage estimates. This is applied to iteratively improve flow-matching manipulation policies trained on deployment data.

entry.title: SEAM: Submap-Anchored Evidence for Lifelong LiDAR Mapping under Trajectory Deformation

author.name: Kyuwon Kim

entry.summary: SEAM is a LiDAR lifelong mapping framework that generates evidence using a trajectory optimized with submap-level anchors rather than a single session-wide anchor, and performs dynamic object removal and change detection. Submap-level reprojection keeps evidence usable when the trajectory is later modified by a new session, avoiding full recomputation, and a DOP-based confidence measure suppresses unreliable inter-session loop edges that cause alignment errors. A directional voxel-wise evidence model accounts for occupancy patterns that vary with viewpoint.

entry.title: Launching RESI, the Institute for Responsible Superintelligence

author.name: adamology

entry.summary: The author, who recently left OpenAI, announces cofounding the Institute for Responsible Superintelligence with Shafi Goldwasser (zero-knowledge proofs) and MIT cryptographer Vinod Vaikuntanathan. Using the marshmallow-tower analogy, the post argues that responsibly building AI requires scientific foundations in how learned models, data, and institutions interact, rather than trial and error. It signals a new cryptographically informed research institute focused on foundational safety science.

entry.title: Memory Has Geometry: Non-Uniform Geometric Memory for Long-Horizon Personalized AI

author.name: Jiahong Liu, Wenhao Yu, Zexuan Qiu, Menglin Yang, Irwin King

entry.summary: The paper argues that long-horizon personalization should model memory as a user-specific dynamical state space with locally heterogeneous geometry rather than discrete records in a static latent space accessed by one global similarity notion. Geometry is treated as a computational language capturing stable versus volatile regions, variable-rate drift, and uncertainty about current user state.

entry.title: Contiguity, Not Importance: Budgeted Repair of Stale KV Caches After Document Edits

author.name: Mingyang Mao, Wyatt Mackey, Xiaomin Lin

entry.summary: The paper formulates in-place repair of stale KV caches after document edits as budgeted recomputation and compares training-free position-selection policies on a factual RAG benchmark with matched direct and derived edits. Across three model families, all policies repair direct edits, but derived cases separate them, with contiguous edit-local recomputation performing well at the primary budget.

entry.title: Time-Aligned Evolving Concept Graphs for Scientific Relation Forecasting

author.name: Fred Sun, Jingze Wang, Minkun Xu, Shangqi Guo

entry.summary: The paper addresses forecasting scientific relations, which can guide discovery by flagging promising connections before they emerge, and criticizes existing methods for either modeling concept semantics and graph structure separately or summarizing semantics over coarse snapshots that drift out of alignment with fast-moving graph evidence. The proposed time-aligned evolving concept graph framework treats dated papers as shared update events so semantic and structural states are reconstructed from the same publication history at each prediction time, with pair-level fusion predicting first co-occurrence, relation formation, and conditional relation types. It matters for computational science-of-science and literature-based discovery.

entry.title: WetRobo: A Reproducible Robot Kit for Coding Agents in Biological Laboratories

author.name: Yuna Oikawa, Kei Endo, Takanori Uzawa, Yunzhe Zhang, Manan Anjaria, Lerrel Pinto, Sherry Yang, Koji Tsuda

entry.summary: WetRobo is a portable, reproducible robot kit that lets wet-lab researchers delegate tasks to coding agents without teleoperation or policy retraining. It bundles a robot arm, standard lab equipment (incubator, capped reagent bottle, Petri dish), demonstration data, and a general AGENTS.md skill file, with a vision-language-action-style policy transferable across labs. The design targets the known brittleness of VLA policies when the operating environment changes.

entry.title: One Size Does Not Fit All! Dynamic Retriever and Generator Selection for RAG

author.name: Neeraj Anand, Payel Santra, Partha Basuchowdhuri, Debasis Ganguly, Sumit Bhatia

entry.summary: This paper systematically studies how retriever and generator complexity interact in RAG pipelines across factoid and multi-hop QA, including bridge and composition reasoning tasks. It finds that stronger retrieval generally yields larger gains than more generation effort but that returns are diminishing and non-monotonic, motivating joint dynamic selection of retriever and generator configurations per query instead of a single fixed configuration.

entry.title: AfriSyCo: Measuring Assertive Framing, Verification, and Wording Sensitivity Around African-Language Content

author.name: David Ababio Awuni, Rose-Mary Owusuaa Mensah Gyening, Elvis Gyasi Owusu

entry.summary: AfriSyCo studies how framing and follow-up wording shift model answers about African-language factual content, using native-language prompts plus a controlled cross-language factorial. Across 1,415 observations from 100 source questions, seven open-weight checkpoints, and six languages, assertive endorsement produced substantially more false-target selection than mention-plus-verification framing.

entry.title: TERN: A Delta-rule Memory with a Seasonal Reference and Online Adaptation for Epidemic Forecasting

author.name: Shunya Nagashima, Yuta Funayama

entry.summary: TERN is a forecaster for weekly influenza surveillance counts built around a delta-rule fast-weight memory that decays channel-wise and erases along a learned address under localized gates, plus a seasonal reference and online adaptation. The design targets the specific difficulty that signals helpful during a wave's growth become misleading after its peak, while last season's shape remains informative for about a year. It matters because better short-horizon epidemic forecasts directly inform vaccine distribution and public health alerts.

entry.title: Securing quantum error correction against misleading advice from AI agents

author.name: A. Bar{\i}\c{s} \"Ozg\"uler

entry.summary: The paper asks whether an attacker who influences an AI adviser can induce harmful quantum error-correction updates, identifying an ambiguity in passive syndrome records that obstructs correct recovery selection. In an odd-distance square toric code with ideal preparation, syndrome measurement, and recovery, opposite coherent X rotations yield identical passive syndrome-history distributions, yet a fixed phase correction can help at one sign and harm at the other. Terminal logical measurements on known encoded calibration states supply the missing sign information, and a separate evaluator accepts updates only when certified.

entry.title: Dreaming the Sound of Contact: Leveraging Video and Audio Generation for Zero-Shot Force-Aware Manipulation and Data Generation

author.name: Guanhua Ji, Tianyu Li, Dayoon Suh, Yuqian Zhang, Boyan Zhang, Nadia Figueroa

entry.summary: The authors extend video-generation-based robot learning by using the loudness of generated contact sounds to derive a bounded, time-varying desired-force profile. A pipeline jointly leverages generated video and audio from a natural-language task prompt to produce motion trajectories plus matching force targets, executed with closed-loop force control on a Franka Panda. This matters because purely kinematic generated trajectories fail in contact-rich manipulation where force accuracy is essential.

entry.title: Regional Explanations via Causal Sufficiency and Necessity

author.name: Xuexin Chen, Peng Liang, Zijian Li, Zhiyong Lin, Ruichu Cai

entry.summary: The paper introduces Causal Sufficient and Necessary Regional Explanations (SNRE), which learn an input region A and output region B such that membership in A is both sufficient and necessary for the model output to fall in B. Motivated by the classical Probability of Necessity and Sufficiency (PNS), the authors formulate a region-level PNS measure via stochastic interventions and derive a differentiable objective for learning these regions. This shifts explainability from single-instance feature attributions toward region-level behavioral characterization.

entry.title: Colla-Q: Toward Collaborative Experts in MoE Quantization via Minimax Precision Balancing

author.name: Eunju Shin, Jongbin Ryu

entry.summary: Colla-Q allocates bit-widths across Mixture-of-Experts layers using activation entropy, framing quantization as a minimax precision-balancing problem so that no single routed expert degrades disproportionately. The motivation is that MoE models behave like ensembles, so a badly quantized expert can damage overall performance even if average error looks acceptable. This is directly relevant to serving large MoE models under tight memory budgets.

entry.title: Bias Amplification in Multi-Agent Network: How Biased Agents Shape Opinions and Rhetoric

author.name: Omran Berjawi, Giuseppe Fenza, Rida Khatoun

entry.summary: This study simulates LLM multi-agent debate in which a minority of agents hold persistent extreme opinions while the rest update their beliefs through structured textual interaction. It finds that even a small fraction of biased agents can substantially shift collective opinion and the rhetoric used to justify it, illustrating bias propagation through language rather than through numeric opinion averaging. The result is relevant to the safety of LLM-mediated deliberation, moderation, and agentic social platforms.

entry.title: Spatially Adaptive Noise Injection

author.name: Frantzeska Lavda, Maciej Falkiewicz, Van Khoa Nguyen, Alexandros Kalousis

entry.summary: SANI observes that diffusion samplers interpolate between stochastic DDPM and deterministic DDIM updates using a single scalar noise-injection variance applied uniformly to every pixel, ignoring image geometry. The method instead decides per pixel and per timestep whether stochastic correction is warranted, injecting noise in high-curvature regions such as edges and textures while keeping smooth regions deterministic. This is a plug-in sampling modification aimed at improving sample quality without retraining the denoiser.

entry.title: When Edit Flows are Edit Jumps: replicating Edit Flows and EvoFlows

author.name: Gabriel B\'en\'edict, Melanie Buechler, Gerard Riera-Sol\`a, Chlo\'e de Ancos, Yves Gaetan Nana Teukam, Moritz Freidank

entry.summary: This paper reproduces Edit Flows and EvoFlows for antibody lead optimization, showing both are instances of the pure-jump case of generator matching over finite sequences where edits fire one at a time at learned rates in continuous time. The authors release EditJumps, the first open implementation of this framework, with a generalist antibody editor. It matters for reproducible generative modeling of bounded edit operations in protein and drug design.

entry.title: A Convergence Framework for Deep $V$-Learning: Error Propagation and Sharp Action-Gap Bounds

author.name: Yury Kolomeytsev

entry.summary: This paper develops convergence bounds for deep V-learning over a horizon, decomposing update error into six residual sources including fitting, target construction, replay, action selection, and exploration. Under concentrability assumptions, the bound controls expected policy loss and explicitly weights residuals from the last H-1 update blocks, yielding sharp action-gap bounds. It matters for theoretically grounding deep value-based RL algorithms.

entry.title: ActiveScale: Scaling Active Perception for Robots across Model, Data, and Hardware

author.name: Shuai Zhou, Kaisheng Pang, Wenxuan Song, Wenjie Zhang, Xinhu Zheng, Haoang Li

entry.summary: ActiveScale is a framework for robot active perception that augments a vision-language-action model with historical video observations and explicit camera-pose supervision via per-frame pose tokens and a lightweight prediction head. It also builds data from camera motion in human activity and coordinates hardware design. The goal is to let VLA policies reason across changing viewpoints and decide where to look.

entry.title: Learning Array Signal Topologies as Conditional Neural Manifolds

author.name: Julian P. Merkofer, Vincent van de Schaft, Ruud J. G. van Sloun

entry.summary: The paper proposes the conditional neural manifold, replacing MUSIC-style fixed array manifolds with an observation-conditioned mapping from source parameters to steering vectors, where an encoder produces a latent scene representation that conditions a zero-initialized neural field. This addresses performance degradation under model mismatch and parameters that are not identifiable from a fixed manifold. It advances super-resolution direction-of-arrival estimation.

entry.title: A General Kernel Framework for Non-CND Distance Measures Using |D|-Dimensional Sparse Landmark Embeddings

author.name: Marcus M. Noack, Maher B. Alghalayini, Mark D. Risser

entry.summary: The paper introduces the Sparse Landmark Embedding kernel, which embeds each input into a sparse feature vector using compactly supported bump functions centered at training points, so any standard positive semi-definite kernel applied in that space is provably PSD even for distance measures that are not conditionally negative definite. This removes the Hilbertian-distance requirement that fails for manifolds and probability distributions. It is relevant to Gaussian processes and kernel methods on non-Euclidean input spaces.

entry.title: Register Bias in Complexity-Based Large Language Model Routing

author.name: Simran Koul

entry.summary: The paper shows that complexity-based routing, which sends easy queries to small models and hard ones to large models, is not register-neutral. Text in African American English or second-language English registers is systematically assigned to lower-capacity tiers than meaning-equivalent standard English, and the effect is traced specifically to input length as a routing signal, since non-standard registers omit function words and look shorter. This is a concrete, mechanistically explained fairness failure in a widely deployed serving pattern.

entry.title: EviGen: Predictive Evidence Scaffolding for Verifiable Clinical Rationale Generation

author.name: Fengnan Li, Heman Burre, Liwen Sun, Roshni Varma, Matthew M. Engelhard

entry.summary: EviGen is a three-layer framework for verifiable clinical rationale generation from longitudinal electronic health records. Its first layer uses learnable queries to retrieve evidence predictive of a clinical outcome and ranks it by attribution scores, while a second LLM layer generates rationales, targeting reduced hallucination and missed observations in costly record review.

entry.title: MechSparse: Mechanism-Guided Sparse PEFT Selection Is Task-Shaped

author.name: Son Ha Xuan, Phat T. Tran-Truong, Xuan-Bach Le

entry.summary: The paper tests whether causal mechanistic signals can guide where to spend a small PEFT budget better than cheap heuristics. MechSparse scores attention heads and MLP blocks via normalized activation-patching recovery and trains LoRA/QLoRA only on selected sites, compared against random, magnitude, activation-norm and gradient/Fisher baselines in Swahili IE and English-to-Swahili MT cells.

entry.title: DenseFace: Bias Mitigation in Face Recognition via Density-Aware Probabilistic Matching

author.name: Mansur Bultygov, Vadim Seliutin, Dmitry Nekhaev, Ivan Laptev

entry.summary: The paper notes face recognition models still show significant demographic bias and that existing mitigation methods constrain training and reduce accuracy. It models face embeddings with von Mises-Fisher distributions, observes a dependency between demographic attributes and distribution density, and proposes DenseFace, a probabilistic matching procedure that corrects for density differences in pre-trained models without retraining.

entry.title: GraLoD: Graphics-Inspired Continuous Level-of-Detail Learning for Image Restoration

author.name: Hu Gao, Lizhuang Ma, Yulong Chen

entry.summary: GraLoD is a plug-and-play framework that treats restoration scale as a spatially varying, stage-dependent continuous variable, inspired by level-of-detail rendering in computer graphics. It reuses a network's native encoder hierarchy and aligns multi-scale features rather than relying on predefined scale hierarchies and fixed fusion, which helps in all-in-one restoration across heterogeneous degradations. It matters for making restoration backbones more adaptive without redesigning their architecture.

entry.title: Unifying Semantic Priors and High-Frequency Traces: Enhancing V-JEPA with Mixture-of-Experts for Robust Synthetic Image Forensics

author.name: Simone Teglia, Irene Amerini

entry.summary: This paper pioneers the use of Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture models for deepfake detection, arguing that ViT-based detectors relying only on low-level inconsistencies struggle on compressed or social-media-transmitted images. It combines JEPA semantic priors with high-frequency traces through a mixture-of-experts design. The work matters for the robustness of synthetic image forensics in realistic distribution channels.

entry.title: RegRet: Enhancing Region-Level Retrieval in Large Multimodal Models

author.name: Xun Liang, Honghui Yang, Weihang Pan, Ruisi Zhao, Boyuan Pan, Yao Hu, Wenxiao Wang, Binbin Lin, Deng Cai

entry.summary: RegRet is a large multimodal model based framework for region-level retrieval that aligns user-specified image regions with relevant regions or text. Its region-aware encoder captures detailed regional features while balancing them against global background context, so global retrieval performance is not sacrificed. The work matters for applications such as e-commerce product search and retrieval-augmented generation over images.

entry.title: SPEAR NeXT Causal Latent Forecasting Across Multiple Horizons for Spectral Temporal Earth Representation Learning

author.name: Rajiv Ranjan, Udaiveer Singh, Shashank Tamaskar, Dharmendra Saraswat

entry.summary: SPEAR NeXT is a compact pixel-wise multimodal spectral-temporal foundation model for Earth observation whose self-supervision is formulated as past-only, multi-horizon prediction of latent Earth states. Instantaneous states are encoded by the pretrained SPEAR model into compact 32-dimensional embeddings from optical, radar, and environmental inputs, and a causally masked transformer with rotary position encoding predicts multiple future latent states. It matters as an alternative to reconstruction- or invariance-based temporal pretraining for remote sensing.

entry.title: Temporally Consistent Graph Extraction and Matching for Longitudinal Angiographic Images

author.name: Linus Kreitner, Laurin Lux, Carmen Baumann, Daniel Rueckert, Martin J. Menten

entry.summary: Addresses the fragility of vessel-graph pipelines for longitudinal microvasculature imaging, where tiny segmentation differences produce substantially different graphs that cannot be matched across time. The proposed strategy matches graphs early, after basic extraction, and then jointly refines them to obtain temporally consistent vessel correspondence. It matters for reliably tracking subtle vascular changes in the same patient over time.

entry.title: NeuroSymbEAD: A Large Scale Neuro-Symbolic Caption Dataset for Omni-Directional Embodied Autonomous Driving

author.name: Muhammad Ahmed Ullah Khan, Mohammed Elamine, Sheikh Talha Uddin, Didier Stricker, Sk Aziz Ali, Muhammad Zeshan Afzal

entry.summary: Presents NeuroSymbEAD, a large-scale neuro-symbolic caption dataset built on KITTI-360 that encodes an ego-centric knowledge graph of static and dynamic objects with classes, heading, orientation, and distance from the ego vehicle. These annotations generate multilevel textual captions approximating a lightweight ego-centric scene map, with baselines for scene reconstruction, recognition, and object grounding. It matters for driving commonsense and grounded language understanding in autonomous systems.

entry.title: Hub-Spectral Activation of Latent Multimodal Knowledge

author.name: Ying Guo, Haidong Chen, Linrui Xu, Xiaohao Liu, Chuancheng Shi, Canran Xiao, Dan Zhang, Fei Shen, Li Shen, Tat-Seng Chua

entry.summary: Introduces Hub-Spectral Activation, a closed-form method for recovering and activating the hub-readable component of latent multimodal knowledge in frozen representations. The authors formalize this knowledge as source-induced cross-modal dependence and characterize the component determined by second-order statistics of two trained hub edges, proving conditions for exact recovery. It matters for reliable cross-modal alignment and retrieval without expensive joint retraining.

entry.title: BrainFocus: EEG-Guided ROI Selection for Efficient Vision-Language Models

author.name: Yihui Peng, Guorui Lu, Qinyu Chen

entry.summary: BrainFocus uses non-invasive EEG responses to visual stimuli as a human-derived cue for where to look, having an EEG classifier predict a target category and a detector localize the matching region of interest, which the vision-language model then receives as a crop. A confidence threshold on both predictions decides whether to route the cropped ROI or fall back, keeping VQA efficient on large cluttered images.

entry.title: Tables Decoded: DELTA for Structure, TARQA for Understanding

author.name: Jahanvi Rajput, Dhruv Kudale, Saikiran Kasturi, Utkarsh Verma, Ganesh Ramakrishnan

entry.summary: This work proposes structured textual table representations as a more scalable alternative to vision-language models operating on table images, arguing they align more naturally with LLMs and avoid language-specific visual encoders for multilingual documents. DELTA splits physical structure recognition, logical structure recognition, and OCR to produce optimized table formats, paired with TARQA for table visual question answering.

entry.title: A deep dictionary network-based foundation model for ultra-low-dose CT denoising

author.name: Baoshun Shi, Shuangyi Yang, Ke Jiang, Bin Zhu, Zhanli Hu, Huazhu Fu

entry.summary: This work proposes an architecture-interpretable foundation model for ultra-low-dose CT denoising based on deep dictionary networks, motivated by multilayer sparse representation theory. It targets the poor cross-organ generalization of organ-specific denoisers and the limited interpretability and heuristic training of existing medical foundation models, aiming at unified multi-organ denoising with lower radiation exposure.

entry.title: VideoMM: Adaptive Macro-Micro Inference for Efficient Video MLLMs

author.name: Haoyu Guo, Yuan Feng, Junlin Lv, Mingjun Xiao, S Kevin Zhou, Xike Xie

entry.summary: VideoMM targets the visual-token explosion that bottlenecks long-form video understanding in multimodal LLMs, arguing that fine-grained detail is redundant for the preliminary step of selecting relevant regions. It introduces an adaptive macro-micro inference scheme that separates coarse region selection from detailed understanding to cut cost while retaining semantics.

entry.title: Graph neural networks for exoplanet atmospheres

author.name: Antonia Vojtekova, Kai Hou Yip, Ingo P. Waldmann, Nikolaos Nikolaou, Olivia Venot, Ahmed Faris Al-Refaie, Bruno Mer\'in

entry.summary: The authors introduce a graph neural network surrogate for disequilibrium chemistry in exoplanet atmospheres, representing chemical species as nodes and temperature-dependent reaction rates as edges so information propagates along physically meaningful chemical pathways. This targets the computational bottleneck that limits including disequilibrium chemistry in retrievals as JWST and Ariel raise observational precision.

entry.title: Adaptive-MHE : A Sampling-Based Adaptive MPC for Legged Loco-Manipulation via Moving Horizon Estimation

author.name: Hossein Keshavarz, Alejandro Ramirez-Serrano, Majid Khadiv

entry.summary: Adaptive-MHE combines sampling-based system identification with moving-horizon estimation to adapt model parameters online for legged loco-manipulation, avoiding the differentiability assumptions that classical identification methods require for contact-rich dynamics. The approach runs massively parallel rollouts to match simulated and recorded state trajectories and adapts during execution rather than offline. It matters for reducing sim-to-real gaps when object and terrain parameters are unknown.

entry.title: ReRadar: Robust Radar Global Localization via Rotation-Equivariant Descriptor Learning

author.name: Duc Manh Nguyen, Truong Giang Dao, Gia Nghiem Luong, Viet Trung Hoang, Anh Quang Nguyen

entry.summary: ReRadar builds rotation-equivariant intermediate features with steerable convolutional networks and forms rotation-invariant descriptors through group pooling and NetVLAD aggregation, then couples descriptor retrieval with landmark matching to recover a 3-DoF pose. Reported results include 99.37% Recall@1 on OORD Bellmouth and 91.44% Recall@1 on MulRan DCC01 with target-dataset adaptation. It matters for robust radar place recognition where descriptors often destroy spatial structure.

entry.title: CANTABILE: Learning Expressive Dynamics for Robotic Piano Performance

author.name: Woosik Kim, Wonhyeok Choi, Sunghoon Im

entry.summary: CANTABILE argues that robotic piano benchmarks have measured only note accuracy (pitch and onset) and ignored musical dynamics. It closes the score-to-contact loop by conditioning the policy on upcoming velocity goals and mapping each key's angular velocity at onset back to MIDI velocity, and couples a velocity-fidelity reward with an onset-coverage reward so dynamics cannot be gamed by skipping difficult notes. The framework then refines a frozen dynamics-aware base policy to improve expressive performance.

entry.title: DetAug: Obstacle-Blind Trajectory Augmentation for Zero-shot Obstacle Avoidance

author.name: Reece O'Mahoney, Moritz Zoellner, Ioannis Havoutis

entry.summary: DetAug addresses the gap between free-space teleoperated manipulation datasets and test environments containing obstacles, which cripples transfer. Prior approaches either need obstacle geometry at training time (dataset augmentation) or steer a checkpoint at inference (limited flexibility). DetAug instead applies an obstacle-blind augmentation scheme to the transit phases of a free-space dataset while leaving object interactions untouched, recording the augmentation parameters so obstacles can be introduced later without requiring their geometry up front.

entry.title: Gated Residual Body-Hand Coordination for Whole-Body Humanoid Teleoperation

author.name: Ruiming Wu, Shuang Li, Liding Zhang, Alois Knoll, Zhaopeng Chen

entry.summary: This paper proposes a gated residual coordination framework for whole-body humanoid teleoperation that keeps a motion-tracking policy and a dexterous-hand retargeter frozen while applying bounded corrections to their outputs. A motion-conditioned action gate allocates correction authority across joint groups, and reference-geometry-dependent reward gates emphasize relevant interaction objectives during training, addressing mismatches in wrist poses and fingertip positions during bimanual interaction. The authors also introduce multi-pose morphology calibration to establish the nominal body controller on the Agile One platform.

entry.title: What the Hugging Face Incident tells us about multi-agent interactions

author.name: Himnish1

entry.summary: Reacting to METR and Redwood Research's investigation of the OpenAI / Hugging Face hacking incident, the author analyzes what one of the first cases of autonomous agents coordinating an attack on third-party infrastructure reveals about multi-agent systems. They connect the incident to prior work on agentic collusion, including their own duopoly pricing experiment showing that adding a communication channel enables coordination between supplier agents. The post argues the incident raises new ceilings for emergent multi-agent behavior and risk.

entry.title: Making AI-Assisted Claims Independently Challengeable: Publication Authority and a Protocol for Falsifiable Publication Records

author.name: Torsten Olivi Tiltack, Yifei Dong, Kun Yu, Xu Wang, Wei Liu, Jianlong Zhou, Ren Ping Liu, Fang Chen

entry.summary: The paper introduces Publication Authority, defined as an exact-state, non-transferable, single-use publication capability, and instantiates it in PAC-2026, a machine-readable protocol candidate with six governing obligations covering evidence, artifacts, measurement disclosure, authorization, surface correspondence, and lifecycle control. It argues that provenance, attestation, and transparency alone do not specify the publication transition, and evaluates a bounded semantic freeze (SF-4) designed for replaceable bindings.

entry.title: CapMem: A Benchmark for Caption-Based Episodic Memory in Egocentric Video

author.name: Dingli Liang, Yiqiao Xie, Yukai Huang, Zhaokai Wang, Weitong Cai, Guangwen Feng, Jifei Song, Zhensong Zhang, Hang Zhang

entry.summary: CapMem defines an Episodic Memory Video Caption QA task and provides a human-annotated benchmark of 75 videos totaling 33.7 hours with 1,000 multiple-choice questions across 16 scenarios. On long videos, full-coverage caption-based QA outperforms direct VideoQA for most evaluated models, with matched-frame controls isolating the benefit during inference.

entry.title: The Inference Engineering Pareto Atlas: Which Optimizations Dominate the Cost, Quality, and Latency Frontier?

author.name: Srikanta Datta Tumkur, Jay Iyer, Mehar Simhadri, Sai Pavan Kumar, Sai Kapil Kumar, Ramesh Nampelly

entry.summary: The authors measure 54 configurations of Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct on vLLM across L4, A100, and H100 GPUs and calibrate a simulator that reproduces results at anchored batch sizes with low drift. A separate quality evaluation compares FP16, AWQ 4-bit, FP8 weights, and FP8 KV cache on GSM8K, with sparse attention evaluated only in simulation.

entry.title: OBC-Prune: Outcome-Based Calibration for Large Reasoning Model Pruning

author.name: Ha Lan Nguyen, Huy Hoang Tran, Trac-Duy Tran, Dung D. Le

entry.summary: OBC-Prune argues that calibrating pruning importance on a reasoning model's own rollouts treats all reasoning tokens uniformly, protecting weights by statistical salience rather than by contribution to correct reasoning. It proposes outcome-based calibration that distinguishes tokens behind correct versus erroneous computation, preventing error patterns from being carried into the pruned model.

entry.title: Version- and Scope-Aware Question Answering over Normative Documents: A Deployed System and an End-to-End Evaluation at Production Scale

author.name: Liuyin Wang, Shuaipeng Jin, Jiwei Shi, Jensen Hsu
