entry.summary: This paper addresses question answering over normative documents where correctness depends on information beyond any single passage: whether the retrieved document version is currently in force, whether it applies to the relevant jurisdiction, subject, and date, and whether claims can be traced to source text. The authors evaluate the common default of uploading documents to a hosted retrieval service against roughly 73,000 candidate normative documents in a production deployment. Evaluation uses a stratified sample of 200 questions from a published benchmark.

entry.title: Rethinking Domain Specialization for Open-Ended Scientific Reasoning in Astronomy Language Models

author.name: Vanessa Lama, Sanjay Das, Emily Herron, Yuan-Sen Ting, Tijmen de Haan, Junqi Yin, Tirthankar Ghosal, Feiyi Wang

entry.summary: This study asks when domain-specific fine-tuning still adds value for open-ended scientific reasoning, using a curated astronomy QA benchmark drawn from 2017-2026 Olympiad-style materials with 300 free-response questions, 96 of them image-linked. It compares open-weight and API-served general-purpose, multimodal and astronomy-specialized models using judge-based correctness and complementary reference metrics, finding strong general-purpose models set the highest correctness baseline.

entry.title: REVERSAL-BENCH: A Reversibility Axis and Reset Oracle for Measuring the Reset-Free RL Cliff

author.name: Riyaaz Shaik, Chandru Venkataraman

entry.summary: REVERSAL-BENCH introduces a benchmark that controls environmental reversibility with a continuous parameter between zero and one and supplies a reset oracle for ground-truth verification of state recoverability across eight manipulation settings in five physics engines. It evaluates actor-critic, safe RL and specialized reset-free frameworks to quantify how performance degrades as reversibility disappears, which matters for real-world manipulation where actions cannot be undone.

entry.title: HINT-Plan: Human Intention-Aware Robot Task Planning in Context-Rich Environments using Vision Language Models

author.name: Yuchen Liu, Luigi Palmieri, Lujun Li, Radu State, Ilche Georgievski, Marco Aiello

entry.summary: The paper introduces HINT-Plan, which uses Vision Language Models to infer high-level human intentions from third-person images, converts those intentions into goal states, and solves joint human-robot task-planning problems. Hierarchical scene graphs represent the environment, extending human-awareness beyond simple collision avoidance into higher-level decision making.

entry.title: Information Set Emulation: Causal Certificates for AI Derived EHR Features

author.name: Takes Fujita (VRI), Nobutaka Hattori (Department of Neurology, Juntendo University School of Medicine)

entry.summary: The paper introduces information set emulation, attaching typed evidence such as source, timing, availability, representation version, and proposed causal roles to AI-extracted EHR features under a locked target trial. Causal certificates make those role assignments auditable, and features with unresolved roles are routed to compatible reporting or separate analyses.

entry.title: Learning Multi-Humanoid Pickup and Transport via Decentralized Object-Centric Control

author.name: Bikram Pandit, Mohitvishnu S. Gadde, Aayam Kumar Shrestha, Alan Fern

entry.summary: This paper studies cooperative multi-humanoid pickup and transport of objects with varying size, weight, and geometry using decentralized object-centric control. Each humanoid learns gripperless bimanual pinching of an assigned attachment region, providing a shared abstraction that spans single-robot pickup, multi-robot transport, and robot-to-robot handover without task-specific redesign.

entry.title: Newer Is Not Fairer: Gender Stereotyping in Text-to-Image AI Across Model Generations

author.name: Shesh Narayan Gupta, Nik Bear Brown

entry.summary: This study evaluates gender representation across 20 occupations, 5 prompt templates, and 4 Stable Diffusion generations, generating 8,000 images classified with DeepFace. It finds pervasive male over-representation overall and, strikingly, male subjects in a majority of images for historically female-coded occupations, with newer model generations not necessarily fairer.

entry.title: Physics-Informed Neural Networks for Fast Multilayer Spectral Inversion of H{\alpha} 6562.8 A and Ca II 8542.1 A Spectra

author.name: Ziyang Zhang, Qin Li, Vasyl B. Yurchyshyn, Kangwoo Yi, Haimin Wang, Wenda Cao, Bo Shen

entry.summary: This work applies physics-informed neural networks to accelerate multilayer spectral inversion of chromospheric absorption lines such as H-alpha and Ca II, replacing slow pixel-by-pixel nonlinear least-squares fitting. The network predicts inversion parameters directly from observed line profiles and passes them through a differentiable radiative-transfer formulation. It matters because it could make large imaging spectroscopy datasets from solar observatories tractable.

entry.title: PentestChain: A Cost-Aware, MCP-Orchestrated Framework for Automated Penetration Testing with Free-Tier LLMs

author.name: Rushabh Vipulkumar Patel, Dipo Dunsin, Mohammed Almaiah, Mohamed Chahine Ghanem

entry.summary: PentestChain is a ten-phase automated penetration-testing framework that pairs a deterministic exploit map with a cost-aware model cascade (local Ollama qwen2.5-7b, then free-tier OpenRouter and Cerebras, plus rule-based fallback). It exposes eleven tools via a Model Context Protocol server and treats US-dollar cost per engagement as a first-class evaluation metric. It aims to make continuous automated security testing affordable for smaller organizations.

entry.title: VoiceTrace: A Benchmark and Retrieval Framework for Who-Said-What Speech Retrieval

author.name: Aaron Yee, Fengjie Lu, Jiarui Hai, Chenang Jiang, Helin Wang, Siwei Tu, Weitao You, Lingyun Sun

entry.summary: VoiceTrace-Bench targets hybrid speech retrieval where a query combines text specifying what to retrieve with a reference speech utterance specifying who it should be attributed to, rather than a predefined speaker identity. Existing benchmarks focus on semantic content while overlooking speaker attribution, so the authors build a benchmark and a matching retrieval framework. It matters for meeting, lecture, podcast, and video search where users naturally want the words of a specific person.

entry.title: BadQubits: An LLM-Based Framework for Static Pre-Execution Detection of Structurally Harmful Quantum Circuits

author.name: Justin Woodring, Lamine Noureddine, Aisha Ali-Gombe

entry.summary: BadQubits applies LLM code understanding to statically detect structurally harmful OpenQASM 2.0 circuits before execution, targeting physical-execution-layer threats where dynamic inspection is constrained by measurement irreversibility and the exponential cost of state simulation. The authors evaluate four code-understanding LLM architectures on 1,500 circuits comprising 1,000 benign MQTBench programs and 500 synthetic attack circuits derived from three documented threat primitives. A fine-tuned Qwen Coder 2.5 7B reaches 92.67 percent classification accuracy and 96.1 percent harmful-circuit recall.

entry.title: WordPolo: Evaluating Language Models Through Iterative Semantic Feedback

author.name: Tyler McDonald, Ali Emami

entry.summary: WordPolo is a word-finding task in which a model must discover an unknown target word using only semantic similarity distance scores as feedback, starting from zero knowledge and iteratively narrowing a semantic search space. Because success requires interpreting scores and adapting search strategy, the design makes iterative reasoning directly observable rather than inferring it from dataset accuracy. The authors evaluate recent LLMs and large reasoning models including GPT-4.1, Llama 4, and Claude.

entry.title: Fathom: Per-Query Read Depth for Sparse Decoding over Offloaded KV Caches

author.name: Vivek Kalyanarangan

entry.summary: Fathom targets the memory-bound scan that ranks keys during top-k sparse attention decoding when agentic sessions reach a million tokens and the KV cache and index live in host memory. The 4-bit K cache is stored channel-major as bit planes, so the query can choose how many bits of each key channel to read, allocating its bit budget by reverse water-filling over variance-weighted channel importance. At one million tokens on Qwen3-8B, a decode step is reportedly 1.67x faster in GPU time than prior sparse-attention scans.

entry.title: DSD: Learning Diverse and Reusable Motor Skills via Diffusion Skill Discovery

author.name: Sun Woo Kim, Xue Bin Peng

entry.summary: DSD proposes a method for learning a diverse repertoire of reusable motor skills for simulated characters via diffusion-based skill discovery. It builds on the common approach of maximizing mutual information between skill latents and visited states, which combines marginal state entropy for behavioral coverage with conditional entropy for behavioral consistency, but directly estimating these terms is difficult. The goal is a skill library that supports many downstream tasks with both distinct behaviors and spatial and temporal variation within each.

entry.title: Learning Fractional-Order Dynamics from a Single Trajectory

author.name: Xiaole Zhang, Ziyi Zhang, Zehao Zhao, Stephen Tu, Guannan Qu, Yorie Nakahira, Paul Bogdan

entry.summary: The paper studies system identification for discrete-time fractional-order linear time-invariant systems from a single trajectory, capturing long-range dependence via the Grunwald-Letnikov difference operator. Because fractional-order systems couple estimation across the entire history, standard Markovian analysis does not apply; the authors propose Fractional-Order Ordinary-Least-Squares Grid-Search (FO-GS), a two-stage estimator exploiting diagonal structure. This matters for modeling non-Markovian physical, biological, and financial processes with memory.

entry.title: The evolution of sex for artificial intelligence: a population-genetic framework for multigenerational model populations

author.name: Giorgio F. Gilestro

entry.summary: This conceptual and empirical paper draws an analogy between multigenerational AI model development and biological population genetics, framing weight averaging and retraining on peer outputs as sexual versus asexual reproduction. The author formalizes this with an exact inheritance model and tests it on recurrent, feedforward, and VAE networks as well as large language models, finding the analogies broadly hold with architecture-specific biases. It matters because it offers a formal lens on model collapse and lineage dynamics as models are increasingly trained on synthesized data from other models.

entry.title: Decoding Extrahepatic Targeting of Lipid Nanoparticles with Interpretable Machine Learning

author.name: Asal Mehradfar, Mohammad Shahab Sepehri, Owen Antholine, Varun Shankar, Glen S. Kwon, Salman Avestimehr, Morteza Rasoulianboroujeni

entry.summary: The authors curate a dataset of 476 intravenous lipid nanoparticle formulations from 81 published studies, integrating composition, lipid chemical structure and IVIS biodistribution profiles, then train interpretable models to predict hepatic versus extrahepatic accumulation using standardized SMILES representations. The aim is to extract molecular design rules for delivering RNA therapeutics to tissues beyond the liver, a major limitation of current LNP platforms. It matters as a data-driven route to formulation design in a space usually explored by trial and error.

entry.title: Self-Supervised Learning for Robust Resonance Mass Regression in Cascade Decays

author.name: Ho Fung Tsoi, Alex Yang, Luis Felipe Gutierrez Zagazeta, Shion Chen, Dylan Rankin

entry.summary: This collider physics paper applies a foundation-model-style approach, pretraining a transformer encoder with VICReg on unlabeled events to learn a representation invariant to systematic variations, then using it to reconstruct resonance masses from cascade decays with missing energy. The motivation is that supervised regressors generalize poorly under distribution shift and that exhaustively enumerating labeled variations is computationally prohibitive. Robust mass reconstruction directly affects sensitivity in new physics searches and the reliability of measured resonance widths.

entry.title: Similarity Pairing with Energy Mover's Distance for Self-Supervised Pre-Training at the LHC

author.name: Ho Fung Tsoi, Dylan Rankin

entry.summary: This paper replaces hand-designed data augmentations with a data-driven pairing strategy for self-supervised pretraining at the Large Hadron Collider, using the energy mover's distance to measure how physically similar two collision events are in terms of their energy flow. The motivation is that augmentation choices are arbitrary and fragile, and that modifying or simulating events either breaks physical fidelity or is computationally expensive. Pair-based objectives could therefore make collider foundation models more principled and cheaper to train.

entry.title: Can VLMs Reliably Assess Sidewalk Accessibility Attributes from Pedestrian-Level Imagery?

author.name: Seung Jae Lieu, Diego Morra, Chiara Cadoni, Wonseop Song, Martina Mazzarello, Carlo Ratti

entry.summary: The authors test whether four vision-language models can judge sidewalk accessibility attributes such as effective width, longitudinal and cross slope, and pavement condition from street-level photos, using 514 images from Seoul with field-measured ground truth. They apply sampling-based conformal prediction, reportedly the first such use for VLM accessibility assessment, and find nominal 90 percent coverage is achievable but that the calibrated intervals vary widely in usefulness across attributes. The work matters as an early empirical check on whether VLM-based urban accessibility auditing can be trusted with quantified uncertainty.

entry.title: Exact semantic readout from compressed vector representations

author.name: Daniel Quigley

entry.summary: Quigley characterizes when compressed vector representations admit exact linear or affine readouts of a finite lexicon's truth conditions, giving a necessary and sufficient row-space condition and a minimum dimension equal to the rank of the augmented truth matrix. Exact readouts live in a shared truth basis where Boolean connectives act unchanged, while mere separability needs an added threshold, and bilinear readout of identity or strict total order requires linearly independent entity vectors. Experiments with GloVe and word2vec distinguish cases of exact affine recovery from approximate ones.

entry.title: Characterizing Replay Retention Under Dynamics Shift in Model-Based Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Everest Yang, Skye Thompson, George D. Konidaris

entry.summary: Yang, Thompson, and Konidaris study when recent transitions should be preferred to the full replay history in continual model-based reinforcement learning under changes in robot dynamics. They identify two characterizing quantities, the magnitude of the change and an age-staleness area-under-the-curve measure of how well transition age separates stale from fresh data. The analysis shows that forgetting stale data helps after large permanent shifts but hurts when dynamics recur and older experience becomes useful again.

entry.title: RecMorph: Topology-Guided Spatial Recurrence for Generalized Morphology Control

author.name: Quanrui Rao, Yong Liu, Xueming Xiao, Yingbo Luo, Kun Wu, Zhenyu Xu, Meibao Yao

entry.summary: RecMorph is a control architecture for robots with differing body morphologies that converts the kinematic tree into a depth-first traversal sequence, then uses shared bidirectional recurrent transitions for cross-limb communication and representation transformation. The design aims to keep a single policy efficient as body size grows, with residual preservation and normalization for stability. It matters for transferable whole-body control across heterogeneous robot designs.

entry.title: LSR-Net: Learning the Forward Evolution Operator for Nonlinear Fluid Dynamics

author.name: Qian Hou, Sutrisno, Yuqing Li, Zecheng Gan

entry.summary: LSR-Net is a neural operator architecture that learns system evolution solely from pairs of initial and future state snapshots, splitting the learnable integral kernel into long-range and short-range components in stacked blocks. The long-range part uses a sum-of-exponentials representation enabling global interactions as a trainable Fourier multiplier with near-linear complexity. It targets data-driven forward modeling of nonlinear fluid dynamics.

entry.title: Too Good to Be Real? Diagnosing and Reducing the Gap Between AI Preference and Real User Engagement

author.name: Xinglang Zhang, Yuanmeng Xiang, Yunyao Zhang, Zeliang Chen, Junqing Yu, Zikai Song

entry.summary: Using 1.17 million answers to 25,978 questions from Zhihu, Quora, and Reddit, the authors compare real and AI-generated answers across four within-question engagement levels. Their Ontological Preference Measurement represents answers along logic, affect, and expression, revealing a systematic gap: as target engagement rises, LLMs add explicit logical structure, while real engagement correlates more with affective features. The work matters for LLM-as-judge validity and for content generation aimed at real audiences.

entry.title: Align, Integrate, and Fire: Efficient Token-Level Alignment for Zero-Shot SpeechLLMs

author.name: Abderrahmane Issam, Yusuf Can Semerci, Jan Scholtes, Gerasimos Spanakis

entry.summary: This paper introduces Aligned Continuous Integrate-and-Fire, a framework for zero-shot speech processing that compresses continuous acoustic frames to exactly match the target text token length using dynamic time warping alignments. The approach avoids expensive full-model fine-tuning and inefficient projector token lengths, establishing strong acoustic alignment in an initial training stage.

entry.title: DyMT-ESB: Dynamic Multi-Turn Evaluation of Social Bias in User-LLM Interactions

author.name: Rem Hida, Masahiro Kaneko, Daisuke Oba, Danushka Bollegala, Naoaki Okazaki

entry.summary: This paper studies social bias dynamics in response-conditioned multi-turn interactions, using a controlled protocol that generates follow-up user queries from evolving dialogue history and allows variable dialogue lengths. It addresses the limitation of template-based, fixed-length multi-turn bias evaluations that do not adapt to model responses.

entry.title: ReFigBench: Benchmarking Scientific Figure Reconstruction as Editable PowerPoint Artifacts

author.name: Liyang Fan, Chi Wei, Yitai Li, Xinping Bi, Guhong Chen, Chenghao Sun, Haoxiang Yang, Qingwen Li, Kai Yan, Hong Li, Bo Li

entry.summary: ReFigBench evaluates multimodal coding agents on reconstructing scientific overview figures as editable PowerPoint slides that preserve text, topology, layout, and native document structure. Built on 1,000 real overview figures from arXiv papers, it aims to disentangle whether failures stem from perception, planning, or the agent harness.

entry.title: LangSelect: Cost-Aware Target-Language Routing for LLM Code Generation

author.name: Son Ha Xuan, Phat T. Tran-Truong, Xuan-Bach Le, Nghia Duong-Trung

entry.summary: The paper argues that when a programming task can be solved in several languages checked by the same tests, the pre-decoding choice of target language is a measurable cost lever because verified solutions differ in generated-token length. It introduces LangSelect, a verification-aware router that picks a language before generation and falls back if the first attempt fails, evaluated on verified-solution replay and live GPT-5 generation.

entry.title: Playing log(N)-Questions over Wikipedia Abstracts: Communication Efficiency Between Paired Frontier Models

author.name: Peter Potash

entry.summary: This study evaluates six frontier language models on a two-agent log(N)-Questions game where a questioner must identify a hidden Wikipedia paragraph using exactly log2(N) yes/no questions and an answerer replies with one word, both running on the same provider. Across 408 games costing $363, the leading five models (including GLM-5.3, GPT-5.6 Sol, Grok 4.6, Gemini 3.8 Flash, and Kimi K3) were only marginally separable, while Claude Opus 5 finished well behind.

entry.title: Decentralized Gossip Learning and Federated Averaging for Histopathology Image Classification

author.name: Yusuf Ozturk, Enes Goltekin, Bengisu Atli, Akin Ozturk, Ulas Bagci

entry.summary: This study compares server-based Federated Averaging, fully decentralized gossip learning, and a hybrid scheme for classifying invasive ductal carcinoma patches across six simulated institutions. Using 277,524 patches and patient-disjoint splits, it evaluates ring, random degree-3, and fully connected gossip topologies with sensitivity analyses on heterogeneity, mixing and learning rate. It matters for privacy-preserving medical AI where pooling data across hospitals is restricted.

entry.title: VPRef: A Cross-Domain Benchmark for Referring Remote Sensing Image Segmentation

author.name: Quanwei Liu, Tao Huang, Jiaqi Yang, Wei Xiang

entry.summary: VPRef is presented as the first cross-domain benchmark for Referring Remote Sensing Image Segmentation, with 46,972 language-image-annotation triplets organized in a three-tier linguistic hierarchy. The authors frame deployment failures as a dual-drift problem combining visual domain drift from resolution and spectral mismatch with textual logic drift from variable user-input granularity, and build a tailored parameter-efficient method on top. It matters for robust Earth observation applications.

entry.title: SAVTrack: Selective Vote Aggregation for Reliability-Aware Point Cloud Tracking

author.name: Sifan Zhou, Linyue Tan, Qiwei Wang, Ziyu Zhao, Xiaobo Lu

entry.summary: SAVTrack targets 3D single object tracking in LiDAR point clouds, where sparse and incomplete observations make some point-to-center votes far less reliable than others. The framework explicitly estimates per-vote reliability and selectively aggregates hypotheses so that inaccurate votes do not contaminate proposal clustering. It matters because vote reliability is typically ignored in point-based trackers, which limits localization accuracy in autonomous perception settings.

entry.title: Efficient Quantization-Aware Distillation with Cross-Modal Alignment for Edge Vision-Language Models

author.name: Jinwoo Jeon, GyuYeop Do, Yubin Lim, Nam-Joon Kim, Hyun Gon Ryu, Hyuk-Jae Lee, Byung-Jun Lee

entry.summary: The paper reworks two-stage quantization-aware distillation of CLIP into lightweight multi-modal encoders, where the original approach used different objectives for distillation and quantization and performed contrastive learning inside the quantized student space. It unifies the optimization and addresses modality imbalance caused by applying identical supervision to RGB and non-RGB inputs. This matters for running open-vocabulary classification on resource-constrained edge hardware.

entry.title: Hyper-RED: Scalable Event Pre-training via Semantic Hypergraph Distillation

author.name: Meisen Wang, Zhiqiang Tian, Wei Bao, Chengjie Wang, Shaoyi Du, Siqi Li

entry.summary: Hyper-RED transfers high-order semantic structure from pretrained image models to event camera representations using hypergraphs, rather than rigid pixel-wise or token-wise alignment that ignores modality differences in texture, density, and appearance. It aims to avoid semantic collapse and improve transferability when scaling event representation learning. The work matters because large-scale annotated event data remains scarce.

entry.title: NeuroTS-Net: Multi-Class Semantic Segmentation of Pediatric Brain Tumors in Multi-Modal MRI

author.name: Darius Peteleaza, Razvan-Gabriel Dumitru, Bogdan Neamtu, Arpad Gellert, Mariana Sandu, Claudiu Matei

entry.summary: Introduces NeuroTS-Net, a three-dimensional encoder-decoder CNN for multi-class semantic segmentation of pediatric brain tumors on multi-modal MRI. It combines a dual-scale raw-detail stream, adaptive low-resolution context selection, and detail-preserving multipath downsampling to retain fine intensity and boundary cues while modeling broader tumor context. This matters because pediatric tumors are rare, small, and low-contrast, making manual delineation difficult and automated support clinically valuable.

entry.title: Event-based Selective Attention for Multi-resolution Fast Region of Interest (ROI) Detection

author.name: Luca Peres, Giulia D'Angelo, Chiara Bartolozzi, Oliver Rhodes

entry.summary: Investigates a training-free, saliency-based, bottom-up attention model that operates directly on low-resolution event-camera input to select regions of interest. The method is evaluated across downscaling factors up to 256x reduction in input resolution on the Prophesee Automotive dataset, showing robust ROI selection. It matters for bandwidth-, memory-, and energy-constrained edge neuromorphic vision.

entry.title: InfoTaxa: Information-Calibrated Label-Free Clustering for Fine-Grained Visual Taxonomy

author.name: David Ahmedt-Aristizabal, Mohammad Ali Armin, Lars Petersson

entry.summary: This paper studies why label-free clustering of frozen visual embeddings recovers broad taxonomic groups but stalls at species level, using BIOSCAN-5M and BioCLIP 2 features with UMAP and HDBSCAN. The authors introduce InfoTaxa, an information-calibrated method that tests whether the residual plateau is a limitation of the clustering method or of the available image information, with implications for scalable biodiversity monitoring.

entry.title: SSC-Priors: Exploring Semantic and Visibility Priors to Boost Lidar Semantic Scene Completion

author.name: Tetiana Martyniuk, Jonathan Seele, Alexandre Boulch, Gilles Puy, Renaud Marlet, Raoul de Charette

entry.summary: SSC-Priors argues that recent lidar semantic scene completion work has over-invested in heavier architectures and instead shows that injecting two inexpensive priors, semantic pseudo-labels and sensor visibility information, as extra network inputs improves existing models with minimal architectural change. The authors, from an automotive research context, present it as a simple, possibly noisy, but effective boost to current SSC networks.

entry.title: DRT&R: Direct Radar Teach & Repeat

author.name: Alexander Krawciw, Daniil Lisus, Cedric Le Gentil, Timothy D. Barfoot

entry.summary: DRT&R brings direct, whole-scan radar methods to off-road closed-loop navigation, addressing problems such as degraded viewpoint-dependent radar features and the lack of global localization in field settings. The framework uses teach-and-repeat style mapping and localization with direct radar scans rather than sparse extracted points. It matters because radar keeps working in dust, fog, smoke and precipitation where lidar often fails.

entry.title: Geometric Shortcuts for Complex Trunk Postures: Dual-Helicity Coupling Enables Low-Dimensional Control

author.name: Huishi Huang, Danlu Chen, Matteo Lo Preti, Jun Liu, Marcelo H. Ang Jr., Cecilia Laschi

entry.summary: The authors hypothesize that elephant trunks achieve complex postures partly through a low-dimensional geometric shortcut: dual-helicity coupling between oppositely handed oblique muscles. Using a simplified soft-robotic prototype, they show that varying only two geometric parameters yields a broad library of elephant-like postures, suggesting a dual-layer control architecture. It matters for both continuum robot design and biological motor-control hypotheses.

entry.title: WAVE-Go: World-Model Navigation with Adaptive Execution for Wheel-Legged Robots

author.name: Mingyi Li, Ji Li, Zhihao Ouyang, Yage He, B\"orje F. Karlsson

entry.summary: WAVE-Go is an image-goal navigation framework for wheel-legged robots that separates world-action prediction from interruptible command execution, so predicted action sequences can be partially executed and cancelled when new observations invalidate them. A conditional-risk formulation governs how much of an action prefix to commit under an estimated cumulative failure budget, and posture/locomotion-mode transitions require clearance, stability, and task-evidence checks. Reported navigation evaluation shows 74.x percent success (number truncated).

entry.title: QMSR: Query-Conditioned Mask-wise Expert Routing for Robust Open-Vocabulary Underwater Object Retrieval

author.name: Fuming Zhang, Dongyue Huang, Junjie Wen, Lihua Xie

entry.summary: QMSR is a query-conditioned, mask-wise expert routing framework for open-vocabulary object retrieval in complex underwater environments. It selects a pretrained underwater image enhancement expert per query-candidate pair and predicts a continuous fusion strength between raw and enhanced representations, rather than applying uniform enhancement, which the authors note can be worse than raw imagery for retrieval. Training uses a privileged ranking oracle to guide expert selection.

entry.title: SOL-SLAM: Inverse Compositional Gauss-Newton Direct Registration for Fast Sonar-Only Local SLAM

author.name: Kalvik Jakkala, Jason O'Kane

entry.summary: SOL-SLAM introduces a dense direct registration approach for forward-looking-sonar-only local SLAM, aligning sonar returns efficiently using an inverse compositional Gauss-Newton formulation. It targets local consistency for reactive behaviors like coarse navigation and obstacle avoidance rather than expensive global accuracy, a capability the authors note is largely unaddressed. The approach contrasts with acoustic SLAM frameworks that rely on sparse feature extraction and discard much of the already information-sparse sonar returns.

entry.title: Investigating Adversarial Robustness of Heterogeneous Cooperative Perception

author.name: Chenyi Wang, Yutong Liu, Qingzhao Zhang, Ming F. Li

entry.summary: The paper tests the widespread assumption that heterogeneity in cooperative perception (connected vehicles with different sensors and translation modules) naturally defends against feature-map poisoning attacks. Using crafted adversarial features, the authors show that this protection is largely illusory because translation modules and unknown victim detectors do not actually scramble adversarial gradients enough. It matters because cooperative perception is a core safety mechanism for autonomous driving and this exposes a real attack surface.

entry.title: Thought anchors don't transfer between models

author.name: therootof3

entry.summary: This MATS project extends the Thought Anchors line of work by testing whether resampling-based importance of Chain-of-Thought sentences transfers across models. It finds that sentences important in one model's CoT are unremarkable when another reasoning model reads the same trace, so importance is model-specific rather than a property of the text; by contrast, a hidden nudge embedded in a CoT does transfer when teacher-forced into another model, but only if the trace already discusses the answer options. This has implications for CoT monitoring and cross-model oversight.

entry.title: J-space auditing might be unreliable

author.name: Kartikay Luthra

entry.summary: A negative empirical result testing whether decoded J-space, or global workspace, representations from a model are informative about reward-hacking behavior. The readouts stayed largely similar across checkpoints and monitoring conditions despite real behavioral differences, and supplying J-space to an LLM auditor added little discriminating power, though the author cautions the findings span only one model family and one behavioral setting.

entry.title: BENCHCOMPASS: From Scores to Signals for Training and Harness Decisions in Payment-Domain LLMs

author.name: Sijie Dong, Wei Ren, Xuanwei Hu, Jiawei Luo, Zifan Wang, Xiaoyun Feng, Hui Cai, Lyuxin Xue, Peng Lu, Jianshe Li, Xin Zhang, Wei Wu

entry.summary: The paper argues that the value of LLMs in payment operations is unclear because rules change quickly, evidence is fragmented, and correct behavior depends on transaction state, participant role, region, and payment rail. BENCHCOMPASS is a payment-domain benchmark whose pipeline builds scenario-grounded tasks from typed evidence packs, applies LLM-based quality checks, creates task-input attack variants, and reserves final item admission to domain experts. It matters because it aims to diagnose whether failures come from missing domain knowledge, poor use of supplied evidence, or brittleness in the surrounding harness, rather than producing a single opaque score.

entry.title: CALOS: Control-Affine Lyapunov On-manifold Safety Layer for Safe Deep Reinforcement Learning for Quadrotors

author.name: Fabrizio Cesareo, Sebastiano Mengozzi, Nicola Mimmo, Andrea Acquaviva

entry.summary: CALOS is a runtime safety layer for quadrotor control that enforces attitude constraints without altering the underlying RL algorithm. It formulates four tilt-angle inequalities plus a Lyapunov descent condition as a single quadratic program solved exactly by active-set enumeration over the three-dimensional torque space, yielding a minimum-norm correction to the policy's nominal torque at a cost low enough for real-time enforcement.

entry.title: GenStream: Semantic Streaming Framework for Generative Reconstruction of Human-centric Media

author.name: Emanuele Artioli, Daniele Lorenzi, Shivi Vats, Farzad Tashtarian, Christian Timmerer

entry.summary: GenStream replaces dense video frames in human-centric content with compact structured metadata, encoding each scene as skeletal keypoints, camera viewpoint parameters, and related semantic descriptors, then reconstructing the media generatively at the receiver. The argument is that conventional codecs waste bandwidth by re-encoding static backgrounds and salient actors with equal treatment. It matters for sports, performance, and interactive media where bandwidth efficiency and semantic structure align naturally.

entry.title: Beyond Embedding Transfer: Component Roles in Grokking Transfer and Stability

author.name: Zeyu Jia

entry.summary: This study dissects which model components drive gains from warm-start transfer on algorithmic tasks, separating early-learning speed from post-generalization stability. Using a scale-matched battery of 108 runs across 12 seed blocks on modular arithmetic, the author finds that transferring attention and MLP weights alongside token embeddings and readout improves early accuracy by 5.46 percentage points and cuts confirmation latency substantially. The result matters for understanding grokking dynamics and for practical warm-start training recipes.

entry.title: How Many Labels Does Model Choice Need? Certificates and Budgets for Selective Prediction

author.name: Tetsuji Kuboyama

entry.summary: This paper quantifies how many labeled examples are needed to determine which classifier performs best under selective prediction metrics such as AUGRC, when models may make identical predictions but different confidence rankings. It gives a prelabel lower bound, a covering linear program bounding certificate size, and asymptotic results for exact acquisition policies. It matters for efficient model evaluation and label-budget planning in selective prediction and abstention settings.

entry.title: Making Political Text Scaling Comparable: Infrastructure and Hyperparameter Sensitivity for 17 Algorithms

author.name: Patrick Parschan

entry.summary: This paper argues that computational text-based ideal point estimation methods are better understood as configurable measurement pipelines than as fixed algorithms, and builds shared infrastructure that makes seventeen heterogeneous scaling methods jointly executable. Across 5,537 experimental runs and roughly 4.25 million left-right position estimates, it quantifies how sensitive results are to hyperparameter choices using variance partitioning and SHAP-based sensitivity analysis. It matters for reproducibility and comparability in computational social science.

entry.title: English Word Sense Disambiguation in 2026: When the Labels Become the Bottleneck

author.name: Vassili Philippov, Amro Salman, Dmitrii Andreev, Penny Hands, Emil Kaiumov, Pavel Katunin, Anton Nikolaev

entry.summary: The authors argue that in all-words English word sense disambiguation the gold labels, not the models, now limit benchmark rankings. They release lexEN, a human-adjudicated correction layer over the ALL_NEW benchmark (211 labels changed, 56 removed), and SenseBench, an auditable evaluation harness and living leaderboard spanning 57 models and 192 runs. Because the task is inventory-constrained multiple choice, reported accuracies bound what models can achieve without inventory redefinition.

entry.title: RankGround: Efficient High-Resolution GUI Grounding via Lightweight Reranker-Guided Crop Selection

author.name: Liyang Fan, Xinping Bi, Yitai Li, Shuaimin Li, Hui Li, Min Yang

entry.summary: The paper tackles GUI grounding for multimodal agents, where full-image inference misses small or visually similar UI elements and multi-crop strategies require many expensive VLM calls. RankGround is a two-stage framework using GroundRanker, a lightweight multimodal reranker, to select the most promising crop so that only a single VLM call is needed per query.

entry.title: G3AR: Graph-Guided Neural Visual Geometry for Scalable Multi-Sequence Aerial Registration

author.name: Jeng Wen Joshua Lean, Ting-Yu Yen, Wei-Fang Sun, Simon See, Hung-Kuo Chu, Shih-Hsuan Hung

entry.summary: G3AR builds a geometrically verified image-proximity graph before local neural inference, using it to define bounded overlapping chunks and a chunk graph whose maximum spanning tree sets the alignment topology. Shared-image predictions then estimate Sim(3) transforms that register local cameras and geometry into a common frame, enabling dense neural geometry at aerial-collection scale. It matters for large-scale 3D reconstruction where full-context neural methods are impractical and naive chunking fails.

entry.title: Channel-Wise and Token-Aware Post-Training Quantization for Visual State Space Duality

author.name: Jonghyeon Lim, Changhoon Yim

entry.summary: The paper characterizes low-bit post-training quantization behavior of Visual State Space Duality models, finding activation quantization to be the dominant bottleneck and that inputs to certain linear layers show strong channel-wise magnitude variation with token-localized extremes. It proposes CTOAC, which learns per-input-channel clipping bounds by minimizing a token-balanced reconstruction loss. It matters for deploying Mamba-style vision backbones efficiently under low-bit constraints.

entry.title: Efficient 3D Whole-Body PET Image Denoising via Conditional Rectified Flow With Optimized Sampling Strategy

author.name: Jiale Shen, Guolin Wang, Chenhao Wang, Xinhui Su, Wei Luo, Feng Yu

entry.summary: This work proposes a one-pass conditional 3D rectified flow framework with an optimized non-uniform sampling schedule for denoising whole-body PET volumes. The goal is to preserve volumetric consistency while avoiding the long inference times of diffusion models and the inconsistency of fast 2D alternatives. It matters for lowering radiation dose in PET imaging without sacrificing diagnostic quality.

entry.title: 3D Field Data Reduction with Adaptive Sample-Based Gaussian-Encoded Reconstruction

author.name: Michael R. Martin, Joseph Insley, Victor A. Mateevitsi, Silvio Rizzi, Kwan-Liu Ma

entry.summary: This paper presents a unified sample-based Gaussian encoding that represents structured grids, unstructured meshes, and particle data under a single fixed-budget formulation, initializing and refining Gaussian primitives directly from input samples. It targets scientific visualization data reduction, preserving a prescribed primitive count and encoded size across heterogeneous field data formats that normally require separate pipelines.

entry.title: Visual Cue Guided Video Planning for Generalizable Robot Navigation

author.name: Hojin Lee, Sizhe Lester Li, Maximilian Hilger, Susie Lu, Achim J. Lilienthal, Vincent Sitzmann, Daniel A. Duecker

entry.summary: CueNav combines visual-cue-guided video planning with an embodiment-specific inverse-dynamics model for robot navigation, using a bird's-eye-view map for global context and partially retained robot-body pixels for embodiment context. The video planner predicts future observations while the IDM translates them into executable actions, addressing longer-horizon planning and video-to-action grounding.

entry.title: Feedback-Modulated Harmonic Policies for Quadruped Locomotion

author.name: Yixuan Jia, Steven Roche, Jonathan P. How

entry.summary: Instead of directly mapping observations to joint actions, this work represents each joint trajectory as a command-conditioned Fourier series whose coefficients and per-step feedback weights are generated by a context network, adjusting offsets, harmonic gains, frequency and phase online. Experiments in simulation compare this explicit periodic structure with an MLP policy's hidden activations. It matters as an inductive-bias approach that builds locomotion's cyclic structure into the policy representation.

entry.title: Prior Evolution and Task Alignment for Aerial Grasping

author.name: Weiliang Deng, Zhengyang Dang, Yao Mu, Ximin Lyu

entry.summary: Inspired by predatory birds, this work studies aerial grasping and attacks two limitations of trajectory-optimization formulations: severe nonconvexity and initialization sensitivity under limited computation, and human-designed numerical objectives that may not capture what actually determines task success. The authors investigate prior evolution and task alignment to improve the quality and fidelity of optimized grasping maneuvers. It matters for making dynamic aerial capture reliable outside carefully tuned settings.

entry.title: EvolveTrade: Experience-Driven Policy Refinement for Self-Evolving LLM Trading Agents

author.name: Sehee Kim, Yumin Choi, Minki Kang, Sung Ju Hwang

entry.summary: EvolveTrade treats the system prompt of a tool-using trading agent as a text-parameterized policy that a Policy Agent revises using accumulated decision traces and realized portfolio feedback, while keeping the backbone LLM frozen. This enables the agent to adapt how it gathers evidence, invokes tools, and manages risk as market regimes change.

entry.title: ERPBench: A State-Grounded Evaluation Paradigm for Computer-Use Agents in Enterprise Software

author.name: Kratika Bhagtani, Kusha Sridhar, Maziyar Baran Pouyan, Yuying Zhao, Eugene Siow

entry.summary: ERPBench evaluates screenshot-only computer-use agents on a live, reproducible ERP system and scores tasks against ground-truth business state rather than UI appearance alone. It targets enterprise challenges such as dense interfaces, coordinated multi-step interactions, and errors that mutate persistent business records.

entry.title: AeroWeaver: An Embodied-Agent Harness for Weaving Aerial Skills into Distributed, Adaptive Swarm Execution

author.name: Jiabin Lou, Yirong Yang, Haopeng Wang, Xuxin Lv, Xinyu Liu, Diyuan Hou, Xuehong Liu, Rongye Shi, Wenjun Wu

entry.summary: AeroWeaver is an embodied-agent harness that uses LLM agents as a semantic interface between natural-language mission descriptions and distributed UAV swarm behaviour. It tackles grounding model decisions in executable capabilities, reconciling global task reasoning with distributed local execution, and adapting to changing conditions. The aim is to turn high-level language plans into skills that individual vehicles can execute while coordinating collectively.

entry.title: Clueing up LLMs with Tool-Augmented Deductive Reasoning

author.name: Rebecca Ansell, Autumn Toney-Wails

entry.summary: The authors implement a text-based, multi-agent version of the classic board game Clue as an environment for evaluating multi-step, agentic deductive reasoning. Agents must infer hidden information from sequences of observations, maintain consistency across turns, and reason over an evolving belief state. The environment is designed to expose limitations in deductive consistency and to test tool-augmented reasoning enhancements.

entry.title: MUSE: Benchmarking Large Vision-Language Models on Multi-Modal Understanding in Situated Education

author.name: Luyao Zhu, Xun Wei Yee, Wei Li, Mun Thye Mak, Wee Siong Ng

entry.summary: MUSE is a new benchmark evaluating large vision-language models on artistic imagery within situated educational applications such as AI-assisted language learning. It decouples image annotation from question generation to better probe semantic, affective and cultural understanding of visual context, filling a gap left by benchmarks focused on real-world photos or narrow educational reasoning.

entry.title: When AI Generates Covariates: Causal Typing and Estimand Drift in Sequential Experiments

author.name: Takes Fujita (VRI), Nobutaka Hattori (Department of Neurology, Juntendo University School of Medicine)

entry.summary: This work argues that AI-generated covariates in sequential experiments can silently change the causal question when their roles are left ambiguous. It proposes a causal type discipline combining a versioned representation map, a role classifier, a claim-status filter, and an estimand lock to preserve a target proximal effect under identification assumptions.

entry.title: Principled Koopman Representations with Kalman Inference for Efficient Time-Series Prediction

author.name: Ruiquan Li, Yuheng Bu

entry.summary: The paper critiques neural methods that learn latent Koopman spaces without mathematical consistency, and introduces K-squared SVD, which explicitly learns leading singular functions of the Koopman operator via a Hilbert-Schmidt objective. This yields a valid low-rank, interpretable linear approximation paired with Kalman-based inference for efficient forecasting.

entry.title: Does AI Assistance Leave a Temporal Fingerprint? Detecting Overreliance in AI-Assisted Writing and Programming

author.name: Eduardo Davalos, Yike Zhang

entry.summary: The authors ask whether AI assistance leaves a detectable temporal signature in process data, and whether it generalizes from writing to programming. They analyze keystroke-level co-writing corpora, programmer editor telemetry, and a pre-LLM human-only baseline to distinguish minimal-AI work, collaborative AI use, and wholesale delegation.

entry.title: Mask 2D-3D: Adaptive Dual-Masked Autoencoder Network for Image-to-Point Cloud Registration

author.name: Zhixin Cheng, Jiacheng Deng, Xiaotian Yin, Baoqun Yin, Richang Hong, Tianzhu Zhang

entry.summary: The paper proposes ID-MAE, an intermodal dual-masked autoencoder with a similarity-based reinforcement-learning masking strategy for detection-free image-to-point-cloud registration. It targets erroneous correspondences caused by modality gaps, weak feature sensitivity, and non-overlapping regions, arguing random masking in standard MAE misses key regions. It offers a self-supervised route to better cross-modal 3D registration.

entry.title: Knowledge-Graph Based Augmentation versus Retrieval Augmented Generation for Cultural-Related Question Answering

author.name: Pablo Poulenard, Yannis Karmim, Valentin Barri\`ere

entry.summary: The paper benchmarks Graph-RAG against standard RAG on LatamQA, a culturally grounded multiple-choice dataset spanning eight thematic categories, with graphs built end-to-end from Wikipedia using the KGGen extractor. It targets the long-tail deficit where culturally specific facts about regions such as Latin America are too rare in pretraining to be memorized. Results bear on whether structured grounding beats text retrieval for cultural knowledge.

entry.title: Interpretable Patch-Based Deep Learning for Wildfire Spread Prediction from Ensemble Simulations

author.name: Marcin Lawenda, Aleksandra Krasicka, David Caballero, Luis Torres, {\L}ukasz Szustak

entry.summary: This study trains deep learning surrogates on 10,584 wildfire spread simulations at two-meter resolution for the Rectoret region of Catalonia, comparing a patch-based U-Net, a transfer-learned ResNet-50, a physics-informed network constrained by the wind-driven advection equation, and a Swin-Unet transformer. Among terrain and vegetation variables, only surface fuel load predicts burn probability with meaningful strength, and including it lowers prediction error by 21 percent. It matters because surrogate models could replace costly physics-based ensemble simulators while remaining interpretable for emergency planning.

entry.title: Structural Inference under Hidden Agents

author.name: Zhongben Gong, Xiaoqun Wu, Mingyang Zhou, Hui Huang

entry.summary: This work formulates structural inference when some agents in a multi-agent dynamical system are unobserved due to sensing limits, occlusion, or communication failure. Unlike prior work on unseen-node estimation or imputation, it jointly recovers hidden-agent trajectories and the interaction structure among all agents. The problem is relevant to modeling interacting systems such as swarms, traffic, and epidemiological or social dynamics where full observability is unrealistic.

entry.title: Transformation Laws in Neural Representations: Structure, Realisability, and Construction

author.name: Yuan Sun

entry.summary: This work formalizes when a transformation defined on inputs can be realized as a compatible action on internal neural features, linking representation analysis to internal intervention. In a linear setting the authors show the obstruction is governed by how much information the transformation requires that the encoder has discarded, measured in the metric induced by the representation. On a rectified network they separate two distinguishable sources of failure, connecting abstract representation theory to concrete architectural constraints.

entry.title: Accurate Trace Estimation with Fewer Random Bits via Recursive TensorSketch

author.name: Mohammad Azhar Khan, Rameshwar Pratap, Amit Sharma

entry.summary: This paper tackles estimating the trace of very large implicit matrices accessible only through matrix-vector products, as in the classical Hutchinson estimator. The authors propose a recursive TensorSketch approach that achieves accurate trace estimates while consuming substantially fewer random bits, which matters because randomness generation and storage can be a practical bottleneck in large-scale sketching and kernel methods.

entry.title: R\'enyi Tracking Bounds for Langevin Dynamics with Moving Targets

author.name: Yuchen Xin, Jingxin Zhan, Zhihua Zhang

entry.summary: This paper studies Langevin diffusion and Langevin Monte Carlo when the target distribution itself changes over time, deriving non-asymptotic Renyi-divergence guarantees under a log-Sobolev inequality for tracking the current target. The framework covers continuous-time dynamics and discretizations and is applied to nonsmooth sampling via successive Moreau envelopes with explicit smoothing and step-size choices. The authors describe these as the first non-asymptotic Renyi-divergence tracking bounds for Langevin dynamics with discrete target updates.

entry.title: Fourier Analysis of Parametrized Interactive Quantum Classifiers

author.name: F\'abio Novaes, Fernando M. de Paula Neto, Jo\~ao V. M. Cardoso

entry.summary: This work derives a closed-form expression for the reduced quantum channel of a parametrized interactive quantum classifier with a single target qubit, a family of models inspired by open quantum systems. The analytic solution shows explicitly how Hamiltonian parameters control the constant, sine, and cosine components of the classifier output, giving an interpretable Fourier-style picture of the model. It matters as theory that explains why particular Hamiltonian parameterizations empirically classify better.

entry.title: Benchmarking Tabular Foundation Models as Surrogates in Expensive Evolutionary Optimization

author.name: Lu Han, Jin Wang, Yuchen Li, Haoran Gu, Shulei Liu, Ziyang Shi, Wenao Lu, Handing Wang

entry.summary: This study evaluates TabPFN, a tabular prior-data fitted network, as the surrogate model inside surrogate-assisted evolutionary algorithms for expensive optimization problems where most evaluations must be avoided. It combines extensive experiments across offline and online settings with theoretical analysis to probe when TabPFN actually helps. The contribution is a careful empirical and analytical assessment of whether tabular foundation models transfer usefully into the optimization loop.

entry.title: Learning from Distributed Eyes: Leveraging Collaborative Perception for Automated Model Adaptation

author.name: Yanan Ma, Yihang Tao, Zhengru Fang, Zihan Fang, Yiqin Deng, Xianhao Chen, Yuguang Fang

entry.summary: The paper proposes LDE, a framework that uses collaborative perception among connected vehicles as a source of high-quality pseudo-labels for unsupervised domain adaptation of perception models. It claims the approach is hyperparameter-insensitive and more reliable than ego-vehicle-only pseudo-labeling, while addressing the communication costs that naive implementations incur. It is relevant to autonomous driving robustness under domain shift.

entry.title: Stable Filters for Generative Modeling of Graph Signals

author.name: Martin Schmidt, Gonzalo Mateos

entry.summary: The authors analyze structural stability of graph-aware continuous-time generative models whose drift combines a graph filter with a learned graph neural network, deriving explicit Wasserstein stability bounds quantifying how relative graph perturbations affect generated distributions. Motivated by these bounds, they introduce a filter design intended to improve robustness. This matters for permutation-equivariant generative models on graphs where topology may be noisy or uncertain.

entry.title: How AI Assistants Respond to Repeated Abuse

author.name: William Guey, Wei Zhang, Pierrick Bougault, Yi Wang, Agoston Bodo, Vitor D de Moura, Jos\'e O Gomes

entry.summary: The authors build a bilingual, multi-turn framework distinguishing hard disengagement from soft withdrawal, then run 448 five-turn conversations across eight API configurations, producing 2,240 responses and 6,720 blinded model judgments. The design separates sustained abuse from constant frustration to see how repeated verbal abuse changes engagement on an otherwise benign task. It provides rare systematic evidence about a common but understudied interaction pattern.

entry.title: Emotion Experience, Expression, and Perception: Emotion Analysis on Multimodal Social Media Posts

author.name: Christopher Bagdon, Carina Silberer, Roman Klinger

entry.summary: The paper studies how well readers can reconstruct an author's emotional intent from multimodal social media posts, incorporating both images and the real-world events that triggered the emotion. It argues prior emotion analysis has neglected the image modality and the triggering-event context, and builds an analysis linking author experience to post content.

entry.title: M-SQE: Multilingual Skill Quality Estimation for Enhancing Language Equality in Agentic Skill Use

author.name: Yilun Liu, Shimin Tao, Minggui He, Chenxin Liu, Li Zhang, Chen Liu, Miao Zhang, Jiaxin Guo, Min Zhang, Liqun Deng, Xiaojun Meng, Daimeng Wei

entry.summary: The paper audits agent skill libraries and finds them heavily English-centric, with low-resource languages like Swahili and Hindi lacking in-language skills, causing cross-language retrieval failures. It proposes M-SQE, a multilingual skill quality estimation method to filter synthesized in-language skills so retrieval surfaces usable rather than merely related candidates.

entry.title: Selection Is Retrieval, Abstention Is Not: On-Device Tool Routing over 70 Korean-English Actions

author.name: Janghoon Lee (Redrob)

entry.summary: This paper analyzes on-device tool routing, distinguishing the decision of which tool to invoke from whether any tool applies. It argues that replacing a language model with a retriever is asymmetric across these decisions, since retrievers always return a top candidate and cannot signal that no catalog action is valid, and studies this over 70 Korean-English actions.

entry.title: Zero-Shot Cross-Lingual Recognition of Sign Language Handshapes

author.name: Marcel Granero-Moya, Carolina del Corral Farrar\'os, Gloria Haro, Coloma Ballester, Ricardo Marques

entry.summary: This paper presents the first zero-shot cross-lingual framework for sign language handshape recognition, transferring from American Sign Language to Catalan Sign Language. It decomposes handshapes into five shared phonological features and decodes LSC handshapes via a composite phonological distance metric, evaluating MLP, SL-GCN, and SHuBERT architectures trained on two ASL corpora.

entry.title: A Benchmark Suite and Ground-Truth Methodology for Formal Verification of IEC 61131-3 Ladder Diagram Programs

author.name: Pierre Dantas, Lucas Cordeiro, Waldir Junior

entry.summary: The authors present what they describe as the first benchmark suite for formal verification of PLC programs that pairs controlled ground truth with coverage of both Structured Text and graphical Ladder Diagram encodings. The suite has 50 programs in 83 variants across ten industrial domains, each paired with a formal property, machine-checkable expected verdict, and a violation witness.

entry.title: Encoder Awakening via Adapters: Effective Domain-Adaptive Fine-tuning of Speech-LLMs

author.name: Mohan Shi, Zilai Wang, Natarajan Balaji Shankar, Kaiyuan Zhang, Eray Eren, Abeer Alwan

entry.summary: The paper argues that in Speech-LLMs, where cross-entropy loss is applied only at the LLM output, the speech encoder receives insufficient adaptation to shifted acoustic conditions such as child or dialectal speech. It proposes Encoder Awakening via Adapters (EAVA), a domain-adaptive fine-tuning method that adds lightweight adaptation to the encoder under limited target-domain data.

entry.title: MDN-Control: Mask-Depth-Noise Guided Region Control for Multi-Subject Video Editing

author.name: Jiayi Yu, Xi Ye, Lina Wang, Yunkun Xia

entry.summary: MDN-Control is a training-free framework for multi-subject video editing that jointly controls target localization, occlusion geometry and appearance initialization. Mask-guided localization keeps targets consistent, depth-aware occlusion control resolves ambiguous boundaries between overlapping subjects, and noise latent prompting retrieves relevant Gaussian initializations from a noise library. It matters for reducing cross-subject attribute leakage in video editing.

entry.title: Bridging the Perceptual Gap: Residual-Enhanced Downscaling and Manifold-Aware Perception Alignment Adaptation for NR-IQA

author.name: Yu Li, Zhengran Shen, Yachun Mi, Puchao Zhou, Shaohui Liu

entry.summary: This work diagnoses a phenomenon it calls perceptual submergence, where CLIP-style contrastive pretraining suppresses subtle quality signals, and standard cropping and interpolation further destroy high-frequency cues. It proposes a manifold-aware cross-modal perception alignment adapter with a perception-sensitive feature extractor to disentangle distortions from dominant semantics. The contribution matters for no-reference image quality assessment, where foundation-model features are strong on semantics but weak on fine-grained distortion.

entry.title: PriorPose: Reference-Guided Joint Deformation and Alignment for Category-Level Object Pose Estimation

author.name: Yihan Chen, Huan Ren, Wenfei Yang, Hang Du, Tianzhu Zhang, Feng Wu

entry.summary: PriorPose estimates a similarity transform for unseen object instances without instance-specific CAD models, using a reference-guided correspondence framework. It avoids the serial deform-then-align pipeline whose underconstrained canonical completion can corrupt correspondences and cascade errors into pose. The work matters for category-level pose estimation robustness under distribution shift.

entry.title: HLC-GS: Risk-Map-Guided Height-Layer Consistency Gaussian Splatting for DSM Reconstruction from Optical Satellite Imagery

author.name: Jie Yang, Yingdong Pi, Qiyan Luo, Xiaoyu Wang, Lekang Wen, Mi Wang

entry.summary: HLC-GS addresses a specific artifact in 3D Gaussian Splatting based digital surface model generation, where alpha-weighted aggregation blends splats from different height layers at the same pixel and produces non-physical intermediate elevations. It introduces a risk-map-guided height-layer consistency mechanism to suppress that mixing. The work matters for the geospatial accuracy of satellite-derived elevation products.

entry.title: tcnerv:dual-domain temporal context modeling for implicit neural video compression

author.name: Xuezhi Xiang, Yixin Zhao, Heqi Xiang, Jiayao Liu, Shanjun Zhang

entry.summary: TCNeRV is an implicit neural representation for video compression that conditions decoding on reconstructed context in both feature and embedding domains, using multi-scale temporal context fusion and temporal embedding residual coding. The design injects gated historical features at multiple decoder scales and codes only the residual of each predicted content embedding. With roughly 3 million parameters it reports an average PSNR of 36.08 dB on UVG, outperforming HNeRV-style baselines.

entry.title: Exploring 2D backbone effects for indoor semantic occupancy prediction

author.name: Shizhang Fanga, Wanling Yea, Qi Zheng

entry.summary: This work isolates the image encoder in an RGB-D semantic occupancy pipeline, keeping the projection, depth branch, and occupancy head fixed while swapping CLIP-ResNet, CLIP-ViT, BLIP2, and DINOv2 backbones. It reports that the choice of 2D backbone changes occupancy mIoU more than several carefully designed occupancy-specific architectures.

entry.title: ORCA: Occlusion-Aware Refinement and Completion for Novel View Synthesis

author.name: Weronika Jakubowska, Maciej Zi\k{e}ba, Przemys{\l}aw Spurek

entry.summary: ORCA addresses single-image novel view synthesis by recognizing that many artifacts revealed when the camera moves are small gaps near depth boundaries rather than truly unknown content needing generative hallucination. It introduces 3D structure into a Gaussian-anchor representation using monocular depth while preserving camera-ray consistency, reconstructing and completing explorable 3D scenes without expensive image generation.

entry.title: The Neverwhere Visual Parkour Benchmark Suite

author.name: Ziyu Chen, Henghui Bao, Haoran Chang, Alan Yu, Ran Choi, Kai McClennen, Gio Huh, Kevin Yang, Ri-Zhao Qiu, Yajvan Ravan, John J. Leonard, Xiaolong Wang, Phillip Isola, Ge Yang, Yue Wang

entry.summary: Neverwhere is a suite of hyper-photorealistic, closed-loop evaluation environments built from over sixty 3D Gaussian Splatting reconstructions of urban indoor and outdoor scenes, targeting visual locomotion and parkour controllers. The authors aim to close the train/evaluation gap for robot deployment and warn about pitfalls of relying solely on 3DGS reconstructions.

entry.title: Neural noise enables accurate internal simulation of rare events

author.name: Heng Zhang, Pawel Herman, Zenas C. Chao

entry.summary: Using a Bayesian Confidence Propagation Neural Network trained on sequences from a Markov-chain random walk with controlled event frequencies, the authors examine how the brain could build accurate internal models of rare events despite limited sampling. They show neural noise plays a functional role in counteracting the under- or over-estimation of rare-event frequencies.

entry.title: Fetch My Beer: Synthetic-to-real Hierarchical Policy for Smooth Pick-and-place

author.name: Yingyue Li, Chenyangguang Zhang, Ruida Zhang, Bowen Fu, Guangyao Zhai, Xiangyang Ji

entry.summary: This paper studies stable transport of liquid-filled containers, where success requires suppressing sloshing throughout the trajectory rather than merely reaching the goal. It identifies obstacles in existing approaches, including costly fluid simulation for online RL, sloshing-inducing accelerations from teleoperation data, and policy limitations, and proposes a synthetic-to-real hierarchical policy for smooth pick-and-place. It matters for dynamically sensitive manipulation tasks common in service settings.

entry.title: LUMO: Designing Luminous Contact Morphology for Repeatable Whole-Finger Contact Observation

author.name: Dong Ho Kang, Youngsu Ko, Luis Sentis

entry.summary: LUMO addresses the ambiguity in low-impedance robot fingers where a single joint-torque reading cannot distinguish a small fingertip force from a large force near the joint, so contact location must be resolved. The design embeds LEDs in a compliant silicone pad whose deformation alters the light pattern emerging from the finger side, making contact location externally observable. The same structure carries the load, so its cross-section (pad profile, rigid carrier, lateral void) is jointly optimized for mechanical compliance and repeatable optical contact sensing.

entry.title: Body-Motion Control of a Simulated Aerial Swarm from a First-Person View

author.name: Yang Chen, Darius Giannoli, Dario Floreano

entry.summary: This paper presents an upper-body interface for first-person-view teleoperation of aerial swarms, mapping torso inclination, hand position, and head rotation to five continuous command dimensions with per-participant calibration of neutral postures and motion ranges. In a within-subject study, 14 participants navigated a simulated 15-agent swarm through 3D obstacle courses using both this interface and a conventional transmitter. Body-motion control reduced completion time by 19.4 percent and centroid path length by 7.0 percent, with much lower command variation and more frequent concurrent command changes.

entry.title: Loco-Loco-RL: Low-Cost Terrain Mapping for Humanoid Locomotion with Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Jordan Dowdy, Gryffin Reizian, Jean Chagas Vaz

entry.summary: The authors replace expensive depth cameras and LiDAR with a low-cost time-of-flight sensor to produce a compact 3D local terrain representation for humanoid locomotion policies. They introduce a token-compressed temporal transformer that tokenizes proprioceptive and terrain observations and uses self-attention to capture within-timestep relationships before compressing tokens. The work targets cheaper, lower-power terrain perception without losing the information needed for robust RL locomotion.

entry.title: Always ask your agent to be honest

author.name: jennyyhuang

entry.summary: This post introduces a set of reporting dilemmas drawn from realistic agent work, such as experiments with notable design flaws, incomplete execution traces, and hallucinated data, all framed as the model's own past work. It measures whether current models volunteer unflattering information when asked to report on that work and finds they often do not when it would undermine a successful-looking report. A short instruction to be honest in reporting substantially improves candor, giving a simple mitigation.

entry.title: Re2A: Situated Conversational Recommendation via Rubric-based Preference Reasoning and Alignment

author.name: Dongding Lin, Jian Wang, Xiaoyan Zhao, Wenjie Li

entry.summary: The paper targets situated conversational recommendation, where a recommender assistant must jointly reason over dialogue history, a co-observed physical scene, and in-scene item attributes, arguing that current methods struggle with understanding situated preferences and generating grounded responses. Re2A formulates the task as a structured reason-then-align process using rubric-based preference reasoning. It matters for grounding recommendation systems in shared physical environments rather than purely textual histories.

entry.title: Risk-Aware World Modeling with Flow-Guided Occupancy Evolution for Selective Trajectory Planning in Automated Driving

author.name: Rongxiang Zeng, Linsen Cai, Jiafu Zhang, Yijie Zhong, Yide Tao, Shuai Wang, Nan Zheng, Hai L. Vu, Alvaro Garcia Hernandez, Yongqi Dong

entry.summary: RiskWorld is a risk-aware world-modeling framework for automated driving that jointly forecasts occupancy and decides when to replace an existing planned trajectory. It fuses spatial risk fields and temporal actor context with bird's-eye-view features, uses flow-guided evolution with signed residual corrections to transport occupancy, and scores candidate trajectories against a persistence reference to produce a collision-score correction. The approach targets the problem of anticipating evolving traffic risk rather than replanning blindly at every step.

entry.title: Physics-based prediction, uncertainty quantification and decision-making for IN718 crystallographic texture intensity across LPBF defocus regimes

author.name: Yisheng Lu, John Riris, Jie Song, Yao Fu, Jie Chen

entry.summary: This paper develops a two-stage physics-based model for predicting crystallographic texture in laser powder bed fusion of Inconel 718, first mapping process variables to melt pool geometry and then combining an empirical physics model with a random-forest residual correction. A k-nearest-neighbor weight attenuates corrections for poorly supported queries, and a beam-power-density criterion withholds predictions outside the valid regime. It matters for additive manufacturing qualification, where distinguishing weak data support from loss of physical validity is essential.

entry.title: Stability-Constrained Approximation in Spline KANs: Exact Layer Balancing and Budget-Compatible Saturation

author.name: Aleksander Tankman

entry.summary: This paper studies approximation with deep spline superposition networks under a hard layerwise Lipschitz budget, organizing the analysis around a factorisation stability complexity and a budget-compatible approximation complexity for discretization operators. It gives an exact solution to the finite-depth diagonal balancing problem, showing the optimal uniform layer budget equals a specific infinity-norm product raised to the power one over the depth, attained by an explicit one-pass minimizer. The results clarify the trade-off between approximation order and stability across depth in spline KAN-style architectures.

entry.title: Benchmarking Large Language Models for Biomedical Relation Extraction

author.name: Claudiu Creanga, Teodor Marchitan, Liviu P. Dinu

entry.summary: The authors benchmark masked language models, hybrid architectures, and recent LLMs on the SNPPhenA corpus for SNP-phenotype association extraction across sentence-level, abstract-level, and association-strength classification. OpenAI O1 reached state-of-the-art few-shot results for sentence-level and abstract-level extraction, while association-strength classification remained difficult and was first evaluated with LLMs.

entry.title: PageRecall: Measuring Page Selection in Literature-Grounded Question Answering

author.name: Aaditya Chauhan

entry.summary: This system paper for the LitTraceQA challenge retrieves relevant papers from a pool of 27,487, cites the page and figure or table containing the answer, and responds in a requested format. A key finding is that evidence grounding is bottlenecked by retrieval rather than reading: the page selector surfaced the gold page only about 52.6% of the time, while the evidence locator cited the correct page in 45 of 48 cases when given it, and rarely flagged missing pages.

entry.title: Noise2Noise Revisited: Training Pair Distributions Dominate Loss Choice in Self-Supervised Denoising

author.name: Dingyan Shang, Zhenyu Xu, Youting Wang, Bonan Shen, Bowen Liu

entry.summary: This paper stress-tests two common explanations for why L1 beats L2 in Noise2Noise self-supervised denoising, showing that the sparsity hypothesis confuses the loss with Lasso regularization and that population optima of the two losses coincide for symmetric posteriors. It concludes that measured differences are dominated by optimization dynamics such as bounded-influence gradients and training pair distributions.

entry.title: Indicators of resilience for autonomous control systems

author.name: Jasper van Beers, Da-Hwi Kim, Prashant Solanki, Coen de Visser

entry.summary: The paper adapts generic resilience indicators based on critical slowing down, originally used to anticipate tipping points in natural systems, to autonomously detect subtle degradation of stability in nonlinear control systems. The authors show how to systematically design these indicators so that safety schemes do not become misaligned with a system that has drifted through partial faults or wear. This offers an early-warning signal for failures that ordinary fault prediction methods miss.

entry.title: Physics-Constrained Digital Twins for Sensor Integrity in Urban Pedestrian Flow: Detecting Stealthy False Data Injection with Conformal Guarantees

author.name: Oscar Mogollon Gutierrez, Fatemeh Ghasemi, Mohammadhossein Homaei, Andres Caro, Mar Avila

entry.summary: The work formalizes stealthy false data injection for city-scale pedestrian counting, where latent-to-observed flow mappings are far more rank deficient than in power or water networks. The digital twin estimates directed flows on a pedestrian street graph, assimilates counts through a learned graph-localized gain, and combines innovation with a flow-conservation residual for detection with conformal thresholds.

entry.title: What You Can't See Is Still What You Learn: A Preregistered Sixty-Society Confirmation That Evidence Masking Drives Compositional Generalization

author.name: Narcis Marincat

entry.summary: A preregistered study with sixty four-cell systems sharing a frozen language-model backbone tests whether restricting what modules can read improves compositional generalization. Across six initialization clusters and two data orders, masking improved held-out two- and three-operation composition accuracy with all twelve pairs clearing required margins, and an unmarked replication also passed the behavioral criterion.

entry.title: Collaborative Memory for Multi-Agent VLM Systems

author.name: Huixin Zhang, Shao-Jun Xia, Di Wang, Liangxi Liu, Hainan Xiong, Zihao Wang

entry.summary: The paper frames memory hierarchy, cross-agent sharing, and consistency mechanisms as central to multi-agent vision-language collaboration, where different agents inspect different image regions, frames, or visual representations. Effective collaboration requires agents to build on each other's contributions, recover missing visual context, and reconcile differing interpretations as new evidence emerges.

entry.title: Cultural Competence in Context: A Large Language Model Passes the Turing Test in Finland

author.name: Otto Segersven, Pentti Henttonen

entry.summary: The authors ran a Turing Test in Finnish with Finnish-speaking participants and a large language model, expecting degraded performance because Finnish and its cultural context are underrepresented in training data. Contrary to expectation, the model passed, with the main error source being participants who over-relied on colloquial Finnish as a marker of human authorship. The work also introduces model-generated role prompting as a replicable technique for comparative, culturally situated Turing Tests and reframes the test from an intelligence measure toward a test of cultural competence.

entry.title: Reasoning through Evolution: Automatic Meta-path Discovery for LLM-based Fake News Detection

author.name: Ziyi Zhou, Xiaoming Zhang, Hui Pang, Yuting Zhang, Tiesunlong Shen, Bingyu Yan, Erik Cambria, Litian Zhang

entry.summary: MAGER is a multi-agent genetic evolution framework that automatically discovers meta-paths which compress complex news propagation graphs into subgraphs suitable for LLM reasoning. It targets the modality mismatch and information overload that make zero-shot or few-shot LLM reasoning over raw propagation graphs unreliable, while reducing reliance on large labelled datasets needed by supervised GNN baselines. The evolved meta-paths are optimised specifically for downstream LLM reasoning.

entry.title: AI and Human Approaches to Mathematical Problem Solving

author.name: Yang Ding

entry.summary: This study compares public accounts of AI attacks on eleven long-standing math problems with 58 human papers addressing the same targets, constructing 31 within-problem comparisons. Six validated text-based measures capture resolution, method articulation, uncertainty, successor questions, generality, and cross-disciplinary integration, finding systematic differences in how AI and human research are framed.

entry.title: QiT: Quantum-Inspired Transformer for Visual Recognition Task

author.name: Badri N. Patro, Vijay Agneeswaran

entry.summary: QiT ports structural ideas from quantum machine learning, notably angle-encoded states and Hilbert-space periodic similarities, into scalable classical Transformer operations for vision. It introduces angle-inspired token encoding and related components to capture quantum-style representations without the hardware constraints of real quantum devices.

entry.title: Procedural Pretraining for Molecular Property Prediction

author.name: Moritz Friedemann, Zachary Shinnick, Philip Torr, Bruno Andreis

entry.summary: The authors ask whether abstract, procedurally generated data can instill useful inductive biases before a model sees any molecules. Their three-stage pipeline of procedural pretraining, SMILES molecular pretraining, and downstream fine-tuning shows gains on tasks such as lipophilicity, using procedural tasks spanning sequence structure, cellular automata, and graph reasoning.

entry.title: Learning Nuclear Structure with AI: Radii and Collectivity

author.name: Giuliano Giacalone, Sokratis Trifinopoulos, Mike Williams

entry.summary: The authors build held-out ensembles on top of NuCLR, a multi-task model of nuclear data, to study charge radii and electric-quadrupole transition strengths across the chart of nuclides. Out-of-fold validation shows shared representations outperform single-task learning, achieving small RMS deviations across hundreds of nuclei.

entry.title: APGEM: Adaptive Policy-Guided Error Mitigation for Quantum Reinforcement Learning on a Real-World CVRP Case Study

author.name: Shabir Ahmad Sofi, Bisma Majid, Mir Mohammad Yousuf

entry.summary: APGEM is a controller for quantum reinforcement learning policies represented as variational quantum circuits, selecting among ZNE, PEC, CDR, and readout error mitigation online using a fidelity-, entropy-, and cost-aware utility with epsilon-greedy exploration. It is evaluated on a real-world Capacitated Vehicle Routing Problem, where fixed error mitigation strategies are typically applied statically. It matters for making NISQ-era quantum RL practical.

entry.title: Multitask Reinforcement Learning for Assisting Choice Model Specification

author.name: Gabriel Nova, Stephane Hess, Sander Van Cranenburgh

entry.summary: Delphos frames discrete choice model specification as a sequential decision-making problem, using multitask reinforcement learning with a DeepSet-Q architecture to learn transferable specification strategies across transport choice datasets.
