The agent applies a sequence of modelling actions and receives feedback from an estimation environment based on model performance and convergence, with utility specifications represented as sets of terms so decisions transfer across datasets with different variables. It matters as a rare application of RL to econometric model building, a task usually done by hand over hours or days.

entry.title: A Scalable Framework for Automated NER Annotation Correction in Low-Resource Languages

author.name: Toqeer Ehsan, Thamar Solorio

entry.summary: This paper presents a multi-step framework for improving Named Entity Recognition dataset quality through automated annotation correction, using a frequency-based iterative self-training approach with a dual-threshold mechanism to control inference confidence. It also explores whether generative LLMs can perform NER for low-resource languages. It matters because noisy annotations remain a major bottleneck for state-of-the-art NER in languages with little labeled data.

entry.title: Dose-Aware Cold Diffusion with Physics Consistency for Generalizable Low-Dose CT Reconstruction

author.name: Md Imam Ahasan, Guangchao Yang, A F M Abdun Noor, S M Hasan Mahmud, Md Mahfuzur Rahman

entry.summary: The paper proposes Dose-Aware Cold Diffusion, a physics-consistent reconstruction framework that models radiation dose as a continuous latent factor inside a cold diffusion process. It combines dose-aware perception, multi-scale structural prior extraction, and dose-calibrated step allocation to handle continuous and previously unseen dose levels. The goal is to reduce artifacts and preserve anatomical detail where existing low-dose CT methods fail to generalize.

entry.title: TalkMatrix: Generating Character Dialogue that is Both Consistent and Diverse

author.name: Ayuto Tsutsumi, Yuu Jinnai

entry.summary: The paper formulates structured multi-prompt, multi-completion selection, where one completion must be chosen per prompt from a candidate pool so as to optimize a collection-level objective that is not decomposable per prompt. It instantiates this in character dialogue, requiring each character to stay consistent across situations, each line to fit its situation, and characters and situations to remain mutually distinguishable. TalkMatrix generates candidates for every character-situation pair and jointly selects a full matrix using four embedding-based criteria.

entry.title: Affora: A Design System for Agent-Friendly Interfaces

author.name: Jin Gao

entry.summary: This paper introduces Affora, a design system aimed at making user interfaces legible to both computer-use agents and human users. Through three controlled studies on component implementations, visual variation, and interaction-design principles, the authors derive guidance spanning individual components up to whole sites, complete with reusable implementations and executable checks. The key finding is that agent performance hinges on the interaction meaning exposed through the interface representation, and that substantial visual variation can be preserved as long as that meaning survives.

entry.title: Temperon: Full-Time SAM Quality at a Third Less Wall-Clock

author.name: Stamatis Mastromichalakis

entry.summary: Temperon is a training schedule that spends the first 43 percent of the epoch budget with plain SGD exploration and then hands off the entire final cosine anneal to a sharpness-aware minimization (SAM) version of Muon. On CIFAR-10/100, SVHN, and Tiny ImageNet across five seeds, it matches the best full-time SAM recipe in accuracy while reaching the hardest common target roughly 32 to 35 percent sooner on most benchmarks. The result suggests where expensive sharpness-aware training should be concentrated.

entry.title: SAM-on-the-Curve: Sharpness-Aware Mode Connectivity for Robust Weight-Space Interpolation

author.name: Alejandro Calatrava, Xu Zhang, Ren Wang

entry.summary: The authors argue that low-loss mode connectivity is an incomplete geometric criterion, because it constrains loss only along a one-dimensional trajectory while leaving the surrounding weight-space neighborhood unconstrained, so optimized curves may traverse sharp ridges that are fragile under distribution shift. They reformulate mode connectivity as neighborhood-robust path optimization, seeking curves whose entire local neighborhood maintains low loss. The approach is connected to practical techniques such as weight averaging, ensembling, and model merging.

entry.title: Long-Context Demonstration Selection Using State Space Models

author.name: Ziniu Zhang, Zhenshuo Zhang, Ruoxuan Xiong, Gene Cooperman, Hongyang R. Zhang

entry.summary: The paper studies demonstration selection, where a subset of examples is chosen to prepend to a query for a language model, a problem that becomes costly in long-context regimes because transformer inference scales quadratically with sequence length. The authors build on state space models, which have linear inference time, and propose two algorithms: one that learns a small set of SSMs by distilling a trained transformer after partitioning layers into consecutive groups. This targets in-context learning efficiency.

entry.title: Beyond the Previous Layer: Residual Predictive Structure in Sparse MoE Routing

author.name: Hao Li, Yasuyuki Tahara, Yuichi Sei

entry.summary: This paper asks whether the immediately preceding expert selection is sufficient to predict the next router decision in sparse mixture-of-experts models. Using frozen OLMoE and JetMoE models, the authors measure held-out predictive gain from earlier expert selections while keeping the most recent selection as a baseline, finding that extending history from one to eleven layers raises router-logit R-squared from about 0.599 to 0.665 in OLMoE. A preregistered JetMoE replication yields four-layer gains with paired bootstrap intervals above zero, and the gains survive nonlinear decoding.

entry.title: Provable Guarantees for Spectral Structured Prediction

author.name: Violet Zheng, Jean Honorio

entry.summary: This paper analyzes binary node label recovery on signed graphs with edge-flip noise using a simple spectral decoder that reads labels off the sign pattern of the principal eigenvector of the noisy signed adjacency matrix. It derives graph-structure-agnostic guarantees for approximate recovery and bounds on maximum angle deviation from the ground-truth labeling, using matrix concentration and eigenvector perturbation tools. The results strengthen theory for spectral structured prediction, a model previously studied in this line of work.

entry.title: Peak-Aware Short-Term Load Forecasting Across Distribution Grid Aggregation Levels

author.name: Souhardya Chattopadhyay, Julian Oelhaf, Antonia Schoening, Jessica Deuschel, Bitan Bhattacharyya, Christian Bergler, Andreas Maier, Siming Bayer

entry.summary: This applied paper studies short-term electricity load forecasting for distribution system operators with explicit attention to high-demand periods, where errors are most costly. Using open UK and Swiss datasets, it benchmarks statistical baselines, gradient-boosted trees, and time-series foundation models across three grid aggregation levels (area codes, secondary substations, low-voltage feeders). It matters because peak-period accuracy directly affects congestion management and grid reliability.

entry.title: Robust and Efficient AI Frameworks for Scalable Material Design and Property Prediction

author.name: Kishalay Das

entry.summary: This doctoral thesis develops machine learning frameworks for crystal property prediction and crystal structure generation, motivated by the expense of density functional theory and the scarcity of labeled materials data. It introduces CrysXPP, which learns transferable crystal representations through unsupervised graph autoencoding, and CrysGNN, a larger graph-based model, among other contributions spanning pretraining, multimodal learning and generative modeling. The work is a consolidated account of an ML-for-materials research program rather than a single new result.

entry.title: TACTICS: Taxonomy-Aware Intelligent Corpus Sampling for Machine Translation

author.name: Prasanth Bathala, Anubhav Shrimal, Sukhdeep Singh Kharbhanda, Pradyumna Lanka, Rohit Dhaipule

entry.summary: TACTICS proposes coverage-optimized sampling for machine translation evaluation, arguing that random samples inherit whatever distribution a corpus happens to have and give no robustness coverage guarantee. It induces a hierarchical taxonomy from locale style guides, classifies segments against it, and selects samples that cover rule-governed conventions like terminology and formatting alongside context-dependent phenomena like tone and document coherence. The contribution is a more defensible evaluation-set construction method for MT systems.

entry.title: Mixed-Integer Nonlinear Differentiable Predictive Control for Underground Pumped Hydro Energy Storage Systems

author.name: Honghui Zheng, J\'an Boldock\'y, Yury Dvorkin, J\'an Drgo\v{n}a

entry.summary: This paper extends mixed-integer differentiable predictive control to handle multi-modal discrete decisions and nonconvex polynomial dynamics in underground pumped hydro storage. A neural policy with a Gumbel-Softmax layer maps problem parameters to continuous setpoints and integer mode selections, trained self-supervised by differentiating through the nonlinear dynamics. Contributions include a parallel differentiable simulator, a Transformer encoder for long-range temporal dependencies, and a Gumbel-Softmax annealing schedule, targeting a real energy-storage application.

entry.title: The Operable Pareto Front: Distilling Offline Search into Run-Time Control for Multi-Objective UAV Edge-Computing Scheduling

author.name: Qiao Liao, Zhiyong Feng, Bin Wu, Guodong Fan

entry.summary: The paper proposes PrefDT, a preference-conditioned Decision Transformer for joint trajectory, association, and offloading scheduling in UAV mobile edge computing, where fleets trade energy against delay. By feeding the desired trade-off point as an input, a single offline-trained model can return any point on the Pareto front in one rollout at run time. Attention pooling with a per-user bypass makes the scheduler robust to missing user reports.

entry.title: COMPASS-ABS: Reducing Fragmentation in Shared GPU Clusters for Deep Learning Training Workloads

author.name: Yukai Zhou, Hongfan Wu

entry.summary: The paper introduces Scheduler-Induced Fragmentation, a workload-independent metric built on partial nodes, and the COMPASS-ABS scheduler to keep resource fragmentation low in shared GPU clusters running deep learning training jobs. It targets the underutilization and long turnaround times caused by fragmented GPU allocations. This matters for the economics of large-scale training infrastructure.

entry.title: Variational Quantum Transformer Architecture for Synthetic Language Generation

author.name: Julian Hager, Michael K\"olle, Gerhard Stenzel, Tobias Rohe, Jonas Stein, Claudia Linnhoff-Popien

entry.summary: The authors propose a compact NISQ-compatible quantum transformer for synthetic quantum natural language processing, replacing attention and feed-forward sublayers with variational quantum encoder blocks, connector circuits, decoder blocks, and a two-qubit measurement readout. Token contexts are angle-encoded into small quantum registers producing a distribution over a four-token vocabulary, benchmarked against a classical transformer on grammar-generation tasks. It explores whether hybrid quantum architectures can support autoregressive sequence modeling.

entry.title: TTM-Bench: A Framework for Text-to-Music System Performance Benchmarking

author.name: Giorgia Adorni, Michela Papandrea, Battista Rimoldi, Tiziano Leidi

entry.summary: TTM-Bench defines a common protocol for reproducible benchmarking of text-to-music systems, evaluating musical-content alignment via interpretable semantic, genre, and musical-descriptor agreement, alongside a second dimension of system performance. The motivation is that heterogeneous architectures, conditioning options, and fragmented metrics make comparisons unreliable. It matters as a standardization effort for a fast-growing generative audio area.

entry.title: Large Language Models Versus Physicians in Traditional Chinese Medicine: A Real-World Clinical Case Evaluation

author.name: Jiacheng Xie, Xiaoting Tang, Yang Yu, Jinpu Li, Shouli Li, Congcong Jing, Yantao Yang, Zhiyong Zhao, Ziyang Zhang, Qilin Song, Guanghui An, Dong Xu

entry.summary: The study assembled 349 de-identified outpatient cases from 62 hospitals and had five senior TCM experts score 16 LLMs and 60 practicing physicians on nine diagnostic and therapeutic dimensions using 60 representative cases. Cutting-edge general-purpose LLMs outscored physician comparators on medical advice and treatment principles, though limitations remain. It matters as a large, expert-adjudicated comparison of LLMs against human clinicians in a non-Western medical tradition.

entry.title: Size Matters: Foundation Model for Czech HTML documents

author.name: Martin Dvo\v{r}\'ak, V\'it Tlusto\v{s}, Artyom Voronin, Martin Habrovec, Kate\v{r}ina Podlesn\'a, Barbora Ri\v{s}ov\'a, Josef Von\'a\v{s}ek

entry.summary: The authors present HTML-LM, a compact 154M-parameter foundation model for representing Czech HTML web documents, built on a ModernBERT architecture with HTML-aware training. It was trained on 100 million web documents using masked language modeling, bag-of-words prediction, and contrastive distillation, targeting performant and economical industrial deployment.

entry.title: HearInContext: A Benchmark for Implicit Context in Speech Recognition

author.name: Yifan Gao, Yao Tian, Hongbin Suo

entry.summary: HearInContext is a Mandarin-English benchmark pairing shared synthetic speech with assistant replies that support different interpretations, comprising 3,764 semantic test cases built around homophones. It separates implicit from explicit context and includes no-context and unrelated-context controls, and shows fine-tuning Qwen3-ASR-1.7B improves implicit-context target recall by roughly 11 percentage points.

entry.title: How Much is a Human Right Worth? ECtHR-NPD: A Benchmark for Predicting Non-Pecuniary Damage Awards

author.name: Yanyi Pu, Damian A. Gonzalez-Salzberg, Zheng Yuan, Nikolaos Aletras

entry.summary: ECtHR-NPD is presented as the first benchmark for predicting non-pecuniary damage awards at the European Court of Human Rights from case information, where no statutory formula determines the amount. It contains 14,575 cases with nominal-euro awards, chronological splits, and a protocol separating target construction from model input, evaluated across constant predictors, gradient-boosted trees, retrieval, fine-tuned encoders, prompted decoders, and knowledge-augmented agents.

entry.title: TeleAntiFraud 2.0: A Refreshable, Profile-Grounded, and Audio-Based Benchmark for Telecom Fraud Detection

author.name: Huiyuan Liu, Zhiming Ma, Yanxing Liu, Shun Zhang, Qifan Wang, Di Liu, Yifan Wang, Yuyang Deng, Haoyang Meng, Yijin Zhou, Yuxi Zhao, Chengxian Hu, Peidong Wang, Peng Chen

entry.summary: The paper argues telecom fraud evaluation needs benchmarks that can incorporate new scam patterns without overwriting prior test sets and must distinguish fraud from lawful near-domain calls rather than topic-separated negatives. TeleAntiFraud 2.0 uses a Mixed-Tree Anti-Fraud Generation Pipeline with profile-grounded scenarios and a monthly frozen evaluation protocol, generating both fraud and non-fraud dialogue paths.

entry.title: Code Consistency Preference Optimization Verification for Language Model Alignment

author.name: Yunlong Tan, Mingqiao Mo, Hao Zhang

entry.summary: The paper argues that execution-based verification improves mathematical reasoning through computational soundness and dependency-aware filtering, but prior preference optimization methods built on Bradley-Terry reward models fail to capture logical dependencies and execution consistency in scientific tasks. It proposes generating computationally sound solutions with dependency graphs to drive execution-consistent preference optimization, building a dataset from UltraFeedback prompts with verification and consistency results.

entry.title: MechReason: Benchmarking Multi-Image Multi-Hop Reasoning in Mechanical Engineering

author.name: Tengyue Wang, Kang An, Chenxu Du, Zhongyu Yang, Yuanchi Zhu, Xinqi Yang, Hebao Zhu, Ziliang Wang, FaQiang Qian, Yunli Yang, Qibing Ren

entry.summary: The paper argues existing multimodal benchmarks emphasize basic tasks like drawing recognition or single-chart querying and do not test whether models can combine multiple images, textual conditions, physical principles, and engineering constraints. MechReason is a benchmark derived from real mechanical engineering papers with roughly 12k question-answer pairs targeting multi-image, multi-hop reasoning.

entry.title: Can Knowledge Transfer Parameters Be Learned? LePoKet for Efficient Robotic Vision

author.name: Yanick C. Tchenko, Felix Mohr, Hicham Hadj-Abdelkader, Hedi Tabia

entry.summary: LePoKet builds on Hereditary Knowledge Transfer to embed knowledge inheritance directly into the forward computation of a compact network, using a block-wise Extract-Transform-Mix interface whose interaction parameters are optimized jointly with the child network via a learnable genetic approach. It challenges the reliance on fixed distillation objectives or hand-designed interaction mechanisms for transferring knowledge from large pretrained models. It matters for perception under tight compute, memory and latency budgets in robotics.

entry.title: IMVS: Interactive Medical Volume Segmentation with Test-Time Adaptation - A New Method for Annotating Radiology Datasets

author.name: Abhilaksh Singh Reen, Kushal Borkar, Ritvik Mahapatra

entry.summary: IMVS is a human-in-the-loop annotation framework for 3D radiology volumes that pairs a lightweight 2D slice mask adapter fine-tuned online from user scribbles with a frozen volume mask tracker. Rather than introducing a new segmentation primitive, it closes the loop so the propagator adapts to the target volume instead of drifting on low-contrast or pathological structures. It matters for reducing the manual burden of slice-by-slice delineation in dataset creation.

entry.title: PSMP-CLIP: Patch-Prompt SAM and Multi-Semantic Prompting for CLIP-Based Zero-Shot Anomaly Detection

author.name: Xuezhi Xiang, Guanghao Wu, Heqi Xiang, Jiayao Liu, Xiaoheng Li, Yiming Chen, Shanjun Zhang

entry.summary: PSMP-CLIP combines patch-prompt SAM2 segmentation, which samples prompts directly from intermediate patch features to avoid threshold drift, with multi-semantic guided prompt regularization anchored by learnable prompts. The goal is finer anomaly maps and better preserved generalization in zero-shot anomaly detection. It reports the best pixel-level AUROC across seven datasets including MVTec AD and several medical benchmarks.

entry.title: TecoPrompt: Temporal-Conservative Prompt Learning for Vision-Language Models

author.name: Zeyi Shao, Haowen Hua, Jiaxin Zhang, John See, Zeyd Boukhers, Cong Yang

entry.summary: TecoPrompt is a robust prompt-learning framework for CLIP-style models that revisits optimal transport pseudo-labeling from a temporal perspective. Entropic optimal transport proposes globally consistent label candidates in the CLIP semantic space, and a candidate is only accepted if it stays stable across a K-epoch window and passes an exponential-moving-average confidence gate. It matters for keeping few-shot prompt optimization stable when labels are noisy.

entry.title: GRACE: Geometry- and Ray-Aware Camera-Efficient Multi-View Pedestrian Tracking

author.name: Taigo Sakai, Kazuhiro Hotta, Hiroki Kouno, Naoki Kato

entry.summary: GRACE is a camera-efficient multi-view pedestrian tracker combining homography-based BEV features with features lifted through 3D space, and exposing each camera's viewing direction to the fusion network via ray conditioning. Its BEV track recovery module uses low-confidence detections only to continue existing tracks, never to start new ones, mitigating track splits from short score drops. It improves MOTA with only two WildTrack cameras relative to the authors' baseline.

entry.title: FROD: Feature Matching Residual Denoising Oracle Bone Decipher

author.name: Yanbin Hou, Biao Xiong, Guojun Xu, Jianwen Xiang, Cheng Tan, Yanchao Yang, Junwei Zhou

entry.summary: FROD reformulates oracle bone script decipherment assistance as cross-era image translation, exploiting the fact that ancient characters often preserve local topological invariants at the radical level. It uses fast feature matching to gate segmentation supervision for paired samples, aiming to automate part of a traditionally expert-driven and labor-intensive epigraphic workflow.

entry.title: ConGraspXL: Controllable Constraint-Conditioned Dexterous Grasping Motion Synthesis

author.name: Hui Zhang, Mirko Meboldt, Jie Song

entry.summary: ConGraspXL extends the earlier GraspXL framework to synthesize dexterous grasping motions that satisfy diverse task-driven constraints such as approach direction, contact regions, wrist trajectories and functional hand poses. It introduces a hierarchical constraint formulation and a masked residual interface that allows flexible composition of multiple constraints in one generative model.

entry.title: CLARE: Scalable Class-Incremental Continual Learning via a Sparsity-Based Framework

author.name: Yunxiang Fu, Meng Lou, Zicheng Liao, Yizhou Yu

entry.summary: CLARE is a two-stage sparsity-driven continual-learning framework that first identifies a sparse task-critical parameter set and then leverages it to combat forgetting and loss of plasticity when pretrained models are trained sequentially on many tasks. It targets the scalability bottleneck where existing methods degrade under long task streams due to inter-task interference.

entry.title: Neuro-Symbolic Hierarchical Intention Anticipation in Human Behavior

author.name: Farnaz Soleimani (LISSI), Abdelghani Chibani (LISSI), Yacine Amirat (LISSI), Ghazaleh Khodabandelou (LISSI)

entry.summary: The paper formulates human intention anticipation as goal inference from partially observed multimodal episodes plus structured prediction over four ontological levels, rather than exact motor forecasting. A compact Hierarchical Planning Decoder is attached to a frozen neuro-symbolic encoder and trained with soft regularization and hard reachability masks enforcing ontology constraints.

entry.title: SPROUT: The Open-Source Soft Growing Robot for Search and Rescue

author.name: Antonio Alvarez Valdivia, Ciera McFarland, Robert Reeve, Ankush Dhawan, Chad Council, Megan Richardson, Margaret McGuinness, Nathaniel Hanson

entry.summary: SPROUT is an open-source soft growing robot designed for urban search and rescue, developed over years of collaboration with professional search-and-rescue teams to operate in dusty, wet and confined conditions. The paper releases code, parts manifests, CAD assemblies and build instructions so other labs can replicate the system. It matters for lowering the barrier to fielding soft robotics outside the laboratory.

entry.title: VCTP: Vehicle-Conditioned Terrain Planning for Off-Road Navigation

author.name: Akshay Naik, Ramavarapu S. Sreenivas, Dustin Nottage, Ahmet Soylemezoglu

entry.summary: VCTP plans off-road routes by evaluating shared elevation and surface-identity layers at eight headings, so that body geometry constrains admissible poses while loaded wheel contacts drive modeled surface cost, pitch and roll predictions. It uses D* Lite and vehicle-state search to produce forward and reverse routes and recomputes affected queries when observations change. It matters because heading-dependent terrain interaction is usually ignored in planners.

entry.title: Real-Time Bounded Catenary Solver for UAV Tether Modeling

author.name: Max Beffert, Andreas Zell

entry.summary: This paper targets real-time simulation of tether forces acting on non-stationary tethered multirotor UAVs, where online use imposes a hard bound on maximum solve time. Prior quasi-analytical catenary work reached a mean solve time of about 0.51 ms using a general-purpose root finder but lacked worst-case guarantees. The authors reformulate the inner solver by reducing the catenary boundary-value problem to a single transcendental equation in one well-conditioned unknown, deriving a closed-form bracket and proving monotonicity, convexity, and existence/uniqueness of the root to guarantee convergence.

entry.title: Active perception for robotic harvesting: 3D reconstruction and localisation of tomatoes hidden within clusters in a Mediterranean greenhouse

author.name: Fernando Ca\~nadas-Ar\'anega, Rowan Border, Jos\'e C. Moreno, Jos\'e L. Blanco-Claraco

entry.summary: This study presents a pipeline for 3D reconstruction and precise localization of individual tomatoes within clusters, including heavily occluded fruits, in Mediterranean greenhouse conditions. It breaks the problem into five sequential stages and uses active perception because fixed robot-mounted sensors cannot see fruits hidden behind the visible surface. The work addresses cluster-growing crops, which are less studied than isolated-fruit crops such as apples or peppers.

entry.title: Towards Interaction Regulation from Human Feedback via Free Energy Minimization

author.name: Maria Paula Diaz Monfort, Cinzia Tomaselli, Michael Richardson, Giovanni Russo

entry.summary: Inspired by the free energy principle from computational neuroscience, the authors build a control-theoretic framework that integrates human preferences online into an agent policy and release it as an open control architecture. They validate it with a human-in-the-loop rover testbed where a remote human in VR headsets shares the rover's sensory information and communicates preferences via gestures, inducing both cooperative and competitive interactions. It matters for mechanisms that regulate human-agent interaction rather than just optimizing task reward.

entry.title: What Counts as Strategic Reasoning? A Systematic Mapping of Chess Research on Humans, Engines, and Language Models

author.name: Paolo Ciancarini, Remo Pareschi

entry.summary: This systematic mapping study surveys recent chess research across human players, classical engines, neural and reinforcement-learning systems, LLMs, and hybrid approaches, treating chess as a controlled environment for studying strategic reasoning. The final map comprises 84 core study families classified by agent type, strategic-reasoning stage, and evaluation dimensions. It matters because it reveals where the literature concentrates, notably on situation assessment, evaluation, and action selection, and highlights the aspects of strategic reasoning that remain understudied as LLMs are drawn into the domain.

entry.title: TRIPROBE: Probing Task Separability Beyond Classification for XAI

author.name: Amirhossein Sadough, Freek Hens, Aleksa Bok\v{s}an, Mohammad Mahdi Dehshibi, Mahyar Shahsavari

entry.summary: TriProbe is a multi-level probing framework for explainable diagnosis of task separability, tracing how separability evolves across inputs, learned features, and final classifiers. It decomposes multi-task problems into binary subtasks and applies foundational, latent, and final probes, using the Maximum Fisher's Discriminant Ratio as a principled separability metric. The goal is to identify bottlenecks and problematic task pairs instead of reducing evaluation to downstream accuracy.

entry.title: Evolutionary Ensemble Search: Council-Guided Program Evolution with Persistent Memory

author.name: Juan P. Madrigal-Cianci, Eshan Chordia

entry.summary: Evolutionary Ensemble Search constructs machine-learning pipelines through expert-guided program evolution, where a role-specialized council converts task evidence into structured search directions that an orchestrator routes to execution specialists and an evolutionary engine. Descendants are produced by code mutation, structured pipeline edits and crossover, must execute and earn their own validation evidence, and compatible predictions compete in a validation-gated ensemble stage with parent-relative operator credit and session memory.

entry.title: RoboVAD: A Large Cross-Domain Evaluation Benchmark for Anomaly Detection in Robotic Arm Manipulation Videos

author.name: Alexandru-Bogdan Dura, Sebastian Balmus, Radu Tudor Ionescu

entry.summary: RoboVAD is a large-scale benchmark for video anomaly detection in robotic arm manipulation, featuring cross-domain evaluation scenarios where task actions and anomaly types vary. It addresses the scarcity of resources for detecting anomalies in robotic manipulation videos, which matters for recovery procedures and improved interaction learning.

entry.title: On-the-Fly Homographies Calibration for Multi-Camera Tracking

author.name: David Voihanski, Mor Sinai, Ben Zion Bobrovsky

entry.summary: This system performs on-the-fly geometric refinement for multi-camera tracking, starting from coarse manual homographies and using a centroid-based projection optimization that continuously aligns ground-plane geometry from live detection streams. It is designed for large deployments where recording video for offline calibration is blocked by privacy rules, bandwidth prevents synchronizing many high-resolution streams, and physical calibration targets are impractical. It matters as a privacy-aware alternative to rigorous 3D site calibration for city-scale tracking.

entry.title: NeuroECG: ECGFounder-Based Deep ECG Representation for EEG-Free Neurological Prognostication After Cardiac Arrest

author.name: Jiaju Gao, Yi Zhao, Chenyang Xu, Yuxi Zhou, Hao Wang

entry.summary: NeuroECG adapts a pretrained ECG foundation model to predict neurological outcomes after cardiac arrest using only low-cost bedside single-lead ECG, avoiding the resource-intensive EEG typically required. The pipeline fine-tunes the encoder with gradual unfreezing, encodes multiple ECG segments per patient, and aggregates segment features via quantile pooling with principal component compression. The contribution is a clinically motivated, resource-light alternative for post-arrest prognostication.

entry.title: Beyond Static RAG: An Adaptive, Tri-Metric Routing Framework for Efficient Long-Context Inference on Commodity GPUs

author.name: Saipraveen Vabbilisetty, Ajay Kumar Boddepalli, Deep Narayan Mishra, Shashank Kapadia, Haoan Wang, Anupriya Sharma

entry.summary: The paper identifies a Compression Paradox in retrieval-augmented generation on commodity GPUs, where neural prompt compression can add KV cache contention and preprocessing latency that outweigh generation savings, while skipping compression can cause out-of-memory failures on long contexts. It introduces a Tri-Metric Router, a deterministic training-free policy that chooses among raw, neural (LLMLingua-2), and lexical (BM25) pipelines using CPU-side signals. The contributions are two identified failure mechanisms under co-deployed vLLM and PyTorch compressors plus the routing policy.

entry.title: NObSP: Functional Decomposition of Neural Networks via Oblique Subspace Projections

author.name: Alexander Caicedo, V\'ictor De La Hoz, Santiago Alf\'erez

entry.summary: NObSP is a framework that decomposes network predictions into explicit per-feature contribution functions plus an interaction residual, exploiting the linear final layer of a trained network and using oblique projections in sample space to reduce double counting when learned feature subspaces overlap. It supports local explanations and global functional analysis, connects to functional ANOVA and the Kolmogorov-Arnold representation theorem, and provides an efficient partial regression algorithm for out-of-sample evaluation. A convolutional variant, NObSP-CAM, produces class activation maps.

entry.title: FedPGT: Progressive Gradient Transmission for Vehicular Federated Learning over Time-Varying Channels

author.name: Jintao Yan, Tan Chen, Yuxuan Sun, Sheng Zhou, Zhisheng Niu

entry.summary: FedPGT proposes a progressive gradient transmission scheme for vehicular federated learning in which vehicles send high-magnitude gradient entries incrementally in response to instantaneous channel conditions rather than under a fixed sparsification plan. The authors provide a convergence bound capturing the effect of transmission decisions on training, addressing the failure of predetermined allocation under fast channel variation from vehicle mobility. It targets communication-efficient, privacy-preserving training for intelligent transportation systems.

entry.title: Learning to Program Adaptive Non-Local Observables for Machine Learning

author.name: Yu-Ting Lee, Samuel Yen-Chi Chen, Huan-Hsin Tseng

entry.summary: This paper proposes QFWP-ANO, an architecture in which a classical hypernetwork dynamically programs variational quantum circuit parameters and non-local observables conditioned on each input, addressing the limitation that prior adaptive-observable methods learn only a single static observable. On multivariate time-series forecasting across four ETT datasets, the method achieves the lowest MSE in most settings. It matters as a step toward more expressive input-conditioned quantum neural networks.

entry.title: Enhancing Extubation Failure Prediction with LLM-Derived Features from Respiratory Therapy Clinical Notes

author.name: Izzy Chaiken, Aditya Khowal, Neha A. Sathe, Mark M. Wurfel, Lucy Lu Wang

entry.summary: This clinical NLP study extracts features from free-text respiratory therapy notes using a large language model plus a logistic regression pipeline and adds them to structured patient data to predict extubation failure. Applied to a University of Washington Medicine cohort, the added features improve prediction and are clinically interpretable. The authors also note that inconsistent inclusion criteria and definitions across prior extubation studies create systematic differences that complicate comparison.

entry.title: Generic Characteristic-Zero Equivalence Between Derivative B\'ezout Inversion and Multipoint Evaluation

author.name: Zijian Zeng

entry.summary: The paper analyzes the arithmetic complexity of computing the normalized Bezout pair satisfying sZ plus tZ prime equals one for a polynomial split over distinct field elements. Over an infinite field of characteristic zero, it proves that computing all coefficients of the canonical Bezout pair is equivalent, up to additive cost, to arbitrary-node multipoint evaluation and interpolation in the generic rational straight-line-program model, via an explicit differential reconstruction. The result sharpens earlier bounds that did not match the fast multipoint evaluation complexity.

entry.title: Beyond Direct Sensing: Harnessing Indirect Observations from Third-Party Sensors in Vehicle Tracking

author.name: Gaofeng Dong, Vamsi Eyunni, Pragya Sharma, Kang Yang, Mani Srivastava

entry.summary: This work investigates whether weak, indirect observations from third-party sensing assets with uncertain spatial and temporal cues can supplement sparse direct measurements in vehicle tracking. Conventional tracking assumes strong direct sensors providing identity and location, but ownership, privacy, cost, and operational constraints often prevent raw-data access. The paper studies how such indirect signals can be integrated to fill long tracking gaps.

entry.title: Rank and computation of the pathlifting Jacobian of a DAG ReLU network

author.name: Manon Verbockhaven (OCKHAM)

entry.summary: The paper gives a self-contained proof of the rank of the pathlifting Jacobian for DAG ReLU networks via induction on hidden nodes, using a sparse skeleton matrix encoding network paths. It also offers a way to compute this Jacobian without backpropagation at reportedly very efficient practical cost. The result is a theoretical contribution to understanding ReLU network geometry and computation.

entry.title: How Calibration Content Shapes Attention-Based Reranking

author.name: Petros Karypis, Hossein Rajaby Faghihi, Peter Chen, Rui Zhu, Noveen Sachdeva, Yan Zhu, Julian McAuley

entry.summary: Attention-based rerankers subtract a null-query calibration pass to strip positional and structural bias, but the authors show the null pass can become relevance-aware when prompt content such as constraints, instructions, personas, and demonstrations enters the scoring readout. Calibration then removes genuine signal, and the harm grows with longer, more detailed instructions. They propose interpolated null calibration, a training-free modification that mitigates this failure.

entry.title: Long-Lived Characters, Local Inference: Incremental Memory Maintenance for Game NPCs

author.name: Zimu Xu

entry.summary: This work studies incremental memory maintenance for long-lived game NPCs running on a quantized Qwen hybrid recurrent-attention model locally. The runtime removes superseded attention KV entries and computes replacement representations so that revising a few memories does not invalidate a long reusable prefix, keeping preparation cost from competing with dialogue and other characters.

entry.title: Reading Between the Lines: Can LLMs Discover the Question Behind the Text?

author.name: Claudiu Creanga, Liviu P. Dinu

entry.summary: The paper introduces question archaeology, an evaluation task requiring a model to infer the single authentic genesis question that motivated a complete text, distinct from generic question generation. Using a new dataset of commissioned texts with original research questions and distractors, the authors find newer proprietary and open models outperform earlier versions while BERT-based models perform poorly.

entry.title: FRAUDSkill: Structured Frozen-Weight Skill Optimization for Audio Anti-Fraud Detection

author.name: Chengxian Hu, Zhiming Ma, Mingjun Pan, Yifan Wang, Shun Zhang, Qifan Wang, Zhilei Zhao, Yijin Zhou, Yuxi Zhao, Huiyuan Liu, Peidong Wang, Peng Chen

entry.summary: The paper notes that deploying audio-language models for anti-fraud detection requires predictions to follow a predefined label space and a structured decision protocol covering service-scenario identification, fraud detection, and conditional fraud-type classification. FRAUDSkill is a structured frozen-weight adaptation framework that keeps the underlying audio-language model unchanged, easing adaptation as fraud patterns and labeling policies evolve.

entry.title: Counterfactual Reasoning for Robust Visual Question Answering

author.name: Truong-Binh Duong, Thanh-Ngan Tran, Ngoc-Thao Nguyen, Bac Le

entry.summary: This work tackles language bias and spurious correlation in VQA models by enhancing counterfactual contrastive learning. It introduces a three-stage curriculum for stable multi-objective optimization, an improved batch-contrastive loss for more discriminative features, and two regularizers including an answer-contrastive loss. It matters for out-of-distribution robustness in multimodal question answering.

entry.title: Lesion-centered 3D mapping of colonoscopy procedures: validation of a hierarchical ensemble pipeline on public benchmark videos

author.name: Hyunjun Kim, Hyeonwoo Na, Jaewoo Lee

entry.summary: The paper assembles a four-layer pipeline, spanning a global topological map, lesion-level spatio-temporal tracks, on-demand local 3D reconstruction, and persistent lesion identity, to build a lesion-centered spatial record from colonoscopy video. It is validated end to end on four public videos without requiring full-colon 3D reconstruction. The work matters clinically because spatial information in procedure video is currently discarded at the end of each exam.

entry.title: Evaluating Mesh Reconstruction Methods for Crop Phenotyping

author.name: Karanvir Singh, Theo Morales, Binh-Son Hua, Mukesh Saini

entry.summary: Benchmarks seven mesh reconstruction pipelines for digitizing agricultural crops, measuring fidelity and consistency both qualitatively and quantitatively. The goal is to let crop specialists study plants at remote sites through 3D models instead of on-site inspection. The study matters as a practical guide for choosing reconstruction methods in agricultural phenotyping.

entry.title: Automated Distinction of Intimal and Medial Intracranial Arterial Calcification from CT Head

author.name: Benjamin Jin, Maria del C. Vald\'es Hern\'andez, Richard Bortsov, Joanna M. Wardlaw, Daniel Bos, Grant Mair

entry.summary: This study compares three automated approaches for classifying intracranial arterial calcification as intimal or medial from head CT segmentation masks: an adaptation of the established radiological visual score, a sphericity-based shape method, and shape embeddings from a medical shape foundation model. The distinction matters clinically because the subtypes differ in aetiology and carry different neurovascular risk implications.

entry.title: Differentiable Mesh State Estimation via Factor Graph Inference for Deformable Object Reconstruction

author.name: Lidia Al-Zogbi, Fangjie Li, Samuel Tobin, James Ferguson, Nithesh Kumar, Alejandro Chara, Kuan-I Chung, Mingxing Rao, Ayberk Acar, Susheela Sharma Stern, Robert Webster, Daniel Moyer, Alan Kuntz, Caleb Rucker, Tucker Hermans, Jie Ying Wu

entry.summary: This work introduces a factor-graph framework for probabilistic mesh state estimation of deformable objects, directly updating a tetrahedral mesh by fusing physics priors, noisy sensor measurements and temporal smoothness within a single nonlinear least-squares formulation solved via Levenberg-Marquardt. It is validated on ex vivo central-airway obstruction experiments and deforming cube simulations.

entry.title: Knowledge as Orbit: Finite Collections as Phases of an Exactly Periodic Latent Generator

author.name: Siddharth Pal, Viktoria Rojkova

entry.summary: The paper explores storing a finite collection intensionally as the decoded orbit of a compact periodic latent generator, encoding item i as the i-th phase of a fixed rotation in a learned latent space. Using a real discrete Fourier operator, the design guarantees exact closure so that the generator returns to its starting point rather than having to learn that property, with looping video as the natural use case.

entry.title: Multi-Session Multimodal Underwater Mapping with Acoustic and Optical Imaging

author.name: Precious Philip-Ifabiyi, Valerio Franchi, Fausto Ferreira, Nuno Gracias

entry.summary: This paper presents a factor-graph framework for multi-session underwater mapping that jointly optimizes vehicle trajectories, 3D landmarks, sensor extrinsics and per-session alignment transforms, fusing side-scan sonar and optical imagery. It combines rigid inter-session corrections with local trajectory deformation to handle positioning drift and sensor offsets. It matters for marine science, archaeology and environmental monitoring where surveys are repeated across sessions.

entry.title: Information-Based Trajectory Planning for Spacecraft-to-Spacecraft Tracking and Navigation in Cislunar Space

author.name: Trevor N. Wolf, Brandon A. Jones, Jay W. McMahon

entry.summary: This paper develops a trajectory planning method that balances information collection against control effort for spacecraft-to-spacecraft absolute tracking in cislunar space. It exploits nonlinear dynamical tracers encoded in relative measurements to infer the absolute states of observer and target, and designs observer trajectories that jointly optimize control effort and an information-theoretic objective. The work supports reduced reliance on ground-based navigation support as cislunar activity expands.

entry.title: PRISM: Predictive Representation of Interaction Style and Motion for Social Robot Navigation

author.name: Bo-Han Chen, Hiromu Taketsugu, Norimichi Ukita

entry.summary: PRISM infers pedestrians' latent interaction traits from passive observations of human-human interactions, encoding trajectories into a continuous ordinal latent space with a transformer trained via Rank-N-Contrast loss. Each inferred trait is paired with a temporal-stability score fed to the navigation policy, and in randomized crowd simulations PRISM reduces collisions relative to geometry-only baselines. It matters because most crowd navigation stacks treat pedestrians as homogeneous geometric agents, ignoring individual behavioral differences.

entry.title: Reducing the Resource Gap Between Lab and External Safety Researchers

author.name: Alexandra Narin

entry.summary: Drawing on Geodesic Research's experience deploying philanthropic funding for a compute-heavy safety agenda, this post identifies non-obvious procurement bottlenecks that slow independent AI safety nonprofits from scaling research. It outlines concrete ways philanthropies can support outside organizations and includes an appendix describing a large multi-year compute deal and the procurement strategy behind it. It matters because the compute asymmetry between frontier labs and independent safety researchers threatens the viability of external oversight work.

entry.title: How to Open Them Up – Part I

author.name: ValueShift Research

entry.summary: ValueShift Research outlines a systematization of mechanistic interpretability aimed at four tasks: locating a concept's representation, establishing its causal role, establishing its necessity, and steering it to change behavior. The first part reviews methods for finding concepts, including linear probes, difference-in-means, sparse autoencoders, and PCA with clustering, discussing trade-offs in cost and precision.

entry.title: Hyperbolic Graph Representation Learning for Differential Diagnosis on Biomedical Knowledge Graphs

author.name: Pietro Miotto, Lucia Mellini, Tommaso Marzi, Cesare Alippi, Elena Casiraghi, Alberto Paccanaro, Giorgio Valentini, Mauricio Soto-Gomez

entry.summary: The paper studies whether hyperbolic embeddings, which suit tree-like structure, remain useful on biomedical knowledge graphs that mix ontology hierarchies with transversal associations among phenotypes, diseases, genes, proteins, and patients. Experiments on isolated ontology subgraphs show hyperbolic models match strong performance at substantially lower dimensionality than Euclidean baselines. The authors then evaluate them on a link-prediction task that ranks candidate diagnoses.

entry.title: Maximum Strong Independent Sets in Hypergraphs: Reductions, Bounds, and Greedy Certificates

author.name: Yingquan (Cody), Wu, Jason Cong

entry.summary: The paper formalizes the maximum strong independent set problem on hypergraphs, where the goal is the largest vertex set intersecting each hyperedge in at most one vertex. It develops an incidence-structural toolkit with exact reductions for dominance, incidence twins, and weight-1 blocks, closed-form upper bounds, and puncturing/covering certificates, motivated by multi-band LSH-MinHash deduplication where connected-component contraction creates spurious global equivalences. The contribution is mainly combinatorial algorithmics with a concrete applied hook in data deduplication.

entry.title: Behavioral Fingerprinting and Navigation Prediction in Web Browsing

author.name: Ralph Elsaghbini, Omran Berjawi, Walid Fahs, Rida Khatoun

entry.summary: This empirical study compares two behavioral inference tasks derived from the same anonymized browsing event stream: session-level user identification and next-domain prediction. Classical and neural models are evaluated on session-level behavioral and domain features for identification, while next-domain prediction combines graph-based modeling with sequence modeling. The results bear on both privacy risk, since short browsing fragments can fingerprint users, and on predictive modeling of navigation behavior.

entry.title: Faking Good and Faking Bad in LLMs: Response Distortion Across Dark Triad Personality Traits

author.name: Victoria Popa, Guglielmo Cola, Caterina Senette, Maurizio Tesconi

entry.summary: This study tests whether seven state-of-the-art LLMs distort their personality responses the way humans do under impression-management pressure. Framing prompts as employment-selection or forensic contexts produced systematic shifts in measured Machiavellianism, narcissism, and psychopathy relative to self-assessment baselines. The work matters for anyone using LLM personality scores as proxies or data, since trait estimates appear context-sensitive and manipulable.

entry.title: Correlation-Guided Encoder Selection for Multi-Encoder Large Audio-Language Models

author.name: Pei-Jun Liao, Hung-Shin Lee, Wenze Ren, Kuo-Hsuan Hung, Hung-yi Lee, Hsin-Min Wang

entry.summary: The paper notes that multi-encoder fusion in Large Audio-Language Models is often chosen by intuition or exhaustive search, adding redundant representations and compute cost. It proposes CUES, a lightweight heuristic that estimates encoder complementarity from task- and category-level Pearson correlations between single-encoder performance profiles, requiring no fusion training during selection, evaluated on XARES-LLM with a frozen SmolLM2-135M backbone.

entry.title: Hyperbolic Contrastive Learning with Entailment for Spatial Transcriptomics

author.name: Daniela Vega, Paula C\'ardenas, Hannah Ceballos, Leonardo Manrique, Pablo Arbela\'ez

entry.summary: The paper notes that spatial transcriptomics is costly and equipment-intensive, motivating computer vision methods that predict spatial gene expression from histopathology images, though current approaches over-smooth expression and produce uniform predictions. It proposes hyperbolic contrastive learning with entailment to capture the hierarchical, asymmetric structure of gene regulation and tissue morphology.

entry.title: TEDi: Temporal Memory-Enhanced and Denoising Transformer for Surgical Instrument Segmentation

author.name: Jiahong Yuan, Weiming Mi, Tao Zhang, Haoyin Zhou

entry.summary: TEDi is a query-based segmentation transformer for surgical instruments that adds a query-level memory bank with memory search enhancement and a temporal consistency denoising mechanism. It addresses the tendency of per-frame query methods to produce unstable representations and inconsistent category recognition. The work matters for reliable scene understanding in computer-assisted surgery.

entry.title: Measuring Annotation Efficiency for Handwritten Devanagari Recognition: Sample-Complexity Curves for Four Pretraining Regimes

author.name: Manglesh Kumar Pandey, Sumit Kumar Banshal

entry.summary: This study measures how many manually transcribed word images are needed before a handwritten Devanagari recognizer becomes useful, holding the recognizer, optimizer, and evaluation protocol fixed while varying fine-tuning budgets across nine levels and four pretraining regimes. It directly quantifies how much transcription cost pretraining can remove. The work matters for low-resource scripts where transcription depends on scarce specialists.

entry.title: A Sentinel-2 benchmark dataset for deep-learning active-fire segmentation across 25 California wildfires

author.name: Shreyan Mitra, Mohammadreza Narimani, Parastoo Farajpoor

entry.summary: The paper releases an open image-mask dataset of 2,148 Sentinel-2 chip pairs from 25 California wildfires spanning 2020 to 2026 for training active-fire segmentation models. Masks distinguish background, SWIR-rule active fire and invalid observations, and the release includes metadata plus an incident-disjoint partition to prevent leakage.

entry.title: The Cost of Becoming: Developmental Encoding Increases Phenotypic Diversity but Reduces Locality and Recombination Robustness in Evolved Robots

author.name: Lyes Saad Saoud

entry.summary: This controlled evolutionary-robotics study compares direct encoding, a static generative encoding and a temporal zygotic developmental encoding under matched genomes, controllers, mutation, crossover, environments and evaluation budgets. It finds that developmental encoding raises phenotypic diversity but reduces locality and recombination robustness, challenging the assumption that structured genotype-to-phenotype maps are uniformly beneficial.

entry.title: Characterizing Refraction-Induced Ranging Bias in Underwater Collaborative Localization

author.name: Timothy Kogucki, Alan Papalia

entry.summary: The paper studies how sound-speed variability bends acoustic rays and systematically biases range measurements to be longer than the straight-line assumption used in standard sensor fusion, examining effects across oceanographic conditions and spatial scales. It characterizes this bias for multi-agent range-aided underwater localization. It matters because collaborative underwater navigation accuracy depends strongly on range-measurement quality.

entry.title: Examining the Difference in Human Behavior Between Virtual and Real-World Human-Robot Teaming

author.name: Sean Dallas, Absalat Getachew, Motaz AbuHijleh, Andrea Macklem-Zabel, Douglas Zytko, Mark Brudnak, Wing-Yue Geoffrey Louie

entry.summary: This paper presents a mixed-methods user study comparing human behavior in a human-robot teaming scenario conducted in virtual versus real environments. It examines team performance and human factors to test whether virtual experimentation validly substitutes for costly real-world prototyping and evaluation. Quantitative results showed a significant difference in workload between the two conditions, raising questions about the consistency assumptions behind virtual HRT studies.

entry.title: Fenchel-Young Duality Gaps: Certified Early Stopping for Regularized Inverse Problems

author.name: Pierre-Cyril Aubin-Frankowski (CERMICS UMR 9032, ENPC), Yohann de Castro (ICJ, ECL, IUF, PSPM)

entry.summary: The authors derive an exact duality-gap identity that decomposes the total gap of a regularized inverse problem into a Fenchel-Young data-fidelity loss and a Fenchel-Young regularizer loss, valid for any primal-dual pair. Because the data-fidelity loss is the Bregman divergence of a strictly convex F, this gives computable error bounds and a certified early-stopping criterion. This provides practical, rigorous stopping rules for regularized inverse problems.

entry.title: Is METR A Meaningful Check On Anthropic?

author.name: SE Gyges

entry.summary: A critique of Anthropic's commitment, per Dario Amodei's September 2026 essay on pacing the frontier, to give embedded third-party evaluators like METR ongoing employee-like access to verify safety practices and report incidents. The author argues METR is not meaningfully independent, is understaffed, and holds no authority that Anthropic could not revoke, making the arrangement a weak check that may even undermine genuine oversight.

entry.title: GVD: Governed Versioning and Deduplication for Document Repositories

author.name: Mohammadreza Sediqin, Shivali Dalmia, Sumukha Thoppanahalli, Abhishek Mukherji

entry.summary: GVD unifies cross-document version linking with rule-level conflict resolution under an auditable update policy, assigning incoming documents to version families through bidirectional rule alignment. It treats versioning, duplicate detection, and contradiction detection as a combined collection-level problem rather than isolated pairwise tasks.

entry.title: SAGE: Governed Artifact Generation from Enterprise Guidelines

author.name: Mohammadreza Sediqin, Shivali Dalmia, Sumukha Thoppanahalli, Srinivasa Karthikeya Reddy Kovvuri, Abhishek Mukherji

entry.summary: SAGE is a governed multi-stage LLM pipeline that converts enterprise guideline documents, mixing narrative text, tables, and embedded images, into structured work artifacts. It uses a shared versioned rule store with stable identifiers, schema-validated inter-stage contracts, and end-to-end provenance tracking, with deterministic structural validation plus LLM-based semantic scoring and a consistency module.

entry.title: FairCompressAgent: An Agentic Framework for Fairness-Aware Model Compression for FPGA Deployment

author.name: Yuanbo Guo, Yiyu Shi

entry.summary: FairCompressAgent integrates fairness-aware pruning, incremental quantization, and sparse low-rank factorization behind a common operator interface, with a language-model planner selecting compression configurations from model profiles and measured outcomes. An execution layer handles compression, fine-tuning, evaluation, and constraint-based selection, and the framework supports requirement updates with violation reporting.

entry.title: Building Trust in Artificial Intelligence: A Necessity for Railway Applications

author.name: Lefebvre Renard Cl\'ement, L\'eb\'e Vincent, Da Silva Ribeiro Pereira Ricardo, Sundell Johan, Jaoul Arnaud Saiah Kenza, Mijatov\'ic Nenad

entry.summary: The paper notes that AI in railways remains largely confined to non-safety-critical uses because of strict standards and regulation, and reviews the three areas it considers necessary for trust and compliance: robustness, operational design domain, and explainability. It anchors these to standards including ISO 24029 for robustness and DIN DKE SPEC 99004 for explicit definition of operating conditions. It matters as a regulatory-facing synthesis of what must be demonstrated before AI can enter safety-critical railway functions.

entry.title: WARD: Runtime Workload-Adaptive Vision TRansformer Framework for Dependable Edge AI

author.name: Mahdi Taheri, Pramit Kumar Bhaduri, Mohammad Masoumi, Ali Mahani

entry.summary: WARD is a runtime-adaptive framework for Vision Transformers on edge accelerators that combines channel-wise subnetwork partitioning with reliability-aware mechanisms so a model can keep adapting online under shifting power budgets, fault conditions and input distributions. It targets long-running deployments such as autonomous systems, industrial monitoring and satellite onboard intelligence where static fault-tolerance assumptions break down.

entry.title: Decentralized Optimal Equilibrium Learning Over Dynamic Networks

author.name: Seref Taha Kiremitci, Muhammed O. Sayin

entry.summary: This paper studies decentralized learning of socially optimal equilibria in finite normal-form games over time-varying communication networks, where each agent knows only its realized payoffs and exchanges low-bandwidth messages with neighbors. Agents generate randomized semantic content/discontent signals from local payoff comparisons and exchange time-stamped stacked tables rather than raw actions or estimates, with table fusion and temporal majority reconstruction handling dynamic topology.

entry.title: SAiFE-gym: Model-based Environments for Automated Market Making with Concentrated Liquidity

author.name: Georgios Chionas, Charalampos Kleitsikas, Stefanos Leonardos, Leandro S\'anchez-Betancourt, Carmine Ventre

entry.summary: The authors present SAiFE_gym, a Python module of simulation environments for trading in constant product markets with concentrated liquidity. The environments decompose market microstructure into interactive components and use vectorized computation to support scalable, high-dimensional reinforcement learning workflows.

entry.title: Adaptive hybrid coupling with operator inference, the overlapping Schwarz alternating method and reinforcement learning

author.name: Trishit Mondal, Irina Tezaur, Anthony Gruber

entry.summary: This work introduces a reinforcement-learning approach for online adaptation of hybrid full-order/reduced-order models coupled through the overlapping Schwarz alternating method. A deep Q-network decides when and where to switch subdomains to high-fidelity resolution, targeting transient problems where localized features move through the domain.

entry.title: Lexara-RF: Reference-Free Metrics for Evaluating Conversational Visual Analytics Agents

author.name: Srishti Palani, Vidya Setlur

entry.summary: Lexara-RF is a reference-free evaluation approach for conversational visual analytics agents, scoring multimodal outputs using only the prompt, data, and model response. It recasts evaluation as verification with thirteen metrics grounded in visualization design theory and Gricean cooperative principles, covering consistency, intent alignment, and design validity.

entry.title: CPR: Combining global composing, local performing and full-sequence refining in piano rendering with continuous autoregressive modelling

author.name: Chong Jing, Junan Zhang, Zhizheng Wu

entry.summary: CPR addresses prompt-conditioned piano MIDI-to-audio rendering, aiming to render target notes while matching a reference recording's timbre. It combines discrete autoregressive modeling's causal structure with continuous autoregressive representation learning and full-sequence refinement, avoiding both quantization loss and the cost of flow-matching attention. The contribution is a hybrid generation pipeline for expressive music synthesis.

entry.title: I code or AI code: A comparative evaluation of AI-rated scores in classroom observations

author.name: Y. Fong, J. Xiang, T. Y. D. Chan, K. Lee, E. Y. H. Lau

entry.summary: The study tests whether an LLM (GPT-5) can score teacher-child interactions in early childhood classrooms using the CLASS framework, benchmarking against trained human raters on 87 video-recorded observations from 38 classrooms across 30 Hong Kong kindergartens. It compares correlations and mean differences between AI and human domain scores. It matters for the feasibility of scaling educational quality assessment with AI.

entry.title: CoRe-MARL: Cooperative Redistribution Under Unknown Dynamics Using Recurrent Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Naimur Rahman Chowdhury, Shatabdi Sen Prapti, Md. Salehin Seyam, Limon Bin Hossain

entry.summary: CoRe-MARL formulates relief-supply redistribution among decentralized local centers as a decentralized partially observable Markov decision process and trains agents with recurrent multi-agent reinforcement learning under uncertain demand, supply, and disrupted transportation. Each center acts independently with limited information, so the framework is designed to reduce supply imbalances without central coordination. It matters for emergency management, where inconsistent local availability of supplies has direct humanitarian consequences.

entry.title: GrainSpeech: Less Context, More Detail for Compact Speech Synthesis

author.name: Zitao Liang, Chang Gao

entry.summary: This work studies two levers for compact text-to-speech acoustic models: how much encoder context is needed and how Mel-spectrogram supervision is formulated. A receptive-field study finds no consistent pitch, energy, or duration gains beyond roughly fifteen phonemes of self-attention context, motivating a fixed-receptive-field convolutional encoder that cuts those prediction errors by 36.0, 17.3, and 3.4 percent respectively. It also shows that naively importing image-domain gradient-variance supervision restores fine detail but harms predicted quality, prompting a Mel-specific variant.

entry.title: StableEval Arena: A Cost-Aware Agentic Benchmark for Stablecoin Price Stability Prediction

author.name: Sean Wan, Dongping Liu, Luyao Zhang

entry.summary: StableEval Arena is a cost-aware benchmark for evaluating LLM-backed agentic systems on stablecoin peg-risk prediction, asking them to diagnose peg stress and forecast deviations from the one-dollar peg over a hidden seven-day horizon using leakage-safe historical replay of exchange price-volume data. It reports a 120-case stress-enriched validation block and a 507-case natural-distribution arena block across six LLM agent configurations. Beyond prediction quality, it measures calibrated labels, structured-output reliability, latency, token consumption, and estimated cost.

entry.title: When the Gradient Sees Rank: Provable Necessity, Causal Recruitment, and Composition in Trained Matrix Memories

author.name: Samuel Larson

entry.summary: This paper asks whether gradient-based training can learn the rank needed to store and compose associations in a matrix memory, testing matrix memories on fresh key-value bindings whose exact linear recovery requires rank Z of at least K. A fixed linear readout queries a single matrix state without access to the original bindings, and recovery is measured by cosine similarity above 0.9. Learned effective rank rises with K, and training-time rank caps produce a recovery transition near k equals K, supporting provable necessity and causal recruitment claims.

entry.title: Composite-Gradient Learning for Shared Control Authority Between Deep Reinforcement Learning and Model Predictive Control

author.name: Giray \"On\"ur, Azita Dabiri, Bart De Schutter

entry.summary: This paper proposes composite-gradient learning (CGL) for settings in which a deep reinforcement learning agent and a model predictive control controller each determine part of the control input. Standard formulations treat the MPC controller as part of the environment, so they do not explicitly account for its contribution to control or its interaction with the learning agent. CGL instead integrates the two by propagating gradient information across both components to improve learning under shared control authority.

entry.title: Symmetry without a manifold: intrinsic dimension on orbits

author.name: Chon-Fai Kam, Miloud Bessafi, Fr\'ed\'eric Cadet

entry.summary: This paper examines the geometric derivation of neural scaling exponents, which normally takes the intrinsic dimension of a data manifold as input, and shows that this input is undefined for modular addition in Z_p. There, the exact algebraic solution is an orbit of Z_p acting by isometries, and transitivity makes the ratio statistic underlying the standard dimension estimator a point mass, with the two nearest-neighbor distances coinciding exactly. Breaking the symmetry at scale epsilon returns a number, but one that only tracks one over epsilon with no scale-free plateau, suggesting the failure is general for finite orbits of isometry groups.

entry.title: F-DACE: Fuzzy Disagreement-Aware Causal Evidence Fusion for Abstention-Safe Conversational Retail Decision Support

author.name: Sourish Dey

entry.summary: F-DACE sits on top of a causal estimation engine that identifies a conditional average treatment effect via backdoor adjustment, estimates it with an EconML causal forest and DoWhy linear regression, and checks it with two-way fixed effects before converting estimates into candidate levers. The decision layer represents precision, propensity overlap, placebo-refutation stability, interval overlap, and directional agreement as fuzzy memberships, with hard vetoes forcing abstention when diagnostics fail or signs conflict. It argues that systems should abstain rather than surface one causal estimate when plausible estimators disagree.

entry.title: ReDIL-GNN: Resynthesis Domain Incremental Learning for Circuit Graph Neural Networks

author.name: Rupesh Raj Karn, Johann Knechtel, Ozgur Sinanoglu

entry.summary: This paper introduces a domain-incremental learning framework for circuit graph neural networks facing domain shift from logic resynthesis, where circuit structure changes but task labels do not. It proposes a Resynthesis Adaptability Index that scores whether a shift is worth adapting to, and evaluates retention across previously seen domains in hardware-security tasks. It matters for EDA and hardware security, where models must stay useful across evolving synthesis toolchains.

entry.title: The Unbearable Weight: Scaling Models and Methods for UAV Audio Classification

author.name: Andrew P. Berg, Qian Zhang, Mia Y. Wang

entry.summary: This paper systematically varies model size and fine-tuning strategy for classifying drones from audio, using a custom dataset of 3,100 clips across 31 drone classes. It asks when the heavy approach of fully fine-tuning large pretrained networks is justified versus when lighter parameter-efficient alternatives suffice for resource-constrained edge deployment. The practical takeaway concerns tradeoffs between accuracy, memory, and retraining speed for emerging UAV platforms.

entry.title: Behavior2Value: Benchmarking and Empowering LLMs for Consumer Value Measurement from E-commerce Behaviors

author.name: Peixuan Hou, Bin Chen, Li He, Jian Xu, Bo Zheng, Xiuli Ma, Guojie Song

entry.summary: The authors define the Behavior-to-Value task of inferring consumer value orientations from e-commerce behavioral trajectories, introducing the E-commerce Consumption Value Taxonomy and B2V-Bench, claimed as the first dataset and benchmark for this task built on anonymized behavioral data. They benchmark large language models on the task and propose methods to improve their value measurement capability. It matters as an attempt to model stable motivational drivers of purchasing rather than short-term interests.

entry.title: Toward Composable Network Digital Twins: A Subgraph-Based Latency Prediction Study

author.name: Shenjia Ding, David Flynn, Paul Harvey

entry.summary: The paper proposes a composable network digital twin approach that decomposes networks into subgraphs represented by reusable unit twins capturing structure, configuration, and traffic behavior, with a lightweight composer aggregating them to predict per-route performance. This contrasts with monolithic whole-topology ML twins that are not reusable under topology or traffic changes. It targets fast what-if performance estimation in dynamic networks.

entry.title: Legal LLM Hallucination Should Be Evaluated as Failure of Legal Warrant

author.name: Maksym Taranukhin, Vered Shwartz

entry.summary: This position paper argues that legal LLM hallucinations should be judged as failures of legal warrant rather than mere factual inaccuracy or citation error. It defines claim-authority warrant as a context-sensitive relation requiring the cited authority to exist, apply to the jurisdiction, be current, carry the represented legal status, and actually support the claim. The authors predict that warrant-based metrics will expose failures that answer accuracy and citation-existence checks miss.

entry.title: LocQE: Principled Domain Adaptation for Localisation Quality Estimation by Leveraging Post-Edits

author.name: Kathy H\"ammerl, Gabriel Bretschner, Joern Wuebker

entry.summary: This paper shows that learned quality estimation models like COMETKiwi struggle on unseen localisation domains and are insensitive to factors such as number accuracy and spacing/punctuation preservation. It proposes a principled domain adaptation approach that leverages post-edit data to improve ranking of translations and localisation quality estimation.

entry.title: Beyond frequency measures: Can contextual embeddings capture meaning change in scientific texts?

author.name: Jianying Liu (STL, BETA, CEIPI), Kim Gerdes (LISN, Qatent, STL), Jean-Marc Deltorn (CEIPI)

entry.summary: This study tests whether contextual embeddings can complement frequency-based methods for tracking diachronic semantic change in scientific terminology. Using Astrophysics and NLP corpora from 2010 to 2024, it extracts candidate terms with KeyBERT/SciBERT, filters by frequency increase, and validates embedding-based drift against expert-labeled ground truth.

entry.title: PersonaPath: Towards Knowledge-Centric Personalized Learning Path Planning

author.name: Yu Liu, Zeming Liu, Tianle Zhang, Zihao Cheng, Yuhang Guo, Kehai Chen, Min Zhang, Yunhong Wang, Haifeng Wang

entry.summary: This paper reformulates learning path planning from exercise-centric recommendation to knowledge-centric planning, where a planner reasons over learner profiles, mastery states, and prerequisite knowledge structures. It introduces PersonaPath, a benchmark pairing 2,000 fine-grained learner personas with a hierarchical curriculum structure.

entry.title: G-Mamba: Sparse Graph-Guided Mamba for Audio-Visual Speech Enhancement

author.name: Guo-Ruei Tseng, Hung-Shin Lee, Hsin-Min Wang, Berlin Chen

entry.summary: The paper addresses the trade-off between efficiency and cross-modal alignment in lightweight audio-visual speech enhancement, arguing concatenation is inexpressive while dense cross-attention is costly and fragile under strong interference. It proposes SG-Mamba, which couples a sparse heterogeneous graph with content-adaptive attention and cross-frame audio-visual links to a linear-complexity Mamba backbone capturing long-range temporal context.

entry.title: Divide and Conquer: Mixture-of-Bottleneck Experts in Informative Ordinal Space for Video-based Multimodal Sentiment Analysis

author.name: Ronghao Lin, Qiaolin He, Zefeng Lu, Yichu Liu, Li Huang, Sijie Mai, Haifeng Hu, Yap-peng Tan

entry.summary: The paper reformulates video-based multimodal sentiment analysis as an ordinal regression problem, decoupling polarity recognition from intensity prediction, and notes that most models ignore the ordinal nature of sentiment. It introduces a Mixture-of-Bottleneck framework, motivated by information theory, that assigns distinct latents to polarity- and intensity-specific cues for better multimodal fusion.

entry.title: JewelTry: Mask-Free Scale Aware Jewelry Virtual Try-On

author.name: Xinlei Niu, Peixia Li, Jun Wang, Chenchen Xu, Jiayu Yang, Jing Zhang, Pulak Purkait, Hongdong Li

entry.summary: JewelTry tackles jewelry virtual try-on, an underexplored category because jewelry is small, rigid and sensitive to fine detail, and realistic results require both faithful appearance transfer and correct scale and placement on the wearer. The authors introduce JVTO-Bench, a benchmark for scale-faithful jewelry try-on with reference data, and a mask-free scale-aware method. It matters for e-commerce applications where existing garment VTON techniques do not transfer well.

entry.title: De-GAN - Dynamic Parameter Tuned GAN for 3D Medical Image Segmentation: A Step Towards Generalisation

author.name: Zoha Usama, Azadeh Alavi

entry.summary: DE-GAN is a contrast-enhancing conditional GAN that uses input-adaptive dynamic convolutions, style-aware feature mixing, and coordinate encoding to synthesize slice-adaptive FLAIR images. A label-guided conditional target separates tumor core and enhancing tumor intensities while preserving anatomy, and the synthetic FLAIR is concatenated with original modalities for a 3D U-Net. Evaluated across BraTS 2015, 2018, and 2019, it improves segmentation over baselines, especially on the low-contrast enhancing tumor class.

entry.title: Det-LIME: Detector-Aware, Multi-Instance Local Interpretable Model-Agnostic Explanations for Automated Marine Mammal Detection

author.name: Jiayi Zhou, David W. Johnston, Brinnae Bent

entry.summary: Det-LIME adapts LIME to object detection by producing detector-aware, multi-instance explanations that account for multiple animals detected in a single scene, addressing the failure of classification-oriented explainability tools on colonial or social species imagery. The authors frame it around conservation workflows, arguing current explanations are low-resolution and biologically irrelevant, limiting debugging and targeted data collection.

entry.title: Human-Centric Grasp State Assessment: Toward Transferring Subjective Evaluation to Robots

author.name: Ryohei Kobayashi, Kosei Isomoto, Yuga Yano, Yuichiro Tanaka, Hakaru Tamukoh

entry.summary: The paper proposes a framework that transfers tacit human subjective criteria for grasping deformable objects to robotic systems, combining a vision-language-model-based semi-automated supervisor with a lightweight grasp-state predictor. Minimal human-annotated trials serve as contextual anchors that propagate subjective criteria to unannotated data, avoiding prohibitive annotation costs for each new object.

entry.title: Real-Time Service Robot Replanning via Simple Button Interaction for Improved Task Success and User Experience

author.name: Ryo Terashima, Yuga Yano, Koshun Arimura, Hakaru Tamukoh

entry.summary: This paper proposes a real-time human-in-the-loop feedback function that lets users press a single tablet button when a service robot acts incorrectly, prompting the robot to reinterpret the failure and replan. Experiments compare task performance and user experience with and without the feedback mechanism to test whether such minimal interaction avoids degrading the user experience. It matters as a lightweight, low-burden interface for recovering from robot failures in real deployments.

entry.title: Toward 3D Printable Non-Planar Electroadhesive Structures for Active Anchoring

author.name: Mostafa A. Atalla, Carol R. Derla, Pep Canyelles Peric\`as, Gijs Krijnen

entry.summary: This paper investigates multi-material 3D printing of non-planar electroadhesive structures with printed conductive interdigitated electrode patterns. It reports normal-force measurements for flat pads (about 0.11-0.13 N at 3 kV) and cylindrical pads (about 0.16 N at 5 N preload), showing voltage-controlled adhesion modulation in both geometries. The results are an early step toward printed parts with built-in electrically controlled adhesion and friction.

entry.title: HAP: A Hand-Driven Active Perception Framework for Egocentric Head Motion Prediction

author.name: Yunji Feng, Junyi Ma, Guanzhong Sun, Chenyang Xu, Hesheng Wang

entry.summary: HAP formulates 6-DoF head motion prediction conditioned on observed hand motion and inferred target context, addressing the neglected problem of egocentric head-motion forecasting during manipulation. It infers per-object target confidence from hand motion and geometry, then builds a dynamic Predictive Target-Centric Amodal Occlusion Graph to model current and potential occlusions among candidate objects. This supports applications like AR/VR, teleoperation, and predictive perception for assistive systems.

entry.title: Random tilts to find stationary points in stochastic convex optimization

author.name: Felipe Areces, John C. Duchi, Malo Sommers

entry.summary: This paper addresses finding stationary points of stochastic convex functions and related variational inequalities, showing that regularized empirical risk minimization with a random tilting perturbation attains a stationarity residual of order sqrt(d/n) in d dimensions with n observations. It also gives minimax lower bounds scaling as sqrt(log d / n), establishing that some dimension dependence is unavoidable in this setting. The result sharpens understanding of what stationarity guarantees are achievable statistically.

entry.title: Multimodal Conditioning of Fine-Tuned Stable Diffusion XL for Controllable and Culturally Faithful Ulos Motif Generation

author.name: Humasak Simanjuntak, Tamara Yunika Sianipar, Bronson T. M Siallagan, Difya Laurensya Ambarita, Arlinta Barus

entry.summary: This work builds a multimodal generative framework that combines a LoRA fine-tuned Stable Diffusion XL with a multimodal large language model to generate Batak Ulos weaving motifs that are controllable and culturally faithful. Four conditioning mechanisms (text, image, representation, and a ControlNet semantic map) each govern a different aspect of generation, from semantic intent to spatial layout, and the design is evaluated through a five-level ablation across shape transformation, color variation and related scenarios.
