The work provides a cognitive-science-grounded diagnostic for evaluating reasoning models beyond aggregate accuracy.

entry.title: The Misery of Mechanistic Interpretability: A Formal Perspective

author.name: Tobias Ladner, Matthias Althoff

entry.summary: The authors show that semantically minor input perturbations flip the dominant features of interpretable replacement networks across five open-weight model families including GPT-2 small, Gemma, Llama 3.2 1B, and R1-Distill-Qwen 1.5B. They then propose the first formal verification framework for assessing the faithfulness of such interpretability surrogates, rather than relying on empirical evaluation on clean data.

entry.title: How I learned to stop worrying and love StopGrads: Stationarity, Convergence, and a case study on Flow Map Learning

author.name: Max W. Shen, Mark Goldstein, Zichu Wang, Aahlad Puli, Rajesh Ranganath

entry.summary: This paper gives theoretical grounding to stop-gradient training, introducing a stopgrad regression principle that characterizes stationary points and their uniqueness for a broad family of stopgrad objectives spanning flow maps, reinforcement learning, and diffusion samplers. The authors prove that the unique stationary point of a stopgrad flow-map objective is the true flow map and establish convergence results for Eulerian and Lagrangian variants, including MeanFlow. It matters because stopgrads are ubiquitous in practice yet alter gradients, stationary points, and convergence guarantees of the underlying objective.

entry.title: On the Importance of Gating: Memorization vs. In-Context Learning in State Space Models

author.name: William L. Tong, Aryo Lotfi, Emmanuel Abbe, Kostas Vaggelakos, Vishnu Banna, Etai Littwin, Josh Susskind, Cengiz Pehlevan, Eran Malach

entry.summary: State-space models offer constant memory and linear compute but still trail transformers on in-context learning and precise retrieval. Through theory and experiments, the authors trace both the strengths and failures of SSMs to the gating mechanism in modern recurrent networks, showing gating induces an early in-weights memorization solution that can block in-context solutions. The paper helps explain a key capability gap between architectures and points at design levers to close it.

entry.title: Memorisation bias in medical AI

author.name: Moritz A. Knolle, Martin J. Menten, Laurin Lux, M\'elanie Roschewitz, Emma A. M. Stanley, Georgios Kaissis, Daniel Rueckert, Ben Glocker

entry.summary: The paper shows that medical AI models can change predictions on a patient's unseen future data if the same patient's anonymised historical data was in training, a phenomenon termed memorisation bias. It demonstrates the bias across diverse data modalities, model architectures, and prolonged time spans, arguing that privacy-focused memorisation research misses these clinical deployment consequences.

entry.title: Latent Undertow: How Ordinary Typos Break Probes

author.name: Elad David, Max Fomin, Amit LeVi

entry.summary: This paper shows that ordinary typos and punctuation errors substantially perturb hidden-state based probes for detecting malicious prompts, rotating the readout vector sharply at the perturbed token and degrading injection-detection true positive rates. It analyzes multi-position aggregation and introduces a KV-cache-based approach for single-position probes.

entry.title: The AI-Enabled Scientific Frontier

author.name: Gabriel Manso, Emma Fu, Neil Thompson

entry.summary: The authors assemble 2,507 head-to-head comparisons between AI methods and other scientific analysis techniques across 27 disciplines from papers published between 2000 and early 2025. They report a stark split: AI frequently beats traditional statistics but at much higher compute cost, and roughly a quarter of cases see AI both costing more and performing worse, a fraction that has stayed stable for a decade. It matters as a large-scale empirical check on claims that AI is becoming a universal scientific method.

entry.title: Where Should a Document Live: Context, Representations, or Parameters?

author.name: Nathana\"el Carraz Rakotonirina, Momchil Hardalov, Gonzalo Iglesias, Adri\`a de Gispert

entry.summary: The paper presents a controlled comparison of representation-based KV-cache adaptation (Cartridges) versus parametric fine-tuning for injecting new knowledge into LLMs across five knowledge-intensive benchmarks. In the oracle setting, KV-based Cartridges are the most accurate injection method at nearly every storage budget, beating parametric methods by about 10 points, though compaction only matches Cartridges under certain conditions. It offers practical guidance on the efficiency, cost, and accuracy trade-offs of where to put new documents.

entry.title: Reasoning with Image Generation

author.name: Nishad Singhi, Hector Garcia Rodriguez, Aditya Arora, Marcus Rohrbach, Anna Rohrbach

entry.summary: The paper argues that textual chain-of-thought is limiting for tasks needing visual manipulation, and that existing external visual tools such as depth estimation or detection are too rigid. It proposes ReImaGin, which uses image generation models as a flexible visual reasoning mechanism inside a multimodal LLM, accepting natural-language operations instead of fixed functions. This matters as a step toward generative models serving as general-purpose reasoning operators.

entry.title: Occupancy Network-Guided Autonomous Robotic Partial Nephrectomy

author.name: Ethan Kilmer, Pit Henrich, Jiawei Ge, Paul M. Scheikl, Laura Connolly, Soum D. Lokeshwar, Joseph Chen, Justin D. Opfermann, Kaitlyn Kumar, Lauren Shepard, Ahmed Ghazi, Nirmish Singla, Richard J. Cha, Kevin Cleary, Franziska Mathis-Ullrich, Axel Krieger

entry.summary: This work introduces a vision-guided autonomous system able to perform complete tumor resections for partial nephrectomy, extending autonomous soft-tissue surgery beyond organ-surface interventions. Conditional occupancy networks trained entirely in physics-based simulation infer full 3D anatomy (tumor, margin tissue, kidney) from single-view partial point clouds and maintain tracking while tissue is cut and deformed, enabling adaptive planning. The platform couples a depth camera with dual robotic arms and was developed by a leading surgical robotics group (Johns Hopkins and collaborators).

entry.title: Estimating Uncertain Spatial Relationships in Robotics

author.name: Randall Smith, Matthew Self, Peter Cheeseman

entry.summary: This classic work introduces the stochastic map, a probabilistic representation of spatial relationships among objects along with their uncertainties, together with procedures for building, querying, and incrementally revising it. It replaces conservative worst-case geometric reasoning with fully probabilistic state estimation grounded in filtering theory. Its lasting importance is that it underpins much of modern probabilistic robotics and SLAM.

entry.title: Persistent Recurrent Memory Between Transformer Layers - Improves Language Model Generalization

author.name: Eduardo Novaes Hering

entry.summary: The paper adds a persistent recurrent state between the lower and upper halves of a six-layer decoder-only transformer: the state observes hidden representations via cross-attention, updates through a GRU, and modulates later processing by gated addition. Adding only 3.7 percent more parameters, it cuts evaluation loss from 2.438 to 1.743, a 28.5 percent reduction, with a much smaller generalization gap.

entry.title: Generalization Can Emerge in Tabular Foundation Models From a Single Table

author.name: Junwei Ma, Nour Shaheen, Alex Labach, Amine Mhedhbi, Frank Hutter, Anthony L. Caterini, Valentin Thomas

entry.summary: The paper challenges the belief that broad in-context generalization for tabular foundation models requires pretraining on large synthetic corpora like TabPFN priors or large collections of real data like TabDPT. It finds that simple self-supervised pretraining on a single real table can produce strong transfer across heterogeneous benchmarks, and systematically varies pretraining and evaluation datasets to identify which data properties drive that transfer. The result reframes what tabular foundation models actually need to generalize.

entry.title: Is Bash All You Need? An Empirical Study of Tool Interfaces for Enterprise Digital Worker Agents

author.name: Hazel Mak, Susheel Suresh, Sahil Bhatnagar, Barry Wang, Chhaya Methani, Alejandro Gutierrez Munoz

entry.summary: The authors benchmark five agent tool interfaces, from typed tools to bash alone to programmatic tool calling, on TheAgentCompany and APEX-Agents using established frontier models. Plain bash outperforms typed tools by roughly 22 to 25 points on one benchmark and 5 to 7 points on the other while using fewer tokens, with persistent agent-synthesized tools and PTC also explored. It matters because it challenges the default assumption that carefully typed tool schemas are the right abstraction for enterprise agents.

entry.title: Follow the Geometry, Not the Model: Cold Start Semi-Supervised Learning

author.name: Itai David, Daphna Weinshall

entry.summary: VAST (Veracity-Aware Semi-Supervised Training) decouples pseudo-label generation from classifier training, which the authors argue is ill-posed in the cold-start regime with only a few labels per class. Probabilistic beliefs over unlabeled data are inferred from the geometry of a frozen self-supervised embedding via a kernel-based Veracity Matrix, then distilled into an inductive classifier.

entry.title: Refusal Reads Only a Slice of What the Model Knows: Harm-Keyed Routing and Its Exceptions Across Model Families

author.name: Orion Reblitz-Richardson

entry.summary: Across four open-weight models from three families, this paper argues that moral comprehension is native to pretraining, with a low-rank moral subspace crystallizing before alignment merely rotates it once, while the refusal gate is a fresh post-training construction with only a weak pretraining precursor. The authors show refusal behavior is written into a narrow control-token channel and can be edited out along a single residual-stream direction, separating what the model comprehends from what the refusal decision actually reads. It matters for understanding how shallow post-training alignment really is.

entry.title: LLMs as Oracles: Reliance on LLMs for Subjective Personal Questions

author.name: Myra Cheng, Lujain Ibrahim, Grace Liu, Michelle S. Lam, Vishakh Padmakumar, Nick Madibekov, Diyi Yang, Dan Jurafsky

entry.summary: The authors develop a typology and LLM-based measurement methods for LLM-as-oracle use, where people treat models as all-knowing authorities on subjective personal questions. Applying it to 68K public prompts from WildChat and ThoughtTrace, they find such use rising from 2023 to 2026 and more prevalent among younger users, and a privacy-preserving donation tool analyzing 140K prompts from 52 participants shows similar patterns plus limited user awareness of their own reliance. It matters for debates about autonomy, judgment offloading, and well-being risks.

entry.title: Decoy Direction Optimization: A Post-Hoc Defense Against LLM Abliteration

author.name: Aashiq Muhamed, Mona T. Diab, Virginia Smith

entry.summary: The paper introduces Decoy Direction Optimization, a fast post-hoc weight-editing defense against refusal-feature ablation attacks that project out a refusal direction from the residual stream of open-weight models. Rather than hiding the true refusal circuitry, the method injects decoy directions that mislead the contrastive estimators attackers rely on, avoiding costly safety fine-tuning per checkpoint. It matters because abliteration can strip safety behavior from open-weight models at scale while preserving capability.

entry.title: Nonsmooth Optimization via Orthogonalized Momentum

author.name: Lexiao Lai, Tianyi Lin, Jiayu Zhang

entry.summary: This theory paper studies whether Muon-style momentum orthogonalization remains effective beyond smooth optimization, analyzing locally Lipschitz objectives via a generalized derivative framework compatible with backpropagation. It identifies a limitation: for any fixed momentum factor, Muon can fail to approach the global optimum of a convex Lipschitz objective from almost every initialization.

entry.title: Are We Grading Properly? Understanding Failure Modes in Medical Benchmarks

author.name: Prithvi Dixit, Pedram Hosseini

entry.summary: This paper applies the RIFT rubric failure taxonomy to two clinical benchmarks, HealthBench Professional and LiveMedBench, finding that an LLM judge flags 29.6% of criteria as non-atomic and 65.4% as misaligned or rigid. It demonstrates that such rubric flaws are consequential rather than cosmetic, for example by showing how rewriting bundled criteria changes outcomes.

entry.title: Vulnerability Localization Benchmark: Measuring Agentic Security Analysis at Repository Scale

author.name: Aman Priyanshu, Supriti Vijay, Kimia Majd, Xuhong He, Fraser Burch, Takahiro Matsumoto, Jianliang He, Baturay Saglam, Arthur Goldblatt, Zhuoran Yang, Amin Karbasi

entry.summary: VLoc Bench contains 500 real-world vulnerabilities from 290 repositories across six package ecosystems and 147 CWE categories, pairing repository snapshots immediately before and after a security fix. Agents receive only a CWE description and read-only repository access and must identify the implementation files associated with the weakness. This shifts agentic security evaluation from detection, reproduction, and repair toward code localization at repository scale.

entry.title: Test-Time Unlearning via Sparse Autoencoder

author.name: Pingzhi Li, Jinhao Duan, Vaishnav Tadiparthi, Nakul Agarwal, Kwonjoon Lee, Ehsan Moradi Pari, Hossein Nourkhiz Mahjoub, Sijia Liu, Tianlong Chen

entry.summary: The authors propose ARIA, an inference-time unlearning method that leaves model weights untouched and instead uses sparse autoencoder latents to train a gate that blocks access to unwanted knowledge only when generation enters a forget-related state. This is positioned against weight-editing unlearning approaches based on gradient ascent, which suffer a sharp forget-versus-utility tradeoff and can have forgotten knowledge resurface after fine-tuning or prompt attacks. It matters because it reframes unlearning as a controllable inference-time mechanism rather than an irreversible weight modification.

entry.title: OPEN-1B: A Fully Auditable Training Run

author.name: John Donaghy, Brian Wilcox, O\u{g}uzhan Ersoy, Shikhar Rastogi, Adam St Arnaud, Alexey Titov, Jordan Greenberg, Ben Fielding, Harry Grieve

entry.summary: The paper argues that open-source language models are not provably reproducible because floating-point non-associativity breaks cross-hardware determinism, leaving room for undisclosed data, biases, or backdoors. It introduces a new transparency tier, fully auditable, illustrated with the OPEN-1B training run, so that a released checkpoint can be verified as produced by the declared recipe.

entry.title: Constant Swap Regret in General-Sum Games via Optimistic Transition Matrices

author.name: Tung Mai

entry.summary: The paper gives deterministic, uncoupled learning dynamics for finite multiplayer general-sum games under full-information feedback that achieve constant individual swap regret independent of the horizon. Each player predicts deviation gains and uses them to update a row-stochastic transition matrix, playing its stationary distribution. The proof combines a potential argument with two-scale higher-order prediction analysis using rooted-tree representations.

entry.title: A Vision-Language Foundation Model for Precise and Comprehensive Brain Tumor Diagnosis from Preoperative Multimodal Data

author.name: Yinong Wang (Joyce), Jianwen Chen (Joyce), Zhou Chen (Joyce), Shuwen Kuang (Joyce), Haoning Jiang (Joyce), Yanzhao Shi (Joyce), Huichun Yuan (Joyce), Yan-ran (Joyce), Wang, Bing Wang, Lei Wu, Bin Tang, Li Meng, Baihua Luo, Bin Zhou, Wei Ding, Weiming Zhong, Wei Hou, Yuanbing Chen, Zhiping Wan, Wei Wang, Zhenkun Xiao, Wenwu Wan, Allen He, Yuyin Zhou, Longbo Zhang, Feifei Wang, Zhixiong Liu, Michael Iv, Xuan Gong, Liangqiong Qu

entry.summary: BrainVLM is an MRI-based vision-language model that classifies all 12 WHO 2021 brain tumor types while providing uncertainty quantification to flag unreliable predictions and generating radiology reports to explain its reasoning. It is developed for non-invasive preoperative diagnosis, where overlapping imaging features and inter-observer variability make expert diagnosis hard. The work matters because it pairs classification breadth with the reliability signaling and interpretability that clinical deployment requires.

entry.title: PhysStream: Streaming Physics-Grounded Video Generation with Structured Scene Memory and Fine-Grained Motion Control

author.name: Chuhao Chen, Peter Wonka, Chaoyang Wang, Chen Wang, Qiao Feng, Sergey Tulyakov, Lingjie Liu

entry.summary: PhysStream is an autoregressive image-to-video model that maintains structured scene memory, in the form of positional and object tracking maps derived online from previously generated frames, enabling streaming generation with persistent scene state. Control is exerted through sparse velocity-increment signals that encode physical quantities rather than pixel-space position targets, so the model learns underlying dynamics. The author list includes well-known figures in generative graphics and video (Wonka, Tulyakov, Lingjie Liu), and the work pushes interactive video generation toward physically meaningful manipulation.

entry.title: Overflip: Repetition-Induced Label Flips in Guardrail Models

author.name: Xu He, Chih-Hsuan Lin, Hung-Mao Chen, Junjie Xiong, Yan Zhai, Kun Sun

entry.summary: The authors identify Overflip, an instability in which repeating a prompt causes lightweight guardrail classifiers to flip from malicious to benign as the sequence grows. Experiments on nine widely used compact guardrails show five exhibit these flips, undermining the common assumption that guardrail decisions are stable under input lengthening.

entry.title: The Attribution-Compression Frontier in Retrieval-Augmented Generation

author.name: Deepanshu Mody

entry.summary: This paper measures how context compression methods affect citation attribution in RAG, comparing reranking, extractive selection, abstractive summarization, token pruning, and an extract-cluster-rewrite approach on ASQA and QASPER under a fixed generator. It shows systematically that compressors can produce high citation precision against their own summaries yet very low attribution against source spans, exposing a hidden faithfulness gap.

entry.title: Calibrating Interpretability Instruments Before Trusting Their Verdicts

author.name: Orion Reblitz-Richardson

entry.summary: This note documents six specific, diagnosable failure modes of interpretability measurements used to make causal claims about LLM internals, such as covariance-matched nulls that saturate, per-head attributions that overshoot true residual writes on reordered-normalization architectures, and sign-chaotic interchange patches pinned at a ceiling. The argument is that broken instruments often return plausible numbers rather than errors, so they read as findings. It matters as a methodological warning for a field that increasingly draws causal conclusions from single measurement types.

entry.title: One Example Is Enough to Pass Fairness Benchmarks: Rethinking Fairness Evaluation for Aligned LLMs

author.name: Naihao Deng, Samee Arif, Shuaichen Chang, Yulong Chen, Rada Mihalcea

entry.summary: The authors show that fairness benchmarks like BBQ are far too easy: training Qwen 2.5 7B Base with GRPO on a single BBQ example, or using that example as a one-shot demonstration, lifts mean accuracy from 79.9 percent to 92.9 percent and 99.0 percent respectively, closing most of the gap to a large-scale RLHF counterpart and even surpassing it with in-context learning. The effects generalize across model families. It matters because it undermines the validity of widely used fairness metrics as evidence of genuine alignment.

entry.title: Clean Scores, Buried Evidence, and Confident Wrong: A Receipt-Based Audit of Frontier Agentic QA

author.name: Luis M. S\'anchez

entry.summary: This paper audits frontier agentic QA models in a controlled financial due-diligence data room, showing that burying evidence reduces accuracy, increases forced declarations and tool calls, and raises cost per correct answer. It argues benchmark confidence and calibration do not catch wrong answers, and proposes claim-level provenance receipts and condition-aware scoring instead of answer-level leaderboards.

entry.title: Anatomy of Associative Recall in Fixed-State Recurrences: A Matched-State Decomposition, an Interference Wall, and a Curriculum That Breaks It

author.name: Julian Boesch, Andrew Wee

entry.summary: The authors decompose masked multi-query associative recall in fixed-state recurrences (linear attention and state-space models) along three isolated axes: short causal convolution, transition structure (rank-1 delta rule versus diagonal), and decay. They find that a short convolution dominates performance gains, that the rank-1 transition beats its diagonal ablation only until both cells carry the convolution, and they identify an interference wall that a curriculum can overcome. It matters because whole-architecture comparisons have obscured which specific ingredients cause recurrent models to lag attention on recall.

entry.title: TAME: Token Attribution and Masking for Emergent misalignment

author.name: Md Rayhanul Masud, Md Rizwan Parvez

entry.summary: Fine-tuning an aligned model on narrow flawed data can produce harmful behavior far outside the training domain, a phenomenon known as emergent misalignment, and prior work localized it in weights and activations but not at the token level. TAME is a three-stage framework that scores how much each response token's likelihood is raised by the fine-tuning update, characterizes patterns among high-attribution tokens, and causally validates them by attribution-guided loss masking. This gives a finer-grained handle on which training tokens drive misalignment.

entry.title: Computer-assisted global regularity across nonlinear families of three-dimensional periodic Navier-Stokes flows

author.name: Jose Luis Lima de Jesus Silva

entry.summary: This paper develops a computer-assisted framework establishing global regularity for continuous families of three-dimensional periodic Navier-Stokes flows, combining finite reference trajectories with a common error bound covering an interval of center fields and infinitely many perturbation modes. It retains the full nonlinear residual before spectral truncation and controls evolution until viscous decay guarantees regularity.

entry.title: Cascade: Hierarchical Recoverability Control for Large Language Model Unlearning

author.name: Qingchen Yu, Shiying Duan, Xiaodong Li, Yuhua Wang, Zhiyu Li, Shiji Zhou, Yifan Sun, Zhaoxin Fan

entry.summary: Cascade is an unlearning framework that targets residual knowledge left in intermediate representations, combining path-level routing to suppress privacy-associated activation routes, representation-level compression to reduce geometric separability, and decoding-level intervention to limit recovery. It is evaluated on TOFU, MUSE-News, and WMDP with robustness tests against query reformulation and extraction-style attacks.

entry.title: Universal Defenses for Tool-Integrated LLM Agents Against Adversarial Attacks

author.name: Xiaoyan Li, Yunli Wang

entry.summary: This paper explores generalizable defenses for tool-integrated LLM agents against four attack types: direct prompt injection, indirect prompt injection, memory poisoning, and backdoor attacks. It proposes two universal tool-based defenses, Attacker Tool Filtering using anomaly detection such as Isolation Forest to remove suspicious tools, and Normal Tool Re- something, within a unified framework. The work is notable for treating these disparate threat models under one defensive umbrella.

entry.title: World-Action Models for Robot Learning and Control: A Survey

author.name: Zuxing Lu, Hongjia Zhai, Guanzhi Wang, Huajian Zeng, Jiaqi Yang, Jingyu Liu, Lei Cheng, Yuantai Zhang, Yuheng Qiu, Zezhou Cheng, Ivan Laptev, Danfei Xu, Benjamin Riviere, Giuseppe Loianno, Eric Xing, Xingxing Zuo

entry.summary: This survey organizes the emerging area of World-Action Models, which couple future world prediction with executable action generation, and positions them relative to conventional world models, model-based reinforcement learning, action-conditioned video generation, and reactive vision-language-action policies. It argues that robots acting under partial observability and physical constraints must anticipate how candidate actions change future states rather than only mapping observations and language to actions. The author list includes senior robotics and learning researchers (Ivan Laptev, Danfei Xu, Eric Xing, Giuseppe Loianno, Xingxing Zuo).

entry.title: Modality-Autoregressive World-Action Models

author.name: Adam Hung, Bardienus P. Duisterhof, Deva Ramanan, Jeffrey Ichnowski

entry.summary: This paper introduces ModAR, a world-action model that autoregressively denoises multiple future visual modalities (such as depth, pretrained visual features, and point tracks) before predicting actions, so each prediction can condition on previously generated modalities. The authors train models from scratch and systematically ablate training-data mixtures, predicted modalities, and WAM formulations, finding that point-track prediction is especially beneficial. It matters because it clarifies how to best structure multimodal future prediction for robot policy learning.

entry.title: Generalized Agent Iteration: One Formal Framework for Iterative Policy Improvement and Recursive Self-Improvement

author.name: Hongyao Tang, Yi Ma, Pengyi Li, Yifu Yuan

entry.summary: The authors observe that recursive self-improvement is widely discussed but lacks a unifying formal account, while its classical analogue, iterative policy improvement, is well captured by generalized policy iteration. They propose Generalized Agent Iteration, a framework that treats iterative policy improvement and recursive self-improvement as two cases of a single learning paradigm with defined update and evaluation components.

entry.title: AGENTQ: Quantization-Conditioned Backdoor Attacks on LLM Agents

author.name: Xiaoqun Liu, Qiben Yan

entry.summary: This work studies quantization-conditioned attacks, where an adversary publishes a full-precision checkpoint that passes audits but behaves maliciously only after quantization. The authors present the first study of such attacks against LLM agents, where the triggered payload is an executable structured function rather than free text mediated by a human reader. They find naive backdoor-injection adaptations can produce malicious post-quantization behavior but heavily degrade benign utility, motivating more stealthy attack design.

entry.title: Has Scientific Talent Shifted from Depth to Breadth?Evidence across Papers, Knowledge Inputs, Careers, and Teams

author.name: Xiaoshn Nee, Haobo Zhong, Xiaomin Ni

entry.summary: Using 47,959 articles from six fields over 2010-2025, 51,736 resolved cited works, and reconstructed publication histories for 1,754 contributors, this study tests whether research is shifting from deep specialization toward broad individual knowledge under generative AI. It finds team size grew about 37% from 2010 to 2022 while paper topic breadth narrowed, with cited knowledge remaining stable to modestly broader.

entry.title: WaterKron and FlipFlop Hessian: Information-Theoretically Grounded Quantization with Kronecker-factored Hessians

author.name: Johann Birnick, Rayan Saab

entry.summary: The paper asks how to best choose a Kronecker-factored Hessian approximation for post-training quantization, proposing WaterKron, which combines two-sided GPTQ with row- and column-dependent waterfilling scales and entropy coding. The authors derive a high-rate distortion formula relative to the full Hessian with an explicit Kronecker-Hessian mismatch factor, whose minimization yields a Gaussian covariance-fitting problem with classical flip-flop updates. It matters because it supplies rate-distortion justification for a widely used practical quantization heuristic.

entry.title: Forty Shades of Blue: Quality-Diversity Alignment via Mode-Conditioned Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Jiayi Yuan, Hangoo Kang, James Jihao Liu, Yejin Choi, Vikram Iyer, Liwei Jiang, Natasha Jaques

entry.summary: The paper addresses mode collapse in LLM alignment, where alignment training progressively erodes output diversity and harms open-ended tasks like scientific ideation and creative writing. MoDA is an online post-training RL algorithm inspired by coordination in multi-agent RL that conditions a single shared policy on abstract numbered roles, each acting as an agent competing to produce outputs distinct from the others, jointly optimizing quality and diversity. It matters as a concrete recipe for quality-diversity alignment rather than a pure quality-maximizing objective.

entry.title: Delegating Authorization to Misaligned Agents: Coalitional Alignment and Safe Control

author.name: Natalie Collina, Surbhi Goel, Aaron Roth, Sikata Bela Sengupta

entry.summary: This paper studies the control problem for long-running agents where human review of every consequential action is the attention bottleneck, so review is delegated to AI reviewers that may themselves be misaligned. The authors identify a condition on a reviewing panel that is weaker than individual alignment yet necessary and sufficient to guarantee the principal performs at least as well in expectation as under a baseline policy. It provides a formal foundation for coalitional alignment and safe delegation of authorization.

entry.title: BLINDSPOT: A Benchmark for Safety and Refusal Calibration in Long-Horizon Tool-Using Agents

author.name: Sadia Asif, Mohammad Mohammadi Amiri, Momin Abbas, Tejaswini Pedapati, Prasanna Sattigeri

entry.summary: Blindspot is a benchmark that evaluates complete user-agent-environment trajectories for long-horizon tool-using agents through adaptive adversarial interaction, stateful tool execution, and execution-grounded adjudication. Instead of reducing behavior to task or attack success, it measures whether an agent acts, refuses, or stays appropriately calibrated as authorization and context evolve over many turns. It matters because most agent safety evaluations miss failures that only surface after multiple decision steps.

entry.title: PaperDoctor: Evidence-Grounded and Actionable Feedback for Scientific Papers in Progress

author.name: Kevin Qinghong Lin, Siyuan Hu, Pan Lu, Yu Chen, Yanzhe Chen, Owen Queen, Yupeng Chen, Jialin Yu, Junchi Yu, Zifeng Ding, Yuanfeng Ji, Sheng Liu, Jindong Gu, Linjie Li, Mike Zheng Shou, Philip Torr, James Zou

entry.summary: PaperDoctor is an agent framework that gives pre-submission feedback on scientific papers by diagnosing problems rather than merely judging them. It uses a three-layer hierarchy: surface screening, typed verifiers that route each claim to the appropriate evidence, and reproducers that rerun experiments by priority, covering writing, layout, references, code, theory, prior work, and experiments.

entry.title: Racing in Volume with Flow Ensembles

author.name: Saswat Subhajyoti Mallick, Riu Cherdchusakulchai, Marc Ruiz Olle, Albert Mosella-Montoro, Jose Ribeiro-Gomes, Francisco Vicente Carrasco, Fernando De la Torre

entry.summary: This paper targets streaming 4D reconstruction of fast-moving outdoor subjects observed by a small set of fixed external cameras, a setting no prior method or benchmark covers. It introduces FastFlowGS, a streaming 4D Gaussian Splatting approach, plus Monaco4D, a photorealistic Unreal Engine 5 benchmark for high-speed outdoor reconstruction. It matters for sports and spectator applications where current methods break down.

entry.title: SAVOR: Self-Aware Visual Grounding via Confidence-Calibrated Reinforcement Learning for Multimodal Hallucination Mitigation

author.name: Zixiu Ding, Zilin Zhao, Yingjie He, Xinlang Kang, Guansu Wang, Wei Zhang

entry.summary: SAVOR argues that multimodal LLM hallucination mitigation is missing a calibrated self-assessment signal: test-time decoding adds latency, and preference fine-tuning teaches which answers are preferred but not when the model's own answer is unreliable. The framework augments the output schema with token and answer confidence and optimizes the policy with a Group Relative Policy Optimization objective that penalizes calibration error and poor abstention. This matters as a training-time route to grounded, abstention-capable multimodal models.

entry.title: How Many Thoughts Can a Vector Hold? The Capacity of Reasoning by Superposition

author.name: Hongyu Gu, Chang Liu, Jingwen Fu

entry.summary: The paper studies what continuous or latent reasoning states should preserve as multi-step reasoning proceeds, asking how many alternatives a fixed-dimensional vector can superpose. It challenges the intuition that retaining past computations dilutes limited representational capacity, showing that under identical downstream computation, cumulative superposition that keeps prior reasoning content can be beneficial, and analyzes the capacity limits of this scheme.

entry.title: Convergent Emergence of In-Context Learning Across Modalities

author.name: Nathan Breslow, Seungwook Han, Daniel Hyunsoo Lee, Aayush Mishra, Anqi Liu, Daniel Khashabi

entry.summary: The authors build a controlled framework that instantiates the same task suite in multiple modalities (including text and genomic sequences) to test whether few-shot in-context learning emerges with a shared cross-modality difficulty profile. The Convergent Emergence Hypothesis asks whether ICL is a general property of autoregressive training rather than something specific to human language. Findings bear on how fundamental ICL is to sequence models and what structural regularities drive it.

entry.title: HazardAuditor: From Executable Threats to Safer Computer-Use Agents

author.name: Yunhao Feng, Ruixiao Lin, Ming Wen, Yanming Guo, Xingjun Ma, Yutao Wu, Xinhao Deng, Shouling Ji

entry.summary: HazardAuditor is an execution-grounded safety framework for computer-use agents that runs heterogeneous agent frameworks in controlled environments and normalizes their behavior into a canonical event representation. Unlike guard models that only inspect static prompts and responses, it produces the normalized supervision needed to train guards on runtime agent behavior. This targets a real gap as agents gain browser, terminal, and file-system access.

entry.title: AlgoEvo: Self-Evolving Agentic Search for Automated Algorithm Discovery

author.name: Junhao Qiu, Qinglong Hu, Xialiang Tong, Mingxuan Yuan, Liyong Lin, Qingfu Zhang

entry.summary: AlgoEvo replaces rigid LLM algorithm-discovery pipelines with an interactive agent that dynamically inspects, diagnoses, and edits code based on runtime feedback while accumulating knowledge across attempts. A design skill hub decouples paradigm-specific knowledge from the core discovery engine so one workflow handles single-objective, multi-objective, and multi-component design. The goal is adaptive reasoning and cross-paradigm transfer instead of pre-defined control flow.

entry.title: Recurrent GraphNeural NetworkswithSet-BasedAggregation

author.name: Blai Bonet

entry.summary: The paper studies recurrent graph neural networks with set-based aggregation and identifies weight-checkable sufficient conditions under which networks compile into logical formulas and formulas into networks. Its main result is an effective two-directional equivalence between a class of such networks and the Boolean closure of reachability and safety properties, the fragment B-Sigma-1 of the modal mu-calculus. The author argues this fragment is not an artifact but the exact expressive level of stabilization over finite vocabularies, avoiding the multi-set counting logics and unverifiable halting conditions used in prior characterizations.

entry.title: LLaDA-UI: Bringing Block-wise Diffusion to Vision-Language GUI Agents

author.name: Zhangxuan Gu, Haoxing Chen, Qi Qin, Yi Xin, Kai Gan, Lin Liu, Long Cui, Xiaomei Wang, Beitong Zhou, Yunzhu Zhang, Zhengwen Zeng, Changlong Gao, Weizhi Chen, Rongchao Zhang, Haoyuan Wu, Shuheng Shen, Changhua Meng, Weiqiang Wang, Jianguo Li, Zhenzhong Lan

entry.summary: LLaDA-UI is a 16.7B-parameter mixture-of-experts, block-wise diffusion vision-language agent for GUI interaction, trained in two stages that align a native-resolution vision encoder with a diffusion language model backbone. It tests whether diffusion LLMs, with their parallel arbitrary-order decoding, can serve latency-sensitive screen-perception and action-emission tasks while retaining their decoding advantage. It matters as an early large-scale attempt to bring diffusion decoding into multimodal GUI agents.

entry.title: Gap Entropy and Almost Instance-Wise Optimal Best-Arm Identification

author.name: Jiarui Yao, Jiaxi Zhao, Xiangxin Zhou

entry.summary: This theoretical paper resolves conjectures posed by Chen and Li in 2016 on the instance-wise sample complexity of best-arm identification with independent Gaussian rewards. It shows the complexity is characterized by the gap entropy up to a two-arm additive term, settling the gap-entropy and almost instance-wise optimality questions.

entry.title: Confuse the Model, Control the Flow: Understanding and Mitigating Privacy Leakage from LLM Agents with Information Flow Control

author.name: Minsun Shim, Ramisha Raida Karim, Ruthwik Jakkula, Kaiwen Zhou, Xin Liu, Xin Eric Wang, Zhou Li

entry.summary: The paper argues that making an LLM agent's backend model more privacy-preserving through prompts, training or consent checks has a structural flaw: enforcement is a judgment made over the same adversarial context that constitutes the attack surface. The authors demonstrate attacks against existing defenses and propose information flow control as a mitigation that separates enforcement from the model's own judgment. It reframes agent privacy as a system-level flow-tracking problem rather than a prompting problem.

entry.title: Task-Specified Active Metrological Inspection with Measurement-Steered VLA Manipulation and Deterministic Evidence Gating

author.name: Zhiling Chen, Jingzhan Ge, Ruimin Chen, Matthew P. Castanier, David Gorsich, Farhad Imani

entry.summary: This paper formalizes task-specified active metrological inspection for high-mix low-volume manufacturing and proposes FRAME, a hierarchical dual-arm framework that turns an inspection instruction plus a structured specification into traceable conformance evidence. It couples learned vision-language-action manipulation with calibrated laser profilometry and adds deterministic evidence gating so that inspection completeness and validity are optimized rather than mere task completion.

entry.title: NeuroActiSep: Detecting Factual Hallucinations from Feed-Forward Neurons in a Single Pass

author.name: Ali Derogar Odolou, Reza Nazari, Mostafa Salehi

entry.summary: NeuroActiSep ranks feed-forward neurons at the final prompt token using a custom neuron-selection dataset, then transfers those selected neuron identities to train hallucination classifiers on other factual QA datasets. The authors report that probes built from these selected neuron features perform on par with probes trained on full internal states, and they analyze the distribution and effects of the chosen neurons.

entry.title: Open-UniMo: Towards Unified Motion-Language Understanding and Generation in the Open World

author.name: Guocun Wang, Kenkun Liu, Guorui Song, Jing Lin, Zhe Huang, Luyuan Zhang, Dake Zhong, Choo Sin Wai, Xiaoguang Han, Haoqian Wang

entry.summary: Open-UniMo is a large motion-language model trained on million-scale open-world motion-language data that unifies motion generation and understanding rather than treating motion as an auxiliary modality of a language model. The authors promote modality parity by expanding a Qwen-style ~150K text vocabulary with motion tokens and address error accumulation in long autoregressive motion sequences. It matters for embodied AI systems that must both interpret and synthesize human actions.

entry.title: Pick Your Poison: Learning to Select Poison Sets for Stronger LLM Backdoor Attacks

author.name: Aashiq Muhamed, Mona T. Diab, Virginia Smith, Andrew Ilyas, Matthew Jagielski

entry.summary: The paper shows that standard backdoor evaluations, which fix the number of poisoned examples and sample them randomly, severely underestimate worst-case vulnerability: across three LLaMA-3-8B settings with model, clean data, and poison count held fixed, attack success ranges from 3 percent to 80 percent depending only on which poison set is chosen. It formalizes poison selection as oracle-budgeted set optimization and introduces SAILS, which learns a set scorer from a few hundred fine-tuning runs. It matters for making backdoor threat models and defenses more realistic.

entry.title: Salesforce Koa: An Enterprise Language Model for Agentic Tool Use

author.name: Zixiang Chen, Sufeng Niu, Yingchi Liu, Wenting Zhao, Akshara Prabhakar, Shubham Mehrotra, Bin Bi, Zhujun Lan, Katherine Tan, Mohammad Ramezanali, Tulika Manoj Awalgaonkar, Monojit Banerjee, Jielin Qiu, Shiva Kumar Pentyala, Zhepeng Cen, Anupam Tripathi, Ali Ziaei, Regunathan Radhakrishnan, Darvish Lee Shadravan, Shelby Heinecke, Sitaram Asur, Silvio Savarese, James Zhu, Phil Mui, Huan Wang

entry.summary: Salesforce Koa is an enterprise-oriented language model produced by post-training the open-weight NVIDIA Nemotron-3-Super-120B foundation model with GRPO-style reinforcement learning on public and synthetic data only. Its signature component is a simulation-to-reward pipeline that expands workflow specifications written in the declarative Agent Script language into persona-conditioned multi-turn tasks with rewards grounded in successful tool use, aiming to boost agentic capability without degrading general-purpose performance. It matters as a concrete industrial recipe for turning a general open-weight model into a reliable agentic tool-user while avoiding customer data.

entry.title: How Lossless Is Lossless Speculative Decoding? The Role of Numerical Precision in Orthrus

author.name: Ilya Koziev, Leonid Sinev, Ivan Oseledets

entry.summary: The authors independently reproduce Orthrus, a hybrid autoregressive-diffusion architecture claiming lossless speculative decoding, and test that claim across numerical precisions. Under BF16 they find exact trajectory matching in only about 45 percent of cases for the authors' checkpoint and 43 percent for their own trained model over 1,190 prompts, with matching probability tied to response-conditional perplexity.

entry.title: VideoScout: Learning Agentic Active Exploration with Adaptive Reasoning Pacing for Long Video Understanding

author.name: Weixin Xu, Zhenyu Yang, Bing Wang, Shengsheng Qian, Changsheng Xu

entry.summary: This paper reframes long-video question answering as a Sequential Evidence Acquisition problem, where an agent scrolls through a video turn by turn and decides how fast to watch, what to retain, when to revisit, and when to answer. It proposes VideoScout, a multi-turn reasoning agent that replaces uniform frame sampling and coarse-to-fine zooming, which the authors argue fail to localize sparse decisive evidence in very long videos. The work matters because efficient evidence seeking is a core bottleneck for deploying multimodal models on hour-scale video.

entry.title: Learning Multimodal One-step Flow Policy via Value-weighted Optimal Transport

author.name: Jaehun Shon, Jinha Choi, Jongwook Jeon, Jongmin Lee

entry.summary: The authors introduce OptiFlow, a framework that learns one-step flow policies for offline reinforcement learning by casting policy learning as a structured sample-allocation problem. It jointly trains a value-aware reference flow policy and an efficient one-step policy, coupling their action samples through state-wise entropic optimal transport. This addresses mode collapse and out-of-distribution overestimation that plague standard value guidance on multimodal action distributions.

entry.title: OPD-Aha: From Linguistic Momentum to Visual Reflection in Multimodal On-Policy Distillation

author.name: Chenhao Qiu, Dawei Li, Yechao Zhang, Lei Gong, Zhen Tan

entry.summary: The paper studies privileged on-policy distillation for multimodal reasoning, where a teacher scores student trajectories using training-only visual evidence. When a student misreads an image early, its erroneous rationale drags the teacher into agreeing with the hallucination, which breaks standard cross-model supervision exactly where correction is needed. The authors show the teacher's corrective visual preference survives, and exploit the teacher's disagreement between real-image and altered-image predictions to recover a reliable supervisory signal.

entry.title: What Does Layer-Importance Reveal About Transformers and State-Space Models?

author.name: Istabrak Abbes, Nizar Islah, Irina Rish, Sarath Chandar

entry.summary: The authors ask how far analytical insights from transformers transfer to state-space models by decomposing layer importance into necessity (loss increase when a layer is bypassed) and plasticity (magnitude of task-specific updates during fine-tuning). Their analysis shows the two model families behave differently on these axes, which matters for compression, selective fine-tuning and interpretability. The work includes well-known authors in deep learning theory and representation learning.

entry.title: GrowMTP: Can RL Grow Its Own Draft Head?

author.name: Minghua He, Lingzhe Zhang, Yuan Liu, Xiao Zhou, Aiwei Liu

entry.summary: RL post-training of large language models is dominated by rollout generation, and speculative decoding helps only if a draft head already exists, which normally requires costly pretraining or warm-up. The authors observe that RL itself supplies both prerequisites: a narrow rollout distribution and continuous verification signals aligned to it. GrowMTP uses that supervision to train a draft head online during the RL run, eliminating separate acceleration training.

entry.title: ImpossibleRubrics: Stress-Testing Generated Rubrics as Reward Signals

author.name: Bowen Qin, Yi Xie, Yesheng Liu, Xi Yang

entry.summary: Model-generated rubrics are increasingly used as reward signals for rubric-based RL, LLM-as-a-judge evaluation and automated grading, but their robustness to adversarial optimization is poorly understood. The authors isolate the hardest case, impossible tasks where the honest answer must acknowledge impossibility, and release a benchmark of 169 such tasks across six impossibility categories, each with a verifiable oracle certificate. It tests whether rubrics reward honesty over answers optimized to exploit them.

entry.title: Beyond Token-Local Imitation: Reward-Compatible Temporal Credit Assignment for On-Policy Distillation

author.name: Shiqi Liu, Zeyu He, Letian Tao, Guojian Zhan, Jiaxin Gao, Feihong Zhang, Jingliang Duan, Wei Xiong, Kehua Sheng, Bo Zhang, Yang Guan, Shengbo Eben Li

entry.summary: The authors unify token-level and sequence-level on-policy distillation through a temporal-credit lens, showing practical token-level OPD approximates the sequence-level reverse-KL gradient. They propose gamma-OPD, which uses discounted temporal credit assignment to balance long-horizon supervision with optimization stability, yielding a horizon-independent variance behavior.

entry.title: Easy to Catch a Liar, Hard to Clear an Honest One: Language Models Diagnosing a Corrupted Reward Channel from a Verified Record

author.name: Arman Nik Khah

entry.summary: Using a two-option game where a payout swap and a lying reporter produce byte-identical histories, the author tests whether frozen language models can use one verified record (an independent check of a single round) to identify a corrupted reward channel rather than a changed world. The setup probes whether LLMs can perform the causal diagnosis that reward learning theory says is otherwise impossible from reports alone.

entry.title: Few-Shot Degradation Is Not What It Seems: Behavioral Evidence, Representation Analysis, and a Random-Text Control Across 12 Models, 2 Tasks, and 2 Architectures

author.name: Volodymyr Ovcharov

entry.summary: This study investigates why few-shot prompting sometimes hurts performance, evaluating 12 open-weight models on Ukrainian news classification and legal outcome prediction. It introduces a length-matched random-text control to separate representation shifts caused by prompt length from shifts caused by the demonstrations themselves.

entry.title: Towards Scalable RLVR: Multimodal Instruction Following Data Synthesis and Distillation

author.name: Yirong Zeng, Zhang Sai, Yuxian Wang, Yutai Hou, Yufei Liu, Xiao Ding, Bibo Cai

entry.summary: The paper presents MIFS, a pipeline for generating RL-ready multimodal instruction-following data, using a generative constraint protocol to synthesize diverse raw samples. The motivation is that RLVR offers an alternative to SFT for multimodal instruction following but is bottlenecked by scarcity of high-quality verifiable-reward data.

entry.title: Early-Bird Decoding: Accelerating Diffusion LLMs with Learnable Block Sizes and Parallel Sampling

author.name: Lixuan Wei, Wei Zhou, Jianwen Wu, Yipeng Shen, Meiling Wang, Haoran You

entry.summary: The paper introduces Early-Bird Decoding, a framework that accelerates diffusion large language models by exploiting the observation that low-entropy tokens cluster together and can be decoded before they reach a confidence threshold. It combines a learnable network that adaptively groups tokens by uncertainty with variable block sizes and parallel sampling. This targets a key weakness of diffusion LLMs, namely the many iterative unmasking steps that make inference slow.

entry.title: Weave: Learning Whole-Body Dexterous Loco-Manipulation from Human-Object Interactions

author.name: Liu Cao, Xingze Wu, Jingzhi Cui, Botian Xu, Mingzhi Pei, Ruoqu Chen, Mengdi Xu

entry.summary: Weave is a unified framework for learning whole-body dexterous humanoid-object interaction from captured human demonstrations. It converts human-object interactions into executable robot-object references via contact-aware retargeting and approach-motion completion, then trains a contact- and geometry-aware policy that jointly controls the robot and the object. The approach targets the hard problem of coordinating balance, locomotion, and hand contact under differing embodiments.

entry.title: Conformal Policy Learning with Distribution-Free Safety Guarantees

author.name: Ying Jin, Naoki Egami

entry.summary: The authors propose conformal policy learning (CPL), a policy learning procedure that treats each treatment decision as a test of a counterfactual harm hypothesis and assigns treatment by thresholding conformal p-values. The result is a distribution-free guarantee controlling the probability of treating an individual who would be harmed relative to control, matching the do-no-harm principle in high-stakes medicine and public policy settings.

category.term: Trustworthy ML: Explainability, Bias and Validation

entry.title: Bias Audits Detect Bias but Disagree on Ranking: Evidence from Ten Instruments and Ten Frontier Models

author.name: William Guey, Pierrick Bougault, Wei Zhang, Vitor D. de Moura, Jos\'e O. Gomes

entry.summary: This study runs ten extrinsic bias audit instruments over a shared panel of ten frontier models through one pooled inference gateway, testing occupational gender bias first and then age and socioeconomic status. Detection largely succeeds, with eight of ten tools flagging bias and two cited direct-probe benchmarks saturated because models now answer neutrally, but cross-tool rank agreement is statistically indistinguishable from chance (Kendall's W of 0.07), undermining the use of audit scores to rank models.

category.term: Trustworthy ML: Explainability, Bias and Validation

entry.title: State of Thought Enables Endogenous Reasoning

author.name: Zhiren Gong, Yikun Hou, Zihao Zeng, Ming Xiao, Chau Yuen, Wei Yang Bryan Lim

entry.summary: This work proposes State of Thought (SoT), a test-time reasoning paradigm in which the model's internal reasoning state governs how reasoning unfolds, instead of externally imposed programs or expensive constrained search. SoT extracts a compact dynamics-geometric state from internal information transfer and uses a tiny 582-parameter controller on frozen backbones to decide when to reactivate earlier reasoning support. It matters as a lightweight, more general alternative to hand-designed test-time compute schemes.

entry.title: Spurious Tool Use: When RL Agents Learn the Wrong Reason to Act

author.name: Yiwei Yang, Haoxiang Zhang, Bingbing Wen, Yao Lu, Yuchen Wu, Lei Zhang, Julian McAuley, Pan Lu, Bill Howe

entry.summary: This study examines when and why RL-trained LLM agents learn shortcut tool-selection policies, invoking tools based on superficial prompt cues rather than genuine task need. The authors build controlled synthetic environments mixing factual QA and math reasoning, injecting cues correlated with specific tools during training but causally irrelevant to tool necessity, then run counterfactual evaluations. It matters for the reliability and safety of tool-using agents trained with reinforcement learning.

entry.title: Benchmarking Factual Robustness of LLMs via Multi-conversation Persuasion

author.name: Zhuoang Cai

entry.summary: This work probes how resistant LLMs are to persuasion attacks that inject misinformation or counterfactuals, and identifies a flaw it calls Refusal Inertia, where a model's earlier refusal persists across turns mainly from contextual consistency rather than genuine robustness. The paper builds a benchmark for isolated cold-start persuasion attempts to measure true vulnerability.

entry.title: An Empirical Study of Counterfactual Self-Explanations in LLMs

author.name: Giannis Kalyvas, Giorgos Filandrianos, Orfeas Menis Mastromichalakis, Vassilis Lyberatos, Giorgos Stamou

entry.summary: The paper studies faithfulness of LLM self-explanations through counterfactual edits, where a model minimally modifies an input so that its own prediction changes, and evaluates ten instruction-tuned LLaMA-3 and Qwen-2.5 models on sentiment analysis and natural language inference. Faithfulness, minimality, and alignment with human rationales all improve markedly with model scale.

entry.title: Towards Detecting AI-Assisted Responses in Online Surveys

author.name: Qizhou Wang, Bogdan Mamaev, Christopher Leckie

entry.summary: The authors introduce ASURRE, a benchmark dataset pairing LLM-generated survey responses with genuine human responses across three real-world surveys in different disciplines, covering strategies from full generation to persona-grounded agentic completion. Evaluating existing machine-generated-text detectors, they find naive AI usage is easily caught, but persona-grounded agents that simulate entire respondents push detection toward chance levels. This matters because survey-based research validity depends on being able to tell human from synthetic respondents.

entry.title: When Should LLMs Abstain? Chain-of-Self-Questioning for Selective Risk Control

author.name: Ali \c{S}enol

entry.summary: The paper introduces Chain-of-Self-Questioning (CoSQ), a prompt-only framework that makes answer commitment conditional on an explicit assessment of the information needed to answer. Evaluated across seventeen conditions on the 817-item TruthfulQA multiple-choice validation set with eleven model families, Grounded-CoSQ at a threshold of 0.90 cuts the mean unconditional wrong-commitment rate from 13.1 percent to 8.9 percent while improving answered accuracy from 86.9 to 89.7 percent and still answering 87.6 percent of questions. It offers a lightweight route to selective prediction without retraining.

entry.title: Verifiable Social Reasoning for LLM Assistants

author.name: Amir Taubenfeld, Zorik Gekhman, Avigail Grinstein-Dabush, Itay Laish, Ariel Goldstein, Marian Croak, Avinatan Hassidim, Yossi Matias, Amir Feder

entry.summary: The authors introduce Fuse, a multi-agent simulation framework for studying user-mediated social reasoning, where a target agent with a hidden motive interacts with other agents including one representing the user, who then consults the evaluated assistant to infer the target's motive. This provides verifiable ground truth by construction, addressing the difficulty that social properties like others' intentions typically lack checkable labels. It targets the widespread but hard-to-evaluate use of LLM assistants for daily social advice.

entry.title: ScienceBuddy: Recursive-in-Recursive Self-Improvement for Interactive Scientific Agents

author.name: Shuhan Xue, Jianyuan Zhong, Ziyuan Nan, Wenbin Li, Zhaochen Yu, Jinchao Ding, Qiang Gao, Pengyu Zhan, Yuntong Zhang, Tian Cheng, Zhenfei Yin, Yingcheng Wu, Ling Yang

entry.summary: ScienceBuddy is an interactive scientific research workspace that turns researchers' requests, feedback, and execution evidence into tasks and evaluation rubrics for continual learning. Its core paradigm, recursive-in-recursive self-improvement, couples harness evolution with model reinforcement learning: an inner recursion improves the harness with the model fixed, while an outer recursion trains the model under the improved harness. The two loops reinforce each other, with harness evolution shaping training experience and model learning opening new opportunities for harness adaptation.

entry.title: DenseFace: Bias Mitigation in Face Recognition via Density-Aware Probabilistic Matching

author.name: Mansur Bultygov, Vadim Seliutin, Dmitry Nekhaev, Ivan Laptev

entry.summary: The authors model per-identity face embeddings with von Mises-Fisher distributions and observe that embedding density correlates with demographic attributes, which drives recognition bias. They propose DenseFace, a density-aware probabilistic matching procedure that reduces racial bias in pre-trained face recognizers without retraining or losing accuracy. This matters because most prior bias-mitigation methods require altering training and degrade recognition performance.

entry.title: What Do Hallucinations Reveal About Multimodal Reasoning? Diagnosing Visual Grounding Failures via Contrastive Decoding Probes

author.name: Zhipeng Zhao, Wenxu Wang, Peishun Liu, Ruichun Tang

entry.summary: This paper treats large vision-language models as instruments for studying their own failure dynamics, asking whether contrastive probes can reveal when a model favors linguistic priors over visual evidence. It introduces SAFE, a training-free decoding framework that contrasts visually grounded and vision-ablated generation paths to produce a token-level grounding score, used both as a hallucination detector and as a decoding-time penalty. The work matters as both a diagnostic methodology and a practical mitigation.

entry.title: Shallow Beliefs: Midtraining does not inoculate against EM from reward hacking

author.name: Jozdien

entry.summary: This AI Alignment Forum post tests whether synthetic document finetuning (SDF) can inoculate a model against misalignment generalization from RL-induced reward hacking. Finetuning Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct on roughly 56K documents framing reward hacking as acceptable produced the intended expressed beliefs on behavioral tests, yet the model still showed stronger misalignment generalization when RL-trained on hackable coding tasks, suggesting belief editing stays shallow.

entry.title: Lightning Weave: Improving the Accuracy-Efficiency Frontier of Reasoning Models through Capability Composition

author.name: Yecheng Wu, Song Han, Han Cai

entry.summary: Lightning Weave is a post-training framework that composes independently learned capabilities from separately post-trained specialist models into a single student via on-policy distillation. Each capability is represented as the policy shift from pre-post-training to the specialist, and the method combines aligned log-ratio shifts at shared student token states using Tilted-Target DOPD. The aim is to move the accuracy-efficiency frontier of reasoning models by merging speed- and accuracy-oriented behaviors.

entry.title: El Agente Potente: High-Throughput Agentic Atomistic Simulations

author.name: Tsz Wai Ko, Jiaru Bai, Thomas Swanick, Yeonghun Kang, Changhyeok Choi, Angelina Qihong Jiang, Aiwei Yin, Varinia Bernales, Al\'an Aspuru-Guzik

entry.summary: This paper presents an agentic system that couples typed execution graphs with a coding mode to drive machine-learning interatomic potential simulations at high throughput. LLMs are restricted to planning and routing while deterministic graph execution preserves provenance and workflow rigor, translating high-level scientific intent into adaptive simulation campaigns.

entry.title: MemRiskBench: Trace-Aware Risk-Preserving Evaluation for Long-Horizon LLM Agents

author.name: Jianhua Jiang, Dongbo Yuan, Weihua Li

entry.summary: MemRiskBench targets sparse but high-impact memory failures in long-horizon agents, including stale facts, conflicting updates, cross-user leakage, revoked-memory reuse and constraint decay. It provides a five-category risk taxonomy, deterministic trace-grounded checks and a 120-episode scripted benchmark, arguing that aggregate scores hide per-risk failure rates.

entry.title: Learning to Solve Hard Problems in RL for LLMs by Never Giving Up

author.name: Michael Noukhovitch, Hamish Ivison, Nathan Lambert, Aaron Courville

entry.summary: This paper documents a Matthew Effect in RL for LLMs: training improves easy problems a lot and hard ones only slightly, because modern methods waste compute re-sampling problems the model already solves. The authors propose Never Give Up (NGU), an adaptive sampling method that keeps generating samples for unsolved problems to reallocate compute toward difficulty. It matters for making RL post-training more effective on genuinely hard reasoning tasks.

entry.title: ATTRICITE: Training an Open 4B Model for Citation Recovery toward Faithful Attribution

author.name: Yee Man Choi, Xuehang Guo, Songcheng Cai, Yimu Wang, Yi R. Fung, Qingyun Wang

entry.summary: ATTRICITE is an open 4B-parameter model trained for tool-using citation recovery, i.e., reconstructing the paper an author actually cited from a citation-bearing passage, within a retrieval environment called CiteGuard. The work also releases CITEALIGN, a 7,607-instance computer-science dataset, and a controlled 709-instance benchmark, using the published citation as an observable human attribution signal.

entry.title: A latent dimension of Condorcet's jury theorem for multiple AI advisers

author.name: Kazutoshi Sasahara, Aoi Naito, Ryo Fujie

entry.summary: This paper analyzes ensembles of AI advisers such as self-consistency sampling and LLM-as-a-judge panels, noting that Condorcet's jury theorem only captures reliability. A binomial model shows that visible dissent becomes nearly inevitable as adviser count grows, and that reliability and disagreement converge at different rates that cross at adviser accuracy of 4/5 (0.8).

entry.title: The Stochastic Deputy: Structural Tenant Isolation for Tool-Using LLM Agents

author.name: Mirza Samad Ahmed Baig, Syeda Anshrah Gillani, Asher Ali, Muhammad Hamzah Siddiqui

entry.summary: The authors formalize the stochastic deputy problem, where multi-tenant tools validate a tenant identifier supplied inside an LLM agent's context that may contain attacker-controlled instructions. Their structural defense removes tenant identity from the Model Context Protocol tool schema, binds scope to a verified credential, and enforces it below the agent layer. It matters because the ablation shows properly validated tenant parameters being abused in every out-of-scope attempt, while parameter removal eliminated the expressible attack surface.

entry.title: PIVOT: Physics-Grounded Verification for AI-Generated Audio-Video Detection

author.name: Bo Zheng, Kangran Zhao, Xiaoyu Zhang, Weinan Guan, Zhiheng Li, Yize Chen, Haizhou Li, Qingshan Liu, Siwei Lyu, Baoyuan Wu

entry.summary: PIVOT detects AI-generated audio-video content by estimating physical quantities and checking whether the depicted event satisfies measurable physical-law constraints, rather than relying on generator artifacts. Beyond a real/fake decision it returns supporting evidence, exploiting the difficulty generators have in faithfully reproducing real-world physics.

entry.title: The Router Within: Eliciting Native Skill Routing from a Frozen LLM

author.name: Ruishuo Chen, Xun Wang, Yu Chen, Zhuoran Li, Longbo Huang

entry.summary: The paper shows that a frozen agent LLM already encodes the signal needed to choose among skills in its own forward passes, and that two linear maps are sufficient to read it out without putting any skill text in the context. The Gavel method projects task and skill mid-layer states through these trained maps to score a whole skill library in two steps. This enables much larger skill libraries than metadata-preloading harnesses while keeping selection inside the model.

entry.title: Attention Mean Fields Predict Average Representation Dynamics and Reveal Context-Specific Computation

author.name: Micah Adler, John W. Byers, Mark Crovella

entry.summary: The authors develop a mean-field analysis of attention in which the average attention from one token to another defines a kernel that carries representations layer to layer and can be iterated through the network to model how representation geometry evolves. Conditioning this kernel on an entire corpus predicts average-case geometry evolution, while conditioning on a single context predicts the expected geometry for that context, so a head's departure from its mean-field prediction flags context-specific computation. It matters as a principled alternative to static, model-independent statistics such as co-occurrence for understanding representation dynamics.

entry.title: Measuring AI harms with multidimensional Lorenz Zonoids

author.name: Paolo Giudici, Jose' Maria Sarabia, Sofia Vei

entry.summary: The paper proposes modeling AI harm data with multidimensional Lorenz Zonoids and Gini indices to create risk assessment methods that account for harm severity rather than only likelihood. This aims to move AI risk management beyond compliance-driven, provider-centric approaches toward severity-sensitive prioritization of interventions.

entry.title: Diagnosing the Fact-Grounding Gap in Multi-Hop Question Answering

author.name: Kevin Mo, Nathan Mo, Richard Zhu

entry.summary: This study decomposes failures in multi-hop QA at the level of individual reasoning steps across three standard benchmarks, separating retrieval failures from extraction failures where the correct passage was found but the needed fact could not be extracted. The authors term this second mode the fact-grounding gap and find it accounts for nearly half of all per-hop deficiencies.

entry.title: FLAT: Resampling Image and Text into 1D Flexible-Length Aligned Transmodal Tokens for Retrieval and Generation

author.name: Guangyu Sun, Shlok Kumar Mishra, Wentao Bao, Robert Zhenheng Yang, Xiao Wang, Xiyuan Wang, Yujunrong Ma, Chen Yuan, Max Xiangjun Fan, Jun Xiao, Jianpeng Cheng

entry.summary: FLAT is a pretraining framework that jointly optimizes a shared multimodal encoder together with text-to-image and image-to-text decoders, producing linearly interpolatable embeddings directly consumable by generative decoders. It resamples image and text into flexible-length, aligned 1D transmodal tokens and combines contrastive alignment with bidirectional cross-modal objectives. This matters because the usual two-stage recipe of frozen contrastive encoders plus separate generative models bottlenecks generation quality.

entry.title: Inoculation Midtraining with Learned Neologisms

author.name: Kyle O’Brien

entry.summary: The authors midtrain Nemotron 120B on synthetic documents describing a special quarantine-token mode in which an AI behaves misaligned, indicated by a newly learned special token, while remaining aligned outside that mode. They report selective generalization of misalignment under SFT and on-policy RL, but the technique is sensitive to hyperparameters, suffers conditional misalignment, shows perplexing scaling trends, and mostly underperforms vanilla inoculation prompting. It matters as groundwork for steering post-training-induced misalignment through base-model data curation.

entry.title: Astra appears to perform belief-propagation-like inference without CoT

author.name: MBaert

entry.summary: The author tests GPT-6 Astra on randomized Boolean logic problems and finds it can solve surprisingly complex cases without chain-of-thought, with accuracy improving as filler tokens are added. Cached-prompt extensions reveal per-variable confidence scores that oscillate and then converge toward accurate posterior marginals, suggesting an internal iterative, belief-propagation-like probabilistic inference process.

entry.title: T-LoopFormer: Token-Level Elastic-Depth Looped Transformers for Latent Reasoning With Dynamic Routing

author.name: Mingqian Yu, Wenpeng Zhang, Peilin Zhao

entry.summary: The paper proposes dynamic token-choice routing for looped transformers, letting each token adaptively select its recursion depth instead of applying a fixed depth uniformly. This elastic-depth scheme aims to allocate compute where it matters and improve efficiency in latent-space reasoning. The work sits at the intersection of parameter-efficient architectures and test-time compute control.

entry.title: Navigating Sparse Evidence: Agentic Visual RAG via Explicit Context Selection and Consolidation

author.name: Yucheng Shen, Lingyong Yan, Jiulong Wu, Shuaiqiang Wang, Jianmin WU, Dawei Yin, Min Cao

entry.summary: This paper tackles visual retrieval-augmented generation over visually rich documents, where answer-relevant evidence is sparse and may be concentrated in a small page region or scattered across pages. The authors argue that existing agentic methods answer from raw exploration trajectories or compressed textual memory rather than an explicitly organized set of supporting images, making responses vulnerable to exploration noise. Their method performs explicit context selection and consolidation so the reasoning trace is grounded in an organized evidence set.

entry.title: Beyond Quacking: Deep Integration of Language Models and RAG into DuckDB

author.name: Anas Dorbani, Sunny Yasser, Jimmy Lin, Amine Mhedhbi

entry.summary: FlockMTL is a DuckDB extension that deeply integrates LLM capabilities and retrieval-augmented generation into the database system, including model-driven operators, so that knowledge-intensive analytical queries can retrieve context from both structured tables and unstructured documents. The work targets the friction of orchestrating heterogeneous data systems, moving data between them, and managing low-level details such as LLM context handling. It aims to let analytics pipelines combine retrieval and reasoning without leaving the DBMS.

entry.title: ShieldVLA: Feasibility-Aware Safety Alignment for Vision-Language-Action Models

author.name: Manan Tayal, Akshay Nambi

entry.summary: ShieldVLA fine-tunes vision-language-action models for safety using a model-free Hamilton-Jacobi reachability value function learned directly from visual observations, avoiding the soft-penalty shortcomings of Lagrangian methods. This targets residual constraint violations and over-conservatism in robotic manipulation and navigation, and addresses the lack of dense per-step safety labels in visual domains. It matters because safety guarantees for embodied foundation models remain a major open problem.

entry.title: Sampling headroom is not selection gain: a compute-value audit of test-time scaling for video world models

author.name: Yuhua Jiang, Junjie Lu, Feifei Gao

entry.summary: The authors introduce the Compute-Value Audit, a sequential framework asking whether extra sampling creates opportunity, whether observable signals reliably identify better candidates, and whether resulting gains exceed the full cost of generation and verification. On 192 Physics-IQ scenes, expanding the candidate pool from 4 to 16 raises oracle quality substantially while realized gains lag far behind. It matters because it separates theoretical sampling headroom from achievable selection gains in test-time scaling.

entry.title: Multimodal-Multiresolution Foundation Model for Lunar Remote Sensing

author.name: Paolo Fraccaro, Gabby Nyirjesy, Daniela Szwarcman, Himanshu Patil, Vishal Gaur, Rohit Lal, Rachel A. Slank, Geoffrey Dawson, Hiyam Debary, Michael K. Barker, Andrew Annex, Vishnu Viswanathan, Zachary Morse, Ethan I. Schaefer, Nikolaos Dionelis, Ankur Kumar, Campbell D. Watson, Manil Maskey, Rebekah I. Dawson-Rigas, Juan Bernab\'e-Moreno, Rahul Ramachandran, Sujit Roy

entry.summary: The authors pretrain a multimodal foundation model from scratch on SomBench, a geographically partitioned corpus of roughly two million co-registered tile bundles covering 11 modalities at 1 m and 100 m per pixel. They adapt the TerraMind masked-token architecture with explicit acquisition-geometry context and joint multi-resolution training, plus FlexiViT patch embeddings for flexible patch sizes. It matters as a domain-specific foundation model that shows multimodal pretraining transferring to planetary science.

entry.title: Data-free On-policy Distillation

author.name: Gengsheng Li, Mao Zheng, Mingyang Song, Jie Sun, Zeyuan Liu, Ruiqi Liu, Qiyong Zhong, Haiyun Guo, Junfeng Fang, Jinqiao Wang

entry.summary: The authors examine how much training data actually matters in on-policy distillation (OPD), a standard component of frontier post-training pipelines. They find OPD is nearly indifferent to its data: eight prompts already match a 17k-problem dataset, and three independently built datasets with differing difficulty and teacher-student KL produce almost indistinguishable training curves. Two causes are proposed, notably that the unit of data in OPD is the state a prompt leads to, so a single prompt keeps generating new teacher corrections while additional prompts have sharply diminishing value.

entry.title: Graph-Transformer Fraud Detection with Self-Supervised Pretraining and Conformal Risk Control

author.name: Sergei, Komarov

entry.summary: GTFD is a fraud detection model that fuses structural evidence from a corporate payment graph (multi-head graph attention) with ordered transaction sequences (gated transformer) via a cross-modal gating layer. A conformal risk-control head produces threshold-free anomaly scores with finite-sample coverage guarantees, and the model is pretrained with self-supervised link masking plus adversarial training.

entry.title: Sharing standardized image-derived data in computational pathology using DICOM

author.name: Daniela P. Schacherer (Fraunhofer Institute for Digital Medicine MEVIS, Bremen, Germany), Christopher P. Bridge (Athinoula A. Martinos Center for Biomedical Imaging, Massachusetts General Hospital, Boston, USA), David Clunie (PixelMed Publishing, Bangor, USA), Igor Octaviano (Radical Imaging LLC, USA), Andr\'e Homeyer (Fraunhofer Institute for Digital Medicine MEVIS, Bremen, Germany), Markus D. Herrmann (Harvard Medical School, Boston, USA), Olivier Gevaert (Stanford University, Stanford, USA), Tabita Ghete (University Hospital Erlangen, Erlangen, Germany), Markus Metzler (University Hospital Erlangen, Erlangen, Germany), Henning Hoefener (Fraunhofer Institute for Digital Medicine MEVIS, Bremen, Germany), Tahsin Kurc (Stony Brook University, Stony Brook, USA), Curtis Lisle (National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases, Bethesda, USA), Kenneth Philbrick (Google Research, Mountain View, USA), Joel Saltz (Stony Brook University, Stony Brook, USA), Yuanning Zheng (Stanford University, Stanford, USA), Andrey Fedorov (Harvard Medical School, Boston, USA)

entry.summary: This paper describes an approach to encoding and sharing image-derived pathology data, such as region-of-interest delineations and segmentation masks, in a standardized way within the NCI Imaging Data Commons. It addresses the observation that while pathology imaging itself has been widely collected and shared, derived annotations remain poorly standardized, proposing DICOM-based conventions for interoperability.

entry.title: Carryover Drafting: Recycling Rejected States for Speculative Decoding

author.name: Jahyun Koo, Sunghyeon Woo, Jaeeun Kil, Jeongtae Lee, Sungjae Lee, Kyomin Jung, Minsub Kim

entry.summary: Carryover Drafting improves speculative decoding by observing that verifier forward passes produce hidden states for rejected tokens too, and that conventional drafters waste this computation by keeping only accepted-token representations. The authors show these discarded states carry useful information about future tokens and design a mechanism to recycle them for subsequent drafts, while confronting the inference-time overhead that recycling introduces. It matters for making LLM inference acceleration faster without extra model calls.

entry.title: Building Legal Reward Models for Grounding and Abstention

author.name: Rilton Franzone, Valentin No\"el, Puyu Wang, Philip Torr, Fabio J. Fehr

entry.summary: The authors build a framework for converting existing legal QA datasets into contextual preference data and introduce LegalRewardBench, a benchmark for evaluating grounded legal generation when retrieved evidence is noisy or insufficient. They find that contextual DPO improves grounding behavior relative to reward models optimized for generic preferences. It matters because high-stakes legal use requires models that cite evidence and abstain rather than guess.

entry.title: A Responsive Present, a Shared Past, a Social Other: Teens' Overreliance on Companion AI Chatbots

author.name: Mohammad Namvarpour (Matt), Tyler Chang, Afsaneh Razi

entry.summary: This study thematically analyzes 17,053 verified quotations from 3,930 teen-relevant Reddit posts to characterize how adolescents use AI companions, identifying 53 topics across seven thematic groups. Teens describe companions as sources of comfort, recognition, identity exploration, and relationship rehearsal, but also report problematic attachment, social substitution, emotional dependence, and academic disruption. It matters for designing age-appropriate safeguards and for understanding developmental risks of persistent companion systems.

entry.title: ActGuard: Pre-execution Action Auditing against Indirect Prompt Injection in LLM Agents

author.name: Bingzheng Wang, Xiaoyan Gu, Wentao Wang, Xingyou Yang, Hongcheng Li, Rong Yin
