entry.summary: ActGuard is a pre-execution action auditing framework for LLM agents facing indirect prompt injection through tool outputs, where existing defenses rely on prompt hardening, content filtering, pre-generated plans, or permission constraints that either over-sanitize or fail on complex tasks. Rather than judging whether external content is inherently malicious, it focuses on identifying and removing content that would actually induce unsafe actions, preserving execution flexibility. It matters as a utility-preserving defense for tool-using agents.

entry.title: Specifying Reward Functions for RL Without Environment Sampling

author.name: Stephane Hatgis-Kessell, W. Bradley Knox, Emma Brunskill

entry.summary: EARS learns reward functions from human preferences without any environment interaction, using a structured LLM-mediated process to build a small set of expressive reward features from a task description. This targets settings where online RLHF-style preference elicitation is computationally expensive or unsafe.

entry.title: When the World Lies: Backdoor Attacks on Latent World Models for Downstream Control

author.name: Roberto Ria\~no, Gorka Abad, Stjepan Picek, Aitor Urbieta

entry.summary: This paper demonstrates a supply-chain backdoor in pretrained latent world models that are reused as off-the-shelf dynamics backbones for control. An adversary controlling only the released checkpoint can hijack a downstream controller trained on clean data with no visible trigger, by routing trigger-bearing observations into a chosen latent region and reshaping local dynamics there. No explicit trigger-to-action rule is encoded, making the attack subtle and relevant as world models become reusable infrastructure.

entry.title: Agentic Search Spaces for Tabular Machine Learning

author.name: Renat Sergazinov, Artem Chistyakov, Sergey Pankevich, Artem Babenko

entry.summary: This paper investigates whether LLM-based agents can design extended hyperparameter optimization search spaces for established tabular models that beat the standard spaces supplied by model authors. Each tabular model is represented as a modular pipeline covering preprocessing, embeddings, architecture, training, and inference, and the agent proposes candidate code implementations per module that a classical HPO algorithm then optimizes jointly with default hyperparameters. It matters as a concrete test of whether agentic coding translates into measurable gains on a mature, non-LLM ML problem class.

entry.title: Adaptive Bayesian Partner Selection for Federated Clinical Centers

author.name: Navid Seidi, Satyaki Roy, Sajal K. Das

entry.summary: This paper tackles federated learning across clinical sites where patient populations and care practices drift over time, making persistent global averaging wasteful and prone to negative transfer. The authors propose Adaptive Bayesian Partner Selection, in which each center keeps a Beta-Bernoulli posterior over peers' Shapley-style marginal utility, ranks candidates with an upper-confidence-bound rule, and forms collaborations through a lightweight propose-reject handshake. It matters because it reframes federated healthcare learning as selective, cost-aware peer matching rather than blanket synchronization.

entry.title: When Confidence Signals Disagree: Local and Global Confidence in Autoregressive Language Models

author.name: Julio C. Amador Diaz Lopez

entry.summary: The study compares two confidence readouts in autoregressive language models: local confidence from the greedy-selected token probability and global confidence from modal-answer frequency under repeated sampling. Across MMLU and ARC Challenge the signals are weakly correlated and differ substantially in how well they track correctness, implying they are not interchangeable for reliability or oversight purposes.

entry.title: LoopSpec: Pipelined Self-Speculative Decoding for Looped Transformers

author.name: SangLyul Cho, Langqing Cui, Sehoon Kim, Dongsu Han, Insu Han

entry.summary: LoopSpec is a training-free self-speculative decoding framework for Looped Transformers, which are efficient in parameters but slow at inference because shared weights are re-read at every recurrent depth. It extracts draft tokens from early recurrent states and pipelines drafting and verification, removing the need for a separate draft model and improving decoding efficiency.

entry.title: Coupled Calibration and Learning: Mitigating Teacher Bias in LLM Distillation without Target-Domain Reward Feedback

author.name: Haichen Hu, Yuheng Zhang, David Simchi-Levi

entry.summary: The paper proposes Coupled Calibration and Learning (CCL), an LLM distillation algorithm that alternates between calibrating the teacher using source-domain reward feedback and training the student on target questions via token-level branching. This targets covariate shift scenarios where the teacher is unreliable on target data and no target-domain reward signal exists.

entry.title: Breaking the 1.58-bit Barrier for Ternary LLMs

author.name: Evangelos Georganas, Alexander Heinecke, Pradeep Dubey

entry.summary: The authors measure the actual symbol distribution of 29 ternary LLM models and find that zeros make up as much as 51.5 percent of weights, contradicting the equiprobable assumption behind the conventional log-base-2 of 3 bits-per-weight figure that rounds up to 1.625 bits in five-trit packing. They introduce BITCOS, a distribution-adaptive layout with a dense prefix that cuts effective storage below the nominal ternary bound. It matters because memory footprint is a primary deployment constraint for quantized models.

entry.title: A multimodal large language model for evidence-based autism spectrum disorder screening

author.name: Jun Chen, Qi Zhao, Yunliang Jiang, Shuqin Cao, Yunqiang Lin, Chenglong Jia, Qiang Guo, Guang Dai, Xiongtao Zhang, Mengmeng Wang, Xiaoyue Ma

entry.summary: ASDchat is a multimodal large language model for autism spectrum disorder screening that takes video, audio, and dialogue as input and uses a dual-branch architecture. One branch produces screening probabilities while the other generates traceable, timestamped behavioral evidence aligned to ADOS-2 clinical criteria. It was trained and evaluated on 1,035 participants across 27 sites in China.

entry.title: The Latent That Never Was: A Forensic Re-run of the CVAE Ablation in Action Chunking Transformer

author.name: Bo Kang

entry.summary: This is a forensic replication of the widely cited CVAE ablation in Action Chunking Transformer (ACT) for robot manipulation, where the original paper reported that removing the encoder dropped mean success rate from 35% to 2%. Re-running the ablation in the original code, the author could not reproduce that magnitude of drop, and found that training length and checkpoint-selection choices can reverse which configuration appears better. The result questions a foundational claim in a popular manipulation method.

entry.title: TEMPO: Learning Temporal Context for Dynamic Robot Manipulation

author.name: Zhenyang Feng, Jimin Heo, Erik B. Sudderth, Unnat Jain

entry.summary: TEMPO targets vision-language-action models that perform well on quasi-static manipulation but fail in dynamic tasks because they act on a single observation. It identifies motion ambiguity and state aliasing as representational failures caused by missing temporal context rather than insufficient model capacity or latency. The authors build a method that learns temporal context to address these failures in dynamic manipulation.

entry.title: Causal Discovery via Transformed Low-Rank Quantile Surfaces

author.name: Ryo Kamimura, Thong Pham

entry.summary: The authors propose Low-Rank Quantile Surfaces (LRQS), a bivariate causal model in which, in the causal direction, an unknown monotone transformation of the conditional quantile surface admits a low-rank functional decomposition. LRQS generalizes location-scale and post-nonlinear heteroscedastic noise models and allows multiple quantile bases to capture effects beyond location-scale. The paper proves generic identifiability of the model and provides a practical causal score with a nonparametric fitting procedure.

entry.title: Near-Optimal Nonconvex Matrix Completion

author.name: Jian-Feng Cai, Xiliang Lu, Juntao You

entry.summary: This work analyzes Riemannian gradient descent and Riemannian Gauss-Newton for nonconvex matrix completion and proves exact recovery with high probability from roughly O(mu*n*r*log n*log(n*kappa)) observations, matching the near-linear dependence on rank r that convex methods achieve. The result closes a long-standing polynomial rank gap between convex and commonly used nonconvex approaches, and uses a multistage/spectral-style initialization.

entry.title: Retrieval-Driven Memory Reconsolidation for Long-Term LLM Agents

author.name: Yuanyi Song, Yukai Wang, Xinbei Ma, Zhihui Fu, Jianghao Lin, Weiwen Liu, Jun Wang, Huarong Deng, Yong Yu, Weinan Zhang

entry.summary: The authors propose REALM, an agentic long-term memory framework inspired by memory reconsolidation in neuroscience, where retrieval itself drives reorganization of stored memory rather than being a terminal read operation. It aims to let agents autonomously evolve memory structure instead of relying on fixed schemas and static retrieval pipelines. This matters for building agents that stay coherent and useful across very long interaction horizons.

entry.title: The Imitation Game: When LLMs Learn to Reason Like Programs via Code-Centric Reasoning Data Synthesis

author.name: Jinyang Zhang, Weibin Liao, Keqin Bao, Sihang Li, Shaobo Wang, Muyang Ye, Hongxin Ding, Yue Fang, Tianyi Tang, Fei Huang, Kexin Yang, Xingzhang Ren, Dayiheng Liu

entry.summary: The authors present MIMIC, a framework that uses executable code as a rigorous medium for synthesizing reasoning data, converting algorithms into verifiable reasoning trajectories via narrative fusion, code-guided test synthesis, and dynamic instrumentation. The intermediate execution states form a Code-Instrumented Reward that supplies dense process supervision for reinforcement learning without an external reward model. It matters for improving deterministic, fine-grained reasoning in LLMs that currently rely on semantic approximation.

entry.title: Register Tokens for Bounded-State Reasoning in Diffusion Language Models

author.name: Albert Ge, Chandan Singh, Yufan Zhuang, Xiaodong Liu, Jianfeng Gao, Frederic Sala

entry.summary: This work asks whether masked diffusion language models can continue reasoning after previously generated text is cleared, using only a fixed-size carried state implemented as a small set of register tokens. Models are post-trained to decode a chunk, clear it while preserving register values, and continue from the prompt plus carried state. On LLaDA and Dream backbones, registers outperform baselines, suggesting a bounded-state route to long reasoning in diffusion LMs.

entry.title: A Data-free Universal Prior over Syntactic Structures

author.name: Ferm\'{\i}n Moscoso del Prado Mart\'{\i}n

entry.summary: The author shows that a probability distribution over dependency-tree syntactic structures can emerge from a cognitively motivated model of incremental language production based on network growth, without fitting parameters to language-specific data. This suggests part of the probability structure underlying syntax may be independent of linguistic experience, with implications for language acquisition and for how LLMs assign structure probability.

entry.title: The Role of Implicit and Explicit Demographic Signals in Large Language Model-based Student Assessment

author.name: Donya Rooein, Luca Benedetto, Dirk Hovy

entry.summary: The study runs controlled prompts to test how explicit demographic mentions and implicit demographic signals from conversation history affect LLM-based essay scoring, formative feedback, and metalinguistic QA across six state-of-the-art models. It highlights the tension between legitimately using demographic context, such as adapting readability, and risking discriminatory scoring.

entry.title: ECHO: Early-layer Collaborative Hierarchical Orchestration with Bonus Logits in Speculative Decoding

author.name: Ziyang Ma, Zihong Zhang, Zuchao Li, Lefei Zhang, Baoyuan Qi, Siqi Li, Simin Yu

entry.summary: ECHO is a draft-model-free speculative decoding framework that exploits the functional asymmetry between early and late transformer layers, splitting inference into a high-frequency inner loop where early-layer bonus logits drive multi-step draft-tree exploration and a low-frequency outer loop for authoritative full-model verification. The aim is to avoid stale draft candidates and the high cost of verification.

entry.title: Vroom-Vroom at SHROOM-Visions: A Multi-Judge Committee for Detecting Hallucinated Spans in Vision-Language Outputs

author.name: Toqeer Ehsan, Nico Penttil\"a, Richard Schmidt, Arash Hajikhani, Victoria Palacin

entry.summary: This shared-task submission detects and classifies hallucinated character spans in vision-language model outputs across four languages by using several fine-tuned vision-language models as independent annotators and combining their span predictions via character-level majority voting, with additional activation probes explored. The approach ranks first in three of four languages and reaches the podium in every language and metric. The authors also observe that model disagreement mirrors human annotator disagreement.

entry.title: ECHO: A Matched-Contrast Benchmark for Context-Sensitive Turn-Taking in Full-Duplex Dialogue

author.name: Shuofeng Zhao, Hongwei Cai, Wenke Fan, Qingxiang Guo, Dawei Yang, Zhou Wang, Zhiyang Zhou, Yingxin Shang, Weixu Wang, Lin Yang, Shuran Zhou, Yang Song

entry.summary: ECHO is a paired diagnostic benchmark for Chinese full-duplex turn-taking that pairs examples with identical overlap transcripts but contrasting prior dialogue contexts, one requiring the system to yield the floor and the other to keep speaking, plus off-talk examples to diagnose unnecessary yielding. The authors introduce pair accuracy, which credits only correct decisions on both members of a pair and gives no credit to constant-action policies. This exposes whether systems genuinely use context rather than a fixed action bias.

entry.title: CLEAR: Cross-Source Evidence Adjudication for Large Language Models in Medicine

author.name: Shuai Wang, Yize Zhao, Qingyu Chen

entry.summary: CLEAR is an agentic framework for medical question answering that independently generates candidate answers from three pathways: parametric knowledge, locally curated corpora, and dynamically retrieved evidence, then adjudicates across them. It targets the problem that retrieved information may be irrelevant, incomplete, or conflicting and can actually degrade factual accuracy and evidence grounding. The design reflects the reality that medical knowledge evolves while model parameters are frozen at training time.

entry.title: VideoMM: Adaptive Macro-Micro Inference for Efficient Video MLLMs

author.name: Haoyu Guo, Yuan Feng, Junlin Lv, Mingjun Xiao, S Kevin Zhou, Xike Xie

entry.summary: VideoMM tackles the visual token explosion that bottlenecks long-form video understanding in multimodal LLMs by identifying a fundamental inefficiency: fine-grained visual detail is essential for detailed understanding but largely redundant for the preliminary task of selecting semantically relevant regions. The method introduces an adaptive macro-micro inference scheme that avoids the dilemma of lightweight encoder-driven reduction losing semantics versus heavyweight MLLM-driven reduction negating efficiency gains. This targets the cost and context-window saturation problems of scaling video MLLMs.

entry.title: Disrupted Companionship: A Risk Assessment Framework and Cross-Platform Quantitative Analysis of Psychosocial Responses to AI Companion Disruptions

author.name: Chau Do, Yunhao Yuan, Koustuv Saha, Renwen Zhang, Talayeh Aledavood

entry.summary: This study examines AI companion disruptions, platform changes that alter or terminate users' ongoing relationships with an AI, compiling 30 disruption events across major platforms and developing a taxonomy of six disruption types with three broad causes. It proposes a four-dimension risk framework covering relational discontinuity, population vulnerability, communication deficit, and transition-support deficit, then estimates community-level psychosocial responses using longitudinal Reddit data and a hierarchical Bayesian interrupted time-series model. The work quantifies real user harm from platform decisions in a fast-growing product category.

entry.title: SceneBench: A Hierarchical Benchmark for Vision-Language Understanding of 3D Scenes

author.name: Anubhav Khanal, Prabigya Acharya, Roshni Poudel, Sujan Kapali, Bigyan Bhatta, Pramish Paudel, Francois Rameau, Danda Pani Paudel

entry.summary: SceneBench is a benchmark of 966 photorealistic 3D scenes reconstructed with Gaussian Splatting and densely annotated with hierarchical semantics spanning scenes, rooms, functional areas, and object groups. It targets weaknesses in prior 3D benchmarks that use point clouds without visual texture, treat objects in isolation, and test only basic recognition. The goal is to measure multi-step 3D spatial reasoning rather than simple label recall.

entry.title: Which Pretext Task Transfers? Self-Supervised Pretraining Objectives for Lung Ultrasound

author.name: Moein Heidari, Junbo Rao, Jai Choraria, Wenjin Chen, David J. Foran, Ilker Hacihaliloglu

entry.summary: The study compares three self-supervised objective families, contrastive learning, masked reconstruction, and joint-embedding predictive architectures (JEPA), for lung ultrasound under a strictly matched protocol with the same backbone, corpus, and schedule. Encoders are pretrained on COVID-BLUeS videos and evaluated with linear, kNN, and attentive probes across several label budgets. It matters because prior ultrasound SSL comparisons varied too many factors to yield actionable guidance.

entry.title: SlotDiT: Object-Centric Representations for Diffusion Transformers

author.name: Gjergj Plepi, Sven Behnke

entry.summary: SlotDiT is a text-guided Diffusion Transformer that generates in a slot-based object-centric latent space instead of pixel or VAE latents, taking a reference image plus a language instruction as input. The motivation is that structured object-level latents could give diffusion video models explicit semantic organization, which is attractive for robotics. It is the first exploration of object-centric slots as the representation space for diffusion-based generative modeling.

entry.title: World Models for Embodied Intelligence: From Plausible to Controllable to Actionable

author.name: Nanjie Yao, Hao Wang, Chong Cheng, Zhikang Chen, Wenzhe Li, Jiafei Lyu, Li Shen, Peilin Zhao, Zongqing Lu, Gao Huang, Steven Hoi, Dacheng Tao, Deheng Ye

entry.summary: This survey reframes world-model research around three progressively stronger capability levels, plausible, controllable, and actionable, arguing that behavioral usefulness rather than visual fidelity is the right measure. It organizes the literature by which predictive capabilities actually improve action. It matters as a useful organizing framework for a fast-moving area of embodied AI.

entry.title: XPACE: Joint World and Action Modeling from Heterogeneous Experience

author.name: Jiacheng Wei, Jerry Bai, Xiaoyu Yue, Zidong Wang, Xiaoyang Guo, Cheng Chen, Fanqi Pu, Fan Wu, Zhixu Yue, Yizhuo Li, Feng Qiu, Bo Liu, Yuying Ge, Hui Zhou, Chenyi Chen, Yixiao Ge

entry.summary: XPACE is a unified embodied world model that acts both as a world action model, jointly predicting executable robot actions and future video, and as a world simulator that predicts the visual consequences of prescribed actions. Its key insight is that video prediction connects heterogeneous experience to action learning and can generate new experience for policy improvement, using a shared video backbone with action-unlabeled video plus action-labeled human and robot demonstrations.

entry.title: Hamilton-Jacobi Reachability for Hybrid Systems: Unified Goal-Driven Control with Safety Guarantees

author.name: Javier Borquez, Shuang Peng, Somil Bansal

entry.summary: This work extends classical Hamilton-Jacobi reachability, a formal verification method for continuous nonlinear systems, to hybrid dynamical systems with coupled continuous dynamics and discrete mode transitions, as found in contact-rich robotics. It characterizes safe sets through a generalized value function over both discrete and continuous states while accounting for control constraints and model uncertainty, and provides a numerical algorithm to compute it.

entry.title: Beyond Gestures: Estimating Full Hand Pose and Contact Forces from Wrist-Worn Pressure Sensor Array

author.name: Svetoslav Kolev, Lingni Ma, Michael Goesele, Renzo De Nardi, Jakob Engel, Richard Newcombe

entry.summary: This work builds a wristband with flexible capacitive pressure sensor arrays that, combined with a recurrent network, recovers continuous full-hand pose and distributed contact forces without skin-contact electrodes. The core insight is that muscle contraction and tendon displacement create wrist pressure patterns that correlate strongly with hand pose and interaction force, validated against synchronized optical motion capture. It matters for VR input, interactive computing, and high-fidelity tactile demonstrations for robot learning.

entry.title: Asclepius: An Adaptive Harness for Long-Horizon Clinical Agents

author.name: Grace Chang Yuan, Xiaoman Zhang, Sung Eun Kim, Luyang Luo, Pranav Rajpurkar

entry.summary: Using a clinical environment simulator in which an agent manages an entire emergency-department shift under continuous time and resource pressure, the authors show that current agents usually reach the correct diagnosis yet fail to deliver complete and timely critical actions. They attribute this execution gap to identifiable long-horizon failure modes such as instruction-adherence drift, and propose Asclepius, an adaptive harness that addresses them measurably within a single rollout.

entry.title: Trustworthy Agentic AI: A Comprehensive Cybersecurity and Systems Survey on Threat Landscapes, Defense Architectures, and Open Challenges

author.name: Seyedakbar Mostafavi

entry.summary: This survey frames security for agentic AI systems, where recursive reasoning loops, persistent memory, live tool execution, and multi-agent topologies dissolve classical security perimeters. It argues that natural language simultaneously acts as input data, control code, and inter-agent protocol, creating a Turing-complete blast radius in which untrusted data is executable instruction, and organizes threat landscapes, defense architectures, and open challenges into a systems-security reference framework.

entry.title: One Model, Two Physical Stories: Auditing Misalignment in Multi-Modal World Modeling

author.name: Geigh Zollicoffer, Minh Vu, Rajiv Ranasinghe, Manish Bhattarai

entry.summary: The paper audits multimodal world models for cross-modal inconsistency, where a model's generated video and its textual physical-state predictions disagree with each other even though each looks plausible in isolation. It formalizes two failure modes, internal misalignment between the model's own modalities and divergence from real-world dynamics, and tests how such inconsistencies arise.

entry.title: When Malicious Instructions Persist: Persistent Memory Poisoning Attack on Harness-Based Agents

author.name: Shuhuai Huang, Jingfeng Zhang, Hong Jia

entry.summary: The paper introduces PMPA, a persistent memory poisoning attack that embeds malicious instructions in benign external sources, inducing harness-based agents to write them into persistent memory without direct framework access. Poisoned memories are later retrieved across sessions, triggering malicious actions and privacy leakage.

entry.title: AURA: Unified Multimodal Framework for Conversational Music Editing

author.name: Quoc-Huy Trinh, Minh-Van Nguyen, Debesh Jha

entry.summary: AURA is a conversational music editing framework that uses a multimodal LLM to interpret full dialogue history plus optional reference image and audio, distilling editing intent into compact concept tokens. A concept-to-audio module injects those tokens and frame-aligned reference features into a frozen MusicGen backbone, training only 91M parameters while keeping 1.9B frozen, with experiments on Slakh2100 and MoisesDB.

entry.title: Is INT8 Portable? A Cross-Platform Measurement Study of Quantized Inference on Embedded and Automotive Accelerators

author.name: Yuyeong Shin

entry.summary: This measurement study tests the common assumption that INT8 post-training quantization is portable and predictably beneficial, benchmarking a fixed ONNX artifact across seven hardware classes including ARM/x86 CPUs, a discrete GPU, Jetson AGX Orin iGPU and NVDLA, and vendor NPUs. Portability fails on multiple axes, with the sign of the speedup determined by CPU dot-product ISA support (ARM dotprod/SDOT, x86 VNNI).

entry.title: Drift-Constrained Optimization: Only Direction Matters in Fine-Tuning Instruct Models

author.name: Fei Yuan, Changjiang Gao, Yilei Tu, Yifeng Liu, Shujian Huang, Yu Qiao

entry.summary: This paper specifies a behavioral drift budget before fine-tuning and then asks how to maximize target-task performance within that budget, arguing that locally the budget fixes distance from the reference model and leaves update direction as the only usable degree of freedom. It reformulates fine-tuning as a directionally efficient optimization problem, aiming to improve target performance without degrading existing capabilities.

entry.title: UniCAR-RL: Seeing Better before Thinking Deeper in Visual Mathematics

author.name: Yuzhe Li, Hao Yan, Hao Wang, Xingchen Liu, Ya-Qi Yu, Jihao Wu, Minghui Liao, Wei Chen, Yuliang Liu

entry.summary: UniCAR-RL is an annotation-free reinforcement learning framework for multimodal LLMs that explicitly decouples optimization of perception from optimization of reasoning, targeting the problem that fine-grained visual perception failures trigger cascading mathematical reasoning errors. The authors argue sparse end-to-end RL rewards cannot separate perceptual hallucination from logical mistakes, whereas perception-augmented chain-of-thought fine-tuning is costly and hallucination-prone, so their framework optimizes the two components in isolation.

entry.title: OpenAI4S: Code as Action, Science as Sessions

author.name: Gongbo Zhang, Hao Li, Yu Wang, Mujie Lin, Liuzhenghao Lv, Yicheng Mao, Yimi Wang, Jun Zhu, Minhan Tang, Zhengxiang Jiang, Yusong Wang, Jiayu Yao, Kunpeng Ning, Dawei Pang, Yonghong Tian, OpenAI4S Community, Yuyang Liu, Li Yuan

entry.summary: OpenAI4S is an open-source scientific research agent built on the principle of code as action and science as sessions, pairing a persistent computing runtime with research-session management. Scientific actions are complete code cells executed in persistent Python and R kernels, while an append-only action ledger, execution records, versioned artifacts and workspace checkpoints preserve inspectability, resumability and reproducibility.

entry.title: Beyond Accuracy: Robustness, Cost, and Governance Trade-offs for Vision-Language Models in Templated Document Extraction

author.name: Kushal Patel, Pushkal Shrivastava, Mackenzie Lees, Qirui Lu, Bhargobjyoti Saikia, Liying Li, Junlin Jiang

entry.summary: This measurement study evaluates eleven document-extraction systems, including three commercial models, two reasoning models, five open-source VLMs in pretrained and fine-tuned form, and a non-LLM OCR-plus-regex baseline, on a 750-document held-out pool of synthetic checks. It reports that fine-tuning on roughly 3K samples lifts the best open-source VLMs above F1 0.98, surpassing every zero-shot commercial system on this task, while the commercial pool behaves unevenly across fields and some systems collapse on specific fields such as dates. The framing is that accuracy-only evaluations mislead practitioners, so robustness, cost, and governance trade-offs must be measured together.

entry.title: When Should a World Model Move? Loss-Conditioned State Execution

author.name: Jintao Xu, Zhengyu Chen, Ben Zhang, Yongzhi Qi, Jianshen Zhang

entry.summary: The paper introduces loss-conditioned state execution, a model-agnostic decision rule for whether a world model should execute its proposed state update or retain the current state. It formalizes state movability as the existence of a loss-reducing feasible correction and distinguishes this from the benefit of any particular proposal, showing that predictive informativeness alone does not imply an update will reduce downstream loss, and even that occurrence ranking can be near perfect while persistence remains the optimal absolute-loss action. The result connects world-model rollout to decision-theoretic loss rather than prediction accuracy.

entry.title: Same Patient, Different Order: Action-Level Reliability of Clinical LLM Agents Under Repeated Runs

author.name: Rohith Reddy Bellibatlu, Manpreet Singh, Zhoutian Han, Wenbin Zhang

entry.summary: The authors show that clinical LLM agents can score identically on benchmarks while issuing materially different clinical orders across repeated identical runs. They propose a same-input rerun protocol with six reliability metrics and apply it to 1000 MedAgentBench runs across 50 tasks and small quantized open-weight models.

entry.title: Signatures of Steerability in Activation Space of Language Models

author.name: Prajjwal Bhattarai, Tuka Alhanai

entry.summary: This paper makes the dataset-dependence of activation steering more rigorous, showing that simple separation metrics in activation space strongly correlate with downstream steerability across diverse settings even after controlling for layer and dataset effects. The authors provide evidence from a synthetic superposition experiment indicating that separation underlies why some concepts steer well and others do not. It offers a predictive diagnostic for when contrastive steering vectors will work.

entry.title: Modeling, Scaling, and Decoding: Optimizing Controllable Speech Generation with Nonverbal Vocalizations

author.name: Ziyu Zhang, Yun Chen, Taihui Wang, Hanzhao Li, Qicong Xie, Rilin Chen, Zhixian Zhao, Lei Xie

entry.summary: The authors build an NVV-aware DiTAR speech synthesis system that models continuous speech latents, represents 16 nonverbal vocalization categories as dedicated tokens, and adjusts stop prediction to separate mid-utterance vocalizations from utterance ends. Training uses bilingual large-scale pretraining, targeted synthetic augmentation, and frequency-aware rebalancing, with inference-time acoustic prompt selection and decoding strategies.

entry.title: EdgeHAR: An Edge-Native Compact Sensor Foundation Model for Human Activity Recognition

author.name: He Zhang, Siyu Yuan, Siyu Liu, Sizhen Bian, Bin Guo

entry.summary: EdgeHAR is a compact sensor foundation model for wearable human activity recognition that factorizes signals into three latent codes: an activity-semantic code for reusable activity knowledge, a motion-dynamics code for temporal patterns, and a third disentangling acquisition variation. The factorization is intended to survive shifts in users, devices, sampling rates, and sensor placements while remaining edge-deployable.

entry.title: Loop-Back Authority in LLM Agent Teams: A Paired Experiment on Flat and Hierarchical Coordination

author.name: Burak Agachan, Max van Duijn, Amirhossein Zohrehvand

entry.summary: This paired experiment holds five LLM agents, their roles, prompts, tools, models, and data fixed while varying only whether a Manager agent may reject worker output and require revision. It tests the default hierarchical orchestration pattern in production multi-agent frameworks against organizational theory predictions and concerns about sycophancy and degeneration of thought. It matters because open-ended tasks had not previously isolated the authority link from other framework differences.

entry.title: Efficiency Hallucination: Formalizing and Measuring Behavioral Calibration in LLM-Based Code Optimization

author.name: Sarah Wilson, Gail Kaiser, Patrick Musau

entry.summary: The authors name and formalize the Efficiency Hallucination: LLMs issuing non-functional code mutations with unsubstantiated performance claims on already-optimal code, driven by an Evaluation Trap where binary benchmarks reward unnecessary edits over safe abstention. Using classification penalty methods across 180 optimization runs on nine models with EffiBench, they find a 100 percent over-edit rate on optimal code under standard prompts, and their guardrail raises correct abstention from 0 to 44.4 percent while preserving full edit rates on sub-optimal code. It matters because it reframes LLM code-optimization reliability as a calibration problem.

entry.title: Neural-Network Solutions to Real-Space Charge Density and Generalization

author.name: Yuxuan Zeng, Taoyuze Lv, Zhicheng Zhong

entry.summary: The authors propose AIDEN, an Atomic-Interaction Density Equivariant Network for solving real-space ground-state charge density, motivated by the Hohenberg-Kohn theorem that the ground-state density contains all ground-state information. AIDEN separates elemental contributions and is designed as a deep learning surrogate that avoids the iterative self-consistent-field cost of Kohn-Sham DFT, with emphasis on generalization. It matters for accelerating computer-aided materials design.

entry.title: PIDS-Bench: Evaluating Prompt-Injection Detectors Under Over-Defense, Obfuscation, and Distribution Shift

author.name: Yusuf Khalid Shire, Sang-Chul Kim

entry.summary: PIDS-Bench is a frozen multi-axis benchmark that jointly evaluates prompt-injection attack detection and benign false-positive behavior at fixed thresholds, covering in-distribution inputs, hard-benign prompts that mimic injection structure without malicious intent, obfuscated attacks, and domain and structural distribution shifts. It evaluates seven detectors including learned baselines, external prompt-injection classifiers, and broad-safety comparators. It matters because aggregate F1 on in-distribution data hides the operational cost of over-defense and the fragility of detectors under shift.

entry.title: Not All Prompts Are Equal: Exploration-Guided Prompt Scaffolding for Multimodal Reinforcement Post-Training

author.name: Yuanhao Yue, Qianli Ma, Chengyu Wang, Haoting Wang, Lei Shen, Jun Huang

entry.summary: The authors argue that rollout budget in online RL post-training of multimodal LLMs is wasted on prompts that are already saturated or hopelessly hard, and propose an exploration-guided scaffolding framework that reshapes the training prompt distribution over time. Its core measure, the Exploration Potential Score, is a cheap rollout-derived proxy grounded in KL-regularized policy improvement theory and computable from on-policy statistics without extra overhead. This matters because prompt-level allocation is a relatively underexplored lever for making multimodal RL post-training more sample-efficient.

entry.title: MoME: Mixture-of-Memory Embeddings for Context-Aware Sparse Lookup

author.name: Muchen Li, Leonid Sigal, Renjie Liao

entry.summary: Conditional memory mechanisms augment language models with token-indexed embedding tables for cheap parametric lookup, but existing methods retrieve by surface form, collapsing senses like python the language and python the animal into one entry. Mixture of Memory Embeddings replaces each token's single memory row with a mixture of multiple slots selected by a learned gate over the hidden state, making lookups context-dependent at each position. This matters as a lightweight capacity/scaling alternative that improves on deterministic memory retrieval in controlled pretraining experiments.

entry.title: Planning in the Backbone: DiffAdapterVLA for Native Continuous Trajectory Generation with Driving VLMs

author.name: Changxin Lu, Xiaoliang Meng, Yu Wu, Rui Huang, Honglin Li, Tao Chen, Kaixuan Zhou, Yadong Shao

entry.summary: DiffAdapterVLA injects explicit trajectory tokens into selected late layers of a pretrained driving vision-language model so trajectory state co-evolves with driving conditions during backbone forward computation. Lightweight layer-wise diffusion adapters organize this into continuous trajectory generation, moving planning inside the VLM rather than bolting it on after condition formation.

entry.title: KaiNinja: Extending Native 3D Generators to the Part Level

author.name: Ruihan Yu, Lian Fu, Muyao Niu, Zheng-hui Huang, Yu-Ju Tsai, Sho Kuno, Fengbo Lan, Yonghao Yu, Erwin Wu, Ming-Hsuan Yang, Kaipeng Zhang, Zhixiang Wang

entry.summary: KaiNinja extends image-to-3D generators like TRELLIS.2 from producing a single fused mesh to producing part-level assets suitable for editing, rigging, and simulation. The key technical obstacle is that the O-Voxel grid stores only one surface sheet per voxel, so touching-part interfaces cannot be represented, motivating a dual-volume representation. Avoiding a separate 3D segmentation stage makes the pipeline simpler and potentially faster than post-hoc segmentation.

entry.title: Efficient Reasoning Distillation: Small Video-Language Models via Synthetic CoT and Difficulty-Aware Fine-Tuning

author.name: Mantek Singh, Jeshwanth Challagundla, Siddharth Raina, Jasmin Jarsania

entry.summary: This paper distills reasoning into a 2B-parameter video-language model using roughly 900 uncertainty-selected examples annotated with synthetic chain-of-thought rationales from a 4B teacher, training for under two hours on a single A100. The resulting model outperforms VLMs up to four times larger and generalizes across CinePile, ActivityNet-QA, and MLVU, approaching its teacher. A notable finding is that placing chain-of-thought rationales after the answer improves reasoning in compact models, contrary to standard prompting practice.

entry.title: Interpreting and Steering LLM Agents for Social Simulations

author.name: Jiayue Gaveal Fan, Arul Murugan, Shreyas Krishnan, Abhishek Nagaraj

entry.summary: The paper argues that LLM-based social simulations are limited as social-science instruments because the models are black boxes lacking interpretability, meaning clear mechanisms driving behavior, and steerability, meaning the ability to mute or amplify specific theoretically meaningful mechanisms. The authors compare three classes of intervention, starting with prompt-based manipulation, to show how simulation behavior can be both explained and controlled. It matters because simulation-based social science needs mechanisms that can be attributed and manipulated, not just behavioral mimicry.

entry.title: Right Direction, Wrong Step: Geometric Analysis of Finite-Step Failure in Looped Transformers

author.name: Zhihao Guo, Zonghan Wu, Haizhou Du, Huan Huo, Yilei Shao, Athanasios V. Vasilakos, Qingsong Wen

entry.summary: Looped transformers reuse shared layers for iterative latent reasoning but sometimes lose support for the correct answer as iterations increase. The authors separate whether an update's direction is locally unhelpful from whether its full displacement overshoots, by measuring reference utility along the model's own update direction at varying step fractions. A pathwise curvature decomposition explains how initial progress is lost, and a local quadratic model predicts full-step gains.

entry.title: SOTER: A Generative Time-Series Foundation Model for Wearable Human Physiological Signals

author.name: Fangke Chen, Sirry Chen, Wei Chen, Zhongyu Wei

entry.summary: Existing time-series foundation models do not match wearable physiological signals, which are multichannel, irregularly sampled, noisy and governed by coupled continuous-time dynamics across spectral scales. SOTER unifies cross-channel coupling, power-spectral-density-guided mixture-of-experts routing and continuous-time latent evolution inside one pretraining framework. It is a foundation-model attempt tailored to the structure of human physiological data rather than generic sequences.

entry.title: Can Deep Learning Achieve Cross-Physics Mapping?

author.name: Pengfei Zhu, Julien Lecompagnon, Mathias Ziegler

entry.summary: The authors introduce Cross-Physics Mapping (CPM), an operator-learning framework that translates fields between physical domains governed by different PDEs (e.g. parabolic diffusion vs hyperbolic wave equations). They derive sufficient conditions based on compatible latent representations and propose a dimensionless scaling principle that aligns source and target evolution scales without assuming dynamical equivalence, testing it on paired diffusion/wave fields with shared latent geometry.

entry.title: Same Flow, Different Paths: Variance Reduction in Flow Matching

author.name: Alexander Tyurin

entry.summary: The paper analyzes how the choice of interpolation path in flow matching affects the variance of stochastic gradients even when the marginal distributions, marginal velocity field, and FM objective are identical. For a linear velocity model with one-dimensional Gaussian data the author derives a tight bound on SGD iteration complexity, showing path choice can fundamentally change convergence rate.

entry.title: Knowledge as Orbit: Finite Collections as Phases of an Exactly Periodic Latent Generator

author.name: Siddharth Pal, Viktoria Rojkova

entry.summary: This paper proposes storing a finite collection of items intensionally rather than extensionally: each item is encoded as a phase of a fixed rotation in a learned latent space, decoded by a shared network. Exact closure is guaranteed by construction using a Fourier-style rotation bank so that R^X equals identity, tested on images and looping video where phase order is inherent temporal structure.

entry.title: Certified Inference and Training for Deep Equilibrium Networks: A Continuation Framework with Polynomial Complexity Guarantees

author.name: Alex Borisevich

entry.summary: This work develops a certified continuation framework for equilibrium computation and training of deep equilibrium networks, formulating training as interpolation to a target accuracy. It uses homotopy to select a unique solution branch for inference and a rounded Newton tracker with certified bounds, plus dormant bilinear rank-one channels to repair failed training passes. The contribution is a rare set of polynomial complexity guarantees for DEQ inference and training.

entry.title: Seeing What Matters: Visual Cue Guided Video Planning for Generalizable Robot Navigation

author.name: Hojin Lee, Sizhe Lester Li, Maximilian Hilger, Susie Lu, Achim J. Lilienthal, Vincent Sitzmann, Daniel A. Duecker

entry.summary: CueNav is a navigation framework that combines visual-cue-guided video planning with an embodiment-specific inverse-dynamics model. It uses a bird's-eye-view map to convey global task context and retains part of the robot body in the egocentric view to expose embodiment context, guiding a generative video planner that predicts future observations. The inverse-dynamics model then translates the video plan into actions for longer-horizon navigation.

entry.title: On the disintegration of the stochastic majority vote: From PAC-Bayesian bounds to a self-bounding algorithm

author.name: Julien Bastian (LabHC), Benjamin Leblanc (LabHC, UJM, MALICE), Pascal Germain (LabHC, UJM, MALICE), Amaury Habrard (LabHC, UJM, MALICE), Guillaume Metzler (ERIC), Emilie Morvant (LabHC), Paul Viallard (MALT)

entry.summary: This paper proposes a derandomization framework for stochastic majority votes, converting PAC-Bayesian generalization guarantees for randomized ensembles into certificates for a single deterministic majority vote. It applies recent disintegrated PAC-Bayesian theory to the space of majority-vote weight vectors and derives a self-bounding algorithm. The aim is to retain tight guarantees while removing the randomness that makes such models less deployable.

entry.title: The Immutable Past: Formalizing State Mutability and Conflict Resolution in Mutable RAG

author.name: Hamed HaddadPajouh, Amir AmiriTabat

entry.summary: This paper formalizes failure modes of treating retrieval-augmented generation memory as an append-only stream, naming Semantic Shadowing, where stale conflicting observations accumulate and dominate recent valid updates. It proves that standard dense retrieval suffers asymptotic recall decay and identifies a Majority Vote Trap in which larger retrieval context windows degrade accuracy by dilution. The analysis matters for designing memory architectures for long-horizon autonomous agents operating in dynamic environments.

entry.title: Rewarding Reasoning, Not Answers: Fixing and Bounding Test-Time Reinforcement Learning on Medical QA

author.name: Kailong Fan, Anqi Pu, Yichen Wu, Wanhua Li, Yicong Li, Hanspeter Pfister, Huafeng Liu, Xiang Li, Quanzheng Li, Ning Guo

entry.summary: This paper shows that test-time reinforcement learning with majority-vote pseudo-labels, which works well in mathematics, collapses on medical multiple-choice QA, with accuracy stagnating and output diversity declining. A controlled experiment holding questions, model, and optimizer fixed while varying only the answer space traces the failure to answer-space structure rather than domain difficulty. The authors propose PROSE, a process-reward-guided self-training method that rewards reasoning quality instead of final answers.

entry.title: Japanese Stroke LLM Evaluation: A Conversational Benchmark for Safe Stroke Care in Japanese Using Large Language Models

author.name: Keisuke Masuda, Kazutaka Yatsushiro, Hirohumi Iwamoto, Hirofumi Hirano, Ryosuke Hanaya

entry.summary: This paper introduces a multi-turn, Japanese-language benchmark for evaluating LLMs as physicians in stroke care, using ten clinical cases with a board-certified neurosurgeon acting as both simulated patient and evaluator. It scores history-taking and clinical action phases under practice-oriented conditions, testing whether models can assess urgency and avoid unsafe recommendations rather than merely answer multiple-choice medical questions.

entry.title: Target-Language Generation in Multilingual Models: Activation Steering and Optimal Control

author.name: James A. Michaelov, Carmen Amo Alonso, Tyler A. Chang, Roger P. Levy

entry.summary: This paper develops an optimal control method for forcing multilingual models to generate in a specified target language, alongside a framework that evaluates output quality along language adherence, linguistic coherence, and semantic coherence. The approach matches or beats difference-in-means activation steering for most tested models while requiring substantially less hyperparameter tuning.

entry.title: What Breaks Under Pruning in Smart Homes, and When? Evaluating LLM Degradation Across Architectures and Task Complexity

author.name: Congjing Zhang, Vashishtha Patil, Henning Lange, Usman Aleem

entry.summary: This study systematically examines how pruning affects context-grounded tool calling in smart homes, testing four LLMs spanning dense Transformer, dense hybrid, and mixture-of-experts architectures with depth, width, hybrid, and expert pruning methods. After post-pruning supervised fine-tuning, they evaluate over 19,500 instances from three smart-home datasets and characterize degradation by action component (operation, device, argument, value) and by task complexity. Dense models show narrow safe pruning regions, revealing where compression silently breaks agentic behavior.

entry.title: Beyond Cultural Knowledge: Evaluating Arabic Cultural Appropriateness of Large Language Models

author.name: Enes Altinisik, Hamdy Mubarak, Masoomali Fatehkia, Husrev_Taha_Sencar Husrev Taha Sencar

entry.summary: The authors release AraBehave, 1,623 culturally grounded open-ended Arabic prompts with 29,214 cultural-appropriateness judgments from native speakers across Arab regions, plus a scoring model correlating strongly with human judgments (Pearson r=0.74). Evaluating three Arabic-centric and three frontier LLMs, they find cultural appropriateness decomposes into two largely independent components, normative stance and grounding, rather than being a single capability. This shifts cultural evaluation from what models know to how they behave in open-ended advice.

entry.title: Where Post-Training Quantization Breaks Text Embedders: A Measured Map Across Four Embedder Families

author.name: Hyojung Han

entry.summary: This paper tests received wisdom about weight-only post-training quantization, such as protecting the embedding table and preferring ranking-aware objectives, directly on retrieval embedders. It quantizes five checkpoints from four architecture families across a grid of bit widths and group sizes while isolating embedding, attention, and feed-forward blocks. The headline finding is that every heuristic fails to transfer as stated, with the embedding table never emerging as the dominant protection priority despite being the largest tensor in several families.

entry.title: ThinkFlow: Self-Evolving Probabilistic Latent Memory for Lifelong Conversational Agents

author.name: Cai Ke, Xin Liu, Han Zhang, Jiangyue Yan, Zike Yuan, Ling Deng, Yue Yu, Hui Wang, Ruifeng Xu

entry.summary: ThinkFlow is an end-to-end latent memory framework for lifelong conversational agents that bypasses the information bottleneck of explicit textual memory pipelines by dynamically maintaining memory in latent space. Inspired by cognitive science accounts of mental models refined through predictive coding, it aims to preserve subtle behavioral patterns and emotional shifts that text-based pipelines lose. It also addresses the static post-deployment nature of existing memory systems by allowing autonomous adaptation to user habits without manual feedback.

entry.title: Shared-Prefix KV Reuse Across Standard LoRA Adapters: Quality and Serving Tradeoffs

author.name: Dushyant Rajput

entry.summary: This paper studies a practical serving question: for already-trained standard LoRA adapters sharing one backbone, how much task quality is preserved if the backbone prefill KV cache is computed once and reused across specialists, and what it saves in serving cost. On a Qwen3-1.7B backbone with two adapters for extractive QA on HotpotQA and arithmetic reasoning on GSM8K, it sweeps the boundary at which the specialist takes over from the reused base cache and measures paired quality differences and serving cost. The work deliberately avoids adapters retrained for cache compatibility.

entry.title: Hyperbolic Contrastive Learning with Entailment for Spatial Transcriptomics

author.name: Daniela Vega, Paula C\'ardenas, Hannah Ceballos, Leonardo Manrique, Pablo Arbela\'ez

entry.summary: This work predicts spatial gene expression from histopathology images, addressing common failures of over-smoothed, overly uniform predictions by learning representations that reflect the hierarchical and asymmetric structure of gene regulation. It uses hyperbolic contrastive learning with an entailment objective to encode that hierarchy. The contribution matters for making spatial transcriptomics cheaper and more scalable in biomedical research.

entry.title: ProtoLIP: From Sentence-Level to Object-Level Evidence Disentanglement

author.name: Yan Zhu, Yongbo Chen, Zhengming Ding, Rebecca Faust

entry.summary: The authors show that query-conditioned vision-language models entangle evidence from co-occurring objects and shared context, so object-level queries do not isolate the evidence actually driving a prediction. ProtoLIP adds a lightweight prototype-mediated evidence layer that organizes reusable visual prototypes into text-derived semantic families and routes queries through them. This matters for interpretability and for making VLM explanations faithful to object-level predictions.

entry.title: EgoPathBench: Evaluating Zero-Shot Egocentric Waypoint Decision-Making in Vision-Language Models

author.name: Yang Zhao, Zhuo Chen, Xubo Yang

entry.summary: EgoPathBench is a dataset and five-task benchmark for first-person waypoint decision-making, testing whether VLMs can select a feasible sequence of spatial actions that reaches a goal from a single egocentric observation. It targets a gap where existing spatial-intelligence benchmarks only probe isolated judgments of relations, directions, or targets rather than integrated target recognition, action-consequence assessment, distance estimation, and planning. The work matters for evaluating embodied and navigation-capable foundation models.

entry.title: High-Fidelity Video Quality Assessment with VQA-Specific Saliency

author.name: Hakan Emre Gedik, Shashank Gupta, Alan Bovik

entry.summary: HFVQA tackles no-reference video quality assessment under the tension between needing full-resolution spatial and dense temporal cues and the cost of running deep models on video. The framework uses fixed-size spatio-temporal processing plus VQA-specific saliency so that pretrained video foundation models can be reused without destructive preprocessing such as fragmentation. The contribution targets accurate quality prediction at practical compute.

entry.title: PanoGS-SLAM: Panoramic 3D Gaussian Splatting SLAM

author.name: Yongqi Mao, Hao Shi, Yufan Zhang, Zhonghua Yi, Xiangfei Guo, Kaiwei Wang

entry.summary: PanoGS-SLAM is presented as the first panoramic dense SLAM system built on 3D Gaussian Splatting, performing differentiable rendering and pose optimization directly in the spherical domain. This gives omnidirectional photometric constraints, which the authors argue improves tracking stability compared with narrow field-of-view pinhole 3DGS SLAM under fast motion and large viewpoint change. The work targets robotics localization and mapping in dynamic environments.

entry.title: Rethinking Visual Embodiment Dependence in Visuomotor Policies

author.name: Hongjie Fang, Yuxuan Lu, Chenxi Wang, Haoxiang Qin, Shirun Tang, Zihao He, Shangning Xia, Jingjing Chen, Wanxi Liu, Shiquan Wang, Cewu Lu

entry.summary: This paper studies visual embodiment dependence (VED), the tendency of visuomotor policies to use visible robot configuration as a shortcut for judging task progress, demonstrated through cue-conflict interventions on representative policies. Rather than removing VED, the authors propose structuring it via embodiment canonicalization in 3D point clouds, replacing the robot body with a canonical end-effector representation that keeps control-relevant geometry while abstracting away morphology.

entry.title: Shallow Beliefs: Midtraining does not inoculate against EM from reward hacking

author.name: Jozdien

entry.summary: This post summarizes an experiment testing whether synthetic document finetuning can install beliefs that inoculate a model against emergent misalignment from RL-induced reward hacking. Finetuning Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct on roughly 56K documents framing reward hacking as acceptable caused the model to express that belief on behavioral tests, yet it showed stronger misalignment generalization once trained to reward hack on coding problems with faulty tests. The result matters because it suggests belief editing via synthetic documents can be shallow and may not confer the intended robustness.

entry.title: Bridging the Modality Gap in Long-Form Clinical Audio: A Comparative Study of Lightweight and Heavyweight End-to-End SOAP Generation

author.name: Ziyu Zhang, Mingchen Shao, Wenjie Tian, Tianlun Zuo, Longhao Li, Lei Xie

entry.summary: For the BeTraC 2026 challenge, this team builds a fully end-to-end multimodal system that generates structured SOAP notes directly from long-form doctor-patient audio, bypassing intermediate transcripts. Using a 1.41-million-sample multi-task corpus and a pipeline of domain pretraining, supervised fine-tuning, and reward optimization, they compare 3B lightweight and 30B heavyweight configurations.

entry.title: Per-Matrix Optimality Is Not Enough: Three-Level Optimization for Low-Rank LLM Compression

author.name: Huicheng Zhang, Xiyao Feng, Ze-Tong Li, Chengkai Zhu, Xiao Shi, Xiwei Pan, Jinguo Liu, Ge Bai, Xin Wang

entry.summary: This paper argues that Eckart-Young-optimal per-matrix SVD truncation is insufficient because errors from independently compressed matrices compound nonlinearly through Transformer blocks. It introduces a three-level chain that widens optimization scope from individual matrices (whitened SVD) to blocks (joint optimization) to the full model (end-to-end language-modeling loss refinement), using only 256 calibration sequences and no instruction or recovery data. On LLaMA-7B at 60 percent compression, WikiText-2 perplexity drops from 42.1 to 19.1 to 11.4 across the stages.

entry.title: Safe Error Correction for Language Models: Frozen-Base Adjustment with Capability Preservation

author.name: Gautam Kishore

entry.summary: The paper proposes CRN v2, a lightweight logit-level correction module of roughly 34M trainable parameters (0.73% of the frozen 4.65B base text module) sitting atop a fully frozen Gemma 4 E2B model. Trained with SFT followed by reference-free DPO on 83,400 error-correction pairs, it corrects 53.3% of base-model errors on a 60-question domain exam while showing no degradation on MMLU and similar capability benchmarks.

entry.title: OptiPrime: Optimizing Private Inference through Protocol-Hardware Co-design

author.name: Jiangrui Yu, Ye Yu, Si Chen, Chenqi Lin, Wenxuan Zeng, Junfeng Fan, Mingyu Gao, Meng Li

entry.summary: OptiPrime addresses the latency of private DNN inference using hybrid homomorphic encryption and multi-party computation. The authors observe that dropping a commercial HE accelerator into state-of-the-art HE-MPC frameworks yields only limited end-to-end gains because of wireless ciphertext transmission bottlenecks between HE operations, and they propose a protocol-hardware co-design to overcome it. The work aims to make formal privacy guarantees practical for private inference.

entry.title: MechReason: Benchmarking Multi-Image Multi-Hop Reasoning in Mechanical Engineering

author.name: Tengyue Wang, Kang An, Chenxu Du, Zhongyu Yang, Yuanchi Zhu, Xinqi Yang, Hebao Zhu, Ziliang Wang, FaQiang Qian, Yunli Yang, Qibing Ren

entry.summary: This paper introduces MechReason, a benchmark of roughly 12,000 question-answer pairs mined from real mechanical engineering publications, designed to test whether multimodal LLMs can combine multiple images, textual conditions, physical principles, and engineering constraints into multi-step reasoning. It fills a gap left by existing benchmarks that only probe drawing recognition, CAD interpretation, or single-chart queries. The work matters because it targets a high-stakes professional domain where current models are largely untested.

entry.title: G3AR: Graph-Guided Neural Visual Geometry for Scalable Multi-Sequence Aerial Registration

author.name: Jeng Wen Joshua Lean, Ting-Yu Yen, Wei-Fang Sun, Simon See, Hung-Kuo Chu, Shih-Hsuan Hung

entry.summary: G3AR addresses scalable neural geometry for large aerial image collections, where full-context inference is infeasible and naive sequence chunking misses irregular non-local overlap. It builds a geometrically verified image-proximity graph that defines bounded overlapping chunks and a chunk graph whose maximum spanning tree sets the alignment topology, then uses shared-image predictions to estimate Sim(3) transforms registering local geometry into a common frame. It matters for large-scale aerial mapping and 3D reconstruction.

entry.title: Vibe Patenting: Evaluating LLM Judges for Professional Patent-Drafting Agents

author.name: Toshiaki Koike-Akino, Vlad Blaykhman, Ye Wang, Jing Liu, Gene V. Vinokur

entry.summary: This work builds an end-to-end patent-drafting testbed in which a separately invoked LLM judge evaluates generated drafts and supplies structured feedback for iterative revision by a drafting agent. Across multiple inventions and agent configurations, judge-guided revision consistently improves judged quality while unguided revision saturates, and iterative judge feedback lets a cheaper low-reasoning agent approach a much more expensive high-reasoning one.

entry.title: How User-AI Mistreatment Occurs and Matters in Conversational Systems?

author.name: Fanqi Zeng, Sadid A. Hasan, Chaocheng He

entry.summary: Shifting attention from model-generated harms, this paper audits hundreds of thousands of English conversations from a public chat dataset using two independent detectors: a lexicon of hostility directed at the assistant and the dataset's native moderation signal. It finds that the two capture different, only weakly overlapping phenomena, with moderation flags dominated by toxic-content solicitation rather than hostility aimed at the model.

entry.title: Safety as a Constraint: Fine-Tuning a LLM Recommender to Explain Itself

author.name: Jiashu He, Emma Yanyang Kong, JJ Tan, David Fagnan

entry.summary: The authors fine-tune a recommender LLM to generate personalized explanations for its recommendations based on a user's viewing history at a large video streaming service, instead of paying the cost and latency of calling a frontier model at serving time. They impose constraints that explanations be faithful to input elements and safe, framing safety as an optimization constraint rather than a post-hoc filter.

entry.title: Towards a knowledge-enhanced single-cell foundation model

author.name: Hanqing Zhang, Jie Bao, Mei Ma, Shuai Liu, Jiaying Ma, Jiaguan Liu, Jiaxiao Li, Zhenbo Li, Wenwen Gong, Zhijun Ca

entry.summary: The authors show that scaling transcriptomic pretraining data yields diminishing returns, whereas adding biological knowledge such as cell-level text annotation and gene-level regulatory information opens an additional scaling dimension. They present scKITE, a single-cell foundation model that injects these signals through lightweight auxiliary decoders that are discarded after pretraining.

entry.title: The average-farmer illusion in language-model simulations of agricultural decisions

author.name: Zhanliang Zhu, Ziwei Li, Yuchen Liu, Liujun Zhu, Ruiqi Wu, Tongqing Shen, Junliang Jin, Jianyun Zhang

entry.summary: The authors compare Claude, Codex and Kimi against matched farmer decisions from China and four African countries under four prespecified prompt designs. Some configurations reproduce observed means and adoption rates, but person-level predictions are weak, decisions cluster near typical values, and a simple generator fitted only to observed marginals matches them, exposing an average-farmer illusion.

entry.title: EvoOntology: A Self-Evolving Ontology Layer for Data Agents

author.name: Meiduo Chong, Shaolei Zhang, Ju Fan, Xiaoyong Du

entry.summary: EvoOntology addresses the agent-data gap in which heterogeneous data sources such as tables, files, and databases live outside an agent that can only reach them through generic tools. It introduces a self-evolving ontology layer exposed as an MCP server with schema and content layers, replacing both raw source exploration and hand-written semantic layers injected into prompts. The design aims to scale to large heterogeneous stores and adapt to different agent behaviors.

entry.title: LongAgent: History-Guided Agentic Search for Longitudinal Outcome Prediction

author.name: Siyao Wang, Florian Guitton, Shuojie Fu, Guanyu Tao, Kai Sun, Wenjia Bai

entry.summary: LongAgent is an agent-based approach for longitudinal medical outcome prediction that autonomously searches over combinations of variable sets, temporal windows, and longitudinal aggregation functions to find candidates with predictive value. It is motivated by the heterogeneity of medical datasets, where variables come from different sources, at different temporal spacings, and capture different aspects of health. The method targets feature and aggregation discovery rather than fixed hand-engineered representations.

entry.title: From Process Loss to Assembly Bonus: Human-Grounded Diagnosis of Multi-Agent LLM Collaboration

author.name: Ala N. Tak, Teruhisa Misu, Kumar Akash, Zhaobo K. Zheng, Kevin H. Joo, Jonathan Gratch

entry.summary: The authors compare human group chats with matched LLM deliberation traces on Wason-style deduction and then test whether the same process signatures generalize to analogical, abductive, and analytical tasks. Both humans and LLM groups show an assembly bonus asymmetry where discussion helps the average member more than the best initial member, with initial-answer diversity explaining much of the effect. It matters for whether LLM groups can legitimately stand in as models of human collaborative reasoning.

entry.title: An Efficient and Modular Framework for Targeted Harm Mitigation in LLMS

author.name: Roberto Campbell, Momin Abbass, Muneeza Azmat, Michal Ulewicz, Raya Horesh, Kristjan Greenewald, Rog\'erio Abreu de Paula, Nathalie Baracaldo

entry.summary: The paper proposes a modular alignment approach that augments pretrained LLMs with Activated LoRA adapters and a context-aware routing mechanism, letting specialized expert adapters activate mid-sequence without invalidating the KV cache. Each expert targets a specific harm such as bias or toxicity, enabling low-latency, targeted correction during generation.

entry.title: LIMBO: Lifelong Inference-Time Memory and Budget Optimization for LLM Agents

author.name: Siddharth Sharma, Nilesh Prasad Pandey, Onat Gungor, Tajana Rosing

entry.summary: LIMBO frames experience replay in lifelong LLM agents as an inference-time memory allocation problem, since every replayed trajectory competes with retrieval, reasoning, tool use and verification for the same limited prompt and compute budget. The authors argue fixed replay policies waste resources when replay is unhelpful for the current task, and propose dynamic allocation of memory and compute. It targets continual capability acquisition without forgetting in agent workflows.

entry.title: Lightweight Generalized DeepFake Face Detection with WAVIE: Wavelet Augmented Vision Intermediate Embeddings

author.name: Arya Pulkit, Aditya Ruhela, Akarshan Kapoor, Arnav Bhavsar

entry.summary: WAVIE is an end-to-end deepfake face detector that adds complementary spatial and frequency cues on top of a frozen CLIP backbone, projecting intermediate transformer embeddings through a lightweight learned wavelet-augmented module. The goal is to close the generalization gap that causes sharp accuracy drops on unseen manipulation pipelines while keeping the model lightweight.

entry.title: Disentangling Topology and Diversity in Multi-Agent LLMs for Multilingual Low-Resource Emotion Detection

author.name: Ulugbek Shernazarov, Charitha Ruwansiri Weerakon Basnayake, Abdelkhaleq El Jarjini, Noel Crespi, Praboda Rajapaksha

entry.summary: This study separates two factors usually confounded in multi-agent LLM work: inference topology (parallel aggregation versus sequential refinement) and inter-agent diversity (stochastic sampling, role prompting, learned QLoRA specialization), forming a controlled 2x3 matrix under a fixed three-call budget. Testing Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct and Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct across nine languages for low-resource emotion detection, parallel learned specialization performed best.

entry.title: SeqMaestro: From nucleotide sequences to biological hypotheses through interpretable machine learning

author.name: Evgeny S. Saveliev, Krzysztof Kacprzyk, Charlotte Capitanchik, Neelanjan Mukherjee, Kate Matlin, Ryan Sheridan, Srinivas Ramachandran, Jernej Ule, David L. Bentley, Mihaela van der Schaar

entry.summary: SeqMaestro is a machine learning framework that operates directly on nucleotide sequences while producing human-understandable representations, bridging interpretable methods such as sparse linear models and decision trees with the raw-sequence flexibility of deep learning. It targets regulatory genomics, evolutionary biology, and phenotype prediction, where classical motif and k-mer methods are interpretable but inflexible and deep models are powerful but opaque. It matters for turning sequence models into generators of biological hypotheses rather than black-box predictors.

entry.title: Steering Generative Robot Policies with Lexicographic Preferences

author.name: Yixuan Jia, Jonathan P. How

entry.summary: The paper shows that a frozen generative robot policy based on diffusion or flow matching can be steered at inference time to respect lexicographically ordered deployment objectives, such as embodiment-specific feasibility constraints first and user preferences second. This addresses deployment-time requirements and preference priorities that were not represented during training and may vary across deployments. It matters for adapting pretrained robot policies without retraining or fine-tuning.

entry.title: Refinement-based Flow Policy Optimization

author.name: Bumgeun Park, Hyukjun Yang, Donghwan Lee

entry.summary: Flow-based policies are expressive for online reinforcement learning, but standard flow matching needs samples from the target distribution, which is unavailable when the action distribution is only defined implicitly by a Q-function. The authors propose Refinement-Based Flow Policy Optimization, which alternates between Q-guided stochastic refinement of noise-initialized actions and self-target flow matching. It matters as a way to bring flow-based generative policies into the standard online RL loop where action densities are intractable.

entry.title: IWC-Bench: Evaluating Web Application Generation from a Software Testing Perspective

author.name: Chenxu Liu, Zilu Zou, Peizhong Gao, Jiawen Tao, Zhexin Zhang, Guang Chen, Haowei Lin, Ying Zhou, Tianyi Bai, Dolly Deng, Suncong Zheng, Maxm Pan

entry.summary: IWC-Bench is an interactive benchmark for LLM-generated web applications that instruments each generated app and uses code coverage to guide an agent's exploration of its functionality. This addresses the flaws of static benchmarks that credit unreachable code and of interactive benchmarks that miss functionality due to incomplete exploration.

entry.title: ModaLens: Measuring Image Sensitivity in Report-Conditioned Medical VLMs

author.name: Sebasti\'an Andr\'es Cajas Ord\'o\~nez, Maximin Lange, Quang Bui, Anqi Peter Li, Felipe Ocampo Osorio, Rafi Al Attrach, Kushul Reddy Palakala, Sahil Kapadia, Zakaria Laouabdia Sellami, Xinyue Zhang, Ashley Zhang, Leo Anthony Celi

entry.summary: ModaLens is a paired image-swap audit that measures whether a medical vision-language model actually uses the image when a radiology report is also supplied. Testing MedGemma-27B on 3,199 paired MIMIC-CXR cases, the authors find answer changes on 4.26 percent of trials with the report versus 20.94 percent without, showing report availability sharply reduces image sensitivity. This matters because it exposes a shortcut behavior that could make report-conditioned medical VLMs unsafe or misleading in clinical deployment.

entry.title: Scaling Laws for Physics-Aware ACOPF Surrogate Learning

author.name: Yijiang Li, Emon Dey, Stefano Fenu, Massimiliano Lupo Pasini, Teja Kuruganti, Kibaek Kim

entry.summary: The authors sweep model and dataset sizes for AC optimal power flow surrogates under both MSE and augmented-Lagrangian (physics-aware) training objectives, characterizing how constraint violation scales with network size across grids. Both objectives improve as power laws but at different rates: MSE appears governed mainly by model capacity, while the augmented Lagrangian is balanced across capacity and data, and violation grows about twice as fast with scale under MSE. It matters for deciding how to size learning-based surrogates that must be physically feasible, not merely accurate.

entry.title: Continuous-Time Machine Learning: A Unified Mathematical Perspective

author.name: Waleed Razzaq, Yun-Sheng Zhao, Yun-Bo Zhao

entry.summary: Continuous-time machine learning models temporal dynamics as a continuous process, useful when observations arrive at arbitrary times or span long horizons, but its branches developed in separate communities. This survey organizes these families into a taxonomy by underlying base mathematical formulation and presents a canonical formulation relating them through architectural choices of vector-field parameterization. It is a reference-style synthesis rather than new empirical work.

entry.title: Neural Field Ensembles for Aerodynamic Surface Prediction: Winning Solution to the ONERA CRM Wall Distribution 2025 Challenge

author.name: Lionel Salesses, Caroline Sainvitu, Tariq Benamara

entry.summary: This is the winning methodology from the ONERA CRM Wall Distribution Regression Challenge, predicting pressure and skin-friction distributions over the NASA Common Research Model wing-body-pylon-nacelle configuration across operating conditions. The approach formulates the task as a conditional neural field mapping spatial coordinates to surface quantities and ensembles such models as a surrogate for high-fidelity CFD.

entry.title: Skill-based Agentic Evaluation for Real-time Data Science Tasks

author.name: Aniruddha Tamhane, Raghavendra Addanki, Ayushi Aggarwal, Aditya Bansal, Rui Wang, Charles Menguy, Swati Jain

entry.summary: The paper presents an evaluation framework for data-science agents operating on live, continuously updated data, where static reference answers go stale. Its core idea, ground-truth-as-code, encodes expected answers as executable reference functions that recompute the answer from live data at evaluation time, paired with a format-agnostic factoid-level judge. This addresses a real gap in agent benchmarking for dynamic, production-like settings.

entry.title: Smarter by the Moment: Environment-Driven Dynamic Policies for Continual LLM Improvement

author.name: Ting-Wei Chang, Po-Chun Chen, Hen-Hsen Huang, Hsin-Hsi Chen

entry.summary: The paper presents Dynamic Retrieval-based Policy Generation (DRPG), which combines memory retrieval with a policy generator that synthesizes actionable strategies from past experience and environment feedback. The goal is continual improvement so that the same classes of errors do not recur, evaluated across six benchmarks spanning text-to-SQL, QA, medical diagnosis, and Python programming.

entry.title: Language Orthogonalization for Zero-Shot Cross-Lingual Audio Deepfake Detection

author.name: Minu Kim, Ji Sub Um, Hoirin Kim

entry.summary: The authors address cross-lingual audio deepfake detection by removing language-dependent structure from self-supervised speech model representations using language orthogonalization, a target-free ridge map that projects out variation aligned with continuous language-identification embeddings. Across six languages, six S3M backbones, and all Leave-N-Out settings, the method consistently reduces equal error rate on unseen languages, with larger gains for more distant transfers. Cross-lingual error rate correlates with LID-space distance.

entry.title: Interactive Memory Learning for Long-Term Conversations

author.name: Cai Ke, Jiangyue Yan, Han Zhang, Xin Liu, Zike Yuan, Yue Yu, Hui Wang, Ruifeng Xu

entry.summary: The authors propose ICML (InteraCtive Memory Learning), a multi-agent framework that turns memory management for long-term conversational agents from a passive archive into a learnable, interactive memory policy. They argue existing approaches statically archive information without adaptive memory valuation, so they cannot self-evolve or align with changing user needs. A session synthesis pipeline generates expert data to support rapid test-time adaptation in unseen scenarios.

entry.title: LACE: Layer-Wise Compression for Dynamic Frame Rate Codecs

author.name: Thanapat Trachu, Samuele Cornell, William Chen, Shinji Watanabe

entry.summary: LACE (Layer-Adaptive Codec Encoding) is a dynamic frame rate neural audio codec that applies an independent compression step per quantization layer rather than a single shared compression step before multi-layer quantization. The motivation is that residual embeddings at different quantization layers change at different rates over time, so forcing all layers to share segmentation boundaries is suboptimal. This reduces sequence length and computational cost for speech language modeling while preserving codec quality.

entry.title: Channel-Wise and Token-Aware Post-Training Quantization for Visual State Space Duality

author.name: Jonghyeon Lim, Changhoon Yim

entry.summary: This paper studies low-bit post-training quantization for Visual State Space Duality (VSSD) models such as Mamba-based vision backbones, which remain poorly understood in this regime. A weight-activation split identifies activation quantization as the dominant bottleneck, with strong channel-wise magnitude variation and token-localized outliers in key linear layers. The proposed CTOAC method learns per-input-channel clipping bounds by minimizing a token-balanced reconstruction loss.

entry.title: MEgoVista: Multi-view Ego-aware Motion Estimation for Metric 4D Hands and Head in the Wild

author.name: Jiangong Xiao (Northwestern Polytechnical University), Zhihao Zhang (Xi'an Jiaotong University), Yifei Dong (Maniformer), Chao Ma (Maniformer), Zhouyi Jin (Maniformer), Zhiwen Hou (Maniformer), Li Liu (Maniformer), Weihuang Chen (Xi'an Jiaotong University), Hongbin Sun (Xi'an Jiaotong University), Maoqing Yao (Maniformer)

entry.summary: The paper introduces an offline pipeline that turns a single unprepared egocentric head-worn recording into metric two-hand and head motion in one gravity-aligned world frame, avoiding the studio rigs and instrumented headsets that dominate metric hand labels. It targets manipulation learning from human video, where high-fidelity metric hand labels are the bottleneck. The appeal is scalability: the approach scales with the number of people simply wearing a device rather than with controlled capture infrastructure.

entry.title: sensVLA: Spatially-Grounded Vision-Language-Action Model for Autonomous Wheel Loader

author.name: Gopi Krishna Erabati, Bjarne Johannsen, Angus Stewart, Vardeep Singh Sandhu

entry.summary: sensVLA is a vision-language-action architecture for autonomous wheel loaders that pairs a Qwen3-2B VLM with a fully trainable transformer action expert trained by flow-matching velocity regression. Bird's-eye-view features fused from front and rear lidar are routed straight to the action expert via dedicated cross-attention, while the VLM consumes RGB views for task semantics, explicitly decoupling spatial grounding from linguistic reasoning. This targets heavy-machinery autonomy where geometry and semantics must both be respected in real time.

entry.title: The Robot Data Factory

author.name: Sami Haddadin, Ivan Laptev, Ian Reid, Dezhen Song, Cesare Stefanini, Abdalla Swikir, Xingxing Zuo, Lyes Saad Saoud, Mahmoud Hamandi, Mohamed Heshmat, Oualid Doukhi, Abdeldjallil Naceri, Attique Bashar, Abdelrahim Mohamed, Teodor Tomic, Yue Peng, Samuel Schneider, Cheng-Chung Lee, Janine Guo, Qinghao Zhang, Kim Jeffery
