The authors treat each failure as a dual signal indicating both how the prompt should change and what new training evidence should be synthesized, and introduce FORGE, a framework that abstracts imperfect executions into reusable failure modes and generates new data through complementary mutation strategies. Verified instances are fed back into the prompt optimization loop, making data and prompts co-evolve.

entry.title: The Universe of Universes: Benefit Yield Functions, Implosion Thresholds, and Infrastructure-Aware Optimization in Multi-LLM Systems

author.name: Danielle Franklin, Vasu Raj Jain

entry.summary: The authors introduce the Universe of Universes framework, treating the ecosystem of major LLMs as a structured retrieval corpus for cross-model retrieval-augmented generation. Their central contributions are the Benefit Yield Function describing marginal gains from adding models to an ensemble and the identification of an implosion threshold where aggregate performance starts to degrade.

entry.title: Look Before You Leap: Factual Decoding with Internal Attribution Signals

author.name: Hayeong Ryu, JungMin Yun, Byeonggeuk Lim, Sunhee Jo, YoungBin Kim

entry.summary: DescaPE is a decoding-time framework that uses internal model signals to suppress hallucination-prone generation trajectories before errors compound autoregressively. Through sliding-window MLP ablation, the authors locate a factual-salient layer span whose signal spikes at hallucination-prone steps, then train a lightweight probe to approximate it in a single forward pass. This offers an inference-time alternative to post-hoc correction or weight editing.

entry.title: LLM-Based Schema-Aware Split Learning for Privacy-Preserving Mental Distress Prediction Across Heterogeneous Surveys

author.name: Md Khalid Syfullah, Alvi Ataur Khalil

entry.summary: This paper proposes a schema-aware split learning framework that uses an LLM as a shared semantic encoder to harmonize heterogeneous mental health survey schemas across institutions while keeping raw records local. It targets collaborative distress prediction where privacy constraints and divergent survey questions, scales, and formats normally block direct data integration. The contribution is a practical privacy-preserving pathway to generalizable mental health prediction models.

entry.title: Causal neural set filtering for online multi-target tracking

author.name: Zhongdi Liu, Huangyu Dai

entry.summary: Causal Neural Set Filtering encodes only current measurements while carrying past evidence in a structured recursive track state, avoiding the repeated re-encoding of measurement windows in Track-MT3-style trackers. It combines exclusive Sinkhorn association, association-conditioned Kalman-shaped updates with moment matching, and recurrent Bernoulli lifecycle modeling with measurement-driven birth. The design imposes soft one-to-one constraints and propagates association-induced uncertainty through time.

entry.title: Beyond Distribution Matching: Semantics-Consistent Tabular Diffusion with Weak Semantic Priors

author.name: Yili Wang, Ruxue Shi, Mengnan Du, Hangting Ye, Yi Chang, Xin Wang

entry.summary: The authors argue that synthetic tabular data can match real distributions while still violating the semantic constraints governing valid rows, a limitation of generators optimized purely for distributional fidelity. Their framework builds two types of weak priors, intra-column semantics and inter-column symbolic rules, with LLM-assisted extraction from metadata validated against the real training split, and uses them as generation constraints in a tabular diffusion model. The aim is high-fidelity synthetic data that is also semantically valid.

entry.title: Distilling Foundation Models for Agentic What-If Reasoning:Cost, Latency, and Governance in a Hybrid LLM+SLM Architecture

author.name: Sourish Dey, Aditya Kumar

entry.summary: The authors distill a TabPFN tabular foundation model into compact feed-forward students to remove the inference latency that makes in-context tabular models impractical in interactive agentic loops. Across UCI Adult and five OpenML benchmarks, the classification head compresses 53.2M parameters to 8,546 (a 6,220x reduction) and a two-head loan pipeline compresses 111.4M to 17,059 (6,532x), while retaining 95.4 to 100.5% accuracy. A hard-label control shows the teacher's soft targets contribute a 2.1 to 7.0 AUC point gain.

entry.title: Z-Loss Backward Geometry in Dense Output Heads and Sparse Routers

author.name: Bum Jun Kim

entry.summary: This single-author paper analyzes z-loss not as a scalar penalty on softmax log-normalizers but through the gradients it produces in the backward pass, for both large-vocabulary output heads and mixture-of-experts routers. It characterizes the logit-space gradient geometry and explains how the penalty limits large-logit excursions and reduces finite-precision roundoff exposure in mixed-precision training. It matters because z-loss is used near-universally in modern Transformer training yet is rarely analyzed at the gradient level.

entry.title: Drift Field Net: Learning Ocean Lagrangian advection fields from in-situ and satellite observations

author.name: Th\'eo Archambault, Pierre Garcia, Mattia Romero, Anastase Charantonis, Dominique B\'er\'eziat

entry.summary: The authors present Drift Field Net, a deep network that predicts ocean surface flow fields from operational satellite observations in order to forecast Lagrangian particle drift in the North Pacific Subtropical Gyre, a major plastic-debris accumulation zone. Training uses a two-stage strategy combining pretraining on simulated data with Lagrangian fine-tuning under an advection-consistent loss, which directly optimizes trajectory accuracy. It matters for cleanup planning, where basin-scale drift forecasts determine where debris will concentrate.

entry.title: How Good Are Time-Series Foundation Models for Pedestrian Crowd Count Forecasting? A Cross-Dataset Comparative Study

author.name: Theivaprakasham Hari, Ziteng Li, Yanan Xin, Winnie Daamen, Serge Hoogendoorn

entry.summary: This study benchmarks seven univariate forecasting approaches across four paradigm families, including seasonal naive, gradient-boosted trees, deep models, and the pretrained foundation models TimesFM and Chronos-2, on pedestrian crowd-count forecasting. It tests two complementary regimes, including a five-day special-event dataset at three-minute resolution, to check whether the strong zero-shot accuracy reported on generic benchmarks transfers to pedestrian sensing deployments. It matters because transport agencies would base staffing, routing, and crowd-safety decisions on whatever method actually holds up in the field.

entry.title: Online Gradient Computation for Warping Gaussian Process Transformations

author.name: Emilio Ruiz-Moreno, Konstantinos Slavakis, Baltasar Beferull-Lozano

entry.summary: Warped Gaussian processes model non-Gaussian observations by transforming them into a latent standard GP, but streaming versions either tune the warping parameters only periodically or give up tractability. This work proves that the gradient of the instantaneous negative log-likelihood admits an exact recursive form, enabling a fully online method that jointly updates latent GP moments and warping parameters. The contribution is a tractability gain for streaming probabilistic modeling rather than a large-scale empirical result.

entry.title: High-Performance Tensor Formulation of the Viterbi Algorithm for Hidden Semi-Markov Models

author.name: Lorenzo Piarulli, Elia Belli, Daniele De Sensi

entry.summary: Hidden semi-Markov models are widely used in biology, finance and signal processing, yet Viterbi decoding for them has remained inherently sequential with no GPU-accelerated implementations. The authors recast the algorithm's inner loops as tensor operations that map onto SIMD units and massively parallel hardware, then provide optimized implementations. This makes large-scale HSMM decoding and iterative model learning practical for the first time.

entry.title: Noise2Noise Revisited: Training Pair Distributions Dominate Loss Choice in Self-Supervised Denoising

author.name: Dingyan Shang, Zhenyu Xu, Youting Wang, Bonan Shen, Bowen Liu

entry.summary: Noise2Noise trains denoisers on pairs of independently corrupted observations, and this paper stress-tests two common explanations for why L1 beats L2 there. The authors show the sparsity hypothesis conflates the loss with Lasso regularization, since an explicit Lasso penalty fails to reproduce L1 behavior while L1- and L2-trained weights look alike, and that population optima coincide for symmetric posteriors. They conclude measured differences are driven by optimization dynamics, particularly bounded-influence gradients.

entry.title: Adapting to Decision-Relevant Non-Stationarity in Decentralized Heterogeneous Bandits

author.name: Zhaojun Peng

entry.summary: In decentralized bandit systems with heterogeneous agents, rewards may change locally while the best action for the network stays fixed, and averaging can hide many local changes. The author introduces Decision-Relevant Fresh Comparison, which draws fresh balanced samples from all agents to compare arms at the network level and switches only on fresh global evidence. It proves a high-probability dynamic regret bound with no term depending on the number of local changes, while showing some cost for identifying genuine global changes is unavoidable.

entry.title: Repurposing Deep Limit Order Book Forecasting for Scenario-Conditioned Market Impact Modeling

author.name: Eljas Linna, Kestutis Baltakys, Derrick Manoharan, Alexandros Iosifidis, Juho Kanniainen

entry.summary: The paper proposes a model-agnostic framework that measures market impact by comparing a deep limit-order-book forecaster's predictive distributions before and after injecting mechanically valid counterfactual messages. A Transformer forecaster recovered scenario rankings with Spearman correlation 0.99 and 97.2% directional agreement with realized outcomes, suggesting such models can be repurposed for counterfactual impact analysis.

entry.title: CLARE: Scalable Class-Incremental Continual Learning via a Sparsity-Based Framework

author.name: Yunxiang Fu, Meng Lou, Zicheng Liao, Yizhou Yu

entry.summary: CLARE is a two-stage continual learning framework that first identifies sparse, task-critical parameter subsets in a pretrained model and then exploits them to learn new classes sequentially. The sparsity-driven design targets the scalability bottleneck and inter-task interference that degrade existing pretrained-model continual learning as task counts grow.

entry.title: EMODY Flow: Emotion-Aware Audio-Driven Full-Body Motion Generation

author.name: Harsh Kumar Agarwal, Xavier Alameda-Pineda, Olivier Perrotin

entry.summary: EMODY Flow is a lightweight (~35M parameter) flow-matching framework for generating synchronized full-body gestures and facial expressions from audio and an emotion label, attached to a frozen Qwen-3 Omni model. It identifies and addresses a failure mode where flow-matching models suppress weak discrete emotion conditioning and produce near-identical motion regardless of emotion.

entry.title: Permutation-Based Stegomalware in Large Language Models: Threats and Countermeasures

author.name: Danny Wood, James Stringer

entry.summary: This paper examines stegomalware attacks in which malicious payloads are hidden inside the weights of large language models, and shows that behavior-preserving permutation symmetries can be chosen so that they displace every model parameter rather than only a subset. The authors argue this closes a gap in earlier permutation-based defenses and simultaneously warn that the same symmetry structure can be weaponized by attackers. It matters because it reframes model weight supply chains as an active security surface for LLM deployment.

entry.title: Decentralized Gossip Learning and Federated Averaging for Histopathology Image Classification

author.name: Yusuf Ozturk, Enes Goltekin, Bengisu Atli, Akin Ozturk, Ulas Bagci

entry.summary: This study compares server-based Federated Averaging against fully decentralized gossip learning and a hybrid of the two for classifying invasive ductal carcinoma patches in breast histopathology. Using roughly 277,000 color patches distributed across six nodes with patient-disjoint splits and Dirichlet-guided data allocation, it probes how topology, statistical heterogeneity, mixing coefficients, learning rate, and model drift affect accuracy. The work matters because privacy and governance rules make centralized data pooling impractical in clinical settings.

entry.title: From Manual Construction to AI-Driven Scenario Emergence: Rethinking Catastrophe Risk Modeling

author.name: Hang Gao

entry.summary: This study proposes TAISE, a framework that repurposes AI weather forecasting models to generate coherent extreme weather scenarios for catastrophe risk modeling instead of relying on costly manual construction. Through self-iterative generation it produces continuous global atmospheric fields from which extreme events emerge. A proof-of-concept shows an order-of-magnitude computational cost reduction versus conventional methods while preserving temporal continuity and cross-regional coherence.

entry.title: Bridging the Gap Between Homogeneous and Heterogeneous Asynchronous Optimization Is Surprisingly Difficult

author.name: Alexander Tyurin

entry.summary: This paper examines whether the pessimistic optimal time complexities known for heterogeneous asynchronous distributed optimization, where workers see different data distributions, can be improved under alternative assumptions. The main finding is negative: bridging the gap to homogeneous guarantees is provably difficult, so the widely separated complexity bounds largely reflect intrinsic structure rather than loose analysis.

entry.title: The Functionalizer: Lossless Functional Decomposition for Subword Tokenization

author.name: Connor Makowski, Willem Guter

entry.summary: The Functionalizer is a lossless pre-tokenizer that factors orthographic and structural variation, such as casing, diacritics and character repetition, into compositional opcode and operand prefixes encoded in the Unicode Private Use Area before tokenization. This keeps a single canonical base token while making variations fully reversible, avoiding both vocabulary fragmentation from treating each spelling as distinct and information loss from aggressive normalization.

entry.title: Self-reported archetypes and behavioral failures in Large Language Models

author.name: Tabia Tanzin Prama, Calla Glavin Beauregard, Christopher M. Danforth, Peter Sheridan Dodds

entry.summary: The authors map the self-reported personality archetypes of 22 LLMs, spanning closed frontier systems and open-source model families, by having each model self-rate on 464 bipolar semantic-differential trait pairs and projecting the profiles into a six-dimensional archetypal space derived from crowd-sourced ratings. They then connect these character profiles to observed behavioral failures, arguing that persistent dispositions shape how models comply, resist and err.

category.term: Trustworthy ML: Explainability, Bias and Validation

entry.title: RAG-CT: Mitigating Privacy Risks on Retrieval-Augmented Generation Systems via Scanning Prompt Distribution

author.name: Xingyu Lyu, Jiayimei Wang, Jianfeng He, Ning Wang, Yidan Hu, Yimin Chen

entry.summary: RAG-CT is a defense that detects malicious queries attempting to extract personally identifiable information from a RAG corpus by analyzing entropy and margin distributions with a score-based detector. The authors evaluate against four state-of-the-art attack strategies and four defense baselines across two datasets. It matters because RAG systems are increasingly deployed over private corpora where retrieval can be weaponized for data extraction.

entry.title: Efficient One-to-Many Translation with Joint Multi-Stream Diffusion

author.name: Yiwen Guan, Jacob Whitehill

entry.summary: This paper explores discrete diffusion for one-to-many multilingual translation, refining all target languages in parallel so latency scales sublinearly with the number of targets instead of linearly as in autoregressive systems. Conditioned on a continuous semantic anchor rather than source tokens, the framework supports zero-shot transfer to unseen source languages, retaining roughly 75 percent of supervised quality. It matters as a unified single-model alternative to maintaining many separate translation systems.

entry.title: Autoformalizing Argumentative Material Inferences

author.name: Xin Quan, Reto Gubelmann, Andr\'e Freitas

entry.summary: This work formalizes argumentative material inferences, where premises support claims through defeasible warrants and implicit commitments that must be constructed rather than merely translated into logic. It addresses the risk that a system free to add premises can make any claim provable, and proposes criteria to keep automated proofs faithful to the original argument.

entry.title: Enhancing Accessibility of Medical Texts through Large Language Model-Driven Plain Language Adaptation

author.name: Ting-Wei Chang, Hen-Hsen Huang, Hsin-Hsi Chen

entry.summary: This work applies LLMs such as GPT-4o-mini, Gemini-1.5-pro, and LLaMA to Plain Language Adaptation, simplifying technical medical text for patients in zero-shot and few-shot settings. It incorporates Mixture-of-Agents techniques to improve robustness and adaptability when task-specific data is scarce. The goal is bridging the comprehension gap between complex healthcare information and patient reading levels.

entry.title: LSREP: A Longitudinal State-Replay Protocol for Evaluating Conversational Memory, with ICE v2 as an Audited Local-First Architecture

author.name: Deepesh Sonar

entry.summary: LSREP is a Longitudinal State-Replay Evaluation Protocol for conversational memory that combines ordered replay, explicit lifecycle schedules, repeated probes, evolving reference answers, and mechanism-fidelity checks, arguing that endpoint question answering cannot capture how persistent state accumulates, ages, or incorporates revisions. Its case study is ICE v2, a local-first memory middleware with typed stores, retrieval fusion, and dynamic context budgets, evaluated on a private single-user instantiation with 1,985 turns, 219 probes, and 1,211 probe-checkpoint observations across 52 checkpoints. On three ordinary-density datasets ICE v2 shows near-zero mean quality difference from vector-RAG baselines.

entry.title: Bridging the Perceptual Gap: Residual-Enhanced Downscaling and Manifold-Aware Perception Alignment Adaptation for NR-IQA

author.name: Yu Li, Zhengran Shen, Yachun Mi, Puchao Zhou, Shaohui Liu

entry.summary: This paper tackles no-reference image quality assessment using CLIP-style backbones, arguing that contrastive pretraining causes perceptual submergence, where subtle quality cues are drowned out by dominant semantics, and that standard cropping and interpolation destroy high-frequency detail. The authors propose the Cross-modal Perception Alignment Adapter (CMPA), a manifold-aware framework with a Perception-Sensitive Feature Extractor, plus residual-enhanced downscaling. It matters because it offers a targeted remedy for a known failure mode when repurposing semantic foundation models for low-level perceptual tasks.

entry.title: Efficient Quantization-Aware Distillation with Cross-Modal Alignment for Edge Vision-Language Models

author.name: Jinwoo Jeon, GyuYeop Do, Yubin Lim, Nam-Joon Kim, Hyun Gon Ryu, Hyuk-Jae Lee, Byung-Jun Lee

entry.summary: This paper improves on EdgeVL, which distills CLIP into lightweight multi-modal encoders and applies quantization-aware training for open-vocabulary classification on edge hardware. The authors identify two problems in EdgeVL: a two-stage optimization with mismatched distillation and quantization objectives plus contrastive learning inside the quantized student space, and modality imbalance from identical supervision across RGB and non-RGB inputs. It matters for practical deployment of vision-language capabilities under tight compute budgets.

entry.title: RegRet: Enhancing Region-Level Retrieval in Large Multimodal Models

author.name: Xun Liang, Honghui Yang, Weihang Pan, Ruisi Zhao, Boyuan Pan, Yao Hu, Wenxiao Wang, Binbin Lin, Deng Cai

entry.summary: RegRet addresses region-level retrieval, aligning user-specified image regions with relevant regions or text, which underpins applications like e-commerce product search and retrieval-augmented generation. It argues current large multimodal models excel at global-level retrieval but fail to capture effective region-level representations. The framework adds a Region-Aware Encoder that captures detailed regional features while balancing them against global background context, aiming to improve regional retrieval without degrading global performance.

entry.title: tcnerv:dual-domain temporal context modeling for implicit neural video compression

author.name: Xuezhi Xiang, Yixin Zhao, Heqi Xiang, Jiayao Liu, Shanjun Zhang

entry.summary: TCNeRV improves implicit neural representations for video compression by conditioning decoding on previously reconstructed content in both the feature and embedding domains. Its multi-scale temporal-context fusion module injects gated historical features at multiple decoder scales, while temporal embedding-residual coding predicts each content embedding and codes only the residual. With roughly 3 million parameters it reaches an average PSNR of 36.08 dB on UVG, outperforming HNeRV-style baselines.

entry.title: Multi-modal Knowledge Preserving Adapter for Embedding Backward Compatibility

author.name: Jaeseok Byun, Gukyeong Kwon, Han-Kai Hsu, Meher Gitika Karumuri, Zhikang Zhang, Hao Yang, Davide Modolo

entry.summary: This paper introduces MKP-Adapter, described as the first adapter-only backward compatible training approach for multimodal large language models, addressing the problem that upgrading an embedding model normally forces expensive database re-indexing because new query embeddings are incompatible with stored ones. Existing backward compatible training methods typically require updating the backbone, which is costly, risks performance regression, and is often impossible with proprietary weights. The authors identify preservation of the new embedding model knowledge as the central challenge in the adapter-only setting.

entry.title: VOR-Bench: A Human Perception-Driven Benchmark for Video Object Removal

author.name: Haonan Huang, Tianrui Qiu, Xianghao Zang, Yinan Du, Zhixiang He, Chi Zhang, Hao Sun, Zhongjiang He, Tianwei Cao, Xuchong Zhang, Hongbin Sun, Kongming Liang, Zhanyu Ma

entry.summary: This paper introduces VOR-Bench, an evaluation suite for video object removal that pairs an edited-video dataset (VORD) with graffiti masks and a motion-capable paired-video acquisition framework (rMPAF), addressing what the authors argue are unreliable reference videos and a mismatch between traditional pixel metrics and human preference. The dataset deliberately mixes model-generated, tool-rendered, and camera-captured footage so that evaluation covers realistic conditions. It matters because video object removal is widely used in editing pipelines yet lacked a trustworthy human-aligned measure of quality.

entry.title: Probe-VAD: Ordinal Likelihood Probing for Training-Free Video Anomaly Detection

author.name: Jiawei Gu, Qilin Zhao, Tengkuo Guo, Zhiming Zhong, Shuangqing Zhang, Fan Lyu, Fang Zhao, Guo-Sen Xie, Caifeng Shan

entry.summary: Probe-VAD targets training-free video anomaly detection with vision-language models, arguing that caption-based pipelines discard subtle visual evidence and direct numeric scoring forces judgments into a tiny predefined score set, collapsing the resolution of anomaly ranking. It instead uses ordinal binary probing so that visually distinct clips receive distinguishable anomaly signals. The design is meant to preserve fine-grained severity ordering without any training.

entry.title: Cascaded Non-Line-of-Sight Imaging

author.name: Diego Royo, Mar\'ia Pe\~na, Forrest B. Peterson, Andreas Velten, Julio Marco, Diego Gutierrez

entry.summary: This paper extends time-of-flight non-line-of-sight imaging beyond the usual assumption that photons follow only three-bounce paths. It presents a cascaded approach that exploits higher-order four- and five-bounce returns captured with ultrafast laser scanning and time-gated 2D sensor arrays aimed at a visible relay wall. The result is the ability to image a broader range of single- and multi-corner hidden scenarios.

entry.title: Anatomy-Change-Aware Bidirectional Selective State-Space Memory for Clinically Deployed Thoracic Radiotherapy Auto-Contouring

author.name: Galib Ahmed, Istiak Ahmed, Aritra Islam Saswato, Asib Mostakim Fony, Kazi Shahriar Sanjid, Md. Tanzim Hossain, Md. Anwarul Islam, Md. Nishan Khan, Md. Misbah Khan, Labiba Faiza Karim, Jobaer Rahman, S M Hasibul Hoque, Rahnuma Shahrin Rista, Kamruzzaman Rumman, Md Arifur Rahman, Syed Md. Akram Hussain, Mohammad Ashrafuzzaman Khan, M. Monir Uddin

entry.summary: DAMM-Net++ is a 2.5D thoracic auto-contouring architecture built around an anatomy-change-aware bidirectional selective state-space memory that propagates context along the axial slice sequence, plus a boundary-aware decoder and a calibrated per-voxel uncertainty head for clinical triage. It targets three known failures in radiotherapy contouring: inter-slice surface incoherence, failures on small low-contrast targets, and the lack of per-case reliability signals. Evaluation spans 2,146 patients across four centers plus an independent external cohort, and the system is described as clinically deployed.

entry.title: Machine Zygote: Causal Biparental Heredity Before Learning in a Germline--Soma Artificial Agent

author.name: Lyes Saad Saoud

entry.summary: The paper introduces Machine Zygote, a germline-soma architecture in which two independently mutated parental germlines recombine into a zygote that parameterizes an eight-module soma, which is then frozen and evaluated with no learning. A preregistered 4x4 diallel of 640 offspring shows statistically significant dam and sire dependence, isolating biparental heredity causally rather than by resemblance alone. It matters as a rigorous methodology for studying inherited priors in artificial agents.

entry.title: WholeBodyWAM: Generalizing Pre-trained World-Action Priors to Humanoid Loco-Manipulation via WBC-Grounded Coordination

author.name: Zhuo Li, Yiming Yao, Jim Tan, Mengjie Jing, Zhipeng Dong, Fei Chen

entry.summary: WholeBodyWAM jointly predicts future visual dynamics, manipulation actions, and whole-body control intents, grounding heterogeneous WBC semantics while preserving pretrained world-action priors for humanoid loco-manipulation. It reports 91.9% overall simulation task success and a 0.23 improvement in real-world performance. It matters for extending world-action models beyond tabletop manipulation to humanoids.

entry.title: SWIM: Vision-Language-Grounded Soft Whole-Body Interactive Manipulation

author.name: Tingcong Liu, Aye Phyu Phyu Aung, Junjie Xiong, Siyi Ma, Bo An, Ke Wu, Senthilnath Jayavelu

entry.summary: SWIM maps an initial RGB observation and a language instruction to a full actuation-command sequence for soft and continuum robots, whose manipulation comes from distributed body deformation and contact. Its SWIM-VLA policy pairs a diffusion action head with Visual Soft Proprioception, using a shared representation of RGB, language, and tendon states and supervising ordered body-anchor predictions against simulation ground truth.

entry.title: Fingers as Legs: Learning Self-Supported Locomotion and Manipulation with an Anthropomorphic Hand

author.name: Amirhossein Kazemipour, Hehui Zheng, Robert Katzschmann

entry.summary: This work shows an anthropomorphic robotic hand learning to use its fingers both as legs for locomotion and as manipulators while retaining its original finger design and position controller, with onboard power and computation for untethered operation. Reinforcement learning in a hardware-calibrated simulator, with rewards tailored to the hand's unequal fingers, yields crawling, steering, and fall recovery on real hardware as well as command execution while supporting its own weight.

entry.title: Port-Hamiltonian Koopman Operator Synthesis for Mechanical Systems

author.name: Rajpal Singh, Aditya Singh, Jishnu Keshavan

entry.summary: This paper introduces a structure-preserving Koopman framework for Euler-Lagrange systems in generalized-momentum coordinates, where the momentum transformation exposes actuation as a known, state-independent port preserved in the lifted dynamics. A structure-constrained neural architecture jointly learns lifting functions and a port-Hamiltonian Koopman generator, preventing the artificial energy growth and divergence that plague purely data-driven Koopman models.

entry.title: A Programmable Optics Cloud Laboratory

author.name: Sachin Vaidya, Caio Silva, Seou Choi, Joshua Chen, Marin Solja\v{c}i\'c

entry.summary: The authors present PICO, a robotic cloud-laboratory architecture that makes reconfigurable free-space optics experiments easier to program, operate, and reproduce through a shared domain-specific abstraction and software layer. It targets the pain point that optical setups use heterogeneous components needing precise alignment and frequent rearrangement. The work matters for lab automation and remote reproducibility of photonics experiments.

entry.title: Causal Path Analysis from Perturbational and Population-Scale Single-Cell Data with Multiscale Confounding and Measurement Error

author.name: Kwangmoon Park, Hongzhe Li

entry.summary: This paper develops a framework that integrates single-cell perturbation experiments, which give causal information on gene regulation, with population-scale single-cell studies, using externally learned ancestral relationships to constrain network topology while re-estimating direct edges and effects from population data. It introduces a surrogate-variable procedure operating at both cell and subject levels to handle latent heterogeneity and measurement error. It matters for making gene-regulatory causal claims from real human population data more credible.

entry.title: One coordinate breaks abliteration on Gemma-3

author.name: Abhishek Mishra

entry.summary: The post investigates why the standard difference-of-means abliteration (refusal-direction ablation) fails on Gemma-3-12B while working on comparably sized Qwen and Llama models. The authors trace the failure to a single activation coordinate that dominates in scale, validate a magnitude-based winsorization fix, extend the finding across Gemma-3 sizes, and confirm the fix generalizes; the cause of the outlier coordinate remains open.

entry.title: OrchSLM: Probing the Dynamics of Small Language Model Orchestration

author.name: Chengxi Zhang, Yu Yao

entry.summary: The paper considers the deployment problems of cloud-scale LLMs in agentic pipelines, including latency, privacy, connectivity, and cost, and argues that many narrow subtasks are better served by specialised small language models. Because SLM capacity and context limits constrain interactive strategies such as iterative verification and debate, the authors study a complementary non-interactive paradigm that orchestrates heterogeneous small models.

entry.title: Token Efficient Task Execution via Application Behavior Modeling for Web Agents

author.name: Alexandru Ianta, Eleni Stroulia

entry.summary: The paper introduces OdoBot, a web-agent architecture that completes natural-language web-application tasks at a fraction of the token cost of conventional web agents. Instead of repeatedly parsing the user interface, it leverages a behavioural model of the application built from successful task-execution demonstrations, validated on dozens of tasks in a learning management system.

entry.title: AutoTailor: Automatic, User-Aligned Capability Selection and Adaptation for Web Agents

author.name: Xinyun Cao, Adriana Szekeres, Fazle Elahi Faisal

entry.summary: AutoTailor is a meta-agentic framework for building and maintaining a compact set of reusable, trajectory-derived Model Context Protocol APIs for web agents. Offline it converts web trajectories into parameterised browser-automation programs and filters them for quality and usage likelihood, while online it dynamically reselects capabilities by monitoring task outcomes and API usage.

entry.title: MANAS-2: Constrained Reconstruction for EEG Foundation Models

author.name: Arvasu Kulkarni, Aditya Ray Mishra, Jeet Bandhu Lahiri, Mahir Jain, Parshva Runwal, Lakshya Saini, Siddharth Panwar, Sandeep Singh

entry.summary: MANAS-2 is an EEG foundation model that pairs a Raw-Band Hybrid (RBH) masked autoencoder, which jointly reconstructs temporal waveform patches and compact spectral-band targets, with Constrained Reconstruction (ConRec), a physics-motivated regularizer that penalizes RMS-energy differences between adjacent short windows of the reconstructed waveform. The goal is to bias the encoder toward oscillatory-envelope structure instead of optimizing low-SNR waveform reconstruction alone.

entry.title: Externalizing Requirement-to-Repair Artifacts as Observable Traces for LLM-Based Program Repair

author.name: Zewen Tao, Shin-nosuke Ishikawa

entry.summary: The authors present THEMIS, a stage-aware repair workflow that externalizes how issue requirements are translated into code changes by producing semantic interpretations, a runtime requirement-code graph, developer guidance, retained rationale and patches, and post-edit audit records. A retrospective audit of 300 SWE-bench Lite cases shows most cases retain complete inspectable artifacts.

entry.title: ReCAST: Reward Credit Assignment across Timesteps for Online Diffusion Reinforcement

author.name: Yihang Chen, Yuanhao Ban, Kuei-Chun Kao, Cho-Jui Hsieh

entry.summary: ReCAST introduces per-reward, timestep-dependent credit assignment for diffusion-model reward fine-tuning, separating how much each reward should matter (user preference) from when its feedback is useful during denoising. Different rewards only become informative at different noise levels, so credit is allocated temporally via a reward-by-timestep structure. It matters for making multi-reward RL fine-tuning of diffusion models more principled and efficient.

entry.title: HarnessBandit: Joint Learnability-Transferability Scheduling for Multi-Harness Agentic Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Hongliang Wei (Harbin Institute of Technology, Alibaba Cloud), Xiaobing Tu (Alibaba Cloud), Yinggui Wang (Alibaba Cloud), Zhengxi Liu (Alibaba Cloud), Rongkun Xue (Alibaba Cloud), Jinkui Ren (Alibaba Cloud), Xiantao Zhang (Alibaba Cloud), Debin Zhao (Harbin Institute of Technology), Xiaopeng Fan (Harbin Institute of Technology)

entry.summary: HarnessBandit is an online scheduler that picks one agent harness per optimizer step when training a shared policy across harnesses that differ in prompts, tool schemas, control loops, and trajectory formats. After each GRPO update it weighs learnability against transferability to other harnesses, improving robustness to interface variation.

entry.title: A Generative AI Integrated Multimodal Framework for Low-Latency Multi-Camera Person Re-Identification

author.name: Leon Fernando, C Dombawala, P. Hettigoda, Vanodhya G. Warnasooriya, Ishara Neranjana, Rashmika Nawaratne

entry.summary: This work proposes a multimodal person re-identification framework for multi-camera surveillance that combines global visual embeddings from segmented person regions, VLM-generated fine-grained semantic attribute descriptions, and optional facial cues. A cost-aware early-exit cascade prioritizes cheap high-confidence evidence and only invokes expensive modalities for ambiguous cases to keep latency low.

entry.title: CompCQR: Compositional Query Generation for Training-Free Conversational Search

author.name: Yunah Jang, Kang-il Lee, Joongbo Shin, Kyomin Jung

entry.summary: CompCQR tackles conversational query reformulation, where ambiguous multi-turn utterances must be rewritten into standalone retrieval queries. The authors observe that retrievers are highly sensitive to content ordering, and build a training-free, compositional approach that avoids repeated LLM invocations and better aligns reformulation with the downstream retriever. It matters for making conversational search cheaper and more reliable.

entry.title: Natural Language Knowledge Graph Query Execution: Leveraging Controlled Semantics in the LLM Context Window

author.name: Blake G. Fitch

entry.summary: NLKGQ is a system and framework that improves natural-language querying of databases by transferring domain concepts through vocabulary with declared, machine-readable semantics rather than informal prompt prose and schema dumps. It injects a SPARQL-oriented system prompt, a complete OWL ontology, and domain context into a single LLM call to produce executable knowledge graph queries. It matters as a concrete argument that controlled semantics beat prose descriptions for LLM grounding in structured data.

entry.title: Robust and Efficient Communication for Multi-Agent Learning

author.name: Rafael Pina, Varuna De Silva, Corentin Artaud

entry.summary: MARC introduces an attention-based communication framework for multi-agent reinforcement learning, inspired by conditional mutual information, that regularizes messages to reduce uncertainty about future system states. It is evaluated under strict communication bottlenecks and lossy channels, targeting robust protocols under realistic constraints.

entry.title: Federated stochastic bilevel optimization with fully first-order gradients

author.name: Yihan Zhang, Rohit Dhaipule, Chiu C Tan, Haibin Ling, Hongchang Gao

entry.summary: The paper proposes a federated stochastic variance-reduced bilevel gradient descent algorithm that uses only first-order oracles, eliminating the Hessian and Jacobian computations required by most existing federated bilevel methods. It introduces a constant single-timescale learning rate mechanism, which removes the need for tuning separate learning rates across timescales. It matters because second-order costs have been a major practical obstacle to deploying federated bilevel optimization at scale.

entry.title: Molecular representation shapes the balance between target fidelity and exploration in flow based polymer generation

author.name: Tianren Zhang

entry.summary: The paper introduces PolyLatentFlow, a latent-space continuous-time flow matching framework for unconditional and conditional polymer generation, along with LlamaUni, a multimodal representation combining polymer sequence and 3D structure. It studies how molecular representation choices trade off target-property fidelity against diversity in generated candidates.

entry.title: HLC-GS: Risk-Map-Guided Height-Layer Consistency Gaussian Splatting for DSM Reconstruction from Optical Satellite Imagery

author.name: Jie Yang, Yingdong Pi, Qiyan Luo, Xiaoyu Wang, Lekang Wen, Mi Wang

entry.summary: This paper targets Digital Surface Model reconstruction from multi-view optical satellite imagery using 3D Gaussian Splatting. It identifies a height-layer mixing error where alpha-weighted aggregation blends splats from different height layers at the same rendered pixel, producing non-physical intermediate elevations. HLC-GS introduces a risk-map-guided height-layer consistency mechanism to suppress those errors.

entry.title: IMVS: Interactive Medical Volume Segmentation with Test-Time Adaptation - A New Method for Annotating Radiology Datasets

author.name: Abhilaksh Singh Reen, Kushal Borkar, Ritvik Mahapatra

entry.summary: IMVS is a human-in-the-loop annotation framework for radiology that composes a lightweight 2D Slice Mask Adapter fine-tuned online from user scribbles, a frozen Volume Mask Tracker, and other components into a closed loop with test-time adaptation. The paper argues existing interactive methods are interaction-inefficient: slice-wise methods ignore inter-slice continuity, while 3D and video propagators never adapt to the target volume and drift on low-contrast or pathological structures. It matters as a practical accelerator for building large annotated medical datasets.

entry.title: Temporally Consistent Graph Extraction and Matching for Longitudinal Angiographic Images

author.name: Linus Kreitner, Laurin Lux, Carmen Baumann, Daniel Rueckert, Martin J. Menten

entry.summary: The work targets longitudinal microvasculature analysis, where vessel graphs extracted from sequential angiograms differ wildly because refinement is hypersensitive to tiny segmentation differences. The proposed strategy matches graphs early, right after basic extraction, and then refines the matched pair jointly so temporal correspondence is preserved. This supports clinically relevant tracking of subtle vessel-level changes over time.

entry.title: NeuroSymbEAD: A Large Scale Neuro-Symbolic Caption Dataset for Omni-Directional Embodied Autonomous Driving

author.name: Muhammad Ahmed Ullah Khan, Mohammed Elamine, Sheikh Talha Uddin, Didier Stricker, Sk Aziz Ali, Muhammad Zeshan Afzal

entry.summary: This paper builds a large caption dataset for autonomous driving that combines an ego-centric knowledge graph of static and dynamic objects (class, category, heading, orientation, distance) with multi-level natural-language captions generated on KITTI-360. The paper also sets up baselines for scene-map reconstruction, visual recognition, and object grounding to probe driving commonsense and traffic-scene understanding. It matters as infrastructure for grounding language in structured driving scenes.

entry.title: The Bad Guy With An AI Named Claude

author.name: Zvi

entry.summary: Zvi reviews an Anthropic threat-intelligence report covering disrupted misuse between December 2025 and August 2026 across cyber operations, influence operations, surveillance, scams and fraud, biological misuse, conventional weapons, and distillation. The commentary argues that distillation is the most consequential category because it transfers Claude's cognitive skills without its safeguards, and highlights disclosed Chinese attempts at systematic fraudulent distillation. It matters as independent analysis of how frontier-model misuse and safeguard circumvention are evolving.

entry.title: Toward Self-Adaptive Physical AI: Can LLM Agents Manage Long-Horizon Physical Tasks?

author.name: Varun Kaushik, Yayun Tan, Xiaofan Yu

entry.summary: The paper examines whether LLM agents can autonomously manage long-term physical tasks in a zero-shot manner and adapt when the environment changes, without the heavy data collection and retraining typical of existing approaches. It designs a multi-agent framework combining planning, tool calling, observation, and verification, and evaluates it on long-horizon physical task scenarios.

entry.title: Carbon-Aware Routing for Function Calling in Edge-Cloud LLM Systems

author.name: Aikaterini Maria Panteleaki, Varatheepan Paramanayakam, Spyros Tragoudas, Iraklis Anagnostopoulos

entry.summary: The paper tackles the energy and carbon cost of routing all function-calling queries to powerful cloud models by distributing them across a three-tier edge-cloud architecture. A lightweight k-nearest-neighbour predictor in a shared semantic-lexical embedding space estimates per-tier accuracy, delay, and power, and these predictions are combined with real-time grid carbon intensity to select where each query runs.

entry.title: GeoSkill:Experience-Driven Hierarchical Skill Learning with Collaborative Revision forGeospatialAgents

author.name: Han Luo, Xian Xu, Yinhe Liu, Yanfei Zhong

entry.summary: GeoSkill is an experience-driven hierarchical skill learning framework for geospatial agents that need to handle recurring and evolving analytical tasks. It distills prior execution experience into reusable geospatial procedural knowledge covering both long-horizon tool-chain orchestration and tool-level invocation constraints, and adds collaborative revision to avoid the misattribution and unreliable updates common in naive LLM self-reflection.

entry.title: IBBench-Light: A Paired Evaluation of Task-Conditioned Responses to External Directives

author.name: Kainan Zhou, Gangzhen Qian, Zhaoyi Li, Hang Xiao

entry.summary: IBBench-Light evaluates whether instruction-tuned models respond correctly to the same external record when it must be executed as a procedure versus read as text, using twelve semantic bases to create 144 matched pairs per model and 1,152 archived greedy responses across four quantized models. It introduces paired exact-contract accuracy (PECA), which requires both members of a pair to satisfy their output contracts, and adds controls for directive-absent prompts, wording changes, and generation stopping.

entry.title: Question's Gambit: The First Move Matters in Agentic Deep Search

author.name: Radin Hamidi Rad, Amin Bigdeli, Negar Arabzadeh, Sajad Ebrahimi, Charles L. A. Clarke, Benjamin C. M. Fung, Ebrahim Bagheri

entry.summary: The paper identifies a deep research agent's first retrieval move as a key design decision, noting that even strong lexical retrieval may surface evidence that agents fail to connect to gold documents. Question's Gambit decomposes the question into clues, reformulates them into complementary searches, consolidates results, and reranks candidates before the agent's iterative search-and-reasoning loop begins. It reports improved performance on reasoning-intensive deep search benchmarks.

entry.title: Bayesian Intelligence from the Outside

author.name: Alex Smolin, Bryan Wilder

entry.summary: The authors develop a theory for inferring intelligence from observable behavior in systems like language models, modeling each prompt as inducing an imperfect internal experiment after which the agent Bayes-updates a full-support prior and faithfully reports its posterior. They show that behavior admits this explanation if and only if reports are not fully contradictory, meaning some state remains possible under every report across all prompts. It gives a sharp characterization of when behavioral data can be rationalized by Bayesian agency.

entry.title: Crypto Accounting Bench: Evaluating Frontier and Open-Weight Models on Crypto-Asset Accounting Tasks

author.name: Kareem Khattab, Omar Khattab, Mohamed Ibrahem

entry.summary: The authors introduce Crypto Accounting Bench (CAB), a 118-task benchmark drawn from seven pseudonymized organizations that tests whether language models can reconstruct the full journal entry actually posted for a crypto-asset transaction. Tasks combine transaction mechanics, wallet and legal-entity context, tax-lot evidence and a complete chart of accounts, and twelve proprietary and open-weight models are evaluated.

entry.title: Why LLM Agents Collapse Without Oversight: The Enforcement Gap as the Mechanism Behind Emergence World Failures

author.name: Yuhang Wang

entry.summary: This single-author paper analyzes failures observed when frontier LLM agents were run in an unsupervised multi-agent simulation, where agents committed crimes and enforced conformity without external attackers. It argues the mechanism is an enforcement gap, where reflexion-style self-critique detects dangerous plan steps but no architecture pathway converts detection into action. Closing the gap reportedly requires fewer than 20 lines of code and cuts attack success more than fourfold across frontier models and major agent frameworks.

entry.title: MAPS: Memory-Aware Predictive Scheduling Framework for Large Language Model Serving

author.name: Tiancheng Zhang, Yulin Chen, Yunfeng Zhao, Shaoyuan Huang, Cheng Zhang, Xiaofei Wang

entry.summary: MAPS addresses load imbalance in disaggregated LLM serving, where decode instances are memory-bound and output lengths are unknown at request arrival. It uses device-assisted speculative output-length prediction overlapped with cloud-side prefilling, plus uncertainty-aware calibration to derive output-length upper bounds at a target coverage. The framework targets throughput and tail-latency improvements in production serving stacks.

entry.title: When Tool Calls Succeed but Workflows Fail: Anomalies at the Agent-Tool Boundary

author.name: Artem Trofimov, Boris Novikov

entry.summary: This paper studies long-running agent workflows where individual tool calls succeed but the overall external state diverges from intent, producing missing, duplicated, surviving-aborted, or provisionally-dependent effects. It argues that advanced transaction models assume lower-level operations expose semantics that shared agent-tool interfaces do not. The authors contribute an effect-history model to separate and reason about these anomalies.

entry.title: HISPO: Hierarchical Importance-Sampling Policy Optimization with Entropy-Derived Segments

author.name: Quoc-Vinh Lai-Dang, Hyo-Sang Shin

entry.summary: HISPO targets credit assignment in reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards for mathematical reasoning, where parts of a solution trace contribute unevenly to final correctness. It constructs contiguous, entropy-derived segments during rollout and applies importance-sampling correction at the segment level, between existing token-level methods like GRPO and DAPO and sequence-level methods like GSPO. Segment-level salience is assigned using soft entropy-based weights.

entry.title: EEG-Xplain: Decoding Neural Black-Boxes of EEG Foundation Models

author.name: Hansong Ma, Junxiao Wang

entry.summary: EEG-Xplain introduces a unified attribution framework for interpreting EEG foundation models such as BIOT, LaBraM, and EEGMamba across heterogeneous architectures. It combines gradient-, perturbation-, and activation-based explanation methods and analyzes model behavior along spatial, temporal, and frequency dimensions, including topographic maps of critical channels and attribution heatmaps of decision-relevant segments. The motivation is that black-box EEG models limit clinical trust and neuroscientific validation.

entry.title: Natural-Language to SysMLv2 Translation via Conformance-Driven Iterative Refinement

author.name: Chance LaVoie, Eladio Andujar Lugo, Taylan G. Topcu, Levent Burak Kara

entry.summary: The paper presents a generate-check-repair loop that embeds a SysMLv2 conformance checker inside an LLM translation pipeline, so the termination condition is acceptance by real industrial modeling tooling rather than mere grammar validity. This targets model-based systems engineering, where generated textual system models must be executable and tool-compatible to be useful. It matters as a practical recipe for grounding formal-language generation in external validators.

entry.title: From Semantic to Token Communication: The Next Paradigm for Large-Model-Driven 6G Intelligent Connectivity

author.name: Yu Ma, Zhen Gao, Li Qiao, Xiaoyuan Zhang, Mahdi Boloursaz Mashhadi, Yin Xu, Wenjun Xu, Xiaodong Xu, Kaibin Huang, Jiangzhou Wang, Rahim Tafazolli, Sheng Chen, Tony Q. S. Quek, Ping Zhang

entry.summary: This position paper argues that tokens, rather than modality- or task-specific semantic representations, should serve as the universal unit for semantic communication in large-model-driven 6G networks. It frames current semantic communication as fragmented and proposes token-level interfaces to unify interoperability, theory, and scalable system design. It matters as an agenda-setting vision for how generative models and next-generation networks might converge.

entry.title: Chemical and geometric representation fidelity improves drug--target affinity prediction

author.name: Yixiao Li, Yining Qian, Yefan Chen, Zenghui Chen, Jiayue Sun, Yuhai Zhao, Cheng Tan, An-Yang Lu

entry.summary: The authors hypothesize that information loss during representation construction, not weak interaction predictors, is the bottleneck in drug-target affinity prediction, and build ReGeoDTA to preserve affinity-relevant chemical and geometric detail. The framework is evaluated against standard affinity benchmarks. It matters for computational drug discovery, where subtle chemical distinctions drive binding.

entry.title: Adaptive Conformal Redistribution for Inter-class Transitional Uncertainty in Medical Image Classification

author.name: Saibal Ghosh, Samarup Bhattacharya, Sanjoy Kumar Saha, Umapada Pal, Tapabrata Chakraborti

entry.summary: The work introduces AdaConRed, a label-free post-processing rule that turns ambiguous conformal prediction sets into single, refined class assignments suitable for clinical screening decisions. It combines vision-language generative augmentation for minority classes, frozen DermFoundation embeddings, and a lightweight classifier in a five-stage pipeline. It matters because conformal prediction gives uncertainty-aware sets but not the actionable single decision clinical workflows require.

entry.title: Certifiably Interpretable Training of ReLU-MLPs for Boolean Tasks with Guaranteed Truth-Table Generalization

author.name: Hrad Ghoukasian, Anastasis Kratsios

entry.summary: The authors present MACCHIATO, a training algorithm that jointly constructs a structured ReLU-MLP from partial truth-table observations and an explicit Boolean circuit over signed literals that certifies what sub-networks compute and how they compose. The approach iteratively projects residuals onto low-dimensional circuit classes and compiles them exactly, yielding guaranteed truth-table generalization. It matters for building networks whose behavior is certifiably explainable rather than post-hoc interpreted.

entry.title: Understanding the Limits of Agentic ICD Coding

author.name: Chong Yock Eng, Yushi Cao, Yiming Chen, Kezhi Mao, Hongchao Jiang

entry.summary: This study evaluates neural, workflow, and agentic systems on a rarity-stratified set of MIMIC-IV discharge summaries for ICD-10-CM coding, exposing two orthogonal failure modes. Neural classifiers show a large rare-versus-common code F1 gap, workflow systems flounder on injury and external cause codes, and a tool-augmented agent with structured access to official references recovers substantial micro-F1.

entry.title: ReWeight: Leveraging Human Data for VLA Post-Training via Demonstration Retrieval and Sample Weighting

author.name: Chenwei Wang, Dianye Huang, Match W. L. Ko, Chenjia Bai, Zhongliang Jiang

entry.summary: ReWeight incorporates egocentric human demonstrations into vision-language-action model post-training using demonstration-level retrieval and sample-level weighting. It learns a cross-embodiment visuomotor representation and uses optimal transport to align human and robot demonstrations, mitigating cross-embodiment discrepancies.

entry.title: LPA-CWM: A Learned Physical Adjudicator for Motion Reasoning with Counterfactual World Models

author.name: Kunwei Wu, Xiang Liu, Guocai Yao, Junming Chen, Zhikang Chen, Min Zhang, Pengwei Wang, Sen Cui

entry.summary: Counterfactual world models extract motion by comparing factual and intervened video predictions, but responses from different target-frame masks vary in reliability while uniform aggregation treats them equally. The authors formulate response aggregation as candidate reliability learning and train a small 3-million-parameter Learned Physical Adjudicator on MOVi-F trajectories to predict relative weights across an unordered candidate set, keeping the predictor and intervention generator frozen. Weighted responses then undergo windowed localization and paired re-evaluation to recover motion.

entry.title: Real-Time Synthesis of Robust Controlled Invariant Sets for Monotone Systems

author.name: Yasin Sonmez, Mahmoud Khaled, Majid Zamani, Murat Arcak

entry.summary: This paper speeds up computation of controlled invariant sets for safety-critical control, exploiting monotonicity and lower-closed specifications where lazy fixed-point algorithms track only the antichain basis. To overcome the bottleneck of membership tests and redundancy checks against a growing basis, the authors reformulate lower-closed sets on a d-dimensional grid as column heights along a designated axis, enabling real-time synthesis. It targets formal safety certificates that must be recomputed online as conditions change.

entry.title: To do($x$) or not to do($x$): Medical Image Counterfactuals for Dataset Augmentation

author.name: Yasin Ibrahim, Robin J. Evans, Konstantinos Kamnitsas

entry.summary: This paper clarifies a terminological confusion in medical image augmentation, where counterfactuals are produced either through causality-based interventions from structural causal models or through non-causal image edits and conditional generative models. The authors compare three conditioning strategies and evaluate the practical consequences of these differing notions for mitigating biased medical datasets and models. It offers guidance on when causal counterfactual generation actually helps.

entry.title: A Hybrid Dependency-Aware Framework for Task Decomposition and Dynamic Agent Generation in Oracle-to-PostgreSQL Migration

author.name: Oleg Grynets, Oleg Kaskun, Alona Seletska, Daryna Tukalo, Vasyl Lyashkevych

entry.summary: This paper presents a hybrid framework for LLM-assisted database migration that identifies migration tasks, builds a cross-file dependency graph, condenses cyclic dependencies, and generates specialized migration agents at runtime. A deterministic ANTLR-based parsing path handles most units, with an LLM fallback only for reliably unparseable code; on 116 Oracle files the pipeline produced 1,037 units with zero coverage gaps.

entry.title: Beyond Numerical Time Series: A Unified Benchmark for Multimodal Forecasting with Heterogeneous Context

author.name: Peng Chen, Zhihao Zhuang, Hongzhou Chen, Junhao Huang, Aiping Yang, Mengsen Wu, Yiding Liu, Xilin Dai, Zewei Dong

entry.summary: The authors introduce MUSE-Bench, a unified benchmark for time series forecasting that incorporates heterogeneous contextual signals rather than only numeric histories. It spans fourteen datasets across eight domains and six context types, including metadata, events, holidays, news, images, and numerical covariates, and it evaluates statistical, data-specific, foundation, multimodal, and general-purpose LLM forecasters. The contribution matters because existing benchmarks under-cover context and rely on aggregate metrics that can hide model-specific weaknesses.

entry.title: ChatGPT Images 2.5 in the Wild: A Launch-Period Dataset and Detector Evaluation

author.name: Dennis Ng, Xingyu Shen, Ankit Raj, Kidus Zewde, Tommy Duong, Yuchen Zhou, Yuxin Zhang, Neo Tiangratanakul, Simiao Ren

entry.summary: The authors assemble a frozen launch-period dataset of 3,478 images from 2,440 posts across eight sources, collected within roughly the first 51 hours after the ChatGPT Images 2.5 announcement, to study version attribution and detector behavior. Because an image tool can swap its underlying generator while keeping its public name, the paper records multiple attribution tiers and treats caption claims and host records as admission evidence rather than verified generator identity. It also evaluates six frozen detectors and shows how source mixture skews the apparent content profile.

entry.title: PACE: Progressive Angular-to-Norm Contrastive Embedding

author.name: Yanping Li, Wei Zhou, Yawen Liu, Yibo Wang, Ke Zhu, Guangda Huzhang, Qing-Guo Chen, Zhao Xu, Jun Zhang, Wei Wei

entry.summary: Multimodal embedding models usually train with cosine-based contrastive objectives, which stabilizes training but confines semantic compatibility to angular geometry and prevents embedding norms from carrying meaning. Directly optimizing dot-product similarity uses both angle and norm but trains unstably, which the authors attribute to premature expansion of the optimization space manifesting as angular-norm entanglement and anisotropy. PACE progressively moves from angular to norm-aware contrastive training, aiming to recover the expressiveness of dot products without the instability.

entry.title: EMR: Self-Evolving Medical Multi-Agent System via Experience Mining and Reuse

author.name: Dongsheng Shi, Yue Li, Xin Yi, Linlin Wang

entry.summary: Existing LLM multi-agent clinical reasoning systems use static strategies and lack persistent memory, so they cannot improve from earlier diagnostic successes and failures. EMR maintains a hierarchical clinical experience library with clinical principles, diagnostic patterns, and representative cases, and at inference time simulates multidisciplinary consultation with a planner coordinating department-specific agents and a summary agent producing the final answer. It matters as a concrete mechanism for turning medical multi-agent systems into ones that accumulate and reuse clinical experience.

entry.title: Concept-Grounded Reasoning with Prompt-Driven Localization for Interpretable Structured Report Generation

author.name: Xinyue Xu, Hongbin Lin, Juangui Xu, Hualiang Wang, Lehan Wang, Lijie Hu, Weiyang Liu, Adrian Weller, Xiaomeng Li

entry.summary: CORAL is a multimodal framework for medical report generation that integrates spatial grounding and concept-level supervision into a unified reasoning process. It uses a prompt-driven segmentation model to localize lesions and then reasons over clinically defined intermediate attributes, improving grounding and interpretability over end-to-end fusion approaches.

entry.title: SlipSense: Multimodal Tactile Learning for Low-Latency and Generalized Slip Detection

author.name: Tong Jian, Aditya Thurvas Senthil Kumar, Xinyi Li, Ziling Chen, Tianyu Dai, Ali Sengul, Matteo Grimaldi, Wenjie Lu, Saleh Nabi, Tao Yu

entry.summary: SlipSense is a multimodal tactile slip-detection framework built on TacV5, a compact sensor combining a 32x32 piezoresistive array at 240 Hz with a 3-axis MEMS accelerometer at 8 kHz. The method performs modality-specific encoding, intra-sensor fusion, and cross-modal attention with causal temporal prediction at 240 Hz, trained on 1.4 million frames. It targets precise latency characterization and cross-platform generalization, both weaknesses of prior slip-detection systems.

entry.title: Driver Behavior Estimation at Signalized Intersections Using a Physics-Constrained Decision-Conditioned Autoregressive Transformer

author.name: Mohammad Khoshkdahan, Pavel Laskov, Alexey Vinel

entry.summary: The authors analyze and predict human driver stop-go decisions and longitudinal trajectories during traffic signal transitions using a physics-constrained, decision-conditioned autoregressive transformer. Data comprise 449 real-world approach runs recorded with centimeter-accurate RTK GNSS, plus driver heart rate and comfort ratings, with careful spatial and temporal calibration between vehicle state and signal timing. Statistical analysis identifies required deceleration as the dominant predictor of the stop-go decision.

entry.title: Evaluating Open-Weight E-Commerce Agents with Environment-Grounded Verification

author.name: Nimit Shah, Haitz S\'aez de Oc\'ariz Borde

entry.summary: The authors build a deterministic, reproducible e-commerce environment that precommits each trial's persona, difficulty, target cart, and item reveal schedule, then has a simulated consumer attempt to buy the target cart with help from the evaluated model. Environment state and every assistant action are recorded, letting the evaluator grade individual parts of the conversation against retained evidence rather than collapsing everything into a single task-success rate. This addresses the fact that many conversation routes lead to the same cart.

entry.title: SWB-DM: A Calibrated Sliced-Wasserstein-Barycenter Aggregator with Delayed-Momentum Caching for Byzantine-Robust Federated Learning under Partial Participation

author.name: Saranraj S, Saranya M S, Alex David S, Ajay Kumar A

entry.summary: The paper challenges the fragile assumption behind robust federated aggregation, that participating clients in a round fairly represent the population, noting that coordinate-wise median, Krum, Bulyan, and trimmed mean all lose their finite-sample guarantees under partial participation. SWB-DM treats each slice of a client update as a one-dimensional distribution, computes a trimmed Wasserstein barycenter across clients, and recovers coordinate identity via a medoid-based gauge-fixing step, adding delayed-momentum caching. The authors explicitly present the gauge-fixing step as a heuristic they do not claim to be principled.

entry.title: LLMs as Master Forgers: Generating Synthetic Time Series Data for Manufacturing

author.name: Mantek Singh, Jeshwanth Challagundla, Prateek Karnal, Gagan Ganapathy, Vineet Shah, Ridam Arora

entry.summary: This paper proposes a framework that fine-tunes large language models on manufacturing process instructions and adds retrieval-augmented generation to synthesize realistic time series data, motivated by the scarcity of labeled industrial time-series data. The authors benchmark their synthetic data against classical generators such as ARIMA and LSTM models using quantitative metrics and PCA-based distributional comparisons. It matters because synthetic data generation is a practical route to bootstrapping predictive maintenance and process models where real labeled records are expensive or rare.

entry.title: Certified Uncertainty Propagation in One-Shot Federated Bayesian Models via Posterior Event Transport

author.name: Mahyar Mohammadi, Mohammad Hossein Badiei, Abolfazl Yaghmaei, Hamed Kebriaei

entry.summary: This paper develops a deployment-consistent certification framework for one-shot federated Bayesian learning, where the deployed model results from aggregating parameters drawn from client-specific posteriors so local certificates do not guarantee safety of the aggregate. Clients construct disjoint hyper-rectangular regions in parameter space with computed probability masses, and the server propagates these posterior events through the aggregation rule, with an exact geometric characterization for Federated Averaging. It matters because it bridges probabilistic neural network certification and federated deployment.

entry.title: FlowATC: Aircraft Trajectory Prediction via Flow Matching

author.name: Mathurin Petit, Emir Torun, Louis Brusset, Jordan Kam, Alexandre M. Bayen

entry.summary: This paper builds a flow-matching trajectory predictor trained only on historical aircraft tracks, with no route labels or chart supervision, using 1.15 million ADS-B windows from the San Francisco Bay Area. The generated trajectory distributions reproduce real airspace structure, including the shape of a published departure procedure, and the model works directly on native irregular ADS-B sampling intervals. It is a strong demonstration of generative modeling for air traffic decision support.

entry.title: A Weighted Kernel Method for Approximation that Adapts to Learned Multivariable Structure

author.name: John E. Darges, Laura Weidensager

entry.summary: Approximating black-box multivariable functions from limited data is hard when input importance and interactions are unknown. The authors introduce total sensitivity kernels (TSKs) built on families of weighted ANOVA kernels that learn weights per input component, selecting the reproducing kernel Hilbert space in which the target has minimum norm. They prove uniqueness under suitable conditions and establish consistency for a finite-sample estimator.

entry.title: Geometry of learning dynamics: Gradient descent versus natural gradient on the ridge of optimization

author.name: Akira Tamamori

entry.summary: High-capacity Kernel Logistic Regression associative memories exhibit a Ridge of Optimization with extreme stability and a skewed weight spectrum, but how learning reaches that regime was unclear. This paper analyzes trajectories on the statistical manifold of a KLR-trained Hopfield network, comparing gradient descent with natural gradient descent. It finds learning on the ridge proceeds in two distinct phases and that the ridge's extreme curvature makes plain gradient descent oscillate.

entry.title: Information Geometric Self-Organization at the Edge of Stability in High-Capacity Kernel Associative Memories

author.name: Akira Tamamori

entry.summary: Kernel Logistic Regression associative memories show exceptional storage and robustness, with prior empirical work locating a hyperparameter regime called the Ridge of Optimization where attractor stability peaks. This paper examines the static geometry of parameter space and gradient descent trajectories in KLR-trained Hopfield networks using the Hessian eigenvalue spectrum. It finds the ridge is a phase boundary adjacent to a rank-1 spectral collapse, acting as a geometric singularity.

entry.title: Repurposing Unified Topological Signatures for Graph Representation Learning

author.name: Sanyam Sanjay Jain, Anshika Krishnatray, Aditya Sharma, Vinti Agarwal

entry.summary: To overcome the 1-WL expressiveness ceiling of message-passing GNNs, the authors introduce two Unified Topological Signature variants derived from persistent homology: Graph_UTS, a static signature of input topology, and Embedding_UTS, a dynamic signature of evolving embeddings. These provide multi-scale global topology cues that help distinguish non-isomorphic graphs with identical local structure.

entry.title: Learning-Guided Planning in Large Dynamic Action Spaces: Budgeted Tree Search for One-to-Many Mobile Charging

author.name: Liang-Ching Tao, Pi-Chung Wang

entry.summary: LP-BTS combines a graph proposal policy, a learned value critic, and edge-budgeted PUCT search to handle sequential decisions where the candidate action set is large, geometrically structured, and changes with state. The motivating application is one-to-many mobile charging for 250 sensors, where a single stop serves multiple in-range sensors and the action universe shifts as sensors deplete.

entry.title: Compute-Optimal Pretrain--Fine-tune in Ridge Gradient Descent

author.name: Alex Buna, Fanghui Liu, Patrick Rebeschini

entry.summary: The paper formalizes pretrain-then-fine-tune as a compute-split problem with a fixed total optimization budget, using regularized least squares trained by gradient descent as a tractable model. It characterizes the optimal allocation between upstream and downstream training under data-dependent evaluation geometries induced by the fine-tuning task, showing the split depends on how pretraining directions align with downstream structure. It matters because compute allocation between pretraining and adaptation is a central practical question in modern model development.

entry.title: Carry-Through Checksum: A Lightweight Fault-Detection for CNN Inference at the Edge

author.name: Kyrylo Nazarevych, Mohammad Hasan Ahmadilivani, Krister Kaldre, Davide Bertozzi, Jaan Raik

entry.summary: This work introduces carry-through checksum, a lightweight scheme for detecting soft errors during CNN inference on resource-constrained embedded GPUs. It contrasts with existing algorithm-based fault tolerance methods that rely on matrix augmentation and per-operation checksum verification and impose prohibitive overhead. The goal is low compute, memory, and latency cost while integrating with standard GPU inference pipelines.

entry.title: MedPCFM-TED: One-Step Point Cloud Flow Matching for Implant Generation via Teacher-Guided Endpoint Distillation

author.name: Kamil Kwarciak, Marek Wodzinski

entry.summary: The paper presents Teacher-guided Endpoint Distillation (TED), a one-step distillation framework for conditional cranial implant generation on point clouds. It trains a one-step student model using teacher-guided endpoint supervision and geometric matching losses, avoiding explicit path straightening, to reduce the multiple neural function evaluations required by flow matching. Evaluated on SkullFix and SkullBreak, TED achieves strong overall performance.

entry.title: Splitting the Difference: Interpretable Causal Forests for Treatment Effect Heterogeneity and Bias

author.name: Nicolas Alexander Ihlo, Merle Behr

entry.summary: This paper introduces a decision-tree and random-forest algorithm for estimating individual treatment effects that behaves like a standard random forest but swaps in a different splitting criterion, avoiding extra machinery such as double machine learning or orthogonalization. Because the splits are themselves interpretable, the method aims to explain why a treatment effect is larger for some individuals than others, which matters for medicine and marketing where prediction alone is not enough to justify decisions.

entry.title: Optimization over covariance matrices with a parameterized metric

author.name: Yibang Li, Bamdev Mishra, Pratik Jawanpuria, Cyrus Mostajeran

entry.summary: The authors define a two-parameter family of Riemannian metrics on covariance matrices, solving X^p L X^q + X^q L X^p = U for each tangent vector, which contains the Euclidean, Bures-Wasserstein and affine-invariant metrics as special cases at (0,0), (1,0) and (1,1). They analyze the conditioning of the Riemannian Hessian at the solution and show a lower bound depending on the parameters only through the exponent r = p + q, framing metric choice as problem-specific preconditioning.

entry.title: Optimal Model Activation Policies for Inference Networks of Large Language Models

author.name: Foivos Charalampakos, Md Ibrahim Ibne Alam, Iordanis Koutsopoulos, Koushik Kar

entry.summary: The authors introduce inference networks, a graph framework where nodes represent LLM experts and links represent conditional model activations, allowing simple queries to be routed to cheaper models and complex ones to more capable, costly models. The framework derives optimal activation policies for cost-performance trade-offs in ensemble or cascaded inference setups, addressing the lack of principled guidance on how to combine available experts.

entry.title: Beyond the Name: Demographic Leakage in De-Identified R\'esum\'es and Evaluation Artifacts in LLM Bias Audits

author.name: Qiangju Chen, Yang Xiao

entry.summary: This audit tests whether removing explicit language fields eliminates ethnocultural inference in de-identified resume screening, using nine open-weight models and 620 counterfactual resumes across five ethnocultural conditions and three cue-salience tiers. Target-group recovery averages 0.757 and saturates at 1.000 under high salience, showing unstructured prose alone sustains demographic inference, while models diverge mainly under faint cues. It matters for the validity of LLM bias audits and for claims that redaction makes screening fair.

entry.title: RoleBreak: Benchmarking Long-Horizon Role-Playing Robustness in Spoken Dialogue

author.name: Yuqi Wang, Fengyuan Liu, Haochen Luo, Zhiqi Yu, Qi Liu

entry.summary: RoleBreak is an open benchmark for long-horizon role-playing robustness in speech-to-speech dialogue, containing 310 character-based and user-centered roles, 6,688 human-verified turns, and 11,743 fine-grained evaluation criteria, with expressive emotion targets on many turns. Its scenarios stress role consistency, interaction quality, safety, and affect over extended interactions. It matters because existing spoken role-play benchmarks are short-horizon and mostly limited to predefined fictional characters.

entry.title: TIAO: Token Importance-Aware Policy Optimization for Text Summarization

author.name: Qixiu Li, Chenlong Bao, Xiang Zhu, Xiaoyong Li, Ruixin Cao, Shukai Chen, Zhenxiong Zhou

entry.summary: The authors propose TIAO, a reinforcement learning strategy for summarization that identifies core tokens via token dependency and reweights trajectory advantages according to token-level importance. This addresses the common practice of applying reward signals uniformly across all tokens, which ignores how much individual tokens contribute to consistency, coherence, and overall summary quality.

entry.title: Can LLMs Follow the Pulse of a Crisis? Evaluating Crisis Sentiment in Bangladesh's July Uprising

author.name: Md. Samiul Alim, Mahir Shahriar Tamim, Tanvir Ahmed Khan, Sharjil Khan, Rafia Ferdous Duti, Shahriyar Zaman Ridoy, Mohammad Ali Moni

entry.summary: The paper introduces UNRESTSENT200K, a Bangla crisis-sentiment dataset of roughly 200,000 Facebook and YouTube comments from the July-August 2024 Bangladesh uprising, organized into five event-aligned phases from escalation through internet blackout to regime transition and a later flood crisis. Comments are linked to parent posts so models can be evaluated with and without discourse context, with fully human annotation achieving substantial agreement.

entry.title: Lesion-centered 3D mapping of colonoscopy procedures: validation of a hierarchical ensemble pipeline on public benchmark videos

author.name: Hyunjun Kim, Hyeonwoo Na, Jaewoo Lee

entry.summary: The work asks whether a lesion-centered spatial record of a colonoscopy can be built and validated without full-colon 3D reconstruction, since video spatial information is normally discarded after a procedure. A four-layer hierarchical pipeline is assembled, covering a global topological map, lesion-level spatio-temporal tracks, on-demand local 3D reconstruction, and persistent lesion identity across repeat observations, then run end to end on public benchmark videos. It matters as a clinically motivated step toward automated procedure mapping and polyp re-identification.

entry.title: MAETrack: Unleashing the Potential of Pretrained Geometric Priors for 3D Single Object Tracking

author.name: Sifan Zhou, Qiwei Wang, Linyue Tan, Ziyu Liu, Ziyu Zhao, Xiaobo Lu

entry.summary: This work studies transferability of large-scale pretraining to 3D single object tracking, observing that naive fine-tuning of self-supervised 3D encoders such as masked autoencoders adapts poorly. The authors interpret this as a layer-wise transfer mismatch, where shallow layers retain transferable geometric cues while deeper layers become specialized to the reconstruction pretext task. It matters for understanding how to reuse 3D pretrained backbones in spatial-temporal matching tasks.

entry.title: TecoPrompt: Temporal-Conservative Prompt Learning for Vision-Language Models

author.name: Zeyi Shao, Haowen Hua, Jiaxin Zhang, John See, Zeyd Boukhers, Cong Yang

entry.summary: TecoPrompt is a closed-loop robust prompt-learning framework for vision-language models such as CLIP, targeting the problem that even moderate label noise disrupts prompt optimization under few-shot supervision. It revisits optimal transport pseudo-labeling from a temporal angle: an entropic optimal transport plan in CLIP semantic space generates globally consistent label candidates, and a candidate is only accepted as a rewrite if it stays stable across a K-epoch window and passes a confidence gate based on an exponential moving average. It matters for reliability of few-shot CLIP adaptation in noisy real-world settings.

entry.title: Accelerated Decoding of Centroid Positional Encoding for Instance Segmentation
