entry.title: Physically Aware Radiomics Without Interpolation: Disentangling Voxel Geometry and Signal Modification in CT and MRI

author.name: David Corral Fontecha, Juan Miranda Bautista, Pablo Menendez Fern\'andez-Miranda, Sergio Rubio-Mart\'in, Lara Lloret Iglesias, Jose A. Vega

entry.summary: The authors modify PyRadiomics so texture features respect physical voxel spacing instead of voxel-index neighborhoods, avoiding resampling. They compare native extraction, isotropic resampling, spacing-aware extraction, and a fake-isotropic control that swaps metadata without changing pixels. The study matters because it isolates how much of reported radiomic signal comes from true anatomy versus interpolation artifacts, a long-standing methodological confound in CT and MRI analysis.

entry.title: An Evolutionary Computation Framework for Multi-Agent Q-Learning with Mean-Field Environmental Feedback

author.name: Lichen Wang, Shijia Hua, Linjie Liu

entry.summary: The authors formulate a coupled learning-environment model where agents update stateless Q-values on a fixed graph while their average behavior drives an environmental variable that reshapes payoffs. A first-order mean-field closure yields a deterministic transport equation for the Q-value distribution, validated against finite-network Monte Carlo simulations on several graph types. It matters for understanding emergent dynamics in large networked multi-agent populations.

entry.title: Decoupling Error Attribution in Cloud-Native Graph-RAG: A Data Integrity Diagnostic Framework

author.name: Shuai Yan, Yuhang Wu, Xiaodong Huang, Ke Wang

entry.summary: The authors propose a three-layer diagnostic framework that attributes cloud-native Graph-RAG errors separately to reasoning loss, knowledge-graph defects, and Cypher generation errors. Testing on a spatio-temporal ecological KG with eight defect types, they find data integrity, not algorithmic reasoning, is the dominant bottleneck, with structural defects dropping accuracy from 0.93 to 0.39, and they describe a Parametric Knowledge Masking Effect where LLMs compensate for broken retrieval. It is a useful reminder that RAG pipelines often fail on data quality rather than model capability.

entry.title: A Three-Axis Stress Test of LLM vs Classical ML for Network Intrusion Detection under Distribution Shift and Adversarial Evasion

author.name: Muhammad Ebad Atif, Muhammad Haider Ali

entry.summary: This study compares XGBoost and a RoBERTa-LoRA model for network intrusion detection across same-dataset performance, cross-dataset transfer, and adversarial evasion using two independently collected NetFlow v2 networks. Same-dataset results are statistically tied, but XGBoost wins decisively under cross-dataset shift (by 15 F1 points), while the transformer's false positive rate reaches 0.78 on the target network. It matters because typical same-dataset benchmarks for LLM-based NIDS are shown to be misleading.

entry.title: A property-registry contract for retrieve-or-refuse thermal-mechanical lattice search

author.name: Shaoliang Yang, Henry Chu, Zu Yashengjiang, Jun Wang

entry.summary: This work applies established conflict diagnosis to a catalogue of homogenized thermal-mechanical lattice properties so that a design system can refuse to answer when no cell satisfies a request, and can identify which requirement to relax and by how much. Searching 1,397 unit cells and 19 base materials across 26,543 combinations either returns a catalogue row that a second solver can rebuild or an inclusion-minimal unsatisfiable subset of at most eight constraints. It matters as a concrete retrieve-or-refuse contract that prevents generative models from fabricating infeasible designs.

entry.title: Mind Which Bird You Favour: Parameterizing Adequacy-Fluency Balance in Meta-Evaluation of Machine Translation

author.name: Behzad Shayegh, Niloofar Kazemi

entry.summary: The paper points out that machine translation meta-evaluation embeds an implicit tradeoff between alignment with adequacy and with fluency, and that this balance depends on the particular mix of systems in the meta-evaluation set, which is a small and unrepresentative sample that shifts by year and language pair. The authors expose the balance as a tunable choice by reweighting systems to hit a target balance while minimizing distortion from uniform weighting. It matters for sensitive domains where controlling this balance is critical.

entry.title: Pre-PEFT Probing: Weight Statistics and Perturbation Robustness for Layer Selection in VLM Vision Encoders

author.name: Qingtao Xia, Jiahua Bao, Siyao Cheng, Jie Liu

entry.summary: Rather than applying LoRA and similar adapters to all layers by heuristic rule, the authors probe each transformer layer of a vision-language model's vision encoder before fine-tuning to estimate its adaptability. They characterize layers both by statistical properties of Q/K/V projection weights, such as norms and condition numbers, and by robustness under controlled parameter perturbations, then compare these indicators against downstream gains from selective adaptation. It matters for making parameter-efficient fine-tuning of VLMs cheaper and more reliably targeted.

entry.title: Multi-Label Proportion Learning for Sea-Ice Type Prediction

author.name: Samira Alkaee Taleghan, Younghyun Koo, Andrew P. Barrett, Farnoush Banaei-Kashani

entry.summary: This paper addresses sea-ice type prediction, where the only labels come from manually produced ice charts that annotate polygons rather than patches or pixels. Existing supervised approaches approximate patch labels by assigning each sample the dominant ice class from its polygon, discarding the mixed composition that ice charts actually encode; the authors instead formulate multi-label proportion learning. It matters for climate monitoring, polar navigation, and automated ice-chart production where polygon-level annotation is the practical bottleneck.

entry.title: Bounded Adjustment with Reliability-Guided Embedding for Imbalanced Learning with Noisy Labels

author.name: Mushir Akhtar, Akarsh J., M. Tanveer, Mohd. Arshad

entry.summary: The paper identifies a coupled failure mode in which class-balanced learning corrects for frequency but can amplify incorrectly labeled minority examples, and proposes BARGE, a single-stage objective combining a bounded prior-adjusted density-power score with reliability-guided angular geometry. The authors show the classification score is strictly proper in the adjusted probability space and recovers balanced Bayes ordering under clean supervision, while the bounded range limits risk perturbation under label contamination and the logit gradient redescends on confidently wrong predictions. It matters for real-world training data that is simultaneously imbalanced and noisy.

entry.title: Lit3R: Retrieve-Relate-Read for Evidence-Grounded Question Answering over Scientific Literature

author.name: Akira Ise, Kotaro Kumagai, Yuta Yamaguchi, Hisanori Ozaki, Yukio Uematsu, Ikuya Yamada

entry.summary: Lit3R is a shared-task system for literature-grounded QA that must retrieve relevant papers, locate supporting evidence, and generate answers with evidence traces. It chains off-the-shelf BM25 sparse and dense retrieval, cross-encoder reranking, LLM-based verification, and paper-to-paper expansion, then synthesizes evidence across papers without any task-specific training.

entry.title: TEDi: Temporal Memory-Enhanced and Denoising Transformer for Surgical Instrument Segmentation

author.name: Jiahong Yuan, Weiming Mi, Tao Zhang, Haoyin Zhou

entry.summary: TEDi addresses surgical instrument segmentation and recognition by adding temporal modeling to query-based segmentation, which usually makes per-frame predictions and ignores cross-frame priors. It introduces Memory Search Enhancement with a query-level memory bank and Temporal Consistency Denoising to stabilize query representations and improve category recognition. It matters for scene understanding and downstream tasks in computer-assisted surgery.

entry.title: Event-based Selective Attention for Multi-resolution Fast Region of Interest (ROI) Detection

author.name: Luca Peres, Giulia D'Angelo, Chiara Bartolozzi, Oliver Rhodes

entry.summary: The paper investigates a training-free, saliency-driven bottom-up attention model that operates directly on low-resolution event camera streams to select regions of interest. It is evaluated across multiple downscaling factors, with input resolution reduced by up to 256x relative to full resolution, on the large Prophesee Automotive dataset. The motivation is bandwidth, memory, and energy constraints in neuromorphic edge vision.

entry.title: Conditioning noise is a free regularizer for LoRA fine-tuning: no pathology encoder required for diffusion-based artifact detection in histopathology

author.name: Konstantinos Moutselos, Ilias Maglogiannis

entry.summary: The paper shows that fine-tuning a diffusion artifact detector while conditioning on random Gaussian embeddings, resampled each step from precomputed statistics with no encoder or cache, consistently widens the gap between clean and artifact-laden histopathology patches. A four-step ablation chain demonstrates the effect does not require embedding content, provenance, a tuned intensity, or per-patch identity, and a LoRA-dropout control attributes it to the conditioning pathway itself. The finding is offered as a free regularizer for LoRA fine-tuning.

entry.title: Collision-Aware Humanoid Whole-Body Control under Imperfect Tracking Targets

author.name: Mohitvishnu S. Gadde, Ashish Malik, Pranay Dugar, Aayam Kumar Shrestha, Alan Fern

entry.summary: RECAL is a Robot-Environment Cross-Attention Layer that wraps a collision-blind whole-body controller, using point-cloud representations of robot, held objects, and environment to trade off target tracking against collision avoidance. It supports floating-base and end-effector commands, including avoidance for held objects. It matters for making humanoid WBCs robust to geometrically unsafe targets from perception, planning, or teleoperation errors.

entry.title: Covariate Selection for Doubly Robust Double/debiased Machine Learning Estimators for Causal Inference

author.name: Muwon Kwon, Peter M. Steiner

entry.summary: This paper examines how machine-learning-based covariate selection interacts with the double robustness property of double/debiased machine learning estimators, noting that ML selection can cause differential selection or simultaneous misspecification of both nuisance models. The authors propose using the union of covariates selected for the treatment and outcome models as a practical remedy. It matters for applied causal inference with high-dimensional data where specification choices are otherwise opaque.

entry.title: How we might actually pace the frontier: A proposal for AI companies to do public pacing exercises.

author.name: Dewi Erwan

entry.summary: This proposal suggests frontier AI companies periodically halt all pre-training and reinforcement learning for 2-3 days as public 'pacing exercises', announcing scope in advance, inviting independent evaluators to define compliance evidence, and publishing findings afterward. The goal is to build institutional muscle and trust for larger slowdowns, buying time for alignment and societal preparedness.

entry.title: A Hybrid Agentic AI Framework for Intelligent Supply Chain Analytics

author.name: Xian Yeow Lee, Teppei Inoue, Haiyan Wang, Chetan Gupta

entry.summary: This paper proposes an agentic system for supply chain analytics in which a coordinator agent interprets user intent and delegates subtasks to specialised agents, covering database querying, KPI analysis, demand forecasting, and performance diagnosis. The design explicitly supports both exploratory analysis and deterministic workflows so planners can move between ad hoc questions and structured processes.

entry.title: Solar Intelligence

author.name: Jyotsna Singh

entry.summary: This paper presents Solar Intelligence, a hybrid retrieval-augmented framework that unifies structured solar analytics, evidence-grounded scientific question answering, and machine-learning forecasting in a single platform. It combines NASA POWER solar and meteorological data, Biosphere 2 ground-sensor readings, and a curated corpus of papers and reports, using DuckDB SQL for structured queries and a hybrid retriever that fuses BM25 with dense ChromaDB embeddings for scientific questions.

entry.title: Bypass Observation: A Conceptual Design of a Non-Intrusive Layer-Wise Semantic Extraction Architecture

author.name: Haibin Tong, Jiang Yu

entry.summary: The paper proposes Bypass Observation, a read-only architecture that attaches observation heads to selected Transformer layers to extract layer-wise semantic readouts without feeding those outputs back into the backbone, preserving the original model's behavior. It considers shared, layer-specific, and adaptive head variants and derives a closed-form overhead approximation governed mainly by the vocabulary-to-dimension ratio, discussing cost reductions via sparse observation, low-rank factorization, and top-k readout.

entry.title: VeriDx: Earning the Right to Diagnose with Disease-Centric Verification

author.name: Zhong Cao, Shuying Chen

entry.summary: VeriDx argues that a correct diagnosis can be reached for the wrong reasons, and introduces a disease-centric verification framework that links free-form clinical reasoning to structured disease profiles. It tracks whether each hypothesis satisfies, leaves unresolved, or violates its clinical obligations, exposing failures like missing critical tests or unresolved contradictions. This shifts medical LLM evaluation from final answers toward the commitments that hypotheses create.

entry.title: DynSTEER: Dynamic Stage-wise Trajectory Evaluation and Execution-time Review for Agents

author.name: Zhichao Shi, Xuhui Jiang, Wenjie Zhang, Xiaojun Wu, Cehao Yang, Chengjin Xu, Jian Guo, Yuanzhuo Wang

entry.summary: DynSTEER addresses the granularity problem in evaluating long-horizon LLM agent trajectories: whole-trajectory verification is too coarse to localize failures, while atomic step scoring is noisy and expensive. It introduces stage-wise dynamic evaluation that identifies meaningful stages, enabling earlier feedback and stopping during execution. The framework aims to replace single-reference trajectory comparison with assessment of the broader space of valid execution paths.

entry.title: Converting Sequenced Fuzzy Cognitive Maps to Causal Virtual Worlds with Large Video Generators

author.name: Akash Kumar Panda, Olaoluwa Adigun, Bart Kosko

entry.summary: The paper shows how users and agents built on LLMs and large video models can construct and manipulate causal virtual worlds. Feedback fuzzy cognitive maps encode local causal rules whose global equilibria define scenarios, and sequenced dynamical meta-rules of an if-then form select and drive the causal scenes rendered as video.

entry.title: STHMoE: Hypergraph-Enhanced Heterogeneous Dependency Coordination for LLM-Based Urban Traffic Data Forecasting

author.name: Jiawen Chen, Qi Shao, Yongjian Chang, Mingtong Zhou, Duxin Chen, Wenwu Yu

entry.summary: STHMoE is a spatio-temporal hypergraph-enhanced mixture-of-experts framework for urban traffic forecasting that combines frequency-domain decomposition with pairwise spatial and higher-order structural signals. The authors argue existing deep and LLM-based forecasting methods are too temporally centered and fail to coordinate heterogeneous dependencies under shifting traffic regimes. It targets practical intelligent-transportation analytics.

category.term: Domain Applications (Time Series, Finance, ESG, Education)

entry.title: CWM: Controllable White-Box Meta-Prompting for Adaptive Retrieval-Augmented Generation and Reasoning Ability

author.name: Keuntae Kim, Eunhye Jeong, Yong Suk Choi

entry.summary: CWM is a unified, task-agnostic framework that jointly addresses reasoning and retrieval-augmented generation through controllable white-box meta-prompting. The authors position it as a low-cost alternative to black-box approaches for adaptive RAG, avoiding dependence on external models. It contributes to the push for general-purpose rather than task-specialized LLM pipelines.

entry.title: Parameter-Efficient Adaptation of Pretrained Language Models for Time-Series Forecasting

author.name: Tamanna Kumavat, Georg Brunner, Kyriakos Flouris

entry.summary: The paper studies parameter-efficient transfer from pretrained language models to univariate time-series forecasting by projecting time-series patches directly into a GPT-2 embedding space, bypassing tokenization. Controlled ablations across seven datasets in energy, weather, traffic, and finance probe which design choices drive effective cross-modal transfer. It clarifies when language-model priors help numerical sequence modeling.

category.term: Domain Applications (Time Series, Finance, ESG, Education)

entry.title: Empirical Evaluation of Task-Based Permission Scoping Architecture for AI Agents

author.name: Halil Burak Noyan

entry.summary: The paper evaluates a task-based permission scoping architecture for AI agents, arguing that provisioning agents with static deployment-time credentials mirrors an outdated compromise made for human role-based access. It builds on prior work defining the task-context mismatch and proposes three sources of permission control: role-based ceilings, a task permission classifier, and policy-based prohibitions. The aim is to eliminate standing exposure of credentials not needed for the current task.

entry.title: Potential of Artificial Intelligence Algorithms for Identification of Relevant Diagnostic and Prognostic Biomarkers of Early-Stage Liver Cancer

author.name: Ali Bou Nassif, Darko Castven, Manar Abu Talib, Jibran Sualeh Muhammad, Ahmed Ammar Kubba, Jens Marquardt, Abdalla Sayed Ali

entry.summary: This study applies deep learning plus explainable AI to transcriptomic data to diagnose hepatocellular carcinoma and identify biomarkers across five disease stages, using a semi-supervised constructed dataset drawn from three source datasets. The best model reached 90.74 percent accuracy with 15 genes selected by SelectKBest, and a lower-loss variant used 20 genes. It is a domain application paper aimed at improving early detection of a cancer with poor late-stage outcomes.

entry.title: Pilot Early, Commit Late: A Real-Options Model of Enterprise AI Adoption under Rapid Technological Progress

author.name: Gaurav Tewari

entry.summary: This paper develops a two-period decision model of enterprise AI deployment under uncertainty in which a firm chooses among immediate deployment, a limited pilot, and waiting. Deployment captures current operating value but risks architectural obsolescence, waiting preserves the option to adopt later, and a pilot sacrifices current value to build organization-specific learning without full commitment. The model yields five central timing results plus a comparative result on where learning occurs.

entry.title: Multilingual Agent System for Inclusive Wildfire Evacuation Guidance

author.name: Shruti Kulkarni, Lynn Tong, Aditi Namboodiripad, Chelyah Miller, Helen Lin, Peeyush Patel, Bogdan Bistriceanu, Diane Myung-kyung Woodbridge

entry.summary: The authors build BEACON, a multilingual agent service that delivers personalized evacuation routing, checklists, and chatbot guidance in a user's own language, motivated by the fact that most US emergency messaging is English-only despite millions of residents with limited English proficiency. The work sits at the intersection of agent systems, multilingual NLP, and disaster response equity. It matters as a concrete deployment-oriented example of language technology aimed at marginalized communities.

entry.title: Forward-Facing Near-Infrared Adds Little to Colour for Farm-Machinery Traversability: A Site-Disjoint Evaluation of Sensor-Dependent Spatial Leakage

author.name: Sungwoo Kang

entry.summary: The study shows that reported advantages of near-infrared over color imagery for daytime agricultural traversability largely disappear when evaluation uses strictly held-out recording sites rather than sequence-level splits. None of color, NIR, a luminance control, or their fusion reliably outperforms plain color across five traversability classes. It matters as a clear demonstration of spatial data leakage inflating sensor-benefit claims in applied computer vision.

entry.title: Conflict-Predictive Variable Horizons in Multi-Drone Distributed Model Predictive Control

author.name: Linda M\"{u}mken, Michael Schwung, Stefan Lier, Andreas Schwung

entry.summary: The authors let each drone in a distributed model predictive control scheme set its own prediction horizon based on closed-form estimates of time to conflict with neighbors, extrapolated using confidence funnels. This avoids the fixed-horizon tradeoff between cheap but late reactions and costly long-horizon anticipation, without modifying the underlying controller. It matters for scalable collision avoidance in multi-drone operations.

entry.title: IMM-based Multiple Object Tracking using a State Prediction Neural Network

author.name: Chan-Bin Lim, Dong-Hee Paek, Seung-Hyun Kong

entry.summary: The paper adds a transformer-based state predictor that uses radar Doppler measurements as an additional Interacting Multiple Model mode alongside constant-velocity, constant-acceleration, and constant-turn physics models. The goal is better nonlinear motion representation while preserving the stability and interpretability of physics-based tracking. It matters for robust autonomous-vehicle perception in adverse weather where radar is dependable.

entry.title: Task-Aware Federated Fine-Tuning for MoE-based Large Language Models

author.name: Tingqi Wang, Hongyu Ke, Haoxin Wang, Rafal Angryk, Zhipeng Cai

entry.summary: FedTAR tackles federated fine-tuning of mixture-of-experts LLMs, where heterogeneous client task preferences cause naive aggregation to erode expert specialization and create conflicting updates on shared experts. The method introduces task-aware aggregation that preserves expert specialization across clients. It matters for privacy-preserving, resource-constrained distributed training of large MoE models.

entry.title: Attention Is All You Need (to Avoid Spurious Oscillations)

author.name: Jinyoung Jeong, Joseph B. Choi, Xinlun Cheng, H. S. Udaykumar, Sanghun Choi, Stephen S. Baek

entry.summary: The authors develop a conservative, fixed-grid finite-volume scheme in which a CFL-conditioned attention flux selects upstream information according to the transport required by the current timestep. Tested on one-dimensional inviscid Burgers transport, the learned flux stays reliable in small-step regimes and, at four times larger timesteps, preserves sharp shocks with one stage per update, benchmarked against WENO-5 with SSP-RK3. It matters as an attempt to bring learned attention mechanisms into conservative numerical PDE solvers.

entry.title: Not all Negation Cues are Equal: Affixal Negations Yield Better Negation Understanding

author.name: Tian Tan, Eduardo Blanco

entry.summary: The authors build NegCue, a dataset of over 1.8M samples spanning single-word, multi-word, and affixal negation with more than 200 unique cues, then pretrain encoder-only LMs and LLMs on it. Results across five benchmarks show negation types contribute unevenly, with affixal negation producing notably better negation understanding.

entry.title: Exploring Automated Vulnerability Identification in JavaScript Code Using Large Language Models

author.name: Manit Kaushik, Ishir Bhardwaj, Pranav Gupta, Pankaj Jalote, Arun Balaji Buduru

entry.summary: This empirical study evaluates three LLM families (Gemini 1.5 Flash, GPT-4o Mini, DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-8B) across zero-shot, chain-of-thought, and few-shot prompting plus fine-tuning for identifying JavaScript vulnerabilities. It uses 1,125 snippets spanning five CWE categories, motivated by SAST tools' failures on isolated code snippets.

entry.title: CRITICS - Critical Science Without Borders: Language Models to Promote Critical Thinking in Science Education

author.name: Rodrigo Agerri, Itziar Aldabe, Elena Cabrio, Mark Cieliebak, Jan Deriu, Mariana Flores, Jurgita Kapociute-Dzikiene, Dovile Kuiziniene, Arantza Rico, Aritz Ruiz-Gonzalez, Aitor Soroa, Mantas Vaskevicius, Serena Villata

entry.summary: CRITICS is a project proposal that combines LLM-based machine translation optimized for scientific content with educational technology, aiming to make scientific material accessible in students' native languages without losing technical accuracy. Building on these translations, it explores curriculum-aligned teaching and learning designs and investigates scientific argumentation and critical thinking. It is more of a research agenda and consortium description than a completed empirical study.

entry.title: RA-CoA: Training-free Fashion Image Captioning via Retrieval-Augmented Chain-of-Attributes

author.name: Abhirama Subramanyam Penamakuri, Shreya Shukla, Anand Mishra

entry.summary: This paper proposes a training-free fashion image captioning method built on instruction-tuned vision-language models, using retrieval-augmented chain-of-attributes reasoning. It targets fine-grained domain attributes such as neckline, closure types, patterns and silhouettes, and addresses the need for scalability as fashion inventories evolve rapidly with new vocabulary. Being training-free makes it adaptable without retraining as trends change.

entry.title: A New Transformer-Based Approach for Audio-Based Kinship Verification and a New Uncontrolled Mandarin Kinship Speech Dataset

author.name: Qiyang Sun, Langqing Zhang, Yupei Li, Bj\"orn Schuller

entry.summary: The authors propose CONVTRAP-TN, described as the first application of transformer architectures to audio-based kinship verification, and perform an ablation study on the design. They also release ARKIN, a Mandarin speech dataset with kinship labels recorded under everyday conditions, addressing the scarcity of such data. Existing kinship speech datasets either use extremely noisy internet data or are recorded in controlled settings.

entry.title: Bi-Level Routing and Sparse Spatial Attention based Multi-View BEV 3D Object Detection for Autonomous Driving

author.name: Jing Zhang, Jiaqi Liu, Zibo Wang

entry.summary: This paper proposes Sparse-BEVNet, an improved multi-view BEV 3D object detection algorithm for autonomous driving. It introduces Bi-Level Routing Attention into the image feature extraction backbone to cut computation, uses Cascaded Group Attention in the fusion module for cross-level interaction without extra overhead, and adopts a Sparse Spatial Cross-Attention mechanism for the 2D-to-BEV transformation. The focus is on reducing the cost and density of existing BEV pipelines.

entry.title: SpermYOLO: A Coordinated YOLO-Based Detector for Accurate and Efficient Sperm and Impurity Detection in Microscopic Images

author.name: Shengqi Chen, Zilin Wang, Xingyu Pan, Wenting Yu, Pengchao Deng, Guohua Wu

entry.summary: SpermYOLO is a compact YOLOv11-derived detector for joint sperm and impurity detection in microscopic semen images, adding channel-wise discriminative feature extraction (C3k2-IDB), spatial-spectral semantic enhancement (D2SEM), adaptive multi-scale fusion (MFM), and a detail-enhanced shared-prediction head. It reports 97.2% sperm AP and 75.4% impurity AP on the SVIA benchmark.

entry.title: PeerPen: AI-Assisted Writing for Online Mental Health Peer Support

author.name: Jiwon Kim, Sherry Gong, Maya Ajit, Soorya Ram Shimgekar, Yunhao Yuan, Dong Whi Yoo, Eshwar Chandrasekharan, Koustuv Saha

entry.summary: PeerPen is a writing assistance tool embedded in a Reddit-like interface that supports draft generation and revision of user-written responses in online mental health peer support communities. In semi-structured interviews with 15 participants, the authors find the tool reduced the burden of composing supportive replies and increased confidence, while participants wanted AI to assist without displacing their personal voice, raising questions of authorship, ownership, and trust. It matters for designing AI co-writing that preserves the authenticity central to peer support.

entry.title: CAL-MOS: Bridging Layers with Adapters for Robust MOS Prediction Across Speech Foundation Models

author.name: Alef Iury Siqueira Ferreira, Pedro Lustosa Rege Botelho, Fernanda Silva, Daniel Casanova, Rafael Faustino, Frederico Oliveira, Arlindo Galv\~ao Filho, Anderson da Silva Soares

entry.summary: CAL-MOS addresses non-intrusive speech quality assessment using Speech Foundation Models, where it is unclear which layer depths are most informative for MOS prediction and how to combine multi-layer information reliably. The authors benchmark ten SFMs on four MOS datasets under full fine-tuning, frozen last-layer probing, and naive cross-layer weighted aggregation, finding the best layer is strongly backbone- and dataset-dependent and naive fusion is unstable, then evaluate a layer-calibrated aggregation with adapters. It matters for making speech quality predictors robust across backbones and datasets.

entry.title: Rethinking Procedural Audio Pre-training: Source Scaling and Objective Adaptation

author.name: Jiajun Peng, Fengrui Liu, Xinyu Liu, Feng Liu

entry.summary: This work revisits procedural synthetic audio as a data source for transferable audio representation learning, separating scale into formula-class coverage and within-class rendering diversity. Using a controlled source with FDSL and AudioMAE, the authors find the two forms of scale help differently depending on the learning objective and downstream task, and that procedural audio favors much lower mask ratios (roughly 10-25 percent) than natural-audio datasets like AudioSet. The takeaway is that recipe choices from natural audio do not simply transfer, which matters for anyone building cheap, scalable audio pretraining pipelines.

entry.title: DepthBenchCAD: When Does Deeper Auditing Yield More Reliable Conclusions?

author.name: Hongye Yang, Zhihao Xie, Shengjun Xiong, Boxiao Huang

entry.summary: This paper questions the intuition that auditing generative CAD programs more thoroughly always yields better model-level conclusions, noting that under a fixed budget deeper per-program checks come at the expense of task and generation coverage. The authors decompose behavioral evaluation into task templates, stochastic generations, and within-program edits, define an average failure risk invariant to audit depth, and combine variance and measured execution costs to identify when deeper auditing helps or hurts. It matters as a methodological caution for evaluation design in code- and CAD-generating models.

entry.title: When Correlations Mislead: Confounder-Aware Multi-View Urban Region Representation Learning

author.name: Sean Bin Yang, Ying Sun, Zongyi Xu, Tung Kieu, Jilin Hu, Bin Yang, Kristian Torp, Hua Lu, Torben Bach Pedersen

entry.summary: This paper proposes CURE, a confounder-aware framework for multi-view urban region representation learning. Instead of only strengthening cross-view interactions, CURE encodes view-specific regional graphs and explicitly addresses spurious correlations induced by shared latent factors, which can destabilize downstream predictions in tasks like mobility analysis and safety forecasting.

entry.title: Multi-View Molecular Representation Learning with Hierarchical Graphs and Contextualized Fingerprints

author.name: Gwang-Hyeon Yun, Jong-Hoon Park, Bing Hu, Helen Chen, Anita Layton, Young-Rae Cho

entry.summary: HiFi-Mol pre-trains two complementary molecular encoders, a hierarchical graph encoder with fragment-aware masking and a contextualized fingerprint encoder that tokenizes chemical patterns, then integrates them for downstream property prediction. The goal is better generalization from limited labeled data to structurally novel compounds. It matters for drug discovery and chemistry where labeled data is scarce and single-view pretraining is limiting.

entry.title: A panoramic aerodynamic performance prediction method for turbomachinery cascades using transformer-enhanced neural operator

author.name: Qineng Wang, Zhendong Guo, Liming Song, Tianyuan Liu

entry.summary: This paper proposes a panoramic prediction framework that first predicts basic Navier-Stokes field quantities such as temperature, pressure, and density, then derives key turbine stage meridian-plane performance parameters from them, functioning more like a surrogate CFD simulator than a direct objective regressor. A transformer-enhanced neural operator is used to improve accuracy. The design aims to let designers query many objectives of interest quickly during turbomachinery design.

category.term: Scientific Machine Learning and Engineering Optimization

entry.title: Schema-Adaptive Action-Conditioned JEPA for Cross-Machine CNC Transfer under Partial Sensor Overlap

author.name: Ayoub Louaye Bouaziz, Matthieu Ostertag, Anton Demasles

entry.summary: This study examines schema-adaptive action-conditioned JEPA world models for CNC dynamics when the target machine shares only 10 of the source's 17 sensor channels, a realistic cross-machine transfer setting involving changed dynamics, sensing interfaces, sampling regimes, and control units. Evaluation uses group-disjoint source splits, source-only normalization, held-out self-supervised validation, unit audits, and a sealed target test after model locking. Notably, JEPA pretraining yields no clean-source forecasting gain, with scratch and pretrained-body models reaching nearly identical RMSE.

category.term: Scientific Machine Learning and Engineering Optimization

entry.title: Skeletal Prototypes on Iterative Nerve Expansions

author.name: Jordan Eckert, Henry Schenck

entry.summary: The paper introduces SPINE, a prototype-reduction method that represents each class as an embedded 1-complex (a graph-like skeleton) built from a class-conditional Mapper graph, rather than as a set of isolated points. Vertices are then fitted under a classification objective, and novel observations are assigned to the class whose complex is nearest, so the edge structure participates in the decision rule. It matters as a topologically motivated alternative to standard prototype selection, evaluated on seventeen benchmark datasets under stratified cross-validation.

entry.title: Decoder Design Matters for ECG Delineation

author.name: Joseph Scharpf, William Han, Chaojing Duan, Michael A. Rosenberg, Emerson Liu, Ding Zhao

entry.summary: ECG delineation finds the boundaries of P waves, QRS complexes and T waves, and accurate models need scarce manual annotations, motivating semi-supervised learning. The authors argue decoder architecture has been under-explored and propose R-U-Net, pairing a ResNet-18 encoder with a U-Net decoder, reporting consistent gains over a ResNet-18 plus fully convolutional head baseline across 16 in-domain semi-supervised settings. It is a practical architectural finding for medical waveform analysis.

entry.title: A Systematic Evaluation of Machine Learning Methods for Fault Detection and Line Identification in Electrical Power Grids

author.name: Julian Oelhaf, Georg Kordowich, Paula Andrea P\'erez-Toro, Tom\'as Arias-Vergara, Andreas Maier, Johann J\"ager, Siming Bayer

entry.summary: Renewable integration complicates grid protection, since static relay rules and thresholds handle faults such as short circuits poorly. This paper systematically benchmarks machine learning approaches for fault detection and identification of the affected line, comparing them against conventional protection practice and discussing safety-standard compliance. It offers an empirical map of which ML method families are suitable for this safety-critical task.

entry.title: Personalized Federated Learning through Global Knowledge Distillation and Local Head Adaptation

author.name: Polycarpo Souza Neto, Jos\'e Mairton Barros da Silva J\'unior, Charles Casimiro Cavalcante

entry.summary: pFedKDH aggregates only a shared backbone across clients, keeps persistent client-specific heads, and uses a recalibrated global head as a teacher during local training to handle statistical heterogeneity. Experiments on MNIST, Fashion-MNIST, CIFAR10, and CIFAR100 under Dirichlet class partitions show large accuracy gains over weak baselines with low variance.

entry.title: Hybrid Variational Quantum Circuits for Multivariate Regression and High-Dimensional Data Reconstruction

author.name: Koffi Ognandon Ayena (ICB), Fr\'ed\'eric Holweck (ICB), Serge Iovleff (UR4662), Amah S d'Almeida

entry.summary: The authors propose a hybrid variational quantum circuit that adds a classical affine post-measurement layer, enabling vector-valued regression without the linear overhead of independent scalar circuits. They show elementary one- and two-qubit circuits can approximate quadratic functions and products via data re-uploading and entanglement, and report performance matching Gaussian Process Regression and beating XGBoost and Random Forest on benchmarks.

entry.title: Crash Narrative-Guided Countermeasure Recommendation Using Large Language Models: A Retrieval-Augmented Generation Framework for Intersection Safety

author.name: Abu Saif Md Nasim Uddin, Mohamed Abdel-Aty, Zubayer Islam, Parvez Anowar, Chenzhu Wang

entry.summary: This study builds a retrieval-augmented generation framework that converts crash narratives into mechanism attributes (traffic control, signal indication, driver fault, vehicle movement) and then recommends site-specific countermeasures for intersection safety. It aims to replace labor-intensive expert judgment with a scalable LLM-based pipeline.

entry.title: Towards Surrogate Based Dequantization of Quantum Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Pablo Rodriguez-Grasa, Sofiene Jerbi, Mikel Sanz, Ryan Sweke

entry.summary: Building on recent kernel-based dequantization results, the authors construct efficient classical algorithms intended to match the performance of variational quantum reinforcement learning methods such as quantum Q-learning. The surrogate-based approach probes whether variational quantum policies can offer provable advantages over classical counterparts on practically relevant problems. It matters for setting realistic expectations about near-term quantum RL.

entry.title: Physics Informed Random Feature Neural Networks for Solving PDEs

author.name: Chi-An Chen, Chunyang Liao, Ming Zhong

entry.summary: The authors introduce a physics-informed random feature method that mitigates part of the spectral bias faced by physics-informed neural networks on certain classes of PDEs. Random feature methods approximate large-scale kernel machines and can be viewed as specialized randomized neural networks, and the proposed variant needs far fewer collocation points than state-of-the-art PINN solvers. It matters as a lighter-weight alternative in the fast-growing physics-informed solver literature.

entry.title: On the Expressive Power of Implicit Line-Graph Higher-Order Weisfeiler--Leman

author.name: Fan Yang

entry.summary: Motivated by Whitney's theorem, which lets isomorphism testing of most connected simple graphs be recast as distinguishing their line graphs, the paper studies Implicit Line-Graph WL, which is exactly k-dimensional Weisfeiler-Leman run on the line graph but executed over edges of the original graph using incidence-derived relations without constructing the line graph explicitly. It shows that on the Whitney-general class the relationship between root-domain and line-graph WL depends on k, with k equal to 1 or 2 adding no power beyond root-domain 1-WL. It matters for understanding the expressive limits of graph learning architectures tied to WL hierarchies.

entry.title: Measuring Annotation Efficiency for Handwritten Devanagari Recognition: Sample-Complexity Curves for Four Pretraining Regimes

author.name: Manglesh Kumar Pandey, Sumit Kumar Banshal

entry.summary: This study measures how many manually transcribed words are needed for a handwritten Devanagari recognizer to become useful, and how much of that cost pretraining can remove. Holding the recognizer, optimizer, and evaluation protocol fixed, it varies only the number of real transcribed words used for fine-tuning across nine budgets and four pretraining regimes. The work is relevant to low-resource scripts where annotation is bottlenecked by scarce specialists.

entry.title: Neuro-Symbolic Hierarchical Intention Anticipation in Human Behavior

author.name: Farnaz Soleimani (LISSI), Abdelghani Chibani (LISSI), Yacine Amirat (LISSI), Ghazaleh Khodabandelou (LISSI)

entry.summary: The paper formulates intention anticipation as goal inference plus structured prediction of remaining behavior from a partially observed multimodal episode, rather than exact motor forecasting. A compact Hierarchical Planning Decoder is attached to a frozen neuro-symbolic recognition encoder and predicts next actions, remaining activities and low-level intentions, and the episode-level high-level intention across four ontological levels, trained with soft neuro-symbolic regularization and decoded with hard reachability masks.

entry.title: Goal-oriented probabilistic forecasting for dynamic PRB allocation in 5G networks

author.name: Oier Larumbe-Lizarraga, Roberto Pereira, Cristian J. Vaca-Rubio

entry.summary: The paper argues that conventional symmetric error metrics ignore the asymmetry in 5G resource allocation, where under-provisioning degrades service far more expensively than over-provisioning wastes capacity. It trains DeepAR and Temporal Fusion Transformer models with a pinball loss and derives the cost-optimal allocation quantile from the operator's cost matrix, reducing operational cost on a real beam-level 5G traffic dataset.

entry.title: Tables Decoded: DELTA for Structure, TARQA for Understanding

author.name: Jahanvi Rajput, Dhruv Kudale, Saikiran Kasturi, Utkarsh Verma, Ganesh Ramakrishnan

entry.summary: This paper argues for structured textual representations of tables instead of table images processed by vision-language models, claiming better scalability and natural alignment with LLMs, especially for multilingual documents. It presents DELTA, which separates physical structure recognition, logical structure recognition and OCR to extract layout and content, and TARQA for table visual question answering.

entry.title: FRPSS: Feature Rearrangement in Pre-Shape Space for Single-Image Generation

author.name: Yuexing Han, Haoxuan Zhang, Bing Wang

entry.summary: FRPSS targets single-image generative models, which often fail to balance global structural integrity with local diversity and drift structurally when shapes vary. Its core module replaces randomly initialized low-scale generator features with rearranged pre-shape features and augments them on a geodesic surface to impose explicit global structural constraints. It matters for few-shot generative applications where only one training image exists.

entry.title: De-GAN - Dynamic Parameter Tuned GAN for 3D Medical Image Segmentation: A Step Towards Generalisation

author.name: Zoha Usama, Azadeh Alavi

entry.summary: This paper proposes DE-GAN, a contrast-enhancing conditional GAN that synthesizes slice-adaptive FLAIR images to improve brain tumor segmentation, targeting the low contrast of enhancing tumor and cross-site domain shift. It combines input-adaptive dynamic convolutions, style-aware feature mixing, and coordinate encoding, with a label-guided class-conditional target separating tumor-core and enhancing-tumor intensities. Synthetic FLAIR is concatenated with original modalities to train a 3D U-Net across BraTS 2015, 2018, and 2019.

entry.title: FAHCD-Net: Frequency-Adaptive Heatmap-Conditional Diffusion Networks for Robust Facial Landmark Detection

author.name: Jun Wan, Jiwei Hu, Shengkai Hu, Qilu Zhu

entry.summary: FAHCD-Net targets facial landmark detection under challenging conditions such as facial structural variation, information loss, and noise, where learned features lose integrity and accuracy. It cascades a Frequency-Adaptive Heatmap-Conditional Diffusion model with a Smoothness Regularization loss, and includes a Hierarchical Frequency Adaptation module that suppresses redundant high-frequency content. It matters for robustness of a foundational face-analysis primitive.

entry.title: FROD: Feature Matching Residual Denoising Oracle Bone Decipher

author.name: Yanbin Hou, Biao Xiong, Guojun Xu, Jianwen Xiang, Cheng Tan, Yanchao Yang, Junwei Zhou

entry.summary: FROD formulates oracle bone script decipherment assistance as cross-era image translation, since ancient characters often preserve radical-level topological invariants relative to modern counterparts. During training it uses fast feature matching to provide gated segmentation supervision, so paired samples with sufficient matches guide the translation while weak pairs are downweighted. This offers a computational aid to the otherwise expert-intensive study of early Chinese writing.

entry.title: ORCA: Occlusion-Aware Refinement and Completion for Novel View Synthesis

author.name: Weronika Jakubowska, Maciej Zi\k{e}ba, Przemys{\l}aw Spurek

entry.summary: ORCA tackles single-image novel view synthesis by distinguishing small depth-boundary holes, which need geometric refinement, from large disocclusions, which need generative completion. It injects 3D structure into a Gaussian-anchor representation using monocular depth while preserving original camera rays, avoiding expensive generative filling for the trivial gaps. The pitch is that most artifacts in this setting are not missing content but unresolved geometry.

entry.title: Automated Distinction of Intimal and Medial Intracranial Arterial Calcification from CT Head

author.name: Benjamin Jin, Maria del C. Vald\'es Hern\'andez, Richard Bortsov, Joanna M. Wardlaw, Daniel Bos, Grant Mair

entry.summary: This study compares three automated approaches for classifying intracranial arterial calcification into intimal versus medial subtypes from head CT segmentation masks: an adaptation of the radiologist visual score, a sphericity-based shape method, and shape embeddings from a medical shape foundation model. The distinction matters because the two subtypes differ in aetiology and clinical relevance and are normally separated by human visual assessment of calcification shape. It is a comparative evaluation on clinical neurovascular data with strong clinical co-authors.

entry.title: Structure-Preserving Quantum Circuit Architectures for Robot Kinematics

author.name: Andrea Morghen, Pierluigi Arpenti, Roberto Schiattarella, Giovanni Acampora, Bruno Siciliano

entry.summary: The authors design a quantum representation and circuit architecture for rigid-body transformations, specialized to Denavit-Hartenberg kinematics, factorizing translations into a classical magnitude and a single-qubit Bloch-vector direction with a selector register for normalization. The goal is structure-preserving encodings implementable on finite-depth hardware. It matters as an early step toward quantum formulations of robot kinematics.

entry.title: Auto-HSI: Personalized human control of a robot swarm on demand by using LLMs for online automatic code generation

author.name: Alessandro Nazzari, Nathan Cerisara, Dorian Tonnis, Raina Zakir, Lorenzo Labarile, Weixu Zhu, Marco Dorigo, Mary Katherine Heinrich

entry.summary: Auto-HSI uses natural-language descriptions and gesture demonstrations from untrained operators to automatically generate personalized state-machine code for controlling a robot swarm, covering motion, formation shape, and deformation. The prototype supports one- and two-handed gestures for centralized control. It matters for lowering the barrier to human-swarm interaction.

entry.title: ProxiDex: Learning Dynamics-Guided Proximity Policy for Dexterous Manipulation

author.name: Yushan Bai, Boyu Zheng, Zhiyang Mao, Hongzheng Sun, Yuchuang Tong, En Li, Zhengtao Zhang

entry.summary: ProxiDex treats hand-object proximity as an interaction state, reconstructing interaction point clouds and converting geometric distances into hardware-agnostic proximity cues to replace or augment tactile sensing. This provides feedback under occlusion and contact uncertainty for multi-finger manipulation. It matters as a sensor-agnostic alternative to tactile hardware for dexterous policies.

entry.title: IL-ACT: Imitation Learning with Adaptive Cartesian Tracking Control for a 30-ton Excavator

author.name: Mehdi Heydari Shahna, Seihun Kim, Soyi Jung, Soohyun Park, Jouni Mattila, Joongheon Kim

entry.summary: IL-ACT combines a 14-input imitation policy pretrained on operator demonstrations with adaptive Cartesian feedback, gated gain/bias estimation, and a stopping-distance governor for a 30-ton excavator. Evaluation covers 100 sequential goals plus tracking patterns across seeds, initializations, and speeds under hydraulic and sensing variation. It matters as a demonstration of learning-based control on heavy industrial machinery.

entry.title: FluxVLA Engine: A One-Stop VLA Engineering Platform for Embodied Intelligence

author.name: Yinhao Li, Weixin Mao, Zihan Lan, Jikun Rong, Qirui Hu, Yiming Zhang, Weipeng Deng, Bowen Shen, Minzhao Zhu, Yiming Mao, Yan Yang, Chenguang Cui, Hongyuan Chen, Xu Huang, Zheyi Zhao, Pinxi Shen, Bozhen He, Zhen Fu, Yifan Wang, Zexin Zhang, Ang Gao, Haoyu Chen, Chengqi Shi, Hua Chen

entry.summary: FluxVLA Engine is an open, configuration-driven platform that turns heterogeneous embodied-policy components, including datasets, vision-language and world models, action heads, and distributed training, into a reproducible data-to-deployment workflow. Rather than proposing another policy, it standardizes interfaces and evaluation protocols to reduce fragmentation in vision-language-action and world-action model research.

entry.title: Exact Fusion and Coordinated Exploration in Multi-Robot Active Inference

author.name: Peng Wu, Mohsen Imani, Amidu Kamara, Md Tamzeed Islam, Seyede Fatemeh Ghoreishi, Mahdi Imani

entry.summary: This paper analyzes how robot teams sharing a common environment model double-count evidence at fusion and converge on identical unknowns at planning, because the shared conjugate prior is effectively counted once per robot. It removes both errors by adding evidence increments to the shared natural parameter, using realized increments at fusion and expected increments at planning, so that corrected gains sum to the joint gain and redundancy is properly removed.

entry.title: Residual Fault Adaptation for Dexterous In-Hand Manipulation Under Runtime Joint Faults

author.name: Linan Deng, Xing Liu, Lin Hong, Feng Hua, Guijun Ma, Zuogong Yue, Fumin Zhang

entry.summary: Residual fault adaptation (RFA) is a teacher-anchored framework for compensating hidden command-channel faults during dexterous in-hand manipulation, keeping a frozen healthy teacher for nominal behavior while training a recurrent residual policy to infer corrections from proprioceptive and command-response history. Training uses fault-injection domain randomization over fault mode, affected joint, severity, and onset time, with adaptive sampling favoring poorly performing fault modes.

entry.title: Dissecting Motion-Prior Regularization for Data-Scarce Robotic Insertion

author.name: Ning Hu, Shuai Li, Jindong Tan

entry.summary: This study asks whether training-time motion-prior regularization improves insertion success when a diffusion policy is learned from only 15 demonstrations. It compares minimum jerk, speed-curvature coupling, their combination, no prior, and generic smoothness across 80 real-robot trials per setting in four condition classes, finding joint and minimum-jerk-only priors each reaching 70 out of 80 successes versus 66 for neither prior.

entry.title: RobResilience: Implementing and Evaluating a Resilience Framework for Cyber-Physical Embodied Systems

author.name: Gysella Imrell, Emanuele Miotto, Mahya Mohammadi Kashani, Mauro Conti, Alberto Giaretta

entry.summary: RobResilience implements a formal resilience framework for embodied cyber-physical systems in Webots using a PR2 robot and ROS2, evaluating whether an active attack has caused tolerable degradation or a state outside safe operating bounds. It targets the gap where detection systems cannot tell a safe degraded state from a catastrophic hazard during an ongoing attack. The work matters for runtime safety guarantees in autonomous robotic systems under adversarial conditions.

entry.title: FedV-KGQA in Practice: Design Lessons and an Interactive Prototype

author.name: Md Saikat Islam Khan Bappy, Oshani Seneviratne

entry.summary: This poster reports empirical findings on FedV-KGQA, which performs multi-hop question answering over vertically partitioned knowledge graphs where separate organizations own disjoint relation types over a shared entity space. Each silo trains a local knowledge graph embedding, and a server concatenates entity views and ranks candidates, keeping raw triples and relation embeddings inside each silo.

entry.title: LLM-Enhanced Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning for Unified Electric Vehicles-Charging Station-Grid Optimization in Public Charging Systems

author.name: Yang Zhang, Lindong Xie, Chongyu Wang, Gaojunjie Li, Siqi Bu, Edward Chung

entry.summary: This paper proposes an LLM-enhanced multi-agent reinforcement learning framework that jointly optimizes grid stability, EV charging satisfaction, and charging-station profitability in a single loop. The LLM component addresses two bottlenecks in conventional MARL for this setting: interpretable feature selection from massive IoT sensing data and adaptive balancing among conflicting stakeholder objectives.

entry.title: AI Deployment Accountability Engineering: A Vision for Accountable AI in Safety-Critical Socio-Technical Systems

author.name: Murat Kantarcioglu

entry.summary: This vision paper argues that model-centric evaluation properties like accuracy, robustness, fairness, and interpretability are necessary but insufficient once AI operates inside changing socio-technical environments with distribution shifts, institutional constraints, human feedback loops, privacy requirements, and multi-agent interactions. It proposes AI Deployment Accountability Engineering as a new engineering subdiscipline focused on post-deployment accountability. It is a framing contribution for how AI engineering should handle the operational lifecycle.

entry.title: Another Blueprint In The Wall: How to Ask Frontier AI Like a Kid?

author.name: Afshin Khadangi

entry.summary: The author runs ten prompt sessions per model across six frontier systems from OpenAI, Anthropic, xAI and Google DeepMind, asking them to design an architecture for a school audience. Responses repeatedly converged on a common pattern involving persistent latent state, adaptive computation, memory, specialist routing, verification, stopping control and delayed decoding, with the audience framing appearing to be a key condition.

entry.title: TryOnReward: Learning Foveated Consistency for Reinforcement Fine-Tuning of Virtual Try-On

author.name: Xueheng Li, Yong Liu, Xiaolong Fu, Wen Xue, Chengjun Xie, Yipeng Sun, Yan Li, Simiu Gu

entry.summary: The paper builds a fine-grained reward model for virtual try-on, arguing that generic VLMs and classic fidelity metrics correlate poorly with human judgments and cause reward hacking during reinforcement fine-tuning. The reward is built on a vision-language backbone with a foveated consistency design targeting garment and person detail preservation. It matters for making preference optimization in image generation more robust in detail-critical domains.

entry.title: BEACON: Behavior and Appearance Control for Subject-Specific Video Generation

author.name: Pokrzywa Baptiste, Nabyl Quignon, Yara Bahram, Muhammad Osama Zeeshan, Antitza Dantcheva, Eric Granger

entry.summary: BEACON is a lightweight framework for person-specific video generation that disentangles visual identity from subject-specific expressive behavior, addressing the tendency of single-reference-image methods to produce identity-preserving but behaviorally flat videos. It targets the facial dynamics that characterize how an individual expresses emotion over time. It matters for personalized avatar and human-centric video synthesis quality.

entry.title: Pedestrian Crossing Intent Classification From Event-Based Vision Using Convolutional Spiking Neural Networks With Temporal Augmentation

author.name: Henok Teklu, Mustafa Sakhai, Maciej Wielgosz, Matej Mertik

entry.summary: This work builds an end-to-end pipeline that converts JAAD driving footage into synthetic DVS event streams and augments training with CARLA-simulated event data to classify pedestrian crossing intent using convolutional spiking neural networks. The goal is safety-critical, low-latency, energy-efficient perception that tolerates motion blur, high dynamic range, and class imbalance better than frame-based RGB networks. It matters for neuromorphic perception in autonomous driving.

entry.title: Predictive audio representations for early detection and tracking of hidden dynamic objects

author.name: Katerina Vinciguerra, Moritz Brandes, Danilo Hollosi, Letizia Marchegiani

entry.summary: This work extends audio-based perception for autonomous vehicles from single-vehicle scenarios to early detection and tracking of occluded, hidden traffic agents using predictive audio representations. It argues omnidirectional auditory cues complement vision, which is constrained by field of view, enabling earlier danger anticipation.

entry.title: Entropy-Punctured Bloom Filters for Memory-Efficient Machine Learning

author.name: John Cartmell, Mihaela Cardei, Ionut Cardei

entry.summary: The paper proposes entropy-punctured Bloom Filters, a memory-aware encoding that removes low-variability bit positions identified via empirical entropy from fixed-length Bloom Filter encodings of quantized features. The resulting reduced representations preserve predictive structure while improving prediction performance in some settings. It also extends Bloom Filter encodings toward regression tasks, which prior work largely ignored.

entry.title: AlgoRAG: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Theoretical Computer Science Education -- A Comprehensive Evaluation Framework for Algorithm Analysis and Complexity Theory

author.name: Sushan Adhikari

entry.summary: The paper introduces AlgoRAG, a retrieval-augmented generation system built specifically for teaching theoretical computer science topics such as algorithm analysis and asymptotic complexity. It pairs an LLM with a curated knowledge base of textbooks, hundreds of lecture slides, practice problems, proof templates and complexity worksheets, and adds domain-specific handling for mathematical notation and entity recognition. It matters because it targets a niche where generic chatbots struggle: formal proofs and notation-heavy reasoning that students need explained adaptively.

entry.title: Cross-Block Conditioning in Deep Boltzmann Machines for Statistical Data Fusion

author.name: Junichiro Niimi

entry.summary: The paper studies statistical data fusion, where two panels share covariates but observe disjoint outcome blocks so that no row observes both outcomes, which rules out standard discriminative training of a Deep Boltzmann Machine. It proposes observed-block multi-prediction, restricting the multi-prediction objective to targets each row actually observes, well defined for any missingness pattern and reducing to the original criterion for complete rows. It matters for clarifying when a joint model is actually needed versus simpler conditioning.

entry.title: Circuit-MLLM: Topological Logic-Guided Latent-Space Visual Reasoning for Circuit Schematic Understanding

author.name: Jinyuan Deng, Yuqi Jiang, Wenjing Huang, Xin Li, Qi Sun, Cheng Zhuo

entry.summary: Circuit-MLLM targets multimodal reasoning over circuit schematics, which generalize poorly for current MLLMs because of dense component layouts and distinctive topological logic. It reformulates circuit analysis as device localization, path tracing, and sequential reasoning in latent space, supported by a circuit knowledge mining mechanism that aligns latent representations with multi-granularity structural features. The work is relevant to electronic design automation and engineering assistants.

entry.title: Privacy-enhanced federated learning via asynchronous aggregation and local differential perturbation

author.name: Zhen Zhong (Georgetown University, Washington, D.C., USA), Shini Yang (LinkedIn, CA, USA), Liesheng Wei (Shanghai Ocean University, Shanghai, China)

entry.summary: This study presents a federated learning framework combining dynamic differential privacy, lightweight homomorphic encryption, and local differential privacy, together with an asynchronous aggregation strategy using version control. Experiments on CIFAR-10 and Purchase-100 report accuracy up to 82.6% even under strict privacy budgets (epsilon = 0.1) while reducing communication overhead. It contributes a layered privacy design for distributed training in asynchronous environments.

entry.title: From Foundation Embeddings to Cropland Maps: Label Efficiency, Temporal Transferability and Independent Human Validation

author.name: Mohammad Ammar Mughees, Giovanni Montefoschi, Zhongxin Chen, Maria Antonia Brovelli

entry.summary: The study tests whether annual AlphaEarth geospatial foundation embeddings support cultivated versus non-cultivated cropland mapping in Maine, using 192 spatially separated patches and USDA Cropland Data Layer labels. Without fine-tuning the foundation model, a lightweight classifier reaches 93.7 percent overall and 90.8 percent balanced accuracy, with logistic regression nearly matching a gradient-boosted ensemble and a parameter-free nearest-centroid rule also performing well, plus temporal transferability checks and independent human validation.

category.term: Trustworthy ML: Explainability, Bias and Validation

entry.title: Continual Learning for Traversability Prediction with Uncertainty-Aware Adaptation

author.name: Hojin Lee, Yunho Lee, Daniel A Duecker, Cheolhyeon Kwon

entry.summary: This paper proposes a continual learning framework for traversability prediction in unstructured environments that incrementally adapts to new terrains using a generative experience recall model, addressing catastrophic forgetting of previously learned terrain experience. It couples the replay mechanism with uncertainty-aware adaptation so the robot can gauge reliability when terrain conditions shift.

entry.title: Quantum-Inspired Trainable and Parameter-Efficient Tensor Networks for Image Inpainting

author.name: Shiwen An, Konstantinos Slavakis

entry.summary: This work introduces quantum-inspired tensor-network circuits as trainable transforms for image inpainting, including a diagonal quantum Fourier transform relaxation that is invertible with O(N^2 log N) cost for N-by-N images. The circuit structure inherently preserves minimum coherence during training, removing the need for explicit coherence penalties, and unconstrained gradient-based phase optimization lets the learned transform generalize to test images through fixed sampling masks.

entry.title: Type-IV Code Clone Detection via Layer-Wise Non-Contrastive Representation Learning

author.name: Luciano Marchezan, Kevin Delcourt, Eugene Syriani, Houari Sahraoui

entry.summary: The authors propose LWVIC4Code, a non-contrastive representation learning approach for detecting Type-IV code clones, which are semantically equivalent but syntactically different code fragments. Built on VICReg-style variance-invariance-covariance regularization with layer-wise training, it avoids the careful negative sampling and bias that contrastive methods require.

entry.title: AraMIP: Extending MIPVU Towards Metaphor Identification in Arabic

author.name: Mandar Marathe, Manar Ali, Sara Nabhani, Raia Abu Ahmad, Ibrahim Baroud, Omar Momen

entry.summary: AraMIP is a new annotation guideline for metaphor identification in Arabic that adapts the widely used MIPVU procedure to Arabic-specific properties, distinguishing Isti'ara (metaphor), kinaya (metonymy and indirect expression), and related figurative categories. The work targets a language that remains under-resourced for metaphor research.

entry.title: Vision And Text Transformer For Predicting Answerability On Visual Question Answering

author.name: Tung Le, Huy Tien Nguyen, Le Minh Nguyen

entry.summary: The paper reframes VQA answerability, whether a given image-question pair can be answered at all, as a regression task rather than a binary mapping derived from a VQA system's output. It proposes VT-Transformer, which fuses visual and textual features via a Transformer, and validates on the VizWiz 2020 dataset against competitive baselines. The framing matters for accessibility-oriented VQA where questions are frequently unanswerable.

entry.title: FSANet: Frequency-Spatial Aware Network for Image Segmentation

author.name: Ruibo Wang, Ziyi Shen, Huaming Wu, Dong Liang, Kun Shang

entry.summary: FSANet aims to improve image segmentation under occlusions, poor lighting, and irregular structures by combining prior knowledge with a dual-domain solver. It proposes a Structure Prior Module to recover overlooked details, a Dual-Domain Awareness Module to capture salient features while disentangling noise, and an edge estimation component. The critique of transformer-based segmentation is their reliance on long-range spatial features and resulting computational cost.

entry.title: Evaluating Mesh Reconstruction Methods for Crop Phenotyping

author.name: Karanvir Singh, Theo Morales, Binh-Son Hua, Mukesh Saini

entry.summary: The study benchmarks seven mesh reconstruction pipelines for digitizing agricultural crops, measuring output fidelity and consistency qualitatively and quantitatively. The goal is remote phenotyping, letting specialists inspect 3D crop models without being physically on site for the whole growth cycle. Results indicate that certain newer pipelines (GGGS, PGSR and others) produce the most usable meshes.

entry.title: ConGraspXL: Controllable Constraint-Conditioned Dexterous Grasping Motion Synthesis

author.name: Hui Zhang, Mirko Meboldt, Jie Song

entry.summary: ConGraspXL extends the authors' prior GraspXL system to generate dexterous grasping motions that satisfy heterogeneous task-driven constraints such as approach direction, desired contact regions, wrist trajectories, and functional hand poses. It introduces a hierarchical constraint formulation and a masked residual interface for flexible constraint composition. The goal is controllable, scalable grasping motion synthesis across objects and hand morphologies.

entry.title: LLMDE: A Large Language Model-Driven Differential Evolution Algorithm for Portfolio Optimization

author.name: Rong Chai, Vaclav Snasel, Xiaopeng Wang, Seyedali Mirjalili, Crina Grosan

entry.summary: LLMDE uses prompt engineering to let a large language model dynamically choose mutation strategies and configure control parameters for differential evolution based on optimization feedback, reducing reliance on handcrafted hyperparameter design. The method is evaluated on the CEC2022 benchmark suite against standard DE and representative metaheuristics, then applied to a CVaR portfolio optimization problem using factor analysis and K-means clustering for stock selection. It is an instance of LLMs being used as adaptive controllers for classical optimizers.

entry.title: UDAV: Uncertainty-Driven Adaptive VLM Waypoint Planner

author.name: Ghazal Farhani, Shabnam Shabani

entry.summary: UDAV draws multiple stochastic trajectory predictions from a vision-language model, selects the medoid as a nominal route, and estimates predictive uncertainty from spatial dispersion, triggering a reconsideration stage when interior-waypoint uncertainty exceeds a threshold. It is evaluated on 400 held-out queries from two UAV flights for UAV-guided ground-vehicle navigation. It matters for making VLM-based navigation reliability-aware.

entry.title: CorrRisk-WM: Corridor-Conditioned Risk World Modeling for Safety-Critical Trajectory Planning

author.name: Tingyu Guo, Reza Langari

entry.summary: CorrRisk-WM couples a latent environment model that recursively predicts agent states and interactions with a lightweight recurrent risk module that estimates per-slice intrusion and near-miss hazards over candidate-trajectory corridors, aggregating them into survival-based first-entry risk. The design is explicitly planning-oriented, evaluating candidate-specific risk rather than generic motion prediction. It matters for safety-critical autonomous driving planning.

entry.title: Why I'm doing the Susan Calvin Project

author.name: Haoxing Du

entry.summary: The author explains the motivation for the Susan Calvin Project, an independent observatory that collects AI agent trajectories from real-world deployments to monitor, measure, and understand AI behavior in the wild. The argument is that the evals ecosystem needs to be complemented by real-world monitoring, with labs monitoring their own traffic alongside an independent voice covering open models and holding labs accountable. It matters as infrastructure for detecting misbehavior and incidents in actual usage rather than benchmark settings.

entry.title: How to think about LLM effort

author.name: Tao Lin

entry.summary: The post formalizes the 'effort' setting on an LLM as an input to both the model and its RL reward function, modeling reward as raw reward minus a penalty term that grows with token length and shrinks with effort. It argues the model should spend tokens up to the point of zero marginal net reward, providing a framework for reasoning about over- and under-thinking.

entry.title: Enabling Creative Exploration for Vibe Design Agents

author.name: Yifan Zhang, Nghi D. Q. Bui, Georgios Evangelopoulos, Arnaud Benard

entry.summary: This paper addresses the problem that vibe design agents produce one valid page rather than coherent alternatives, and that raising token temperature varies aesthetics and syntax together. It separates exploration from implementation with a pre-pass that proposes structured design specifications with typicality scores, an external selector, and a downstream generator that realizes the chosen specification.

entry.title: CRAF: Cross-View Residual-Aware Fusion for Deepfake Speech Detection

author.name: Minh-Xuan Phan, Khalid Zaman, Candy Olivia Mawalim, Masashi Unoki

entry.summary: CRAF fuses self-supervised speech representations, which capture low-level acoustic detail, with auditory large language model representations that provide higher-level context for deepfake speech detection. The residual-aware fusion explicitly disentangles view-shared information from view-specific complementary cues to improve generalization to unseen spoofing attacks.

entry.title: Benchmarking Intra-Patient 3D Deformable Multimodal Image Registration

author.name: Matteo Barbieri, Giammarco La Barbera, Juan Pablo De La Plata, Sabine Sarnacki, Isabelle Bloch, Pietro Gori

entry.summary: This benchmark compares classical optimization-based and modern learning-based methods, including foundation models, for intra-patient 3D multimodal deformable image registration across three datasets spanning different anatomies. Evaluation uses complementary metrics such as Dice similarity and 95th-percentile Hausdorff distance on both synthetic deformation recovery and real clinical data. It provides a rare apples-to-apples comparison in a clinically critical but hard-to-evaluate area.

entry.title: CiteGuard-RAG: A Validation-Centered AI System for Evidence-Grounded Question Answering

author.name: Sumit Barua, Guan Hong, Halil Dursunoglu, Charles Rodgers, Alvis Fong

entry.summary: CiteGuard-RAG combines hybrid semantic-lexical retrieval, citation-constrained generation, sentence-level grounding validation, and single-pass regeneration, using runtime validation to decide whether a candidate answer is accepted, refused, or regenerated. It is evaluated on 400 questions across a controlled housing-law dataset, PrivacyQA, and CUAD. The system's contribution is treating validation as a first-class runtime control rather than a post-hoc filter.

entry.title: Signed p-adic Residual Encodings of Finite-Domain All-Different Systems with a Sudoku Case Study

author.name: Greg Baker

entry.summary: This work studies signed, weighted affine p-adic residual objectives as native encodings of finite-domain constraints, showing that appropriately weighted positive unary rows pin coefficients to allowed sets while negative rows reward unequal endpoints or clause satisfaction. A coordinatewise domination theorem places every global minimizer inside the finite domain, with the loss reducing to all-different conflict counts or negated satisfied-clause counts. Standard Sudoku provides an 81-coefficient case study without a one-hot lift.

category.term: Scientific Machine Learning and Engineering Optimization

entry.title: You Don't Need To Train: Agentic Heuristic Learning Studio for Executable Human Activity Recognition

author.name: Siyu Yuan, He Zhang, Sizhen Bian, Bin Guo

entry.summary: AHL Studio applies an agentic heuristic learning approach to human activity recognition, where a learning-time agent reasons over sensor protocols, proposes executable heuristic policies, records repair traces, and exports an LLM-free policy for edge deployment. The motivation is that people learn activities by remembering examples, forming rules, and repairing mistakes rather than by backpropagation. On eleven HAR datasets, the resulting executable policies reach strong performance while avoiding gradient-based training.

entry.title: HuMemSLAM: Efficient Human-Inspired Semantic Place Recognition for Robust Visual SLAM

author.name: Mayowa Adebambo, Sebastian Donnelly, Armand Amaritei, Andrew Bradley, Alexander Rast

entry.summary: HuMem-VPR is a human-memory-inspired visual place recognition module that exploits the bidirectional relationship between bottom-up perceptual evidence and top-down semantic expectation, intended to improve robustness under perceptual aliasing and perceptual variation. It targets the dual requirement of high retrieval accuracy and low latency for real-time semantic SLAM deployment. The framing borrows from human memory and perception to organize the recognition pipeline.

entry.title: Learning Choice Model Trees for Feature-Based Multi-Product Pricing: Exact Optimization and Field Evidence

author.name: Jiajie Zhang, Yanqiu Ruan, Xiao Jin, Chung Piaw Teo

entry.summary: The authors develop OCMT-MNL, which jointly optimizes a customer-segmentation tree and multinomial logit demand models within each leaf at a prescribed depth, instead of the usual greedy one-split-at-a-time construction. The exact dynamic program derives closed-form Fenchel lower bounds during constrained Newton iterations and propagates them across nested and disjoint customer subsets to avoid redundant fitting. The work matters for interpretable, feature-based pricing that also reports field evidence.

category.term: Applications in Pricing and Revenue Management

entry.title: Governing at Machine Speed: An Adaptive Intelligence Architecture for Real-Time AI Policy Enforcement

author.name: Sandeep Bokkasam, B. Durgalakshmi

entry.summary: This paper describes an attestation deficit in enterprise AI governance: organisations have policies but cannot produce auditable, tamper-evident evidence of enforcement within regulatory timelines. It draws on survey and incident statistics and argues the failure is organisational and architectural rather than a matter of intent, then outlines an adaptive intelligence architecture for real-time policy enforcement.

entry.title: Windowed A-K-MDP

author.name: Xiangwen Yang, Frankie Cho, Iadine Chades

entry.summary: The authors show that the existing A-K-MDP algorithm for building interpretable abstract MDPs can skip better abstract states because it picks a discretisation divisor via binary search. They propose Windowed A-K-MDP, which enumerates every distinct feasible partition induced within a declared divisor window and evaluates candidates until it achieves zero value loss or exhausts the family, tested across 33 K-MDP instances.

entry.title: Partition Scores Are Not System Scores: Deployment-Fidelity Gaps in Decomposed Algorithm Selection

author.name: Jiachen Zhang, Yu Tang, Li Zhu

entry.summary: The paper defines the deployment-fidelity gap as the difference between partition-level oracle-style scores and genuinely deployable end-to-end utility in decomposed algorithm selection. It derives accounting consequences, including a per-instance margin-regret stability condition indicating when a partition-time family choice transfers to a learned within-family selector, arguing that commonly reported oracle quantities overstate deployable performance.

entry.title: AcquireBound: Runtime Authorization for Resources Acquired by AI Agents

author.name: Genliang Zhu

entry.summary: AcquireBound targets a post-fulfillment activation gap in which autonomous agents acquire compute, credentials, accounts, services, or other agents, and standard payment, budget, OAuth, mandate, or fulfillment checks do not decide whether a returned resource may become usable authority. The proposed provenance-bounded runtime authorization architecture quarantines acquired outputs, resolves actual capabilities from authenticated provider evidence via a versioned resolver, and activates them only through a current activation transaction. It spans tool-mediated creation, inter-agent delegation, and agentic commerce.

entry.title: ANASSA: An Agentic AI Orchestration Framework for Spatial Intelligence

author.name: Constantinos Papantoniou, Brian Hilton

entry.summary: This work surveys and synthesizes recent agentic GIS frameworks, benchmarks and surveys to identify limitations in spatial reasoning, execution robustness and evaluation. It then proposes ANASSA, an orchestration framework that combines LLM/LMM reasoning with tool-based geospatial execution to make expert-driven GIS workflows semi-autonomous.

entry.title: Rolling Day-Wise Mortality Prediction in Critically Ill Patients With AKI on CRRT Utilizing Machine Pressure Waveforms

author.name: Shehan Irteza Pranto, Joanna Yang, Joshua Lambert, Stuart L. Goldstein, Lili Chan, Girish N. Nadkarni, Tiago K. Colicchio, Javier A. Neyra, Jin Chen

entry.summary: This clinical ML study uses minute-level circuit pressure waveforms from CRRT machines, which are normally discarded due to shared-device records and artifacts, to predict day-wise mortality in critically ill AKI patients. The authors align machine records to charted therapy intervals to prevent cross-patient leakage and clean non-physiological minutes before modeling. It matters because continuous device data could reveal deterioration earlier than periodic lab-based risk reassessment.

entry.title: A Voxel-Spacing-Aware Extension of PyRadiomics for Anisotropic Texture Analysis
