author.name: David Corral Fontecha, Juan Miranda Bautista, Pablo Menendez Fern\'andez-Miranda, Andrea Trapote Fernandez, Lara Lloret Iglesias, Jose A. Vega

entry.summary: The authors implement and validate a voxel-spacing-aware extension of the PyRadiomics toolkit so that texture features reflect physical distances in anisotropic CT and MRI acquisitions without generating interpolated gray levels. The framework modifies GLCM, NGTDM, GLRLM, GLDM and GLSZM computations across the Python frontend, C wrapper and computational backend, and is validated with synthetic 3D phantoms. It addresses a known methodological flaw in radiomic feature extraction.

entry.title: Surrogate-Assisted Genetic Programming with Phenotypic Characterisation in Dynamic Multi-Mode Project Scheduling

author.name: Yuan Tian, Yi Mei, Mengjie Zhang

entry.summary: This study investigates phenotypic characterisation (PC) within surrogate-assisted genetic programming to evolve scheduling heuristics for dynamic multi-mode resource-constrained project scheduling under a fixed budget of expensive full-simulation fitness evaluations. It compares three PC encoding schemes to determine how individuals should be encoded to support effective surrogate fitness estimation.

entry.title: From Visual Feedback to Textual Reviews: A Multi-Agent Vision-Language Framework for Image-Grounded Review Assistance

author.name: Utsav Kumar Nareti, Ayush Bansal, Kumari Priya, Chandranath Adak, Soumi Chattopadhyay, Muhammad Saqib, Saeed Anwar

entry.summary: The paper defines image-grounded review assistance, a new task where editable review drafts are generated from user-uploaded product images, going beyond objective captioning to require contextual explanation and subjective opinion. A multi-agent vision-language framework is proposed to produce these drafts from visual feedback such as defect, packaging, and usage photos. It matters for e-commerce, where visual feedback is abundant but users rarely write detailed text.

entry.title: Physics Informed Neural Network model for the dynamical study of Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm

author.name: Adri\'an Robles Arques, Mart\'in Ruiz Fernandez, Javier Sanchis, Miguel A. Teruel, Juan Trujillo

entry.summary: This work develops a three-dimensional physics-informed neural network framework to simulate pulsatile blood flow in the human aorta over a two-minute interval, extracting high-fidelity pressure and velocity fields. Wall stress is quantified via Laplace's law with temporal averaging, and the approach avoids the mesh generation and computational cost of conventional CFD by exploiting automatic differentiation. It matters as a demonstration of PINNs as a practical alternative for patient-specific hemodynamic analysis.

entry.title: TEAR: Table Extraction with Attribute Recommendation from Texts via Large Language Models

author.name: Tong Li, Shuye Ding, Jiachuan Wang, Yongqi Zhang, Shuangyin Li, Lei Chen, Bo Li

entry.summary: Prior LLM-based table extraction work assumes inputs are table descriptions or specialized documents, overlooking naturally occurring text such as news reports and social media posts. TEAR targets two resulting difficulties: high variability and absent structural cues that break fixed heuristic prompts, and manually predefined schemas that fail to capture unexpected attributes. It matters for information systems that need to turn unstructured narrative text into structured tables with recommended attributes rather than a rigid preset schema.

entry.title: End-to-End Cell Detection via Instance-aware Graph Modeling

author.name: Ruochen Liu, Yalin Zheng, Jingxin Liu, Jianfeng Zhang, Shoujun Huang, Dexing Kong, Haofeng Li, Wei Lou

entry.summary: This work proposes an end-to-end framework for cell detection and classification that jointly models visual appearance and relational structure among cell nuclei, avoiding the usual two-stage pipeline of visual extraction followed by graph-based relational modeling. The goal is simpler training and joint optimization for pathology analysis.

entry.title: More Than Just Access: Generative AI as Communication Intermediary for Blind and Low-Vision Users

author.name: Protik Dey, Mohd Saifuzzaman, Taslima Akter

entry.summary: Based on semi-structured interviews with 19 blind and low-vision participants, this study examines generative AI tools such as ChatGPT, Gemini, Be My AI, and Seeing AI as communication intermediaries for reading labels, describing scenes, and substituting for asking other people for help. It documents both benefits and risks as these tools displace interpersonal assistance. The work matters for accessible AI design and for understanding dependency and trust dynamics.

entry.title: A Dynamic Aggregation Strategy Enhanced Efficient Global Optimization Algorithm for Solving High-Dimensional Turbomachinery Design Problems

author.name: Qineng Wang, Zhendong Guo, Yun Chen, Guangjian Ma, Liming Song, Jun Li

entry.summary: DA-EGO decomposes a high-dimensional (d at least 30) expensive black-box design space into low-dimensional subspaces for surrogate-based search, then combines subspace optima into an elite point for the global search. Crucially, subspaces are not fixed: their variables are updated each iteration based on variable interaction analysis in both sub- and full spaces, detected via perturbation methods and analysis of variance. The target application is budget-constrained turbomachinery design.

category.term: Scientific Machine Learning and Engineering Optimization

entry.title: Channel-Informed Neural Network for Physical Layer Key Generation

author.name: Jose Angel Sanchez Viloria, George Sklivanitis, Dimitris Pados, Elizabeth Serena Bentley

entry.summary: The paper proposes a channel-informed neural network for physical-layer key generation that derives binary key features directly from received IQ measurements while grounding the learned representation in the underlying multipath channel. A multi-task recurrent network jointly learns reciprocity-preserving binary features and an auxiliary channel estimate, trained with a combined objective. It matters for edge and resource-constrained wireless deployments that need lightweight key establishment without centralized infrastructure.

entry.title: Balancing Trial and Reorder: A Hybrid Sequential Transformer-GBDT Ranker for On-Demand Delivery

author.name: Marcel Kurovski, Attila Nagy, Steffen Klempau, Aleksandr Fedintsev

entry.summary: The paper presents Universal Venue Ranker, a production store-ranking system deployed at Wolt that pairs a bidirectional transformer encoder for sequential user modeling with a gradient-boosted decision tree ranker using contextual, user, and store features. It handles the tension between surfacing new stores for trial and preserving ranking quality for reorder-intent sessions, while enforcing local delivery constraints at inference and replacing four previously separate ranking models. It matters as a documented industrial case of hybrid deep-sequential plus GBDT ranking under real operational constraints.

entry.title: Beyond Measurement Metrics: A Human-Centered Framework for Semantic Validation of Network Traffic Classification

author.name: Igor Cherepanov, David Sessler, Alex Ulmer, Thorsten May, J\"orn Kohlhammer

entry.summary: The authors adapt a knowledge-generation framework to network traffic classification, combining data, ML models, explainability, visualization and expert reasoning so analysts can iteratively explore and verify whether a classifier learned semantically meaningful traffic patterns rather than spurious correlations. It matters because near-perfect predictive metrics currently say nothing about whether a deployed security model is trustworthy.

category.term: Trustworthy ML: Explainability, Bias and Validation

entry.title: Bio-Inspired Palette Evolution in Indirectly Encoded Substrates: Timescale Compatibility Shapes Activation Function Discovery

author.name: Romain Claret, Michael O'Neill, Paul Cotofrei, Kilian Stoffel

entry.summary: The paper treats the choice of which activation functions should be available to nodes in indirectly encoded neural networks as a meta-learning problem, designing 13 strategies (11 inspired by biological adaptation mechanisms, plus baseline and oracle controls) that add or remove functions during evolution. A key finding is that timescale compatibility between the palette dynamics and the evolutionary process determines whether useful activation functions are discovered.

entry.title: PunGraph: Retrieval-Enhanced Phonetic-Semantic Graph Reasoning for Pun Understanding

author.name: Yuchen Su, Zijian Huang, Yaotian Shi, Shaoxin Zhong, Ruofan Wang, Mengze Li, Yonghua Zhu, Diana Benavides-Prado, Michael Witbrock

entry.summary: PunGraph is a retrieval-enhanced knowledge graph framework that builds a phonetic-semantic lexical graph from phonetic dictionaries, IPA and grapheme-to-phoneme representations, and WordNet definitions to constrain LLM reasoning over candidate words and senses. The authors also release WebPun, a new large-scale dataset for pun understanding. It matters because puns expose weaknesses in LLMs' phonetic modeling and uncontrolled end-to-end generation.

entry.title: Reduplicative constructions in Mandarin: Socio-emotional profiling through distributional semantics

author.name: Chaoyi Wu, Yu-Hsiang Tseng, R. Harald Baayen

entry.summary: This study uses word embeddings from distributional semantics to analyze two productive Mandarin reduplicative constructions, testing whether embeddings can recover their semantic, grammatical, and socio-emotional properties. It also examines how useful embedding spaces are for understanding a semantically complex word-formation process.

entry.title: Geometry vs Structure: Graph-Based Diagnostics for LiDAR Point-Cloud Simulation Fidelity

author.name: Ghazal Farhani, Taufiq Rahman

entry.summary: The paper argues that conventional geometric metrics such as Chamfer distance can miss structural discrepancies when validating simulated LiDAR point clouds against real scans for digital-twin testing of autonomous driving and ADAS pipelines. It proposes a graph-based framework that builds graphs from real and simulated point clouds to capture connectivity, topology, and object-level organization. The contribution is a diagnostic methodology for simulation fidelity rather than a new simulator.

entry.title: Bi-MoDe: Bilateral Control-based Imitation Learning via Modifier-Conditioned Decoding for Modulation of Execution Speed and Contact Intensity

author.name: Takumi Kobayashi, Masato Kobayashi, Yuki Uranishi

entry.summary: Bi-MoDe injects a constrained latent modifier into every layer of a Transformer action decoder via adaLN-Zero, letting operators specify execution speed and contact firmness at inference time in bilateral-control imitation learning. It is evaluated on a real whiteboard-wiping task with temporal and physical modifiers. It matters for giving humans runtime control over contact-rich learned manipulation.

entry.title: Tendon-Driven Continuum Robot with Modular Stiffness and In-Situ Self Pose Estimation

author.name: Guo Ning (Andrew), Sue, Zheng Cao, Junzhe Hu, Xiangyun Bu, David Quinn, Tiancheng Wu, Zackory Erickson, Carmel Majidi

entry.summary: This paper presents a modular continuum robot built from interchangeable joints with analytically precomputed stiffness, combined with onboard magnetic-sensor proprioception and a per-joint learning model reused across configurations. The system is self-contained and avoids external sensing infrastructure. It matters for adaptable, deployable continuum robots in confined environments.

entry.title: Artificial Intelligence-Enabled Space Robot Operations: Technologies, Challenges and Prospects

author.name: Zeyuan Huang, Gang Chen, Zixuan Hao, Guoqin Tang, Junyi Zong, Guoyou Ban, Jiale Wang, Haoyang Lv, Chaoqian Ren, Sitong Liu

entry.summary: A review of AI-enabled space robot operations (AI-SRO) organized around capability building, covering operational scenarios, autonomy trends, and space-specific constraints such as scarce mission data, unusual dynamics and sensing, limited onboard resources, and strict safety requirements. It serves as a roadmap for transferring robot learning and embodied foundation models to orbit and planetary missions.

entry.title: DriveMCP: An Agentic AI framework for Advanced Driver Assistance System

author.name: Farzad Nadiri, Mehdi Cina, Ahmad B. Rad

entry.summary: DriveMCP is an agentic driver-assistance framework that combines perception, compliance reasoning, vehicle-state interpretation, and safety arbitration into a modular, auditable pipeline. It uses DriveLM as a vision-language front end to produce graph-structured scene understanding and language-grounded driving information, derives compliance cues such as speed limits through a structured parsing layer rather than simulator ground truth, and orchestrates specialized experts via a Model Context Protocol style interface.

entry.title: Online Geometric Change Detection via Scene Decomposition

author.name: David Thorne, Samuel Jia Cong Chua, Nakul Joshi, Aiden Wong, Christa S. Robison, Philip Osteen, Brett T. Lopez

entry.summary: The CDSD framework performs accurate online geometric change detection for long-duration single- and multi-session robot missions using LiDAR or RGB-D sensors, identifying changes such as fallen trees or opened doors that inform online planning. Instead of expensive global map comparisons, it spatially decomposes mapped environments so changes can be detected online within a single session.

entry.title: Optimized Wrench Polytope Analysis for Real-Time Stability Control of Legged Robots in Complex Multi-Contact Configurations

author.name: Friedrich Graaf, Elias Birkefeld, Christian Eichmann, Elias Hofele, Tristan Schnell, Georg Heppner, Arne Roennau, R\"udiger Dillmann

entry.summary: This paper proposes an optimized algorithm for evaluating the full actuatable wrench polytope in arbitrary contact scenarios for legged robots traversing difficult terrain such as slopes, caves, and scaffolding. The speedup allows per-joint torques to be computed within a 49 Hz control loop, and the stability controller is evaluated extensively in simulation and validated on a walking robot.

entry.title: Geometric Flow enhanced Graph Coarsening

author.name: Chaoqun Fei, Guoxuan Li, Tinglve Zhou, Chuanqing Wang, Yangyang Li

entry.summary: This paper proposes a graph pooling/coarsening method that moves beyond rough topology-based node clustering by exploiting higher-order mutual connections among neighbors. It uses a geometric flow perspective to capture how easily information passes along edges, reflecting neighborhood closeness, to improve pooling quality in graph convolutional networks.

entry.title: Building a Production Greek-English Speech Recognizer

author.name: Christos Petrocheilos, Cleopatra Papadopoulou, Chris Porikis, Ioakeim Perros, Ayoub Kirouane, Themistoklis Nikolis

entry.summary: This engineering report describes building Sophea, a production bilingual Greek-English ASR system, evaluated against nine production gates covering word error rate in both languages, language identification, and hallucinations on non-speech audio. Across 23 training iterations and two architectures, no single data composition passed all gates, revealing tight tradeoffs between Greek noisy-environment accuracy and English language identification. It matters as a candid account of real-world ASR deployment tradeoffs for lower-resource languages.

entry.title: Trustworthy, Explainable, and Sustainable Decentralized Intelligence for 6G Networks

author.name: Giovanni Perin, Michele Rossi, Enrique Tom\'as Mart\'inez Beltr\'an, Fernando Torres-Vega, Jos\'e Mar\'ia Jorquera Valero, Manuel Gil P\'erez, Eunjeong Jeong, Nikolaos Pappas, Farah Abed Zadeh, Chamara Sandeepa, Bartlomiej Siniarski, Madhusanka Liyanage, Bet\"ul G\"uven\c{c} Paltun, Leyli Kara\c{c}ay, Ioannis Pitsiorlas, Marios Kountouris

entry.summary: This paper argues that AI in 6G shifts from an add-on optimization tool to a distributed structural layer spanning an edge-cloud continuum, making centralized cloud analytics untenable due to latency, bandwidth, and governance costs. It surveys decentralized intelligence approaches addressing trustworthiness, explainability, and sustainability across 6G domains.

entry.title: FedLTLib: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Federated Long-Tail Learning

author.name: Changkun Lin, Junxiao Wang

entry.summary: FedLTLib introduces a benchmark for federated learning under long-tail data distributions, which the authors formalize as double heterogeneity spanning both client-level non-IID data and severe class imbalance. It targets realistic mobile and edge settings where rare but critical classes are extremely scarce. The benchmark aims to standardize evaluation of methods meant to handle this combined challenge.

entry.title: Semantic-Aware Neural Video Codec for Error-Resilient Low-Latency Transmission

author.name: Matin Mortaheb, Homa Esfahanizadeh, Jinfeng Du, Harish Viswanathan

entry.summary: The paper proposes a semantic-aware multi-level neural video coding scheme built on the real-time DCVC-RT codec, partitioning encoded representations into packets by semantic and latent-feature importance and assigning them to prioritized streams over packet-erasure channels. An error-resilient entropy module and unequal protection support low-latency, task-oriented video communication for physical AI systems. It matters for robot and embodied systems that need reliable video over unreliable wireless links.

entry.title: ViperQ: Order Flow Pattern Recognition via Auction Market Theory for Reinforcement Learning Trading

author.name: Asser Moustafa, Rares-Mihail Neagu, Jugal Kalita

entry.summary: ViperQ builds a reinforcement learning trading system whose state representation is constructed explicitly from Auction Market Theory primitives such as Volume Point of Control, Value Area position, Low Volume Node flags, Cumulative Volume Delta divergence, and tape-velocity signatures, assembled into a 20-dimensional normalized vector. Two proximal policy optimization agents are trained on this representation, offering the first peer-reviewed computational instantiation of these practitioner microstructure concepts.

entry.title: SAILOR: Solver-Assisted Interactive LLM-based Optimization Recovery

author.name: Shaghayegh Sadeghi, Stephen L. Smith, David C. Del Rey Fern'andez

entry.summary: SAILOR targets natural-language optimization problem statements that omit necessary numerical data, detecting unsupported numeric choices, asking the user targeted follow-up questions, and revising the model before solving. Missing values are prioritized using uncertainty plus solver-derived sensitivity estimates of how much each value affects the current model. The pipeline is tested on 1,723 instances across seven masked benchmarks, showing a practical route to reliable LLM-to-solver translation.

entry.title: MOSCOPT: Mixture-of-Skills Collective Optimization for LLM Agents

author.name: Zhenyu Zhang1, Jiudong Yang

entry.summary: MOSCOPT proposes a text-native, gradient-free method that jointly optimizes a pool of N natural-language skills plus a gating skill that dynamically selects K skills per step, instead of optimizing a single prompt template. Optimization uses EditAdam with maintained dual states, yielding monotonic improvement through interleaved three-phase updates without parameter tuning. The paper reports experiments and ablations across several benchmarks showing gains from composing complementary strategies.

entry.title: AppliedScientist: Automated Scientific Revision Through Iterative AI Reviewing

author.name: Vidushee Vats, Karun Sharma, Shengzhi Li, Shichao Pei

entry.summary: AppliedScientist is a closed-loop system pairing an autonomous AI scientist with an AI reviewer, evaluated by iteratively revising rejected papers across multiple research subfields. The scientist can access its own prior drafts to mimic how human authors build on earlier versions, while each review is generated independently so the reviewer has no memory of earlier feedback or scores. Three revision settings are compared, including one initialized with original venue reviews, testing whether acting on reviews measurably improves papers.

entry.title: ProIQA: A Process-Based Framework for Fine-Grained Math Item Quality Assessment

author.name: Junkai Tong, Mingjia Li, Haoran Chen, Yaoyu Jiang, Hanjie Ge, Yixuan Wang, Hong Qian

entry.summary: ProIQA proposes process-aware quality assessment for automatically generated math problems, scoring items along knowledge concepts, difficulty, and disciplinary competencies. The authors argue existing item quality methods rely on manual review or shallow stem-level metrics that miss the reasoning required for math. The work targets reliable automatic item generation for personalized education.

category.term: Domain Applications (Time Series, Finance, ESG, Education)

entry.title: Option-Aware Retrieval and Task-Specific VLM Adaptation for Medical VQA

author.name: Tristan Kirscher (ICube, Institut Strauss), Niklas C. Koser (CAU), Soren Pirk (CAU)

entry.summary: This is a MedReason 2026 challenge submission covering multiple-choice and open-ended medical visual question answering under fully offline, containerized inference. The authors report that multiple-choice retrieval must compare answer semantics rather than answer labels, since labels are assigned per question, raising retrieval-only accuracy from 20.0 to 57.5 percent on a 200-case holdout. They also attribute system accuracy through ablation of task-specific low-rank adaptation.

entry.title: Data storytelling meets interpretable machine learning: Decoding AI decisions for non-experts without revealing sensitive data and model details

author.name: Lemen Chao, Zixuan Yang, Anran Fang, Mingran Sun, Ming Lei

entry.summary: This design-science study integrates data storytelling with interpretable machine learning to make AI decisions comprehensible to non-experts without exposing sensitive data or proprietary model internals. It proposes a formal definition of data storytelling within IML, introduces the DIST Pyramid to align the two, and presents an I-P-O model plus an architecture for generating decision explanations. The focus is bridging the accessibility gap between technical explanations and lay audiences.

entry.title: Variational Template Matching with Statistical Fusion for Anomaly Detection in Patterned Structures

author.name: Qinwu Xu, Yifan Jiang

entry.summary: The paper proposes representing anomaly templates as a family of transformed instances and detecting defects via normalized cross-correlation over that transformation space, adding a kernel-density-estimation anomaly score for robustness. The goal is to retain the interpretability of classical template matching while handling scale, rotation, and perspective variation in small-data regimes. It matters for industrial inspection settings where deep learning is impractical.

entry.title: Bridging Thought and Action: Taming Long-Horizon Instability in Open-Source LLM Agents with a MetaTool-Enhanced ROS Framework

author.name: Kazi Abrar Mahmud, Nilotpaul Kundu Dhurubo, Tamal Kirttonia, Sabbir Hossain Ujjal, Mohammad Ariful Haque

entry.summary: The paper addresses unstable long-horizon reasoning and inefficient action execution when open-source LLMs drive robotic agents, proposing an intermediate MetaTool mechanism that forces the model to produce a pseudo-code plan of tool invocations stored in the ROS-Agent scratchpad. This persistent structured plan is meant to improve task reliability and execution efficiency in agentic robotics. It is relevant to making open-weight models viable for embodied control.

entry.title: Adaptive Phase-Switching for Communication-Efficient Federated LoRA Fine-Tuning

author.name: Jerry Adams Franklin

entry.summary: This paper measures per-round upload and download bytes for a bidirectional B-only federated LoRA protocol, correcting common accounting that ignores asymmetric transition rounds and grouped-query attention shapes. It places five methods on a single communication-quality frontier and introduces ReverseAdaptive, an aggregator that locates the frontier knee by monitoring relative global-loss improvement. It matters for more honest and efficient communication budgeting in federated LLM adaptation.

entry.title: Oops, Not Now: PEARL, a RAG-Based Support Agent for Gameplay and What Players Want from AI Help

author.name: Jiahong Li, Sai Siddartha Maram, Atieh Kashani, Ulia Zaman, Zhiyu Lin, Cameron Marano, Roger Azevedo, Jichen Zhu, Magy Seif El-Nasr

entry.summary: PEARL is a dual-component retrieval-augmented generation system for gameplay support in a puzzle game teaching parallel programming, combining semantic knowledge retrieval with structural board-state matching to deliver contextualized scaffolding. The paper also reports player expectations for AI help in games.

entry.title: Personalizing Personal Health Interfaces: Co-Design with Generative AI

author.name: Karthik S. Bhat, Vidhi Shah, Vedika Agnihotri, Dong Whi Yoo, Koustuv Saha

entry.summary: A co-design study in which 14 participants used Figma Make to redesign Google and Apple Health dashboards, exploring what personalized wellbeing interfaces might look like when generative AI lowers the technical barrier to design. Participants produced interfaces supporting personal context, future planning, and interactive experiences, yet their conversational AI designs converged on familiar chat-window conventions, and AI helped materialize vague ideas while also constraining the design space. It matters for HCI and health-tech practice by showing both the promise and the homogenizing pull of generative design tools.

entry.title: Spook the Machine: Gamified Exploration of Human Imagination of Machine Fear

author.name: Levin Brinkmann, Hiromu Yakura, Sonia Nicoletti, Mar Canet Sola, Thomas F. Eisenmann, Ali Dasmeh, Omar Sherif, Bramantyo Ibrahim Supriyatno, Prateek Gupta, Ignacio Serna, Rodrigo Bermudez Schettino, Iyad Rahwan

entry.summary: Spook the Machine is a gamified public-art platform where participants generate images to frighten AI agents given personality-driven phobias, with machines responding from calm analysis to pleas for mercy. In a Halloween 2024 deployment, 832 participants produced 15,719 artifacts across 89 machines in a 2x2 design varying emotional expressiveness and reward structure.

entry.title: Beyond AI Literacy: A Structured Review and Exploratory Meta-Analysis of Measures for Competent Generative-AI Use

author.name: Daniele Veri'

entry.summary: This structured review scans 24 focal empirical publications to catalog how researchers measure competent generative-AI use, grouping instruments into knowledge and use, epistemic oversight, reliance calibration, and operational control of tool-using agents. An exploratory meta-analysis of three subjective-objective correlations finds a near-zero pooled effect with wide confidence intervals. The paper highlights a measurement-validity gap that could undermine workplace AI-skills research.

entry.title: HintMiner: Automatic Question Hints Mining From Q&A Web Posts with Language Model via Self-Supervised Learning

author.name: Zhenyu Zhang, JiuDong Yang

entry.summary: HintMiner automatically generates hints for users' questions by retrieving large numbers of web Q&A posts and extracting hints from them with MiningNet, a transformer encoder-decoder equipped with copying mechanisms. The authors design a self-supervised objective to train the extraction model using the abundant online Q&A corpus rather than manual annotation. The goal is to help users find answers faster when forums such as Stack Overflow respond slowly or unsurprisingly.

entry.title: Pseudo-Label Augmentation for Affect Sensing in Small Collaborative Groups

author.name: Meisam Jamshidi Seikavandi, Tanya Ignatenko, Fabricio Batista Narcizo, Paolo Burelli, Jesper B\"unsow Boldt, Andrew Burke Dittberner

entry.summary: Using GroupAffect-4, a four-person collaborative dataset with wearable physiology, eye tracking, Big Five personality data, and post-task valence-arousal-dominance labels, the authors study pseudo-label augmentation for affect sensing under sparse supervision. They compare no augmentation, Gaussian Process pseudo-labelling, personality-aware trust weighting, and joint personality-plus-confidence weighting in a shared target-construction pipeline. Pseudo-label augmentation improves over the labelled-only baseline in known-team settings.

entry.title: FreqSpaNet: Frequency and Spatial Learning of SFPF for Physical Layer Hardware Integrity Detection

author.name: Xiaoxuan Huang, Jinlong Xu, YiZhe Wang, Meng Zhang, Xian Li, Yuying Bian

entry.summary: FreqSpaNet learns representations of spatio-frequency polarization fingerprints to detect unauthorized hardware replacement in wireless devices via open-set anomaly detection. It uses separate frequency and geometry-aware spatial branches with adaptive fusion, capturing device-dependent responses across frequencies and directions.

entry.title: A Sentinel-2 benchmark dataset for deep-learning active-fire segmentation across 25 California wildfires

author.name: Shreyan Mitra, Mohammadreza Narimani, Parastoo Farajpoor

entry.summary: The authors release an open dataset of 2,148 image-mask pairs covering 25 California wildfires between July 2020 and August 2026, built from Sentinel-2 Level-2A shortwave-infrared and near-infrared bands at 20 m sampling with a fixed rendering pipeline. Masks label background, active fire, and invalid pixels, and the release includes chip-level metadata plus an incident-disjoint partition. This matters because active-fire segmentation has lacked standardized, reproducible benchmarks for satellite-based deep learning.

entry.title: Learned Look-Ahead Splitting Rule for CART

author.name: Andrew Gao, Tianlin Liu, Ruichen Han, Lu Tian

entry.summary: Standard classification and regression trees use greedy splits maximizing immediate error reduction, which can discard splits with small short-term gains but large downstream benefit. The authors propose a look-ahead method that scores candidate splits by the error reduction after growing a conventional CART subtree beneath them, plus a smart variant that learns downstream split values from node-level features to control cost. It matters because decision trees remain foundational in tabular ML and interpretable modeling.

entry.title: Kernel-Based Metrics Learning for Uncertain Opponent Vehicle Trajectory Prediction in Autonomous Racing

author.name: Hojin Lee, Youngim Nam, Sanghun Lee, Cheolhyeon Kwon

entry.summary: The work introduces heterogeneous kernel metrics for deep kernel learning to capture the diverse and unknown driving policies of opponent vehicles in autonomous racing, and to predict their trajectories together with associated uncertainties. The kernels align similar driving policies and separate dissimilar ones in an unsupervised way from observed ego-opponent interactions, supporting safer overtaking decisions.

entry.title: ParsHate: A Benchmark Dataset for Hate and Target Detection in Persian

author.name: Zahra Bokaei, Walid Magdy, Bonnie Webber

entry.summary: ParsHate is a manually annotated dataset of 10,000 Persian tweets spanning 2013 to 2022, supporting hate detection and multi-label fine-grained target identification across seven categories. It distinguishes explicit from implicit hate, marks explicit and implicit targets, and provides span-level rationales, with sampling designed to reduce keyword-driven bias. State-of-the-art Persian hate-speech models reach only moderate performance on it, highlighting remaining difficulty.

entry.title: Multisource Remote Sensing and Geospatial Analysis of Vineyard Wildfire Impacts and Resilience: The 2019 Kincade Fire

author.name: Parastoo Farajpoor, Mahla Ardebili Pour, Mohammad Bagher Ghiasi, Mohammadreza Narimani

entry.summary: Using an open, event-anchored geospatial framework covering 4,581 vineyard fields (about 8,813 hectares) in Sonoma County, the authors analyze vineyard wildfire resilience during the 2019 Kincade Fire. Sentinel-2, OpenET, gridMET, soils, terrain, NOAA smoke polygons, an ignition-date OpenStreetMap road network, and 3D inventories are combined at native decision scales, with vineyard pixels showing notably lower descriptive burn severity. The framing is that working agricultural landscapes are managed fuel mosaics and infrastructure, not mere background to wildfire.

entry.title: AssemblyGrid v1: A Benchmark for Multi-Robot Production with Temporary Coalitions, Local Information, and Geometric Constraints

author.name: Fouad Bahrpeyma, David Heik, Dirk Reichelt

entry.summary: AssemblyGrid v1 is a reproducible benchmark for repeated multi-robot production that combines process progression, decentralized partial observations, temporary coalitions, shared resources, and workspace geometry. It is designed to stress cooperative multi-agent decision making under partial observability and resource contention. It matters as shared infrastructure for evaluating decentralized multi-robot manufacturing policies.

entry.title: XRoboToolKit-T: Teleoperation with High Stability and Precision with Tactile Sensing for Contact-rich Manipulation

author.name: Xiwen Dengxiong, Xueting Wang, Ke Jing, Rui Li, Yunbo Zhang

entry.summary: XRoboToolKit-T is a teleoperation system with a tactile-informed force-control architecture and a stabilizer haptic module that analyzes normal forces to enable stable, high-frequency tactile feedback during contact-rich manipulation. The goal is higher-quality robot data collection for contact-rich skills. It matters for improving demonstration quality in tactile-heavy manipulation.

entry.title: Motion planning in high dimensional spaces hybridizing RRT and HAR via position-direction decoupling

author.name: Frederic Cazals, Nelson Feyeux

entry.summary: The authors propose sampling-based planners that hybridize Rapidly-exploring Random Trees with Hit-and-Run random walks by decoupling the extension point from the extension direction, showing RRT and HAR as special cases of a generic biased algorithm. A sparse-move strategy that moves only a fraction of robots per step helps with cluttered, narrow-passage instances. It matters for high-dimensional motion planning with tight clearances.

entry.title: Fleet-To-Lab: A Transfer Learning Framework For Lunar Rover Slippage Estimation Via Model Fusion

author.name: Riccardo Viviano, Saki Omi, Andrej Orsula, Miguel Olivares-Mendez

entry.summary: Fleet-to-Lab addresses wheel slip estimation for lunar rovers, where terrestrial-trained models generalize poorly and real lunar data are scarce. It fuses heterogeneous expert models from previously deployed rovers into one architecture using a modest post-deployment dataset, introducing AcoMerge, a hybrid swarm-intelligence algorithm for model fusion.

entry.title: Swim-and-Breach at Palm Scale: A Rudder-Steered Two-Propeller Underwater Robot Platform with Differential-Thrust Pitch Control

author.name: Daehyun Choi, Ian Bergerson, Hengjia Zhu, Tianjun Lan, Saad Bhamla

entry.summary: This paper presents a palm-scale 65 mm, 34 g underwater robot that uses two vertically stacked propellers for propulsion and differential-thrust pitch control under a PID loop, plus a tail rudder for yaw. Flow-simulated hull design cuts drag roughly fivefold versus a cuboid, B-series propeller modeling is validated on a dynamometer, and the robot reaches 13.9 body lengths per second and 209 degrees per second while performing breach maneuvers.

entry.title: Supervising the Chain Ladder

author.name: Stephan Marais, James Grove

entry.summary: The paper reframes actuarial chain-ladder pattern selection as a supervised-learning problem, expressing practitioner judgement on pattern adjustments as explicit penalties and hyperparameters on the chain ladder's loss function. Data weights are generalized with decay and power parameters for recency and volume weighting, and smoothness enters through a reference penalty and Whittaker-Henderson smoothing, yielding a strictly convex objective minimized by a single linear system. It matters for making reserving judgement reproducible and formally specified.

entry.title: GGUF-Metadata Prediction of Single-Sequence llama.cpp Throughput Across Three Systems

author.name: Xinyu Qiu, Chuhong Xu, Bo Su, Ziyao Chen, Ruiyang Xu, Shimeng Dai

entry.summary: This paper predicts single-sequence inference throughput directly from GGUF metadata using roofline-shaped predictors with quantization-specific scale factors. Evaluated on 318 measurements from 53 host-file configurations across two Apple M4 Max systems and an RTX 5080, an active-parameter decode model substantially outperforms total-parameter baselines.

entry.title: ProtoCAM: Interpretable Few-Shot Mask-Guided Prototypical Learning for Breast Lesion Classification in Ultrasound Imaging

author.name: Ashkan Ebadi

entry.summary: ProtoCAM combines mask-guided feature encoding, prototypical metric learning, and gradient-based visual explanations into an explainable few-shot framework for breast lesion classification in ultrasound. It targets the dual problem of scarce annotated medical data and the need for interpretable predictions. The work matters for deploying trustworthy computer-aided diagnosis under low-label regimes.

entry.title: GEAR: From Dynamic Encoding to Dynamic Activation in Social Trajectory Prediction

author.name: Jiaheng Chen, Jiaxing Li, Leixia Wang, Jianan Ju, Tinghe Zhang

entry.summary: GEAR argues that dynamic social encoding in trajectory prediction does not automatically yield dynamic social activation, and that interaction context should be activated with varying strength across future horizons and scene densities. The method adjusts how encoded social context influences future trajectory generation rather than only how it is encoded.

entry.title: PU classification under Non-SCAR: clustering-assisted logistic model with oversampling enhancement

author.name: Konrad Furma\'nczyk, Kacper Paczutkowski

entry.summary: This study examines positive-unlabeled classification when the SCAR assumption (selected completely at random) is violated, using logistic-regression variants built on a clustering approach with strict and non-strict Lasso regularization. Its main contribution is integrating SMOTE to counter class imbalance, applying 2-means clustering to derive cleaning labels before training on the cleaned data. It matters for realistic PU settings where labeled positives are not a random sample.

entry.title: Big Brains and Changing Environments: Cause or Consequence?

author.name: Sian Heesom-Green, Jonathan Shock, Geoff Nitschke

entry.summary: Using neuro-evolution in an artificial seasonal foraging task, the authors compare agents evolved only in changing environments against agents first evolved in static environments and then transitioned. Larger neural networks in dynamic environments mainly arose from prior static evolution, which they argue supports a colonization account over strict Cognitive Buffer Hypothesis predictions.

entry.title: CIDERS: Cloud-Edge LLM Collaborative Learning via Accelerating Personalized Bilevel Optimization

author.name: Victor H. Chen, Hairui Yu, Stella K. Chung, Hong Yan

entry.summary: CIDERS formalizes cloud-edge LLM collaboration as a personalized bilevel optimization problem, with the upper level optimizing edge-side personalization and the lower level governing cloud-side knowledge transfer. The authors claim this is the first such formulation for balancing global consensus with local adaptation. It matters for practical deployment of LLMs across resource-constrained edge devices.

entry.title: Nationally Consistent, Locally Incomplete: A Bayesian Remote-Sensing Audit of Rooftop Photovoltaic Registries

author.name: Gabriel Kasmi, Yves-Marie Saint-Drenan, Laurent Dubus, Philippe Blanc

entry.summary: The authors introduce a Bayesian framework that converts imperfect rooftop-PV detections from remote sensing into an uncertainty-aware estimate of true installed capacity, effectively turning a noisy detector into a calibrated measurement instrument. Applied to France, it estimates about 4.03 GWp of rooftop PV below 36 kWp, matching transmission system operator connection data within a few percent nationally while revealing local registry gaps. It matters for auditing energy-transition statistics that are known to be inaccurate but previously unquantified.

entry.title: Empirical Evaluation of Open-Source Large Language Models for Retrieval-Augmented Generation in ESG Domain

author.name: Motaz Saad, Anna Borrelli, Ivan Gentile, Kianna Kazemi, Francesco Piccialli, Antonella Longo

entry.summary: The paper evaluates seven open-source models from 2B to 30B parameters on ESG key-performance-indicator extraction using 498 real-world reports from EU-listed companies and 100 persona-based synthetic question-answer pairs. The models tested include glm-4.7-flash, nemotron-3-nano, qwen3 4b instruct, gemma3 4b, gemma4 variants, and ministral-3 8b, all of which predate the coverage date and are treated here as existing systems. It provides a structured evaluation resource for a compliance-heavy domain.

category.term: Domain Applications (Time Series, Finance, ESG, Education)

entry.title: Predicting build orientation for SLM dental parts: a comparison of rotation representations and direct vector regression

author.name: Felix Schmalzel, Reimar Waitz, Moritz Kronberger, Thorsten Sch\"oler

entry.summary: This work treats the choice of build orientation for selective laser melting of dental parts, normally made manually by technicians, as supervised learning of a part up-axis from labeled production data. Using roughly 2400 patient-specific dental parts, the authors train a ResNet-50 multi-view image backbone and a PointNeXt-S point-cloud backbone on 13 up-axis representations spanning six classical SO(3) parameterizations and seven direct unit-sphere representations, evaluating geodesic angular error. It matters as a careful empirical study of rotation representation choice for a real manufacturing task.

entry.title: LayerRoute: Adaptive Layer-Skipping with LoRA-Preserved Quality for Efficient LLM Inference

author.name: Prateek Kumar Sikdar

entry.summary: LayerRoute combines per-layer hard-gated routing trained with a straight-through estimator and joint LoRA fine-tuning to skip transformer layers adaptively. On Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct it converges to the same skip pattern across ten seeds and yields verified wallclock speedups of roughly 1.02x to 1.06x.

entry.title: Interpreting hierarchical organisation of speaker embeddings

author.name: Yanze Xu, Wenwu Wang, Mark D. Plumbley

entry.summary: Speaker recognition networks learn embeddings whose internal organization remains poorly explained, and the authors frame the question explicitly through explainable AI rather than treating analysis as an engineering diagnostic. They apply single-linkage hierarchical clustering to determine whether speaker embeddings naturally form clusters with hierarchical relationships, then interpret the resulting structure. It matters modestly as a step toward interpretable representations in speech systems.

entry.title: A Conservative OCR-Enabled Workflow for R214 Sodium Screening of South African Packaged Foods

author.name: Mayimunah Nagayi, Alice Scaria Khan, Tamryn Frank, Rina Swart, Clement Nyirenda

entry.summary: This applied study presents a conservative image-based pipeline for monitoring sodium content in South African packaged foods against R214 regulatory limits. It combines region detection, OCR, product identity and sodium evidence extraction, deterministic category assignment and threshold comparison, evaluated on 442 products and nearly 4,000 package images.

entry.title: Sylvas: Synergistic Learning Value based Device Scheduling in Federated Continual Learning

author.name: Yuxuan Sun, Yuxuan Bai, Tan Chen, Sheng Zhou, Zhisheng Niu

entry.summary: Sylvas is a device-scheduling framework for federated continual learning at the wireless edge that scores each device's learning value from distributional and other perspectives before selecting which clients to train in each round. It targets non-stationary, label-scarce data streams in IoT settings like intelligent transportation and industrial monitoring. The contribution is a principled way to allocate limited communication resources to the most valuable contributors.

entry.title: Event-Native Symbolic-Temporal Spike Encoding Framework for Heterogeneous Cyber Streams

author.name: Dalton Diez, Peyton Andras, Max Shroyer, James Ghawaly Jr

entry.summary: This work proposes a spike encoding scheme for spiking neural networks that handles heterogeneous cyber telemetry, including categorical identifiers, irregular timing, and local behavioral context, which standard rate- and population-based encodings handle poorly. It aims to bring the low-power, event-driven advantages of SNNs to intrusion detection without forcing cyber data through conventional numeric-signal pipelines. The framing matters for energy-efficient security monitoring at the edge.

entry.title: Digital Persuasion: Understanding the Impact of Online Influencers on Public Opinion

author.name: Omran Berjawi, Rida Khatoun, Giuseppe Fenza

entry.summary: This work proposes a Friedkin-Johnsen-based framework to identify influential users in social networks and measure their impact on community opinion dynamics, distinguishing initial from expressed opinions. It runs opinion-manipulation experiments comparing influential versus random users and validates the framework on a tweet dataset from a U.S. presidential context.

entry.title: NepKANUN: A RAG-Based Nepali Legal Assistant

author.name: Bhabuk Thapa, Prasiddha Koirala, Ranjit Raut, Sunil Regmi, Bal Krishna Bal

entry.summary: The paper presents a retrieval-augmented generation legal assistant for Nepali legal texts, built on a fine-tuned large language model and trained on a custom dataset of high-quality question-answer pairs. It reports BERTScore F1 of 0.82 for simple, 0.77 for moderate and 0.71 for complex questions, with expert reviews supporting usability, aiming to democratize access to legal information in a low-resource setting.

entry.title: Negation Beyond the Verbal Channel: Temporal Multimodal Correlates in Dialogue

author.name: Leon Hammerla, Patrick Schrottenbacher, Alexander Mehler

entry.summary: This study asks whether contexts around spoken negation cues carry measurable multimodal behavioral information, using 27 human-human interviews in virtual reality with aligned gaze, facial, head, body, hand, and finger signals plus 964 annotated negation cues. It compares 20 time-series models on classification as a predictive probe while excluding lexical and acoustic input. The findings bear on how negation is signaled nonverbally and whether it propagates to dialogue partners.

entry.title: Towards Illusions Awareness in Cyber-Physical System's Design

author.name: Anna Di Placido (UniCA, Laboratoire I3S - COMRED, KAIROS), Nicolas Ferry (UniCA, Laboratoire I3S - COMRED, KAIROS), Julien Deantoni (UniCA, Laboratoire I3S - COMRED, KAIROS)

entry.summary: This paper reframes the reality gap in cyber-physical systems, where design-time assumptions are invalidated at runtime, as a source of reusable design knowledge rather than something to only minimize. The authors call invalidated assumptions illusions and argue for a unified methodology to structure and exploit them in CPS design models.

entry.title: Det-LIME: Detector-Aware, Multi-Instance Local Interpretable Model-Agnostic Explanations for Automated Marine Mammal Detection

author.name: Jiayi Zhou, David W. Johnston, Brinnae Bent

entry.summary: Det-LIME adapts LIME-based explanation to object detection tasks that contain multiple individuals in a scene, such as colonial or social marine mammals, instead of producing single-instance heatmaps. The authors argue that standard classifier explainability tools blur evidence across animals and yield low-resolution visuals of little biological use. The goal is to support debugging, targeted data augmentation, and better conservation data collection.

entry.title: A Spatiotemporal Extension of the Neuromorphic DBSCAN Implementation

author.name: Charles P. Rizzo, James S. Plank

entry.summary: This work extends prior neuromorphic DBSCAN implementations (flat and systolic) with spatiotemporal constructions that better exploit the timing structure of event-sensor data, plus segmented variants for resource-constrained hardware. All network constructions are released open-source. It matters for efficient on-sensor clustering in neuromorphic and event-camera pipelines.

entry.title: Waggle Dance Inspired Motion Communication for Multiple UAVs in MuJoCo

author.name: Zhang Nengbo

entry.summary: Inspired by honeybee waggle dances, this work builds a MuJoCo system in which a performer UAV broadcasts a six-bit navigation payload through four flight primitives and explicit null signals, while one to five observers extract optical-flow trajectories from their own RGB images, decode the message, and navigate only after confirming a complete frame. Reception state and execution triggers are separated per observer with shared simulation control and safety checks.

entry.title: CAD-Based Relation Learning and Geometric-Symbolic Planning for Robotic Assembly

author.name: Fabian Harlacher, Christian Friedrich

entry.summary: This hybrid assembly sequence planning framework combines learning-based relation extraction with geometric-symbolic reasoning to generate feasible robotic disassembly sequences from imperfect CAD data. A neural network predicts semantic geometric relations from point clouds, and human-in-the-loop verification corrects uncertain predictions and planning failures before relations are transformed into planning constraints.

entry.title: Homeostatic Continual Learning

author.name: Yue Jin

entry.summary: This single-author paper formulates a continual learning problem and proposes Homeostatic Continual Learning, in which an agent detects outliers in environment data when it experiences an outlier in its own output, gradually completing its model and policy across increasingly many contexts without catastrophic forgetting. The author also sketches how the method could support a world model that factorizes objects into features, abstracts them into comparable concept instances, and maps concepts to intents.

entry.title: Horizon-specific Expert Fusion for Photovoltaic Power Forecasting

author.name: Xu Yuqing, Zhou Liguo, Sun Ze, Yu Lei, Jiang Mingming

entry.summary: This study develops a hierarchical ensemble for short-term photovoltaic power forecasting that blends temporal neural models, historical analogs, state climatology and gradient-boosted trees. Horizon-specific convex weights combine predictions, with a separate calibration step correcting recent bias, evaluated on PVDAQ and GEFCom2014 solar zones.

entry.title: Through the Eyes of the Beholder: Biometric and Demographic Conditioning for Multimodal Sexism Detection

author.name: Ana-Maria Luisa Mocanu, Sebastian Mocanu, Ciprian-Octavian Truic\u{a}, Elena-Simona Apostol

entry.summary: The VANGUARD team describes a human-centered multimodal framework for the EXIST 2026 sexism-detection challenge that conditions predictions on annotator psychological and demographic traits. It fuses five modalities via cross-attention with Feature-wise Linear Modulation, using Gemma 4 for meme visual description, NLLB-200 for translation, and LoRA-adapted XLM-RoBERTa plus CLIP encoders. The novelty lies in explicitly modeling annotator subjectivity rather than treating labels as objective ground truth.

entry.title: FairLint-DL: An IDE-Native Tool for Fairness Debugging of Deep Learning Software

author.name: Archit Rathod, Saeid Tizpaz-Niari

entry.summary: FairLint-DL is a Visual Studio Code extension implementing a shift-left fairness testing approach, detecting bias directly on tabular datasets before training completes by fitting a configurable proxy neural network. It applies information-theoretic Quantitative Individual Discrimination metrics grounded in Shannon and min-entropy to measure how protected attributes causally influence predictions, using a two-phase gradient-guided search to find discriminatory regions. It matters because most fairness tools operate only after full model development.

entry.title: Fast-Convergent Meta-RL via Gradient-Clustered BS Sampling for Edge Caching

author.name: Farnaz Niknia, Ping Wang

entry.summary: The paper addresses meta-reinforcement learning for wireless edge caching, where each base station has its own request rate and content popularity but a structurally identical decision problem, making meta-training the scaling bottleneck. Uniformly sampling base stations for meta-gradient estimation yields high variance, so the authors propose gradient-clustered base-station sampling to speed convergence. It matters for deploying adaptive caching agents across large networks.

entry.title: Moral Rebel Agents: Decision-Making Under Conflicting Obligations

author.name: Hector Munoz-Avila, David W. Aha, Paola Rizzo

entry.summary: This paper formalizes moral rebellion: an autonomous agent deviating from a user-assigned task when morally justified, and lays out five architectures ranging from an amoral task-pursuing agent to several moral rebel variants. The variants include utilitarian agents that opportunistically maximize outcomes, deontic agents enforcing normative constraints, and combined utilitarian-deontic agents. It contributes a formal vocabulary for conflicts between obedience to users and emerging moral obligations.

entry.title: Authorship attribution and aesthetic evaluation of AI poetry: a case study with Haiku

author.name: Livia Oddi, Simone Scardapane, Toru Sugimoto, Donatella Genovese

entry.summary: This case study generates Japanese haiku with a heterogeneous set of open- and closed-source LLMs via few-shot prompting, then mixes them with human-written poems in a questionnaire given to Tokyo university students. It examines whether readers can distinguish AI from human authorship and how they judge aesthetic quality in this constrained form.

entry.title: Transfer Learning for Socioeconomic Estimation in Forced-Displacement Settings

author.name: Steven Ndung'u, Adel Daoud, Ismael Yacoubou Djima, Hai-Anh H. Dang, Patrick Michael Brock

entry.summary: This paper investigates whether Earth-observation and machine-learning models developed for general populations transfer to forcibly displaced populations, where survey data are periodic and conditions change rapidly between rounds. The aim is spatially granular, more frequently updated socioeconomic estimates to inform operational prioritization in conflict-affected settings. It matters for humanitarian targeting and for testing transfer-learning assumptions across distribution shifts.

entry.title: Improving Reduced-Order Rotating Detonation Engine Models with Data Assimilation and Machine Learning

author.name: Ashwin Suriyanarayanan, Romit Maulik

entry.summary: The paper applies continuous data assimilation (nudging) to synchronize a low-order one-dimensional Koch-Kutz model of a rotating detonation engine with high-fidelity temperature data, adding the prediction-observation mismatch as a relaxation term in the energy equation. Sparse observations are interpolated to supply targets at each update. It matters for propulsion modeling because it aims to give cheap reduced-order surrogates fidelity closer to DNS/LES at a fraction of the cost.

entry.title: Multimodal Cultural Heritage Architectural Style Classification for Residential Buildings in the UAE Based on CLIP Embeddings and SVM

author.name: Ahmed Ammar Kubba, Manar Abu Talib, Iman Ibrahim, Qassim Nasir

entry.summary: This paper builds a multimodal classification framework for Emirati residential architectural styles using CLIP, fusing image features with expert textual descriptions into a unified 512-dimensional embedding. It applies UMAP for visualization and K-Means for unsupervised clustering, then classifies with an SVM, partly to fill the gap in non-western region-specific heritage datasets. The contribution is largely an applied pipeline for cultural heritage analysis.

entry.title: HairCS: Reconstructing Strand-Based Hair from Hair Cards

author.name: Zixuan Lu (University of Utah), Tongtong Wang (LIGHTSPEED), Yuefan Shen (LIGHTSPEED), Zhongtian Zheng (LIGHTSPEED), Chenfanfu Jiang (UCLA), Yin Yang (University of Utah), Kui Wu (LIGHTSPEED)

entry.summary: HairCS is an automated pipeline converting hair-card models, textured triangular or quad strips, into strand-based hairstyles. The output preserves the original look while adding fine-scale geometric detail and meets production constraints: strands originate from the scalp, roots are uniformly distributed, and hair volume is plausibly filled. The resulting assets work with strand-based rendering, physics simulation, and standard grooming modifiers such as clumping, curling, and noise.

entry.title: Optimal Excitation Trajectories for System Identification of Underwater Vehicles

author.name: Fotis Panetsos, Kostas J. Kyriakopoulos

entry.summary: The paper parameterizes excitation trajectories with Bezier curves and solves an optimization problem for dynamically feasible, safety-constrained trajectories that maximize data quality for least-squares identification of underwater vehicle dynamics. Validation is performed in a laboratory water tank. It matters for reliable model-based control of underwater robots.

entry.title: From Ideas to Actions: A Public-Data Decision-Support Toolchain Across the Venture Lifecycle

author.name: Lei Qu (Shanghai Xing Yun Zhi Li AI Institute)

entry.summary: This paper presents a public-data toolchain for founder decisions, covering pre-founding idea evaluation and post-founding operating and investor-fit analysis using auditable investor-company event chains. The frozen pipeline reports F0.5 of 0.5357 on a validation sample and 0.6301 versus 0.2734 for a raw LLM baseline on combined data. It is a niche applied system focused on reproducible scoring rather than new modeling.

category.term: Domain Applications (Time Series, Finance, ESG, Education)

entry.title: New Conditions for Philosophers to Catch the Wave of Citizen Deliberation in the Age of Artificial Intelligence in advance

author.name: Bernard Reber (CEVIPOF)

entry.summary: The paper argues that large language models could support citizen deliberation and citizens assemblies through moderation, translation, facilitation, summarization, and writing assistance, but that this potential remains largely unrealized. It describes the Democratic Commons project, an interdisciplinary effort from philosophy to computer science that evaluates LLMs against five proposed democratic principles. The contribution is conceptual and normative rather than technical.

entry.title: Design of a Deep Learning Credit Risk Early Warning System Integrating Multi-source Heterogeneous Data

author.name: LiYang Wang (Washington University in St. Louis), Zhen Zhong (Georgetown University), Zhen Tian (University of Glasgow), Keyu Chen (Wuyi University), Keyu Chen (Wuyi University)

entry.summary: The paper proposes a credit risk early warning system that fuses heterogeneous information sources such as transaction behavior and social network data using a deep neural network with attention mechanisms. The aim is to overcome information silos and monitoring delays in traditional financial risk systems by extracting multidimensional features and enabling earlier identification of corporate and individual credit risk. System testing reportedly shows improved accuracy and timeliness.

entry.title: The Agentic Company OS: Substrate Inversion for Sustained Enterprise Agent Deployment

author.name: Oliver Aleksander Larsen, Mahyar T. Moghaddam

entry.summary: This position paper argues that enterprise AI agents fail in sustained production because they reason over data structures designed for human operators and traditional applications rather than for language models. The authors propose a substrate inversion: rebuilding the shared cognitive environment around model-native representations so agents can retain feedback and improve over repeated runs. It frames a widely observed pilot-to-production gap in architectural terms.

entry.title: Investigating the Impacts of Generative AI on Information Seeking

author.name: Alexi Orchard, Shannon Lodoen

entry.summary: This is an encore submission of a 2026 journal article on expertise and information seeking in the age of generative AI, extended for a CSCW 2026 workshop on broader impacts of GenAI in communication. It uses procedural rhetoric to analyze how chatbot language signals expertise and intelligence, shaping users' trust judgments, and aims to build cross-disciplinary vocabulary for describing and mitigating these risks. It matters for understanding how conversational interfaces can subtly influence epistemic trust.

entry.title: Ensemble Complexity in Photovoltaic Forecasting

author.name: Sun Ze, Zhou Liguo, Xu Yuqing, Yu Lei, Jiang Mingming

entry.summary: This paper asks whether adding ensemble components to photovoltaic forecasting actually helps, using matched comparisons and ablations of a fixed heterogeneous predictor bank across GEFCom2014 and three other public datasets with chronological splits and multiple seeds. Static fusion reduced scaled mean absolute error versus matched boosting on several datasets, but only one improvement survived multiple-comparison correction, and weather gating gave no consistent benefit. Member-removal probes reveal group-level dependence alongside individual redundancy, suggesting many ensemble members add computation without reliable gains.

entry.title: Cross-Domain Inference for Human Localization: Applying Wi-Fi RSSI Data to CSI-Trained Models

author.name: Ariel Duschanek-Myers, Thomas Welsh, Helmut Neukirchen

entry.summary: This paper investigates whether cheap Received Signal Strength Indicator data, usable even on IoT devices with restricted permissions, can substitute for Channel State Information in models that predict human locations. It repurposes an existing Wi-Fi pose prediction project trained on CSI to build an RSSI-based model and discusses the privacy risks of such localization.

entry.title: Comment on arXiv:2607.01233: Survivorship Bias in Published-Paper Baselines for Research-Idea Distributions

author.name: Fredrik A. Dahl

entry.summary: This short comment raises an identification concern about a distributional evaluation of LLM-generated research ideas: the human baseline consists of published papers while the LLM baseline consists of one-shot proposals. Because easy-to-generate, bridge-like or synthesis-like ideas are less likely to survive publication, the published human baseline may understate their prevalence, so the reported human-LLM gap could be partly or largely survivorship bias.

category.term: Trustworthy ML: Explainability, Bias and Validation

entry.title: Nepali Legal Expertise through Generative and Extractive Pre-trained Transformers (NepLEGiT)

author.name: Ranjit Raut, Tishya Dhakal, Aaryan Shakya, Bhabuk Thapa, Prasiddha Koirala, Bal Krishna Bal

entry.summary: This paper introduces NepLEGiT, a small decoder-only language model (GPT-2 architecture) pretrained from scratch on roughly 4 million tokens of Nepali legal text covering constitutional, civil, criminal, and administrative material. It also builds extractive components to support legal question answering and information access for citizens who lack legal expertise. The work matters as a case study in democratizing legal knowledge in a low-resource language where commercial legal services are scarce.

entry.title: Quantifying Organizational Environmental Action from Web Data and Large Language Models

author.name: Quinn Reynolds, Daniel Shore, Vianey Leos Barajas, Tanhum Yoreh, Meredith Franklin

entry.summary: This paper presents a scalable computational framework that converts organizational web content into structured measures of environmental action, demonstrated on US Jewish congregations. The authors build a national database of 4,964 congregations, crawl 2,657 active websites into 154,454 webpages, and use LLMs to extract structured indicators from unstructured text. It matters as an example of LLM-assisted environmental data science at scale.

entry.title: Joint UAV Activation and Placement for Post-Disaster Wireless Restoration via a Hybrid Quantum-Inspired Evolutionary Framework

author.name: Fatima Azzahraa Amarcha, Lahcen Hassine, Rachid Saadane, Mohamed Rahouti, Rachid Ahl Laamara, Abdallah Slaoui, Hany S. khalifa

entry.summary: The paper formulates the joint UAV activation-and-placement problem in continuous space for restoring wireless coverage after terrestrial infrastructure failure, minimizing the number of deployed UAVs subject to coverage and minimum-separation constraints. It proposes HKQEA, a hybrid K-means quantum-inspired evolutionary algorithm that combines K-means-guided initialization, a calibrated penalty objective, non-elitist search, and a quantum-inspired learning update. Experiments over 50 independent runs compare it against alternatives.

entry.title: Learning to Optimize UAV Path Planning for Data Sensing in Wireless Sensor Networks

author.name: Sijie Ma, Zeyuan Ma, Weijia Cao, Yue-Jiao Gong, Lingling Ma, Zhiyang Huang, Jun Zhang

entry.summary: The paper proposes Landscape-Aware Meta Differential Evolution (LAMDE), a learning-assisted planning framework for UAV data-sensing paths in wireless sensor networks that aims to overcome hand-crafted design bias and idealized simulation assumptions. It targets better generalization to unseen tasks and more realistic spatial complexity. It matters for practical UAV deployment in sensing applications.

entry.title: Overcoming technical adoption barriers for mobile service robots in rehabilitation

author.name: Christian Sternitzke, Sebastian Blumenthal, Lukas Kleedoerfer, Verena Deserno, Anke Mayfarth

entry.summary: This paper describes how a mobile service robot already approved as a medical device advances to higher technology readiness levels through peripheral functions and incremental improvements that matter for clinical user acceptance. The authors argue that many of these downstream requirements only surface through testing in clinical and operational environments, so healthcare service robot developers should budget for such development time.

entry.title: LOTUSim-Energy: A Maritime Simulator for Human-Drone Interaction in Autonomous Offshore Operation \& Maintenance

author.name: Juliette Grosset (CROSSING), Marie Dubromel (CROSSING), H\'el\`ene Lech\^ene (CROSSING), Quentin Arzel (CROSSING), C\'edric Buche (CROSSING, IMT Atlantique)

entry.summary: LOTUSim-Energy is a real-time maritime simulator for multi-domain human-drone interaction in offshore operation and maintenance. It unifies UAVs, USVs, AUVs, and ROVs in a distributed architecture that couples environmental forcing such as wind, waves, and currents, with desktop and virtual reality supervision interfaces and a structured offshore task library for repeatable evaluation of autonomy stacks.

entry.title: Proving olympiad geometry theorems on a superconducting quantum processor

author.name: Ning Wang, Zheng-Zhi Sun, Zhengyi Cui, Yiren Zou, Aosai Zhang, Fanhao Shen, Jiarun Zhong, Zehang Bao, Zitian Zhu, Han Wang, Jia-Nan Yang, Jiayuan Shen, Gongyu Liu, Yanzhe Wang, Yihang Han, Yiyang He, Jiahua Huang, Sailang Zhou, Xinrong Zhang, Yaozu Wu, Zixuan Song, Jinfeng Deng, Hang Dong, Qi Ye, Weikang Li, Si Jiang, Yixuan Ma, Shuangyue Geng, Zhide Lu, Chao Song, Hekang Li, Pengfei Zhang, Qiujiang Guo, H. Wang, Dong-Ling Deng

entry.summary: Duplicate of yesterday's Research item, This work reports the experimental realization of automated geometry theorem proving on a fully programmable superconducting quantum processor, arguing that quantum encoding and coherent parallelism could accelerate structured symbolic deduction beyond classical neuro-symbolic system limits. It positions the result as a first-of-its-kind bridge between quantum computing and automated theorem proving.

entry.title: Feasibility and Memory Mechanisms of Chern-Simons Context Reservoir Computation

author.name: Jyotiranjan Beuria, Venkatesh H. Chembrolu

entry.summary: This paper asks whether a reservoir computer built on a Chern-Simons (CS) gauge field can serve as a viable computational substrate, and whether evolving the gauge connection actually helps beyond simpler mechanisms. The authors compare four matched reservoir models across ten seeds, showing that fully coupled conserved-current CS dynamics propagates Gauss law to numerical precision and stays stable under refinement. It matters as an unusual physics-inspired test of whether gauge structure buys real computational benefit or just adds complexity.

entry.title: Leakage-Safe and Scheduler-Aware Machine Learning for Grid Job Runtime Prediction

author.name: Ashfaq Ali Shafin, Khandaker Mamun Ahmed

entry.summary: This paper reframes CPU burst time prediction on the AuverGrid workload trace as leakage-safe pre-execution job runtime prediction, restricting features to submission-time attributes and excluding post-execution variables. It evaluates standard regressors and CatBoost under temporal and cold-start settings rather than random cross-validation.

entry.title: LM-PCVMNet: Pediatric Cervical Vertebral Maturation Analysis with Deep Fusion of Landmarks and Metadata

author.name: Peng Wang, Wanzhen Song, Anli Wang, Xueshuo Xie, Xiaohang Guan, Tao Li

entry.summary: LM-PCVMNet is a deep framework for automatic pediatric cervical vertebral maturation staging used in orthodontic treatment timing. It integrates vertebral landmark information, heatmap-guided feature modulation that highlights morphologically relevant regions, and metadata-informed similarity modeling within one learning framework. The contribution is a domain-specific fusion of anatomical priors with deep features.

entry.title: MR-GLi: Mixed Reality-Based Gripper-Linked Overlays for Underwater Robot Arm Teleoperation via Bilateral Control

author.name: Masashi Sasago, Masato Kobayashi, Yuki Uranishi

entry.summary: MR-GLi is a mixed-reality interface that spatially registers a reaction-torque indicator and wrist-camera feed to an underwater robot gripper, compared against a 2D monitor in a within-subject study with twenty participants. Torque-regulation performance was similar, but subjective burden was reduced. It matters for interface design in underwater bilateral teleoperation.

entry.title: Study 3: Steering welfare-relevant directions moved the representation, but not [detectably] the behavior

author.name: ashesfall

entry.summary: A calibration report for an AI welfare research program: steering known welfare-relevant directions moved their projections linearly, but no direction produced a behavioral effect distinguishable from zero or from a same-norm random direction. The planned preregistered study was suspended, and the program shifts to Qwen3.6-27B where an initial probe found a direction-specific signal.

entry.title: Divide, Consult, Conquer: Capability Laundering Through Aligned LLMs

author.name: Mark Russinovich, Blake Bullwinkel, Giorgio Severi, Cristian Ovadiuc, Ahmed Salem

entry.summary: Duplicate of yesterday's Research item, The paper demonstrates capability laundering: a weaker unaligned orchestrator splits a harmful task into benign-looking subproblems, queries a stronger aligned model on each independently, and reassembles the answers. Evaluating GPT-5.5, Claude Opus 4.8, and Grok-4.3 as consultants on CyBench, BountyBench, and harmful CBRN requests, the authors show substantial uplift that per-interaction safety evaluation misses.

entry.title: Corrupt Plans, Clean Traces: Evading Chain-of-Thought Monitoring with Plan Injection

author.name: Keertana Chidambaram, Andrew Ilyas, Vasilis Syrgkanis

entry.summary: Duplicate of yesterday's Research item, This paper identifies plan injection, an attack in which harmful but benign-sounding reasoning planted in an actor model's context steers it toward adversarial actions while evading a chain-of-thought monitor that inspects its reasoning. The attack was first found in the multiple-choice monitorability setting of Lanham et al. and then generalized, achieving monitor evasion rates of 25 to 33 percent across harder tasks. It directly undermines the assumption that visible reasoning traces provide a reliable safety signal.

entry.title: Diffusion-Based Generation of Gait Trajectories

author.name: Damian Benasco, Juan Carballeira-Lopez, Jaime Ramos-Rojas, Julio S. Lora-Millan, Antonio J. Del-Ama, David Rodriguez-Cianca, Pablo Lanillos

entry.summary: This work explores conditional diffusion models for generating lower-limb joint-angle trajectories conditioned on patient-specific gait parameters such as step length, aiming to replace hand-crafted templates and poorly scaling optimization for exoskeleton and rehabilitation reference trajectories. It compares a baseline transformer diffusion model against a controllable diffusion transformer variant. The goal is biomechanically realistic, subject-adaptive gait references for assistive robotics.

entry.title: Single Document Extractive Summarization using Domination in Hypergraph

author.name: Aamir Miyajiwala, Aabha Pingle, Sheetal Sonawane, Surajit Kr. Nath

entry.summary: This work proposes extractive single-document summarization using the domination property in hypergraphs, where sentences are nodes and keywords or named entities form hyperedges containing the sentences in which they occur. The method selects a dominating sentence set as the summary and compares against state-of-the-art graph-based summarizers.

entry.title: Copula Adapted Directed Acyclic Graph for Cluster Representation of Biomedical Data

author.name: Heranga K. Rathnasekara, Norou Diawara, Manar D. Samad

entry.summary: This work proposes a cluster-friendly data representation that combines copula models capturing non-Gaussian, non-linear feature dependence with an ensemble of directed acyclic graph based causal structure discovery methods. The goal is to stratify unlabeled biomedical data without relying on labels or restrictive distributional assumptions common in standard clustering. It matters for biomedical analytics where mislabeling and diagnostic error make unsupervised structure discovery attractive.

entry.title: EBL: Efficient Broad Learning for Distributed Adaptive Harmonic Analysis

author.name: Changhong Li, Georgios Floros, Biswajit Basu, Shreejith Shanker

entry.summary: The paper proposes an Efficient Broad Learning framework for distributed adaptive harmonic estimation in power grids stressed by non-linear loads such as EV charging, using half-cycle inputs for fast high-accuracy estimation. It is implemented as a quantized FPGA acceleration framework for broad-learning-system style estimators. It matters for grid operators needing rapid harmonic control at the injection source.

entry.title: ReMova: Fine-tuning LLMs for English to Belarusian translation

author.name: Mikita Pilinka, Aliaksandr Kliuje\u{u}, David Samuel, Yves Scherrer

entry.summary: The paper presents a Belarusian-specific data-cleaning pipeline and fine-tuning recipe for English-Belarusian machine translation, including a correction tool that handles the language's two orthographies, noise, cross-language interference, and common misspellings. A matched ablation on unfiltered data shows filtering substantially benefits all fine-tuned models, with LLM-based models gaining roughly twice as much as a dedicated encoder-decoder MT system. It argues that data quality, not model capacity, is a primary bottleneck for Belarusian MT.

entry.title: Tracking the Unseen: An Occlusion-Robust Framework for Target Tracking Under Full and Long-Term Occlusion

author.name: Mais Mohammed, Sharifa Mohammed, Hanan Awadh, Haneen Bamaas, Raghad Bawazeer, Elham Alghamdi

entry.summary: This work proposes a three-stage multi-object tracking pipeline combining YOLOv11n detection, Kalman filter motion prediction, and occlusion-aware appearance re-identification to survive full and long-term occlusion. The goal is to prevent premature trajectory termination and identity loss in surveillance and defense settings. It is an engineering integration of off-the-shelf components rather than a new tracking paradigm.

entry.title: Beyond Scene Description: Multi-Agent Orchestration for Non-visual Access to Virtual Worlds

author.name: Toqeer Ali Syed, Ali Akarma, Adeel Ahmad, Danial Hameed

entry.summary: MetaBlind is an architecture that distributes non-visual access to live virtual rooms across eight specialized agents spanning perception, navigation, and other subtasks, rather than relying on single-task assistive tools. The authors argue that narrating every simultaneous element of a live room simply trades a visual barrier for an auditory one, motivating coordinated agent orchestration. It is an accessibility-focused systems design for blind and visually impaired users.

entry.title: Scalability and Performance Evaluation of Federated Learning Frameworks: A Comparative Analysis

author.name: Bassel Soudan, Sohail Abbas, Ahmed Kubba, Manar Wasif Abu Talib, Qassim Nasir

entry.summary: This study experimentally compares FedML, Flower, Substra, and OpenFL across varying client counts, tracking training time, loss, accuracy, and CPU/RAM usage. Results show distinct profiles, including high loss for Flower, low accuracy of 66-79 percent for FedML, and good resource efficiency but exponential growth for Substra. It offers practical guidance for practitioners choosing an FL framework.

entry.title: Mini-batch Sampling Strategies for Long-Tailed Image Classification: An Empirical Study on CIFAR-100-LT

author.name: Siyu Yuan

entry.summary: The study systematically compares four mini-batch sampling strategies for long-tailed image classification, uniform instance sampling, class-balanced sampling, square-root sampling, and progressively balanced sampling, on CIFAR-100-LT. It places all four in a unified bias-variance framework describing how each governs which classes contribute to the stochastic gradient estimate and thus convergence and generalization. It matters as a clarifying reference for a widely used but often ad hoc training choice.

entry.title: You Don’t Have to Trust the AI Labs (in order to take their call for regulation seriously)

author.name: ixotope

entry.summary: This linkpost discusses an essay by Anthropic's CEO proposing a coordinated slowdown of frontier capabilities through embedded independent evaluators, coordination among democratic countries, and eventual global standards. The author argues that the proposal can be taken seriously on its merits without trusting the labs' motives, while inviting critique of their own reasoning. It matters for how the AI safety community evaluates industry-originated regulatory proposals.
