author.name: Honglin Guo, Tao Gui, Yicheng Chen, Guanting Dong, Qiming Ge, Yuyang Hu, Zixian Huang, Jiajie Jin, Alexander Lam, Yining Li, Jiahang Lin, Yanjiang Liu, Xinyu Lu, Haijun Lv, Junlin Shang, Qisheng Su, Guoqiang Wang, Rui Wang, Zhecan Wang, Hao Xiang, Xinchen Xie, Shuhao Xing, Xiaoyu Xing, Wanghan Xu, Xinyu Yang, Yajie Yang, Chengfeng Zhao, Haoran Zhao, Ruojun Zhou, Yunhua Zhou, Yicheng Zou, Kun Cai, Qiye Cai, Xinmeng Che, Haodong Chen, Jiabei Chen, Jiahao Chen, Jiayi Chen, Yujia Chen, Lizhi Cui, Youheng Dai, Xin Deng, Yi Dong, Shihan Dou, Chenya Gu, Xu Guo, Ding Han, Feiyang Hao, Haotan He, Jie Hou, Binze Hu, Zijian Hu, Junhao Huang, Huicheng Jiang, Jiazhen Jiang, Shufan Jiang, Jiahao Kuang, Bowen Lai, Bo Li, Jiaqiang Li, Peng Li, Qilong Li, Zhuoqun Li, Jiaxiang Liu, Shuainan Liu, Tong Liu, Yi Liu, Zhonghang Lu, Jianwen Luo, Yanyi Luo, Huijie Lv, Ningsheng Ma, Zerun Ma, Houcheng Min, Chengjun Pan, Qiyuan Peng, Xiaoxuan Peng, Jianmin Qian, Jiantao Qiu, Wanying Ren, Huayu Sha, Jifei Shan, Zixin Shang, Bing Shao, Zhuohui Sheng, Jiayang Shi, Yang Shu, Aierpanjiang Simayi, Sirui Song, Yuxiao Song, Zhe Sun, Zhichao Sun, Wenzhe Tan, Wenhui Tian, Zhongbo Tian, Hanchen Wang, Pengbo Wang, Rui Wang, Yiding Wang, Yuhui Wang, Zhiheng Xi, Caijun Xu, Chao Xu, Yongfeng Xu, Xiaolei Yang, Zhixiong Yang, Qian Yao, Shihong Yi, Yuankai Ying, Jia Yu, Dingbo Yuan, Hao Yuan, Junjie Yuan, Bo Zhang, Caixian Zhang, Qiuyinzhe Zhang, Jiyuan Zhao, Penghao Zhao, Ying Zhao, Pujun Zheng, Xiaoxue Zhong, Xiaohao Zhou, Xinyu Zhou, Dongsheng Zhu, Guanru Zhu, Yulun Zhu, Yaojie Lu, Tao Ji, Hongyu Lin, Yutao Zhu, Pengfei Cao, Guoxiu He, Xianpei Han, Ben He, Zhicheng Dou, Kang Liu, Qi Zhang, Le Sun, Jun Zhao, Ji-Rong Wen, Xuanjing Huang, Yu-Gang Jiang, Bowen Zhou

entry.summary: Atria Dawn Preview is a foundation agentic language model for scientific research and engineering workflows, trained via a Verifiable Experience Pipeline linking tool-mediated interactions to executable environments with externally verified outcomes. The authors report competitiveness with frontier agents across 16 benchmarks and top scores on five, plus ambitions for agents participating in the development of their successors.

entry.title: Stellar Colosseum: A Many-Agent Harness for Long-Horizon Research in Mathematics and Theoretical Computer Science

author.name: Honghao Lin, David P. Woodruff, Yuan Deng, Jieming Mao, Song Zuo, Vahab Mirrokni

entry.summary: Stellar Colosseum is a model-agnostic harness for allocating inference across long-horizon mathematics and TCS research problems, using strategy exploration, a readiness gate for decomposition, section-level interdependent proof plans, and verifier feedback routing with parallel candidate generation and targeted falsification. It addresses the gap between plausible short proofs and reliable progress on interdependent research-scale problems.

entry.title: From Process Loss to Assembly Bonus: Human-Grounded Diagnosis of Multi-Agent LLM Collaboration

author.name: Ala N. Tak, Teruhisa Misu, Kumar Akash, Zhaobo K. Zheng, Kevin H. Joo, Jonathan Gratch

entry.summary: This study compares human group chats with matched LLM deliberation traces on Wason-style reasoning and other task types, finding that humans and LLMs show the same assembly bonus asymmetry: discussion improves the average member more often than the best initial member, with initial-answer diversity explaining the effect of model heterogeneity. The work validates LLM groups as models of human group processes at the mechanism level. It matters for both multi-agent design and human-group simulation.

entry.title: AGENTQ: Quantization-Conditioned Backdoor Attacks on LLM Agents

author.name: Xiaoqun Liu, Qiben Yan

entry.summary: Presents the first study of quantization-conditioned backdoor attacks against LLM agents, where a released full-precision checkpoint passes audits but executes malicious structured payloads once quantized for deployment. The paper shows naive adaptation of prior backdoor methods degrades benign utility badly, and develops attacks that survive quantization in the agentic setting where harm requires no human mediation.

entry.title: PIDS-Bench: Evaluating Prompt-Injection Detectors Under Over-Defense, Obfuscation, and Distribution Shift

author.name: Yusuf Khalid Shire, Sang-Chul Kim

entry.summary: PIDS-Bench is a frozen multi-axis benchmark evaluating prompt-injection detectors on both attack detection and benign false positives at fixed thresholds, spanning hard-benign prompts, obfuscated attacks, and domain and structural distribution shifts. Evaluating seven detectors, it exposes weaknesses hidden by aggregate in-distribution F1, particularly over-defense costs on the benign side. This fills a real gap in how prompt-injection defenses are assessed.

entry.title: Look Before You Leap: Factual Decoding with Internal Attribution Signals

author.name: Hayeong Ryu, JungMin Yun, Byeonggeuk Lim, Sunhee Jo, YoungBin Kim

entry.summary: DescaPE is a decoding framework that uses internal model signals to suppress hallucination-prone trajectories at inference time. Via sliding-window MLP ablation it identifies a factual-salient layer span whose derived signal spikes at hallucination-prone steps, then trains a lightweight probe to approximate this signal from a single forward pass and steer decoding.

entry.title: Retrieval-Guided Fine-Tuning as Noisy Estimation: Risk bounds and Architectural Analysis

author.name: Bhargav Lad, Yifan Hao

entry.summary: Models retrieval-guided fine-tuning (RAG-FT) as multi-task linear regression through a single-layer linear self-attention OLS proxy, deriving finite-sample risk bounds under retrieval noise. It shows retrieval failure decays exponentially with task separation relative to noise, gives conditions where RAG-FT beats target-only and full-corpus training, and introduces a Distance-Proportional Noise model.

entry.title: Ensemble-Conditioned Molecular Design

author.name: Ross Irwin, Alessandro Tibo, Jon Paul Janet, Simon Olsson

entry.summary: The paper reframes molecular design from optimizing a single bioactive conformation to optimizing properties of full conformational ensembles, introducing ensemble-conditioned guidance that conditions 3D molecular generative models on both ensemble modes (shapes, pharmacophore profiles, protein pockets) and aggregate properties. It matters because candidate drug viability often depends on conformational distributions rather than any single structure, so this better reflects physical reality in generative drug design.

entry.title: The Token Before the Value Is the Key: How Hybrid Architectures Organize Induction Circuits

author.name: Ke Cheng, Xin Xu, Yixiao Chen, Lei Xin, Jianbo Zhao, Fanhu Zeng, Yue Liu, Jun Zhang, Jie Jiang

entry.summary: The paper uses layer-type-agnostic paired probes to study how induction-head roles (carrying, matching, copying) are allocated across heterogeneous layers in hybrid recurrent-global and local-global language models. It finds carrying concentrates in efficient layers and matching in global receivers, with local contributions concentrated on the immediately preceding token.

entry.title: When Can You Trust Your Synthetic Users? Diagnostics and Corrections for LLM Consumer Panels

author.name: Robson Tigre, Hugo Gobato Souto

entry.summary: The paper provides a formal framework for deciding when to trust, correct, or abandon LLM-generated synthetic consumer survey data, decomposing synthetic-panel bias into covariate and concept shift and providing testable diagnostics with interpretable thresholds. It supplies a doubly robust AIPW estimator needing only a small calibration sample (n=50-300), validated on three testbeds. Given growing industry use of synthetic respondents promising 97% cost reductions, this addresses a timely reliability gap.

entry.title: CyclOT: Learning Quadratic Optimal Transport Maps via Synchronized Forward-Backward Interpolants

author.name: Shizhou Xu, Jiachen Liu, Shih-Hsin Wang, Stefan Broecker, Yuhao Huang, Bao Wang, Thomas Strohmer

entry.summary: CyclOT is a bidirectional neural framework for recovering forward and reverse quadratic optimal transport maps from unpaired high-dimensional samples. Training combines bidirectional quadratic action, discriminator-restricted Jensen-Shannon endpoint objectives, and two-sided cycle consistency, with a proven population recovery theorem under stated conditions. It avoids precomputed pairings and explicit convex-potential parameterization.

entry.title: MTAC-IFBench: Benchmarking Instruction-Following in Multi-Turn Agentic Coding

author.name: Bosi Wen, Cunxiang Wang, Jiayi Gui, Haoke Zhang, Yilin Niu, Pei Ke, Dayong Yang, Hongning Wang, Minlie Huang

entry.summary: MTAC-IFBench is a benchmark for instruction-following in multi-turn agentic coding, targeting faithful adherence to process instructions and constraints throughout the development lifecycle rather than just final functional correctness. It addresses the gap left by benchmarks confined to single-turn chat or simple code generation. The work comes from a credible team including Minlie Huang's group.

entry.title: Discovery Foundation Models: Toward Open-Ended Discovery Intelligence

author.name: Ling Yang, Zhenfei Yin, Yingcheng Wu

entry.summary: This position paper proposes Discovery Foundation Models (DFMs), general-purpose model systems for open-ended discovery that operate over a revisable research state and support seven coupled capabilities spanning problem discovery, formulation, representation construction, hypothesis formation, intervention, and evidence evaluation. It argues the next frontier beyond reasoning and tool use is participating in the creation of new knowledge itself. The paper sets an agenda rather than presenting a system.

entry.title: SignMimic: Robust High-Quality Sign Language Motion Generation via Human-Shape-Oblivious Pose Transfer Guidance

author.name: Zhewen He (New York University Abu Dhabi), Junyi Yu (New York University Abu Dhabi), Haomian Huang (New York University Abu Dhabi), Zhenhua Li (ChatSign Technology), Yi Fang (New York University Abu Dhabi, ChatSign Technology)

entry.summary: SignMimic synthesizes sign language video mimicking a driving video from a single reference frame, decomposing the problem into SE(3) rigid canonicalization, non-rigid adaptation preserving hands and face via NIF2D, and Pose-MAE-style completion before conditional video diffusion. This separation prevents handshape drift and spatio-temporal instability that plague monolithic generators.

entry.title: SAM3D-Part: Interactive Part Selection and Generation from 3D Objects

author.name: Jiahao Chang, Dong Du, Wanhu Sun, Yujian Zheng, Chuanyu Pan, Bowen Zhao, Chongjie Ye, Yuanming Hu, Xiaoguang Han

entry.summary: SAM3D-Part is a prompt-driven framework for selectively generating complete, reusable parts of 3D objects, addressing limitations of existing generators that produce all parts regardless of intent and promptable segmentation methods that yield only partial surfaces. It conditions on the source mesh to preserve hidden geometry and accurate part placement.

entry.title: Exact Feasibility Certification and Optimal Responsibility Allocation for Multi-Robot CBF Safety Filters

author.name: Chandan Kumar Sah, Jishnu Keshavan

entry.summary: The paper develops an exact feasibility certificate for multi-robot Control Barrier Function safety filters with heterogeneous control-affine dynamics and convex input sets, decomposing safety demand from actuator supply to diagnose QP infeasibility. It identifies which agents and interactions cause conflicts and proposes an algorithm to optimally allocate shared safety constraints. This provides principled diagnosis and resolution for a known failure mode of CBF filters.

entry.title: UniCAR-RL: Seeing Better before Thinking Deeper in Visual Mathematics

author.name: Yuzhe Li, Hao Yan, Hao Wang, Xingchen Liu, Ya-Qi Yu, Jihao Wu, Minghui Liao, Wei Chen, Yuliang Liu

entry.summary: Proposes UniCAR-RL, an annotation-free RL framework for multimodal LLMs that explicitly decouples perception from reasoning during training, so initial visual hallucinations no longer trigger cascading reasoning failures in complex mathematical visual reasoning. It avoids the costs and hallucinations of perception-enhanced CoT fine-tuning data while enabling targeted perception optimization that sparse end-to-end RL rewards cannot achieve. Addresses a well-documented MLLM failure mode.

entry.title: Bayesian Intelligence from the Outside

author.name: Alex Smolin, Bryan Wilder

entry.summary: The paper develops a theory of when an agent's observable behavior is consistent with Bayesian updating: any non-fully-contradictory pattern of reports across prompts admits an explanation as Bayesian inference with fresh independent draws at a fixed state. Strikingly, report frequencies and probability sizes impose no further constraints. This is a sharp negative-style result with implications for interpreting LLM behavior as evidence of rational belief formation.

entry.title: Semantic-TVM: Structure-Preserving Trustworthy Virtual Memory for Memory-Augmented and Tool-Using Agents

author.name: Yu Li, Qikun Cai, Tao Huang, Chen Hou

entry.summary: Trustworthy Virtual Memory (TVM) is a closed-loop runtime that keeps exact private values local while giving remote LLMs a protected view, replacing protected fields with recoverable handles (Rule-TVM) or masking only sensitive spans predicted by a trusted local model (Semantic-TVM). Experiments on Memory-EHR and Memory-RAP across two providers show span-level masking preserves utility better than whole-field masking.

entry.title: Evaluation Metrics for Safe Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Lindsay Spoor, Aske Plaat, Thomas Moerland

entry.summary: This paper argues that expectation-based safety reporting in constrained MDPs is insufficient to characterize true algorithmic safety, since it misses violation frequency and severity, consistency across tasks and bounds, and divergence between training-time and converged-policy behavior. The authors introduce new evaluation metrics for safe RL along these dimensions. This is a methodological critique with practical implications for how safe RL benchmarks are interpreted.

entry.title: Who Teaches Which Token? Verifier-Gated Multi-Expert On-Policy Distillation for Scientific Reasoning

author.name: Xun Xu, Zaixi Zhang

entry.summary: VG-OPD refines multi-teacher on-policy distillation by assigning supervision at token granularity: a teacher expert's counterfactual gain on a specific answer criterion gates which tokens it teaches, rather than assigning each prompt wholly to one teacher. This reflects the finding that useful teacher signal is sparse and heterogeneous along a reasoning trajectory. The method targets integrating specialist capabilities into a single student model.

entry.title: Beyond Accuracy: Robustness, Cost, and Governance Trade-offs for Vision-Language Models in Templated Document Extraction

author.name: Kushal Patel, Pushkal Shrivastava, Mackenzie Lees, Qirui Lu, Bhargobjyoti Saikia, Liying Li, Junlin Jiang

entry.summary: This measurement-grounded study evaluates eleven systems, including commercial, reasoning, open-source, and fine-tuned VLMs plus an OCR-regex baseline, on a 750-document templated document extraction pool, reporting accuracy, robustness, cost, and governance trade-offs. Fine-tuning 3K samples lifts the best open-source VLMs above F1 0.98, beating every zero-shot commercial system, while GPT-5, an established commercial model released in 2025, leads the commercial pool and Claude Sonnet 4.5 collapses on date fields.

entry.title: Diagnosing Faults in Reinforcement Learning Simulators and World Models with Canonical Polynomial Invariants

author.name: Tesfay Zemuy Gebrekidan, Hadush Hailu Gebrerufael

entry.summary: The authors test the premise that embedding exact physics into learned dynamics improves prediction, using canonical polynomial invariants as reduced Groebner bases recovered from trajectories. Surprisingly, on Acrobot, exactness provides little prediction benefit (a 100% mass error in a recovered potential still accelerates learning), but the invariants excel as diagnostic tools for detecting simulator and world model faults. This reframes physics-informed invariants from a training aid to a verification instrument.

entry.title: Canaries in the Bank: Auditing User-Level Privacy in Private Evolution

author.name: Sai Aparna Aketi, Enayat Ullah, Shripad Gade

entry.summary: The paper introduces a protocol-aware empirical audit of Private Evolution in federated settings, where a server commits to a shared candidate bank and replaces about 1% of entries with probes derived from a known non-private canary. Evaluating eight attack types, it investigates whether adversaries can realize worst-case privacy loss while following the PE protocol.

entry.title: The Attribution-Compression Frontier in Retrieval-Augmented Generation

author.name: Deepanshu Mody

entry.summary: This paper measures how different RAG context-compression methods (reranking, extractive selection, abstractive summarization, token pruning) affect citation attribution quality across compression budgets, revealing that citations can look precise against compressed summaries yet poorly traceable to original sources. It introduces a re-attributability protocol showing a RECOMP-style compressor scoring 0.86 precision against summaries but only 0.12 against source spans.

entry.title: Compositional SVG Generation via VLM-Driven Hierarchical Semantic Parsing

author.name: Sehwan Park, Taehoon Kim, Geonhee Han, Dohyun Kim, Seung Wook Kim, Paul Hongsuck Seo

entry.summary: The authors propose a VLM-driven agentic pipeline that recursively parses visual scenes into semantic and geometric hierarchies using top-down decomposition, visual grounding, and amodal occlusion recovery, producing editable, semantically grouped SVGs rather than flat path collections. They also release a Semantic SVG Benchmark with human-annotated semantic groupings. This addresses a real usability gap since editing flat SVG outputs requires manual path identification.

entry.title: Loop-Back Authority in LLM Agent Teams: A Paired Experiment on Flat and Hierarchical Coordination

author.name: Burak Agachan, Max van Duijn, Amirhossein Zohrehvand

entry.summary: This paper runs a paired experiment isolating a single coordination link in five-agent LLM teams: whether a Manager may reject worker output and require revision, holding roles, prompts, tools, models, and data fixed across 43 paired trials on open-ended work. Competing theory makes opposite predictions (organizational theory predicts faster convergence; sycophancy and degeneration-of-thought work predicts degradation). The design is notable for testing the authority link itself rather than swapping whole frameworks.

entry.title: Steering Generative Robot Policies with Lexicographic Preferences

author.name: Yixuan Jia, Jonathan P. How

entry.summary: The paper shows that frozen generative robot policies based on diffusion or flow matching can be steered at inference time to respect lexicographically ordered deployment objectives, such as satisfying embodiment feasibility constraints before applying user preferences. This enables deployment-time customization without retraining, addressing requirements absent from training. It is valuable for practical robot policy deployment.

entry.title: Branched Optimal Transport Amortization

author.name: Semyon Semenov, Viktor Kovalchuk, Meir Roketlishvili, Albert Baichorov, Fakhri Karray, Martin Takac, Arip Asadulaev

entry.summary: This paper introduces branched optimal transport (BOT) into deep generative modeling, motivated by the tree-like economy of scale seen in natural transport networks. It argues that standard flow matching cannot share pathways or merge flows, and proposes amortized BOT to capture hierarchical branching structure and minimize total transport cost in generative models.

entry.title: Refinement-based Flow Policy Optimization

author.name: Bumgeun Park, Hyukjun Yang, Donghwan Lee

entry.summary: RFPO addresses the challenge of training flow-based policies in online reinforcement learning when the target action distribution is defined only implicitly by a Q-function, making direct sampling intractable. The method alternates between Q-guided refinement of samples generated from Gaussian noise and self-target flow matching, enabling expressive flow policies in online RL.

entry.title: IWC-Bench: Evaluating Web Application Generation from a Software Testing Perspective

author.name: Chenxu Liu, Zilu Zou, Peizhong Gao, Jiawen Tao, Zhexin Zhang, Guang Chen, Haowei Lin, Ying Zhou, Tianyi Bai, Dolly Deng, Suncong Zheng, Maxm Pan

entry.summary: IWC-Bench is an interactive benchmark for evaluating LLM-generated web applications using software testing methodology. It instruments each generated application and uses code coverage to guide an agent in exploring functionality, addressing limits of static benchmarks that credit unreachable code and interactive benchmarks that miss functionality due to incomplete exploration. This separates application defects from agent execution failures and better matches human judgment of quality.

entry.title: Bench2Dex: Benchmarking Visuo-Tactile Bimanual Dexterous Manipulation Across Dexterous Hands

author.name: Zhenjie Yang, Yideng Zhang, Dongjie Zhang, Chenyu Jiang, Xianshuai Liu, Yufeng Li, Zuhao Ge, Xingyu Jiao, Zheng Zhang, Kaiyu He, He Wang, Yuwen Zhong, Yi Deng, Muyun Jiang, Xianliang Huang, Haisheng Su, Donghang Zhang, Jian Zhang, Xue Yang, Hongyang Li, Zuxuan Wu, Yu-Gang Jiang, Xiaosong Jia, Junchi Yan

entry.summary: Bench2Dex is a simulation benchmark for visuo-tactile bimanual dexterous manipulation spanning 12 dexterous hands, adapting robot models with a shared simulated tactile interface that converts local contact geometry into image-like observations. It addresses hardware non-convergence in tactile sensor design and sim-to-real signal mismatch, enabling consistent cross-hand comparison.

entry.title: Do Tabular Foundation Models Still Need Feature Engineering?

author.name: Yifan WU, Pinjun Dong, Jiran Tao, Binyan Jiang

entry.summary: This controlled study asks whether manual feature engineering still matters for tabular foundation models, testing a wide range of feature engineering techniques across several versions of two major TFM families on TabArena benchmarks. The consistent finding is that feature engineering gains concentrate in earlier model generations and become negligible for the strongest models. The results indicate that increasingly capable tabular foundation models are absorbing what feature engineering used to provide.

entry.title: Does Reasoning Improve Psychological Depth in Large Language Models? It Depends on Who's Judging

author.name: Ruichen Zheng, Yihe Wang, Fabrice Y Harel-Canada, Sara Khosravi, Zeynep Senahan Yildiz, Amit Sahai, Nanyun Peng

entry.summary: Using blinded story pairs from GPT-5 vs GPT-4o and DeepSeek-R1 vs DeepSeek-V3, the study finds human readers show no universal preference for reasoning models, with GPT-5 only modestly preferred over GPT-4o and DeepSeek-R1 trailing V3, while LLM judges behave differently. It demonstrates that LLM-as-judge correlation on development sets may not guarantee valid measurement on subjective, closely matched outputs.

entry.title: High-Probability Nash Regret for Decentralized Learning in Markov $\alpha$-Potential Games: Episodic and Fully Online Asynchronous Algorithms with Applications to Markov Congestion Games

author.name: S. Rasoul Etesami

entry.summary: This theoretical work develops KL-projected natural policy gradient algorithms for decentralized learning of Nash equilibria in infinite-horizon Markov alpha-potential games under bandit feedback, in both episodic and fully online asynchronous settings. It establishes finite-time high-probability NE regret bounds of order roughly T^(-1/4) and T^(-2/15), eliminating distribution-mismatch coefficients. It matters for the theory of multi-agent learning in games with potential structure, with applications to congestion settings.

entry.title: Rethinking Correctness for Uncertainty Estimation in Clinical Prediction with Vision-Language Models

author.name: Mingcheng Zhu, Jinning Liang, Tingting Zhu

entry.summary: This paper shows that uncertainty estimation evaluation in clinical prediction depends critically on the correctness criterion used to judge model outputs, which can distort reliability conclusions. It introduces a two-axis framework assessing criteria by agreement with human judgement and fidelity to human-referenced UE performance, evaluating eight criteria across clinical tasks and modalities.

entry.title: Sharp Rates and a One-Line Correction for Spectral Representation Learning

author.name: Dier Tang, Jing Yee Tan, Guangyue Han

entry.summary: The paper shows that the isotropy assumption justifying top-k spectral subspace methods (CCA, HGR maximal correlation, spectral contrastive loss) for self-supervised representation learning is the wrong hypothesis: transfer risk depends on the task covariance compressed onto the operator's leading subspace. The authors derive sharp transfer rates and a simple one-line correction. This offers actionable theory for when off-the-shelf frozen encoder features transfer well and how to fix them cheaply.

entry.title: Survey of Novel Deep Learning Architectures for Denoising Gravitational-wave Signals

author.name: Rohan Raha, Prayush Kumar

entry.summary: This work presents the first controlled comparison of five neural architectures for gravitational-wave denoising, all trained identically across the full spinning binary-black-hole parameter space, motivated by the prohibitive cost of matched filtering at next-generation detector event rates. A unifying design principle emerges from the comparison, informing reliable real-time waveform reconstruction for parameter estimation and tests of general relativity.

entry.title: Odds-Shift Slippage in One-vs-Rest Rankers: Diagnosing and Repairing Reweighting-Induced Top-K Errors

author.name: Akifumi Goto

entry.summary: The paper identifies and measures odds-shift slippage: the gap between the theoretical log-odds shift promised by per-label positive-class weighting (e.g., scale_pos_weight) in one-vs-rest rankers and what finite learners actually realize. On Santander, the standard weight collapses MAP@7 from 0.808 to 0.117, and the paper evaluates which repairs work in practice. This is a practically important diagnosis for anyone using class weighting in rare-label top-K ranking.

entry.title: NeuroFlex: Lossless Element-Level ANN-SNN Co-Execution for Efficient Sparse Inference

author.name: Varun Manjunath, Pranav Ramesh, Gopalakrishnan Srinivasan

entry.summary: NeuroFlex is an accelerator that assigns every output element independently to ANN or SNN execution mode with zero accuracy loss, extending integer-exact ANN-SNN equivalence from layers to individual elements. An offline cost-guided scheduler packs work across processing elements, achieving 97-99% PE utilization versus layer- or tile-granularity hybrids that leave cores idle. This improves energy-latency trade-offs for sparse inference hardware.

entry.title: Learning Multi-Agent Task Assignment and Navigation in the Factory: from Simulation to Real Robots

author.name: Abdalwhab Bakheet Mohamed Abdalwhab, Giovanni Beltrame, David St-Onge

entry.summary: The paper presents FMAPPO, a feature-fusion multi-agent PPO that combines 2D LiDAR with task state for decentralized multi-robot task assignment and navigation in industrial settings. It includes a full sim-to-real pipeline with ROS2 and demonstrates deployment on physical mobile manipulators under realistic factory conditions.

entry.title: Temperature Fragility and the Conditional Benefits of Truncation Sampling

author.name: Francesco La Rosa

entry.summary: This paper measures whether top-p and min-p truncation sampling improve accuracy at the temperature defaults (0.6-1.0) actually used in deployed systems, testing thirteen open-weight models on GSM8K and MMLU-Pro in a controlled pipeline. Results are mixed: benefits appear only at elevated temperatures and depend on the model, revealing temperature fragility.

entry.title: Disentangling Representation Evolution in Transformers through Directional Decomposition

author.name: Shwai He, Haichao Zhang, Shen Yan

entry.summary: The paper decomposes learned transformer representation updates into parallel and perpendicular components relative to the current hidden state, studying functional geometry across pretrained models. Targeted edit experiments reveal a space-dependent asymmetry: value-space parallel manipulation excluding the self token is markedly more robust than residual-space or perpendicular edits. This advances mechanistic interpretability by clarifying how attention and MLP updates shape representations.

entry.title: DenMark: Robust Semantic Watermarking for Diffusion Language Models

author.name: Tianhao Ma, Weihao Xuan, Dong-Dong Wu, Farshid Nooshi, Takashi Ishida, Gang Niu, Naoto Yokoya, Masashi Sugiyama

entry.summary: DenMark extends semantic text watermarking to diffusion language models by injecting key-dependent signals into the denoising process, partitioning output into fixed token regions with temporally structured signals. Existing semantic watermarks assume autoregressive generation and do not transfer to DLMs where tokens update in flexible orders. This anticipates provenance needs as diffusion-based text generation matures.

entry.title: Biomedical Reference Generation Remains Unreliable across 26 Large Language Models

author.name: Maxim Topaz, Zhihong Zhang, Nir Roguin, Pallavi Gupta, Zichao Li, Laura-Maria Peltonen

entry.summary: This systematic evaluation prompted 26 LLMs from eight developers to supply missing references for 69 biomedical passages, classifying outputs as verifiable, partial, fabricated, or declined. The study finds that reference fabrication remains a persistent and widespread reliability problem across model generations. This has direct implications for scientific and medical writing use of LLMs.

entry.title: Psychosis involves a deficit of information compression in connected speech

author.name: Samuele Vallisa, Claudio Palominos, Rui He, Emre Bora, Burcu Verim, Cemal Demirlek, Berna Yalincetin, Philipp Homan, Wolfram Hinzen

entry.summary: Using LLM-derived embeddings and surprisal metrics, the authors find evidence that psychosis is associated with reduced information compression in connected speech, operationalized via intrinsic dimensionality and prediction error across languages. The work leverages LLM representations as scientific instruments for studying neurodiverse conditions. This demonstrates a clinically meaningful application of language model representations to psychiatry.

entry.title: HypoEvolve: Genetic Algorithms Enable Multi-Agent LLMs to Discover Scientific Hypotheses

author.name: Jieyuan Liu, Mengzhou Hu, Jefferson Chen, JungHo Kong, Pratibha Jagannatha, Yiming Gao, Dexter Pratt, Hsin-Yuan Lee, Zhiting Hu, Trey Ideker, Wei Wang, Eric P. Xing, Zhen Wang

entry.summary: HypoEvolve combines multi-agent LLM systems with evolutionary search for scientific hypothesis discovery, making collaboration explicit through successive updates to a hypothesis population and allowing controlled study of how collaboration forms affect hypothesis quality. The framework preserves agents' scientific roles and supports rules for combining, revising, and retaining hypotheses. It contributes to the emerging field of AI-driven scientific discovery.

entry.title: ConeGaussian: Anti-Aliased Gaussian Ray-Tracing for Generic Central Cameras

author.name: Deheng Zhang, Letian Shi, Runyi Yang, Zhendong Li, Lei Sun, Kanzhi Wu, Ajad Chhatkuli, Danda Pani Paudel, Luc Van Gool

entry.summary: ConeGaussian introduces a camera-model-agnostic anti-aliasing framework for Gaussian ray-based rendering that replaces single center rays with pixel-footprint-aware cone sampling, addressing aliasing under minification and unsupported frequencies under magnification. The formulation defines the pixel filter independent of a camera-specific image plane. This improves 3D Gaussian splatting style rendering across camera models, including fisheye and omnidirectional systems.

entry.title: Semantic Privacy Protection with Utility Preservation for 3D Point Clouds

author.name: Jinchang zhang, Jiakai Lin, David Crandall, Guoyu Lu

entry.summary: Proposes a class-transfer semantic encryption framework for 3D point clouds that conceals original class information while preserving downstream task utility and enabling authorized recovery. It builds a shared-backbone Normalizing Flow latent space with LoRA/FiLM parameter-efficient adaptation and diffusion-guided flow alignment.

entry.title: Adapting Open-Weight MLLMs to Generate Point Prompts for Electron Microscopy Segmentation

author.name: Samia Mohinta, Albert Cardona

entry.summary: The paper trains LoRA adapters on open-weight MLLMs to generate centroid point prompts for a frozen microSAM segmenter from natural-language requests, automating promptable EM segmentation. Qwen3-VL reaches AP50 of 0.736 after supervised fine-tuning and reward optimization (up from 0.247), while automatic prompt generation achieves 0.773.

entry.title: SyntheticDoc: A Large Synthetic Dataset for Document Unwarping and Illumination Correction

author.name: Daniel Woortmann, Tanguy Magne, Olga Sorkine-Hornung

entry.summary: SyntheticDoc is a million-sample, procedurally generated dataset for document rectification and illumination correction with pixel-perfect annotations including UV maps, normal maps, albedo, and shading, designed to replace the decade-old, limited Doc3D dataset. The authors emphasize physical realism of the synthetic generation pipeline.

entry.title: V-ICAL Bench: Evaluating Video In-Context Learning for Multimodal Agents in Interactive Environments

author.name: Ziqian Fan, Shibo Xu, Junjie Li, Xiangyu Zhao, Shengyuan Ding, Yifan Yang, Zhenjie Yang, Haodong Duan, Yue Zhou, Zhihang Zhong, Xue Yang

entry.summary: V-ICAL is a benchmark of 342 interactive tasks across 37 environments that evaluates video-based in-context learning for multimodal agents, requiring them to translate human demonstration videos into executable policies, ground them in new visual states, and refine actions from environmental feedback. It fills a gap because multimodal ICL from video demonstrations remains largely unmeasured.

entry.title: Deformable 2D Gaussian Splatting for Efficient 4K Video Compression

author.name: Chenhao Zhang, Fengqing Zhu

entry.summary: This paper applies Gaussian Splatting to ultra-high-definition video compression, representing and compressing groups of pictures with a coarse-to-fine multi-scale deformable 2D Gaussian scheme. The approach targets real-time decoding, avoiding the high latency and memory cost of neural video compression and implicit neural representations.

entry.title: MedVA: An End-to-End Neuro-Symbolic Agentic System for Medical Volume Visualization

author.name: Haill An, Suhyeon Kim, Minjun Kang, Eunwoo Lee, Bin Sheng, Lei Bi, Younhyun Jung

entry.summary: MedVA is a neuro-symbolic agentic system for medical volume visualization that combines natural-language interaction with structured control of ROI selection and visual emphasis, reducing reliance on MLLM inference throughout the workflow. It aims to produce clinically reliable visualization operations without trial-and-error manual tuning.

entry.title: An MRI-Guided Robotic System to Improve Hippocampal Access for Epilepsy Interventions

author.name: John E. Peters, Abby M. Grillo, Mahshid Mansouri, Daniel S. Esser, Sarah Garrow, Nithin S. Kumar, Dario J. Englot, Joseph S. Neimat, William A. Grissom, Robert J. Webster III, Eric J. Barth

entry.summary: This work presents an MRI-guided robot that delivers a curved needle-like laser ablator through the foramen ovale to improve hippocampal access for epilepsy treatment, advancing over straight-line LITT. Phantom experiments achieved cannulation percentages up to 96.5%, exceeding reported clinical benchmarks.

entry.title: EMoG: Emotion-Modulated Gait Generation for Expressive Humanoid Locomotion

author.name: Yi Lu, Tianhao Jiang, Honglong Tian, Yumeng Zhang, Qingrui Zhao, Zhengtao Wang, Xiao-Xiao Long, Qiu Shen, Xun Cao

entry.summary: EMoG introduces an emotion-modulated gait generation framework for humanoid robots, using a continuously adjustable emotional style code to produce expressive yet command-consistent gaits via an MLP, executed by a reinforcement learning tracking policy. The team collected a large-scale emotion-annotated gait dataset from professional performers with an automated extraction pipeline. This is a novel direction connecting affective expression with real-time humanoid locomotion control.

entry.title: Real-World Reinforcement Learning with MPC Scaffolding for Dexterous Manipulation

author.name: Emek Bar{\i}\c{s} K\"u\c{c}\"uktabak, Karankumar Patel, Zhaodong Yang, Jinda Cui, Kazuhiro Sasabuchi, Jun Takamatsu

entry.summary: This work uses sampling-based MPC as scaffolding for real-world dexterous RL, seeding a replay buffer with MPC trajectories to pretrain actor-critic networks and intermittently guiding data collection during online Soft Actor-Critic learning, without human demonstrations. This mitigates inefficient early exploration and costly failures in physical dexterous learning. It contributes a concrete recipe for safe and efficient real-world RL on manipulation.

entry.title: Threat Models for Catastrophic Risks from Decentralised Agent Swarms

author.name: Stephen Elliott

entry.summary: An analysis of whether decentralized, multi-owner LLM agent swarms — as opposed to the centralized swarms seen in recent frontier-lab incidents — could produce catastrophic risks, drawing on cooperative AI and large agent systems literature. The author compares the relative danger of decentralized versus centralized swarms and discusses safety implications.

entry.title: Asclepius: An Adaptive Harness for Long-Horizon Clinical Agents

author.name: Grace Chang Yuan, Xiaoman Zhang, Sung Eun Kim, Luyang Luo, Pranav Rajpurkar

entry.summary: Uses a Clinical Environment Simulator where an agent manages an entire emergency-department shift under time and resource pressure to reveal long-horizon execution failures that short single-task benchmarks miss. It finds current agents usually reach correct diagnoses but fail on complete and timely critical actions, attributing the gap to failure modes like instruction-adherence drift, each operationalized as per-trace counters.

entry.title: Trustworthy Agentic AI: A Comprehensive Cybersecurity and Systems Survey on Threat Landscapes, Defense Architectures, and Open Challenges

author.name: Seyedakbar Mostafavi

entry.summary: A comprehensive systems-security survey of agentic AI, framing how coupling probabilistic neural cores to filesystems, networks, and cloud infrastructure dissolves classical security perimeters, with natural language acting as data, control code, and protocol simultaneously. It organizes threat landscapes, defense architectures, and open challenges for trustworthy autonomous agents. Timely given the rapid shift from passive models to tool-executing agents.

entry.title: Issue Bias in Generative AI Writing Assistance: Political Issues and LLMs in the Swedish 2026 Election

author.name: Bastiaan Bruinsma, Annika Fred\'en, Paul R\"ottger, Moa Johansson, Asad Sayeed

entry.summary: This study examines political stances of six LLMs on Swedish-language writing tasks ahead of the 2026 Swedish parliamentary election, crossing 107 policy propositions with 77 writing templates across neutral, positive, and negative framings to produce roughly 148,000 responses. It analyzes default stance tendencies, framing effects, and cross-issue comparisons. Given evidence that AI assistants influence voter opinions, mapping their issue bias has democratic significance.

entry.title: Recurrent GraphNeural NetworkswithSet-BasedAggregation

author.name: Blai Bonet

entry.summary: The paper studies recurrent GNNs with set-based aggregation and identifies weight-checkable sufficient conditions for two-way compilability between networks and logical formulas. The main result is an effective equivalence between a class of such networks and the Boolean closure of reachability and safety properties in the fragment B Sigma-circ_1 of the modal mu-calculus, shown to be the exact expressive level of stabilization over finite vocabulary.

entry.title: LLMs or Naive Bayes? Old Gems or New Ways

author.name: Mohammad Firas Sada, Dmitry Mishin, John Graham, Seungmin Kim, Mahidhar Tatineni, Frank W\"urthwein

entry.summary: This benchmark study compares Complement Naive Bayes against zero- and few-shot LLMs across four families and a 37x parameter range on text classification. NB dominates once labeled data exists, matching or beating even frontier-scale models on several tasks, while LLMs win only in zero-data regimes where contamination is a confound. It is a valuable cost-benefit reality check for research computing practitioners.

entry.title: Symmetry- and Property-Aware Crystal Generation with Reinforcement Learning for Inverse Materials Design

author.name: Ting-Wei Hsu, Arun Bansil, Qimin Yan

entry.summary: SPARC is a symmetry- and property-aware RL framework for inverse design of crystalline materials that optimizes physical objectives while preserving the crystallographic constraints that make those properties well defined, such as symmetry-required conditions for uniaxial dielectric anisotropy. It demonstrates that favorable numerical property values are meaningless without supporting structural symmetry.

entry.title: An Efficient and Modular Framework for Targeted Harm Mitigation in LLMS

author.name: Roberto Campbell, Momin Abbass, Muneeza Azmat, Michal Ulewicz, Raya Horesh, Kristjan Greenewald, Rog\'erio Abreu de Paula, Nathalie Baracaldo

entry.summary: The paper proposes a modular correction framework using Activated LoRA (aLoRA) adapters with context-aware routing to mitigate biased or toxic LLM outputs. Expert adapters activate mid-sequence without invalidating the KV cache, enabling low-latency targeted correction during generation. This decouples alignment corrections from the base model, offering a scalable alternative to costly model-coupled alignment methods.

entry.title: Follow the Geometry, Not the Model: Cold Start Semi-Supervised Learning

author.name: Itai David, Daphna Weinshall

entry.summary: VAST decouples pseudo-label generation from classifier training for few-label (cold-start) SSL: probabilistic beliefs over unlabeled data are inferred directly from the geometry of a frozen self-supervised embedding via a kernel-based Veracity Matrix, then distilled into an inductive classifier. This sidesteps the ill-posedness of self-supervised pseudo-labeling before any learned classifier exists.

entry.title: AdaVSkip: Adaptive Visual Token Skipping Across Layers For Efficient MLLMs Inference

author.name: Yuyao Sun, Tao Deng, Shuang Li, Deqing Wang

entry.summary: AdaVSkip accelerates multimodal LLM inference by exploiting the observation that vertical redundancy (across layers) varies by input and differs between self-attention and MLP modules. It attaches lightweight routers at each layer that independently decide whether visual tokens pass through or skip attention and MLP components, yielding input-adaptive execution patterns.

entry.title: Self-Evolving Memory for Generative Recommendation

author.name: Xinyu Lin, Zhuosong Jiang, Zixiao Suo, Siqin Wang, Hanqing Zeng, Hanchao Yu, Yinglong Xia, Jiang Zhang, Aashu Singh, Fei Liu, Wenjie Wang, Fuli Feng, Yang Song, Qifan Wang, Tat-Seng Chua

entry.summary: This paper identifies evolution conflict in generative recommendation: continual retraining and distillation-based adaptation of a shared autoregressive model cause heterogeneous user preference shifts to interfere, with dominant patterns crowding out minority ones. The authors propose a self-evolving memory approach that adapts via memory rather than directly updating shared parameters. This addresses a key capability requirement for self-evolving generative recommender systems.

entry.title: T-SMART: Mechanism-Level Attribution for Tool-Augmented Time-Series Question Answering

author.name: Ivan Delgado, Himansi Gupta, Bishal Khatri, Niharika Sapre, Lameta Shamoon, Onat Gungor, Tajana Rosing

entry.summary: Presents T-SMART, a neurosymbolic framework for time-series question answering that separates LLM reasoning, deterministic numerical tools, and structured perception, enabling mechanism-level attribution of performance gains. Controlled ablations show deterministic computation provides the dominant benefit, improving accuracy by 31.7 percentage points.

entry.title: MoARa: Module-Aware Rank Allocation and Structure-Preserving Decomposition for Low-Rank LLM Pre-training

author.name: Keunyoung Kim, Nojun Kwak

entry.summary: MoARa improves low-rank gradient projection methods for LLM pretraining by combining module-aware, profiling-based allocation of projection rank across heterogeneous Transformer components with a block-wise magnitude-direction decomposition of raw gradients. Across five Transformer architectures it reduces steps and wall-clock time to reach target quality while cutting optimizer-state memory. It matters because memory-efficient pretraining is a major lever for democratizing large model training.

entry.title: Self-Indexing Attention for Compression-Compatible Sparse Long-Context LLM Inference

author.name: Xu Yang, Jiapeng Zhang, Zhangke, Changjian Chen, Yuxin Chen, Feiqiang Sun, Chengguang Xu, Feng Jin, Zhuo Tang

entry.summary: Self-Indexing Attention is a training-free sparse attention framework using a shared transform-domain sign-magnitude representation whose 1-bit signs serve as a reusable token index for both grouped prefill selection and decode retrieval, staying compatible with external KV-cache compression. The bitwise-compatible index enables efficient retrieval on modern accelerators, operating at 5% attention density. This addresses a real efficiency pain point in long-context LLM inference.

entry.title: Stochastic Gradient Descent over P2

author.name: Maria Oprea, Qin Li, Yunan Yang

entry.summary: The paper extends diffusion approximations of SGD from Euclidean spaces to optimization over probability measures on Wasserstein space P2, using Lions differentiability to lift the problem to a linear Hilbert space where higher-order calculus applies. It constructs a Gaussian random-field approximation whose velocity field mirrors the classical SGD noise-replacement principle.

entry.title: Learning to Coach for Experiential Learning

author.name: Guanheng Chen, Tianzhu Ye, Li Dong, Xun Wu, Shaohan Huang, Furu Wei

entry.summary: L2C trains a dedicated LLM-as-a-Coach to distill actionable knowledge from an actor model's prior trajectories, optimizing rewards based on whether guided responses are correct, with same-instance and cross-instance transfer rewards. The actor stays frozen while the coach learns to summarize experience effectively. It consistently outperforms baselines on mathematical reasoning and interactive text games, addressing the noise problem in experience-based learning.

entry.title: GRAVA: Grounded Reasoning-to-Action Representation and Learning for Autonomous Driving

author.name: Xiao Liu, Haoyu Li, Jianghao Leng, Lin Wang, Chao Sun

entry.summary: GRAVA unifies grounding, reasoning, and action generation in a single autoregressive stream for driving VLA models, linking language references to visual regions and ego-centric physical states and organizing decisions in a trajectory-anchored typed graph. A VLM produces grounded reasoning followed by a compact executable planner action deterministically decoded into control.

entry.title: NavPatch: Evidence-Guided Object-Level Costmap Correction with Vision-Language Models

author.name: Shiji Sun, Xingyu Tao, Hao Wang, Ling Wang, Zhengyi Chen

entry.summary: NavPatch adds an object-level correction layer to robot costmaps, using a vision-language model to issue ADD, REMOVE, or EXTEND corrections for navigation-relevant objects such as low cables, curtains, or cones. It combines open-vocabulary grounding, LiDAR and RGB-D observations, quality filtering, and cross-frame maintenance to decide when corrections apply. This addresses the well-known mismatch between geometric maps and how obstacles should affect navigation.

entry.title: ResSafe: Learning Safety Filtering with Residual Reinforcement Learning for Humanoids

author.name: Gechen Qu, Tong Zhang, Bike Zhang, Yen-Jen Wang, Koushil Sreenath, Claire Tomlin, Jason Jangho Choi

entry.summary: ResSafe decouples task performance and safety in humanoid robot control by letting a nominal RL policy optimize for task goals while a residual policy learns safety corrections, acting as an implicit safety filter. This architecture improves the performance-safety tradeoff compared to a single policy that must balance all objectives, addressing falls and instability in high-dimensional, contact-rich humanoid dynamics.

entry.title: Root-Cause Attribution Is a Search Problem: Continual Search for Long-Horizon Agent Failures

author.name: Harsh Raj, David Lee, Anas Mahmoud, Renxiong Wang, Razvan-Gabriel Dumitru, Chenguang Wang, Tong Zhao, Yunzhong He, Darvin Yi, Vipul Gupta

entry.summary: Frames automated root-cause attribution of long-horizon agent failures as a search problem over massive execution logs, where relevant evidence is sparse and distant from the visible failure. It proposes continual search methods to replace one-shot LLM judgments, improving diagnostic accuracy for agent reliability.

entry.title: DynSTEER: Dynamic Stage-wise Trajectory Evaluation and Execution-time Review for Agents

author.name: Zhichao Shi, Wenjie Zhang, Xuhui Jiang, Xiaojun Wu, Cehao Yang, Chengjin Xu, Jian Guo, Yuanzhuo Wang

entry.summary: DynSTEER evaluates LLM agent trajectories stage by stage, anchoring segments at key completed actions rather than only terminal outcomes, enabling error localization, support for alternative valid solution paths, and early halting of failing runs at lower cost than post-hoc trajectory judging. It addresses three concrete limitations of current agent evaluation paradigms.

entry.title: Attention Is All You Need (to Avoid Spurious Oscillations)

author.name: Jinyoung Jeong, Joseph B. Choi, Xinlun Cheng, H. S. Udaykumar, Sanghun Choi, Stephen S. Baek

entry.summary: The paper develops a conservative finite-volume scheme in which a CFL-conditioned attention flux selects upstream information for shock transport, demonstrating on 1D inviscid Burgers that the same learned flux preserves sharp shocks with four-times-larger timesteps and one stage per update. Comparisons against WENO-5+SSP-RK3 and controlled Forward Euler variants isolate flux selection from time integration effects.

entry.title: HarnessBandit: Joint Learnability-Transferability Scheduling for Multi-Harness Agentic Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Hongliang Wei (Harbin Institute of Technology, Alibaba Cloud), Xiaobing Tu (Alibaba Cloud), Yinggui Wang (Alibaba Cloud), Zhengxi Liu (Alibaba Cloud), Rongkun Xue (Alibaba Cloud), Jinkui Ren (Alibaba Cloud), Xiantao Zhang (Alibaba Cloud), Debin Zhao (Harbin Institute of Technology), Xiaopeng Fan (Harbin Institute of Technology)

entry.summary: HarnessBandit is an online scheduler for training a single LLM policy across multiple agent harnesses that differ in system prompts, tool schemas, and trajectory formats. After each GRPO update it observes a harness's learnability and predicts transferability to select which harness to train on next, addressing robustness to interface variation in agentic RL. An Alibaba Cloud and HIT collaboration on a practical agentic-RL training problem.

entry.title: ATTRICITE: Training an Open 4B Model for Citation Recovery toward Faithful Attribution

author.name: Yee Man Choi, Xuehang Guo, Songcheng Cai, Yimu Wang, Yi R. Fung, Qingyun Wang

entry.summary: ATTRICITE is an open 4B-parameter, tool-using model trained to recover the paper an original author actually cited from a citation-bearing passage, using this as a proxy for faithful attribution progress. The release includes CITEALIGN, a 7,607-instance computer-science dataset, and a controlled 709-instance benchmark within the CiteGuard retrieval environment.

entry.title: Failure-Guided Co-Evolution of Prompts and Training Data

author.name: Tianyu Yuan, Zhuzhong Qian

entry.summary: FORGE introduces a failure-guided framework for automatic prompt optimization that co-evolves prompts and training data rather than optimizing against a fixed instance set. It abstracts failed executions into reusable failure modes, synthesizes new training data via four mutation strategies, and feeds verified instances back into prompt refinement.

entry.title: Efficient Online Inverse Optimization with $O(d)$ Regret

author.name: Yang Cai, Anupam Gupta, Vineet Gupta, Guru Guruganesh, Yanchen Jiang, Christopher Liaw, Aranyak Mehta, Renato Paes Leme, Grigoris Velegkas, Di Wang

entry.summary: The paper gives the first efficient and proper deterministic algorithm for online inverse linear optimization with O(d) regret uniform in the horizon, at O(d^2) time per round, improving on a recent improper algorithm that cost superpolynomial time per round. The approach builds on variable-metric methods with a self-normalized rank-one update and replaces the log-det potential with a trace power, removing the log T factor. It also extends to non-optimizing experts and corruption robustness.

entry.title: Accuracy Is Not Service: A Decision-Aware Benchmark for Intermittent-Demand Forecasting

author.name: Joo Ern Chin, Shih-Fen Cheng, Aldy Gunawan

entry.summary: Benchmarking 38 forecasting methods on an industrial spare-parts panel and public datasets, the paper shows that forecast-accuracy rank and order-level service rank are negatively correlated (-0.555) in intermittent-demand settings. This decision-aware evaluation reveals that selecting forecasters on accuracy alone can actively harm service outcomes in contract logistics.

entry.title: Multimodal deep learning from spectra for small-molecule structure identification: enhancing robustness with mixed-condition training

author.name: Bowen Gao, Lei Zhu, Yiying Wang, Wenjie Yu

entry.summary: Incorporates spectroscopy and chemistry domain knowledge into mixed-condition training for candidate molecular structure reranking, with modality-specific perturbations and chemically informed spectrum replacements to handle missing or degraded spectra. Evaluates 79,462 test samples across 30 conditions with a mixture-of-experts fusion and a reproducible protocol.

entry.title: Principal-timestep Restricted Init via Sparse Matrix-decomposition in Flow-matching

author.name: Jiayang Gu, Zheng Fang, Lichaun Xiang, Fanghui Liu, Xu Cai, Hongkai Wen

entry.summary: The paper finds that LoRA with spectral initialization, effective for autoregressive LMs, often fails or underperforms vanilla LoRA in flow-matching diffusion fine-tuning due to a mismatch with high-rank gradients induced by the flow-matching objective. It proposes a principal-timestep restricted initialization via sparse matrix decomposition tailored to this setting.

entry.title: Part Grounding, Not Action Knowledge: Locating the Bottleneck in VLM Affordance Prediction

author.name: Sarthak Sattigeri

entry.summary: This study dissects why vision-language models reason poorly about low-level manipulation, separating part identification from action knowledge across 19 articulated objects and eight models from three developers. It finds models fail at identifying the correct part to act on (e.g., describing picking up a camera rather than pressing it), with push chosen once in 64 evaluations where it was correct despite being in the offered label set. This localizes the affordance bottleneck to part grounding rather than action knowledge.

entry.title: SomBench: Benchmark Dataset for Advancing Machine Learning in Lunar Science

author.name: Himanshu Patil, Gabby Nyirjesy, Rachel A. Slank, Vishal Gaur, Daniela Szwarcman, Paolo Fraccaro, Nikolaos Dionelis, Michael K. Barker, Andrew Annex, Vishnu Viswanathan, Zachary Morse, Ethan I. Schaefer, Hiyam Debary, Ankur Kumar, Rohit Lal, Geoffrey Dawson, Campbell Watson, Rebekah I. Dawson-Rigas, Manil Maskey, Juan Bernab\'e-Moreno, Rahul Ramachandran, Sujit Roy

entry.summary: SomBench aggregates 30+ co-registered data layers from ten instruments across four lunar missions into a unified, spatially aligned, ML-ready dataset spanning resolutions from 1 meter to 20 km/pixel, with leakage-safe splits distributed as netCDF. An image-anchored tiling pipeline produces multimodal pretraining-ready tile views to enable reproducible ML for lunar science.

entry.title: Just add noise: Debiasing tree-based variable importance in mixed data

author.name: Jiahe Li, Omar Melikechi

entry.summary: The paper theoretically analyzes the known bias of random-forest variable importance toward continuous predictors over categorical ones and proposes a remarkably simple remedy: adding small noise to each categorical predictor. The correction is validated on simulated and real datasets and combined with path stability selection to enable variable selection with false discovery control on mixed data. A clean, broadly applicable statistical result.

entry.title: Bridging Control, Inference, Transport, and Thermodynamics: From Theory to Applications in Learning

author.name: Emmy Blumenthal, Nikolas Claussen, Benjamin Eysenbach, Catherine Ji, Gautam Reddy, Colin Scheibner, Benjamin Sorkin

entry.summary: This is a review that unifies conceptual threads connecting control theory, optimal transport, probabilistic inference, non-equilibrium thermodynamics, and machine learning. The unifying theme is optimization of free-energy-like functionals under dynamical or statistical constraints, with applications including reinforcement learning and generative modeling. Such syntheses help transfer insights across fields that often use different vocabulary.

entry.title: Can We Trust the Judges? Validation of Factuality Evaluation Methods via Answer Perturbation

author.name: Sarra Gharsallah, Adele Robaldo, Mariia Tokareva, Giovanni Gatti Pinheiro, Ilyana Guendouz, Rapha\"el Troncy, Paolo Papotti, Pietro Michiardi

entry.summary: This meta-evaluation framework tests factuality metrics by generating controlled corruptions of gold answers with known degradation levels and probing how well metrics track truthfulness changes. It finds that pipeline-based methods like RAGAS's factual correctness metric outperform LLM-as-judge approaches, and proposes an improved metric variant. The work speaks directly to the reliability of the evaluation infrastructure underpinning LLM factuality research.

entry.title: RIGOR: Rig-Informed Geometry for Omnidirectional Reconstruction

author.name: Tingjun Huang, Dmitry Rudshin, Mathieu Meyer, Pietro Bonazzi, Marc Pollefeys, Emilia Szyma\'nska

entry.summary: RIGOR is a large-scale feed-forward reconstruction pipeline for gravity-aligned omnidirectional video that addresses long-trajectory inconsistency in demanding environments with repetitive structures and weak textures. It brings 360-degree imagery support to feed-forward 3D reconstruction models, which typically lack it or need fine-tuning. The rig-informed geometric priors leverage the wide coverage of omnidirectional cameras.

entry.title: Mind2Cloud: EEG-to-Point Cloud Generation with Two-Granularity Diffusion Decoding

author.name: Yongyi Lu, Xiongfeng Huang, Zhijing Yang

entry.summary: Mind2Cloud reconstructs 3D point clouds from EEG signals using a two-granularity diffusion decoder that combines a global Transformer branch and a local Point-Voxel CNN branch across diffusion timesteps via a learnable fusion mask. This time-aware design addresses the evolving semantic granularity of both EEG representations and the denoising process.

entry.title: AnchorGUI: Asymmetric Memory for Dual-Scale Learning in GUI Navigation

author.name: Shengjie Jin, Zelong Sun, Hengbo Xu, Yanbiao Ma, Zhiwu Lu

entry.summary: AnchorGUI is a framework for VLM-based GUI navigation agents that handles dense visual histories through a Cognitive State Anchor, exploiting the insight that expected transitions compress well into text while unexpected outcomes need preserved screenshots as causal evidence. This supports both intra-trial error correction and cross-trial experience distillation.

entry.title: SONAR: A Structure-Consistent Neural Operator for Null-Space-Aware Sparse View CT Reconstruction

author.name: Song Ni, Haijun Yu, Haodong Li, Changsheng Fang, Shuyi Fan, Yixing Huang, Hengyong Yu

entry.summary: SONAR is a neural operator for sparse-view CT reconstruction that predicts a low-dimensional null-space-aware representation from projections rather than recovering the full null-space in image space. It separates measurement and pseudo-measurement residuals and lifts results into the image domain through physics constraints, improving robustness of dose-reduced CT.

entry.title: A Novel Robot-Assisted Learning Pedagogy for Children with ASD

author.name: Laura Boccanfuso, Erin Barney, Marilena Mademtzi, Claire Foster, Quan Wang, Colette Torres, Lisa Chen, Brian Scassellati, Pamela Ventola, Frederick Shic

entry.summary: This work introduces a robot-assisted intervention paradigm for children with autism spectrum disorder that incorporates validated classroom teaching pedagogies, addressing the gap between clinical lab-based interventions and mainstream school settings. A credible team from Yale and clinical collaborators grounds the study clinically. The work is significant for translating robot-assisted autism therapy into real educational contexts.

entry.title: DIDO: Distilling Interaction-Centric Dynamics into One-Step Denoising for World Action Models

author.name: Jing Lyu, Shuanghao Bai, Runze Xiao, Zhenyu Liao, Wenxing Tan, Zihan Tang, Ruochuan Shi, Cheng Peng, Yuheng Ji, Yihao Wang, Badong Chen, Pengwei Wang, Zhongyuan Wang, Xiaoguang Zhao

entry.summary: DIDO tackles the latency of multi-step video diffusion in World Action Models by distilling converged interaction-centric dynamics into a one-step denoising model. The key empirical insight is that static backgrounds converge early during denoising while gripper-object interaction dynamics emerge only through subsequent steps, so naive one-step truncation loses the most control-relevant information. DIDO preserves these dynamics while enabling closed-loop control.

entry.title: Generalized Agent Iteration: One Formal Framework for Iterative Policy Improvement and Recursive Self-Improvement

author.name: Hongyao Tang, Yi Ma, Pengyi Li, Yifu Yuan

entry.summary: Presents Generalized Agent Iteration (GAI), a formal framework that unifies classical iterative policy improvement and recursive self-improvement (RSI) as instances of a single learning paradigm. By generalizing generalized policy iteration, it provides theoretical vocabulary for describing emerging RSI claims across scales in autonomous AI systems.

entry.title: Recoverability as a System Primitive for Long-Horizon AI Agents

author.name: Zhihui Zhang, Wei Liu

entry.summary: Introduces recoverability as a first-class system primitive for long-horizon AI agents, making resumption after interruption an explicit decision that binds a starting point to supporting evidence, execution, and independent verification rather than blindly continuing from saved state. A reference architecture connects persistence, validation, and control, evaluated with deterministic and paired runtime experiments. Addresses a real reliability gap in agentic systems.

entry.title: When does a scaling result justify a different allocation? A critical review of resource-allocation evidence for AI systems

author.name: Seyed Morteza Emadi

entry.summary: A critical integrative review asking when scaling results actually support resource-allocation decisions across pretraining, test-time compute, retrieval, and agent evaluation. It identifies three recurring mismatches: success counted before answer selection, information unavailable in deployment, and costs omitted from comparisons. A useful methodological corrective to how scaling evidence is consumed.

entry.title: Crypto Accounting Bench: Evaluating Frontier and Open-Weight Models on Crypto-Asset Accounting Tasks

author.name: Kareem Khattab, Omar Khattab, Mohamed Ibrahem

entry.summary: CAB is a new benchmark of 118 tasks from 7 pseudonymized organizations testing whether language models can reconstruct complete, correctly balanced journal entries for crypto-asset transactions, including accounts, sides, amounts, currencies, and precise quantities. It evaluates 12 proprietary and open-weight models on this structured financial reasoning task.

entry.title: SkillLift: Learning Dense Rubrics from Sparse Oracles for Efficient Skill Evolution

author.name: Haoxiang Kang, Ming Wen

entry.summary: SkillLift addresses the supervision bottleneck in LLM agent skill self-evolution, where each oracle evaluation requires a full agent rollout. Its key insight is that ranking skills is a smoother supervision target than regressing absolute outcomes; it learns an oracle-aligned rubric as a structured evaluation space via a bilevel formulation. This decouples skill search from expensive oracle calls.

entry.title: Beyond Safe Answers: Segment-Aware Listwise Alignment for Reasoning Safety in Large Reasoning Models

author.name: JungMin Yun, Junehyoung Kwon, Hayeong Ryu, Byeonggeuk Lim, Hoejoon Kwon, YoungBin Kim

entry.summary: SaLT-DPO targets the dual-surface safety problem of large reasoning models, where unsafe content in intermediate reasoning traces can be masked by safe-looking final answers. It decomposes responses into reasoning and answer segments, scores each independently, aligns length-normalized segment rewards with listwise soft targets, and applies a weakest-link safety coherence regularization. This extends DPO-style alignment beyond whole-response granularity.

entry.title: EvoOntology: A Self-Evolving Ontology Layer for Data Agents

author.name: Meiduo Chong, Shaolei Zhang, Ju Fan, Xiaoyong Du

entry.summary: EvoOntology introduces a self-evolving ontology layer, exposed as an MCP server with schema, content, and workflow components, to close the agent-data gap for data agents operating over heterogeneous tables, files, and databases. It avoids both raw-data exploration and static hand-built semantic layers by evolving the ontology as agent behavior changes.

entry.title: Task-Based CT Protocol Optimization Using Reinforcement Learning and Virtual Imaging Trials

author.name: Jiaqi Zou, David Fenwick, Vahid Tarokh, Nicholas Felice, Jayasai Rajagopal, Anuj Kapadia, Ehsan Samei, Navid NaderiAlizadeh, Ehsan Abadi

entry.summary: The authors apply a virtual imaging trial framework with PPO-based reinforcement learning to optimize CT protocols across 468 acquisition and reconstruction parameter combinations on 63 computational human models with liver lesions, balancing lesion detectability (d-prime) against radiation dose. This replaces impractical exhaustive physical testing with simulated in-silico trials. It demonstrates a credible pathway to safer, task-optimized medical imaging protocols.

entry.title: Building a Production Greek-English Speech Recognizer

author.name: Christos Petrocheilos, Cleopatra Papadopoulou, Chris Porikis, Ioakeim Perros, Ayoub Kirouane, Themistoklis Nikolis

entry.summary: This paper reports a multi-month engineering effort building Sophea, a production bilingual Greek-English ASR system, evaluated against nine production gates covering word error rate, language identification, and hallucination on non-speech audio across 23 training iterations. No data composition passed all gates simultaneously, revealing fundamental tensions between Greek noisy-environment performance and English language identification, and offering a detailed six-stage data pipeline with audio-quality calibration insights.

entry.title: Understanding the Limits of Agentic ICD Coding

author.name: Chong Yock Eng, Yushi Cao, Yiming Chen, Kezhi Mao, Hongchao Jiang

entry.summary: The study evaluates neural, workflow, and agentic systems for ICD-10-CM medical coding on rarity-stratified MIMIC-IV discharge summaries, revealing two orthogonal failure modes: a 0.43 micro-F1 gap between rare and common codes for classifiers, and near-zero workflow performance on multi-step injury/external-cause codes. A tool-augmented agentic setup with structured access to official ICD references recovers up to 0.34 micro-F1 on the hardest cases. Provides actionable diagnosis of where coding automation breaks down.

entry.title: EdgeHAR: An Edge-Native Compact Sensor Foundation Model for Human Activity Recognition

author.name: He Zhang, Siyu Yuan, Siyu Liu, Sizhen Bian, Bin Guo

entry.summary: EdgeHAR is a compact sensor foundation model for wearable human activity recognition that factorizes signals into three latent codes separating activity semantics, motion dynamics, and acquisition variations, improving transfer across unseen users, devices, sampling rates, and placements. It is designed for edge rather than cloud-scale deployment.

entry.title: CompCQR: Compositional Query Generation for Training-Free Conversational Search

author.name: Yunah Jang, Kang-il Lee, Joongbo Shin, Kyomin Jung

entry.summary: CompCQR is a training-free conversational query reformulation method built on the observation that retrievers are highly sensitive to content ordering, so reordering reformulated content can change retrieval coverage. It decomposes queries compositionally to avoid the repeated LLM invocations and retriever misalignment that plague LLM-based CQR approaches. This matters for efficient multi-turn information seeking with LLMs.

entry.title: Robust and Efficient Communication for Multi-Agent Learning

author.name: Rafael Pina, Varuna De Silva, Corentin Artaud

entry.summary: The paper introduces MARC, a multi-agent reinforcement learning communication framework grounded in information-theoretic principles of conditional mutual information. MARC uses attention-based architectures with a message regularization mechanism that minimizes uncertainty about future system states, inducing representative communication protocols. Crucially, it is evaluated under stringent communication bottlenecks and lossy channels simulating realistic physical constraints.

entry.title: Before You Poll with LLMs: A Deliberative Diagnostic Framework

author.name: Ahmed Wali, Hassaan Tayyab

entry.summary: This paper introduces a Deliberative Polling Diagnostic Framework that tests whether LLM personas update beliefs in response to new arguments like humans do, rather than merely holding correct static opinions. Comparing human and LLM belief shifts after identical informational interventions, it surfaces failures invisible to static evaluation, relevant to silicon sampling for public opinion simulation.

entry.title: Learning Multimodal One-step Flow Policy via Value-weighted Optimal Transport

author.name: Jaehun Shon, Jinha Choi, Jongwook Jeon, Jongmin Lee

entry.summary: OptiFlow is a framework for learning efficient one-step flow policies in offline reinforcement learning, addressing mode collapse and Q-value overestimation by jointly training a value-aware reference flow policy and a one-step policy coupled through state-wise entropic optimal transport. This enables fast inference while representing multimodal action distributions. It advances the practicality of flow-based policies for robot-like decision problems.

entry.title: Toward Optimal Switching Regret for Multi-Armed Bandits with Oblivious Adversary

author.name: Mengxiao Zhang

entry.summary: This theory paper shows that a single bandit algorithm achieves optimal O-tilde(sqrt((S+1)KT)) switching regret for every unknown number of arm switches S against an oblivious adversary, resolving an open problem from Auer et al. 2019. The approach combines fixed-share learners with dyadic-interval subroutines.

entry.title: CyFM: Cylindrical Optimal Transport for Few-Step Complex-Valued Flow Matching

author.name: Marcel Musia{\l}ek, Iga Wolanin, Damian Ryczko, Anna Grelewska, Oleksii Furman

entry.summary: Reframes complex-valued signals like MRI and audio spectrograms on the amplitude-phase cylinder rather than flat two-channel Euclidean space, analyzing the angular-velocity pathologies of Cartesian paths in flow matching. CyFM uses cylindrical optimal transport to enable more efficient few-step complex-valued flow matching.

entry.title: Decision-Oriented Uncertainty Quantification for Risk Control in Earth System Spatiotemporal Foundation Models

author.name: Ji Lu, Huiran Duan, Bo Zhao, Xianglong Wang, Yiru Fang, Kuo Yang, Xiaoqin Feng, Jianping Gou

entry.summary: This paper argues that calibrated intervals from Earth system foundation models are insufficient for high-stakes applications like extreme weather warning and flood control, and proposes a decision-oriented uncertainty quantification framework translating predictive uncertainty into reliable decision risk under specific actions, loss functions, and risk preferences. It matters because it bridges the gap between foundation model predictions and operational risk management decisions.

category.term: AI for Climate and Earth Science

entry.title: Bandits with Probing: Optimal Regret and the Limits of Winner Feedback

author.name: Yongjie Guan

entry.summary: This paper studies bandits where a learner probes k of n arms per round and observes only the maximum reward (winner feedback). It derives minimax regret laws with universal constants for both stochastic and adversarial settings, characterizing exactly when the probing advantage pays off for learning.

entry.title: GroundBench: A Factorized, Counterfactual Benchmark for Locating VLM Affordance Failures

author.name: Sarthak Sattigeri

entry.summary: GroundBench is a diagnostic benchmark that disentangles visual grounding, mechanical reasoning, and category-to-action association in VLM affordance failures via six branch-and-merge information conditions and counterfactual re-asks about alternate parts visible in the same image. Experiments across three OpenAI models and 1,068 predictions show supplying the target region without its identity changes behavior, revealing where models actually fail.

entry.title: Diffusion-Based Multiple-Shooting Indirect Optimal Control for Fuel-Optimal Spacecraft Trajectory Generation

author.name: Saeid Tafazzol, Ehsan Taheri, Ryne Beeson

entry.summary: The paper combines diffusion-based generative models with indirect optimal control for fuel-optimal spacecraft trajectories, using diffusion proposals to warm-start the costate estimates needed for sensitive Hamiltonian boundary-value problems and embedding this in a multiple-shooting scheme. This addresses the lack of optimality guarantees in prior diffusion-based control methods. The result enlarges the convergence domain of indirect methods on long-horizon bang-bang trajectory problems.

entry.title: Partition-Aware Scheduling for Mobile Heterogeneous Inference Co-Execution

author.name: Zhuojin Li, Marco Paolieri, Leana Golubchik

entry.summary: The paper formulates partition-aware DAG scheduling for mobile heterogeneous inference, jointly exploiting inter-operator (operator-to-device assignment) and intra-operator (CPU-GPU partitioning) parallelism for CNNs and vision transformers on platforms combining mobile GPUs and clustered CPU cores. It shows the best strategy depends on DAG structure, motivating an adaptive scheduler that improves inference latency. This is a solid systems contribution for on-device ML.

entry.title: Fusing Spectral Signatures and Activation Clustering for Backdoor Detection in Healthcare Imaging Models: Method, Implementation, and Evaluation

author.name: Suresh Tamang

entry.summary: This paper combines two established backdoor detection techniques — spectral signature analysis and activation clustering — into a fused detector for healthcare imaging models, motivated by sector-level concerns about model poisoning in clinical settings. It provides an implementation and evaluation on medical imaging benchmarks where such detection results are sparse.

entry.title: From matrix inversion to constraints: provably tighter confidence regions for importance weights in label shift

author.name: Mushan Li, Kihyun Han, Yanyuan Ma

entry.summary: This work reframes uncertainty quantification for importance weights in label-shift domain adaptation, moving from Gaussian-elimination-based inversion of interval-valued systems to a direct matrix constraint framework. It derives joint confidence regions and marginal intervals via linear programming that are provably tighter while retaining exact finite-sample validity. Tighter bounds should directly improve downstream domain adaptation under label shift.

entry.title: Graph Matching Relaxations and Amortization for Supervised Graph Prediction

author.name: Federico M\'endez, Paul Krzakala, Gabriel Melo, Charlotte Laclau, R\'emi Flamary, Florence d'Alch\'e-Buc

entry.summary: The paper studies optimal transport relaxations of the permutation-invariant loss needed for end-to-end supervised graph prediction, showing theoretically and empirically that Gromov-Wasserstein is most suitable. It then amortizes the matching step with a differentiable Sinkhorn-based parametric matcher, avoiding an inner optimization per training example.

entry.title: In the Blind: Building Pseudo-References for MT Evaluation

author.name: Diptesh Kanojia, Chi-kiu Lo, Archchana Sindhujan, Samuel Larkin, Greg Hanneman, Alon Lavie

entry.summary: This paper describes constructing pseudo-references for the WMT26 General MT task across language pairs with no human references: seven models translate 3,277 documents under multiple prompts, three reference-free QE models score candidates, and a per-document selector picks translations, with GPT-5.5 post-editing where needed. It also exposes a failure mode where QE metrics rank fluent output in the wrong language highly. Working reference-free at shared-task scale is a significant methodological milestone for MT evaluation.

entry.title: Learning to Refer from Estimated Listener Gaze

author.name: T\'ea Wright, Alane Suhr

entry.summary: The paper finetunes vision-language models to produce more pragmatically optimal referring expressions by converting estimated listener gaze scanpaths into token- and sequence-level rewards for policy optimization. A neural listener maps sampled referring expressions to simulated human fixation sequences, providing learning signal without needing real-time human feedback. This connects pragmatics, gaze modeling, and RL fine-tuning in referential communication.

entry.title: MedTRACE: Tool-Augmented Multimodal Clinical Reasoning Agents for Evidence-Grounded Decision-Making
