author.name: Ji Lu, Lifei Liu, Haoran Yu, Xianglong Wang, Yiru Fang, Kuo Yang, Huiran Duan, Jianping Gou

entry.summary: MedTRACE is a tool-augmented agent for multimodal clinical decision-making that builds a unified patient-state representation from EHRs, images, and physiological signals, then iterates hypothesis formation, tool-aware deliberation, and evidence verification. It dynamically invokes visual grounding, retrieval, and structured parsing tools to assess evidence sufficiency and diagnostic uncertainty rather than mapping inputs directly to diagnoses.

entry.title: RESKILL: Explicit Failure Attribution and Structured Repair for Interactive Language Agents

author.name: Mengyi Deng, Xin Li, Duyi Pan, Zilin Wang, Zhiwei Li, Zhijiang Guo, Wei Wang

entry.summary: RESKILL is a structured repair framework for skill-based language agents that maintains explicit repair state, links failure hypotheses to candidate skill patches via coverage-based attribution, and uses environment retest outcomes to guide iterative repair updates. This replaces opaque one-shot reflection with an accountable, feedback-driven repair loop. It addresses a key reliability bottleneck for agents that accumulate reusable skills.

entry.title: A Cross Community Agenda for Speech AI

author.name: Maria Teleki, Kimi Wenzel, Anna Seo Gyeong Choi, Tobias Weinberg, Shree Harsha Bokkahalli Satish, Stephanny Sanchez, Belu Ticona, Ariadna Sanchez, Yash Sonkar, Aarti Mathur, Christoph Minixhofer, Abraham Glasser, Raja Kushalnagar, James Caverlee, Minha Lee, Shaomei Wu, Alyssa Hillary Zisk, \'Eva Sz\'ekely, Dylan Gaines, Angelika Seeschaaf Veres, Seray Ibrahim, Nicholas Cummins, Allison Koenecke

entry.summary: This position paper, with a large interdisciplinary author list spanning NLP, HCI, and accessibility communities, critiques Speech AI for operating with incomplete models of communication and identity and for measuring the wrong constructs, using AAC (augmentative and alternative communication) as the highest-stakes case. It proposes a cross-community research agenda covering underserved speakers including people who stutter, multilingual speakers, and non-binary speakers. It aims to bridge technical and sociotechnical research communities.

entry.title: StepPrune: Adaptive Sequential Visual Token Selection across Multimodal Large Language Models

author.name: Hansen Zhang, Landi He, Mingde Yao, Lijian Xu

entry.summary: StepPrune formulates visual-token pruning in multimodal LLMs as an adaptive sequential decision process, progressively building the retained token subset conditioned on prior selections and textual context, with a learned STOP action determining per-sample budgets. This addresses the independence and uniform-budget assumptions of top-K pruning methods. A variance-preserving noise gate supports training. It targets inference efficiency where visual prefixes dominate per-layer computation.

entry.title: Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning of Foundation Models for Liver Tumor Segmentation in CT

author.name: Ramtin Mojtahedi, Mohammad Hamghalam, Jacob J. Peoples, Richard K. G. Do, Amber L. Simpson

entry.summary: The study benchmarks PEFT methods (LoRA, QLoRA, Conv-Adapter, and a novel DiSCo spectral adapter) on SAM for liver tumor segmentation in abdominal CT of colorectal liver metastases, training only adapters. DiSCo derives spectral bases from SVD of row-normalized weights with rank-gated coefficients and just 0.14M trainable parameters, evaluated across five prompting regimes.

entry.title: Vision-Language Models for Criterion-Level Grading of Handwritten Examinations in Outcome-Based Education

author.name: Md Khalid Syfullah, Asif Hasan Tonmoy, Saad Ahmed, S. M. Jahangir Alam

entry.summary: A thorough evaluation of vision-language models for criterion-level grading of handwritten exam answers, comparing 20 configurations of Qwen2.5-VL, InternVL3, Pixtral, Donut, and ensembles under zero-shot, few-shot, fine-tuning, and LoRA setups on 1982 records, with two independent faculty markers regrading all 291 test criteria. It assesses accuracy, human agreement, reliability, error concentration, and explanation quality.

entry.title: Learning from Reliable Negatives: Confidence-Anchored Test-Time Adaptation for GUI Grounding

author.name: Yizhou Liu, Fei Tang, Yuchen Yan, Zhengxi Lu, Songqin Nong, Tao Jiang, Wenhao Xu, Wenqi Zhang, Weiming Lu, Jun Xiao, Yongliang Shen

entry.summary: The paper introduces a label-free test-time training paradigm for GUI grounding based on two insights: coordinate-token confidence is a better reliability indicator than full-sequence confidence, and in sparse GUI coordinate spaces negative samples provide more reliable learning signals than noisy positives. Confidence-Anchored Learning filters pseudo-labels and exploits negatives to avoid costly annotation.

entry.title: When Do Learned Priors Help Visual Inertial Estimation? A Controlled Study of Prior Integration, Calibration, Initialization, and Backend Consistency

author.name: Jinchang Zhang, Guoyu Lu

entry.summary: This controlled study provides a framework for disentangling whether gains in learning-augmented visual-inertial estimation come from useful learned priors or from confounds like backend changes, calibration, and initialization. It evaluates four evidence layers using a MonoViT-based motion prior added as a factor to a geometric estimator.

entry.title: Learning Communication-Conditioned Generative Policies for Decentralized Multi-Agent Collision Avoidance

author.name: Prajwal Koirala, Mark Campbell

entry.summary: This work trains a flow-matching policy for decentralized multi-agent collision avoidance where agents generate action sequences conditioned on latent messages learned from privileged offline demonstrations that contained no explicit communication. Agents thus learn to exchange and aggregate interaction-relevant intent, supporting both independent and coordinated behavior at test time.

entry.title: Primitive-Informed Sampling-Based MPC for Multi-Fingered Dexterous Manipulation

author.name: Emek Bar{\i}\c{s} K\"u\c{c}\"uktabak, Karankumar Patel, Jinda Cui, Zhaodong Yang, Kazuhiro Sasabuchi, Jun Takamatsu

entry.summary: The paper proposes biasing sampling-based MPC for multi-fingered manipulation using low-dimensional manipulation primitives encoding coordinated finger motions, while optimizing joint-level residuals to adapt to the current hand-object configuration. Task-related rollout constraints reject infeasible trajectories during forward simulation, improving sampling efficiency. This addresses the inefficiency of direct high-dimensional joint-space exploration in contact-rich manipulation.

entry.title: Governing at Machine Speed: An Adaptive Intelligence Architecture for Real-Time AI Policy Enforcement

author.name: Sandeep Bokkasam, B. Durgalakshmi

entry.summary: This paper addresses the gap between rapid enterprise AI adoption and the ability to govern it, introducing the concept of an attestation deficit: organizations have policies but cannot generate auditable, tamper-evident proof of enforcement within regulatory deadlines. It grounds the problem in recent empirical data on AI incidents, breach costs, and monitoring coverage gaps, and proposes an adaptive intelligence architecture for real-time, verifiable AI policy enforcement.

entry.title: Safety as a Constraint: Fine-Tuning a LLM Recommender to Explain Itself

author.name: Jiashu He, Emma Yanyang Kong, JJ Tan, David Fagnan

entry.summary: Trains a recommender LLM to generate personalized explanations grounded in a user's watching history at a large video streaming service, avoiding costly frontier-model calls in the production pipeline. The work imposes faithfulness and safety constraints on generated explanations, addressing why an item is recommended rather than only what will be recommended. Relevant to industry practitioners deploying explainable recommendation at scale.

entry.title: Safety Signals to Verify NetOps Agents with Action-Level Granularity

author.name: Tobias Labarta, Frederik Pahde, Novak Boskov, Maximilian Dreyer, David Birkenberger, Manzoor Ahmed Khan, Sebastian Lapuschkin, Wojciech Samek

entry.summary: The paper builds action-level ground truth for network repair agents in datacenter fabrics, enabling agents to abstain from high-risk actions by knowing per-action impact before execution. It addresses a gap in NetOps benchmarks, which lack per-action safety labels needed for long-horizon reliability of autonomous control loops. From a credible industrial research group (incl. Lapuschkin, Samek), it contributes to safe agentic deployment.

entry.title: VisInteract: Towards Dynamic Interactive Text-to-Visualization under Imperfect Queries

author.name: Wenxin Xu, Jinwei Lu, Hwanhee Kim, Chen Jason Zhang, Xiao-Yong Wei, Haoyang Li, Yuanfeng Song

entry.summary: VisInteract reframes text-to-visualization as interaction-driven intent recovery, introducing the first benchmark for dynamic, multi-turn Text-to-Vis with controlled imperfection injection and a leakage-controlled user agent providing realistic feedback. Existing systems assume well-specified queries and generate charts in one pass, which fails on ambiguous or incorrect real-world requests. The dual-perspective evaluation covers both code and chart quality.

entry.title: Reason What Matters: Retrieval-Grounded Reasoning for Universal Multimodal Embeddings

author.name: Mingzhou Jiang, Peixi Wu, Hang Cheng, Yunhao Zhou, Biao Yang, Wei Yuan, Yun Li, Fan Yang, Wenwu Ou, Honghui He

entry.summary: This paper improves universal multimodal embeddings by identifying two limitations of GRPO-based Chain-of-Thought training: uniform advantage assignment across all CoT tokens, and latency from generating complete reasoning traces before embedding. The proposed method grounds reasoning in input-supported evidence and stops reasoning once sufficient retrieval evidence is available. This targets corpus-scale deployment of multimodal retrieval models.

entry.title: RSIAgent: Autonomous Exploration for Recursive Self-improvement in New Environments

author.name: Sibo Zhu, Shicheng Fan, Xinyue Wang, Wenyi Wu, Kun Zhou, Biwei Huang

entry.summary: RSIAgent is a training-free multi-agent framework in which curriculum, actor, and verifier agents autonomously explore new environments, validate outcomes, and build memory of reusable causal relationships between actions, conditions, and consequences. A broad-then-deep exploration strategy combines parallel broad exploration with focused deep exploration for hard cases. This targets agent adaptation to environments not covered by pretraining.

entry.title: HISPO: Hierarchical Importance-Sampling Policy Optimization with Entropy-Derived Segments

author.name: Quoc-Vinh Lai-Dang, Hyo-Sang Shin

entry.summary: HISPO addresses the credit-assignment problem in RLVR for long-form mathematical reasoning by constructing entropy-derived contiguous segments at rollout time and assigning soft entropy-based saliency weights, sitting between token-level (GRPO, DAPO) and sequence-level (GSPO) importance-sampling granularities. This segment-level policy optimization aims to better handle unevenly contributing solution traces. It is positioned within the current wave of verifiable-reward RL methods.

entry.title: GRIN+: Towards Fast Yet Effective Machine Unlearning for Imbalanced Medical Data

author.name: Minghui Huang, Junxiao Wang

entry.summary: This paper addresses machine unlearning for medical models subject to GDPR and HIPAA right-to-be-forgotten requirements, focusing on the privacy-efficiency-utility trilemma under severe class imbalance and long-tailed data distributions. The proposed GRIN+ method aims to remove sensitive patient data without deleting features essential for diagnosing rare conditions, which majority-class gradient dominance typically endangers.

entry.title: Navigating Sparse Evidence: Agentic Visual RAG via Explicit Context Selection and Consolidation

author.name: Yucheng Shen, Lingyong Yan, Jiulong Wu, Shuaiqiang Wang, Jianmin WU, Dawei Yin, Min Cao

entry.summary: The paper targets the bottleneck in visual retrieval-augmented generation where answer-relevant evidence is sparse within or across document pages and agentic answers rely on noisy exploration trajectories. It proposes explicit context selection and consolidation of supporting images, giving clearer evidence-backed reasoning traces for visually rich document QA.

entry.title: Natural-Language to SysMLv2 Translation via Conformance-Driven Iterative Refinement

author.name: Chance LaVoie, Eladio Andujar Lugo, Taylan G. Topcu, Levent Burak Kara

entry.summary: The authors present a generate-check-repair loop that translates natural-language system requirements into SysMLv2 models, using an industrial conformance checker rather than mere grammar validity as the acceptance criterion. This addresses a practical gap in model-based systems engineering where generated models must be accepted by real modeling tools. It matters because formal model generation is a key industrial LLM application.

entry.title: BEACON: Behavior and Appearance Control for Subject-Specific Video Generation

author.name: Pokrzywa Baptiste, Nabyl Quignon, Yara Bahram, Muhammad Osama Zeeshan, Antitza Dantcheva, Eric Granger

entry.summary: BEACON is a lightweight framework for person-specific video generation that disentangles visual identity from temporal expressive behavior, addressing the limitation of single-reference-image methods that preserve appearance but produce weakly subject-specific facial expressions. By conditioning on behavior dynamics, it yields more expressive and faithful subject videos. It is a solid advance in controllable human-centric video generation.

entry.title: Chance-Constrained Belief-Space Maneuver Planning for Autonomous Collision Avoidance Under Uncertainty

author.name: Grace Ra Kim, Duncan Eddy, Mykel J. Kochenderfer

entry.summary: This work formulates spacecraft conjunction assessment as a belief-space planning problem, using chance-constrained Monte Carlo tree search over Gaussian state beliefs to reason about future tracking updates before closest approach. It addresses both whether an encounter requires mitigation and whether enough information exists to commit to a maneuver.

entry.title: Generative Interpretability via Scalable Neuro-Symbolic Models

author.name: Xiaocong Yang

entry.summary: This single-author position paper argues that post-hoc interpretability is structurally inadequate for agentic LLM systems whose outputs are irreversible actions, and advocates generative interpretability: architectures whose inference passes natively expose human-understandable, causally intervenable checkpoints. It compares generative interpretability favorably against the post-hoc paradigm, appealing to scalable neuro-symbolic models.

entry.title: Gap Entropy and Almost Instance-Wise Optimal Best-Arm Identification

author.name: Jiarui Yao, Jiaxi Zhao, Xiangxin Zhou

entry.summary: The paper resolves a 2016 conjecture by Chen and Li, proving that the instance-wise sample complexity of best-arm identification with Gaussian arms is characterized by gap entropy up to an additive term from the two-arm problem. This establishes an almost instance-wise optimal characterization of pure-exploration bandit complexity. A theoretical contribution settling a decade-old open question.

entry.title: Graph-Transformer Fraud Detection with Self-Supervised Pretraining and Conformal Risk Control

author.name: Sergei, Komarov

entry.summary: GTFD fuses graph attention over corporate payment networks with a gated transformer over transaction sequences via cross-modal gating, and adds a conformal risk-control head producing threshold-free anomaly scores with finite-sample coverage guarantees. Training uses self-supervised link-mask pretraining with adversarial components.

entry.title: NeuroActiSep: Detecting Factual Hallucinations from Feed-Forward Neurons in a Single Pass

author.name: Ali Derogar Odolou, Reza Nazari, Mostafa Salehi

entry.summary: NeuroActiSep identifies feed-forward neurons correlated with hallucination by ranking them at the final prompt token, then transfers selected neuron identities to train hallucination classifiers on other factual QA datasets. Probes on selected-neuron features perform on par with probes on full internal states, enabling single-pass detection.

entry.title: Diagnosing Temporal Misalignment in Multichannel Time-Series Classification with Minimum Description Length

author.name: Sebastian Buschj\"ager, Michael Frichert, Daniel Kuhe, Jian-Jia Chen

entry.summary: The authors introduce a classifier- and label-free diagnostic that detects temporal misalignment between sensor channels by applying candidate shifts and measuring codelength changes under minimum description length encoding. Increased codelength after a shift indicates destruction of shared structure, revealing synchronization problems that would otherwise silently degrade classifiers. This is a practical tool since existing synchronization fixes are hardware-specific and rarely applicable retroactively.

entry.title: OCT-FedSIR: Toward Trustworthy Federated Ophthalmic Learning under Annotation Noise

author.name: Sina Gholami, Abdulmoneam Ali, Tania Haghighi, Rashadul H. Badhon, Behafarin Emam, Sally S. Y. Ong, Atalie C. Thompson, Theodore Leng, Ahmed Arafa, Jennifer I. Lim, Minhaj Nur Alam

entry.summary: OCT-FedSIR is a reliability-aware spectral framework for federated OCT classification that handles client-dependent annotation noise and heterogeneous data distributions, combining class-balanced spectral estimation, logit adjustment, selective relabeling, and noise-aware federated optimization. It was evaluated across multiple real institutional datasets including Kermany and University of Illinois Chicago data. The work addresses a realistic barrier to multi-site medical AI collaboration.

entry.title: A Responsive Present, a Shared Past, a Social Other: Teens' Overreliance on Companion AI Chatbots

author.name: Mohammad Namvarpour (Matt), Tyler Chang, Afsaneh Razi

entry.summary: A large-scale thematic analysis of 17,053 verified quotations from 3,930 teen-relevant Reddit posts examining how teenagers rely on AI companion chatbots. The study identifies 53 topics across seven thematic groups, covering benefits like comfort and identity exploration alongside risks such as problematic attachment, social substitution, and disrupted academics. It matters for AI safety and youth well-being policy as companion AI adoption grows.

entry.title: When Correlations Mislead: Confounder-Aware Multi-View Urban Region Representation Learning

author.name: Sean Bin Yang, Ying Sun, Zongyi Xu, Tung Kieu, Jilin Hu, Bin Yang, Kristian Torp, Hua Lu, Torben Bach Pedersen

entry.summary: This paper introduces CURE, a confounder-aware framework for urban region representation learning that combines heterogeneous data sources like mobility flows, points of interest, and land-use information. Unlike prior multi-view methods that only strengthen cross-view interactions, CURE explicitly models view-specific regional structures and mitigates spurious correlations induced by shared latent factors. The goal is more stable downstream predictions for tasks such as public safety forecasting and service demand estimation.

entry.title: CodeTS: Verifiable Text-to-Time Series Generation via Executable Code

author.name: Xudong Yuan, Shunyu Liu, Tongya Zheng, Huiping Zhuang, Mingli Song, Kaixuan Chen

entry.summary: This paper introduces CodeTS, a framework that reformulates text-to-time-series generation as a two-step Text-to-Code-to-TS process, where natural language descriptions are first translated into executable code that explicitly encodes the desired temporal patterns. Using code as an intermediate, verifiable interface addresses the lack of an explicit generation-logic mechanism in prior methods. This matters because synthetic time-series data is increasingly valuable when real observations are scarce, and verifiability improves trustworthiness of generated data.

entry.title: Automating Attack Graph Construction for Agentic Pentesting. Towards Neuro-Symbolic Vulnerability Hunting

author.name: Oliver Stevanovic, Jasmin Wachter

entry.summary: This paper presents a semi-automated pipeline translating scanner findings from Trivy, Semgrep, and Nmap into MulVAL predicates, using an LLM-assisted process to build domain-specific Datalog rules that link detectable evidence to attack techniques. MulVAL/XSB then performs symbolic inference to generate auditable logic attack graphs for agentic penetration testing. A web-security case study demonstrates feasibility of this neuro-symbolic approach to vulnerability hunting.

entry.title: Multi-View Molecular Representation Learning with Hierarchical Graphs and Contextualized Fingerprints

author.name: Gwang-Hyeon Yun, Jong-Hoon Park, Bing Hu, Helen Chen, Anita Layton, Young-Rae Cho

entry.summary: HiFi-Mol is a multi-view molecular pretraining framework that separately trains a hierarchical graph encoder with fragment-aware masking and a contextualized fingerprint encoder, then integrates them for property prediction. It aims to generalize from limited labels to structurally novel compounds by combining topological and chemical-pattern views.

entry.title: SPICE: Simple Polysemantic Feature Interpretation via Clustering-based Explanation

author.name: Sehyun Lee, Dahee Kwon, Damin Lee, Jaesik Choi

entry.summary: SPICE is a generalizable framework for analyzing polysemanticity, where single neurons respond to multiple unrelated concepts, avoiding architecture-specific assumptions and manual choices like a fixed number of concept clusters. It applies clustering-based explanation to deep vision architectures, improving generality and scalability relative to prior interpretability heuristics. Polysemanticity is central to mechanistic interpretability, so automated analysis tools are valuable.

entry.title: When Compliance Data Masquerades as Evaluation: Measurement Validity for Deployed AI Systems

author.name: Hung-Yu Lin, Xingran Huang, Qiming Guo, Jinwen Tang

entry.summary: This position paper argues that operational and compliance data, such as autonomous-vehicle disengagement and crash reports, are frequently misinterpreted as valid comparative evaluation despite differences in reporting scope, exposure, and comparator construction. It frames this as a general measurement-validity problem for deployed AI evaluation.

entry.title: Optimal Transport for Efficient, Unsupervised Anomaly Detection on Industrial Data

author.name: Abigail Langbridge, Fearghal O'Donncha, James T Rayfield, Bradley Eck

entry.summary: Presents an Optimal Transport-based anomaly detection framework for industrial time-series sensor data that requires no labels or minimal user input and adapts in real time. The method includes counterfactual explanations for auditability and shows robustness to noise, fluctuations, and data gaps.

entry.title: Nonparametric Variance-Penalized Actor-Critic: Statistical Inference for Risk-Sensitive Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Saunak Kumar Panda, Tong Li, Yisha Xiang, Ruiqi Liu

entry.summary: Proposes a variance-penalized actor-critic framework that replaces a dedicated second variance critic with statistically grounded online estimators based on bootstrapping and random scaling, keeping a single-critic architecture. The approach reduces architectural complexity and estimation-error compounding in risk-sensitive RL.

entry.title: Pathwise Individual Rationality in Federated Learning: A Mechanism-Architecture Co-Design

author.name: Amin Meghrazi, Srinivasan Parthasarathy, Andrew Perrault

entry.summary: This work studies individual rationality in federated learning, requiring that each client receive utility no worse than local training, and shows that along training paths clients can remain below their local baseline for hundreds of rounds. The authors propose capping per-round utility changes as a mechanism-architecture co-design remedy. It matters because it addresses a practical adoption barrier: rational clients may rationally defect before federation benefits materialize.

entry.title: $\mathbb{SL}(n)$ Representation Learning: An Intrinsic Mixed-Curvature Space with Higher Curvature Capacities and Deeper Order-Aware Composition

author.name: Xingrun Li, Yusuke Mukuta, Xin Yang, Yinyu Ye, Tatsuya Harada

entry.summary: This paper introduces the special linear group SL(n) as a representation geometry for mixed-curvature learning, defined by a determinant-one constraint with a Schatten-p Finsler structure. Unlike product manifolds, it intrinsically exhibits negative, zero, and positive curvature without manually specified curvature combinations. This offers a principled new geometric substrate for embedding structured data.

entry.title: Draining Fictitious Knots: Restoring Distance-Awareness Guarantees for High-Dimensional Spline Networks

author.name: Masoud Ataei, Mohammad Javad Khojasteh, Vikas Dhiman

entry.summary: This paper addresses a weakness in DAREK, a method for uncertainty quantification on Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks (KANs) with spline activations. In high-dimensional settings, DAREK's componentwise formulation can produce fictitious knots in the combined input space that do not correspond to actual training data, undermining its distance-aware error bounds. The authors propose a fix to restore the theoretical guarantees of the uncertainty estimates.

entry.title: Same path, different: a mechanistic comparison of looped and stacked transformer encoders on 12-lead ECG

author.name: Pawel Olszowiec, Michal Byra, Grzegorz Gruszczynski, Grzegorz Stefanski, Alberto Presta

entry.summary: This controlled study trains a weight-tied looped ViT (bViT) and a standard ViT on 12-lead ECG classification under identical protocols. Despite an 8.9x parameter reduction, bViT matches ViT accuracy, and geometric similarity metrics show the architectures build comparable representations while differing in representational dynamics.

entry.title: The Limits of Reference-Free Speech Quality Metrics as Evaluators and Rewards on Modern Text-to-Speech

author.name: Antonis Asonitis, Juan Pablo Zuluaga Gomez, Francesco Verdini, Aref Farhadipour, Marzieh Razavi, Pierre-Edouard Honnet, Vijeta Avijeet

entry.summary: This evaluation study tests whether reference-free speech quality predictors (UTMOS, DNSMOS, SCOREQ) track human preference in pairwise comparisons across six human-rated TTS corpora, including their role as reward signals for preference optimization. The finding is that predictors agree with listeners when one clip has audible defects, but none reliably distinguishes two clean clips. This is an important caution for TTS evaluation and for reward-model pipelines built on these metrics.

entry.title: GzDRL: Reproducible and Scalable Deep Reinforcement Learning with Gazebo

author.name: Amal Dev Haridevan, Junjie Kang, Jinjun Shan

entry.summary: GzDRL is a single-process reinforcement learning framework for the Gazebo robotics simulator that replaces middleware-based integration with a direct environment-stepping mechanism synchronizing agent actions and physics updates. This yields deterministic, reproducible, high-throughput RL training and evaluation, achieving the best workstation throughput among evaluated frameworks.

entry.title: Large-scale bioacoustic detection using semantic segmentation: a deep learning framework applied to fin whale calls in ocean-bottom seismometer recordings

author.name: Jocelyn Japnanto, Alex A. Saoulis, Miriam Romagosa, Rita Leit\~ao, Gabrielle Arrieta, M\'onica A. Silva, Matthew Graham, Ana M. G. Ferreira

entry.summary: This paper presents a deep learning semantic segmentation framework that detects 20-Hz fin whale calls in spectrograms from ocean-bottom seismometers (OBS), devices originally deployed for geophysical monitoring that passively record low-frequency ocean sound for months to years. The model assigns per-pixel call probabilities and converts these into time-frequency bounding boxes for individual detections, enabling automated monitoring across large, heterogeneous sensor networks. This repurposes existing geophysical infrastructure into a valuable tool for whale conservation and passive acoustic monitoring at scale.

entry.title: Beyond Point Forecasts: A Survey on Probabilistic Forecasting for Time Series and Spatiotemporal Data

author.name: Donia Besher, Rajdeep Pathak, Madhurima Panja, Tanujit Chakraborty

entry.summary: This survey unifies the fragmented probabilistic forecasting landscape by organizing methods according to where and how uncertainty enters the forecasting pipeline, connecting model-agnostic ensembling and calibration with Bayesian, parametric, distributional, and generative approaches. It also examines the emerging role of time series foundation models in probabilistic prediction.

entry.title: Not All Duplicates Are Coordination: Generic vs. Non-Generic Duplicate Campaigns in Information Operations

author.name: Ashfaq Ali Shafin, Khandaker Mamun Ahmed

entry.summary: This paper analyzes 187,000 tweets from six Russian information operations datasets to distinguish generic, low-information duplicate content from genuinely coordinating duplicate campaigns. It introduces an LLM-assisted labeling protocol with human validation, trains classifiers over sentence embeddings, and shows that filtering generic duplicates reduces noise in coordination graphs. This matters for improving the rigor of influence-operation detection research.

entry.title: Bridging the Synthetic-to-Real Gap for Few-Shot Cryo-ET Classification

author.name: Siddhant Bharadwaj, Ashish Vashist, Rashi Singh, Pranav Vinodh, Nishanth Artham, Runmin Jiang, Xingjian Li, Min Xu

entry.summary: This paper addresses subtomogram classification in cryo-electron tomography, where labeled data is scarce and synthetic training data suffers from a large domain gap. The authors propose a synthetic-to-real adaptation framework with a learnable transformation module that closes the gap at both input and feature levels, outperforming transfer learning baselines in few-shot settings. This matters because cryo-ET is central to structural biology, and reducing annotation requirements could accelerate discoveries in molecular imaging.

entry.title: Riemannian ascent--descent for nonconvex nonconcave minimax landscapes: convergence to basin saddle points and applications to distributionally robust optimization

author.name: Rishabh Dixit, Pranav Upadrashta, Alex Cloninger

entry.summary: This theory paper studies distributionally robust optimization formulated as minimax over a product of Euclidean space and a Riemannian manifold, introducing the notion of a basin saddle point as a local Nash equilibrium. It develops a convergence framework for Riemannian gradient ascent multistep descent to such points under a local Lojasiewicz-type condition. This provides one of the first convergence guarantees for nonconvex nonconcave minimax on mixed Euclidean-Riemannian domains.

entry.title: Towards Anticipatory Databases Through Shared Data and Workload Semantics

author.name: Farzaneh Zirak, Kasper Overgaard Mortensen, Farhana Choudhury, Renata Borovica-Gajic

entry.summary: This position/framework paper argues that database systems should use workload semantics — what queries are examining and how analytical focus evolves — as a first-class control signal for anticipatory decisions, rather than relying only on recency, frequency, and locality. It introduces concepts of semantic locality and semantic trajectories, with a framework modeling semantic context at data, query, and session levels over time.

entry.title: Geometric Signatures of Conceptual Reorganization: A Counterfactual Embedding Framework for Detecting Scientific Revolutions

author.name: Dimitris Ntounis, Ariel Schwartzman, Chris Chafe, Thomas A. Ryckman

entry.summary: The authors use the geometry of document embeddings as a quantitative observable of conceptual reorganization, measuring how removing documents about a concept perturbs the embedding space before and after its historical emergence. They validate the framework on five case studies including special relativity, Godel's theorems, the Higgs mechanism, deep learning, and attention.

entry.title: MAST: Label-Efficient, Robust, and Generalizable Sound Detection for Biodiversity Monitoring via Masked Audio Pretraining and Self-Training

author.name: Tianyi Xu, Daniel Pimentel-Alarc\'on, Zuzana Bu\v{r}ivalov\'a, Claudia Sol\'is-Lemus

entry.summary: This arXiv paper presents MAST, a label-efficient framework for detecting animal vocalizations in passive acoustic monitoring recordings. It combines a ViT-based encoder pretrained via masked audio reconstruction with a lightweight mel-spectrogram detector, adds a box-level contrastive loss to separate animal sounds from background noise, and applies iterative self-training on unlabeled audio to improve robustness. The work addresses a practical bottleneck in biodiversity monitoring where time-frequency annotation is expensive and site-specific.

entry.title: Strong and Compact Policies for Submodular Markov Decision Processes via LP-Based Submodular Orienteering

author.name: Lars Rohwedder, Rico Zenklusen

entry.summary: This paper studies MDPs with monotone submodular reward functions over a finite horizon, generalizing standard additive rewards. The authors connect the problem to Submodular Orienteering and derive strong, compact policy guarantees via LP-based techniques. This matters because submodular rewards capture coverage, influence, and diminishing-returns applications that additive models miss.

entry.title: Measuring the Cost of Variety Conflation in Multilingual MT Evaluation: Adding Mozambican Xichangana, Nyanja and Sena to FLORES+

author.name: Felermino D. M. A. Ali, Delfina L\'azaro Mateus, Manuel Valente Mangue

entry.summary: The paper extends FLORES+ with Portuguese-source test sets for three Mozambican Bantu varieties and shows that conflating them with regional standards (Tsonga, Chichewa) substantially distorts MT evaluation, e.g. 13-15 spBLEU drops from reference swaps alone. Variant-aware fine-tuning of NLLB reverses the pattern on target varieties. This documents a concrete, quantified cost of treating related language varieties as interchangeable.

entry.title: The Garden of Forking Prompts: How Users Explore Narrative Space in Story Generation

author.name: Advait Deshmukh, Nora Benedict, Melanie Walsh, Maria Antoniak

entry.summary: Studying naturally occurring chatbot logs, this work shows users iteratively revise story prompts to explore narrative possibilities, and that static one-shot benchmarks fail to capture this exploratory behavior. The authors construct WildStories, a dataset of 275,635 story generation prompts labeled with revision relationships. This offers a new lens on creative preference and evaluation design.

entry.title: SlopShape: Identifying AI-Generated Commercial Web Content

author.name: Jochen Madler (Sitefire)

entry.summary: SlopShape detects AI-generated commercial web content using 214 structural features, such as how information is ordered and voiced, rather than word-level statistics, replicating prior fiction-detection findings on commercial text. It compares 2,250 pre-ChatGPT human blog posts against 11,250 AI mirrors from five frontier models, validated with human gold annotations. This addresses the brittleness of word-level detectors under rewording, a growing concern for web quality and information integrity.

entry.title: TF-IDF and BM25 Are Exact KL Divergences

author.name: Ivan Silajev

entry.summary: This paper provides an exact probabilistic derivation showing that TF-IDF and the practically used variant of BM25 are Kullback-Leibler divergences between two probability models. This gives the two most widely used IR scoring functions a unified theoretical basis for the first time. The result clarifies what these scores measure and enables principled theoretical comparison with other retrieval methods.

entry.title: Structure-Token Evidence-Anchored Reasoning for Scientific Chart Understanding

author.name: Alberlucia Rafael Soarez, Camila Ferreira, Daniel Kim, Mariana Costa, Alejandro Torres

entry.summary: STEER improves vision-language model chart understanding by adding a chart structure graph encoder, evidence-anchored reasoning that requires each arithmetic step to cite a graph node, and weak-parser strong-reasoner alignment for node attributes, built on a frozen Llama-3.2-Vision encoder. This addresses the common failure where models hallucinate plausible numbers without actually reading the chart coordinate frame. It targets a real, well-documented weakness in multimodal scientific reasoning.

entry.title: Beyond OCR Accuracy: Text-Centric VQA Under Image Degradation with Modular and End-to-End

author.name: Ritali Vatsi, Rachapudi Jagadeesh, Shruti Singh Baghel, Himani Sharma, Amit Shukla, Pawan Goyal

entry.summary: An empirical study comparing modular OCR-based pipelines against an end-to-end vision-language baseline (SA-DBNet, a detector combining ResNet-18 with self-attention and deformable convolutions) for text-centric VQA on degraded images. The evaluation covers 4013 degraded images with 7000 QA pairs under real-world corruptions like blur and compression artifacts.

entry.title: From Density to Biopsy Decisions and Malignancy Prediction: A Benchmark Study of Multimodal Large Language Models Against Radiologists in Digital and Contrast-Enhanced Mammography

author.name: Ali Abbasian Ardakani, Afshin Mohammadi, Taha Yusuf Kuzan, Beyza Nur Kuzan, Alisa Mohebbi, Masume Behruzi, Hamid Khorshidi, Ashkan Ghorbani, Elham Asadiara, Zeinab Khorshidi Lotfi, Ansar Rahman, Nedim Christoph Beste, U. Rajendra Acharya, Sepideh Hatamikia

entry.summary: This clinical benchmark compares four existing multimodal LLMs (ChatGPT-5.2, Gemini-3.1 Pro, Sonnet-4.6, Muse Spark) against three radiologists of varying expertise on breast density assessment, BI-RADS, biopsy candidacy, and malignancy estimation across 179 paired DM/CEM exams. Radiologists exceeded most MLLM accuracies for binary density classification, with image masks adding limited benefit.

entry.title: Closed-form Bayesian homography estimation from noisy point correspondences

author.name: Hanne Beuter, Sebastian Dorn

entry.summary: The paper presents a fast, closed-form Bayesian formulation for homography estimation from noisy point correspondences that incorporates measurement uncertainty and priors, yielding a posterior distribution over homography parameters rather than a point estimate. This supports uncertainty propagation into calibration and 3D reconstruction in safety-critical applications.

entry.title: Diffusion Trajectory Modeling for Semantic Correspondence

author.name: Yusung Choi

entry.summary: The paper shows that intermediate feature maps along the diffusion generative process form meaningful trajectories over timesteps, with patch representations progressively encoding semantics that static snapshots miss. It exploits these trajectories for semantic correspondence, going beyond prior work that uses a single timestep or simple aggregation of features.

entry.title: Physical Kernel: Structured Visual Latents for Dark Manipulation

author.name: Jinting Hang, Hong Li, Zhenhui Cai, Zhihao Zhao, Jian He

entry.summary: The paper studies dark manipulation, where a single brief lit encoding of the scene is captured and then contact-rich skills are executed entirely from latent dynamics without further pixels. On ManiSkill StackCube this open-loop dark policy reaches 68.1% stacking versus 35.6% for per-step lit re-encoding and 0% for frozen encodings, and it is robust to appearance shifts occurring after the write but brittle to shifts at write time.

entry.title: From Vision to Harvest: Benchmarking Vision-Language Models for Multi-Arm Robotic Fruit Harvesting

author.name: Vrishan Inukollu, Adyan Zaman, Anvi Kudaraya, Carlos Lazcano, Yuankai Zhu, Stavros Vougioukas, Xiaofan Yu

entry.summary: This paper introduces the first benchmark for evaluating pretrained vision-language models on zero-shot planning for multi-arm robotic fruit harvesting, using real-world apple and citrus orchard imagery. It compares a VLM-based planning pipeline against traditional perception approaches, addressing generalization and coordination challenges in agricultural robotics.

entry.title: How to Better Train VLAs: Lessons Learned From the REAL-I Challenge at ICRA 2026

author.name: Jiaming Wang, Jizhuo Chen, Diwen Liu, Wang Song, Qiang Wang, Jie Ren, Chao Fu, Dingkun Zhu, Minchi Ruan, Hongtong Li, Yuhua Jiang, Zhiwei Xue, Yongping Pan, Harold Soh

entry.summary: This paper reports on the REAL-I Challenge at ICRA 2026, which compared approaches for training vision-language-action models on a fixed demonstration budget using a shared dual-arm humanoid platform. Top teams combined pretrained VLAs with task-specific imitation, and the write-up distills lessons on data curation, staged adaptation, and action-space design.

entry.title: An Adaptive Fixed-Time Line-of-Sight Guidance Scheme for 3D Path Following of Underwater Vehicles: Theory and Experiment

author.name: Hanzhi Yang, Jalil Chavez-Galaviz, Nina Mahmoudian

entry.summary: The authors develop a fixed-time adaptive line-of-sight guidance framework for 3D path tracking of AUVs, guaranteeing convergence within a preset time independent of initial conditions, unlike asymptotic LOS methods. Notably, it does not require modifying the underlying vehicle controller, making it deployable on commercial platforms, and it includes both theory and experimental validation. This addresses slow disturbance recovery in real marine environments.

entry.title: C$^2$Nav: Compare Before You Commit for Zero-Shot Vision-and-Language Navigation

author.name: Runtian Zheng, Congpeng Zhang, Ying Liu

entry.summary: C2Nav proposes a training-free zero-shot VLN-CE interface where the VLM compares controller-constructed alternatives rather than emitting waypoints, headings, or irreversible arrival decisions, keeping geometry and execution on the robot side. Three coordinated faculties implement ordinal gaze election over vetted candidate views and other comparison-based decisions. This reframing aims to decouple generative VLM outputs from geometric magnitude and commitment.

entry.title: PredTac: Learning Contact-Rich Manipulation with Predicted Touch

author.name: Weijia Fan, Daqiang Guo

entry.summary: PredTac learns to predict tactile states from causal visual observations and robot states, then uses this predicted touch as an explicit interface for policy learning and execution, avoiding physical tactile sensors entirely. This removes hardware, calibration, and synchronization costs that typically complicate contact-rich manipulation deployment. Evaluation spans three contact-rich manipulation tasks.

entry.title: Beyond Single-Axis Testing: Paired Evaluation of Compound Robustness in Vision-Language-Action Policies

author.name: Hiroki Sawada, Shunichi Kasahara

entry.summary: This paper introduces LIBERO-CTRL, a six-axis benchmark for evaluating vision-language-action (VLA) robot policies under compound distribution shifts, pairing each initial state across single-axis and matched simultaneous perturbation conditions. It shows that aggregate success rates can mask two opposing phenomena: emergent failures (all single-axis runs succeed but the combined one fails) and compensation effects, demonstrating that compound robustness cannot be reliably inferred from single-axis evaluations.

entry.title: TimeThink: Eliciting Compositional Reasoning in Timeseries Large Language Models

author.name: Sudarshan Regmi, Arvind Pillai, Yu Yvonne Wu, Yuliang Chen, Bibek Panthi, Tess Z. Griffin, Michael V. Heinz, Lisa Marsch, Nicholas C. Jacobson, Andrew Campbell

entry.summary: Introduces TimeThink, a synthetic framework for eliciting compositional reasoning in timeseries multimodal LLMs, targeting the failure of existing models to explain dynamic temporal patterns in high-stakes settings like healthcare. It decomposes timeseries primitives to enable compositional question answering that generalizes out of distribution, addressing limits of RL-trained timeseries models on narrow data.

entry.title: Surprising Effectiveness of Self-Demonstrations in Enhancing Schema-Ontology Mapping with LLMs

author.name: Siddhesh Thombre, Manasi Patwardhan, Sunita Sarawagi

entry.summary: Shows that directly applying LLMs via one-shot prompting or naive multi-stage pipelines performs poorly on schema-ontology mapping for enterprise databases, and proposes a self-demonstration-driven approach combining neuro-symbolic task decomposition with automatically generated pattern-guided, dependency-aware demonstrations. Addresses semantic heterogeneity, cryptic naming, and the schema-to-ontology abstraction gap. Notable result for enterprise knowledge integration.

entry.title: AcquireBound: Runtime Authorization for Resources Acquired by AI Agents

author.name: Genliang Zhu

entry.summary: AcquireBound addresses the post-fulfillment activation gap: agents acquiring compute, credentials, accounts, services, or other agents introduce new authority that existing payment, OAuth, and budget checks do not gate. It proposes a provenance-bounded runtime authorization architecture that quarantines acquired outputs, resolves their capabilities from authenticated provider evidence, and activates them only via checked activation transactions. A well-timed contribution to agentic security.

entry.title: Domain Generalization for Smartphone-Based Human Activity Recognition: A Systematic Analysis of Components and Interactions

author.name: Ot\'avio Oliveira Napoli, Edson Borin

entry.summary: The authors run a massive controlled benchmark of over 410,000 experiments across four architectures and thirteen training objectives to systematically evaluate domain generalization methods for smartphone HAR under distribution shifts. Unlike prior work evaluating components in isolation, the study quantifies interactions between training objectives, initialization, and architectural choices across pipeline stages.

entry.title: AlgoEvo: Self-Evolving Agentic Search for Automated Algorithm Discovery

author.name: Junhao Qiu, Qinglong Hu, Xialiang Tong, Mingxuan Yuan, Liyong Lin, Qingfu Zhang

entry.summary: AlgoEvo is an agentic framework for automated algorithm discovery in which an agent dynamically inspects, diagnoses, and edits code from runtime feedback rather than following rigid pre-defined search pipelines. A design skill hub decouples paradigm-specific knowledge from the discovery engine, letting one workflow handle single-objective, multi-objective, and multi-component design problems.

entry.title: One Spectrum, Two Resources: Data-Memory Scaling in Autoregressive Prediction

author.name: Chiwun Yang, Xiaoyu Li

entry.summary: This theory paper proves a minimax law unifying data and learned-memory scaling in autoregressive prediction via a single predictive-energy spectrum: data set the resolution 1/n while memory sets the level reached by optimal bit allocation over at most 2^B states. The result characterizes how much learned memory is needed to benefit from additional data.

entry.title: TyPatch: Transforming Patches into Typestate Rules for Kernel Bug Detection

author.name: Ruoyu Wang, Tuo Li, Jia Li

entry.summary: TyPatch converts historical Linux kernel patches into typestate rules for detecting new kernel bugs, decoupling defect-semantics recovery (done by LLMs) from analyzer implementation (handled by typestate machinery like object tracking and interprocedural propagation). This addresses the instability and cost of having LLMs generate complete static-analysis checkers end-to-end. A pragmatic LLM-plus-program-analysis hybrid for security-critical kernel code.

entry.title: Sharing standardized image-derived data in computational pathology using DICOM

author.name: Daniela P. Schacherer (Fraunhofer Institute for Digital Medicine MEVIS, Bremen, Germany), Christopher P. Bridge (Athinoula A. Martinos Center for Biomedical Imaging, Massachusetts General Hospital, Boston, USA), David Clunie (PixelMed Publishing, Bangor, USA), Igor Octaviano (Radical Imaging LLC, USA), Andr\'e Homeyer (Fraunhofer Institute for Digital Medicine MEVIS, Bremen, Germany), Markus D. Herrmann (Harvard Medical School, Boston, USA), Olivier Gevaert (Stanford University, Stanford, USA), Tabita Ghete (University Hospital Erlangen, Erlangen, Germany), Markus Metzler (University Hospital Erlangen, Erlangen, Germany), Henning Hoefener (Fraunhofer Institute for Digital Medicine MEVIS, Bremen, Germany), Tahsin Kurc (Stony Brook University, Stony Brook, USA), Curtis Lisle (National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases, Bethesda, USA), Kenneth Philbrick (Google Research, Mountain View, USA), Joel Saltz (Stony Brook University, Stony Brook, USA), Yuanning Zheng (Stanford University, Stanford, USA), Andrey Fedorov (Harvard Medical School, Boston, USA)

entry.summary: A multi-institutional effort from Fraunhofer, MGH, Stanford, and NCI-affiliated groups describes standardizing sharing of image-derived pathology data (ROI delineations, segmentation masks) via DICOM within the NCI Imaging Data Commons. This addresses the gap between well-developed image sharing and underdeveloped derived-data sharing in computational pathology.

entry.title: IMPACT-VLA: Interaction-aware Multimodal Propagation Attribution via Counterfactual Trajectories for Vision-Language-Action Policies

author.name: Jinwoong Kim, Sangjin Park

entry.summary: IMPACT-VLA provides attribution for vision-language-action robot policies by measuring how multimodal input interventions propagate through subsequent states, observations, and actions using counterfactual trajectories. Unlike prior local-sensitivity or time-aggregated methods, it captures phase-dependent contributions and cross-phase dependencies in manipulation tasks. This improves interpretability and debugging of robot foundation models.

entry.title: Generate to Explore, Select to Exploit: Aligning LLM-based Headline Generation with Personalized Recommendation

author.name: Yi Chen, Rufeng Cheng, Qiang Xie, Tao Li

entry.summary: GESE is an industrial framework that decouples personalized headline generation into generative exploration and selective exploitation at the presentation layer, avoiding mode collapse toward generic headlines that suppress long-tail user interests. LLMs generate diverse candidate headlines aligned with latent intents, and a selection stage exploits them for personalized recommendation.

entry.title: ProtoGuide: Prototype-Driven Guidance for Class-Conditional Graph Generation

author.name: Salvatore Romano, Marco Grassia, Pietro Li\`o, Giuseppe Mangioni

entry.summary: ProtoGuide brings classifier-guidance-like conditioning to discrete diffusion graph generation, where gradients cannot flow through sampled discrete edge states. It relaxes per-edge denoiser outputs into a differentiable soft adjacency, embeds it with a frozen Siamese GNN, and scores against target-class prototypes, yielding a post-hoc, backbone-agnostic conditioning mechanism.

entry.title: On the role of the tokenizer in ECG transformer models

author.name: Jiawei Li, Fabio Bonassi, Johan Sundstr\"om, Thomas B. Sch\"on, Ant\^onio H. Ribeiro

entry.summary: This paper systematically compares eight tokenization strategies for ECG transformer models across four backbones on the CPSC2018 nine-label classification task, controlling input projection and backbone capacity to isolate tokenizer effects. Physiology-aware tokenizations (median-beat and HeartLang) achieve macro-AUCs of 0.893 and 0.889 versus 0.822-0.824 for point-wise and patch-wise approaches, and pooling them yields an 8.2% relative improvement. They also shorten sequences from 1,250 to 158 tokens with reduced compute.

entry.title: A Unified Vision-Language Model for PSMA PET/CT Report Generation, Visual Question Answering, and Lesion Segmentation

author.name: Yang Xing, Jiong Wu, Savas Ozdemir, Yang Zhou, Boxiao Yu, Ying Zhang, Zheren Zhu, Chenyu You, Wei Shao, Yang Lu, Kang Wang, Tinsu Pan, Yang Yang, Kuang Gong

entry.summary: This paper builds a unified PSMA PET/CT vision-language model handling report generation, visual question answering, and 3D lesion segmentation for prostate cancer management. It uses an LLaVA-style architecture with a PET/CT vision encoder, MLP-Mixer projection, LoRA-tuned LLM, and 3D segmentation branch, trained in four stages on 5,747 paired-report datasets and the AutoPET PSMA subset. The model reportedly outperforms task-specific baselines such as PET2REP.

entry.title: Don't Send What You Don't Need: Question-Guided Token Pruning as a Privacy Defense for Vision-Language Models

author.name: Md Khalid Syfullah, Alvi Ataur Khalil

entry.summary: QPriv-VL is a question-guided token-pruning framework for federated, split, and U-shaped split learning in VLMs that prunes visual tokens before transmission based on task utility and privacy sensitivity. A lightweight Dynamic Threshold Predictor jointly estimates a sample-specific pruning ratio and token-level retention mask in one forward pass.

entry.title: Anatomical Grounding and Leakage-Aware Multimodal Contrastive Learning for Alzheimer's Disease Classification from Structural MRI

author.name: Paul-Gabriel Nicolae, Irina Georgiana Mocanu

entry.summary: This study tackles two reliability problems in deep learning for Alzheimer's staging from MRI: networks attending to anatomically irrelevant regions, and multimodal models exploiting table variables that leak the diagnostic label. Using FastSurfer segmentations and YOLOv8 localization (mAP_50 above 0.96) on 1,075 ADNI-1 scans, the authors ground attention anatomically and study leakage-aware contrastive learning with a lightweight ResNet18-Transformer encoder. It offers a careful diagnosis of spurious attention and label leakage in medical imaging models.

entry.title: A Variational Optimal Transport Operator on Incompressible Flow

author.name: Jinjin He, Shenyifan Lu, Sinan Wang, Zhiqi Li, Duowen Chen, Bo Zhu

entry.summary: VIOT is a generative neural operator that amortizes incompressible density transport, predicting divergence-free velocity fields and full transport trajectories in a single feed-forward pass instead of hour-scale adjoint optimization per pair. It combines a stream-function parameterization enforcing incompressibility, a regularized transport objective, and a Fourier Neural Operator backbone.

entry.title: Inherited Heads: Audio language models track speakers with their text backbone's attention, and an attention-mass ranking retrieves a different set

author.name: Bojro Das

entry.summary: Shows that audio language models poorly attribute speech to the correct speaker, but that biasing roughly a hundred attention heads redirects descriptions to a chosen speaker with 90-99% reliability without training. Strikingly, top heads selected from the text-only backbone transfer to steer the audio model, revealing that speaker tracking is largely inherited from text attention.

entry.title: Symmetries and Singularities

author.name: Vishnu Varadarajan, Mihir More, Aritra Das, Debayan Gupta

entry.summary: This paper makes local learning coefficient (LLC) estimation from singular learning theory more tractable at scale by exploiting known model structures such as symmetries, avoiding expensive posterior sampling. LLC characterizes the effective complexity of over-parameterized networks near a solution, which parameter counts and Hessian rank fail to capture. It matters because scalable complexity measures underpin our understanding of generalization in deep learning.

entry.title: Impute-EM: Native Mixed-State Diffusion Models for Heterogeneous Data Imputation

author.name: Sergei Kholkin, Kirill Sokolov, Dmitry Baranchuk, Evgeny Burnaev, Alexander Korotin

entry.summary: Impute-EM is an EM-style framework for imputing missing values in heterogeneous tabular data, alternating between imputation with the current model and refitting a diffusion backbone on completed data. Unlike continuous-relaxation approaches, it uses native mixed-state diffusion combining Gaussian and masked categorical components, better matching the discrete-continuous data structure.

entry.title: Inverse Learning of the Altruism and Cost Level in Mixed-Individual Mean Field Games

author.name: Haoyang Cao, G\"ok\c{c}e Dayan{\i}kl{\i}, Xiaofei Shi

entry.summary: The paper addresses inverse problems in mixed-individual mean field games, where a parameter interpolates between non-cooperative MFG and fully altruistic mean field control. It develops methods to identify unobservable altruism levels and private cost parameters from observed population behavior, relevant to policy and mechanism design.

entry.title: Equilibrium bias and convergence in augmented primal--dual dynamics with sampled constraints

author.name: Kang Liu, Mengxiao Chen, Siqi Xiong, Yi Xia

entry.summary: This control-theoretic work analyzes augmented primal-dual dynamics when constraints are estimated from samples, showing that even unbiased constraint observations can bias the augmented multiplier signal and shift equilibria away from KKT points, including a constructed example with a stable complementarity-violating equilibrium. It proposes recursive constraint estimation and proves boundedness and convergence for smooth convex conic problems via a joint energy analysis. The findings are important for sampling-based constrained optimization.

entry.title: Multi-source conformal prediction: leveraging heterogeneity via localization

author.name: Rohan Hore, Anirban Chatterjee, Sayantan Choudhury

entry.summary: MS-RLCP extends randomly localized conformal prediction to multi-source settings with heterogeneous training data and distribution shift, using data-adaptive source selection to exploit complementary coverage across feature regions. It maintains conformal coverage guarantees under a shared conditional response distribution assumption.

entry.title: Prescreening Point Defects in Semiconductors With Machine Learning

author.name: Paul Karlsson, Joel Davidsson, Rickard Armiento

entry.summary: The paper develops physics-guided ML models to predict defect formation energies and zero-phonon lines in semiconductors, targeting quantum technology and power electronics applications. The models are designed to skip the expensive relaxation step typical of ML interatomic potentials, making them suitable as prescreening filters in high-throughput DFT workflows. This reflects the broader shift from simulation-heavy materials discovery toward ML-accelerated pipelines.

entry.title: A Game-Theoretic Framework for Incentive-Compatible AI training Under Renewable-Energy Constraints

author.name: Konstantinos Varsos, Ramin Khalili, Adamantia Stamou, George D. Stamoulis, Vasillios A. Siris

entry.summary: The paper models carbon-aware, collaborative AI training as a game in which autonomous agents strategically choose participation and training intensity under limited renewable energy availability, deriving incentive-compatible mechanisms. It aims to align distributed compute workloads with low-carbon energy supply.

entry.title: CVSS-X: A Multilingual Speech-to-Speech Translation Corpus for 28 Languages

author.name: Lucas Rafael Stefanel Gris, Alef Iury Siqueira Ferreira, Frederico Santos de Oliveira, Augusto Seben da Rosa, Alexandre Costa Ferro Filho, Arlindo Rodrigues Galv\~ao Filho, Anderson da Silva Soares

entry.summary: CVSS-X is a large synthetic speech-to-speech translation corpus translating English into 28 languages across 12 families, with roughly 240,000 parallel pairs per language and over 16,000 hours, eight times larger than CVSS. It includes canonical-voice and cross-lingual voice-cloning variants, and combined with CVSS enables bidirectional S2ST research. Evaluation shows translation quality comparable to the original corpus.

entry.title: When Tools Get in the Way: The Effect of Unnecessary Tool Availability on LLM Answering

author.name: Saanvi Paturi, Arsen Kenzhebayev, Arham Sethi, Vyas Raina, Ivaxi Sheth, Vatsal Raina

entry.summary: Across 500 query pairs in 10 domains, this paper tests whether making a related-but-unnecessary tool available degrades LLM answers that the model could give from its own knowledge, and whether prior tool interactions worsen this. It shifts attention from tool selection accuracy to the cost of mere tool availability. The findings are relevant to safe agent deployment design.

entry.title: Verifiable by Construction: Claim-Level Evaluation of Verbatim Citation in Clinical Question Answering

author.name: Jiashuo Zhang, Yuling Chen, Yvonne Commodore-Mensah, Michael Oberst

entry.summary: The paper builds a standardized harness to evaluate whether clinical QA systems can provide verbatim quotes from reference material that fully substantiate every factual claim, enabling verification without opening source documents. It measures current models end-to-end across citation generation, verbatim quoting, and entailment. This targets a concrete trust problem for LLM use in clinical settings.

entry.title: Sparsity-Adaptive Sharpness-Aware Minimization

author.name: Shiryu Ueno, Yoshikazu Hayashi, Kunihito Kato

entry.summary: SA-SAM derives a sparsity-dependent SAM/ASAM perturbation radius by keeping the mean absolute perturbation approximately invariant as sparsity increases, improving corruption robustness of pruned networks at deployment-relevant sparsity. A complementary Magnitude-Weighted Hessian criterion from second-order removal-path analysis is also evaluated.

entry.title: Two-Stage Mixture-of-LoRA for Multi-Task Medical Vision-Language Learning

author.name: Zhanghao Chen, Yuanyuan Li, Zhenyu Lu, Shuo Gao, Guangquan Zhou, Yikun Zhang

entry.summary: The paper presents a two-stage Mixture-of-LoRA framework on MedGemma-1.5-4B with one shared LoRA and six task-specific expert LoRAs for joint multi-task medical VLM adaptation across diagnosis classification and report generation. Stage 1 trains all adapters jointly; Stage 2 freezes the backbone and shared components while refining target experts to handle gradient conflicts and imbalanced data.

entry.title: Direct Conditional Transition Sampling for Diffusion Inverse Problems

author.name: Qi Yu, Hanlin Wu, Xiaohui Sun

entry.summary: DCTS provides a direct stochastic-flow approximation to the ideal posterior refresh target in training-free diffusion inverse solvers, estimating the measurement-conditioned clean mean along a short inner path and transporting noise directly to the next noisy state. This avoids the costly probability-flow ODE integration and clean-space MCMC required by prior posterior refresh approaches.

entry.title: Unsupervised Point Cloud Registration via Training-Time Semantic Guidance

author.name: Kezheng Xiong, Shiyun Xu, Sheng Ao, Siqi Shen, Cheng Wang, Chenglu Wen

entry.summary: The authors observe that unsupervised point cloud registration models implicitly encode semantic awareness correlated with registration accuracy, but this structure erodes under noisy geometric pseudo-labels. They propose CAESAR, a teacher-student framework stabilized by semantic guidance from an off-the-shelf 3D segmentation model, improving robustness on challenging LiDAR data like nuScenes.

entry.title: Attention-DP3: Spatially Object-aware 3D Diffusion Policy via Geometry-aligned Attentional Conditioning

author.name: Changbo Yan, Zhongbo Zhang, Zaibin Zhang, Yifan Wang, Lijun Wang, Huchuan Lu

entry.summary: Attention-DP3 improves 3D diffusion policies in cluttered manipulation scenes by injecting object-level geometric cues through attention while leaving the DP3 backbone unchanged. It uses open-vocabulary 2D segmentation on RGB, lifts masks into 3D via calibrated camera geometry, and conditions the policy on object-centric geometric priors to handle occlusion and distractors.

entry.title: Force-Aware Reinforcement Learning with Hybrid Sensorless Force Estimation for Wheeled-Legged Loco-Manipulation

author.name: Xuanqi Zeng, Jiaming Wang, Tianlin Zhang, Lingwei Zhang, Botian Xu, Weipeng Xia, Zhongyu Li, Yun-Hui Liu

entry.summary: This paper presents force-aware reinforcement learning for wheeled-legged loco-manipulation that estimates end-effector forces without a force/torque sensor, combining generalized momentum observation with contact-aware estimation. The structured force estimate serves as an explicit policy observation, enabling force-guided contact behavior on floating-base robots.

entry.title: HarnessVLN: Unifying Training-Free Embodied Navigation through an Agent Harness

author.name: Yang Chen, Lirong Che, Zhenyu Huang, Wenbo Fu, Chuang Wang, Xu Cao, Daqi Liu, Yuzhe Yang, Jian Su, Lan-Zhe Guo

entry.summary: HarnessVLN is a zero-shot, training-free embodied navigation framework whose Agent Harness coordinates perception, retrieval, grounding, navigation, recovery, and termination through a unified tool interface. The Harness validates planner proposals against spatial evidence, geometric feasibility, and subgoal consistency, with structured tools for failure recovery. It addresses the reliability gap when MLLMs propose actions without reconciling them with spatial and task state.

entry.title: WLA$^3$: World Latent Action Modeling for Semantics, Dynamics, and Kinematics

author.name: Peidong Liu, Zhiyuan Xiang, Mingyang Li, Wenhao Li, Jiale Zhang, Jiahao Sun, Jiawei Li

entry.summary: WLA3 builds a generalist policy framework around a World Latent Action Model that learns how multimodal world states change locally, encoding camera views and embodiment-state changes into a compact latent action plus a richer transition representation. This turns abundant unlabeled human egocentric video into action-related supervision, addressing the scarcity of high-quality hand-action labels for scaling generalist policies.

entry.title: What we have is not what we prepared for

author.name: PeacockOfJuno

entry.summary: The author argues that pre-LLM AI risk thinking, grounded in assumptions from 2010s RL agents, no longer fits agentic LLM systems, and catalogs recurring fallacies such as the persistent-agent fallacy (assuming a single coherent agent with stable goals rather than cheap, copyable cognition wrapped in external harnesses). The post urges updating risk models to the actual shape of current systems.

entry.title: JaxAHT: A JAX-Based Library for Ad Hoc Teamwork

author.name: Caroline Wang, Rolando Fernandez, Zelal Su Mustafaoglu, Montek Kundan, Jiaxun Cui, Lingyun Xiao, Zhihan Wang, Di Yang Shi, Aditya Madhan, Johnny Liu, Arrasy Rahman, Peter Stone

entry.summary: Introduces JaxAHT, the first open-source JAX-based library for Ad Hoc Teamwork research, providing standardized benchmarks, teammate generation, ego-agent training, and evaluation against unseen teammates. It achieves roughly 95x wall-clock speedups via JAX parallelization and addresses the field's lack of standardized implementations and validated teammate suites. Strong author list including Peter Stone.

entry.title: Do Not Restart: Residual Completion for Stateful Agent Handoffs

author.name: Runzhi Deng, Yiming Zhong, Fang Zhao, Pan Zhou

entry.summary: Formulates commitment-constrained residual completion for stateful handoffs between models in agent routing and cascades, introducing CFRC, which freezes a residual contract from accepted progress, links continuations into an evidence graph, and admits execution only when the remainder is covered with live receipts. Establishes contract-relative partial correctness guarantees. Complements the batch's other recoverability work by addressing cost-reducing model handoffs.

entry.title: Question's Gambit: The First Move Matters in Agentic Deep Search

author.name: Radin Hamidi Rad, Amin Bigdeli, Negar Arabzadeh, Sajad Ebrahimi, Charles L. A. Clarke, Benjamin C. M. Fung, Ebrahim Bagheri

entry.summary: The paper identifies the first retrieval move of deep research agents as a critical design decision and introduces a module that decomposes the question into clues, reformulates them into complementary searches, consolidates results, and reranks before iterative search-and-reasoning begins. It is motivated by evidence that agents often fail to connect retrieved documents to gold evidence on reasoning-intensive benchmarks like BrowseComp-Plus.

entry.title: A note on goal-based hierarchical RL

author.name: Kevin Murphy

entry.summary: Kevin Murphy notes that the agent-centric general value function (ACGVF) framework, which lets the agent choose which goal to pursue and when a goal is finished, assumes full observability. He extends the construction to partially observed settings by basing the policy on an internal belief state and internal goal, connecting to his own general agent design. A short but substantive theoretical note on the foundations of hierarchical RL.

entry.title: BusMA: A Bus Communication Substrate for Multi-Agent Systems

author.name: Yanwen Peng, Delvin Ce Zhang, Xi Wang, Nikolaos Aletras

entry.summary: BusMA reimagines multi-agent communication using a shared bus architecture inspired by computer systems, letting any agent address peers directly rather than through hierarchical manager-worker or router-based message passing. It comprises agent registration, message routing, and shared memory management, aiming to increase agent autonomy and reduce error propagation from misrouting.

entry.title: MAPS: Memory-Aware Predictive Scheduling Framework for Large Language Model Serving

author.name: Tiancheng Zhang, Yulin Chen, Yunfeng Zhao, Shaoyuan Huang, Cheng Zhang, Xiaofei Wang

entry.summary: MAPS addresses load imbalance in disaggregated LLM serving caused by unknown output lengths, using device-assisted speculative output-length prediction overlapped with cloud-side prefilling. Uncertainty-aware calibration derives output-length upper bounds with target coverage to handle generation unpredictability. The framework targets bursty personal-device workloads on cloud infrastructure.

entry.title: Can AI systems have free will?

author.name: Christian List

entry.summary: Philosopher Christian List sketches a Dennett-inspired framework for asking whether AI systems can have free will, arguing the question reduces to whether there are good explanatory reasons to view a system as an intentional agent capable of choice among alternatives and control over actions. He rejects the need for indeterministic algorithms or unpredictability. This connects AI capability debates with long-standing philosophy of agency.

entry.title: KnowBench: Effort Reduction as a Unified, Deployment-Grounded Benchmark for Clinical AI

author.name: Jocelyn Kang, Caroline Zhang

entry.summary: KnowBench proposes Effort Reduction, defined as the proportion of system-generated clinical work product accepted by the responsible clinician under expert and safety review, as a unified metric for clinical AI across notes, coding, orders, EHR summarization, and decision support. It replaces research-oriented similarity metrics and rubric panels with a deployment-grounded measure of burden reduced rather than resemblance to an artifact.

entry.title: When Should a World Model Move? Loss-Conditioned State Execution

author.name: Jintao Xu, Zhengyu Chen, Ben Zhang, Yongzhi Qi, Jianshen Zhang

entry.summary: The paper formalizes when a world model should execute a proposed state update versus retain the current state, introducing loss-conditioned state execution as a model-agnostic decision rule. It distinguishes state movability from proposal benefit, showing occurrence ranking can look perfect while persistence remains the Bayes-optimal action under absolute loss.

entry.title: Chemical and geometric representation fidelity improves drug--target affinity prediction

author.name: Yixiao Li, Yining Qian, Yefan Chen, Zenghui Chen, Jiayue Sun, Yuhai Zhao, Cheng Tan, An-Yang Lu

entry.summary: ReGeoDTA addresses drug-target affinity prediction by arguing that information loss during representation construction, not insufficiently complex interaction predictors, is the upstream bottleneck. The framework preserves affinity-relevant chemical heterogeneity and geometric detail in drug and protein representations. It matters for computational drug discovery where subtle molecular recognition determinants drive binding.

entry.title: Task-Aware Federated Fine-Tuning for MoE-based Large Language Models

author.name: Tingqi Wang, Hongyu Ke, Haoxin Wang, Rafal Angryk, Zhipeng Cai

entry.summary: FedTAR is a task-aware federated fine-tuning method for MoE-based LLMs that addresses heterogeneous client data by associating clients with experts to avoid weakening expert specialization and conflicting updates on shared experts. It targets resource-constrained distributed environments where MoE sparsity is attractive.

entry.title: Rolling Day-Wise Mortality Prediction in Critically Ill Patients With AKI on CRRT Utilizing Machine Pressure Waveforms

author.name: Shehan Irteza Pranto, Joanna Yang, Joshua Lambert, Stuart L. Goldstein, Lili Chan, Girish N. Nadkarni, Tiago K. Colicchio, Javier A. Neyra, Jin Chen

entry.summary: This clinical ML study uses minute-level CRRT machine pressure waveforms, normally discarded due to artifacts and leakage risks, for rolling day-wise mortality prediction in AKI patients. The pipeline aligns machine records to charted therapy intervals to prevent cross-patient leakage and enables risk reassessment continuous with device operation rather than tied to lab draws.

entry.title: ReWeight: Leveraging Human Data for VLA Post-Training via Demonstration Retrieval and Sample Weighting

author.name: Chenwei Wang, Dianye Huang, Match W. L. Ko, Chenjia Bai, Zhongliang Jiang

entry.summary: ReWeight enables vision-language-action model post-training with cheap egocentric human demonstrations by learning a cross-embodiment visuomotor representation and using optimal transport to retrieve and weight relevant human data relative to robot demonstrations. This mitigates cross-embodiment discrepancies that arise from naively mixing human and robot data. Addresses the data-scarcity bottleneck in VLA training with a scalable human-data pathway.

entry.title: Mizan: A National Benchmark for Evaluating Large Language Models on Iraqi Arabic and the Iraqi Civic Context

author.name: Nawar S. Alseelawi, Mustafa S. Aljumaily

entry.summary: Introduces Mizan, a benchmark pairing an MSA baseline track with an Iraqi Arabic track across six axes including dialect comprehension and generation, bidirectional translation, Iraq-specific knowledge, document field extraction, and safety, built from 340 original samples. It addresses the near-total absence of dialectal Arabic in an evaluation ecosystem saturated on Modern Standard Arabic.

entry.title: Signatures of Steerability in Activation Space of Language Models

author.name: Prajjwal Bhattarai, Tuka Alhanai

entry.summary: Makes the dataset-dependence of activation steering rigorous by showing that simple separation metrics of contrastive representations strongly correlate with downstream steerability across settings, even controlling for layer and dataset effects. A synthetic superposition experiment provides evidence that separation is causally linked to whether steering vectors work.

entry.title: Modeling, Scaling, and Decoding: Optimizing Controllable Speech Generation with Nonverbal Vocalizations

author.name: Ziyu Zhang, Yun Chen, Taihui Wang, Hanzhao Li, Qicong Xie, Rilin Chen, Zhixian Zhao, Lei Xie

entry.summary: The authors build an NVV-aware DiTAR speech generation system that models nonverbal vocalizations (laughs, sighs, etc.) via dedicated tokens and adapted stop prediction, trained with large-scale bilingual pretraining plus synthetic augmentation and frequency-aware rebalancing. The work tackles the acoustic diversity and class imbalance that make controllable expressive speech synthesis difficult.

entry.title: AURA: Unified Multimodal Framework for Conversational Music Editing

author.name: Quoc-Huy Trinh, Minh-Van Nguyen, Debesh Jha

entry.summary: AURA supports multi-turn, instruction-guided music editing by using a multimodal LLM to interpret dialogue history, optional images, and reference audio, distilling editing intent into concept tokens injected into a frozen MusicGen backbone. It trains only 91M parameters against a 1.9B frozen backbone and shows strong results on Slakh2100 and MoisesDB.

entry.title: Bridging the Modality Gap in Long-Form Clinical Audio: A Comparative Study of Lightweight and Heavyweight End-to-End SOAP Generation

author.name: Ziyu Zhang, Mingchen Shao, Wenjie Tian, Tianlun Zuo, Longhao Li, Lei Xie

entry.summary: For the BeTraC 2026 challenge, the authors build a fully end-to-end multimodal system generating structured SOAP clinical notes directly from long doctor-patient audio, trained on a 1.41M-sample multi-task corpus through domain pretraining, SFT, and reward optimization. They compare 3B and 30B model scales, showing each training stage progressively improves performance.

entry.title: Natural Language Knowledge Graph Query Execution: Leveraging Controlled Semantics in the LLM Context Window

author.name: Blake G. Fitch

entry.summary: NLKGQ is a system and framework that transfers knowledge graph semantics to LLMs via controlled, machine-readable representations: an OWL ontology plus domain examples placed in a single context window, enabling the model to produce SPARQL queries directly. The core claim is that declared semantics in context outperform informal transfer through prose, schema dumps, and examples. This offers a reusable pattern for structured-data querying with LLMs.

entry.title: Neural-Network Solutions to Real-Space Charge Density and Generalization

author.name: Yuxuan Zeng, Taoyuze Lv, Zhicheng Zhong

entry.summary: AIDEN is an atomic-interaction density equivariant network for solving real-space charge density in electronic structure, replacing costly iterative self-consistent-field solutions in Kohn-Sham DFT. Built on the Hohenberg-Kohn theorem's insight that the ground-state charge density contains all ground-state information, it targets faster materials design via learned surrogates. This matters for accelerating computational chemistry and materials discovery.

entry.title: Translating the Translator: Decomposing the Cost of English-Forced Inter-Agent Communication

author.name: Kushagra Agrawal, Yuming Feng, Man-Fai Leung

entry.summary: The study quantifies the English-Forcing Tax in multi-agent LLM systems that use English as internal lingua franca, comparing native-language versus English-forced two-agent extraction pipelines across four typologically diverse languages with 300 samples each. It identifies a statistically significant cost from English routing plus back-translation that survives Bonferroni correction.

entry.title: PACE: Progressive Angular-to-Norm Contrastive Embedding

author.name: Yanping Li, Wei Zhou, Yawen Liu, Yibo Wang, Ke Zhu, Guangda Huzhang, Qing-Guo Chen, Zhao Xu, Jun Zhang, Wei Wei
