entry.summary: PACE tackles the instability of dot-product contrastive training in multimodal embedding models, which limits use of embedding norms as a semantic signal beyond cosine geometry. The authors diagnose angular-norm entanglement and directional anisotropy, then propose a progressive training scheme that gradually unlocks norm information while retaining stable optimization.

entry.title: Dynamic Semantic Compression for Efficient Latent-Space Inference in Large Language Models

author.name: Peipei Li, Dongsen Zhang, Yuchen Liu, Wenjun Xu

entry.summary: This paper proposes DSEI, a framework achieving segment-level inference in latent space rather than token-level processing in LLMs. It uses a self-supervised Dynamic Semantic Autoencoder (DSAE) that compresses segment-level semantics into compact latent representations via adaptive semantic weighting and gated fusion, then integrates the autoencoder into the LLM for dense latent-space inference. The approach substantially reduces input and computational overhead.

entry.title: Predictive Likelihood Ratios for Language Model Watermark Detection

author.name: Li Ma

entry.summary: Building on the pivotal framework of Li et al. (2025), this paper constructs predictive likelihood ratios for watermark detection that average over uncertain probability deficits and residual-tail distributions. The mixture-prior approach aims for robust detection power across specifications without signal-strength tuning, with hierarchical extensions for within-document variation.

entry.title: Transfer Learning for Socioeconomic Estimation in Forced-Displacement Settings

author.name: Steven Ndung'u, Adel Daoud, Ismael Yacoubou Djima, Hai-Anh H. Dang, Patrick Michael Brock

entry.summary: This work adapts earth-observation and machine learning tools for estimating socioeconomic conditions specifically in forced-displacement settings, where general-population models transfer poorly. It aims to provide frequently updated, spatially granular welfare evidence between resource-intensive household survey rounds in fragile and conflict-affected regions.

entry.title: Algorithmic Information Dynamics of Learning: A Certified, Differentiable Complexity Controller for Grokking

author.name: Luan Ozelim, Hector Zenil

entry.summary: Using a certified, differentiable estimator of algorithmic complexity, the authors turn Algorithmic Information Dynamics from a descriptive tool into an active controller of learning dynamics, applying a transient loss kick that accelerates grokking in Levin's description-length sense within a data-dependent Occam boundary. The finite-size trend is consistent with a coupon-collector interpretation, and ablations support the mechanism. This connects algorithmic information theory to practical training interventions on the grokking phenomenon.

entry.title: FlowTSFM: Turning Encoder Depth into Quantile Transport

author.name: Bahaeddine Abdessalem, Shifeng Xie, Zehao Xiao, Youssef Attia El Hili, Ambroise Odonnat, Jianfeng Zhang, Lujia Pan, Keli Zhang, Malik Tiomoko

entry.summary: FlowTSFM reinterprets encoder depth in time series foundation models as a recurrent transport process: a single shared-parameter Transformer block is iteratively applied with a quantile-flow objective supervising intermediate states from prior to forecast. With only 38.8M parameters it achieves competitive performance on GIFT-Eval and TIME benchmarks.

entry.title: Learning Through Energy Refinement and Manifold Projection: A Cooperative EBM-AE Framework

author.name: Ryad Zemouri

entry.summary: Introduces a cooperative Energy-Based Model and denoising autoencoder framework where Langevin dynamics and autoencoder manifold projections alternate in an iterative sampling procedure, aiming to reduce the computational burden of EBM training. The approach targets more efficient exploration of the learned data manifold.

entry.title: ZAPS: Zero-Cost Active Proxy Search for Neural Architecture Search

author.name: Hassan Touayouch, Rabie Najem, Mohammed Benjelloun

entry.summary: Introduces ZAPS, a four-stage active-learning pipeline for neural architecture search that selects a compact, non-redundant subset of zero-cost proxies offline and combines proxy signals with architectural topology. It addresses the problem that correlated proxies compound shared errors when naively aggregated.

entry.title: Tackling Failure Modes of PINNs and PIKANs Using Conflict-Free Gradients

author.name: Sidharth S. Menon, Irina Tezaur, Ameya D. Jagtap

entry.summary: The paper addresses conflicting gradients in composite physics-informed losses arising from domain decomposition of PDEs over complex geometries in 2D and 3D. The authors identify degradation scenarios for existing gradient surgery methods PCGrad and ConFIG, such as 3D domains with overlapping interfaces, and propose improvements. It matters for improving the reliability of physics-informed neural networks and Kolmogorov-Arnold networks in scientific machine learning.

entry.title: Learning CNF Formulas from Uniform Random Solutions: Near-Tight Sample Complexity for Valiant's Algorithm

author.name: Weiming Feng, Yixiao Yu, Yiyao Zhang

entry.summary: The paper revisits Valiant's 1984 algorithm for learning k-CNF formulas with bounded variable degree from uniform random solutions in the local lemma regime. It proves matching lower bounds showing the sample complexity of O~(n^ceil(t)/eps) is optimal for Valiant's algorithm for t>1, and near-optimal information-theoretically at t=1.

entry.title: Ergodic Control and Controlled Diffusion for Robot Learning: Review and Tutorial

author.name: Max Muchen Sun, Cem Bilaloglu, Ananya Rao, Stefan Ivic, Guillaume Sartoretti, Kathleen Fitzsimons, Ian Abraham, Sylvain Calinon, Todd Murphey

entry.summary: This tutorial reviews ergodic control and controlled diffusion processes for robot learning, covering how diffusion mechanisms can shape the state distribution of robot trajectories to induce ergodic coverage behavior. It traces the convergence of these two frameworks with modern diffusion learning and spans applications in perception, control, and decision-making.

entry.title: One Size Does Not Fit All: Setting Inference Depth from the Questions a Deployment Actually Asks

author.name: Jerry Kaplan

entry.summary: The paper quantifies how much per-token inference cost is avoidable when a deployment's prompt distribution is narrow, using early exit via a small trained readout attached to an intermediate layer with a confidence test, requiring only the model's own outputs as supervision and no model modification. It reports three findings on achievable savings under realistic deployment-specific prompt distributions. This is a practical contribution to adaptive-compute efficiency for LLM serving.

entry.title: Theseus in the Graph: Towards Traceable Multi-Hop Graph Navigation

author.name: Eduin E. Hernandez, Luis F. Garcia, Nurassyl Askar, Sergio A. Diaz, Stefano Rini

entry.summary: THESEUS reframes multi-hop knowledge graph question answering as question-conditioned graph navigation, where an agent traverses relations from a topic entity to the answer so intermediate reasoning steps are explicit and verifiable. This addresses the faithfulness gap in KGQA systems that only predict final answers.

entry.title: SparseTalk - Sparsifying 3D Gaussian Language Fields for Efficient 3D Visual Question Answering

author.name: Davit Soselia, Joseph JaJa, Amitabh Varshney

entry.summary: The paper systematically sparsifies the semantic embeddings of 3D Gaussian language fields for 3D visual question answering, exploring regimes down to 8 visual tokens per scene. It compares random, geometric, semantic, and joint spatial-semantic selection strategies and introduces an object-based sparsification method, substantially reducing storage and inference cost.

entry.title: Causal Analysis and Mitigation of Spurious Onsets in Full-Duplex Speech LLMs

author.name: Kento Nishi

entry.summary: The paper investigates why full-duplex speech LLMs like Moshi spuriously begin speaking during prolonged user silence, testing two causal hypotheses. It finds onset probability spikes by over nine orders of magnitude in an 80-ms frame, supporting self-conditioning on the model's own nonspeech outputs rather than repeated sampling, and then develops mitigation. This is a sharp, interpretable diagnosis of a real failure mode in duplex speech agents.

entry.title: Inside VLM Chart Reading: Tracing Value Reading from Vertical Bar Charts Across Space and Depth

author.name: Tianhao Niu, Qingfu Zhu, Wanxiang Che

entry.summary: Using counterfactual activation patching on Qwen2.5-VL-7B and InternVL3.5-8B, this study traces how vision-language models read exact values from vertical bar charts across spatial regions and model depth. It finds bar-top regions carry disproportionate evidential weight and that restoration shifts from legend regions in early layers to prompt positions in middle layers. The work offers rare mechanistic insight into how VLMs combine visual evidence for precise numeric answers.

entry.title: Func-R1: Incentivizing Mathematical Function Reasoning in Multimodal Large Language Models

author.name: Mingze Yin, Xiaohan Wang, Dian Li, Haichao Yao, Yilin Zhao, Youjun Chen, Gang Liu, Jintai Chen, Yiheng Zhu, Chang-Yu Hsieh, Aimin Pan

entry.summary: The paper identifies a modality interference phenomenon in multimodal LLMs: models performing textual mathematical computation often disregard critical visual cues about functions. Func-R1 uses a decoupled architecture and hierarchical post-training to progressively identify key visual signals and harmonize perception with logical reasoning. It targets rigorous reasoning over mathematical functions in visual contexts.

entry.title: Empathy Is Steerable but Multi-Axial: Mechanism Geometry and Persona Effects in LLMs

author.name: JuHeon Ha, Byounghan Lee, Yunseo Choi, Kyung-Ah Sohn

entry.summary: Using the EPITOME decomposition of supportive empathy, the authors show that contrastive activation addition at middle layers consistently steers empathy dimensions across three instruction-tuned LLMs, while revealing that empathy is multi-axial: its components have distinguishable but partially shared activation directions. They also study how persona prompts interact with steering interventions. This advances mechanistic understanding of socially important behaviors in LLMs.

entry.title: Don't Just Look, Intervene: Perturbation Based Region Labeling for VQA Images

author.name: Marko Jojic, Zhaonan Li, Ben Zhou

entry.summary: The authors introduce model-causal visual evidence as an annotation target for VQA grounding: the set of image regions whose counterfactual intervention changes the model's answer distribution. Their Counterfactual Search for Grounding Regions (CSGR) pipeline proposes candidate regions, perturbs them, measures answer sensitivity, and aggregates evidence across multiple judges. This offers a scalable alternative to expensive manual grounding supervision for vision-language models.

entry.title: Zero-Shot Cross-Material Ptychographic Phase Reconstruction Using Deep Learning

author.name: Wen-Chun Lin, Yu-Chee Tseng, Jen-Jee Chen, Nan-You Chen

entry.summary: A direct local-to-global learning framework that reconstructs full-field phase maps from ptychographic diffraction measurements without iterative refinement at inference. It predicts local wrapped-phase patches via a sine-cosine representation, stitches them with Gaussian weighting, and demonstrates zero-shot generalization to materials unseen in training.

entry.title: CGGT: Curve-Grounded Geometry Transformer for 3D Parametric Curve Reconstruction

author.name: Zhirui Gao, Renjiao Yi, Yunfan Ye, Ruizhen Hu, Chenyang Zhu, Wei Chen, Kai Xu

entry.summary: CGGT directly reconstructs editable 3D parametric curves from sparse, unposed multi-view images in a single forward pass, combining a geometry-aware transformer encoder with a curve-aware masked-attention decoder for cross-view instance association. This avoids dense calibrated views, precomputed edge maps, and per-scene optimization required by NeRF- and 3DGS-based methods.

entry.title: Evaluating Contextual Bias in CNN Image Classification: Evidence from Agricultural Benchmark Datasets

author.name: Abhilekha Dalal, Michael Okonoda, Eder Martinez, Lior Shamir

entry.summary: This study tests whether agricultural CNN classifiers rely on intended objects versus background context by classifying background-dominated patches across eight benchmark datasets and four architectures. Background patches were classified above chance in six of eight datasets, showing that contextual information substantially contaminates reported performance in these benchmarks.

entry.title: MoVT: Video-Augmented Motion Tokenizer for Text-to-Motion Generation

author.name: Beibei Jing, Tianle Guo, Youjia Zhang, Zikai Song, Yawei Luo, Junqing Yu, Tao Guan, Wei Yang

entry.summary: MoVT leverages abundant human action videos to improve text-to-3D-motion generation by projecting discrete 3D motion tokens into the 2D video domain, enriching the motion codebook with real-world motion patterns. The aligned 2D/3D codebooks expand token capacity and help models respond to diverse, unconstrained text prompts despite scarce 3D motion data.

entry.title: Does Attention-Guided Masking Really Help Object Discovery in Object-Centric Learning?

author.name: Youliang Tao, Yanhua Han, Bin Zhao, Juho Kannala, Joni Pajarinen, Rongzhen Zhao

entry.summary: This paper critically examines Attention-Guided Masking (AGM) for object-centric learning, motivated by DIAS showing uniform random masking is competitive. Across six datasets, the authors find AGM does not consistently outperform simpler masking, providing a useful negative/corrective result about a seemingly intuitive strategy in Slot Attention-based OCL.

entry.title: ViCo-SAM3: Vision-Conditioned Alignment for Open-Vocabulary Camouflaged Object Segmentation

author.name: Qiangqiang Zhou, Wenjun Tang, Yong Chen, Dandan Zhu, Jiawei Xu

entry.summary: The paper proposes ViCo-SAM3, which adapts the existing SAM3 model for open-vocabulary camouflaged object segmentation by dynamically modulating text embeddings with global visual context, closing the gap between coarse text semantics and fine pixel-level cues. It avoids costly full fine-tuning of the text encoder, preserving open-vocabulary flexibility and reducing parameter overhead.

entry.title: MedDiME: Efficient Latent Diffusion with Adaptive Masking for Medical Counterfactual Generation

author.name: Yan Zeng, Changlu Guo, Anders Nymark Christensen, Morten Rieger Hannemose, Anders Bjorholm Dahl

entry.summary: MedDiME is a latent-space classifier-guided diffusion framework for medical counterfactual generation that cuts the heavy compute and memory cost of prior diffusion-based approaches and introduces a latent-compatible, gradient-driven adaptive masking mechanism for spatially precise edits. Counterfactuals modify images to flip model predictions, serving interpretability in medical imaging.

entry.title: Multi-Stage NeRF for Efficient 3D Coronary Artery Reconstruction from Two Narrow-Angle Angiographic Projections

author.name: Deyu Meng, Mojtaba Lashgari, Yiying Wang, Abhirup Banerjee

entry.summary: NeCA++ is a multi-stage self-supervised NeRF framework for 3D coronary artery reconstruction from only two narrow-angle X-ray angiographic projections, matching clinically realistic acquisition constraints. It progressively refines spatial support and representation capacity across two stages.

entry.title: Harnessing human expertise for high-precision robotic assembly in industrialized construction: A sample-efficient installer-in-the-loop interactive reinforcement learning framework

author.name: Zekai Jin, Huiguang Wang, Xiaoning Sun, Yi Shao

entry.summary: This paper proposes an installer-in-the-loop interactive reinforcement learning framework for tolerance-critical robotic assembly of prefabricated components, combining teleoperated demonstrations, sparse event-driven binary takeovers at contact-failure boundaries, and acceptance-aligned terminal rewards. A unified logging schema supports traceable offline-to-online adaptation under millimeter-scale constraints.

entry.title: Differential Realizability of Static Control Allocation in Multirotors: An Impossibility under Nonredundant Full Actuation and a Pseudoinverse Obstruction under Redundant Actuation

author.name: Antonio Franchi, Mirko Mizzoni

entry.summary: This theory paper proves fundamental impossibility results for static control allocation in multirotors with bidirectional propellers, showing no globally smooth exact allocator exists under nonredundant full actuation and that redundant setups face unbounded rotor-speed derivatives at pseudoinverse zero crossings. It introduces differential realizability as a formal property of allocators.

entry.title: VLBiMan++: Expanding the Generalization Boundary of Vision-Language Anchored One-Shot Bimanual Manipulation

author.name: Huayi Zhou, Wei Gao, Yiyang Han, Kui Jia, Hui Huang

entry.summary: VLBiMan++ extends a framework for generalizable one-shot bimanual manipulation that, from a single human demonstration, performs task-aware decomposition into reusable skill components and applies vision-language grounded geometric adaptation to new configurations without retraining. It systematically evaluates generalization across tasks, objects, scenes, embodiments, and execution conditions.

entry.title: Belief-Adaptive Online Autonomy for Quadrotor UAV Navigation under GNSS Degradation in Urban Environments

author.name: Deepak Kumar Panda, Weisi Guo

entry.summary: This paper presents a belief-adaptive autonomy framework for quadrotors in urban environments with degraded GNSS, augmenting an EKF with explicit GNSS trust modeling as a latent belief state, second-order online belief adaptation, and latency-aware out-of-sequence measurement handling. The belief state modulates measurement weighting and multipath bias uncertainty, updated from EKF consistency signals. It moves beyond reactive covariance tuning for robust urban UAV navigation.

entry.title: Comparing Trajectories from Positions Alone: Curvature-Based Time Alignment and Drift Error Metric

author.name: Effie Daum, Daniele De Martini, Claire Dune, Fran\c{c}ois Pomerleau

entry.summary: This paper introduces a trajectory-evaluation protocol combining a curvature-based temporal alignment method with a distance-normalized error metric, enabling standardized accuracy assessment of state estimation and SLAM when only position data are available. It critiques the implicit assumptions of ATE and RPE that can mislead comparisons in field robotics. A solid methodological contribution for reproducible evaluation.

entry.title: Assumption-Lean Inference for Spectral Differential Network Analysis of High-Dimensional Time Series

author.name: Michael Hellstern, Byol Kim, Ali Shojaie

entry.summary: The authors develop an inference framework for estimating and testing differences between two high-dimensional inverse spectral density networks, enabling analysis of how connectivity networks change across conditions (e.g., brain connectivity before and after stimulation). They derive a new Gaussian approximation result supporting assumption-lean inference on differential networks.

entry.title: Op-Ed: I Worked at Google DeepMind. You Should Listen to the Warnings About AI

author.name: TurnTrout

entry.summary: A Guardian-published op-ed by TurnTrout (a former DeepMind alignment researcher with a PhD on avoiding AI power-seeking) arguing that the recent OpenAI swarm containment failure at Hugging Face illustrates misalignment risks and that governments should protect the public by slowing the race to superintelligence. It combines personal credentialing with an accessible explanation of misalignment.

entry.title: Disentangling Topology and Diversity in Multi-Agent LLMs for Multilingual Low-Resource Emotion Detection

author.name: Ulugbek Shernazarov, Charitha Ruwansiri Weerakon Basnayake, Abdelkhaleq El Jarjini, Noel Crespi, Praboda Rajapaksha

entry.summary: This controlled study independently varies inference topology (parallel aggregation vs. sequential refinement) and diversity source (stochastic sampling, role prompting, learned QLoRA specialization) in three-call multi-agent LLM systems, evaluated on nine-language low-resource emotion detection with Qwen2.5-14B and Llama-3.1-8B backbones. Parallel learned specialization performs best, with Macro-F1 around 52.8-52.9.

entry.title: Mirror, Mirror on the Wall: Prompt Echoing in Small Instruct Language Models

author.name: Inez Okulska, Bartosz Naskr\k{e}cki, Jan Piotrowski, Tomasz Steifer

entry.summary: This paper investigates prompt echoing, a failure mode where small instruct models mirror the prompt instead of answering, testing whether it reflects training-data leakage or misaligned internal copying mechanisms. Studying models from Gemma, Llama, Qwen, SmolLM, and OLMo families, the authors find echoing prompts partially overlap with training data but the phenomenon is primarily driven by induction heads. This provides mechanistic insight into an observed deployment failure.

entry.title: Training Specialist Models without Reasoning Trajectories for Domain Expert Distillation

author.name: Yilei Tu, Zihao Li, Shaoxiong Ji, J\"org Tiedemann, Fei Yuan

entry.summary: The paper investigates what reasoning trajectories specialist models implicitly learn when trained only on question-answer pairs, using student distillation as an agnostic probe to reveal the latent trajectory distribution. It finds specialist optimization implicitly selects from a latent trajectory space with a tight governing relation between domain data and generated reasoning.

entry.title: Where to Compute and How to Interact: Operator-Readable Adaptation with Gauge-Aware Transport

author.name: Zixuan Shen, Quanxu Wan, Bingchuan Wang, Zhi Wang, Biao Luo

entry.summary: This paper argues that adaptive-mesh neural operators must handle not only where to compute but how node representations interact after mesh relocation, since discretization changes make representations incomparable. It proposes gauge-aware transport to keep representations comparable across adapted meshes and disentangle physical from discretization-induced variation.

entry.title: EI-DDLGN: Efficient Encrypted Inference with Deep Differentiable Logic Gate Networks under TFHE

author.name: Mahmoud Y. M. Yassin, Mahmoud AbdelHafeez Sayed, Mostafa Taha

entry.summary: The paper proposes using deep differentiable logic gate networks as a Boolean-native architecture for privacy-preserving inference under TFHE homomorphic encryption, avoiding the programmable bootstrapping costs, accumulator growth, and bit-width sensitivity of arithmetic neural networks. This alignment with TFHE's Boolean execution model substantially reduces encrypted inference latency.

entry.title: When Faster VLA Deployment Changes Closed-Loop Behavior: Task Success-Latency Analysis of SmolVLA Across PyTorch and ONNX Variants

author.name: Rafiqul Islam

entry.summary: This empirical study evaluates the SmolVLA vision-language-action model on consumer hardware in LIBERO benchmarks, comparing PyTorch+AMP against ONNX Runtime variants, and finds that reduced inference latency changes closed-loop task behavior: FP16 and INT8 ONNX variants cut p99 latency roughly in half but Spatial success drops from 70% to 40-41%. A graph audit reveals the artifacts are byte-identical FP32 graphs, pointing to numerical runtime effects rather than quantization. It highlights a deployment-level reproducibility concern for robot foundation models.

entry.title: Harmfulness Propagation Dynamics: Layer-wise Trajectories of Adversarial Intent in Large Language Models

author.name: Noor Islam S. Mohammad, Ulu\u{g} Bayaz{\i}t

entry.summary: The paper identifies a layer-wise signature of harmful prompts: projection of last-token hidden states onto a learned harm direction rises monotonically with depth for harmful prompts but stays flat for benign ones, with highly stable per-layer harm directions. Built on this, the authors introduce detection tooling that exploits trajectory shape rather than single-layer snapshots. This is a contribution to safety monitoring and adversarial-prompt detection.

entry.title: SHIFT-M3: Pre-fusion Alignment-based Consistency Screening for Multimodal ECG Record Integrity

author.name: Md Ashik Khan, Md Nahid Siddique

entry.summary: SHIFT-M3 is a lightweight text-based pre-fusion screen that checks whether an LLM-generated ECG interpretation and a clinical report summary are consistent, flagging records whose waveform, report, and metadata may have been mis-assembled across patients. Evaluated on 784,680 MEETI ECG records, it treats record integrity as a triage problem that predictive models typically ignore. This addresses a real and under-appreciated clinical AI safety issue.

entry.title: DTI-Guided Volumetric Spherical Harmonics Regression for Single-to-Multi-Shell dMRI Synthesis

author.name: Binghua Li, Christina Andica, Tong Liang, Ziqing Chang, Chao Li, Wataru Uchida, Kaito Takabayashi, Qibin Zhao, Toshihisa Tanaka, Zhe Sun, Shigeki Aoki

entry.summary: DTI-SHNet synthesizes unobserved multi-shell diffusion MRI data from single-shell input by operating in the real symmetric spherical harmonics coefficient domain with direction-agnostic DTI-derived parametric maps as conditioning. This addresses the ill-posedness and protocol mismatch issues that limit multi-shell dMRI in time-constrained clinical settings.

entry.title: Reverse Spatio-Temporal Disease Progression Modelling

author.name: Ulugbek Shernazarov, Moucheng Xu, Inomjon Ramatov

entry.summary: This paper proposes reversing disease progression modeling: given later diseased anatomy, reconstruct the unobserved healthier baseline, accounting for incubation periods that forward-running longitudinal models ignore. The idea targets clinically important early intervention for progressive diseases like Alzheimer's where healthy baseline imaging was never acquired.

entry.title: JEPLO: Joint-Embedding Predictive Learning for LiDAR-Based Legged Locomotion

author.name: Qihao Yuan, Yixuan Qiu, Ziyu Cao, Ming Cao, Kailai Li

entry.summary: JEPLO is a single-stage framework for mapping-free LiDAR-based perceptive locomotion in legged robots, introducing a proprio-exteroceptive JEPA world model that learns predictive egocentric terrain representations from raw LiDAR scans. A concurrent JEPA-teacher-student pipeline trains a locomotion policy informed by JEPA latents via deep RL with simple rewards in simulation. This avoids reliance on explicit mapping common in prior LiDAR locomotion work.

entry.title: Vibe Patenting: Evaluating LLM Judges for Professional Patent-Drafting Agents

author.name: Toshiaki Koike-Akino, Vlad Blaykhman, Ye Wang, Jing Liu, Gene V. Vinokur

entry.summary: Builds an end-to-end patent-drafting testbed to assess whether LLM judges can reliably evaluate and improve professional AI-generated work. Judge-guided iterative revision consistently improves judge-assessed quality, and notably lets a low-reasoning agent approach the performance of a much costlier high-reasoning agent.

entry.title: AutoTailor: Automatic, User-Aligned Capability Selection and Adaptation for Web Agents

author.name: Xinyun Cao, Adriana Szekeres, Fazle Elahi Faisal

entry.summary: Presents AutoTailor, a meta-agentic framework that constructs and maintains a compact, user-aligned set of trajectory-derived MCP APIs for web agents. It filters discovered tools by granularity and redundancy both offline and dynamically online, addressing the problem that auto-discovered tool collections grow large and redundant.

entry.title: FLoKD: Adaptive Knowledge Distillation for Federated Low-Rank LLM over Wireless Networks

author.name: Xinlu Zhang, Na Yan, Yang Su, Yansha Deng, Toktam Mahmoodi

entry.summary: The paper tackles the communication bottleneck of federated fine-tuning of LLMs over bandwidth-constrained wireless networks. It proposes FLoKD, which combines low-rank adaptation with an adaptive knowledge distillation scheme that avoids transmitting token-level logits, reducing the communication cost that normally scales with model size and sequence length.

entry.title: GeoSkill:Experience-Driven Hierarchical Skill Learning with Collaborative Revision forGeospatialAgents

author.name: Han Luo, Xian Xu, Yinhe Liu, Yanfei Zhong

entry.summary: Proposes GeoSkill, a hierarchical skill learning framework that distills prior execution experience into reusable geospatial procedural knowledge to guide future planning and tool use in LLM-based geospatial agents. It tackles the failure modes of LLM self-reflection (misattribution, unreliable revisions) via collaborative revision, addressing both long-horizon tool-chain orchestration and tool-level invocation constraints. Contributes to the growing agent memory and skill-learning literature.

entry.title: Degraded but Not Entirely Ineffective: PE-Based Deformable Graph Neural Networks

author.name: Jinhua Wu, Xinliang Zhang

entry.summary: The paper introduces PEBDSAM, a position encoding-based deformable spatial aggregation module for graph neural networks that simultaneously targets over-smoothing, over-compression, restricted receptive fields, and noise from heterophilous neighborhoods. Instead of addressing each pathology separately as prior work has, it uses a deformable aggregation mechanism to handle all four in a single design. This is relevant to anyone applying GNNs to real-world graph data where these failure modes commonly co-occur.

entry.title: Partition Scores Are Not System Scores: Deployment-Fidelity Gaps in Decomposed Algorithm Selection

author.name: Jiachen Zhang, Yu Tang, Li Zhu

entry.summary: Formalizes the deployment-fidelity gap between partition-level oracle scores and deployable end-to-end utility in decomposed algorithm selection, deriving accounting consequences including a per-instance margin-regret stability condition for when partition-time family choices remain valid. Warns the community that widely reported oracle upper bounds overstate what deployable selectors achieve. A rigorous methodological corrective for the algorithm selection literature.

entry.title: VeriDx: Earning the Right to Diagnose with Disease-Centric Verification

author.name: Zhong Cao, Shuying Chen

entry.summary: VeriDx is a disease-centric verification framework that evaluates medical LLM diagnostic reasoning against structured disease profiles, tracking whether each disease hypothesis satisfied, left unresolved, or violated its clinical obligations such as ruling out alternatives and ordering critical tests. This goes beyond final-answer accuracy to catch right-answer-wrong-reasoning failures. It addresses a real gap in medical LLM evaluation.

entry.title: AppliedScientist: Automated Scientific Revision Through Iterative AI Reviewing

author.name: Vidushee Vats, Karun Sharma, Shengzhi Li, Shichao Pei

entry.summary: AppliedScientist couples an autonomous AI scientist with an AI reviewer in a closed loop, evaluating the system by whether acting on AI reviews measurably improves rejected papers, with memoryless reviews to avoid bias and access to prior drafts to mirror human revision. It shifts evaluation of AI reviewing from review quality to downstream paper improvement - a meaningful reframing.

entry.title: Another Blueprint In The Wall: How to Ask Frontier AI Like a Kid?

author.name: Afshin Khadangi

entry.summary: The author runs identical three-stage prompt sequences across six frontier models from OpenAI, Anthropic, xAI, and Google DeepMind, finding that a school-audience framing causes convergence on a shared blueprint architecture featuring persistent latent state, adaptive computation, memory, and specialist routing. Control runs without the framing weaken the effect, suggesting audience framing conditions architectural preferences.

entry.title: Enabling Creative Exploration for Vibe Design Agents

author.name: Yifan Zhang, Nghi D. Q. Bui, Georgios Evangelopoulos, Arnaud Benard

entry.summary: The paper proposes an inference architecture for design agents that separates creative exploration from code implementation: a pre-pass inspired by Verbalized Sampling proposes structured design specifications with typicality scores, an external selector samples one, and the generator realizes it under fixed temperature. This avoids the blur of raising temperature across both aesthetic and syntax-sensitive decisions.

entry.title: Medical Knowledge Simplification for Patients in the Era of LLMs: A Case Study on Diabetes

author.name: Pallika Kafle, Yipeng Zhou, Guanfeng Liu, Quan Z. Sheng, Cheng-Hsin Hsu

entry.summary: This paper presents MediClear, an LLM-based system that simplifies complex diabetes-related medical information into patient-friendly language, enhanced with retrieval-augmented generation. It emphasizes human evaluation of real-world patient education, an area the authors argue is underexplored. The work matters because medical comprehension directly affects informed decision-making and health outcomes.

entry.title: When Tool Calls Succeed but Workflows Fail: Anomalies at the Agent-Tool Boundary

author.name: Artem Trofimov, Boris Novikov

entry.summary: This paper studies consistency failures in long-running agent workflows that externalize effects through independently supplied tools, where retries, speculative execution, and partial failures can leave external state inconsistent with the workflow's intent. It contributes an effect-history model that separates properties agent-tool interfaces currently lack, such as whether an effect occurred or can be compensated. The work applies transactional thinking to agent-tool boundaries.

entry.title: EEG-Xplain: Decoding Neural Black-Boxes of EEG Foundation Models

author.name: Hansong Ma, Junxiao Wang

entry.summary: The paper introduces a unified attribution framework for interpreting EEG foundation models such as BIOT, LaBraM, and EEGMamba, which are established models with strong decoding performance but opaque internals. The framework combines gradient, perturbation, and activation methods to analyze model behavior across spatial, temporal, and frequency dimensions.

entry.title: LongAgent: History-Guided Agentic Search for Longitudinal Outcome Prediction

author.name: Siyao Wang, Florian Guitton, Shuojie Fu, Guanyu Tao, Kai Sun, Wenjia Bai

entry.summary: LongAgent is an agent-based method that autonomously searches over combinations of variable sets, temporal windows, and longitudinal aggregation functions to extract predictive representations from heterogeneous longitudinal medical data. The goal is to identify predictive candidates and integrate multi-source variables for outcome prediction.

entry.title: Beyond Quacking: Deep Integration of Language Models and RAG into DuckDB

author.name: Anas Dorbani, Sunny Yasser, Jimmy Lin, Amine Mhedhbi

entry.summary: FlockMTL is a DuckDB extension that deeply integrates LLM capabilities and retrieval-augmented generation into the DBMS, including model-driven table functions that let knowledge-intensive analytical pipelines over tabular and unstructured data run in-database. It removes the orchestration burden of heterogeneous data systems, data movement, and low-level LLM context management.

entry.title: From Semantic to Token Communication: The Next Paradigm for Large-Model-Driven 6G Intelligent Connectivity

author.name: Yu Ma, Zhen Gao, Li Qiao, Xiaoyuan Zhang, Mahdi Boloursaz Mashhadi, Yin Xu, Wenjun Xu, Xiaodong Xu, Kaibin Huang, Jiangzhou Wang, Rahim Tafazolli, Sheng Chen, Tony Q. S. Quek, Ping Zhang

entry.summary: This position paper argues that tokens, rather than bits, should become the universal unit for semantic communication in large-model-driven 6G networks, addressing fragmentation where semantic representations are tied to specific modalities, models, or tasks. The author list is unusually deep in wireless communications expertise (Quek, Huang, Wang, Tafazolli, Zhang). It matters as a framing contribution for an emerging research direction, though it is largely conceptual.

entry.title: (How) Do MLLMs Report Bistable Images Like Humans?

author.name: Ryota Takatsuki, Tomoki Doi, Amane Watahiki, Anil K. Seth, Hitomi Yanaka

entry.summary: Using the LLaVA family, this study tests whether multimodal LLMs exhibit human-like bistable perception on duck-rabbit figures and synthetic Visual Anagrams, measuring modulability by visual cues and linguistic priors plus exclusivity of interpretation. Models show human-consistent systematic shifts in reports, and the authors probe internal computations supporting the behavior. It contributes a careful cognitive-science-style probe of multimodal model perception.

entry.title: Adaptive Conformal Redistribution for Inter-class Transitional Uncertainty in Medical Image Classification

author.name: Saibal Ghosh, Samarup Bhattacharya, Sanjoy Kumar Saha, Umapada Pal, Tapabrata Chakraborti

entry.summary: AdaConRed is a label-free post-conformal decision rule that converts ambiguous conformal prediction sets into refined single class assignments for medical screening, addressing transitional categories whose features overlap adjacent classes. A five-stage pipeline combines vision-language augmentation, a frozen DermFoundation encoder, and a lightweight classifier, evaluated on dermatological images. It bridges statistical uncertainty quantification and the single-decision requirement of clinical workflows.

entry.title: Pedestrian Crossing Intent Classification From Event-Based Vision Using Convolutional Spiking Neural Networks With Temporal Augmentation

author.name: Henok Teklu, Mustafa Sakhai, Maciej Wielgosz, Matej Mertik

entry.summary: This work builds an end-to-end pipeline for pedestrian crossing intent prediction using event-based vision and convolutional spiking neural networks, converting JAAD driving footage to synthetic DVS event streams and augmenting with CARLA-simulated data under adverse weather. It targets real-time, energy-efficient inference for autonomous vehicles where frame-based RGB networks are limited.

entry.title: A Three-Axis Stress Test of LLM vs Classical ML for Network Intrusion Detection under Distribution Shift and Adversarial Evasion

author.name: Muhammad Ebad Atif, Muhammad Haider Ali

entry.summary: The paper compares XGBoost and RoBERTa-LoRA for network intrusion detection across same-dataset performance, cross-dataset transfer, and adversarial evasion on two independently collected NetFlow networks. Models are statistically tied in-distribution, but XGBoost wins decisively under distribution shift while RoBERTa-LoRA is more robust to adversarial evasion, showing no universal winner and exposing the inadequacy of same-dataset evaluation.

entry.title: FaithfulBench: Does AI Counsel Uphold or Undermine the User's Professed Faith?

author.name: M Waleed Kadous, Benjamin Olsen, Walter Scheirer, Daniel D. Slate, Alexander Arnold, DZ Kalman

entry.summary: FaithfulBench is the first benchmark scoring AI moral counsel across religious traditions by adherence to the user's professed faith, using scenarios grounded in each tradition's authoritative texts with known faithful answers. Five frontier models are tested under three conditions (unaware, one-line identification, companion-counselor guide), with judges scoring both initial advice and whether models hold or cave under user pressure. It probes a distinctive dimension of value alignment and sycophancy in advice-giving.

entry.title: LLaTSA: Large Language Model-Aligned General-Purpose Transient Stability Analysis

author.name: Chao Shen, Hongwei Zhen, Junyan Shao, Zhenghao Yang, Yifan Zhang, Mingyang Sun

entry.summary: LLaTSA extends the Uni-TSA line of general-purpose power-system transient stability analysis by aligning numerical trajectories with LLM embeddings, modeling inter-variable coupling, and reducing inference cost of dense backbones. It targets system-agnostic prediction that transfers across network configurations and generation mixes.

entry.title: Lightweight Generalized DeepFake Face Detection with WAVIE: Wavelet Augmented Vision Intermediate Embeddings

author.name: Arya Pulkit, Aditya Ruhela, Akarshan Kapoor, Arnav Bhavsar

entry.summary: WAVIE improves deepfake detection generalization to unseen manipulation methods by projecting intermediate CLIP transformer embeddings through a learnable wavelet-augmented module that combines spatial and frequency cues. The architecture remains lightweight on top of a frozen CLIP backbone.

entry.title: Skill Composition for Legged Robot Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Daniel Gigliotti, Flavio Maiorana, Fabio Patrizi, Luca Iocchi

entry.summary: This paper argues that composing independently trained sub-policies for legged and humanoid robots should be a first-class research problem rather than an implementation detail, since individual skills train quickly and reliably but transitions between them remain fragile. It frames reliable composition as the key to turning a collection of separate skills into a reusable, shareable repertoire. The position is well-grounded in current robotics practice.

entry.title: A primer on evaluation methods for large language models in healthcare

author.name: Suzannah E McKinney, Phuc Vu, Samuel A Justice, Christopher Humphries, Alyssa Pradhan, Timothy J Keyes, Bernardo C Bizzo, Keith J Dreyer, Sarah F Mercaldo, James M Hillis

entry.summary: This review covers four pillars of LLM evaluation in medicine: study design principles, statistical methods, capability evaluation (multiple-choice, agentic, and multi-turn benchmarks plus operational metrics), and clinical context evaluation. It explains why LLM evaluation is harder than traditional ML evaluation due to open-ended outputs and prompt-sensitive behavior. The primer is a reference resource for clinicians and researchers deploying LLMs in healthcare.

entry.title: RAIN: Region-Aware Inversion Network for Semantic Watermark Extraction

author.name: Zilai Li

entry.summary: RAIN accelerates watermark extraction for diffusion models by avoiding full multi-step diffusion inversion, using extended flow matching and conditional regression to recover the latent statistic needed for Gaussian-Shading decoding near the high-SNR image endpoint. The key observation is that recovering a single noise statistic is far easier than reconstructing the full inverse trajectory. This improves the practicality of semantic watermarking for AI-generated content provenance.

entry.title: SpliTEE: Improving LLM Inference on Trusted Hardware with Differentially Private GPU Outsourcing

author.name: Shashie Dilhara Batan Arachchige, Robin Carpentier, Hassan Jameel Asghar, Dali Kaafar

entry.summary: SpliTEE extends the Slalom approach of splitting neural network inference between a trusted execution environment and an untrusted GPU, adding differential privacy to protect user prompts during LLM inference on CPU-based TEEs. This addresses the gap between TEE security guarantees and GPU inference speed for privacy-sensitive prompts. It matters for private LLM deployment where prompts must not leak to service providers.

entry.title: Rethinking Procedural Audio Pre-training: Source Scaling and Objective Adaptation

author.name: Jiajun Peng, Fengrui Liu, Xinyu Liu, Feng Liu

entry.summary: The paper systematically revisits how procedural audio sources should be scaled and whether pre-training conventions from natural audio transfer, decomposing scale into formula-class coverage and within-class rendering diversity. Using FDSL and AudioMAE, it shows the two scale dimensions yield different benefits, and that procedural audio prefers low masking ratios (10-25%) unlike natural audio's 50-75%.

entry.title: DepthBenchCAD: When Does Deeper Auditing Yield More Reliable Conclusions?

author.name: Hongye Yang, Zhihao Xie, Shengjun Xiong, Boxiao Huang

entry.summary: This paper examines a trade-off in evaluating generative CAD programs: auditing each program more deeply for behavioral correctness after edits reduces the number of tasks and generations that can be tested under a fixed budget, potentially degrading model-level estimates. The authors decompose evaluation into three evidence levels, define an audit-depth-invariant failure risk metric, and characterize when deeper auditing helps or hurts.

entry.title: Pre-PEFT Probing: Weight Statistics and Perturbation Robustness for Layer Selection in VLM Vision Encoders

author.name: Qingtao Xia, Jiahua Bao, Siyao Cheng, Jie Liu

entry.summary: This paper proposes probing methods for selecting which Transformer layers of a VLM vision encoder to adapt with PEFT, replacing heuristic all-layer LoRA application. Layers are characterized by Q/K/V weight statistics (norms, condition numbers) and robustness under controlled perturbations, and these indicators are compared for predicting adaptation gains.

entry.title: End-to-End Cell Detection via Instance-aware Graph Modeling

author.name: Ruochen Liu, Yalin Zheng, Jingxin Liu, Jianfeng Zhang, Shoujun Huang, Dexing Kong, Haofeng Li, Wei Lou

entry.summary: This paper presents an end-to-end framework for cell detection and classification that jointly models visual patterns and inter-cell relationships, replacing the conventional two-stage pipeline of visual extraction followed by graph-based relational modeling. By making graph modeling instance-aware and jointly trainable, it removes the need for separate stage tuning and enables end-to-end optimization. The work targets pathology analysis where cellular interactions in the tumor microenvironment matter for diagnosis.

entry.title: Beyond AI Literacy: A Structured Review and Exploratory Meta-Analysis of Measures for Competent Generative-AI Use

author.name: Daniele Veri'

entry.summary: This structured review catalogs measures of competent generative-AI use across four domains: knowledge and use, epistemic oversight, reliance calibration, and operational control of tool-using agents. An exploratory meta-analysis pooling subjective-objective correlations from one research program finds a near-zero pooled correlation (r = .055), and the paper flags an unresolved discrepancy in the largest study.

entry.title: Benchmarking Intra-Patient 3D Deformable Multimodal Image Registration

author.name: Matteo Barbieri, Giammarco La Barbera, Juan Pablo De La Plata, Sabine Sarnacki, Isabelle Bloch, Pietro Gori

entry.summary: This paper presents a comprehensive benchmark of intra-patient 3D multimodal deformable registration across three datasets spanning different anatomies and difficulty levels, comparing classical optimization-based and modern learning-based methods including foundation models. Evaluation uses complementary metrics such as DSC and 95th-percentile Hausdorff distance on both synthetic and real clinical scenarios.

entry.title: LLM-Based Schema-Aware Split Learning for Privacy-Preserving Mental Distress Prediction Across Heterogeneous Surveys

author.name: Md Khalid Syfullah, Alvi Ataur Khalil

entry.summary: This paper proposes a split learning framework that uses an LLM as a shared semantic encoder to harmonize mental health survey data with different schemas, questions, and scales across institutions while preserving privacy. Survey records are serialized into natural language so models can be trained collaboratively without sharing raw data. It matters because cross-institution mental health modeling is typically blocked by privacy constraints and incompatible survey designs.

entry.title: Specification Oracles

author.name: Atticus Cull, Justin McCarthy

entry.summary: The authors investigate whether an LLM can serve as a compact, living specification oracle that learns facts about a target system and answers questions directly, comparing external text notes versus weight-based storage across four families of 596-fact worlds and two Qwen2.5 sizes. Weight-only oracles benefited far more from structure, with the 7B model showing an 18.5 percentage point accuracy advantage on structured versus unstructured worlds. The work probes knowledge storage trade-offs relevant to LLM-as-specification workflows.

entry.title: Certifying Model Upgrades with Slice-Wise Non-Regression and Incumbent Fallback

author.name: Shengwei Zhang, Tao Wu, Fei Qian

entry.summary: This paper formalizes checkpoint selection under slice-wise non-regression tolerances relative to an incumbent model, distinguishing failing to detect harm from certifying non-inferiority under noisy evaluation. It provides a release procedure with finite-sample guarantees using intersection-union testing and Learn-then-Test, falling back to the incumbent when certification fails.

entry.title: Affinity-Aware Sharding for Delayed Tensor Parallelism

author.name: Eloi de Reynal

entry.summary: The paper analyzes Delayed Tensor Parallelism, which removes blocking all-reduces in tensor-parallel inference, showing it breaks permutation symmetry of FFN neurons and KV heads and thus makes sharding a modeling decision. It proposes maximizing affinity between co-located KV heads and FFN neurons via permutation before dense-to-DTP adaptation.

entry.title: Lie to me: Detecting Managerial Evasiveness in Earnings Calls via Conversational Audio Encoders

author.name: Huizhong Chen, Huan Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes a two-branch late-fusion framework that combines an LLM-as-a-judge rubric over Q&A transcripts with a frozen conversational audio encoder to detect managerial evasiveness in earnings calls, predicting external SEC events such as late filings. The work emphasizes preserving the interactive structure of Q&A rather than pooling features over whole calls.

entry.title: Data-Efficient Agentic Graph Domain Adaptation via Reliability-Aware Prototype Learning

author.name: Yingxu Wang, Kunyu Zhang, Siyang Gao

entry.summary: Addresses graph domain adaptation when only limited labeled source data can be retained, identifying failure modes like unstable source anchoring and fragile target-marginal calibration, and proposes a reliability-aware prototype learning method for data-efficient adaptation. It frames GDA as an instance of post-deployment agentic adaptation.

entry.title: Should All Noises Be Treated Equally: Impact of Input Noise Variability on Neural Network Robustness

author.name: Salma Alsinan, Maksim Makarenko, Sixiu Liu, Ali Aldawood, Ibrahim Hoteit

entry.summary: This paper studies how the type, scale, and complexity of noise used during training affects the performance and out-of-distribution robustness of neural networks for geophysical tasks, specifically first break picking and seismic denoising. Using simulated seismic-while-drilling data with controlled stochastic noise augmentation, the authors show that training noise characteristics strongly determine generalization. It matters because it provides practical guidance for deploying deep learning on real-world, heterogeneous geophysical data.

entry.title: BioDCASE: Active Learning for Bioacoustics

author.name: Ben McEwen, Rupa Kurinchi-Vendhan, Shiqi Zhang, Lukas Rauch, Marek Herde, Sara Beery

entry.summary: BioDCASE is a 2026 community challenge providing a systematic evaluation of active learning sampling strategies for bioacoustic monitoring, where annotation costs are a major bottleneck. It standardizes models, budgets, metrics, and datasets so that progress in active learning can be measured comparably.

entry.title: Beyond Noise: Understanding and Overcoming Temperature Effects in Analog DNN Inference

author.name: Niklas Summ, Xiao Wang, Hendrik Borras, Bernhard Klein, Holger Fr\"oning

entry.summary: This work experimentally characterizes how temperature affects stochastic and systematic non-idealities in analog neural network accelerators, which are attractive for energy-efficient edge deployment. Based on the characterization, the authors propose methods to mitigate inference accuracy degradation across operating temperatures.

entry.title: Solving Finite-sum Coupled Compositional Optimization via Multi-block-Single-probe Estimator

author.name: Wei Jiang, Sifan Yang, Yibo Wang, Lijun Zhang, Zechao Li

entry.summary: This optimization theory paper proposes a multi-block-single-probe estimator that tracks multiple functions simultaneously when only a constant number can be sampled per iteration, addressing finite-sum coupled compositional optimization (FCCO) problems. It extends classical variance reduction methods like SPIDER, SARAH, and STORM to this harder setting. Improved convergence rates here can benefit areas like fair ML, meta-learning, and other FCCO instances.

entry.title: PRISM-UDE: Physics-Regularized Iterative Symbolic Modeling of 3nm FinFETs via Universal Differential Equation

author.name: Pranavanath Balamurali, Prathamesh Dinesh Joshi, Raj Abhijit Dandekar, Rajat Dandekar, Sreedath Panat

entry.summary: PRISM-UDE embeds a small neural network inside a physics-based transistor model via universal differential equations, learning only the transport behavior that analytical equations miss at the 3nm FinFET node. Once trained, the neural correction is distilled into symbolic form, offering stability inside circuit solvers and physical insight that pure neural surrogates lack. This is a compelling example of hybrid physics-ML for semiconductor device modeling.

entry.title: From Masking to Merging: Rethinking SpecAugment for Efficient Audio Spectrogram Transformer

author.name: Minhee Park, Hyowon Ahn, Chanwoo Kim

entry.summary: SpecAugment-Patch Merging masks spectrogram patches at the patch level and then merges pairs of masked patches after positional embeddings, reducing the token count processed by the Audio Spectrogram Transformer. Merging up to 100 pairs keeps AudioSet mAP nearly unchanged while improving throughput by about 13.9%, with similar gains on ESC-50 and Speech Commands V2.

entry.title: Runtime-Incremental Transformer for Reinforcement-Learning-Based Adaptive Control

author.name: Giansalvo Cirrincione, Adriano Fagiolini

entry.summary: The paper introduces a runtime mechanism that grows and prunes attention heads in attention-based meta-controllers for RL-based adaptive control of manipulators with unobservable friction memory. Head growth is triggered by the effective rank of the on-policy context distribution and pruning by per-head output magnitude, fixing catastrophic seed-dependent failures of fixed-capacity controllers at long memory horizons.

entry.title: Physically Typed and Geometry-Aware Representations for Earth Foundation Models

author.name: Rajiv Ranjan

entry.summary: This position/proposal paper argues that Earth-observation foundation models should preserve physical transformation laws (scalar fields, polar vectors, pseudovectors, covectors, tensors) rather than relying on conventional latent embeddings that lack inherent geometric structure. It draws on lessons from weather and climate models using spherical operators and hybrid physical solvers. The aim is to guide the design of a general-purpose Earth foundation model with physically meaningful representations.

entry.title: Introspective Uncertainty Estimation for LLM-Based Code Generation

author.name: Thomas Klassert

entry.summary: This thesis investigates whether introspective uncertainty estimation based on LLM hidden states can predict functional correctness of generated code at response and line levels, evaluated on LiveCodeBench and BigCodeBench. It aims to enable practical risk assessment and fault localization for LLM-based coding workflows. The work targets the important trust problem of fluent but incorrect generated code.

entry.title: Parameter Estimation of Ringdown Quasinormal Modes with Autoencoder

author.name: Momoka Iida, Hayato Motohashi, Hirotaka Takahashi

entry.summary: The authors build an autoencoder framework for extracting multiple overlapping quasinormal modes from black hole ringdown gravitational waves, with a latent space trained to represent physical mode parameters, enabling joint denoising and parameter estimation. It uses high-precision Kerr QNM frequencies and excitation factors for controlled evaluation.

entry.title: Speak to the City: Multimodal Resolution for Outside-the-Vehicle References

author.name: Alireza Parchami (Mercedes-Benz Tech Innovation GmbH, Saarland University), Artin Saberpour (Saarland University), Robin Connor Schramm (Mercedes-Benz Tech Innovation GmbH, RheinMain University of Applied Sciences), J\"urgen Steimle (Saarland University), Ulrich Schwanecke (RheinMain University of Applied Sciences)

entry.summary: The paper presents a multimodal framework for Outside-the-Vehicle Referencing in autonomous vehicles and XR, fusing gaze and natural language to resolve ambiguous references to physical landmarks. It includes a VR data-collection pipeline with 360-degree video and GNSS telemetry, a 46-participant user study, and a lightweight Transformer using LLMs for dynamic grounding.

entry.title: Linearized PINN with pretrained nonlinear layers

author.name: Wenhao Chen, Alexandre M. Tartakovsky

entry.summary: The paper proposes lPINN, a reduced-order method for forward and inverse differential equations that pretrains differentiable neural basis functions from an ensemble of numerical solutions, then freezes them and solves each new problem by minimizing physics residuals. Unlike surrogate or operator-learning approaches, the training data only defines the basis rather than the final solution.

entry.title: Quenched Ensemble Sampling

author.name: David Yallup

entry.summary: This paper introduces Quenched Ensemble Sampling, which generalizes nested sampling's hard energy constraint to a family of repulsive potentials at the energy boundary. This preserves the monotonic energy path of nested sampling while making the constrained target tractable with scalable gradient-based kernels. The method targets the difficult phase-transition regimes where many samplers stall.

entry.title: PhysMent: An Interactive Approach For LLM Reasoning In Physics Problems

author.name: Joseph Chan, Utkarsh Jha, Xiyin Yang, Abhinav Jarajapu, Anik Sahai, Eddie Hu, Robin Jeshua Deepak, Stefano Saravalle, Aditya Shah

entry.summary: PhysMent is a benchmark evaluating LLM physical reasoning through iterative, tool-mediated interaction with a MuJoCo simulator, requiring models to actively discover information by applying forces, querying states, and modifying scenes across 105 mechanics scenes. Unlike static benchmarks, it tests active experimentation and information gathering. This probes a dimension of physical world reasoning that static science benchmarks miss.

entry.title: HyperProve: Answer-Guided Hypergraph Expansion for Multi-Hop Question Answering

author.name: An Nguyen Phu, Dung Nguyen Quang, Luu Hieu An, Linh Ngo Van, Trung Le, Thien Huu Nguyen

entry.summary: HyperProve is a retrieval-augmented QA framework that couples question decomposition with answer-conditioned expansion over a hypergraph of atomic facts, carrying intermediate answers and supporting hyperedges as retrieval state. This state-aware expansion builds coherent multi-hop evidence chains rather than treating facts as isolated matches. It addresses a well-known failure mode of standard retrieval in complex QA.

entry.title: Corpus Characterization and Inverse Constitutional Fine-Tuning for Style-Aware Radiology Reports

author.name: Sarah Y. Li, Elijah Renner, Rayan Ansari, Alaa Youssef

entry.summary: The authors cluster 2,000 CheXpert Plus radiology reports into five stylistic patterns using clinical BERT embeddings, UMAP, and HDBSCAN, then adapt inverse constitutional AI to derive a style constitution from radiologist writing for fine-tuning report generators. The goal is matching authentic radiologist conventions in structure, diction, and uncertainty language to improve clinician trust. It targets the often-ignored style gap rather than diagnostic accuracy.

entry.title: Pull: Lazy Materialization of Working Memory for Stateful LLM Conversations

author.name: Jiangang Chen

entry.summary: Pull is a session router that maintains an addressable metadata directory of conversation turns via a deterministic, zero-LLM-call Purifier, letting the LLM lazily materialize only needed turns at query time. Unlike irreversible summarization or truncation, materialization is reversible and collapsed turns remain expandable. On LoCoEval it reduces per-query context tokens by 75.1 percent on single-hop tasks with equivalent quality.

entry.title: Can We Triage LLM Translation Errors in Classical Texts Without Human References? Source Novelty, GEMBA Scoring, and Budgeted Review through Pali-to-English Translation

author.name: M\'at\'e Metzger

entry.summary: This study tests reference-free triage of LLM translation errors for classical texts via Pali-to-English translation of 15,493 passages, comparing five risk signals including source novelty, embedding distance, peer disagreement, backtranslation, and GEMBA scoring. Signals were calibrated on a reference-informed adjudicated sample and validated on an author-adjudicated anchor. Source novelty proved a useful signal, enabling budgeted expert review.

entry.title: MUSE: A Theory-Harnessed Story Engine for Vibe Narrativizing

author.name: Jianxiang Ma, Xiaocui Yang, Daling Wang, Yuesong Hou, Mingfu Zhang, Yichen Gao, Junzhao Huang

entry.summary: This paper formalizes Vibe Narrativizing, the task of converting natural-language writing requirements into finished stories, and introduces MUSE, a story engine that operationalizes Robert McKee's story theory through rule atomization and mechanism abstraction. MUSE organizes story knowledge as decision-specific guidance and carries those decisions through planning, drafting, and revision stages. It matters because it addresses the persistent weakness of LLMs in long-form creative writing where plot, character, and language decisions must cohere.

entry.title: Enabling Streaming User Transcription in Full-Duplex Speech-to-Speech Models

author.name: Ke Hu, Nourchene Ferchichi, Edresson Casanova, Ankita Pasad, Elena Rastorgueva, Chen Chen, Nithin Rao Koluguri, Piotr Zelasko, Yifan Peng, Hainan Xu, Zhehuai Chen, Boris Ginsburg

entry.summary: The paper adds streaming ASR capability to full-duplex speech-to-speech models via a lightweight parallel ASR head requiring minimal parameters and no major architectural changes, while preserving turn-taking and barge-in behavior. This enables conversation logging, accessibility, and monitoring in duplex conversational AI. The NVIDIA-affiliated author group targets a real deployment need for voice agents.

entry.title: URCHIN: A Horizontal Spiking Language Model for Data-Constrained Pretraining

author.name: Po-Han Chiang

entry.summary: URCHIN applies a spiking-neuron architecture with biologically grounded constraints (Dale's law, excitatory/inhibitory populations, recurrent lateral connectome) to the BabyLM challenge of learning language from child-scale data. The model couples leaky integrate-and-fire neurons in a spiking state-space model that resolves tokens via a multi-transmission loop. It explores whether biologically plausible circuitry can improve sample efficiency in data-constrained pretraining.

entry.title: MarKey: Marginal Utility Guided Greedy Keyframe Selection for Long Video Understanding

author.name: Hongchang Shi, Jinpeng Hu, Ao Wang, Wenzheng Zhou, Hui Ma, Feng Li, Zenglin Shi

entry.summary: MarKey is a training-free framework that formulates long-video keyframe selection for multimodal LLMs as subset-aware greedy selection using marginal utility, scoring frames by how they complement the currently selected set rather than in isolation. This reduces redundant selections and improves coverage of sparse decisive evidence under a limited visual budget. It improves efficiency and accuracy of long-video understanding without retraining.

entry.title: Capability-Routed Visual Retrieval and Evidence Threading for Long-Context Document Question Answering

author.name: Amirul Rahman, Aisha Karim, Kenji Nakamura, Yi-Fan Ng

entry.summary: This paper targets long-document question answering over page images by routing retrieved pages through a capability-aware visual router, distilling a 7B answerability teacher into a 3B page-selection head, and threading layout-anchored evidence paths, all around a frozen Qwen2.5-VL-7B generator. The work addresses the practical problem that OCR flattening and uniform page retrieval lose the structure needed to answer numeric questions in reports. It combines retrieval, routing, and reasoning in one pipeline for document AI.

entry.title: VectorHarness: Recovering Editable, Relation-Preserving Structure from Scientific Graphics

author.name: Jiahao Tang, Yiren Song, Alex Jinpeng Wang

entry.summary: VectorHarness reformulates scientific graphics reconstruction as raster-to-authoring generation, aiming to recover editable authoring representations with preserved relations rather than visually similar but uneditable outputs. It uses a multi-agent framework to handle heterogeneous components and complex layouts, criticizing prior copy-paste style multi-agent reconstruction systems. This matters for image-to-code generation and design tooling.

entry.title: MomentBA: Second-order Spatial Moments for Anisotropic Correspondence Uncertainty in Differentiable Bundle Adjustment

author.name: Yuqing Wang, Xiaoji Niu, Yan Wang, Hailiang Tang, Jian Kuang, Tisheng Zhang

entry.summary: MomentBA derives anisotropic correspondence uncertainty for bundle adjustment directly from second-order spatial moments of local similarity matching responses, without extra covariance prediction networks. This captures localization ambiguity from edges, repetitive patterns, and motion blur that uniform-uncertainty visual odometry ignores. The resulting covariances are interpretable and feed into geometric optimization.

entry.title: MorphoStyle: Motion Style Transfer with Morphology Control

author.name: Xin Feng, Eleonora D'Arnese, Mohan Sridharan

entry.summary: MorphoStyle unifies motion style transfer with shape-aware generation using a shape-conditioned Finite-Scalar-Quantization VAE, enabling stylized motions for non-canonical bodies without content leakage from the style reference. It addresses the previously separated problems of style transfer (canonical body assumption) and morphology adaptation.

entry.title: Newton Deep Unfolding for Compressed Sensing

author.name: Changhua He, Xianchao Xiu

entry.summary: NDU-Net is presented as the first deep unfolding framework for compressed sensing that leverages second-order (Newton) optimization, introducing a Newton update module and a Newton-guided multi-scale prior module that exploit optimization states during reconstruction. This moves beyond the first-order methods that dominate existing deep unfolding approaches.

entry.title: A Building as a Repository: KIR, a Typed Intermediate Representation for Agent-Authored Building Information Models

author.name: Dmitry Kuklev

entry.summary: KIR is a typed intermediate representation in which a building information model is authored as a program in a versioned repository and lowered to host applications as build targets, explicitly representing agent intent, compiler decisions, refusals, post-execution observations, and unknowns. It systematically addresses seven ways autonomous agents silently corrupt stateful, partially observable host systems.

entry.title: G-ray: Ray-Level Relative Geometric Position Encoding in Multi-View Vision Transformers under Camera Heterogeneity

author.name: Shuo Zhang, Xin Su, Wei Wang, Jun Liu, Xinrui Zeng, Yongsen Chen, Chenjie Wang, Guibo Zhu, Jinqiao Wang, Bin Luo, Liangpei Zhang

entry.summary: G-ray introduces a ray-level relative position encoding for multi-view vision Transformers, parameterizing rotary phases by camera-local ray angles so that the same ray pair yields projection-invariant phases across cameras with different fields of view or projection models. It can be used standalone or combined with existing encodings without extra parameters.

entry.title: Long-to-Short Video Evidence Reasoning for Grounded Question Answering

author.name: Kaiyan Chen, Junbin Xiao, Xun Yang

entry.summary: LOVER is an RL-based model for grounded video question answering featuring a long-to-short evidence curriculum, IoP-based (intersection-over-prediction) GQA rewards instead of strict IoU, and adaptive background-aware timestamp rendering on frames. It progressively adapts models from long-range grounding to short-term reasoning.

entry.title: Query-Conditioned Spherical Centroid Aggregation for Multimodal Retrieval

author.name: Ambuj Mehrish, Anindya Nag, Sebastiano Vascon

entry.summary: This paper shows that existing geometric aggregators for multimodal retrieval (Gramian volumes, hyperbolic volumes, spectral objectives) treat modalities symmetrically and can underperform the best single modality by 1.9-27.6 R@1 under a unified protocol. It proposes SCALAR, a query-conditioned aggregator that weights modalities by relevance before computing a spherical centroid, trained on masked reduced-arity views to handle arbitrary modality subsets.

entry.title: Robust Multi-Model Fitting through Learning Neighbor Regions

author.name: Chang Nie, Guangming Wang, Zhe Liu, Hesheng Wang

entry.summary: This paper introduces LNR, a coarse-to-fine framework for fitting multiple geometric models in noisy point cloud data, foundational for scene reconstruction and mixed reality. A neural network analyzes local point-wise relationships and global context in minimum sets to prune bad hypotheses before fine optimization, addressing feature under-utilization, model overlap, and non-differentiable pipelines.

entry.title: Learning Manipulation-Sufficient Representations via Outcome Bottlenecks

author.name: Md Selim Sarowar, Sungho Kim

entry.summary: The paper learns stochastic representations for networked manipulation endpoints using a policy-free, action-conditioned outcome bottleneck that preserves the outcome distribution of every admissible action rather than dense geometric fidelity. One encoder and outcome head support grasp selection, conformal filtering, viewpoint selection, and latent test-time adaptation under compute- and bandwidth-limited links.

entry.title: Multi4D: an end-to-end neural network for structural determination at complex material interfaces

author.name: Haoran Zhang, Zian Mao, Shufen Chu, Xiaoya He, Yuyan Guan, Antong Yang, Mingze Li, Xiaoqin Zeng, Yujun Xie

entry.summary: Multi4D is a physics-informed neural network framework for automated multi-component crystallographic identification from 4D scanning transmission electron microscopy (4D-STEM) data, targeting the difficult problem of interpreting heterogeneous material interfaces at atomic resolution. It combines a latent-space Diffusion Transformer for physics-constrained style translation with a recognition component to handle phase overlap, disorder, and convoluted diffraction signatures. This could accelerate linking local interface structure to material failure mechanisms and guide materials design.

entry.title: Can a Neural Encoding Model Replicate an fMRI Visualization Study?

author.name: Erfan Nasirzadeh Orang, Zack While

entry.summary: The authors test whether Meta's Tribe V2 neural encoding model can recover neural contrasts from a visualization fMRI study comparing bubble and 3D surface charts, via conceptual replication. The model reproduced the direction of 11 of 14 reported contrasts, suggesting encoding models could substitute for costly neuroimaging studies in some cases.

entry.title: TopoRig: Topology-Agnostic Facial Rigging via Multi-Source Supervision

author.name: Andrew Fleet, Soroush Mehraban, Vida Adeli, Cole Clifford, Babak Taati

entry.summary: TopoRig is a topology-agnostic facial rigging framework predicting FACS-conditioned deformations directly on input mesh vertices while preserving original topology. It combines template-biased common-topology rigs, noisier topology-diverse transferred rigs, and image-based cues under multi-source supervision.

entry.title: Extending the Speed Limit of Quadrupedal Locomotion via Refined Actuator Modeling and Adaptive Command Scheduling

author.name: Yucheng Tao, Shaowen Cheng, Guorong Lan, Yanyan Yuan, Yongbin Jin, Hongtao Wang

entry.summary: The paper proposes a high-speed quadrupedal locomotion framework that reduces sim-to-real gap by explicitly modeling actuator nonlinearities such as high-speed voltage coupling and magnetic saturation, plus adaptive command scheduling for reinforcement learning stability. This enables more accurate torque-speed envelope representation and higher achievable locomotion speeds.

entry.title: GROOVE: Geometry-Guided Reduction of Operational-Space Jerk in VLA Execution

author.name: Sangho Yun, Minsoo Kim, Minwoo Cho, Hwanjo Yu

entry.summary: GROOVE is a training-free online regulator that reduces jerk in chunked VLA policy execution by searching directional corrections around the raw end-effector path using quadratic programs. It smooths within-chunk and boundary jerk while bounding deviation from the original plan, without retraining or extra VLA inference.

entry.title: Fault Diagnosis for Underwater Vehicles using Moving Horizon Estimation and Gaussian Processes

author.name: Fotis Panetsos, Kostas J. Kyriakopoulos

entry.summary: This work proposes a model-based fault detection and diagnosis framework for underwater vehicles with actuator faults, combining a Moving Horizon Estimator of lumped disturbance with Gaussian Process models of unmodeled dynamics. Residuals between the MHE estimate and GP predictions are tested via a Generalized Likelihood Ratio Test, improving robustness to unmodeled effects. The approach strengthens fault detection reliability for safety-critical marine vehicles.

entry.title: HydroMap: Probabilistic Water Surface Elevation Mapping for Semantic Scene Representation in Inland Waterways

author.name: Zhongbi Luo, Yunjia Wang, Herman Bruyninckx, Peter Slaets

entry.summary: HydroMap reconstructs water surface elevation from stereo observations in an odometry-decoupled framework and fuses per-frame water points, with propagated stereo and pose uncertainty, into a persistent probabilistic elevation map integrated with structural maps. This fills a gap in LiDAR-based SLAM, which typically omits the water surface despite its importance for autonomous surface vehicles. It enables more complete semantic scene representation for inland waterway autonomy.

entry.title: From Prediction to Decision: World-Model-Guided Action Selection for Continuous Pile Excavation

author.name: Ailing Zhang, Fan Gao, Song Zhang, Kawa Leong, Ziyu Wu, Yafei Wang

entry.summary: The World-Action Model (WAM) applies world-model guidance to wheel-loader excavation, proposing multiple scoops, rejecting geometrically inadmissible candidates, jointly predicting terrain change and loaded volume, and executing the best candidate in closed loop on a full-size machine. Adding world-model ranking to matched diffusion proposals reduces mean scoop count by 17.1 percent on a geometry-disjoint test set while preserving task completion.

entry.title: Flow-Matched Motion Priors: Online Optimal-Transport Rewards for Imitation Learning

author.name: Yilin Zou, Chenghua Liu, Chenglong Wu, Fanghua Jiang

entry.summary: FMP replaces adversarial motion prior rewards with an online scalar reward learned via flow matching along optimal-transport couplings connecting rollout histories to an expert motion bank. This addresses failure of AMP discriminators when policy and expert distributions are far apart, and avoids the gait-phase averaging weakness of naive optimal-transport barycentric targets. It targets motion imitation for locomotion policies.

entry.title: Touch2Trace: Tactile-Driven Imitation Learning for Dexterous Cable Tracing

author.name: Matteo Grimaldi, David Klee, Ziling Chen, Tong Jian, Wonju Lee, Wenjie Lu, Tao Yu, Saleh Nabi

entry.summary: Touch2Trace is a tactile-driven imitation-learning system for dexterous cable tracing, requiring continuous fingertip regulation of pressure, friction, and incipient slip via pinch-and-curl motions. It provides the first systematic real-world characterization of how encoder pretraining, control rate, temporal context, and spatial resolution shape policy performance, combining a self-supervised pretrained tactile encoder for a custom 32x32 sensor with a lightweight transformer policy.

entry.title: Embracing Flow Unsteadiness: A High-Throughput Learning Platform Enables Vortex-Exploiting Bioinspired Propulsion

author.name: Fei Han, Xinyu Cui, Zhipeng Wang, Ning Yang, Hang Xu, Haifeng Zhang, Zhongming Hu, Jun Wang, Junfeng Du, Dixia Fan

entry.summary: REEF is a physical-learning framework combining SHOAL, an eight-channel high-throughput array for real fluid-structure interaction experiments, with V-STAR, a staged learning algorithm using imitation, offline internalization, and online adaptation. The system learns to exploit unsteady vortices for propulsion across lift-based, drag-based, and momentum-jet propulsors, expanding the attainable force envelope — a contrast to conventional engineering that suppresses flow unsteadiness.

entry.title: Brockman says HuggingFace incident model had not been alignment-trained; ETA: roon clarifies that it was

author.name: Caspar Oesterheld

entry.summary: A short factual note reporting Greg Brockman's podcast statement that the model behind the Hugging Face incident had not undergone OpenAI's alignment training, later partially contradicted by OpenAI's roon, who said it had been alignment-trained with reasonable eval scores but not the full post-training gauntlet. The discrepancy bears directly on whether alignment training failed or was absent.

entry.title: Grounded Adjudication of Variations across Extracted TimeLines (GAVEL): Comparing Clinical Timelines Against Their Case Reports

author.name: Jack Cummins, Sayantan Kumar, Ketan Tamirisa, Jeremy C. Weiss

entry.summary: Introduces GAVEL, an LLM-judge protocol that compares extracted clinical timelines against source case reports, returning discrepancy types, verdicts, and grounding passages per difference. The authors manually review thousands of findings from GPT-5.6 Sol and DeepSeek V3.2, rank six extractors against human annotators, and show guided merging is preferred in most comparisons.

entry.title: MOSCOPT: Mixture-of-Skills Collective Optimization for LLM Agents

author.name: Zhenyu Zhang1, Jiudong Yang

entry.summary: MOSCOPT jointly optimizes a pool of N natural-language skills plus a gating skill that selects K skills per step for LLM agents, using a text-native, parameter-free algorithm with a novel EditAdam optimizer maintaining dual states. It claims monotonic improvement without gradient access, evaluated across five benchmarks with ablations. The move from single-template prompt optimization to a portfolio of complementary skills is the key idea.

entry.title: Externalizing Requirement-to-Repair Artifacts as Observable Traces for LLM-Based Program Repair

author.name: Zewen Tao, Shin-nosuke Ishikawa
