entry.summary: THEMIS is a stage-aware LLM program repair workflow that externalizes the requirement-to-patch process via semantic interpretation, a runtime requirement-code graph, repair rationale, and post-edit audit records. A retrospective audit of 300 SWE-bench Lite cases shows most cases retain complete auditable traces connecting repair stages.

entry.title: TryOnReward: Learning Foveated Consistency for Reinforcement Fine-Tuning of Virtual Try-On

author.name: Xueheng Li, Yong Liu, Xiaolong Fu, Wen Xue, Chengjun Xie, Yipeng Sun, Yan Li, Simiu Gu

entry.summary: TryOnReward is a fine-grained reward model for virtual try-on built on a vision-language backbone, designed to capture foveated garment and person detail consistency where generic fidelity metrics and general VLMs fail. It enables reinforcement fine-tuning of try-on models without the severe reward hacking seen with coarser reward signals. The work addresses a concrete reward-design bottleneck for preference-aligned generative applications.

entry.title: Certifiably Interpretable Training of ReLU-MLPs for Boolean Tasks with Guaranteed Truth-Table Generalization

author.name: Hrad Ghoukasian, Anastasis Kratsios

entry.summary: MACCHIATO is a training algorithm that jointly constructs explicitly structured ReLU-MLPs from partial truth-table observations and an explicit Boolean circuit over AND/OR/XOR gates that certifies what subnetworks compute. It responds to eroding interpretability of AI systems by guaranteeing truth-table generalization with machine-checkable certificates.

entry.title: LePlanner: An Iterative Amortized Controller For World Models

author.name: Saksham Bansal, Om Naphade, Chayan Aggarwal, Vrishin M

entry.summary: LePlanner is an amortized iterative controller for joint-embedding predictive world models that constructs and refines latent action sequences through a frozen world-model predictor, positioned between costly search-based planners (CEM, MPPI, iCEM) and single-pass policy methods. It aims to retain search quality while cutting per-decision compute, particularly on contact-rich tasks with multimodal demonstrations. A middle path in the model-based RL planning spectrum.

entry.title: From Visual Attribution to Clinical Reasoning: Explainable Parkinson's Disease Screening from Hand-Drawn Patterns

author.name: Aritra Dey, Utsav Kumar Nareti, Chandranath Adak, Soumi Chattopadhyay, Krishna Gopal Sasmal, Saeed Anwar

entry.summary: The paper presents an explainable screening framework for Parkinson's disease from hand-drawn spirals and meanders, combining discriminative visual modeling of tremor-induced distortions with a multi-stage explainability pipeline tied to clinical reasoning. Evaluation uses subject-disjoint protocols for generalization.

entry.title: MANE: A Multi-Path Adaptive Network for Edge Onloading of Deep Neural Networks

author.name: Sokratis Nikolaidis, Stylianos I. Venieris, Leonidas Malachias, Iakovos S. Venieris

entry.summary: MANE is a distributed inference architecture for split computing where a lightweight head runs on IoT devices and a heavier tail runs on an edge server, with adaptive multi-path routing to manage many devices competing for shared server resources. It targets smart-environment scenarios where unmanaged load causes latency SLO violations. This is a practical systems contribution for scaling server-assisted inference.

entry.title: Semantic Fibers and Cross-Gram Interference: A Calculus of Safety Drift in Overcomplete Representations

author.name: Mohammed Ahnouch, Lotfi Elaachack

entry.summary: This theoretical paper formalizes cross-lingual safety drift, where a model refuses a harmful request in one language but complies with its faithful translation, using an audited equivalence relation over representations. It derives an exact linear-algebraic characterization showing the drift is a cross-Gram functional of within-fiber contrast, with worst-case values expressible as support functions. It offers an intrinsic calibrated exposure measure for safety auditing beyond output-behavior observation.

entry.title: FedLTLib: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Federated Long-Tail Learning

author.name: Changkun Lin, Junxiao Wang

entry.summary: FedLTLib is a benchmark for federated learning under long-tailed data distributions, formally characterizing a Double Heterogeneity arising from heterogeneous mobile devices with imbalanced class distributions. It provides a standardized testbed for methods targeting head-class dominance and scarce tail classes in privacy-preserving distributed settings.

entry.title: Machine Unlearning for Speech Question Answering in Large Audio-Language Models

author.name: Zhe Liu

entry.summary: This work studies machine unlearning for speech QA in large audio-language models, a harder setting than text LLMs or ASR because acoustic perception and factual knowledge are tightly coupled. The author evaluates gradient ascent, task arithmetic, and alignment-based fine-tuning that enforces refusal responses, aiming to remove private knowledge while preserving general capability. It extends an important privacy area into the underexplored audio modality.

entry.title: Online Bayesian Node Classification on Inductive Graphs under Distribution Shift

author.name: Jinwen Xu, Gonzalo Mateos Buckstein, Qin Lu

entry.summary: The authors adapt Bayesian last-layer modeling to GNNs with a variational objective that handles the non-conjugate softmax likelihood, enabling both calibrated uncertainty and streaming posterior updates for newly arriving nodes under distribution shift. This addresses safety-sensitive node classification on evolving graphs where standard GNNs are trained once.

entry.title: Admissable: Training Reinforcement Learning Agents against Adversarial Missingness

author.name: Paul Stahlhofen, Luca Hermes, Tim Kochs, Markus Vieth, Barbara Hammer

entry.summary: The paper formally defines adversarial feature missingness for reinforcement learning, where an adversary occludes observation features to degrade performance, and relates it to l_inf adversarial perturbations and missing-data learning. An adversarial training algorithm is proposed and validated on three MuJoCo environments with improved robustness over baselines.

entry.title: Privacy-Aligned Personalized Federated Learning with Compact Adaptation and Variable-Length Gaussian Communication

author.name: Yilin Xu, Chun Hei Michael Shiu, Chih Wei Ling, Linqi Song

entry.summary: The paper identifies a structural misalignment in personalized federated learning where client variation is low-dimensional but repeated high-dimensional updates are released, and proposes releasing a private client context once while confining adaptation to a fixed coefficient space with variable-length Gaussian quantization for communication efficiency. Ablations show most private-training gains are retained via radial evolution of the factorized generator. This advances both privacy and communication efficiency in federated learning.

entry.title: Calibrating subgrid parametrizations of single-column ocean models via simulation-based inference

author.name: Luben M. C. Cabezas, Sacha Wendling, Aur\`ele Gallard, Gabriel Mouttapa, Julien Le Sommer, Pedro L. C. Rodrigues

entry.summary: The paper applies simulation-based inference (SBI) to calibrate free coefficients of vertical-mixing subgrid parametrizations in a JAX-based single-column ocean model (tunax) against large-eddy simulation references, producing full posteriors over parameters instead of unquantified point estimates. This addresses ill-posedness in the inverse problem where distinct configurations fit comparably. Uncertainty-aware calibration improves the reliability of ocean and climate model physics.

entry.title: Certification cost of quantum models: measurement correlation, not parameter count

author.name: Pavel Sulimov, Claude Lehmann

entry.summary: This theoretical work derives the shot-complexity cost of certifying an empirical Fisher matrix for variational quantum models to relative error, showing the exponent is determined by how readout variance and gradient norms scale with register size rather than parameter count. It validates the scaling identity empirically across hundreds of matrix-product-state cells.

entry.title: From Token Probabilities to Semantic Constraints: Towards Declarative Probabilistic Evaluation of Language Models

author.name: Kyle Richardson, Cullen Anderson, Pranav Balakrishnan, Takuto Ban, Daksha Ladia, Ankita Gupta, Marisa Hudspeth

entry.summary: ModelLog is a declarative probabilistic framework for pre-training evaluation that specifies evaluation targets as symbolic constraints over token-level predictions and measures how strongly a model's distribution satisfies them. Applied to tasks on negation, mutual exclusivity, and consistency, it provides formal tools linking evaluation to pre-training learning signals. This bridges symbolic semantic specification with probabilistic model evaluation.

entry.title: Measuring the Creativity of Frontier LLMs in Automated Research

author.name: Yiheng Zhao, Mengzhuo Chen, Chengming Hu, Pengyi Liao, Yiran Pang

entry.summary: The authors propose metrics for evaluating LLM creativity in automated research along valueness (usefulness of ideas) and novelty, with the latter split into exact-match, variable-level, and hypothesis-level novelty relative to retrieved knowledge. Frontier models score similarly on most metrics but differ in specific respects. This contributes an early evaluation framework for AI-generated research ideas.

entry.title: E2A-Bench: Benchmarking Evidence-to-Action Reliability in Financial Chart Reasoning

author.name: Xiaoya Wang, Yutong Xu, Junjie Wang

entry.summary: E2A-Bench is a 969-query benchmark built from 323 HS300 constituents that evaluates whether financial VLMs keep evidence traceable through rationale, confidence, and final action recommendation, using deterministic OHLCV-derived evidence anchors and metrics such as UCR, RCI, ECI, and NDR. Unlike claim-centric hallucination benchmarks, it assesses grounding-to-action reliability. This targets reliability of VLMs in a high-stakes advisory domain.

entry.title: Tone on a Budget: A Reference-Free Metric for Lexical Tone in Massively Multilingual Text-to-Speech

author.name: Moses Daudu, Adeola Enitan Bamidele, Honor-Jesus Bezaleel

entry.summary: The paper introduces DunDun, a reference-free metric for evaluating lexical tone in TTS, motivated by tone languages like Yoruba where standard CER computed from tone-stripped ASR output can hide meaning-changing errors. It reads gold High/Mid/Low sequences from input diacritics, requiring no tone-labeled corpus or reference recording. This makes tone-quality evaluation feasible for low-resource tone languages.

entry.title: Reducing the Output-Mode Gap in Speech Language Models via Joint-Output On-Policy Distillation

author.name: Daxin Tan, Dehua Tao, Chengxi Deng, Hanlin Zhang, Xiao Chen

entry.summary: The paper identifies an output-mode gap in speech LLMs: text generated internally during interleaved speech-to-text-and-speech generation is markedly less accurate than text produced in speech-to-text mode, because acoustic tokens contaminate the context. The proposed Joint-Output On-Policy Distillation transfers the stronger S2T policy into joint generation using student-generated trajectories. This improves the reliability of spoken-response generation in speech LLMs.

entry.title: MARC: Morphology-Aware Regression of Consensus for Cell Segmentation in Subcellular Spatial Transcriptomics

author.name: Xinyu Shu, Andrew Zhang, Jean Yang, Jinman Kim

entry.summary: MARC improves cell segmentation for subcellular spatial transcriptomics by using agreement among complementary segmentation methods as a surrogate for unavailable ground-truth boundaries, regressing consensus in a morphology-aware manner. Accurate boundaries matter because errors propagate into incorrect transcript assignments in downstream analyses. The approach sidesteps costly manual annotation of large cell populations.

entry.title: DynEoMT: Learning Object Dynamicity from Online Segmentation Queries

author.name: Calvin Galagain, Martyna Poreba, Fran\c{c}ois Goulette

entry.summary: DynEoMT augments query-based video segmentation with region-level dynamicity prediction, classifying each segmented region as dynamically moving or statically camera-driven, using only the current frame and propagated queries without optical flow, depth, or camera pose. The authors also introduce new annotations since existing segmentation benchmarks lack this attribute.

entry.title: SCOUT-SLAM: Structurally-Coupled Dual Uncertainty-Aware 3DGS SLAM in the Wild

author.name: Kumaran Karthik, Pramat Shastri Jois, Suresh Sundaram

entry.summary: SCOUT-SLAM addresses the circular dependency between camera tracking accuracy and reconstruction quality in 3D Gaussian Splatting SLAM by estimating tracking and reconstruction uncertainties from a shared base network with low-rank adaptation. It targets real-world conditions with rapid camera motion and dynamic, cluttered environments.

entry.title: Weakly Supervised Spatial Grounding for Discriminative Attention-Based Ultrasound-Histopathology Alignment in Prostate Cancer Grading

author.name: Obed Korshie Dzikunu, Emma Willis, Mohammad Mahdi Abootorabi, Mohamed Harmanani, Zhuoxin Guo, Ferdinand Luger, Adam Kinnaird, Brian Wodlinger, Parvin Mousavi, Purang Abolmaesumi

entry.summary: The paper decouples two roles of a single cross-modal distillation objective in prostate cancer grading: making micro-ultrasound patch features discriminative and selecting which patches enter pooled representations. It uses weak spatial supervision from routinely recorded percentage involvement to constrain predicted malignant-tissue proportions independently of the histopathology alignment loss.

entry.title: nBMS, a Neuromorphic Battery Management System with a Silicon-Validated Spiking State-of-Charge Core for eVTOL Aircraft

author.name: \.Ismail Can Dikmen

entry.summary: nBMS is a neuromorphic battery management architecture whose spiking state-of-charge core runs per-timestep SoC estimation under hard energy and certification budgets for eVTOL aircraft. It uses 34,433 int16 parameters with zero dense MAC operations, achieving 2.45% RMSE versus 1.74% for a tuned conventional baseline.

entry.title: GIFT: Glove-Inferred Force Transfer: Force-Aware Human-to-Robot Skill Transfer from a Wearable Sensing Glove to a Robot Hand Without Tactile Sensors

author.name: Tzah Sarusi

entry.summary: GIFT enables human-to-robot skill transfer where fingertip force measured in newtons on a wearable glove is matched by robot-side force estimated from actuator-current residuals, with no tactile sensors on the robot and no robot present during demonstration. The physical unit of newtons serves as the interface between human demonstration and robot deployment.

entry.title: InterSocialBench: Benchmarking Human and LLM Preferences for Companion-Robot Social Behavior

author.name: Yaodan Xu, Boyang Guo, Yuqing Gu, Qingxin Zhang, Yiwen Deng, Meng Liu, Lintian Li

entry.summary: InterSocialBench is a benchmark of 210 domestic scenarios and 18 high-level behaviors pairing judgments from 100 human participants with 23,520 responses from seven LLMs under 16 personality conditions. Each annotation preserves a preferred action alongside explicitly appropriate and inappropriate candidates, enabling evaluation of both preferred-choice agreement and explicit rejection. It targets companion-robot social behavior where multiple responses may be acceptable.

entry.title: Uncertainty-Guided Sparse Refinement for Action Chunking Transformer Policies

author.name: Chenyang Wang, Yuntian Wang, Xiaoxiong Yang, Dingde Jiang, Siao Liu, Yang Liu

entry.summary: UGR addresses failures in chunk-based visuomotor policies by observing that errors concentrate at a few critical timesteps rather than uniformly across the action chunk. It uses a coarse-to-refine design: predicting a full chunk, estimating per-step temporal uncertainty from coarse hidden states, and refining only the highest-uncertainty steps. This makes refinement targeted and efficient for long-horizon manipulation.

entry.title: OrchSLM: Probing the Dynamics of Small Language Model Orchestration

author.name: Chengxi Zhang, Yu Yao

entry.summary: Explores orchestrating heterogeneous small language models as a non-interactive alternative to monolithic LLMs for agentic workloads, motivated by latency, privacy, and cost constraints of cloud-scale deployment. It analyzes dynamics of SLM orchestration given their limited capacity and context windows for long-horizon reasoning.

entry.title: How User-AI Mistreatment Occurs and Matters in Conversational Systems?

author.name: Fanqi Zeng, Sadid A. Hasan, Chaocheng He

entry.summary: Audits 777K English conversations from LMSYS-Chat-1M with two independent detectors to study hostility, coercion, and adversarial pressure directed at AI models by users, a complement to the usual focus on model-generated harms. It finds the lexicon and moderation signals capture weakly overlapping phenomena, with implications for interpreting model behavior and alignment drift.

entry.title: MANAS-2: Constrained Reconstruction for EEG Foundation Models

author.name: Arvasu Kulkarni, Aditya Ray Mishra, Mahir Jain, Parshva Runwal, Lakshya Saini, Siddharth Panwar, Sandeep Singh

entry.summary: Introduces MANAS-2, an EEG foundation model combining a Raw-Band Hybrid masked autoencoder that reconstructs both temporal patches and spectral-band targets, with ConRec, a physics-motivated regularizer penalizing RMS-energy differences across adjacent windows to bias the encoder toward oscillatory-envelope organization. Evaluated across seven held-out EEG datasets. Contributes to emerging neuroscience foundation models.

entry.title: CoMem: Collective-Individual Memory Synergy for Evolutionary Multi-Agent Systems

author.name: Chengxin Yu, Zhaoxin Fan, Faguo Wu, Hongwei Zheng, Yun Zhou, Zhiyu Li

entry.summary: CoMem is a memory architecture for LLM-driven multi-agent systems that unifies private experience (per-agent sedimentation of useful memories) with curated collective wisdom (shared, validated knowledge). The design counters flat, noisy shared memories by preserving agent-level distinctions while enabling group-level learning over time.

entry.title: Are LLMs Good Financial User Simulators? A Preliminary Study

author.name: Jiajie He, Jiangyuan Hong, Dongling Ni, Wenjin Liu, Xintong Chen

entry.summary: This preliminary study tests whether LLMs can simulate individual financial decisions by predicting 120 volunteers' next-day trading actions, securities, and quantities in a controlled paper-trading environment with real-time market data and no real money. It compares rolling predictions with and without point-in-time market context, finding market information improves action accuracy.

entry.title: Conflict-Predictive Variable Horizons in Multi-Drone Distributed Model Predictive Control

author.name: Linda M\"{u}mken, Michael Schwung, Stefan Lier, Andreas Schwung

entry.summary: The authors propose letting each drone locally set a variable MPC prediction horizon based on closed-form time-to-conflict estimates derived from neighbor flight-line extrapolation with confidence funnels, avoiding the cost-latency compromise of fixed horizons in multi-drone collision avoidance. The distributed MPC scheme itself is unchanged. This is a practical efficiency contribution for drone swarm control.

entry.title: PolicyMem: Geometric Policy Memory for LLM Governance

author.name: Yuanchen Bei, Zhengzhang Chen, Yanjun Zhao, Haoyu Wang, Hanghang Tong, Haifeng Chen

entry.summary: PolicyMem externalizes natural-language governance policies as reusable geometric memory objects, aiming to unify detection, intervention, and verification under persistent policy representations. It positions itself against learning-based guards (coupled to trained taxonomies) and programmable frameworks (requiring manual prompt engineering), offering consistent policy reuse across safeguards. Authored by an IBM-affiliated group working on LLM governance infrastructure.

entry.title: DiTAR+: Dual Optimization for Robust Autoregressive Diffusion Speech Synthesis

author.name: Ziyu Zhang, Tianlun Zuo, Hanzhao Li, Haoyu Zhang, Lei Xie

entry.summary: Proposes DiTAR+, a dual-optimization framework for zero-shot speech generation built on autoregressive diffusion transformers, targeting decoding instability in long or linguistically complex utterances. Dilated Context Sampling expands the historical receptive field without breaking temporal continuity, while a second optimization addresses acoustic inertia in the diffusion decoder that causes semantic conditions to be ignored.

entry.title: Hardware-Aware Learned Representation Compression for Distributed In-Sensor Vision

author.name: Chengwei Zhou, Abu Masum, Xuming Chen, Mehran Moghadam, Sreetama Sarkar, Arnab Sanyal, Md Abdullah-Al Kaiser, M. Hassan Najafi, Sercan Aygun, Gourav Datta

entry.summary: Introduces OASIS, a distributed in-sensor vision framework that uses a lightweight encoder trained with task, entropy, and reconstruction objectives to produce compact task-relevant representations before off-chip transmission from CMOS image sensors. It supports deployment paths including 4-bit quantization with Huffman coding, addressing tight compute and memory constraints of sensor-adjacent logic.

entry.title: A Generative AI Integrated Multimodal Framework for Low-Latency Multi-Camera Person Re-Identification

author.name: Leon Fernando, C Dombawala, P. Hettigoda, Vanodhya G. Warnasooriya, Ishara Neranjana, Rashmika Nawaratne

entry.summary: The authors propose a person re-identification framework combining global visual embeddings, VLM-generated semantic attribute descriptions, and optional facial recognition within a cost-aware early-exit cascade that triggers expensive modalities only for ambiguous cases. It targets robustness to missing cues and low-latency surveillance deployment.

entry.title: How broad is that claim? Mapping Generalisation in NLP Research

author.name: Chenxin Diao, Nataliya Stepanova, Emily Allaway

entry.summary: The authors introduce NLPGenX, a taxonomy classifying scientific claims by level of generalisation, and NLPGenA, an LLM-powered framework that automatically labels sentences from NLP articles into five generalisation classes, validated with human annotators. The goal is detecting over-reliance on generalisations and misrepresentation of findings in scientific communication. This is a meta-science tool applied to the NLP literature itself.

entry.title: Online Language Adaptive Sampling for Better Distributed Cross-lingual Gains

author.name: Quang Phuoc Nguyen, F\'elix Gaschi, David Anugraha, Santiago Mart\'inez Novoa, En-Shiun Annie Lee

entry.summary: The paper proposes an adaptive sampling strategy for realignment-based cross-lingual transfer in multilingual LLMs, assigning trainable sampling probabilities to languages so that poorly aligned languages are sampled more frequently, with the distribution evolving during training. This targets extremely low-resource languages where uniform random sampling of parallel sentences is suboptimal. It offers a simple but effective improvement for multilingual model quality.

entry.title: Augmenting Large Audio-Language Models with Frame-Level Grounding for Fine-Grained Temporal Perception

author.name: Yanfeng Shi, Yan Song, Junhui Li, Tinggan Huang, Wu Guo, Haoyu Song, Ian McLoughlin

entry.summary: The paper improves event localization in large audio-language models by attaching a dedicated frame-level grounding model rather than relying on generative timestamp-token prediction, which lacks explicit correspondence to acoustic evidence. A frozen LALM encodes the event query with audio context, and the grounding model leverages this semantic representation for precise temporal localization.

entry.title: Circuit-MLLM: Topological Logic-Guided Latent-Space Visual Reasoning for Circuit Schematic Understanding

author.name: Jinyuan Deng, Yuqi Jiang, Wenjing Huang, Xin Li, Qi Sun, Cheng Zhuo

entry.summary: Circuit-MLLM reformulates circuit topology analysis in multimodal LLMs as device localization, path tracing, and sequential latent-space reasoning. It introduces a circuit knowledge mining mechanism aligning latent representations with structurally rich features to handle dense component layouts and topological logic that general MLLMs struggle with.

entry.title: Scalable partial information decomposition for symptom networks via supervised embeddings

author.name: Cillian Hourican, Eric Dignum, Rick Quax, Debraj Roy

entry.summary: The paper introduces embedding-based partial information decomposition (ePID), which compresses all nonfocal symptoms into a low-cardinality discrete embedding to make two-source PID tractable, yielding unique, redundant, and synergistic information components for symptom pairs. Benchmarked on synthetic Bayesian networks calibrated to PHQ-9 and 83 real symptom networks, it addresses the computational intractability that has limited PID beyond a few sources. This enables richer-than-pairwise analysis of mental health symptom networks.

entry.title: Multi-Modal Tumor Survival Prediction via Graph-Guided Mixture of Experts

author.name: H Mathavan, H Liu

entry.summary: Proposes a graph-guided mixture-of-experts approach for predicting cancer patient survival from clinical data, cell slides, and genomics, designed to handle missing modalities and modality variation. It leverages LLM-style few-shot capabilities while integrating multiple modalities simultaneously.

entry.title: GSLAD: Prototype-Regularized Graph Structure Learning for Multivariate Time Series Anomaly Detection

author.name: Zepeng Zhang, Fuad Khuri, Keivan Faghih Niresi, Olga Fink

entry.summary: GSLAD detects anomalies in multivariate time series by scoring deviations in learned inter-variable graph structure rather than only trajectory discrepancies, targeting faults that alter structural patterns first. A two-phase strategy learns condition-aware graphs with predictive supervision and clusters normal graphs into structural prototypes for anomaly scoring.

entry.title: From objective discovery to prediction of global ocean eco-provinces: A pathway for trustworthy learning

author.name: Makayla McDevitt, Maike Sonnewald, Stephanie Dutkiewicz

entry.summary: The paper uses unsupervised ML on outputs of a global phytoplankton functional type simulation to identify ocean eco-provinces with uncertainty measures, then builds a hierarchy of explainable dense ensemble networks to predict these provinces from ocean color fields as a proof of concept for satellite-based prediction. The emphasis on objective discovery and explainability targets trustworthy climate-impact tools. It connects climate science, marine ecology, and ML interpretability.

entry.title: Joint Optimization for Federated Learning and Transmission over Unreliable Wireless Networks with Heterogeneous Data

author.name: Changheng Wang, Xianchao Zhang, Zhiqing Wei, Lingzhu Zhao, Zhongming Yang, Zhiyong Feng

entry.summary: The paper proposes FedRW, a federated random walk averaging variant of FedAvg that mitigates client drift from data heterogeneity by updating models along random walk paths, combined with packetized retransmission to handle wireless transmission errors, and a joint optimization of resource allocation to manage transmission delays. It addresses the intersection of data heterogeneity, client drift, and unreliable links in wireless federated learning. Convergence is analyzed for the joint framework.

entry.title: Parameter isolation with domain-specific experts for incremental audio classification

author.name: Jongyeon Park, Do-Hyeon Lim, Sang-won Park, Hong Kook Kim, Kyungdeuk Ko, Hyeongcheol Geum, Jeong Eun Lim

entry.summary: The paper proposes a domain-incremental learning approach for audio classification that uses parameter isolation with domain-specific experts instead of domain-invariant features or weight regularization, aiming to avoid catastrophic forgetting without access to previous domain data. It treats incremental adaptation as a recurrent model update.

entry.title: Artificial entrepreneurial cognition: Locating and causally steering an opportunity recognition dial inside large language models (LLMs)

author.name: Christian Fisch, Angela Altmeier, Martin Obschonka, Michal Kosinski, Pin Ni

entry.summary: The paper introduces the concept of artificial entrepreneurial cognition and applies representation engineering to Llama 3.1 8B-Instruct, constructing 636 matched opportunity-recognition scenario pairs to recover and causally steer an opportunity-recognition direction in the model. It demonstrates mechanistic interpretability methods applied to entrepreneurship research.

entry.title: RFCLLM: Evaluating LLMs' Reasoning Ability of Network Protocol State Machines

author.name: Anqi Chen, Dan Goldwasser, Cristina Nita-Rotaru

entry.summary: RFCLLM assesses whether LLMs correctly interpret natural-language network protocol specifications by comparing their implicit finite-state transition representations against manually built ground truth across 16 protocols and 1482 task queries. It reveals difficulty gaps and judge biases in LLM-generated formal mappings used for security and testing. This matters because such mappings are increasingly trusted in protocol verification pipelines.

entry.title: SALUTE: Benchmarking and Adapting LLMs for the Defense Domain

author.name: Hyeongcheol Park, Sumin In, Suyeon Myeong, Hogun Park, Sangmin Kim, Moonhyun Lee, Daekyeong Park, Sangpil Kim

entry.summary: SALUTE is an end-to-end framework for benchmarking and adapting LLMs to the defense domain, including Salute-Corpus drawn from open-access U.S. military doctrine, Salute-Conv instruction data grounded in doctrine and a decade of defense news, and associated evaluation. It consolidates previously fragmented, task-specific military NLP efforts into a comprehensive pipeline.

entry.title: Language-Guided Representation Learning for Robust Cross-Sensor Material Recognition

author.name: Mashood M. Mohsan, Muhayy Ud Din, Binzhao Xu, Ahmad Abubakar, Irfan Hussain

entry.summary: The authors propose a language-guided distillation framework for tactile representation learning, using natural language descriptions of touch properties (rough, soft, slippery) as a sensor-agnostic supervisory signal to achieve robustness across different vision-based tactile sensors. They build a 39K-sample touch-language dataset to support the approach. This addresses the real problem that tactile observations vary across sensor hardware, hindering generalization in robot manipulation.

entry.title: Selective Tool Use for Agentic Change Visual Question Answering in Remote Sensing

author.name: Yakoub Bazi, Mohamad M. Al Rahhal, Mohamed A. Mekhtiche, Mansour Zuair

entry.summary: The paper proposes a selective tool-use framework in which a vision language model answers change VQA questions directly or invokes a deterministic change analysis tool for questions requiring transition statistics, area measurements, or spatial information. The VLM consumes structured observations from the tool to produce final answers, improving reliability in remote sensing.

entry.title: LIMODENet: Attention-Free Compact Encoders for Information-Preserving Onboard Satellite Image Restoration

author.name: Thanh-Dung Le, Vu Nguyen Ha, Ti Ti Nguyen, Symeon Chatzinotas

entry.summary: LIMODENet is a 0.69M-parameter, softmax- and QKV-free encoder whose residual stages read as ODE discretizations, designed for image restoration on satellite hardware (BrainChip Akida, Intel Loihi-2) that cannot run attention. It outperforms CNN autoencoders and U-Nets at matched parameters on degraded EuroSAT data, and the paper honestly decomposes the fidelity gap to unconstrained models like NAFNet and Restormer.

entry.title: LG-VLN: A Zero-Shot Vision-and-Language Navigation Framework with LangGraph State Orchestration

author.name: Jianhe Zhao, Yanhua Qiu, Zhiyu Zhang, Zibo Zhao, Jinhua Xie

entry.summary: LG-VLN is a zero-shot, monocular vision-and-language navigation framework for continuous environments that shares geometric and navigation features via dense CleanDIFT features and orchestrates navigation states with LangGraph. An online feed-forward 3D reconstruction network predicts depth, poses, and point clouds for pose estimation and global map fusion, avoiding reliance on LiDAR or panoramic sensors.

entry.title: Integrating Multi-view Multi-light Surface Reconstruction into Cultural Heritage Workflows

author.name: Baptiste Brument, Robin Bruneau, Benjamin Coupry, Vincent Demoulin, Jean M\'elou, Antoine Laurent, Fabien Castan, Jean-Denis Durou, Lilian Calvet

entry.summary: This work bridges controlled-light acquisition devices used in cultural heritage, such as RTI domes, with modern multi-view multi-light surface reconstruction methods, going beyond standard photogrammetry software that ignores illumination-varying image sets. The goal is a workflow usable by archaeologists and conservators for fine-scale surface documentation.

entry.title: When is global evolutionary search useful for variational quantum algorithms? A landscape-first study

author.name: Vojt\v{e}ch Nov\'ak, Ivan Zelinka

entry.summary: Using a landscape-first design with controlled QAOA experiments, this paper identifies two mechanisms making local search unreliable for variational quantum algorithms: parameter reuse across circuit layers and competition between 2-local and 3-local cost terms. Adaptive differential evolution achieves lower median error across unseen spin glass instances, MaxCut, Ising, and Heisenberg models.

entry.title: Vision-Force Admittance Learning for Peg Insertion into a Movable Hole

author.name: Yuzhong Chen, Yongqing Liang, Yunzhi Xu, Irving Fang, Chase Kidder, Hui-ping Wang, Raihan Haque, Yubiao Zhang, Chen Feng

entry.summary: VFAL is a framework for peg-in-hole insertion into movable targets that fuses asynchronous vision foundation model pose estimates with high-frequency force-based models, using vision as a regularization term. It adapts insertion strategies online to dynamic motion while maintaining millimeter-level precision.

entry.title: StereoPatch: Patch-Aligned RGB-Depth Fusion for Spatial Perception in Robot Manipulation

author.name: Yanan Zhou, Zhaoyan Qian, James Zhao, Weiming Zhi

entry.summary: StereoPatch introduces a patch-aligned RGB-depth representation that binds registered metric geometry directly to the RGB patches used for action prediction in visuomotor policies. On a shared 2-D patch grid, asymmetric cross-attention injects depth information into corresponding RGB features, avoiding the need for policies to learn RGB-depth correspondence from limited demonstrations. This targets failure cases where visually similar scenes require different actions.

entry.title: Toward Self-Adaptive Physical AI: Can LLM Agents Manage Long-Horizon Physical Tasks?

author.name: Varun Kaushik, Yayun Tan, Xiaofan Yu

entry.summary: Investigates whether LLM agents can manage long-horizon physical tasks zero-shot, without retraining or human intervention, as the environment changes. The authors design a multi-agent framework combining planning, tool calling, observation, and verification to test feasibility of self-adaptive physical AI.

entry.title: Fraglingo: Molecular Design via Attachment-Aware Autoregressive Fragment Generation

author.name: Thao Nguyen, Jeonghwan Kim, Zhenhailong Wang, Heng Ji

entry.summary: Introduces Fraglingo, an autoregressive fragment-based molecular generator that jointly models fragment identity and attachment in a continuous space, mirroring the edits chemists actually make. Unlike prior approaches that decouple fragment selection from attachment prediction, it avoids a closed fragment vocabulary and treats attachment as integral to generation.

entry.title: $\tau$-Elicitation: Benchmarking multi-turn entity extraction in voice agents

author.name: Soham Ray, Victor Barres

entry.summary: Introduces tau-Elicitation, a 200-task voice benchmark spanning ten entity types with controlled difficulty and caller realism, revealing that voice agents achieve exact-capture success of only 0.14 to 0.41 versus perfect performance for a matched text agent. A structured scaffold prescribing spelling, read-back, correction, and confirmation raises robust success by 14 to 31 points at a 21 to 28 percent cost increase.

entry.title: Enhancing Event Candidate Acquisition for Event Linking

author.name: Ziyang Zhang, Yinan Liu, Boyi Xue, Yingxuan Huang, Bin Wang, Xiaochun Yang

entry.summary: Presents MACE, a multi-agent method for event candidate acquisition in event linking, where evidence-specialized LLM agents extract time, location, participant, and event-type evidence before a coordinator revises the evidence set and constructs final candidates. Experiments on two benchmarks show improved candidate acquisition despite short ambiguous mentions and noisy arguments. Addresses a weak but critical stage in the entity/event linking pipeline.

entry.title: Synthetic Data in Marketing Research: How to Evaluate and When to Trust

author.name: Oded Netzer, Rajan Sambandam

entry.summary: This position/reflection paper cuts through polarized debate about LLM-generated synthetic respondents in marketing research, arguing the right question is when synthetic data works rather than whether. It distinguishes ungrounded LLM responses, segment personas, and individual-level digital twins, and proposes a taxonomy of four families of accuracy measures. The framing helps explain why reported accuracy of synthetic respondents ranges from near-perfect to near-chance.

entry.title: AI Deployment Accountability Engineering: A Vision for Accountable AI in Safety-Critical Socio-Technical Systems

author.name: Murat Kantarcioglu

entry.summary: A vision paper proposing AI Deployment Accountability Engineering (ADAE), a new subdiscipline focused on accountability during deployment in changing socio-technical environments, arguing pre-deployment model-centric properties (accuracy, robustness, fairness) are necessary but insufficient. It outlines what such an engineering discipline would cover given distribution shift, human feedback loops, and multi-agent interactions.

entry.title: Moral Rebel Agents: Decision-Making Under Conflicting Obligations

author.name: Hector Munoz-Avila, David W. Aha, Paola Rizzo

entry.summary: The paper formalizes moral rebellion - an autonomous agent deviating from user-assigned tasks when morally justified - across five architectures: amoral, utilitarian, deontic, utilitarian-deontic, and a fourth rebel form. It contributes a formal vocabulary for a safety-relevant capability where agents must weigh assigned tasks against moral obligations arising during execution.

entry.title: ANASSA: An Agentic AI Orchestration Framework for Spatial Intelligence

author.name: Constantinos Papantoniou, Brian Hilton

entry.summary: ANASSA is an agentic framework for GIS that integrates LLM reasoning, tool execution, and evaluation into semiautonomous geospatial analysis workflows. The paper synthesizes recent agentic GIS work to identify limitations in spatial reasoning and execution robustness, then proposes an orchestration architecture addressing fragmented integration of these stages.

entry.title: Four Ledgers, Not One Score: Responsible Communication of LLM-Judge Calibration in Biomedical ML

author.name: Sidi Chang, Peiying Zhu

entry.summary: The paper formalizes four distinct data ledgers for calibrating LLM judges in biomedical settings: planted perturbations, independent detector outputs, human dispositions, and human-added discoveries. Auditing a private Japanese care-handoff workflow, it shows how conflating these categories inflates apparent calibration quality and proposes transparent reporting practices.

entry.title: STHMoE: Hypergraph-Enhanced Heterogeneous Dependency Coordination for LLM-Based Urban Traffic Data Forecasting

author.name: Jiawen Chen, Qi Shao, Yongjian Chang, Mingtong Zhou, Duxin Chen, Wenwu Yu

entry.summary: STHMoE is a spatio-temporal hypergraph-enhanced mixture-of-experts framework for urban traffic forecasting that decouples traffic dynamics across frequency domains and coordinates temporal, spectral, pairwise spatial, and higher-order structural cues. It targets heterogeneous, non-stationary sensor data under evolving traffic regimes. The work advances intelligent transportation analytics by combining hypergraphs with MoE-style expert routing.

entry.title: CWM: Controllable White-Box Meta-Prompting for Adaptive Retrieval-Augmented Generation and Reasoning Ability

author.name: Keuntae Kim, Eunhye Jeong, Yong Suk Choi

entry.summary: CWM proposes a unified, task-agnostic framework integrating reasoning and retrieval-augmented generation via controllable white-box meta-prompting. It offers a low-cost alternative to black-box adaptive RAG methods without requiring external modules, aiming to improve both retrieval decisions and reasoning ability. The work targets the gap of general-purpose methods versus task-specific tuning.

entry.title: Parameter-Efficient Adaptation of Pretrained Language Models for Time-Series Forecasting

author.name: Tamanna Kumavat, Georg Brunner, Kyriakos Flouris

entry.summary: This work studies transferring pretrained language models to univariate time-series forecasting by projecting time-series patches directly into a GPT-2 embedding space, bypassing tokenization. Controlled ablations across seven benchmarks in energy, weather, traffic, and finance identify which design choices drive effective cross-modal transfer. The contribution is an understanding of transfer mechanics rather than a new SOTA forecaster.

entry.title: Empirical Evaluation of Task-Based Permission Scoping Architecture for AI Agents

author.name: Halil Burak Noyan

entry.summary: This single-author paper empirically evaluates a previously proposed task-based permission scoping architecture for AI agents, combining role-based permission ceilings, a task permission classifier, and policy-based prohibitions. It addresses the task-context mismatch that leaves enterprise agents over-provisioned with static credentials compared to human hosts. The evaluation tests whether this three-source architecture reduces credential exposure.

entry.title: Towards Optimizing SQL Generation via LLM Routing

author.name: Mohammadhossein Malekpour, Nour Shaheen, Foutse Khomh, Amine Mhedhbi

entry.summary: This paper introduces the first LLM routing approach for Text-to-SQL, dynamically selecting the most cost-effective LLM per query so simpler queries avoid the latency and dollar cost of the most capable models. Two routing strategies, score-based and classification-based, achieve accuracy comparable to the strongest LLM while reducing cost, with explainable accuracy-cost trade-offs.

entry.title: Physically Aware Radiomics Without Interpolation: Disentangling Voxel Geometry and Signal Modification in CT and MRI

author.name: David Corral Fontecha, Juan Miranda Bautista, Pablo Menendez Fern\'andez-Miranda, Sergio Rubio-Mart\'in, Lara Lloret Iglesias, Jose A. Vega

entry.summary: This medical imaging paper modifies PyRadiomics to compute texture features that respect anisotropic voxel spacing without resampling, avoiding confounds between physical geometry and interpolation-induced signal changes. The authors compare native, resampled, spacing-aware, and fake-isotropic configurations across CT and MRI. This matters because radiomics reproducibility is a persistent clinical problem, and implicit isotropy assumptions can invalidate extracted features.

entry.title: An Evolutionary Computation Framework for Multi-Agent Q-Learning with Mean-Field Environmental Feedback

author.name: Lichen Wang, Shijia Hua, Linjie Liu

entry.summary: The authors formulate a coupled agent-environment model where stateless Q-learners on a graph drive an environmental variable that modifies the payoff matrix, deriving a deterministic transport equation for the Q-value distribution under a mean-field closure, validated against Monte Carlo simulations on random graph families. This provides analytic tools for understanding coupled learning-environment dynamics in multi-agent systems. It contributes theory to MARL rather than a new algorithm.

entry.title: IMM-based Multiple Object Tracking using a State Prediction Neural Network

author.name: Chan-Bin Lim, Dong-Hee Paek, Seung-Hyun Kong

entry.summary: PR-IMM integrates a transformer-based state predictor using radar Doppler measurements as an additional mode within an Interacting Multiple Model tracker alongside CV, CA, and CT motion models, improving nonlinear motion representation while retaining physics-based stability and interpretability. Radar tracking is well suited to adverse-weather autonomous driving. It is a sensible hybrid of learned prediction and classical filtering.

entry.title: The Agentic Company OS: Substrate Inversion for Sustained Enterprise Agent Deployment

author.name: Oliver Aleksander Larsen, Mahyar T. Moghaddam

entry.summary: This position paper argues that enterprise AI agents fail in sustained operation because they reason over data structured for humans rather than for language models, and proposes rebuilding the corporate cognitive substrate around LLM-matched representations. It connects anecdotal pilot-to-production failures to a common architectural root cause.

entry.title: ProtoCAM: Interpretable Few-Shot Mask-Guided Prototypical Learning for Breast Lesion Classification in Ultrasound Imaging

author.name: Ashkan Ebadi

entry.summary: ProtoCAM is an explainable few-shot learning framework for breast lesion classification in ultrasound that combines mask-guided feature encoding, prototypical metric learning, and gradient-based visual explanations. It addresses limited annotated medical data and the need for interpretable predictions in clinical imaging.

entry.title: Predictive audio representations for early detection and tracking of hidden dynamic objects

author.name: Katerina Vinciguerra, Moritz Brandes, Danilo Hollosi, Letizia Marchegiani

entry.summary: This work uses auditory perception to detect and track occluded traffic agents for autonomous vehicle safety, extending prior single-vehicle audio studies to multi-object prediction and tracking. Audio is omnidirectional and unconstrained by field-of-view, offering earlier danger cues than cameras or lidar for hidden road users. It advances audio-based safety perception from classification and direction estimation toward full predictive tracking.

entry.title: CRAF: Cross-View Residual-Aware Fusion for Deepfake Speech Detection

author.name: Minh-Xuan Phan, Khalid Zaman, Candy Olivia Mawalim, Masashi Unoki

entry.summary: CRAF fuses self-supervised speech model representations (fine-grained acoustics) with auditory LLM representations (high-level context) via a residual-aware fusion that disentangles shared from view-specific information, improving generalization to unseen spoofing attacks. It targets the growing deepfake speech threat where generalization beyond known attacks is the key challenge. A timely audio-security contribution.

entry.title: Assessing the Applicability of Existing Design Recommendations to AI Companion Design: A Multi-Method Study

author.name: Soobin Cho, Deveshi Modi, Divya Mavinkurve, Jieqiong Ding, Mark Zachry

entry.summary: This HCI study examines which existing design recommendations for trustworthy and relational AI systems actually apply to LLM-based AI companions, and identifies what makes companionship a difficult design problem. Using a multi-method approach, it maps gaps between prior guidance and the emotional, long-term nature of companion interactions.

entry.title: A Hybrid Dependency-Aware Framework for Task Decomposition and Dynamic Agent Generation in Oracle-to-PostgreSQL Migration

author.name: Oleg Grynets, Oleg Kaskun, Alona Seletska, Daryna Tukalo, Vasyl Lyashkevych

entry.summary: This framework treats Oracle-to-PostgreSQL migration as structured task decomposition: it builds a cross-file dependency graph, condenses cycles, and dynamically generates specialized migration agents, using deterministic ANTLR parsing with LLM fallback only for unreliable units. On 116 Oracle files it produced 1,037 units with reported zero coverage gaps.

entry.title: AlgoRAG: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Theoretical Computer Science Education -- A Comprehensive Evaluation Framework for Algorithm Analysis and Complexity Theory

author.name: Sushan Adhikari

entry.summary: This paper presents AlgoRAG, a retrieval-augmented generation system pairing an LLM with a curated theoretical computer science knowledge base of textbooks, 847 lecture slides, 312 practice problems, 156 proof templates, and complexity worksheets. It adds domain-specific features like mathematical entity recognition and notation-aware retrieval to help students with formal proofs and asymptotic reasoning. The work matters because abstract TCS concepts are poorly served by generic LLM tutoring resources.

entry.title: TriCalRAG: A Three-Strategy, Retrieval-Augmented Benchmark for On-Premise LLM-Based Root Cause Analysis in AIOps

author.name: Rohit Patel, Susil Kumar Mohanty, Jeenal Chaudhary

entry.summary: TriCalRAG benchmarks open-weight LLMs (Qwen2.5-14B, Mistral-Small) served locally via vLLM against the classical DeepLog LSTM anomaly detector for root cause analysis across four public log datasets, comparing zero-shot, few-shot, and RAG prompting strategies. It targets the privacy, latency, and cost problems of cloud LLMs in production AIOps pipelines. The work offers practitioners concrete guidance on on-premise deployment tradeoffs.

entry.title: Enemray: Toward Capable Language Models for Hassaniya

author.name: Cheikh Ahmed

entry.summary: Enemray is a language model for Hassaniya, a very low-resource language, built with a stability-plasticity objective that acquires linguistic and cultural competence while preserving general reasoning and safety of the base instruction-tuned model. The pipeline uses layer-selective continual pretraining and transfers the language-specific update into instruction-tuned parameter space. It matters as a template for extending capable LLMs to underrepresented languages without catastrophic forgetting.

entry.title: Personalizing Personal Health Interfaces: Co-Design with Generative AI

author.name: Karthik S. Bhat, Vidhi Shah, Vedika Agnihotri, Dong Whi Yoo, Koustuv Saha

entry.summary: This HCI study had 14 participants co-redesign Google and Apple Health dashboards using generative AI tools (Figma Make), examining what designs emerge and how AI enables or constrains personalization. Participants created interfaces supporting personal context and future planning, but AI-generated designs tended to converge on chat-window conventions, and AI helped translate vague ideas into concrete designs while imposing structural limits.

entry.title: EMR: Self-Evolving Medical Multi-Agent System via Experience Mining and Reuse

author.name: Dongsheng Shi, Yue Li, Xin Yi, Linlin Wang

entry.summary: EMR is a medical multi-agent system that accumulates clinical experience in a hierarchical library spanning clinical principles, diagnostic patterns, and representative cases, enabling self-evolution from past diagnostic successes and failures. At inference, a planner coordinates department-specific agents in a multidisciplinary consultation pattern with a summary agent synthesizing the final analysis.

entry.title: Turkish MMLU Pro: Traceable Option Augmentation and Its Validity Limits in Turkish Multiple-Choice Evaluation

author.name: M. Ali Bayram

entry.summary: Turkish MMLU Pro is a 12,000-question Turkish benchmark with traceable option augmentation, adding five distractor options per question retrieved via sentence embeddings and selected by a language model, with deterministic verification of all 60,000 additions. A 25-model calibration shows source-key accuracies ranging 34.8%-81.4%, and one API-served model drops from 93.7% with five choices to 83.1% with ten, with most lost candidates attributable to scoring effects rather than genuine knowledge differences. The paper warns that adding options can lower scores without improving assessment validity.

entry.title: Don't Count the Edits, Judge by the Outcome Alone: Reward-Based Evaluation for Grammatical Error Correction

author.name: Hayeong Ryu, Sunhee Jo, Seunguk Yu, YoungBin Kim

entry.summary: The authors propose SURE, a source-conditioned reward evaluator for grammatical error correction (GEC) that judges outputs by outcome rather than reference or edit overlap. It is trained on within-source preferences covering both minimal-edit and rewrite-oriented corrections, jointly learning an overall reward with criteria-level supervision for grammaticality, faithfulness, and fluency, plus span-level grounding. Competitive results on the SEEDA benchmark suggest a practical path beyond reference-based GEC evaluation.

entry.title: Through the Eyes of the Beholder: Biometric and Demographic Conditioning for Multimodal Sexism Detection

author.name: Ana-Maria Luisa Mocanu, Sebastian Mocanu, Ciprian-Octavian Truic\u{a}, Elena-Simona Apostol

entry.summary: The VANGUARD team presents a human-centered multimodal framework for EXIST 2026 Task 2 that incorporates annotator psychological and demographic characteristics into sexism detection. It fuses five modalities via cross-attention with FiLM conditioning, using Gemma 4 for meme description, NLLB-200 translation, and LoRA-adapted XLM-RoBERTa and CLIP encoders.

entry.title: More Than Just Access: Generative AI as Communication Intermediary for Blind and Low-Vision Users

author.name: Protik Dey, Mohd Saifuzzaman, Taslima Akter

entry.summary: Based on semi-structured interviews with 19 blind and low-vision participants, this study examines how generative AI tools like ChatGPT, Gemini, Be My AI, and Seeing AI act as communication intermediaries substituting for interpersonal help with reading and describing. It documents what BLV users gain and risk when these tools replace human assistance.

entry.title: SlipSense: Multimodal Tactile Learning for Low-Latency and Generalized Slip Detection

author.name: Tong Jian, Aditya Thurvas Senthil Kumar, Xinyi Li, Ziling Chen, Tianyu Dai, Ali Sengul, Matteo Grimaldi, Wenjie Lu, Saleh Nabi, Tao Yu

entry.summary: SlipSense is a multimodal tactile slip-detection framework built on a compact sensor combining a 32x32 piezoresistive array at 240 Hz with a high-rate MEMS accelerometer, using modality-specific encoding, intra-sensor fusion, and cross-modal attention with causal temporal prediction. It targets precise low-latency slip detection and cross-platform generalization for dexterous manipulation, validated on 1.4 million frames. This is relevant to tactile perception for robotics.

entry.title: GradRepair-ODE: Certified Gradient Repair for Neural ODE Training

author.name: Ziqian Bi, Xin Liang Chia

entry.summary: GradRepair-ODE is a reliability framework that checks, repairs, and rejects ODE gradients at each optimizer step in neural ODE training, addressing cases where loose step sizes, stiffness, chaos, or event discontinuities yield numerically suspect gradients. This matters for scientific machine learning and continuous-time generative models such as diffusion probability-flow ODEs and flow matching. The work targets a real reliability gap in differentiable ODE pipelines.

entry.title: Operational Range Bounding in Spectroscopy: A Safety Cage Framework for Machine Learning Models

author.name: Nikki Grens, Lu\'is F. Sim\~oes, Kai Hou Yip, Theresa Lueftinger

entry.summary: The authors evaluate a modular safety-cage architecture that runs as a parallel monitoring layer over black-box ML models extracting exoplanet transmission spectra, using uncertainty quantification and out-of-distribution detection to flag invalid predictions without modifying the underlying model. This targets reliability in safety-critical space missions where ground truth is unavailable.

entry.title: Benchmarking Optimizers to Solve Inverse Problems with Differentiable Physics Simulators

author.name: Xiang Chen, Huanhuan Xia

entry.summary: The authors build 12 differentiable physics simulators spanning discrete and continuous mechanics, atomistic simulation, rendering, and semi-empirical models, and benchmark how different optimizers perform on inverse problems across them. The work targets the underexplored optimization layer of physics-based simulation and ML pipelines.

entry.title: Exploring napping paradigm for Recurrent Spiking Neural Networks

author.name: Andreas Massey, Stefano Nichele, Aliaksandr Hubin

entry.summary: Investigates a biologically inspired micro-sleep mechanism for recurrent spiking neural networks that combines proportional weight scaling with stochastic membrane activity, motivated by free-energy arguments about sleep and synaptic downscaling. The goal is to balance model accuracy and generalization in SNNs offline.

entry.title: Bayesian optimization with kernel ensembles and disagreement-based acquisition for source localization and acoustic inversion

author.name: Heng Zhang, Haotian Xiang, Florian Meyer, Qin Lu

entry.summary: Applies Bayesian optimization with a weighted ensemble of Gaussian processes across kernel families, combined with disagreement-based acquisition, to joint source localization and geoacoustic inversion where each forward model evaluation is expensive. The ensemble reduces dependence on any single kernel choice in a seven-dimensional search space.

entry.title: Privacy Preserving Gossip Learning

author.name: Erkan Bayram, Mohamed-Ali Belabbas, Tamer Ba\c{s}ar

entry.summary: The paper proposes a decentralized learning algorithm where each agent contributes one private sample sequentially, with each update preserving previously learned endpoint mappings while protecting private data. Building on Tuning without Forgetting, the authors prove an indistinguishability guarantee for learners under conditions on the protected agent set. It matters because it offers formal privacy properties in fully decentralized settings without a central aggregator.

entry.title: Multi-source Transfer Learning of Time Series with a Shapelet-based Distance Measure

author.name: Jiseok Lee, Brian Kenji Iwana

entry.summary: The paper proposes Shapelet Matching, a training-free method for selecting source datasets in time series transfer learning by comparing discriminative shapelets between target and candidate sources. It avoids the heavy cost of pre-training on each candidate source and mitigates negative transfer through multi-source strategies. This makes transfer learning more practical for data-scarce time series classification.

entry.title: Data-driven Prediction of Satellite-observed Avalanche Activity from Snowpack Simulations

author.name: Jakob Grah, Filippo Maria Bianchi, Bert Kruyt, Karsten M\"uller

entry.summary: The authors build a transformer model that predicts SAR-detected avalanche activity from SNOWPACK snowpack simulations, using five winters of Sentinel-1 avalanche detections across Norway and parts of Sweden. The model consumes five days of simulation outputs on a 20 x 20 km grid to forecast the next day's Avalanche Activity Index, which weights larger debris and spreads detections across possible dates. This helps address the sparsity of field observations over large mountain regions for avalanche forecasting.

entry.title: Knowledge-Enriched Structured EHR Features for 30-Day Hospital Readmission Prediction on MIMIC-IV

author.name: Mohamad Najafi, Hongyun Fu, Mathias Brochhausen, Jian Wu, Yaohang Li

entry.summary: The paper introduces a knowledge-enriched structured feature representation for predicting 30-day hospital readmission on MIMIC-IV, combining EHR data with four medical knowledge sources (disease ontologies, procedure classifications, drug vocabularies, lab aggregation) without relying on clinical notes. Each feature maps to a named clinical concept, yielding an interpretable and computationally cheap alternative to LLM-based discharge summary models. This is relevant for deployable clinical prediction where notes access and compute are constrained.

entry.title: Portable Semantics, Private Dialects: Reuse and Negative Transfer in Latent Communication Between Language-Model Cells

author.name: Narcis Marincat

entry.summary: This companion study audits latent communication protocols among independently trained language-model societies, running a leakage-controlled causal interoperability audit over all 30 ordered pairs of six restricted societies under a preregistered alignment ladder. It finds the six semantically similar interfaces do not form one shared raw packet language, examining where zero-shot transfer fails and whether inherited interface state helps or harms later learning. The work probes emergent convention formation and interoperability in model collectives.

entry.title: Machine learning-assisted calibration of Agent-based Models: surrogate-based optimization with Genetic Algorithm and Particle Swarm Optimization

author.name: Duguma Yeshitla Habtemariam, Jihwan Lee

entry.summary: The paper adapts surrogate-assisted evolutionary computation to calibrate agent-based models, embedding an ML surrogate inside GA and PSO loops so the expensive simulator only validates the top 50% of candidates. A 48-configuration full factorial across two optimizers, five surrogates, and four objectives is evaluated on two ABMs, including the Brock-Hommes asset-pricing model.

entry.title: Generation of Custom Solvers in Rust for Convex Optimization

author.name: Hao Zhu, Joschka Boedecker

entry.summary: cvxgenrust is an open-source code generator that produces specialized Rust solvers for families of parameterized convex optimization problems modeled in CVXPY, canonicalizing problems and emitting a crate that calls the Clarabel cone solver natively. Generated solvers can be re-exposed to Python as custom CVXPY solvers, support problems up to semidefinite and exponential cones, and show reduced runtime versus direct CVXPY solves. This enables fast, safe embedded convex optimization.

entry.title: Toward a Layer-2 Trigger for AI/ML Lifecycle Management in 6G

author.name: Dharmendra Kumar

entry.summary: The paper stress-tests activation and rollback strategies for AI/ML lifecycle management in 6G radio access networks, using 150 PPO policies in a regime-shift environment with controlled delays on corrective commands. It shows stability-gated blending dramatically reduces post-shift SLA violations and quantifies the criticality of lifecycle command latency.

entry.title: Channel-Adaptive Region Adjacency Graph Carriers for Semantic Image Communication

author.name: Karim Abdallah, Maria Slim, Mariette Awad, Hadi Sarieddeen

entry.summary: CA-RAG proposes segmentation-derived region adjacency graphs as interpretable carriers for joint source-channel semantic image communication, with channel-adaptive graph simplification and semantic belief propagation before diffusion-based reconstruction. Payloads are several times smaller than compressed-class baselines on Cityscapes.

entry.title: A Personalized Dynamic Balance Evaluation Paradigm for Hip Exoskeleton-Assisted Walking under Unexpected Ground Perturbations

author.name: Yun Chen, Oluwasegun T. Akinniyi, Qiang Zhang

entry.summary: The paper introduces a participant-specific composite balance cost combining seven biomechanical sub-metrics (stability margins, center-of-mass dynamics, angular momentum) with learned nonnegative fusion weights and an empirical-Bayes hierarchical model to personalize hip exoskeleton assistance under unexpected perturbations. It addresses the small-sample, noisy nature of human-in-the-loop experiments. This supports safer and more effective exoskeleton-assisted gait rehabilitation.

entry.title: Steady-State Convergence of Stochastic Approximation

author.name: Yixuan Zhang, Qiaomin Xie

entry.summary: This paper develops a unified steady-state convergence theory for constant-stepsize stochastic approximation with Markovian, multiplicative noise, covering both locally differentiable and nondifferentiable mean operators. It introduces a multi-step universality framework that reduces the original recursion to tractable auxiliary processes, improving on prior suboptimal rates.

entry.title: Projection-Free Multi-level Algorithms for Stochastic Constrained Compositional Optimization

author.name: Wei Jiang, Sifan Yang, Wenhao Yang, Yibo Wang, Yuanyu Wan, Zechao Li, Lijun Zhang

entry.summary: The paper develops projection-free algorithms, based on linear minimization oracles, for stochastic constrained optimization with nested compositional objectives. It provides variance-reduced methods with complexity guarantees and momentum-based variants under weaker smoothness assumptions. Such methods are relevant wherever projections onto constraint sets are expensive.

entry.title: TestHallVQA: Exploring LVLMs' Document-Level Reasoning under Redundant Contexts from Scientific Exams

author.name: Yongqi Yu, Yu Zhang

entry.summary: TestHallVQA is a multi-image visual question answering benchmark combining document-level scale with redundant, irrelevant visual content drawn from scientific exams. The authors provide theoretical analysis of how irrelevant visual tokens degrade LVLM performance and quantify this systematically. It addresses a real gap: existing benchmarks test either long documents or complex visual reasoning, rarely both with distractors.

entry.title: SyRHM: Symbolic-Language-Enhanced Reasoning with Associative Retrieval for Zero-shot Harmful Meme Detection

author.name: Hanling Wang, Chenlong Wei, Yingjuan Li, Di Wu, Yuchao Zhang, Xiaohui Zhu, Yao Zhu

entry.summary: SyRHM decomposes harmful meme detection into meaning-grounded retrieval of related memes plus symbolic-language-enhanced multi-stage reasoning, converting multimodal inputs into symbolic intermediate representations before planning. It targets implicit harm arising from visual-textual incongruity and cultural stereotypes in a zero-shot setting. This matters for content moderation where harmful intent is rarely explicit.

entry.title: Editorial routing shapes how computational results are qualified in AI-assisted scientific writing

author.name: Jihan Kim

entry.summary: Using fixed computational evidence, this single-author study finds that Claude Sonnet 5, an existing Anthropic model, omits numerical qualifications in constrained sentence-writing when comparisons are routed to a group repository rather than Supporting Information or working notes, while Claude Opus 5 is less sensitive; a simple placement rule restores correct reporting. It shows editorial context, not just accessibility, shapes how AI-assisted writing communicates uncertainty. The result has implications for scientific integrity in AI-assisted manuscripts.

entry.title: TATK: Triple-Aware Top-K Learning with Knowledge-Grounded Verification for LLM-based Sequential Recommendation

author.name: Yuchen Guan, Jiaye Liu, Yifei Han, Zhenxi Zhang, Yixuan Weng, Bin Li

entry.summary: TATK tackles the mismatch between text-generation interfaces in LLM-based sequential recommenders and full-catalog top-K ranking. It combines Top-K Learning with position-aware rewards and a Knowledge-Grounded Verification step that reranks candidates after a single LLM forward pass using a metadata-derived item graph. Evaluations on Amazon Reviews 2023 datasets show improved ranking alignment.

entry.title: Typhoon ASR Streaming: Steerable Low-Latency Thai Speech Recognition with Real-Time Shallow Fusion

author.name: Warit Sirichotedumrong, Tanawin Samutsin, Shah Faisal Wani, Sittipong Sripaisarnmongkol, Kunat Pipatanakul

entry.summary: The paper presents a deployable streaming Thai ASR system enabling decode-time vocabulary steering without retraining, addressing the failure of offline Whisper-based Thai models when run as true streams. Techniques include a cache-aware encoder and a shallow-fusion layer with a GPU n-gram language model and phrase boosting. Streaming models maintain competitive accuracy across two Thai benchmarks and two model sizes.

entry.title: What Limits Us? Analyzing Self-Reported Limitations in NLP Research

author.name: Tawan Thaepprasit, Peeranuth Kehasukcharoen, Ding Wang, Remi Denton, Peerapon Vateekul, Piyawat Lertvittayakumjorn

entry.summary: The authors conduct a large-scale meta-analysis of Limitations sections from ACL and EMNLP papers published between 2020 and 2025 using a novel human-AI hybrid qualitative coding framework. They track trends in what researchers disclose about their own work over time and how limitations correlate with paper attributes. This provides a unique empirical window into the self-assessed weaknesses of the NLP field.

entry.title: Exploring Multimodal Turn-Taking Cues in Face-to-Face Conversation using Voice Activity Projection

author.name: Willem Berner, Julio Cesar Cavalcanti, Kalle {\AA}str\"om, Gabriel Skantze

entry.summary: This work extends the Voice Activity Projection (VAP) model for turn-taking prediction in dialogue by incorporating visual features (gaze, head movement, body pose, facial action units) from the Meta Seamless Interaction dataset of face-to-face conversations. It tests whether visual cues improve turn-taking prediction beyond audio-only signals. The result is relevant to building more natural spoken dialogue systems that time their responses like humans do.

entry.title: GaugeDefect: Detecting Surface Anomalies by Curvature of Feature Transport

author.name: Yefan Wang

entry.summary: GaugeDefect introduces a geometric cue for industrial surface anomaly localization based on the curvature of feature transport, targeting defects like thin scratches and disrupted repeated patterns whose local patches still look individually normal. The core insight is that anomalies often disturb how nearby features vary and connect across a surface rather than changing local appearance. This complements existing appearance-based anomaly detection formulations.

entry.title: Multimodal Foundation Models Adaptation based on Domain-Aware Relaxed Orthogonal Subspace for Remote Sensing

author.name: Han Luo, Ruoyu Yang, Yinhe Liu, Yanfei Zhong

entry.summary: DROS reformulates low-rank adaptation for remote sensing by constructing the adaptation subspace from observed downstream activation distributions, fixing the subspace mismatch that arises when fixed LoRA subspaces face large domain shifts. The framework applies to multimodal foundation models in remote sensing tasks. It addresses a recognized limitation of PEFT under substantial distribution shift.

entry.title: Accelerating HKTex without Mesh Eigensystems: Local Unfolding and Randomized Thermal Features

author.name: Zhewen He, Junyi Hu, Yi Fang

entry.summary: The work removes the Laplace-Beltrami eigendecomposition bottleneck in Heat Kernel Textures by exploiting locality of trained kernels, replacing spectral evaluation with radius-bounded hinge unfolding and an analytic log-map kernel. It improves PSNR slightly while reducing initialization cost by 40.5x and scaling to a 749,570-vertex proxy-backed mesh.

entry.title: Mobile CT Services for Rural, Regional, and Remote Areas: Current Practice and Future Integration with Telehealth and Regulatory-Authorised AI

author.name: Zhicheng Lu, Md Zahid Islam, M Mamun Huda, Kristie Sweeney, Shayne Chau, Oliver Mulcock, Corey Hemopo, Catherine Keniry, Mohammad Ali Moni

entry.summary: A review examining mobile CT deployment platforms (trucks, trailers, ambulances), supporting telehealth technologies, and regulatory-authorised AI for CT in rural, regional, and remote settings, evaluated across clinical applications. It outlines how these elements can combine to extend advanced imaging to resource-limited populations.

entry.title: Rethinking Camouflage Image Generation towards a Training-Free Paradigm

author.name: Haodong Yang, Zhongling Huang, Gong Cheng

entry.summary: This paper reformulates camouflage image generation as a training-free task, addressing foreground preservation, semantic compatibility, and appearance assimilation without task-specific training on camouflage datasets. By avoiding costly domain-specific training, the approach improves generalization beyond the training distribution and reduces computational overhead.

entry.title: PuzzleMate: Benchmarking MLLMs for Egocentric Puzzle Assistance

author.name: Avijit Dasgupta, Shayon Dasgupta, Zakaria Laskar, C. V. Jawahar, Karteek Alahari

entry.summary: This paper introduces a benchmark using jigsaw puzzle solving as a testbed for evaluating whether multimodal large language models can provide grounded, step-by-step guidance for fine-grained physical manipulation tasks in egocentric settings. Puzzle solving demands high-precision spatial reasoning and progress tracking, exposing capabilities beyond general object recognition.

entry.title: Patient-Level, Leakage-Aware Deep Learning for Cross-Center Periapical Radiograph Classification

author.name: Md Jubaer Rahman, Ulas Bagci

entry.summary: This paper presents the first patient-level, leakage-aware classification benchmark for single-tooth periapical radiographs using DentIRO (5,300 images, 3,243 patients, two clinics, four classes), comparing five transfer-learning models under cross-center validation. It directly addresses the common but problematic image-level splits that leak patients between training and test sets.

entry.title: Zero-shot video highlight detection based on text descriptions and synthetic images

author.name: Michal Byra, Alberto Presta, Grzegorz Stefanski, Krzysztof Arendt

entry.summary: This paper proposes a zero-shot video highlight detection pipeline combining CLIP, LLMs, and diffusion models: an LLM generates textual descriptions of likely highlights from video metadata, a diffusion model converts these into synthetic visual prototypes, and CLIP matches them to frames. The approach requires no highlight annotations or dataset-specific training and performs strongly on TVSum and SumMe.

entry.title: AlignUS: MRI-Guided Ultrasound Representation Learning for ALS Classification from Tongue Images

author.name: Kadija Abdel Ghader, Emani Babe, Lorenzo Pettinari, Meya Haroune, Sidaty El Hadramy

entry.summary: AlignUS is a cross-modal distillation framework that transfers anatomical knowledge from MRI to a high-resolution ultrasound tongue classifier for ALS bulbar involvement assessment, requiring only ultrasound at inference. It combines classification loss, supervised contrastive learning, and feature-level distillation, targeting low-resource settings where MRI is unavailable.

entry.title: CapsuleMotion: A Lightweight Real-Time Visual Motion Predictor for Capsule Endoscopy

author.name: Oliver Bause, Julia Werner, Oliver Bringmann

entry.summary: CapsuleMotion is a patient-specific, on-device motion predictor for video capsule endoscopy that uses energy in a goal-directed way to increase the chance of complete gastrointestinal screening, addressing the tight battery constraints of swallowable capsules. It combines metrics from on-board image compression to predict motion between successive frames in real time.

entry.title: What a gated sensing pipeline never looks at: bandwidth reduction and the misses behind it

author.name: Raghu Venkat, Tricha Anjali

entry.summary: The paper evaluates a gated sensing pipeline for airborne sensors on contested communication links that transmits findings instead of video, combining learned detection, image-text comparison, and deterministic scheduling to achieve a large bandwidth reduction (over 40,000x) on staged footage. Notably, it candidly reports that a detection artefact inflated earlier results, and corrected code detects fewer staged events, highlighting the misses hidden by aggressive bandwidth gating.

entry.title: POLARIS: Training-Free Audio Fingerprinting with Saliency-Based Landmarks and Delaunay Grouping

author.name: Jiheng Li

entry.summary: POLARIS is a training-free audio fingerprinting system that selects landmarks from a locally normalized saliency field and groups them via Delaunay triangulation, with query-time two-hop neighborhood expansion for robustness to distortion. It achieves the best performance among training-free methods on synthetic distortion benchmarks and a new real re-recorded music benchmark.

entry.title: Transforming harmonic coefficients for 3D splat compression

author.name: Tam Thuc Do, Philip A. Chou, Gene Cheung

entry.summary: This paper addresses color attribute compression for 3D splats by showing all splat-generated images are linear in the per-channel, per-spherical-harmonic, per-splat coefficients and identifying an inner product that induces squared-error loss on images. Orthonormalizing coefficients under this inner product before coding yields over 2 dB gain.

entry.title: Constraint-Grounded Reinforcement Learning for Variable Impedance Control in Contact-Rich Robotic Insertion

author.name: Lin He, Min Deng

entry.summary: CG-RL is a reinforcement learning framework for variable impedance control in robotic insertion that adapts controller gains online without manual retuning. The policy outputs residual motion, insertion rate, and a requested gain, which a safety layer projects into the admissible range without exposing the range to the policy.

entry.title: Decentralized Multi-Robot Task Allocation Under Degraded Communication: A Benchmark of Performance, Reliability, and Computation

author.name: James Lott, Vahraz Honary

entry.summary: This work benchmarks six decentralized multi-robot task allocation algorithms (CBAA, ACBBA, PI, HIPC, DMCHBA, DGA) across 500 paired instances and 25 communication conditions including packet loss and fading. It characterizes tradeoffs among travel cost, communication robustness, allocation reliability, computation, and scale sensitivity.

entry.title: DreamSat-Bench: Development and Initial Testing of a Testbed for AI-Based Pose Estimation from 3D Reconstruction

author.name: Alex Posadas-Nava, August Berne, Giovanni Lavezzi, Kareena Shah, Alejandro Carrasco, Josiane Uwumukiza, Giacomo Battaglia, Paolo Panicucci, Minduli C. Wijayatunga, Victor Rodriguez-Fernandez, Richard Linares

entry.summary: DreamSat-Bench is a hardware/software-in-the-loop testbed for benchmarking AI-based relative navigation for satellite rendezvous, unifying MuJoCo, Isaac Lab, and LeRobot with robotic arms tracing 3D trajectories. It enables customizable orbital environments and lighting to quantify the simulation-to-reality gap for vision-based navigation.

entry.title: BIG-CBF: Behavior-Imagination-Guided Control Barrier Function with Shared Uncertainty for Mobile Robot Navigation

author.name: Shibo Li, Zhongcheng Wang, Jiahe Cao, Jianhua Yang, Ke Wu

entry.summary: BIG-CBF is a two-rate navigation architecture that couples low-rate maneuver selection among six imagined closed-loop behaviors with high-rate control barrier function safety filtering, sharing uncertainty estimates between the layers.
