It addresses the safe-but-stalled failure of minimum-intervention CBF filters in geometrically ambiguous environments.

entry.title: Learning-Based Dynamic Obstacle Avoidance for a UAV Using Only Three Range Sensors

author.name: Mohammad Reza Ranjbar Divkoti, A. Pedro Aguiar

entry.summary: The authors present a deep reinforcement learning approach using PPO for kinodynamic motion planning of a UAV with extreme sensor limitations (only three range sensors) in unknown dynamic environments. They co-design a behavior grid map representation with the control policy to handle static and dynamic obstacles under severe partial observability. The work is notable for demonstrating that reliable avoidance is possible with very low-cost sensing.

entry.title: Language-Grounded Semantic Target Navigation for Autonomous Surface Vehicles

author.name: Yuqing Lin, Youngroung Kim

entry.summary: SGNav enables autonomous surface vehicles to navigate to maritime targets specified via natural-language descriptions in port and harbor environments, rather than fixed coordinates. The framework combines text-guided semantic grounding, harbor-aware candidate filtering, CLIP-based verification, and grounded target control. It extends language-grounded navigation, well studied on land, to the maritime domain.

entry.title: From Learned-Mode AV-Traffic Pairing to Planner Decisions: A Marginal-Preserving Study on Argoverse 2

author.name: Jingyu Wang

entry.summary: Using a marginal-preserving product control intervention, this study isolates whether joint AV-traffic pairing in learned multimodal motion forecasts actually matters to a downstream planner, evaluated on 1,400 Argoverse 2 scenarios. The intervention changed only 3.0% of route-level offline selections, suggesting pairing structure has limited planner impact. This is a valuable ablation-style contribution to motion forecasting evaluation for autonomous driving.

entry.title: P-POSEMEM: Projective Semantic Memory for Consistent Language Grounding under Pose-Graph Rewrites

author.name: Ha Sier, Ali Salmasi, Mengya Xu, Haizhou Zhang, Jie Lu, Zhuo Zou, Xianjia Yu, Tomi Westerlund

entry.summary: P-POSEMEM addresses the problem of a robot's semantic memory re-binding language queries to different objects when the underlying SLAM pose graph is optimized, loop-closed, or compressed. It stores observations as immutable events at their birth keyframes, retains Bayes-tree elimination conditionals of marginalized keyframes, and integrates semantic likelihood over the reconstructed joint posterior. A total-variation defect metric quantifies grounding consistency.

entry.title: On Large-Scale Multiple Testing Over Networks: A Non-Asymptotic Approach

author.name: Mehrdad Pournaderi

entry.summary: This paper fixes a finite-sample false discovery rate violation in distributed multiple testing caused by a winner's-curse bias, quantifying it at exact order and proposing Cross-Fit Greedy Aggregation (CFGA). By selecting the rejection family on one data half and scoring it on the other, CFGA achieves finite-sample FDR control under tight communication budgets across networked sites.

entry.title: There is a channel to 900M weekly users. What goes in it?

author.name: Charbel-Raphaël

entry.summary: The author argues that Anthropic and OpenAI could communicate catastrophic AI risk directly to nearly a billion weekly users through their products, and urges aggressive use of this channel to wake up politicians before frontier agents can establish rogue deployments. The post advocates informing the public transparently as the best remaining lever for federal regulation.

entry.title: LabAgent: Customize Any Research Hubs for Scientific Discoveries Using AI Agents

author.name: Lei Liu, Yikun Zhang, Jialin Chen, Wanjia Zhao, Rex Ying, Wengong Jin, Hua Xu, James Zou, Tianyu Liu, Hongyu Zhao

entry.summary: Proposes LabAgent, a reproduce-and-discovery harness that preserves a lab's accumulated methods and corrective experiences so research workflows survive staff turnover. It uses verification mechanisms to ensure skills are executable and records corrective methods to prevent repeated errors.

entry.title: IBBench-Light: A Paired Evaluation of Task-Conditioned Responses to External Directives

author.name: Kainan Zhou, Gangzhen Qian, Zhaoyi Li, Hang Xiao

entry.summary: IBBench-Light is a paired evaluation benchmark testing whether instruction-tuned models correctly treat external records as procedures to execute versus text to process, using 144 matched pairs per model and a paired exact-contract accuracy metric requiring both members of a pair to satisfy output contracts. Results show Qwen models satisfy far fewer complete pairs than marginal averages suggest, and follow-up audits cover directive-absent controls and wording changes. Highlights instruction-following brittleness that averaged scores hide.

entry.title: ER-EDF: A Psychology-Grounded Emotion Regulation Framework for Speech Empathetic Dialogue Generation in Large Audio-Language Models

author.name: Hongyu Jin, Wenda Zhang, Runqiu Fei, Gongping Huang, Mike Conway, Ting Dang

entry.summary: ER-EDF explicitly decouples emotion perception from emotion regulation in large audio-language models for spoken empathetic dialogue, grounded in the Perception-Action Model and emotion regulation theory. The framework aims to prevent affect mirroring and instead produce calibrated, supportive responses rather than treating emotion as a direct conditioning signal.

entry.title: Diversified and Perceptible Counterfactual Examples Leveraging Expert Knowledge

author.name: Akram Bensalem (IMT Atlantique - INFO), Fahima Djelil (Lab-STICC\_MOTEL, IMT Atlantique - INFO), Marie-Jeanne Lesot (IMT Atlantique - INFO, Lab-STICC, Lab-STICC\_MOTEL), Gr{\'e}gory Smits (IMT Atlantique - INFO, Lab-STICC, Lab-STICC\_MOTEL)

entry.summary: The paper improves counterfactual explanations in XAI by encoding an explainee's perception through a fuzzy linguistic vocabulary, which imposes structural constraints that break gradient-based generation methods like DiCE. The authors propose a continuous embedding in the fuzzy domain to generate diversified, human-interpretable counterfactuals.

entry.title: Evaluation of MLLM-Agnostic Plug-and-Play Keyframe Selection Methods for Long Video Understanding

author.name: Dilip Sarkar, Md. Safayet Islam, Liang Liang

entry.summary: This paper systematically evaluates training-free, plug-and-play keyframe selection methods that help multimodal LLMs handle long videos within visual-token and compute budgets, contrasting them against retraining and MLLM-specific adapter approaches. It distinguishes query-aware and query-agnostic selection variants. The comparison is useful for practitioners choosing efficient long-video understanding pipelines.

entry.title: Not all Negation Cues are Equal: Affixal Negations Yield Better Negation Understanding

author.name: Tian Tan, Eduardo Blanco

entry.summary: The authors build NegCue, a 1.8M-sample dataset spanning single-word, multi-word, and affixal negation with over 200 unique cues, and pre-train both encoder LMs and LLMs on it. Experiments across five benchmarks show negation types contribute unevenly, with affixal negation yielding outsized gains in negation understanding. This expands negation research beyond the narrow set of high-frequency cues like not and never.

entry.title: LIMBO: Lifelong Inference-Time Memory and Budget Optimization for LLM Agents

author.name: Siddharth Sharma, Nilesh Prasad Pandey, Onat Gungor, Tajana Rosing

entry.summary: Frames inference-time memory allocation as a distinct problem class for lifelong LLM agents, since replayed experience competes with retrieval, reasoning, tool use, and verification for limited prompt and compute budgets. LIMBO replaces fixed replay policies with budget-aware optimization of what past trajectories to inject at inference time.

entry.title: Towards Evolving Context Parameterization for Large Language Models

author.name: Xiaobing Shi, Zherui Li, Yiming Jiang, Kun Wang, Yufei Guo

entry.summary: Formalizes the Memory Updating with Sequential Evolution (MUSE) task and releases MUSE-bench to evaluate whether LLMs can incorporate memory updates while preserving unaffected information and global state. Proposes PLUME, a training-free method building a global update representation to handle evolving rather than static contexts.

entry.title: Mind Which Bird You Favour: Parameterizing Adequacy-Fluency Balance in Meta-Evaluation of Machine Translation

author.name: Behzad Shayegh, Niloofar Kazemi

entry.summary: This paper shows that machine translation meta-evaluation implicitly trades off adequacy versus fluency in a way that depends on the small, filtered system samples in benchmark datasets, making the balance unrepresentative and unstable across years and language pairs. The authors expose the balance as a tunable choice by reweighting systems to hit a target while minimizing distortion from uniform weighting. This gives sensitive-domain users explicit control over evaluation priorities.

entry.title: PeerPen: AI-Assisted Writing for Online Mental Health Peer Support

author.name: Jiwon Kim, Sherry Gong, Maya Ajit, Soorya Ram Shimgekar, Yunhao Yuan, Dong Whi Yoo, Eshwar Chandrasekharan, Koustuv Saha

entry.summary: PeerPen is an AI co-writing tool for online mental health peer-support communities, offering draft generation and revision of user-written responses within a Reddit-like interface. Interviews with 15 participants show it reduced composition burden and increased confidence, while participants wanted AI to assist rather than replace their voice, raising authorship and trust questions. It matters for responsible design of AI assistance in emotionally sensitive contexts.

entry.title: Physics Informed Neural Network model for the dynamical study of Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm

author.name: Adri\'an Robles Arques, Mart\'in Ruiz Fernandez, Javier Sanchis, Miguel A. Teruel, Juan Trujillo

entry.summary: The authors build a 3D physics-informed neural network for simulating pulsatile blood flow in the aorta over two-minute intervals, extracting pressure and velocity fields and quantifying wall stress via Laplace's law. The approach avoids the meshing burden of conventional CFD by exploiting automatic differentiation, offering a faster route to haemodynamic analysis of abdominal aortic aneurysms.

entry.title: CiteGuard-RAG: A Validation-Centered AI System for Evidence-Grounded Question Answering

author.name: Sumit Barua, Guan Hong, Halil Dursunoglu, Charles Rodgers, Alvis Fong

entry.summary: CiteGuard-RAG integrates hybrid semantic-lexical retrieval, citation-constrained generation, sentence-level grounding validation, and single-pass regeneration to ensure RAG answers are grounded, citation-valid, or appropriately refused. It is evaluated on 400 questions across a housing-law dataset, PrivacyQA, and CUAD with runtime accept/refuse/regenerate decisions.

entry.title: A Machine Learning Framework for Fault Detection, Isolation, and Severity Prediction of Autonomous VTOL Aircraft

author.name: Ripon C. Sarker, Pedram H. Dabaghian, Raman Goyal, Atanu Halder

entry.summary: Develops a CNN-based framework for rotor fault detection, isolation, and severity prediction in autonomous VTOL aircraft using real flight data, learning spatio-temporal patterns from multivariate flight dynamics despite sensor noise and nonlinear aerodynamics. The work targets safety-critical early detection of component degradation.

entry.title: Learning Source Acquisition Policies by Offline Planning

author.name: Ziqi Zhao, Run Xu, Qingjian Ni

entry.summary: Introduces O-MPAC, which transfers finite-horizon risk-cost targets from complete training records into a shared source-action scorer for choosing feature groups under an acquisition budget, re-scoring after each query with a hard cost mask. The paper analyzes tied teacher targets and planning horizon effects and validates on routing and six real tasks.

entry.title: Approximating neutron-star radii using gravitational-wave only measurements with symbolic regression

author.name: Micha{\l} Bejger

entry.summary: This paper trains the symbolic regression tool pySR on TOV solutions over piecewise polytropic equations of state to discover an approximate closed-form expression for neutron-star radius from gravitational-wave-only measurements (masses and tidal deformabilities). Such an expression enables multi-messenger astronomy comparisons without electromagnetic data. It demonstrates symbolic regression producing physically interpretable scientific formulas.

entry.title: DARE: Dialectical Agentic Reasoning for Structured Knowledge Fact Checking

author.name: Yifei Li, Xiaohan Zheng, Wentao Qian, Liansheng Zhuang

entry.summary: DARE formulates structured-knowledge fact checking as an iterative retrieve-reason-reflect multi-agent process, addressing LLM program-generation weaknesses such as invalid relations, single-path reasoning, and pro-supporting evidence bias. It integrates relation-grounded evidence with dialectical self-correction. The goal is more reliable verification of natural-language claims against knowledge bases.

entry.title: Beyond Depth and Width: The Information-Slack Dilemma in Streaming Test-Time Compute

author.name: Xiaotian Zhang (Trooly.AI)

entry.summary: This position-style paper articulates the information-slack dilemma: in streaming test-time compute, early computation has time to finish but rests on revisable evidence, while waiting improves information but shrinks computational slack. It proposes taking evidence-dependent computational jobs as the unit of analysis and frames a research agenda covering incremental processing, reusable preparation, and future-dependent speculation.

entry.title: Filling the Unseen: Scene Extrapolation via 3D Gaussian Splatting

author.name: Yunlai Zhou, Yiren Lu, Tuo Liang, Disheng Liu, Vipin Chaudhary, Yu Yin

entry.summary: The paper addresses 3D Gaussian Splatting degradation on out-of-distribution novel views, proposing a holistic extrapolation and interpolation framework with an independent camera view detection mechanism that enables parallel, conflict-free extrapolation, avoiding the accumulated errors of sequential generate-reconstruct-shift cycles. This improves hole-free reconstruction in unobserved regions. The approach scales extrapolation beyond what prior generative methods achieved.

entry.title: TTDF: A Two-Stage Framework for Reliable Surgical Phase Transition Detection

author.name: Yushi Guo, Pietro Valdastri, Duygu Sarikaya

entry.summary: TTDF formulates reliable surgical workflow transition detection as a distinct event-level task operating on outputs of a frozen online phase recognizer, using a causal two-stage framework to suppress temporal jitter and workflow-illegal switches that produce false or duplicate events. This supports context-aware surgical assistance and decision support.

entry.title: From Model Patterns to Abstract Semantics in Compositional Zero-Shot Learning

author.name: Weize Li, Zhicheng Zhao, Fei Su

entry.summary: The paper proposes CLEAR, a cloze-style reasoning and re-ranking framework for compositional zero-shot learning that treats primitive variations as context-driven activation of concrete visual cues rather than independent entities. It re-ranks candidate attribute-object compositions coarse-to-fine, inspired by human perceptual processes, addressing fixed variant capacity and abstract-concrete semantic competition in VLM-based methods.

entry.title: A Memristive Synapse for Online STDP Learning and Inference in SNNs

author.name: Elia Mateu-Barriendos, \'Alvaro G\'omez-Pau, Daniel Arum\'i, Rosa Rodr\'iguez-Monta\~n\'es, Salvador Manich

entry.summary: This work presents a fully analog memristive synaptic circuit enabling online spike-timing-dependent plasticity learning in spiking neural networks, generating gradual conductance updates directly from pre- and post-synaptic spikes without external digital control. Post-layout simulations in 130 nm CMOS demonstrate learning during network operation and unsupervised neuron specialization.

entry.title: Co-Speech with You: Training-Free Personalization of Robot Co-Speech Gestures

author.name: Bosong Ding, Selma Ancel, Giacomo Spigler, Murat Kirtay

entry.summary: This paper introduces a training-free pipeline that personalizes a robot's co-speech gestures to new users by combining a frozen audio-conditioned diffusion prior with a gesture style encoder and lightweight adapters. A reusable style embedding is extracted from about 10 seconds of enrollment motion, accompanied by a Quest 3 capture app and a new dataset of spontaneous co-speech motion.

entry.title: Two-Stage Personalized Gait Phase Estimation in Stroke Survivors During Exoskeleton-Assisted Walking: An Offline Feasibility Study

author.name: Hyungseok Ryu, Pilwon Hur

entry.summary: The study evaluates personalized gait phase estimation for stroke survivors using thigh-mounted IMUs, adapting models pre-trained on healthy gait via distillation regularization followed by low-rank adaptation (LoRA). LSTM, TCN, and Transformer models were compared across five stroke survivors with leave-one-subject-out validation. It demonstrates a careful personalization pipeline relevant to exoskeleton-assisted rehabilitation.

entry.title: Identity Is More Than Recall: A Benchmark for Persistent Identity in Deployed AI Agents

author.name: Zhenyu Zhao, Roy Zhao

entry.summary: Introduces PAI-Bench, a provider-neutral benchmark evaluating whether deployed agents are faithful to a versioned, update-governed identity contract, separating recall from composition, behavioral enactment, resistance, persistence, lineage, and role-conditioned updates. Across 1,536 retained responses, a judge-independent audit finds agents recall direct-parent identifiers perfectly but almost never produce implicit self-portraits consistent with them.

entry.title: LLM-Enhanced Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning for Unified Electric Vehicles-Charging Station-Grid Optimization in Public Charging Systems

author.name: Yang Zhang, Lindong Xie, Chongyu Wang, Gaojunjie Li, Siqi Bu, Edward Chung

entry.summary: Proposes an LLM-enhanced multi-agent RL framework that simultaneously optimizes electric vehicles, charging stations, and the grid in a unified loop, using the LLM for interpretable feature selection and adaptive multi-objective balancing over high-dimensional IoT state spaces. Targets the multi-stakeholder tension between charging satisfaction, station profitability, and grid stability. A first unified treatment of this three-way coordination problem.

entry.title: Forward-Facing Near-Infrared Adds Little to Colour for Farm-Machinery Traversability: A Site-Disjoint Evaluation of Sensor-Dependent Spatial Leakage

author.name: Sungwoo Kang

entry.summary: This negative-result paper shows that near-infrared imaging does not outperform standard color cameras for daytime agricultural traversability once spatial data leakage from sequence-level splits is eliminated, re-evaluating prior benchmarks with strictly site-disjoint testing. Prior apparent NIR advantages were artifacts of spatially autocorrelated test sets. It is a valuable methodological caution about leakage in sensor benchmarking.

entry.title: To do($x$) or not to do($x$): Medical Image Counterfactuals for Dataset Augmentation

author.name: Yasin Ibrahim, Robin J. Evans, Konstantinos Kamnitsas

entry.summary: Disentangles the two conflicting senses of counterfactual image generation in medical imaging, causal interventions from structural causal models versus non-causal edits or conditional generation, and evaluates their practical consequences for dataset augmentation. The work compares three conditioning strategies to determine when causal counterfactuals actually mitigate dataset bias better.

entry.title: ECAS: An Edge-Controlled Agentic System for Validation-Gated Scientific Application Execution

author.name: Baixi Sun, Mingze Xia, Huihuo Zheng

entry.summary: Presents ECAS, an edge-controlled LLM agentic system for closed-loop execution of scientific computing campaigns on HPC with limited human intervention. It separates credential and execution authority from a cloud-hosted model to avoid exposing HPC access, and uses validation gates so that one-shot generation failures can be detected and repaired in site-specific environments.

entry.title: LiftGCN: Efficient Energy-Preserving Graph Learning via Joukowski Spectral Lifting for Finite Element Stress Prediction

author.name: Chen Zeng, Qiao Wang

entry.summary: LiftGCN is a spectrally stable graph network for finite element stress prediction that preserves high-frequency information lost by conventional smoothing message passing, using Joukowski spectral lifting to map the real graph spectrum efficiently. It achieves energy preservation at lower complexity than unitary propagation methods that rely on matrix functions and high-order approximations. This matters for engineering surrogate models on irregular meshes.

entry.title: A Multi-Resolution Multi-Domain Pre-Training Framework for Universal Traffic Forecasting

author.name: Zhouyang Liu, Jindong Han, Hao Wang, Xinyue Liu, Hui Gao, Dongsheng Li, Hao Liu

entry.summary: FlexST is a pre-training framework for heterogeneous spatio-temporal traffic data featuring a multi-resolution diffusion module that captures both short-term fluctuations and long-range trends, plus modularity and adaptivity for cross-domain transfer. It aims to improve generalization and parameter efficiency for universal traffic forecasting.

entry.title: Perceive, Refine, Reason: A Calibrated Pipeline for Measuring Indicators in Strategic Visual Communication on Social Media

author.name: Weihong Qi, Chen Ling

entry.summary: PRR is a calibrated pipeline combining natural-language prompts with vision-language detectors, pixel-level spatial refinement via the Segment Anything Model, and multimodal LLM arbitration to turn flexible detectors into auditable measurement instruments for computational social science. It addresses the gap between coarse image-level labels and the need for object-level, spatially grounded measurements at scale.

entry.title: TRACE: Two-Stage Detector-Response Estimation With Angular Cosine Expansion for Ring Artifact Correction in Photon-Counting CT

author.name: Jigang Duan, Heran Wang, Ligen Shi, Zheng Sun, Ping Yang, Xing Zhao

entry.summary: TRACE corrects ring artifacts in photon-counting detector CT caused by detector response nonuniformity, modeling residual stripe amplitudes that vary slowly with projection angle as a fixed bias plus low-order DCT components. A learnable analysis-synthesis architecture and two-stage unsupervised optimization separate ideal projections from the response-related errors.

entry.title: Mobile Multi-Robot Navigation under Runtime Uncertainty via Koopman Operator Learning and Nonlinear Model Predictive Control

author.name: Xiaobin Zhang, Konstantinos Karydis

entry.summary: The authors develop a nonlinear model predictive control framework using learned Koopman operator dynamics for multi-robot navigation, employing a lifted bilinear model that handles perturbations such as random wheel slipping. The method supports closed-loop target reaching and formation control among obstacles and is validated on hardware.

entry.title: Converge Then Diversify: Decoupling Convergence and Diversity in Multi-Objective Bayesian Optimisation

author.name: Chao Jiang, Yueling Huang, Miqing Li

entry.summary: Proposes decoupling convergence and diversity objectives in multi-objective Bayesian optimisation, arguing that tackling both simultaneously underperforms when search budgets are limited. The method first drives the search toward the Pareto front and then diversifies, improving approximation quality of the solution set.

entry.title: Solar Intelligence

author.name: Jyotsna Singh

entry.summary: Introduces a hybrid retrieval-augmented framework for solar energy decision support that unifies structured solar analytics, evidence-grounded scientific question answering, and ML forecasting. It integrates NASA POWER satellite data, Biosphere 2 ground sensors, and a curated research corpus, using DuckDB SQL for structured queries and a BM25 plus dense retrieval fusion for question answering. It matters as a domain-specific alternative to general-purpose LLMs that answer without evidence.

entry.title: SAILOR: Solver-Assisted Interactive LLM-based Optimization Recovery

author.name: Shaghayegh Sadeghi, Stephen L. Smith, David C. Del Rey Fern'andez

entry.summary: SAILOR is a proof-of-concept pipeline where an LLM translating a natural-language optimization problem into solver code detects missing numerical parameters (costs, capacities, bounds) and asks the user targeted clarifying questions before solving. Questions are prioritized using uncertainty and solver-derived sensitivity estimates of each missing value's impact. Evaluated on 1,723 instances across seven masked benchmarks, it addresses a real gap in natural-language-to-optimization workflows.

entry.title: Schizophrenia Detection from EEG Signals: A Transformer Framework with Spectrogram Representation

author.name: Abtin Shafiei, Mohsen Hooshmand, Majid Ramezani

entry.summary: This arXiv paper presents a framework for automated detection of schizophrenia from EEG recordings, converting preprocessed signals into time-frequency spectrograms via Short-Time Fourier Transform and classifying them with a transformer architecture. The authors emphasize methodological rigor, addressing common shortcomings in prior EEG classification work such as small datasets, inconsistent preprocessing, and subject-level data leakage in evaluation protocols. The work matters because reliable, non-invasive computational screening tools could complement clinical assessment for a disorder affecting millions.

entry.title: Converting Sequenced Fuzzy Cognitive Maps to Causal Virtual Worlds with Large Video Generators

author.name: Akash Kumar Panda, Olaoluwa Adigun, Bart Kosko

entry.summary: The paper shows how fuzzy cognitive maps (FCMs) with feedback structure can define the causal rules and equilibria of virtual worlds, whose scenarios are then rendered by large video generators. Dynamical meta-rules map FCM perturbations to causal scene transitions, enabling users and agents to create and manipulate causally coherent virtual-world videos.

entry.title: ProIQA: A Process-Based Framework for Fine-Grained Math Item Quality Assessment

author.name: Junkai Tong, Mingjia Li, Haoran Chen, Yaoyu Jiang, Hanjie Ge, Yixuan Wang, Hong Qian

entry.summary: ProIQA proposes a process-aware framework for assessing the quality of automatically generated math items, formulating item quality assessment across knowledge concepts, difficulty, and disciplinary competencies. It moves beyond shallow stem-based metrics by capturing the reasoning process required to solve mathematical problems. A process-evaluation dataset is constructed to support the approach.

entry.title: Data storytelling meets interpretable machine learning: Decoding AI decisions for non-experts without revealing sensitive data and model details

author.name: Lemen Chao, Zixuan Yang, Anran Fang, Mingran Sun, Ming Lei

entry.summary: The study integrates data storytelling with interpretable machine learning so that AI-generated decisions can be explained to non-experts without exposing sensitive data or model internals. Following design science research, it defines storytelling in IML, proposes the DIST Pyramid and I-P-O models, and builds an explanatory architecture.

entry.title: Bridging Thought and Action: Taming Long-Horizon Instability in Open-Source LLM Agents with a MetaTool-Enhanced ROS Framework

author.name: Kazi Abrar Mahmud, Nilotpaul Kundu Dhurubo, Tamal Kirttonia, Sabbir Hossain Ujjal, Mohammad Ariful Haque

entry.summary: The paper introduces a MetaTool mechanism for ROS-based robotic agents using open-source LLMs, forcing structured pseudo-code planning of tool invocations that persists in a scratchpad before execution. This improves task reliability and execution efficiency for long-horizon robot tasks compared to direct LLM action generation.

entry.title: On the Equivalence of Stochastic Control and Path Space Formulations for Schr\"odinger Bridges over Compact Connected Lie Groups

author.name: Hamza Mahmood, Georgiy A. Bondar, Abhishek Halder, Adeel Akhtar

entry.summary: This theoretical paper proves that, for dynamics evolving on a compact connected Lie group, the stochastic optimal control formulation of the Schrodinger bridge problem is equivalent to a path space relative entropy minimization problem. The authors use geometric tools such as horizontal lifts and stochastic anti-development to derive a Girsanov-type change-of-measure result, showing expected control energy equals relative entropy of the controlled path law versus a reference Wiener measure. This equivalence supports existence and uniqueness proofs and provides analytical foundations relevant to generative modeling and diffusion-based methods on manifolds.

entry.title: Exploring Automated Vulnerability Identification in JavaScript Code Using Large Language Models

author.name: Manit Kaushik, Ishir Bhardwaj, Pranav Gupta, Pankaj Jalote, Arun Balaji Buduru

entry.summary: An empirical study evaluating three LLM families (Gemini 1.5 Flash, GPT-4o Mini, DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-8B) for JavaScript vulnerability identification across zero-shot, chain-of-thought, and few-shot prompting plus fine-tuning, on 1,125 snippets spanning five CWE categories. It addresses a significant gap since SAST tools often miss real-world vulnerabilities in isolated snippets. Useful practical evidence on where LLMs help in application security.

entry.title: Rethinking the Implications of Human Feedback for Preference Learning in Human-Robot Collaboration

author.name: Qiping Zhang, Kate Candon, Debasmita Ghose, Marynel V\'azquez

entry.summary: Challenges the standard three-step pipeline in human-robot preference learning where fixed implication rules convert sparse binary feedback into accepted or rejected labels for unchosen actions. A user study across two collaborative simulation environments shows human-provided implication labels often diverge from the fixed rule, and using human labels substantially improves reward models.

entry.title: LPA-CWM: A Learned Physical Adjudicator for Motion Reasoning with Counterfactual World Models

author.name: Kunwei Wu, Xiang Liu, Guocai Yao, Junming Chen, Zhikang Chen, Min Zhang, Pengwei Wang, Sen Cui

entry.summary: Formulates response aggregation in counterfactual world models as candidate reliability learning, introducing a 3.0M-parameter Learned Physical Adjudicator that weights candidate motion responses by comparing visual context and response structure. The predictor and intervention generator stay frozen, and weighted responses are refined via windowed localization and paired re-evaluation.

entry.title: Biquaternionic Space with Complex-valued Attention for Temporal Knowledge Graph Completion

author.name: Rushan Geng, Cuicui Luo

entry.summary: BSCA is a temporal knowledge graph embedding model that unifies circular and hyperbolic rotations within a biquaternionic framework, using complex-valued attention to adaptively fuse time-conditioned and relation-conditioned entity representations. Experiments on five benchmarks show competitive results with the largest gains on specific datasets.

entry.title: Interpolation Is Not Invariance: Pair Count Is Not Coverage in Transformation Audits

author.name: Mohammed Ahnouch, Lotfi Elaachak

entry.summary: The paper argues that counting equivalent pairs overstates transformation-audit coverage because pairs from the same semantic object are correlated and contain algebraically redundant edges. It distinguishes four quantities (edge count, effective contrast rank, population support rank, and spectral gap) and characterizes their roles in audit coverage and deployment reliability, deriving conditions under which calibrated readers exist and quantifying unobserved risk. This provides a more rigorous statistical basis for safety audits.

entry.title: Ensemble Complexity in Photovoltaic Forecasting

author.name: Sun Ze, Zhou Liguo, Xu Yuqing, Yu Lei, Jiang Mingming

entry.summary: The paper rigorously evaluates when ensembles actually help photovoltaic power forecasting, using matched comparisons and ablations on a fixed heterogeneous predictor bank across four public datasets. It finds modest error reductions from static fusion that mostly fail multiple-comparison correction, no consistent benefit from weather gating, and evidence of group-level dependence with individual member redundancy.

entry.title: TEAR: Table Extraction with Attribute Recommendation from Texts via Large Language Models

author.name: Tong Li, Shuye Ding, Jiachuan Wang, Yongqi Zhang, Shuangyin Li, Lei Chen, Bo Li

entry.summary: TEAR targets table extraction from naturally occurring texts such as news and social media, where fixed heuristic prompts and predefined schemas fall short. The system uses LLMs with attribute recommendation to dynamically determine extraction boundaries and adapt schemas to the variability of unstructured text.

entry.title: Big Brains and Changing Environments: Cause or Consequence?

author.name: Sian Heesom-Green, Jonathan Shock, Geoff Nitschke

entry.summary: Using neuro-evolution in an artificial seasonal foraging task, this paper tests whether large brains evolve in changing environments (Cognitive Buffer Hypothesis) or in stable conditions and later enable colonization of changing environments. Agents evolved exclusively in changing environments are compared to agents first evolved in static environments before transitioning. Larger networks in dynamic environments arise mainly from prior static evolution and confer superior performance under unpredictable change, challenging strict CBH predictions.

entry.title: CIDERS: Cloud-Edge LLM Collaborative Learning via Accelerating Personalized Bilevel Optimization

author.name: Victor H. Chen, Hairui Yu, Stella K. Chung, Hong Yan

entry.summary: CIDERS introduces a personalized bilevel optimization framework for cloud-edge LLM collaboration, with the upper level optimizing edge-side personalization and the lower level governing cloud-side knowledge transfer. This aims to balance a unified global knowledge foundation with domain-specific adaptation at the edge.

entry.title: BudgetBench: A Budget-Tiered Protocol and Pilot Harness for Memory Strategy Evaluation in Local Large Language Model Agents

author.name: Aditya Karnam Gururaj Rao, Arjun Jaggi

entry.summary: BudgetBench treats per-call input-token budget as the independent variable when comparing memory strategies for local LLM agents, sweeping 2K-32K token budgets while holding model, task, sampler, and decoding fixed, and measuring quality, latency, and budget-violation rates. The core contribution is a reusable measurement surface with a swappable MemoryStrategy contract and explicit budget enforcement. It standardizes an evaluation dimension that most agent memory work ignores.

entry.title: GeoTTER: Leveraging Local Geometry of Optimal Transport for Zero-Shot Classification

author.name: Wei-Yang Alex Lee, Rudrasis Chakraborty, Vishnu Lokhande

entry.summary: GeoTTER reformulates optimal transport for zero-shot classification by adding graph-Laplacian smoothing to enforce neighborhood consistency and correct angular drift, instead of relying on fixed cost matrices from pre-trained embeddings. This addresses miscalibration and manifold jitter in standard OT-based zero-shot methods.

entry.title: Machine Learning under Imperfect Data: Challenges and Methods

author.name: Masoumeh Zareapoor

entry.summary: A short survey organizing methods for learning with missing, corrupted, imbalanced, weakly labeled, or distribution-shifted data around shared mechanisms such as information loss, biased empirical risk, and ambiguous supervision. It unifies problems usually treated separately under a common conceptual lens.

entry.title: GNN4PPM: Multi-Target Predictive Process Monitoring with Relational Graph Convolutional Networks

author.name: Ana Costa, Johannes M\"akelburg, Luise Pufahl

entry.summary: GNN4PPM is a predictive process monitoring approach that predicts all next events along with their full data payloads simultaneously, rather than only activity labels and timestamps. It represents event log information in a heterogeneous knowledge graph processed by relational graph convolutional networks. This matters because it exploits event-log attributes that standard process monitoring methods ignore, improving applicability to real enterprise processes.

entry.title: HGTO: A Unified Graph-Based Physics-Informed Formulation for Structural Topology Optimization

author.name: Kangzheng Liu, Uday Kumar Punna, Leixin Ma

entry.summary: HGTO extends complete neural topology optimization from coordinate-space density and displacement fields to finite-element graph space, parameterizing element densities on the element graph and determining structural state on the corresponding node-edge structure. This better exploits the discrete relationships inherent in finite element meshes than prior coordinate-field physics-informed approaches. It matters for data-free engineering design optimization of structures.

entry.title: Assembling the CREW: A Collaborative Multi-agent Reinforcement Learning Framework for Automated Related Work Generation

author.name: Hai-Dang Dang, Bao-Yen Pham, Bao Nguyen, Tran Thi Huong, Huynh Thi Thanh Binh

entry.summary: CREW is a multi-agent LLM framework where agents use reinforcement learning to dynamically choose actions like Retrieve, Disseminate, and Compose when generating related-work sections, replacing rigid predefined agent pipelines. The work targets automated scientific writing assistance. It matters as an example of RL-based dynamic coordination in multi-agent LLM systems for a concrete scholarly task.

entry.title: ViFA-Council: Multi-Agent LLM Deliberation for Vietnamese Folk Art Generation

author.name: Hai-Dang Nguyen, Minh-Phuong Pham, Thao Thi Phuong Dao, Trong-Le Do, Vinh-Tiep Nguyen, Trung-Nghia Le

entry.summary: ViFA-Council is a three-stage multi-agent framework orchestrating GPT-4o, Gemini 3.1 Pro, and Claude Sonnet 4.6 for culturally complex generation tasks: Vietnamese folk painting outpainting and educational story generation. Structured JSON-schema-mediated deliberation enforces cultural constraints and mitigates stylistic hallucination from single-model pipelines.

entry.title: A pullback-corrected scalar auxiliary variable optimizer with momentum and adaptive mobility

author.name: Jiahao Zhang, Shiheng Zhang, Guang Lin

entry.summary: The paper extends the pullback-corrected scalar auxiliary variable method into an optimizer with momentum and adaptive mobility for scientific machine learning objectives such as PINN loss sums. A mobility nonincreasing in the Loewner order yields an exact modified energy law covering Euclidean and AMSGrad-type choices, applied in a single implicit solve.

entry.title: Conditional Quantum Flow Matching for Data-Scarce Physiological Signal Augmentation

author.name: Chi-Sheng Chen, Samuel Yen-Chi Chen

entry.summary: The paper introduces Conditional Quantum Flow Matching (CQFM), a 306-parameter quantum circuit conditioned on flow time and class label that transports a class-conditional prior toward the target distribution, claimed as the first conditional quantum flow matching model and first EEG augmentation on a parameterized quantum circuit. A nonnegative spectral embedding avoids tomography at readout. Experiments on BCI Competition IV-2a show benefits of starting from an informative prior over noise.

entry.title: HELENA for 5G NR LEO NTN Channel Estimation: A Comparative Evaluation

author.name: Miguel Camelo Botero, Nina Slamnik-Krije\v{s}torac, Johann Marquez-Barja

entry.summary: The authors evaluate whether HELENA, a deep-learning channel estimator designed for terrestrial 5G, remains effective when retrained for Low Earth Orbit non-terrestrial networks, which suffer Doppler and synchronization impairments. They benchmark the unchanged architecture against eight terrestrial-origin models and an NTN-specific model (MDELA) on both high-performance and power-constrained platforms. The work addresses a timely question as satellite-based 5G deployments expand.

entry.title: Shared KV Caching for Replicated 27B Inference: Correctness Failures and Performance Boundaries

author.name: Frank Li

entry.summary: The paper studies cross-replica sharing of KV caches for two vLLM replicas of a 27B model over a shared host-memory LMCache pool, identifying a raw-pointer fallback bug that omits a CUDA stream dependency and causes correctness failures. It documents controlled tests, a working deployment path via the mixed allocator, and performance boundaries including cross-replica time-to-first-token gains.

entry.title: Improving the Last-Iterate Guarantees of Anytime Algorithms for Stochastic Monotone Variational Inequalities

author.name: Jun-Hyun Kim, Ahmet Alacaoglu

entry.summary: The authors analyze a single-loop, single-sample Halpern-anchored stochastic algorithm for convex-concave problems and monotone variational inequalities, proving an anytime last-iterate rate of O(t^-1/4), improving the best-known O(t^-1/5). The analysis covers unbounded feasible sets and stochastic oracles without bounded variance.

entry.title: Learning under Target Shift: Optimal Density Ratio Estimation and Importance-Weighted Regression

author.name: Ren-Rui Liu, Zheng-Chu Guo

entry.summary: This work addresses density ratio estimation and importance-weighted regression under target shift with continuous outputs, a setting far less understood than the discrete case. The authors propose an RKHS spectral regularization method with explicit finite-sample convergence rates and near-minimax optimality. This provides theoretical grounding for covariate/output-shift correction in regression.

entry.title: Sweet Talkers: How Query Formulation Shapes Sycophancy in Romantic Relationship Advice

author.name: Helena Choi, Edric Castel Hao, Karl Bautista, Francis Gabriel Magleo, Renzo Panti, Danielle Beatrice Olalia

entry.summary: Using a 2,400-prompt dataset (RRASP) across five relationship themes, this paper measures social sycophancy with the ELEPHANT framework on GPT-5 Mini and Gemini 3 Flash, two existing consumer models. It finds grammatical mood alone does not drive sycophancy, while perspective-driven framing has stronger effects. The work highlights how face-preserving behavior in emotional-support contexts can reinforce harmful interpersonal dynamics.

entry.title: Formal Properties of Language as Constraints on Neural Dynamics

author.name: Elliot Murphy

entry.summary: The paper proposes the Neural Admissibility Program: deriving algebraic invariants of language, such as non-associative hierarchical grouping, commutativity, recursive closure, and structured workspace transitions, that any neural mechanism implementing language must preserve. It offers candidate mechanisms including content-addressable workspace memory and graph-structured transient dynamics. This is a theory-forward reframing of how to constrain neural models of language.

entry.title: Domain-specific Pretraining Profile and Transformer Performance: Evidence from Modeling Digital Pragmatics in Arabic-English Code-switching

author.name: Fahad Al Hussen, King Saud University, Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, Mohammed Q. Shormani, Ibb University, Ibb, Yemen

entry.summary: This study evaluates how domain-specific pretraining affects Transformer performance on classifying pragmatic functions in Arabic-English code-switched social media text, comparing MARBERT, XLM-R, and BERT on 11,695 X posts. MARBERT substantially outperforms XLM-R, with validation Macro F1 rising from 0.39 to 0.84. The findings underline the importance of pretraining domain match for code-switched, culturally embedded discourse.

entry.title: Merging the Knowledge of LLMs for Automatic Speech Recognition

author.name: Hayato Futami, Tatsuya Kawahara

entry.summary: The paper proposes incorporating external language models into LLM-based ASR systems via model merging rather than decoding-time fusion, using arithmetic operations on LoRA parameters for domain extension and transfer. This eliminates the extra inference cost of shallow fusion or density-ratio methods. It offers a practical efficiency gain for high-quality ASR with strong language modeling.

entry.title: CALICO: A Human-Centered, Codebook-Aligned System for Annotation

author.name: Boqin Yuan, Xiaoyi Gu, Fiona Li, Chang Wan, Angel Hsing-Chi Hwang, Jieyu Zhao

entry.summary: CALICO is a human-centered workflow for LLM-assisted codebook-based annotation that treats prompts as editable, versioned, and optimizable artifacts rather than fixed hidden instructions. It integrates codebook parsing, prompt generation, result inspection, versioning, natural-language human feedback, and label suggestions, enabling non-technical domain experts to diagnose and correct model behavior. This addresses a real gap in reliable, auditable LLM-assisted scientific annotation.

entry.title: SJD-SV: Speculative Jacobi Decoding with Semantics Verification for Autoregressive Image Generation

author.name: Baoquan Zhang, Bingqi Shan, Shihao Fang, Kenghong Lin, Xutao Li, Yunming Ye

entry.summary: The paper analyzes why Speculative Jacobi Decoding suffers from token ambiguity during verification, using visualization to show that vision tokens correspond to small local unclear details unlike text tokens, so a single token cannot express a clear semantic. It proposes SJD-SV, which adds semantics verification to speculative Jacobi decoding for autoregressive image generation. The work both explains a known failure mode and offers a fix that accelerates image generation.

entry.title: RxScribe Bench: A Multi-Axis Benchmark for Evaluating Vision-Language Models on Indian Outpatient Prescriptions

author.name: Somil, Vijay Saini, Vidit Verma, Riya, Aastha Batta, Vibhuti Malhotra, Chayan Khetan, Piyush Mittal, Puneet Poonia

entry.summary: RxScribe Bench evaluates vision-language models on handwritten prescription digitization for Indian outpatient settings, decomposing errors into four axes tied to clinical severity instead of one blended accuracy figure. This distinguishes a fabricated drug name from a misread dose, which carry very different clinical risks. The benchmark provides field-level comparison against human-authored structured ground truth.

entry.title: CirrGuide: A Deep Cascaded Framework for Liver Cirrhosis Segmentation and Severity Classification from T2-Weighted MRI

author.name: Muntaqim Ahmed Raju, Ruizhe Ma

entry.summary: CirrGuide links localization and classification for cirrhotic liver analysis: an Attention U-Net with ResNet50 encoder predicts a soft cirrhotic liver mask that serves as an anatomical prior for a multi-scale classification branch. This targets the challenge of subtle, spatially variable imaging patterns across adjacent cirrhosis stages.

entry.title: Contour-Guided Spectral Routing for Robust Real-Time Pedestrian Detection

author.name: Sam Williams, Yuan Xiang

entry.summary: The paper proposes a unified contour-guided spectral routing view for real-time pedestrian detection, explicitly ordering spectral context augmentation, spatial-spectral cue exchange, and boundary-conditioned cross-scale fusion rather than treating these as independent add-ons. This addresses coupled failure modes of tiny targets, occlusion, and adverse weather in driving scenes.

entry.title: ESAFusion: LiDAR--4-D Radar Fusion via Local Geometric Complementation and Multiscale Adaptive Interaction for 3-D Object Detection

author.name: Gang Ma, Senjie Hu, Junjie Liu, Chao Wang, Hui Wei

entry.summary: ESAFusion is an evidence-aware, scale-adaptive LiDAR-4D radar fusion framework for 3D object detection, introducing an Evidence-Aware Radar Selection module to suppress radar clutter and multiscale adaptive interaction to handle spatially varying modality importance. It targets reliable cross-modal complementation despite sparse radar observations.

entry.title: PC$^2$-AD: Point Cloud Upsampling to Safeguard 3D Anomaly Detection with Resolution-constrained Edge Devices

author.name: Yutong Gu, Yingxi Xie, Kejin Huang, Jian Ning, Hanzhe Liang, Linlin Shen, Jinbao Wang

entry.summary: PC2-AD compensates the train-test sampling-resolution gap in 3D anomaly detection by upsampling sparse test point clouds before detection, using target-domain candidate generation, geometry-aware filtering, and normality-preserving point compensation. This addresses a real deployment problem where low-cost edge sensors produce inputs sparser than training data.

entry.title: DNF-SR: Dual-Input and Negative-Aware Feature Fine-Tuning for Real-World Image Super-Resolution

author.name: Shuhao Han, Wenjie Liao, Hayden Vance, Hang Dong, Rui Zhang, Chun-Le Guo, Chongyi Li

entry.summary: DNF-SR improves one-step diffusion-based real-world image super-resolution by tackling the distribution gap created when low-resolution inputs are fed to a diffusion model. It uses a dual-input strategy and negative-aware feature fine-tuning to avoid the content corruption that naive noise addition to LR latents causes.

entry.title: Deep Learning-based Intelligent Diagnosis of Congenital Uterine Anomalies in 3D Ultrasound

author.name: Yueyue Xu, Yuhao Huang, Jiaxiao Deng, Yuanji Zhang, Haoming Zhang, Jiajia Qu, Shiying Zheng, Xiaomei Tang, Haining Chen, Chengcai Chen, Yiyi Wu, Xin Yang, Dong Ni

entry.summary: CUA-Net classifies congenital uterine anomalies from 3D ultrasound without requiring coronal plane reconstruction, built on 3D ResNet-18 with dynamic resampling, hard sample mining, self-supervised reconstruction, and online augmentation. It was compared against other deep learning methods and junior/senior sonographers to assess clinical applicability.

entry.title: BSC-Net: A Small-Branch-Sensitive Structural Continuity Network for Coronary Vessel Segmentation and Quantitative Angiographic Analysis

author.name: Wanxian Li, Jiaqian Qin, Qingyi Xian, Yazhi Li, Song Chen, Liman Li, Hao He

entry.summary: BSC-Net is a ResNet-U-Net-based segmentation network for X-ray coronary angiography that improves small-vessel representation via targeted sampling and repairs vascular connectivity using long-range context modeling and an Edge-Informed Loss. Accurate vessel maps enable quantitative coronary analysis for artery disease assessment.

entry.title: MambaMPD: A Mamba-Driven Segmentation Framework for Marine Pollution Detection from Remote Sensing Imagery

author.name: Shuaiyu Chen, Wei Han, Peng Ren, Chunbo Luo, Zeyu Fu

entry.summary: MambaMPD adapts vision Mamba architectures to marine pollution detection in remote sensing imagery, adding Frequency-Aware Augmentation with wavelet processing and multi-scale Edge-Guided Attention to handle low signal-to-noise ratios, fragmented pollution patterns, and indistinct boundaries. It targets protection of coastal ecosystems and marine biodiversity.

entry.title: Proximal-Only Transmission Matrix Recovery of an Arbitrarily Deformed Graded-Index Multimode Fiber

author.name: Cole Reynolds

entry.summary: This work presents a machine learning approach to recover transmission matrices of arbitrarily deformed graded-index multimode fibers from proximal-only measurements, aimed at practical fiber endoscopy. It shows neural networks can generalize to unseen deformation states, addressing a key barrier to thin imaging conduits.

entry.title: How Well Do Pseudo-Rigid Body Models Capture Real Plants? In-Field Validation of Simulated Blueberry Canes

author.name: Hannah Kolano, Chelse VanAtter, Wei Yang, Cindy Grimm, Joseph R. Davidson

entry.summary: The paper validates pseudo-rigid body (coupled spring-loaded beam) models of blueberry canes against real plant mechanics in field conditions, targeting simulation tools for robotic pruning. It grounds the model in real material properties and beam bending theory, addressing a rare-but-critical sim-to-real validation gap for deformable agricultural objects.

entry.title: Robotic Servo Tracking of Moving Targets with Dynamic Imitation Constraints

author.name: Yazhe Luo, Sipu Ruan, Yifei Li, Diansheng Chen

entry.summary: The paper proposes a visual servo tracking method for moving targets that imposes explicit trajectory constraints via a dynamic imitation model with time-scalable deformation and trajectory modulation. This prevents trajectory discontinuity, oscillation, and overly conservative behavior common in residual-to-velocity servo mappings, with convergence analysis provided. It contributes to constrained visual servoing for dynamic scenes.

entry.title: An Information-Space Perspective to Scene Graph Sufficiency for Robotic Task Planning

author.name: Ba\c{s}ak Sak\c{c}ak, Francesco Verdoja

entry.summary: This paper formalizes what constitutes a sufficient scene graph for robotic task planning within an information-space framework, defining scene graph transition systems and action semantics for navigation and manipulation. It introduces derived scene graphs via information mappings that merge and prune nodes, providing a general task-centric answer to when a pruned abstract representation still supports correct planning.

entry.title: Distributed Fast Fixed-Point Algorithms for Composite Monotone Inclusions over Networks

author.name: Nghia Nguyen-Trung, Ion Necoara, Quoc Tran-Dinh

entry.summary: The paper proposes two decentralized accelerated algorithms, ND-DFFP and NI-DFFP, for composite monotone inclusion problems where agents hold private operators, integrating Nesterov-type acceleration with primal-dual techniques. It provides exact convergence rates in the primal space, addressing a gap since prior distributed algorithms for this class were non-accelerated with unexplored rates.

entry.title: OpenAI Says It’s Not Responsible for the Leading the Future Super PAC. But Only Its Employees Seem to Believe That.

author.name: garrison

entry.summary: A journalist-compiled post from the Obsolete Substack arguing that OpenAI bears implicit responsibility for the Leading the Future super PAC, situating this within a recent news cycle involving a former researcher resignation warning and an OpenAI agent incident at Hugging Face. It examines the political economy and public-relations posture of the leading AI lab.

entry.title: Token Efficient Task Execution via Application Behavior Modeling for Web Agents

author.name: Alexandru Ianta, Eleni Stroulia

entry.summary: Presents OdoBot, a web-agent architecture that drastically reduces token cost by learning a behavioral model of the underlying web application from successful task demonstrations rather than repeatedly parsing the UI. Experiments on 45 tasks in a Canvas LMS show task completion at a fraction of conventional web-agent cost.

entry.title: Carbon-Aware Routing for Function Calling in Edge-Cloud LLM Systems

author.name: Aikaterini Maria Panteleaki, Varatheepan Paramanayakam, Spyros Tragoudas, Iraklis Anagnostopoulos

entry.summary: Introduces a carbon-aware routing framework that distributes LLM function-calling queries across a three-tier edge-cloud architecture, using a lightweight k-NN predictor to estimate per-query accuracy, delay, and power on each tier. Predictions are combined with real-time grid carbon intensity to route queries, reducing energy use and emissions.

entry.title: Cost Characterization of Vertically Partitioned Federated Knowledge Graphs

author.name: Md Saikat Islam Khan Bappy, Oshani Seneviratne

entry.summary: Formalizes vertical partitioning of knowledge graphs as a design space and compares four partitioning strategies—semantic domain grouping, frequency-balanced, co-occurrence graph-cut, and random—using metrics including communication cost, candidate set size, indexing, load balance, and query latency. Provides the first systematic cost characterization for this setting, informing a key data management decision in multi-organization knowledge graphs.

entry.title: Positioning manuscripts in the scientific landscape with agentic AI

author.name: Jiawen Chen, Zichen Zhang, Bingxuan Li, Quan Sun, Yiyan Zhang, Edric Tam, Jinjie Lin, Didong Li, Yun Li, Bingxin Zhao

entry.summary: Introduces PASS, an agentic LLM system that positions a research manuscript within its literature context to predict its best-matching publication venues, helping researchers navigate the stressful and uncertain submission process. The system performs literature-aware reasoning about venue fit rather than simple classification. A practical application of agentic AI to the scientific workflow.

entry.title: ClinAgent: A ReAct-Based Agent for Conversational Access to Clinical Trial Information

author.name: Antonino Vaccarella, Riccardo Cantini, Domenico Talia, Paolo Trunfio, Marianna Talia, Rosamaria Lappano, Marcello Maggiolini

entry.summary: Introduces ClinAgent, a conversational agentic RAG system letting clinicians query clinical trial registries in plain language with grounded, multi-turn responses, built around a ReAct LLM agent that iteratively reasons, selects among integrated tools, and refines actions from intermediate outputs. Addresses a manual, error-prone registry-querying workflow with cross-source synthesis. A solid applied healthcare NLP system.

entry.title: Semantic Knowledge Technologies: what the Semantic Web lost sight of, and what it never had

author.name: Achille Zappa

entry.summary: A reflective paper diagnosing why the Semantic Web delivered standards as knowledge infrastructure but not the promised machine competence, while LLMs now answer scientific questions without inspectable knowledge accounts. It proposes an extended program, Semantic Knowledge Technologies, that keeps the semantic-web technical core but adds missing pieces: conditions of applicability, provenance, and justification. A substantive position piece on reconciling formal knowledge representation with LLMs.

entry.title: Diffusion-Based Generation of Gait Trajectories

author.name: Damian Benasco, Juan Carballeira-Lopez, Jaime Ramos-Rojas, Julio S. Lora-Millan, Antonio J. Del-Ama, David Rodriguez-Cianca, Pablo Lanillos

entry.summary: The authors apply conditional diffusion models to generate lower-limb joint-angle gait trajectories conditioned on patient-specific parameters like step length, for exoskeleton and rehabilitation robotics. They compare a transformer diffusion baseline with a controllable diffusion transformer variant incorporating additional conditioning. A solid application of modern generative modeling to a biomechanical problem.

entry.title: Empirical Evaluation of Open-Source Large Language Models for Retrieval-Augmented Generation in ESG Domain

author.name: Motaz Saad, Anna Borrelli, Ivan Gentile, Kianna Kazemi, Francesco Piccialli, Antonella Longo

entry.summary: This paper evaluates seven open-source LLMs (2B to 30B parameters, including glm-4.7-flash, nemotron-3-nano, qwen3, gemma3/4, and ministral-3) on RAG-based ESG KPI extraction using 498 real-world ESG reports from EU-listed companies and 100 persona-based synthetic QA pairs. It provides a structured evaluation framework for a domain where open-source model performance is poorly understood. The resource supports corporate accountability automation.

entry.title: NoteVQA: Benchmarking VLMs on Real-Life Questions from Human Communities

author.name: Haonan Jiang, Guojian Zhan, Jiancong Xie, Shijun Wan, Dongiia Zhao, Cheng Chen, Yahui Liu, Yao Hu, Chuan Mu

entry.summary: NoteVQA is a benchmark of 252 photo-grounded visual question answering items curated from real questions that users on Xiaohongshu asked other people, spanning 12 categories and 7 intents, with reference answers distilled from expert community responses. It evaluates vision-language models on the long tail of everyday visual questions rather than predefined capabilities.

entry.title: Multilingual Agent System for Inclusive Wildfire Evacuation Guidance

author.name: Shruti Kulkarni, Lynn Tong, Aditi Namboodiripad, Chelyah Miller, Helen Lin, Peeyush Patel, Bogdan Bistriceanu, Diane Myung-kyung Woodbridge

entry.summary: BEACON is a multilingual agent service providing personalized wildfire evacuation guidance, including navigation routes, checklists, and a chatbot, aimed at the large US population with limited English proficiency who are underserved by English-only emergency alerts. The system applies LLM agents to a high-stakes social-good domain. Its value lies in demonstrating inclusive emergency-response AI rather than novel technique.

entry.title: Adaptive Phase-Switching for Communication-Efficient Federated LoRA Fine-Tuning

author.name: Jerry Adams Franklin

entry.summary: The paper measures per-round upload and download bytes for bidirectional federated LoRA protocols, correcting prior accounting that omits asymmetric transition rounds and grouped-query attention shapes, and places five methods on a single communication-quality frontier. It proposes ReverseAdaptive, an aggregator that locates the frontier knee by monitoring relative loss improvement.

entry.title: Real-Time Synthesis of Robust Controlled Invariant Sets for Monotone Systems

author.name: Yasin Sonmez, Mahmoud Khaled, Majid Zamani, Murat Arcak

entry.summary: Introduces a threshold-function reformulation that represents lower-closed safe sets on a d-dimensional grid via column heights along a designated axis, accelerating controlled invariant set synthesis for monotone systems with lower-closed safety specifications. The approach targets online computation of formal safety certificates for autonomous systems where standard fixed-point algorithms scale poorly.

entry.title: Surrogate-Assisted Genetic Programming with Phenotypic Characterisation in Dynamic Multi-Mode Project Scheduling

author.name: Yuan Tian, Yi Mei, Mengjie Zhang

entry.summary: The paper studies how to encode GP individuals into phenotypic characterisations to build effective surrogates for expensive simulation-based fitness evaluation in dynamic multi-mode resource-constrained project scheduling. It compares three PC encoding schemes under a fixed budget of full evaluations.

entry.title: A property-registry contract for retrieve-or-refuse thermal-mechanical lattice search

author.name: Shaoliang Yang, Henry Chu, Zu Yashengjiang, Jun Wang

entry.summary: This paper applies conflict diagnosis to a catalogue of 1,397 homogenized unit cells and 19 base materials so that a design system can either return a valid lattice candidate or report which requirements are jointly unsatisfiable and which to loosen, rather than returning a nearest match or a hallucinated design. For infeasible constraint sets of up to eight constraints it returns inclusion-minimal unsatisfiable subsets. The retrieve-or-refuse framing is a disciplined alternative to unconstrained generative suggestion.

entry.title: From Visual Feedback to Textual Reviews: A Multi-Agent Vision-Language Framework for Image-Grounded Review Assistance

author.name: Utsav Kumar Nareti, Ayush Bansal, Kumari Priya, Chandranath Adak, Soumi Chattopadhyay, Muhammad Saqib, Saeed Anwar

entry.summary: The authors define a new task, image-grounded review assistance, which generates editable review drafts from user-uploaded product images so visual feedback can be converted into contextual textual reviews for e-commerce. Unlike image captioning, the task requires product-specific analysis of quality, defects, and usage. They propose a multi-agent vision-language framework to solve it.

entry.title: CAL-MOS: Bridging Layers with Adapters for Robust MOS Prediction Across Speech Foundation Models

author.name: Alef Iury Siqueira Ferreira, Pedro Lustosa Rege Botelho, Fernanda Silva, Daniel Casanova, Rafael Faustino, Frederico Oliveira, Arlindo Galv\~ao Filho, Anderson da Silva Soares

entry.summary: CAL-MOS studies mean opinion score (MOS) prediction using speech foundation models, benchmarking ten SFMs across four datasets under full fine-tuning, last-layer probing, and naive cross-layer aggregation. The authors find the best layer is strongly backbone- and dataset-dependent and that naive weighted fusion is unstable, motivating a layer-calibrated adapter-based aggregation method. This improves robustness of speech quality assessment across settings.

entry.title: Spook the Machine: Gamified Exploration of Human Imagination of Machine Fear

author.name: Levin Brinkmann, Hiromu Yakura, Sonia Nicoletti, Mar Canet Sola, Thomas F. Eisenmann, Ali Dasmeh, Omar Sherif, Bramantyo Ibrahim Supriyatno, Prateek Gupta, Ignacio Serna, Rodrigo Bermudez Schettino, Iyad Rahwan

entry.summary: This paper presents Spook the Machine, a gamified platform where 832 participants in a Halloween 2024 public deployment created 15,719 images to frighten AI agents with personality-driven phobias that responded with emotional reactions. Using a 2x2 design varying emotional expressiveness and reward structure, the study examines how humans try to scare machines and how machine emotional expression affects engagement. It offers insights into affective human-AI interaction design.

entry.title: Sylvas: Synergistic Learning Value based Device Scheduling in Federated Continual Learning

author.name: Yuxuan Sun, Yuxuan Bai, Tan Chen, Sheng Zhou, Zhisheng Niu

entry.summary: Sylvas is a device-scheduling framework for federated continual learning at the wireless edge that quantifies each device's contribution to global learning under spatio-temporal distribution dynamics and label scarcity. It evaluates learning value from distributed and synergistic perspectives to schedule the most valuable devices under resource constraints.

entry.title: Discovering and Preserving Category Correlation Knowledge via Adaptive Reciprocal Knowledge Distillation

author.name: Dawen Jiang, Zhishu Shen, Zeyu Liu, Tiehua Zhang

entry.summary: The authors propose adaptive reciprocal knowledge distillation (AR-KD), which adapts the teacher by matching its class correlation matrix to the student's learning state, addressing the large teacher-student size gap and the static, one-way nature of standard distillation. This provides targeted guidance on hard samples and preserves category correlation knowledge. It aims to improve lightweight student model performance in image classification settings.

entry.title: Pre-training with Graph Transformers

author.name: Jiaming Wang, Thomas Laurent, Xavier Bresson

entry.summary: A comprehensive experimental study of pre-training strategies for graph transformers in biochemistry, finding that supervised pre-training on computed molecular properties yields the largest downstream gains and that constraining model capacity is important to avoid overfitting. It provides practical guidance for graph transformer pre-training.

entry.title: An Uncertainty-Aware Hybrid Mathematical-Machine-Learning Model for Smart Irrigation Decision Support

author.name: Andrea Scariolo

entry.summary: The study couples a calibrated water-balance model with a Random Forest that learns only the physical residual, attaches conformal prediction intervals, and applies a risk-aware rule to convert forecasts into defensible irrigation decisions under uncertainty. It addresses agriculture, which accounts for roughly 70 percent of freshwater withdrawals.

entry.title: SH-WRNN: Implicit Spherical Harmonics Weight Field Routing Neural Networks for Asymmetric Edge Intelligence

author.name: Zhibin Jiao, Xiangjing An

entry.summary: SH-WRNN replaces conventional static discrete weight matrices with a differentiable continuous weight field parameterized by spherical harmonics, retrieving layer weights via latitude-longitude coordinates on a mapped plane. This challenges the fully connected layer paradigm by constraining weights within a continuous parametric field. It matters as an exploratory architecture for compact, asymmetric models suited to edge deployment.

entry.title: Sensory Precision Inference for Multimodal Arbitration under Uncertainty

author.name: Tin Mi\v{s}i\'c, Takato Horii

entry.summary: The paper proposes a multimodal perceptual inference model based on active inference in which latent beliefs and modality-specific sensory precisions are jointly updated via iterative free-energy minimization, enabling adaptive arbitration when sensory streams are noisy, missing, or incongruent. It targets autonomous agents operating on multisensory data in real environments. It matters by extending active inference to dynamic precision-weighted multimodal conflict resolution.

entry.title: Rotation-Based Subspace Tracking for Robust Kernel PCA on Streaming Data

author.name: Kris Lokere, John Fossaceca

entry.summary: This paper presents an online robust kernel PCA method that tracks the principal subspace in a kernel Hilbert space under streaming data, data drift, and outliers, using rotation-based subspace updates. It addresses shortcomings of existing online robust kernel PCA algorithms in these realistic conditions.

entry.title: Task-Directed Residual AddUNet:Perfect-Reconstruction Routing for Full-Rate Representations

author.name: Vikram R. Lakkavalli

entry.summary: This paper establishes that the survivor-skip structure of constrained additive U-Nets is exactly equivalent to a critically sampled perfect-reconstruction multirate filter bank, and extends this to a full-rate residual architecture that routes task-irrelevant structure away from task-facing representations while retaining routed information explicitly. Reconstruction is guaranteed for arbitrary shape-compatible inputs. It bridges signal-processing theory and neural architecture design for representation learning.

entry.title: Abstract-LoRA: Unlocking Single-Image Style Transfer through Targeted U-Net Block Training

author.name: Xinglin Hu

entry.summary: Abstract-LoRA enables single-image style transfer in diffusion models by applying lightweight LoRA training targeted at specific U-Net blocks, addressing content loss and style fidelity issues that plague existing single-image methods compared to multi-image approaches. This expands style extraction from scarce artworks where collecting five to ten examples is impractical. It is a practical generative-modeling technique for creative applications.

entry.title: Frame-Synchronous Hand Gesture Detection by Projected Winding Order

author.name: Amey Thakur

entry.summary: For hand-rotation gesture synchronization, the paper derives an exact, classifier-free detector based on a normalized 2D cross product of palm edge projections, proven to factorize with the rotation angle. The method requires no training data or calibration and aligns outputs to the exact frame a gesture occurs, addressing the synchronization gap left by classification-style recognition.

entry.title: Real-World Deployment and Performance Characterisation of Fog-Based Deep Learning for Cold-Chain Temperature Prediction over LoRaWAN

author.name: Jeremiah Taguta, Jean Frederic Isingizwe Nturambirwe, Clement Nthambazale Nyirenda

entry.summary: This paper reports what it claims is the first real-world deployment of fog-based deep learning for cold-chain temperature prediction: an LSTM-GRU model running entirely on a Raspberry Pi 4 with no cloud dependency, using LoRaWAN sensor data from a South African apple cold-storage facility with induced cold-chain breaks. The system generates conditional alerting to enable proactive intervention against food waste. It demonstrates feasibility of edge inference in a realistic agricultural IoT setting.

entry.title: 3D Gait-Based Autism Classification Using Attention-Enhanced Deep Learning with Cross-Fold Statistical Stability Analysis

author.name: Md Nadim Mahamood, Md Arif Shahriar, Md Parvej Sikder, Md Rasul Islam, Md Shafi Ud Doula, Md Ashraful Alam, Kamrul Hasan

entry.summary: The paper presents an attention-enhanced Transformer for autism spectrum disorder classification from 3D gait features, evaluated on two structurally different representations and across two datasets, with formal statistical assessment of fold-to-fold stability rather than merely descriptive cross-validation summaries. Gait serves as a non-invasive behavioral biomarker for early ASD screening. It addresses subjectivity in conventional clinical assessment.

entry.title: Zero-SNR Analyticity of the Scalar MMSE Is Equivalent to Gaussianity

author.name: Yixing Zhang

entry.summary: This paper proves that under a square-exponential moment condition, the scalar minimum mean-square error in a Gaussian channel is analytic at zero SNR if and only if the input is Gaussian. The proof recasts estimation in the Gaussian channel as a backward heat flow on the moment-generating function, showing non-Gaussian inputs force singularities.

entry.title: Token Merging for Multilingual Speech Recognition: A Systematic Study Across Model Scale and Fine-Tuning

author.name: Dylan Luke Holyoak

entry.summary: This systematic study evaluates token merging on the Whisper family across sixteen languages and three model sizes, including interaction with DoRA fine-tuning on low-resource languages. Token merging shortens sequences at inference without retraining, and results show efficiency gains with near-no accuracy loss for most low-resource languages. It offers a practical path to cheaper multilingual ASR deployment.

entry.title: Toward Complete Hospital Discharge Summarization with Abstract Meaning Representation

author.name: Paul Landes, Sitara Rao, Aaron Jeremy Chaise, Barbara Di Eugenio

entry.summary: The authors present an evidence-driven alignment framework for hospital discharge summarization that treats provenance as a first-class constraint, using semantic graphs (AMR) and deep learning to select and organize summary sentences with explicit evidence links to source spans. This directly targets LLM hallucination risks in clinical documentation. Reducing documentation burden safely is a high-value clinical application.

entry.title: A Multi-Stage Agentic Framework for Effective Counter-Narrative Generation and Refinement

author.name: Carmel Kronfeld, Sharva Gogawale, Tetsuro Kobayashi, Irad Ben-Gal

entry.summary: This paper presents a multi-stage agentic framework for generating, refining, and evaluating counter-narratives against pro-Russian hate and misinformation about the Ukraine war, with a pilot human-evaluation experiment identifying effective technique-style pairings such as repetition with emotional framing. It addresses the risk that direct suppression deepens polarization. The framework is claimed to be adaptable to other domains.

entry.title: Document Topic Alignment Metrics for Evaluating Topic Models of Short-Text Public Health Communications on Social Media

author.name: Wangjiaxuan Xin, Shuhua Yin, Yaorong Ge, Shi Chen

entry.summary: The paper proposes DoTA, an assignment-aware evaluation framework measuring semantic alignment between social media posts and their assigned topics, including margin-based and discriminative variants. It evaluates five topic models across three public-health datasets from X and comparable platforms. This fills a gap in topic-model evaluation, which traditionally scores topics in isolation rather than assignments.

entry.title: One Feedback System Does Not Fit All: Localising Data-to-Text Driver Coaching for the United Kingdom and Nigeria

author.name: Iniakpokeikiye Peter Thompson, Jawwad Baig, Ehud Reiter, Dewei Yi

entry.summary: The paper argues that data-to-text driver coaching systems must be localized because usefulness depends on drivers' knowledge, risks, regulation, and infrastructure. Comparing independently developed UK and Nigeria systems, it traces how requirements shape content selection, generation, and field evaluation, revealing divergent design priorities such as post-trip reflection in the UK versus safety education and daily tips in Nigeria.

entry.title: Improving Mathematical Reasoning Capabilities in Large Language Models via Reasoning Process Error Classification

author.name: Runa Yoshida, Kosuke Nishida, Kyosuke Nishida

entry.summary: The authors manually analyze and classify 21 classes of reasoning errors in LLM mathematical problem solving, then use this taxonomy to design prompts that explicitly target the eight most frequent error classes. Experiments show the error-class-informed prompting improves mathematical reasoning. The work links qualitative error analysis to a concrete intervention.

entry.title: Sequential Adapter Stacking for Cross-Lingual Low-Resource ASR

author.name: Thai Thi Thanh Thao Dang, Mengjie Qian, Kate Knill

entry.summary: The authors investigate parameter-efficient transfer on Whisper for low-resource languages, proposing Sequential Adapter Stacking where a trainable target-language adapter sits atop a frozen source-language adapter. Evaluated on target languages unsupported by Whisper, such as Asturian, under controlled experiments. This addresses the sharp performance degradation of multilingual ASR on low-resource languages.

entry.title: Synthetic Leprosy Image Generation Using Mask-Conditioned Latent Diffusion and Transfer Learning from Large Chronic Wound Datasets

author.name: Yusuf Abdulkadir

entry.summary: The paper builds a three-stage pipeline generating synthetic leprosy lesion images: DeepLabV3 segmentation supplies masks for wound datasets lacking them, a mask-conditioned latent diffusion model is trained on 3,280 wound crops with a widened UNet, and knowledge transfers from abundant chronic wound photography to the extremely low-data leprosy setting. This tackles data scarcity for machine learning on neglected tropical diseases. The approach could enable diagnostic model development where annotated images number only in the hundreds.

entry.title: Pixel-wise Planarity for High-Precision Monocular Plane Segmentation

author.name: Ahmetcan Yavuz, Alpay Ozkan, R\'emi Pautrat, Shaohui Liu, Marc Pollefeys

entry.summary: This paper proposes pixel-wise planarity prediction for monocular plane segmentation, adding a planarity head to a pretrained monocular geometric backbone that predicts depth and surface normals, then combining predictions in a lightweight geometrically consistent region-growing procedure. The authors also analyze existing plane ground-truth annotations and find substantial issues. This addresses over-segmentation and false planar detections caused by imprecise grouping and inconsistent supervision.

entry.title: Reliable Egocentric Action Anticipation via Temporal Reliability Suppression and Compositional Graph Decoding

author.name: Mahsa Mohammadi, Sareh Rowlands

entry.summary: The paper tackles egocentric action anticipation under corrupted wearable-sensor conditions with two modules: Temporal Reliability Suppression, which learns per-frame attention penalties from corrupted frames, and Robust Verb-Noun Graph decoding that re-ranks implausible compositions. It explicitly identifies encoding and decoding failure modes under missing frames and noise. This improves robustness for wearable assistive and AR applications.
