entry.title: Global-Local Contextual Progressive Expansion Network for Martian Landslide Segmentation in Multimodal Remote Sensing Imagery

author.name: Leo Thomas Ramos, Sidike Paheding, Abel A. Reyes-Angulo, Rajaneesh A., Sajinkumar K. S., Angel D. Sappa, Thomas Oommen

entry.summary: This paper provides the first comprehensive study of deep segmentation models for Martian landslide segmentation using multimodal orbital imagery combining spectral and topographic cues, and proposes TransCPLES, a U-shaped network with global-local contextual progressive expansion. The domain is underexplored and relevant to future planetary exploration. The benchmark assessment plus new architecture fills a genuine gap.

entry.title: Hyper-LLaVA: Hyperbolic Uncertainty-aware Modality-Balanced Routing for Multimodal Continual Instruction Tuning

author.name: Kunlun Xu, Yanqin Zhang, Wenwen Qiang, Jiahuan Zhou

entry.summary: Hyper-LLaVA improves parameter routing in multimodal continual instruction tuning by using hyperbolic embeddings to capture intra-task diversity and uncertainty-aware modality weighting, since different modalities vary in reliability across tasks. It fixes two flaws of similarity-to-center routing with equal cross-modal fusion. The work addresses catastrophic forgetting and routing errors in incremental multimodal learning.

entry.title: Robust low-rank tensor completion via factorized weighted tensor schatten-p norm minimization

author.name: Binghao Wang, Feng Zhang, Wendong Wang, Jianjun Wang

entry.summary: Proposes two weighted Schatten-p tensor factorization models under the t-product framework that allow component-specific weighting of singular values, avoiding excessive attenuation of dominant low-rank components and costly SVDs. The models support flexible, possibly asymmetric factorizations for completing incomplete and corrupted multidimensional data.

entry.title: Context-Aware Mutual Learning for Blind Image Inpainting and Beyond

author.name: Haoru Zhao, Yufeng Wang, Zhaorui Gu, Bing Zheng, Haiyong Zheng

entry.summary: This work addresses blind image inpainting with unknown masks via a two-stage decomposition of mask estimation and inpainting, and introduces a mutual learning scheme that corrects the excessive one-way dependence of inpainting on mask estimation found in prior methods. The approach improves quality and generalization to real-world contamination.

entry.title: MCIQA-2K: A Multi-Dimensional Dataset and No-Reference Quality Assessment Benchmark for Colorized Images

author.name: Yunkai Zhuang, Qihang Yan, Zicheng Zhang, Guangtao Zhai

entry.summary: MCIQA-2K is a benchmark of 2,000 colorized images from five colorization models with human annotations along three perceptual dimensions: color smearing, semantic color misalignment, and global naturalness, enabling no-reference quality assessment for the inherently ill-posed colorization task. The paper also proposes a method built on this benchmark.

entry.title: Automated Perceptually-Motivated Assessment of Photographic Consistency in Paired Clinical Photographs: Pipeline Development and Internal Evaluation

author.name: Derrick Lin, Samantha Rabinovich, Joclin Rabinovich, Kassra Garoosi, Sumun Khetpal, Evan Delanoy, Neel Bhardwaj, Jason Roostaeian

entry.summary: This work builds an automated pipeline that scores whether paired pre- and post-operative clinical photographs were captured under conditions consistent for comparison, using thirteen calibrated sub-metrics grouped into five clusters and combined into a single consistency score. It addresses a real gap in plastic surgery outcome evidence, where no objective comparability metric previously existed.

entry.title: Hypergraph-Regularized Gramian Volumes for Multimodal Retrieval

author.name: Anindya Nag, Ambuj Mehrish, Sebastiano Vascon

entry.summary: HyVol is a training-time module for volume-based multimodal retrieval that adds hypergraph structure: document hyperedges connect a candidate's modalities while semantic hyperedges link candidates with mutually nearest-neighbor captions. A shallow gated hypergraph network applies residual corrections to modality embeddings before the original volume loss is evaluated.

entry.title: CatchMonitor: a machine learning system for automated fish discard quantification

author.name: Geoff French, Michal Mackiewicz, Mark Fisher, Helen Holah, Rebecca Lamb

entry.summary: CatchMonitor is a prototype computer vision system that automatically quantifies discarded fish from video captured by Remote Electronic Monitoring on fishing trawlers, using semi-supervised learning for species identification and robust object tracking for counting. The work also analyzes variability among expert human analysts to contextualize system accuracy.

entry.title: Complete Suffix Prediction for Recommendation via Latent Retrieval over Process Graphs

author.name: Sarra Madad (UTT, LIST3N - OPTI, QAD), Myriam Maumy (EHESP, LIST3N - OPTI, ARENES), Fr{\'e}d{\'e}ric Bertrand (CEDRIC, LIST3N - OPTI), Yoann Valero (QAD)

entry.summary: The paper reformulates complete suffix prediction in sequential decision settings as latent retrieval over process graphs, encoding prefixes and suffixes as directed attributed graphs with edge-conditioned GNNs. A joint reconstruction and contrastive objective with process-aware hard negatives and spectral normalization stabilizes the retrieval geometry.

entry.title: Novel Ex-vivo Calf Brain Model with Integrated Sub-Skull Force Sensors to Access Simulated Neurosurgical Procedures

author.name: Hamad Binhammad, Matheus Ballestero, Mohammed Babgi, Seana Shaka, Nima Hemati, Rothaina Saeedi, Aiden Mazidi, Bianca Giglio, Rukun Dou, Houssem-Eddine Gueziri, Amir Hooshiar, Rolando F. Del Maestro

entry.summary: The paper presents and validates a portable ex-vivo platform using fresh calf brain tissue in a 3D-printed skull with a 6-DOF force/torque sensor to quantify tool-tissue forces during simulated neurosurgery. Five validation protocols assess accuracy and dynamic fidelity against ground-truth measurement.

entry.title: Beyond Dead Reckoning: A Point of View on Camera--DAS--GNSS Continuity in Road Tunnels

author.name: Lyes Saad Saoud, Hesham A. Rakha, Mona Jaber, Moussa Ayyash

entry.summary: This position paper argues that localization in road tunnels should be treated as infrastructure-assisted cross-modal track continuity, combining portal satellite fixes, distributed acoustic sensing (DAS), camera anchors, onboard sensing, and edge-computed fusion with integrity monitoring. It proposes a falsifiable research and deployment agenda for attributable, integrity-bounded positioning where GNSS is unavailable. It frames an important problem for connected and automated vehicles.

entry.title: Dynamics-Informed Reinforcement Learning for Agile and Energy-Efficient Locomotion of a Monopedal Hopping Quadcopter

author.name: Ruigang Chen, Qi Zhang, Zhicheng Zhong, Zhuorui Yun, Yizhar Or, Mingyi Liu

entry.summary: This work proposes a Dynamics-Informed RL framework for a monopedal hopping quadcopter, embedding a target specific energy in the reward to constrain optimization to a physically viable energy manifold. Phase-consistent rewards encourage bio-inspired stance-phase impulses while penalizing electro-mechanical power waste yields efficient motor impulses. The approach counters typical RL reward hacking toward energy-inefficient gaits.

entry.title: Continuous Manifold-Decomposed Impedance Retargeting for Contact-Rich Imitation Learning

author.name: Jiahao Liu, Kento Kawaharazuka, Tasuku Makabe, Kei Okada

entry.summary: CMDIR extends Manifold-Decomposed Impedance Retargeting to convert fixed-impedance demonstrations into continuous variable-impedance controllers usable as structured supervision for imitation learning. It combines continuous task-manifold impedance representation, demo-relative compromise dynamics, and an automatic solver-structure compilation step with multi-resolution certification of candidate controllers. The target is contact-rich manipulation skills.

entry.title: On Detecting Multiple Simultaneous Change-points in High Dimensional Non-Stationary Time Series

author.name: Richard Song

entry.summary: This paper studies detection of multiple simultaneous change points in high-dimensional non-stationary economic and financial time series using standard and adaptive fused group lasso with mixed L2,1 penalties. It establishes L2 consistency and, with data-dependent reweighting, L0 consistency (correct change-point selection with probability approaching one), characterizing conditions on signal magnitude, change-point count, and sample size.

entry.title: Pilot Early, Commit Late: A Real-Options Model of Enterprise AI Adoption under Rapid Technological Progress

author.name: Gaurav Tewari

entry.summary: This paper develops a two-period real-options decision model for enterprise AI deployment in which a firm chooses among immediate deployment, a limited pilot, or waiting, balancing operating value, architectural obsolescence, and organization-specific learning. It derives five central timing results plus a comparative result on where learning best accrues.

entry.title: A derivative-fidelity failure mode in physics-informed neural networks: strengthened benchmark evidence from function-value training

author.name: Koji Koyamada

entry.summary: This paper identifies derivative fidelity as a distinct failure mode of physics-informed neural networks: visually accurate function approximation on 1D sin and exp benchmarks can coexist with substantially wrong second derivatives under automatic differentiation. Controlled experiments over training-point density, activation functions, and error diagnostics strengthen the claim. The finding is a caution for scientific machine learning where derivative accuracy matters.

entry.title: Bayesian Optimisation Using Product-of-Experts Gaussian Process Models with Uncertainty Calibration

author.name: Yean Hoon Ong

entry.summary: BO-pro-c uses a product-of-experts Gaussian process with uncertainty calibration as the surrogate in Bayesian optimisation, avoiding the cubic cost of a single global GP for large-scale problems. The paper studies how this surrogate combination affects optimisation performance.

entry.title: From Legal Text to AI-specific Risk Sources: A Systematic Analysis of the EU AI Act's High-Risk Requirements

author.name: Ronald Schnitzer, Mike Auer, Rumpa Choudhury, Andreas Hapfelmeier, Maximilian Hoeving, Isabelle Painter, Josiane Xavier Parreira, Sonja Zillner

entry.summary: Presents a systematic classification mapping the EU AI Act's high-risk requirements onto established AI risk taxonomies, addressing the absence of a structured basis for aligning regulatory obligations with risk-management practice. The analysis clarifies which AI-specific risk sources are and are not covered by the Act.

entry.title: Windowed A-K-MDP

author.name: Xiangwen Yang, Frankie Cho, Iadine Chades

entry.summary: Improves the A-K-MDP algorithm for building interpretable abstract MDPs with at most K states, showing that binary search over discretisation divisors can skip better abstract state partitions. The proposed Windowed A-K-MDP evaluates every distinct feasible partition within a divisor window, achieving ideal value loss more often across 33 K-MDP instances. Relevant to interpretable decision support in conservation and other domains.

entry.title: Map Users and Mapmakers: The Scope of Cognitive Attribution from Acquired Representations

author.name: Yiling Wu

entry.summary: A philosophical framework for understanding what cognitive capacities a system gains when it acquires a representation, distinguishing the representation's use from the capacities that produced it. The paper proposes a five-part attribution table covering tracking, application, acquisition from specifications, acquisition from observations, and retention/reuse. It matters for clarifying debates about whether AI systems genuinely understand or merely use acquired artifacts.

entry.title: GGUF-Metadata Prediction of Single-Sequence llama.cpp Throughput Across Three Systems

author.name: Xinyu Qiu, Chuhong Xu, Bo Su, Ziyao Chen, Ruiyang Xu, Shimeng Dai

entry.summary: The paper builds roofline-shaped predictors of single-sequence decode throughput from GGUF file metadata, fitted with quantization-specific scale factors on Apple M4 Max and RTX 5080 systems. Using active parameters rather than total parameters cuts prediction error substantially (13-36% MAPE versus roughly 50%), offering practical hardware-model fit guidance for local LLM deployment.

entry.title: Option-Aware Retrieval and Task-Specific VLM Adaptation for Medical VQA

author.name: Tristan Kirscher (ICube, Institut Strauss), Niklas C. Koser (CAU), Soren Pirk (CAU)

entry.summary: This is a MedReason 2026 challenge submission covering multiple-choice and open-ended medical VQA under offline, containerized inference. Key findings include that answer-option retrieval must compare answer semantics rather than labels (raising retrieval-only accuracy from 20.0% to 57.5%) and an ablation attributing the submitted system's accuracy to task-specific LoRA adaptation. It offers practical lessons for medical VQA system design.

entry.title: Potential of Artificial Intelligence Algorithms for Identification of Relevant Diagnostic and Prognostic Biomarkers of Early-Stage Liver Cancer

author.name: Ali Bou Nassif, Darko Castven, Manar Abu Talib, Jibran Sualeh Muhammad, Ahmed Ammar Kubba, Jens Marquardt, Abdalla Sayed Ali

entry.summary: The study applies deep learning and explainable AI to diagnose hepatocellular carcinoma across five disease stages using a transcriptomic dataset built via semi-supervised learning from three sources. A model using 15 SelectKBest-selected genes reached 90.74% accuracy, and XAI techniques are used to surface candidate biomarkers.

entry.title: LayerRoute: Adaptive Layer-Skipping with LoRA-Preserved Quality for Efficient LLM Inference

author.name: Prateek Kumar Sikdar

entry.summary: LayerRoute combines per-layer hard-gated routing trained via a straight-through estimator with joint LoRA fine-tuning to enable adaptive transformer layer-skipping on Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct. Across 10 seeds it converges to an identical skip pattern (middle layers 8-16 skip-eligible) and delivers verified 1.02x-1.06x wallclock speedups. The consistent emergent skip structure across seeds is an interesting finding about which layers are compressible.

entry.title: Talking to Me or Someone Else? Rethinking Talk-to-Me Detection in Egocentric Videos

author.name: Feiyu Du, Xi He, Jia Li, Yapeng Tian, Weili Wu

entry.summary: Reformulates talk-to-me detection in egocentric video from offline clip-level binary classification to online frame-level prediction, explicitly modeling diverse non-TTM speaking states such as talking to others, self-talking, and background speech. The authors construct a new Online TTM dataset to support this richer formulation.

entry.title: SpermYOLO: A Coordinated YOLO-Based Detector for Accurate and Efficient Sperm and Impurity Detection in Microscopic Images

author.name: Shengqi Chen, Zilin Wang, Xingyu Pan, Wenting Yu, Pengchao Deng, Guohua Wu

entry.summary: SpermYOLO extends YOLOv11 with four architectural modifications for joint sperm and impurity detection in microscopy, including channel-discriminative feature extraction, spatial-spectral enhancement, multi-scale fusion, and a detail-enhanced shared head. It reports 97.2% sperm AP and 75.4% impurity AP on the SVIA benchmark.

entry.title: Validating Hybrid-State Cache Recovery for GLM-5.3-Flash with vLLM and LMCache

author.name: Frank Li

entry.summary: This systems paper validates cache recovery for a hybrid language model served with vLLM and LMCache, identifying a mismatch where external cache transfers succeed but the model resumes from an inconsistent state due to scheduler token-accounting errors. Using the 45-layer GLM-5.3-Flash model under four-way tensor parallelism, the authors align recovery through strict-prefix lookup and improve agreement with a recomputation control from 34/36 to 36/36 generations. It matters for reliability of KV-cache offloading infrastructure.

entry.title: Event-Native Symbolic-Temporal Spike Encoding Framework for Heterogeneous Cyber Streams

author.name: Dalton Diez, Peyton Andras, Max Shroyer, James Ghawaly Jr

entry.summary: This paper proposes a spike encoding framework for spiking neural networks applied to cybersecurity streams, handling categorical identifiers, irregular timing, and local behavioral context that traditional rate- and population-based encodings mishandle. It targets low-power, event-driven intrusion detection on edge hardware.

entry.title: Criticality in Dissimilar Decomposition and Undersampling of Random Datasets with Anomalies

author.name: Ghurumuruhan Ganesan

entry.summary: This theoretical paper models AI-generated data as anomalies linked to main data points and studies decomposition and undersampling of such random datasets using redundancy graphs, deriving bounds for minimum strongly dissimilar decomposition size and demonstrating a phase transition governed by the proportion of anomalies. The motivation is understanding how AI-generated content in training corpora affects future LLM training. It offers a probabilistic lens on model collapse-adjacent questions.

entry.title: Curvature-Independent Regret Bounds for Distributed Online Optimization on Hadamard Manifolds

author.name: Zhanyuan Cai, Emre Sahinoglu, Shahin Shahrampour

entry.summary: The paper studies distributed Riemannian online gradient descent (D-ROGD) on Hadamard manifolds, removing the need for sectional curvature lower bounds by targeting horospherically convex functions, with an implicit Frechet-mean consensus step. It establishes O(sqrt(T)) and O(log T) regret for h-convex and strongly h-convex objectives.

entry.title: Representing Clinical Conditions on Vital Signs from Healthy Individuals using Latent Modeling

author.name: Rafael Pina, Varuna De Silva, Mindula Illeperuma

entry.summary: The authors train a conditional variational autoencoder on ICU data to transform healthy individuals' vital signs into patterns mimicking specific clinical conditions. This generative augmentation could enable clinical signal processing models where representative patient data is unavailable.

entry.title: A family of spectral conjugate gradient algorithms derived by least-squares approximations based on a modified quasi--Newton update with application to a revised robust binary classification model

author.name: Saman Babaie-Kafaki, Maryam Khoshsimaye-Bargard, Ahmad Mousavi

entry.summary: The paper develops a spectral three-term modification of the Hestenes-Stiefel conjugate gradient method preserving anti-jamming and sufficient descent properties, deriving a memoryless BFGS update via a modified secant equation and choosing the spectral parameter by least-squares steering toward the BFGS direction. Convergence is established without convexity assumptions and tested against a robust binary classification application.

entry.title: What Input Resolution Is Required for Bird Species Identification, and What Is Its Latency Cost on an Edge Device? A Study of 14 Input Resolutions and Six Architectures with On-Device Measurements

author.name: Takeshi Nishikawa

entry.summary: This empirical study treats input resolution as a design variable for bird species classification in wind-farm bird-strike mitigation, sweeping 14 resolutions from 16 to 224 pixels across six architectures with 2,520 checkpoints and real latency measurements on a Jetson Orin Nano. Key findings include that swapping architectures yields larger accuracy gains than raising resolution, and that different accuracy targets imply different optimal resolution-architecture pairs. It offers practical deployment guidance for resource-constrained edge vision systems.

entry.title: Evaluation of optimisation and Bayesian inference methods for reaction rates in atmospheric chemical mechanisms

author.name: Valery Ashu, Wenqing Peng, Zhi-Song Liu, Heikki Haario, Andreas Rupp, Taiwo Ashu, Petri Clusius, Lukas Pichelstorfer, Zihao Fu, Michael Boy

entry.summary: This work compares ODE-constrained neural-network optimization against MCMC for constraining reaction rate coefficients in an atmospheric autoxidation mechanism, using synthetic data with known ground truth. It quantifies the trade-off between efficient point estimates and posterior uncertainty quantification.

entry.title: A Functional SVD Framework for Regularized Multivariate Functional PCA with Dual Penalization

author.name: Yue Zhao, Hossein Haghbin, Rebecca Sanders, Mehdi Maadooliat

entry.summary: The authors extend multivariate functional PCA by introducing a functional singular value decomposition within a Hilbert space framework that jointly regularizes principal components and their scores. A sparsity penalty on PC scores filters out irrelevant subject-specific variation, improving interpretability beyond existing covariance-based methods that penalize only one side. This is a methodological advance for analyzing multivariate functional data.

entry.title: Bridging the Gap in ECG-Based Emotion Recognition: A Unified Evaluation of Deep Learning Models

author.name: Timothy C Sweeney-Fanelli, Ajan Ahmed, Masudul Imtiaz

entry.summary: The authors present a unified cross-dataset benchmark of prominent deep learning architectures for emotion recognition from ECG, emphasizing true generalization over dataset adaptability, supported by two open-source frameworks. The work addresses inconsistencies in preprocessing and evaluation that have made prior results incomparable.

entry.title: ReLU Neural Network Approximation to Smooth Functional Operator: Dimensional Decay and Error Analysis

author.name: Shuhao Jiao

entry.summary: The paper establishes nonasymptotic uniform approximation error bounds for deep ReLU networks approximating smooth scalar functionals on infinite-dimensional Hilbert spaces, combining coordinate truncation, anisotropic partitioning, and local Taylor approximation. It quantifies coordinate importance via basis magnitude and directional Frechet sensitivity.

entry.title: Clinical Reasoning Under a Partially Observed Objective in Cone Beam CT Report Generation

author.name: Ajo Babu George, Govind Arun, Sidharth N Krishna, Uma Ranjan

entry.summary: The paper studies maxillofacial CBCT report generation under a composite objective where an LLM judge of factual entailment carries 80 percent weight but only the lexical 20 percent is visible during development. The authors reproduce the lexical metrics exactly and build an offline entailment surrogate with 0.987 AUC, showing that selecting against the full composite objective substantially outperforms lexical-only selection. This highlights the gap between visible metrics and true clinical quality.

entry.title: When Consistency Does Not Mean Reliability: Evaluating Local LLM Judges Against Human Ratings

author.name: Aakash Kumar Tiwari

entry.summary: This single-author study evaluates two open-weight LLM judges (LLaMA-3-8B and Qwen2.5-7B) against nine human annotators on 300 GPT-2-generated responses across five categories. It shows judges can produce consistent scores without agreeing with humans, decoupling consistency from reliability in LLM-as-a-judge setups. The finding cautions against using consistency metrics as proxies for evaluation validity.

entry.title: Neyshekar: An Open Persian Read-Speech Corpus for Automatic Speech Recognition

author.name: Ahmad Amirivojdan, Farzad Nadiri, Abolfazl Alizadeh, Shaghayegh Yaraghi

entry.summary: Neyshekar is an open Persian read-speech corpus with 62,279 validated recordings totaling 99 hours from 190 contributors, covering formal and informal language, named entities, and longer utterances. Recordings were validated against a rubric and text normalized with the shekar library supporting informal Persian. This addresses the scarcity of open Persian speech resources.

entry.title: ScorePrompts: Natural-Language Exploration of Symbolic Music Scores through Analysis

author.name: Emmanouil Karystinaios, Gerhard Widmer

entry.summary: ScorePrompts is an interactive system where users upload symbolic music scores, receive natural-language structural descriptions, and ask passage-level questions, with specialist MIR components estimating harmony, cadence, form, and texture and a schema-constrained LLM converting analysis outputs into descriptions. A deterministic router grounds answers in relevant measures and analytical levels. It demonstrates a sound neuro-symbolic division of labor for music analysis.

entry.title: Human-Grounded Calibration for Long-Text Image-Text Congruence in Vision-Language Models

author.name: Alessandro Gambetti, Qiwei Han

entry.summary: The paper proposes Congruency Score, a lightweight calibration layer mapping raw dual-encoder image-text similarity into a bounded, interpretable congruence measure for long-text scenarios. Evaluating four frozen VLM backbones on DOCCI and Urban1k, it shows that reducing post-projection centroid distance does not uniformly improve retrieval, and provides human-grounded evaluations on DOCCI. This improves the interpretability of image-text congruence scoring for vision-language systems.

entry.title: Target-Checked Reliability Score Refinement for Video Question Answering

author.name: Guoxiang Ren, Rohitash Chandra

entry.summary: This work improves answer-level reliability scores for video question answering under target shift without retraining models or changing their answers, by building response graphs from option probabilities across multiple video samplings and model agreements. A small labeled target pilot is used to train histogram gradient-boosting or regularized logistic-regression score replacements. The approach addresses overconfident wrong answers from video-language models in a lightweight post-hoc way.

entry.title: Quantum-Gated LiteSSD: A Parameter-Efficient Lightweight Hybrid Quantum-Classical Framework for Forward-Looking Sonar Object Detection

author.name: Niloy Kumar Mondal, Poulomi Sarker Puja

entry.summary: A hybrid quantum-classical detector for forward-looking sonar that reformulates multi-circuit quantum processing as an identity-centered channel-gating mechanism for spatial feature modulation. It reaches 90.84% mAP50 on the Marine Debris Watertank dataset with roughly 62x fewer parameters than YOLO26s and 164.3x fewer than another baseline.

entry.title: PRI-Net: A Lightweight Multimodal Framework for 3D UAV Localization

author.name: Zhixuan Chen, Jialiang Lu, Zhong Ye, Yinghui He, Guanding Yu

entry.summary: PRI-Net is an efficient multimodal fusion framework for 3D UAV localization that combines 3D point cloud splatting to densify sparse LiDAR, residual attention fusion to balance modalities, and an information bottleneck to reduce feature transmission over constrained edge-to-server links. It targets practical deployment constraints in UAV systems.

entry.title: ThreshGuide: Class-Aware Labeled-Guided Thresholding for Semi-Supervised 3D Abdominal Multi-Organ Segmentation

author.name: Hongyu Liu, Yinlong Wang, Lusha Li, Hui Meng

entry.summary: ThreshGuide adapts pseudo-label confidence thresholds per organ class in semi-supervised 3D abdominal segmentation, using a teacher model on labeled samples to estimate class-aware threshold targets via an error-aware F-beta criterion. This replaces fixed global thresholds that are suboptimal given large differences in organ size and difficulty.

entry.title: Assessing nnU-Net Generalization across Brain Tumor Populations in BraTS-GoAT 2026

author.name: Tristan Kirscher (ICube, Institut Strauss), Vivian Metzger (Institut Strauss), Philippe Meyer (Institut Strauss, ICube), Xavier Coubez (Institut Strauss, ICube)

entry.summary: This challenge paper evaluates how a conventional 3D nnU-Net trained on 1,351 labeled brain tumor cases generalizes across heterogeneous populations in BraTS-GoAT 2026, reporting DSC scores around 0.78-0.89 for enhancing tumor, tumor core, and whole tumor on pooled validation. It quantifies a notable performance drop from out-of-fold source cases to the pooled validation set and finds limited benefit from mirroring and ensembling.

entry.title: Translation-Invariant Tile-Based Phase Unwrapping with Residual-Weighted Multipath Averaging

author.name: Antoine Moevus, Max Mignotte

entry.summary: The paper proposes a semi-global, tile-based phase unwrapping method for interferometric and coherent imaging that unwraps tiles in the frequency domain via DCT-based least squares and merges them with translation-invariant, residual-weighted multipath averaging. This hybrid spatial-frequency design separates wrapping jumps from noise, discontinuities, under-sampling, and decorrelation.

entry.title: Does Online Gravity Estimation Matter? Revisiting a Silent Design Split in LiDAR-Inertial Odometry

author.name: Jie Xu, Ziyi Jin, Kangjin Yu, Can Jiang, Hongjun Huang, Tongxing Jin, Hongkun Luo, Zhongpu Xia

entry.summary: This paper examines whether LiDAR-inertial odometry systems should keep estimating gravity after initialization, comparing four gravity-bias configurations in FAST-LIO2 and LIO-SAM. Across many dataset sequences, fixing gravity after initialization shows little consistent benefit except during multi-second LiDAR outages where costs become trajectory-dependent.

entry.title: A Vision Based Framework Integrating Attention and Action Cues for Interpretable Cognitive Workload Assessment in Human Robot Collaborative Assembly

author.name: Junyan Xionga, Naiyi Feng, Xingke Xia, Qihang Fan, Suchang Chen, Daqiang Guo

entry.summary: This paper presents a vision-based framework for continuous, interpretable cognitive workload assessment in human-robot collaborative assembly, combining RGB-D observations with robot states and calibrated task areas. It replaces body-worn physiological sensors with attention-action cues to represent operator behavior over time. The goal is practical deployment in evolving manufacturing settings.

entry.title: Goal-Oriented Communications for Physical AI: Design and Testbed

author.name: Shutong Chen, Wenkai Zhang, Adnan Aijaz, Miao Guo, Yansha Deng

entry.summary: The paper develops an end-to-end goal-oriented communication testbed for Physical AI, connecting a PiPER robot arm with an RGB-D camera and 5G modem to an NVIDIA Jetson edge platform. GoC transmits only task-relevant semantic representations to meet the strict latency and bandwidth demands of latency-sensitive video streams that existing 5G cannot support. It moves GoC evaluation from simulation into practical robotic deployment.

entry.title: Watch AI materials-science & bioscience abilities closely

author.name: Yair Halberstadt

entry.summary: Yair Halberstadt proposes that AI capabilities in materials science and bioscience serve as leading indicators for whether near-term LLMs could engineer pandemics, since real-world bio engagement requires iterative lab access — a much higher bar than a single successful deception. Monitoring these spiky abilities gives advance warning and time for alignment work.

entry.title: Teaching future scientists to interrogate AI tools for scientific discovery

author.name: Unknown

entry.summary: An Ai2 blog post describing a University of Washington student challenge that tested Ai2's AutoDiscovery system, showing how AI can surface promising scientific hypotheses while emphasizing that human judgment, domain expertise, and rigorous validation remain essential. The post highlights AI-assisted scientific discovery as an educational and workflow tool. It is a program summary rather than a research paper.

entry.title: Privacy-enhanced federated learning via asynchronous aggregation and local differential perturbation

author.name: Zhen Zhong (Georgetown University, Washington, D.C., USA), Shini Yang (LinkedIn, CA, USA), Liesheng Wei (Shanghai Ocean University, Shanghai, China)

entry.summary: The authors combine dynamic differential privacy, lightweight homomorphic encryption, and local differential privacy with asynchronous aggregation and version control for federated learning. Experiments on CIFAR-10 and Purchase-100 show up to 82.6 percent accuracy under stringent privacy constraints while reducing communication. The work targets practical privacy-preserving distributed training.

entry.title: Low-Dimensional Embeddings for Gaussian Kernels on Manifolds

author.name: Soumik Dutta, Kunal Dutta

entry.summary: The authors extend random-feature embeddings for Gaussian kernel distances from Euclidean balls to arbitrary positive-reach submanifolds, proving a uniform relative-error embedding theorem with feature counts scaling with intrinsic dimension. This improves kernel PCA and spectral clustering cost for manifold-structured data.

entry.title: The University of Melbourne WMT 2026 CreoleMT Submission: A Domain-Balanced Approach to Low-Resource Pacific Creole Machine Translation

author.name: Rapha\"el Merx, Nick Thieberger, Ekaterina Vylomova

entry.summary: A WMT26 shared-task submission building MT models for Pacific creoles (Tok Pisin, Bislama, Solomon Pijin) using domain-balanced fine-tuning after imbalanced pre-training, plus LLM-assisted respelling and alignment, back-translation, and distillation from Gemini. Models beat open baselines by 3+ chrF++ points in all directions, evaluated on Bouquet and a novel spoken-language test set. This advances very low-resource language technology.

entry.title: What Does the Encoder Actually Decide? A Controlled Comparison of Vision Backbones on Joint Tree Segmentation and Stereo Depth

author.name: Yida Lin, Bing Xue, Mengjie Zhang, Sam Schofield, Richard Green

entry.summary: This paper conducts a controlled empirical study of vision encoder choice for a shared multi-task network performing joint tree segmentation and stereo depth estimation, holding dataset, decoders, losses, and schedules fixed while swapping encoders across CNNs, transformers, hybrids, MLP-mixers, and state-space models at a ~25M parameter budget. It answers whether backbone selection, often made by reputation, actually matters for thin-vegetation robotics tasks. The evaluation uses depth on tree pixels only, which is the case that matters for pruning robots.

entry.title: HGSQ: Heatmap-Guided Sparse Query Detector for Real-Time Aerial Small Object Detection

author.name: Yangchen Zeng

entry.summary: HGSQ is a heatmap-guided sparse query detector for real-time aerial small object detection that reduces computation spent on background tokens in Transformer detectors by initializing queries sparsely from heatmaps. It targets deployment-oriented UAV settings where small objects occupy few pixels against large backgrounds. The work claims efficiency gains without sacrificing fine-grained localization.

entry.title: Learning to Exploit Passive Dynamics for Energy-Efficient Target Hopping of a Spring-Legged Quadcopter

author.name: Ruigang Chen, Qi Zhang, Zhicheng Zhong, Zhuorui Yun, Yizhar Or, Mingyi Liu

entry.summary: A companion work to the same group's dynamics-informed RL paper, this study trains a direct estimated-state-to-motor PPO policy for a spring-legged quadcopter without an explicit hopping state machine or low-level attitude PID. The reward combines energy-manifold shaping, apex-state anchoring, and efficiency shaping with a history-aware power estimator to penalize power use. The goal is coordinating active thrust with passive contact dynamics.

entry.title: I am refusing to work on Cloud TPUs

author.name: Yair Halberstadt

entry.summary: A Google Israel L5 software engineer publicly documents refusing reassignment to Cloud TPU work on AI-safety grounds, citing belief that accelerating AI development is dangerously reckless, while noting his strong performance record. The post creates a public record of individual conscience within a frontier lab.

entry.title: Toward a Decision-Assurance Layer for AI-Assisted Flight Planning in Air Traffic Management

author.name: Alexandre Barreto (George Mason University), Shou Matsumoto (George Mason University), Jorge Valverde-Rebaza (Tecnol\'ogico de Monterrey), Cleiton Ataide (DECEA: Department of Airspace Control), Paulo Costa (George Mason University)

entry.summary: Proposes ATAL, a model-agnostic decision-assurance architecture for evaluating whether AI-generated flight-planning outputs are reliable enough for operational use in air traffic management. It combines semantic stability under prompt variation, operational consistency, and normative constraint validation, mapping signals to a decision framework in human-in-the-loop settings.

entry.title: Beyond Scene Description: Multi-Agent Orchestration for Non-visual Access to Virtual Worlds

author.name: Toqeer Ali Syed, Ali Akarma, Adeel Ahmad, Danial Hameed

entry.summary: MetaBlind is an eight-agent architecture providing nonvisual access to live virtual worlds for blind and visually impaired users, distributing perception, navigation, and interaction across specialized agents rather than one narrating tool that would trade a visual barrier for an auditory one. It addresses a genuine accessibility gap as virtual worlds host more social and professional activity.

entry.title: Horizon-specific Expert Fusion for Photovoltaic Power Forecasting

author.name: Xu Yuqing, Zhou Liguo, Sun Ze, Yu Lei, Jiang Mingming

entry.summary: The study builds a hierarchical ensemble for short-term photovoltaic power forecasting that combines temporal neural models, historical analogs, state climatology, and gradient-boosted trees with horizon-specific convex weights and a bias calibration step. It is evaluated on PVDAQ at 15-240 minute horizons and GEFCom2014 solar zones.

entry.title: Oops, Not Now: PEARL, a RAG-Based Support Agent for Gameplay and What Players Want from AI Help

author.name: Jiahong Li, Sai Siddartha Maram, Atieh Kashani, Ulia Zaman, Zhiyu Lin, Cameron Marano, Roger Azevedo, Jichen Zhu, Magy Seif El-Nasr

entry.summary: PEARL is a dual-component RAG system combining semantic knowledge retrieval with structural board-state matching to provide scaffolding hints in a puzzle game for learning parallel programming. It retrieves both conceptual explanations and peer-generated board states as evidence, going beyond what an LLM with raw game-state access achieves, and includes a user study on what players want from AI help. The work bridges game-based learning, RAG grounding, and educational HCI.

entry.title: SGWIB:Sliced Gromov-Wasserstein Information Bottleneck for Video Highlight Detection

author.name: Hanjuan Huang, Yung-Chieh Yeh, Hsing-Kuo Pao

entry.summary: Applies the information bottleneck principle to video highlight detection for the first time, introducing a Sliced Gromov-Monge Gap regularizer to preserve temporal relational structure among segments during compression. The method aims to learn compact discriminative segment representations while retaining inter-segment temporal organization.

entry.title: Authorship attribution and aesthetic evaluation of AI poetry: a case study with Haiku

author.name: Livia Oddi, Simone Scardapane, Toru Sugimoto, Donatella Genovese

entry.summary: This study generates Japanese haiku with a heterogeneous set of LLMs and evaluates them with human raters at Japanese universities, assessing whether respondents can distinguish AI from human authorship and how they judge aesthetics within the constrained haiku form. It examines perception across open- and closed-source, multilingual, and natively Japanese-capable models. The work probes the limits of machine-generated poetry in a culturally specific form.

entry.title: Exploring new directions in enhancing the ACTS parameter optimization suite

author.name: Chance LaVoie, Qi Bin Lei, Rocky Bala Garg, Lauren Tompkins

entry.summary: The paper explores Bayesian optimization methods (Expected Improvement, Upper Confidence Bound) against the existing Optuna TPE auto-tuner for track seeding parameters in the ACTS particle reconstruction toolkit with the Open Data Detector, under matched search ranges and trial budgets. Better tuning of track seeding affects both reconstruction quality and computational cost in high-energy physics. It is a solid applied study of Bayesian optimization in a real scientific pipeline.

entry.title: EMCStereo: Attention-Enhanced Stereo Matching for Thin-Structure Depth Estimation with a Synthetic Tree-Branch Benchmark

author.name: Yida Lin, Bing Xue, Mengjie Zhang, Sam Schofield, Richard Green

entry.summary: EMCStereo integrates three lightweight attention modules (EMA, a learned spatial-pyramid-weight MSFblock, and CoordAtt) into a PSMNet-style stereo backbone, adding minimal size and inference overhead while targeting the hard case of few-pixel-wide tree branches. The paper also contributes a synthetic tree-branch benchmark with dense ground truth that is otherwise nearly impossible to label by hand. Together these advance depth estimation for thin structures in cluttered scenes.

entry.title: Rank-Consistent Set Reasoning for Co-Salient Object Detection

author.name: Yuan Xiang, Matteo Rossi, Yingzhou Chen

entry.summary: RCSR models co-salient object detection groups as unordered sets, ranking how strongly each region agrees with learned group slots across scales and aggregating ranks with a trimmed statistic to suppress accidental matches and outlier domination. This differs from treating image groups as sequences or labels. The robust aggregation is the key mechanism for stable shared group representations.

entry.title: Small Object Detection in Drone Aerial Imagery with LAF-YOLOv10

author.name: Quratulain Nayeem, Fahmina Taranum, Mohammed Mudassir Uddin

entry.summary: LAF-YOLOv10 integrates four architectural techniques into YOLOv10n (partial convolution backbone block, attention-guided FPN, a P2 head replacing P5, and Wise-IoU v3) for small object detection in drone imagery, and importantly stress-tests whether individually validated gains transfer when combined. The study trains across multiple seeds on VisDrone-DET2019 and benchmarks against the unmodified baseline.

entry.title: Multi-Task Visual Perception Network with LLM Conditioning for Autonomous Navigation

author.name: Praveen Kumar, K. R. Guruprasad, Tushar Sandhan

entry.summary: The paper proposes a navigation framework that avoids drift-prone global maps by combining a multi-task visual perception network with LLM interpretation of text or voice commands. The robot generates sequential action plans from local visual cues and egocentric geometric instructions, executed step by step.

entry.title: Understanding User Preferences of a Slope-Aware Variable-Admittance Filter for a Robot Guide Dog

author.name: Federico Esposito, Mario Selvaggio, Aaron Link, Fabio Ruggiero

entry.summary: This letter studies how parameters of a slope-aware variable-admittance filter affect user preferences during physical interaction with a quadruped robot guide dog for visually impaired users. The system combines path following, momentum-based wrench estimation, and online stiffness/damping adaptation from depth-camera slope information. A human-subject study with blindfolded participants and a Taguchi L9 design compares adaptation strategies.

entry.title: DuctAM: A Duct-Assisted Quadrotor-Based Aerial Manipulator Enabling High-Force Push-and-Pull Interactions

author.name: Yi Wang, Rui Jin, Xinhang Xu, Haotian Jin, Ruiyang Liu, Yizhuo Yang, Lihua Xie

entry.summary: DuctAM is a compact aerial manipulator platform that adds two ducted fans along the quadrotor interaction axis to boost horizontal force capability for push-and-pull tasks. An attitude-force decoupled control scheme enables controllable horizontal forces without large attitude changes. Extensive real-world experiments, including figure-eight trajectory tracking, validate the design.

entry.title: Bypass Observation: A Conceptual Design of a Non-Intrusive Layer-Wise Semantic Extraction Architecture

author.name: Haibin Tong, Jiang Yu

entry.summary: Proposes Bypass Observation, a read-only architecture attaching observation heads to selected Transformer layers without feeding outputs back into the backbone, with three head variants and a closed-form overhead approximation for full-vocabulary readout (roughly 30-240 percent) plus cost-reduction strategies. Explicitly labeled a conceptual design rather than an empirical system. Relevant to interpretability and intermediate-representation monitoring of LLMs.

entry.title: Depth and Scale in the Sub-150M Regime: JugnuLM-53M vs JugnuLM-110M

author.name: Dushyant Rajput (AltSlate Labs LLP), Nirdesh Chauhan (AltSlate Labs LLP), Siddharth Kosaraju (AltSlate Labs LLP)

entry.summary: A transparent small-scale pretraining report scaling a conventional Qwen3-style recipe from 53.5M to 109.7M parameters with a deep-and-thin geometry, showing across-the-board gains including BLiMP matching a larger comparison model with fewer parameters and fewer training tokens. Deliberately conventional, the report is positioned as a clean scaling data point in the under-explored sub-150M regime.

entry.title: Geometric Flow enhanced Graph Coarsening

author.name: Chaoqun Fei, Guoxuan Li, Tinglve Zhou, Chuanqing Wang, Yangyang Li

entry.summary: The paper improves GCNN graph pooling by using geometric flow to capture higher-order mutual connectivity among neighbors, moving beyond purely topology-based node clustering in pool assignment. The approach aims to reduce computation cost while preserving richer structural information than existing clustering-based pooling methods.

entry.title: Predicting build orientation for SLM dental parts: a comparison of rotation representations and direct vector regression

author.name: Felix Schmalzel, Reimar Waitz, Moritz Kronberger, Thorsten Sch\"oler

entry.summary: The paper treats build-orientation prediction for selective laser melting of dental parts as supervised learning of a part's up-axis from about 2400 technician-labeled parts, comparing 13 rotation representations spanning six classical SO(3) parameterizations and seven direct unit-sphere representations. ResNet-50 multi-view and PointNeXt-S point-cloud backbones are fine-tuned and evaluated with geodesic angular error.

entry.title: Variational Template Matching with Statistical Fusion for Anomaly Detection in Patterned Structures

author.name: Qinwu Xu, Yifan Jiang

entry.summary: This paper proposes a variational template matching framework that represents anomaly templates as transformed instance families with normalized cross-correlation over the transformation space, fused with a KDE-derived statistical anomaly score for robustness to geometric variation. It targets small-data regimes where deep learning is impractical. The contribution is a practical, interpretable classical-ML enhancement for structured-image anomaly detection.

entry.title: GraMRAG: Orchestrating Multi-Agent Multi-Step Reasoning via Graph Memory with Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Zhongyu Wang

entry.summary: Proposes GraMRAG, a multi-agent RAG framework built on a dynamic multimodal memory graph for stable multi-step reasoning, combining multi-scale entity cropping with a ReAct-style visual toolchain for cross-modal reasoning. The system targets state blindness and shallow retrieval in knowledge-intensive multimodal question answering.

entry.title: A Conservative OCR-Enabled Workflow for R214 Sodium Screening of South African Packaged Foods

author.name: Mayimunah Nagayi, Alice Scaria Khan, Tamryn Frank, Rina Swart, Clement Nyirenda

entry.summary: This applied study builds a conservative image-based pipeline for screening packaged foods against South Africa's R214 sodium limits, combining region detection, OCR, product identity and sodium evidence extraction, category assignment, deterministic threshold comparison, and independent VLM verification. It was evaluated on 442 products with 3,929 package images from a real-world dataset, using a YOLO26s detector with strict post-processing. The workflow prioritizes reliability over recall for regulatory screening.

entry.title: Scalability and Performance Evaluation of Federated Learning Frameworks: A Comparative Analysis

author.name: Bassel Soudan, Sohail Abbas, Ahmed Kubba, Manar Wasif Abu Talib, Qassim Nasir

entry.summary: A systematic experimental comparison of prominent federated learning frameworks (FedML, Flower, Substra, OpenFL) across varying client counts, measuring training time, loss, accuracy, and CPU/RAM usage. Results reveal distinct performance characteristics, including anomalously high loss for Flower and low accuracy for FedML in the tested configurations.

entry.title: Early Prediction of Satellite Collision Probability Using a Hybrid TCN-Transformer Model for a CDM-Based Conjunction Analysis Framework

author.name: Rabia T\"uylek Tok, Burak Ya\u{g}l{\i}o\u{g}lu, Enes Da\u{g}, Emre Onur Kahya

entry.summary: This paper applies a hybrid temporal convolutional network and Transformer architecture to sequences of Conjunction Data Messages to predict collision probability early, helping satellite operators plan low-thrust avoidance maneuvers under time constraints. The nonlinear propagation of orbital uncertainty and PoC sensitivity make sequential CDM interpretation difficult, motivating learned early warning. It addresses a growing operational problem from orbital congestion.

entry.title: Graph Neural Networks for Influence Maximization in Social Networks: An Unsupervised Minimum Dominating Set Approach

author.name: Erfan Ahmadi, Mina Shirazi, Behnam Bahrak

entry.summary: This paper presents an unsupervised GNN framework for the NP-hard Minimum Dominating Set problem, eliminating the need for ground-truth solutions during training, with applications to viral marketing and influence maximization in social networks. It applies learning-based combinatorial optimization to large-scale network coverage problems.

entry.title: Selecting k Paths with the Minimum Longest Path Length in the Stochastic Semi-Bandit Setting

author.name: Shunsuke Aoki, Atsuyoshi Nakamura

entry.summary: The paper formulates an online semi-bandit problem where k paths must be selected each round in a directed network with edge capacity constraints and stochastic transmission times, minimizing the maximum traversal time among selected paths. The authors propose an algorithm motivated by parallel data transmission in networks. It matters for networking applications where worst-case latency across parallel routes is the key objective.

entry.title: QSTAR: Quantum Selective Transfer with Adaptive Routing

author.name: Saim Rehman, Nouhaila Innan, Muhammad Shafique

entry.summary: QSTAR is a selective quantum transfer learning framework that keeps high-confidence classical predictions and routes only low-confidence samples to a quantum fallback branch, asking when the quantum branch is genuinely useful. Using a frozen ResNet18 backbone on Fashion-MNIST, it shows manually designed quantum heads top out at 57.0% accuracy versus 78.5% for the strongest KetGPT-designed head. The honest evaluation of quantum advantage in transfer learning is the paper's main contribution.

entry.title: Early-Stopping Thresholds for ES-HyperNEAT: A Data-Driven Approach from Fitness Dynamics

author.name: Romain Claret, Arthur Gygax, Michael O'Neill, Paul Cotofrei, Pascal Felber

entry.summary: The paper frames early stopping of ES-HyperNEAT runs as binary classification on early fitness trajectories, deriving a threshold rule (generation 3, threshold 0.140) that achieves F1 of 0.872 on validation, retains over 90% of successful trials, and cuts compute by 41.6%. The domain-specific rule outperforms Hyperband in efficiency and mean fitness on this problem.

entry.title: HQARRF: Hierarchical Q-learning and Force-aware Routing for Multi-Charger Scheduling in Wireless Rechargeable Sensor Networks

author.name: Liang-Ching Tao, Pi-Chung Wang

entry.summary: HQARRF is a two-level scheduler for multi-charger scheduling in wireless rechargeable sensor networks, combining an interpretable attraction-repulsion-force scoring scheme for cluster selection with a gated Q-learning controller that decides zone redirection under deadline-based risk. Evaluated over 27 parameter points, it reduces duplicated service and unattended regions compared to local-urgency-driven baselines. It is a niche but concrete application of hierarchical reinforcement learning.

entry.title: Eigenvalue-Decomposition Cost Denoising as an Alternative to Predict-then-Optimize for Shortest-Path Problems

author.name: Henry Aldridge-Krawciw, Irene Aldridge

entry.summary: The paper proposes an alternative to predict-then-optimize methods like SPO+ for shortest-path problems: when many noisy realizations of the same cost process are observed, denoise the realized cost vectors directly via eigenvalue decomposition rather than learning a feature-to-cost mapping. This avoids degradation from linear-model misspecification of nonlinear cost processes.

entry.title: Accelerating Transfer-Learning-Based Autotuning with Predictive LLVM IR Performance Ranking

author.name: Md Arafat Hossain, Thomas Randall, Akash Dutta, Xingfu Wu, Rong Ge, Ali Jannesari

entry.summary: The authors present an autotuning framework for HPC that uses an ensemble ML ranker (Neural Configuration Scorer) over LLVM intermediate representations to prune poor configurations before costly evaluation. This reduces tuning overhead in transfer-learning-based autotuning. It matters for making performance tuning of complex HPC systems cheaper and faster.

entry.title: When Edit Localization Amplifies Relative Selection Bias: Gradient Geometry, Target Mismatch, and Importance Weighting

author.name: Shengwei Zhang, Haoda Dai, Yifei Li, Yuheng Song

entry.summary: The paper analyzes how selective feedback channels interact with edit localization in human-correction data, decomposing localized gradients into edited and retained components. It shows squared relative selection bias is a ratio of quadratics whose behavior under localization can increase, decrease, or change non-monotonically depending on gradient geometry, and derives finite-sample MSE results for importance weighting against a full-gradient target. This is relevant to learning from selectively collected human feedback.

entry.title: Scaling Hindi Quantum Natural Language Processing through Automatic Pregroup Supertagging

author.name: Gautami Sanjay Naik, Krishna Bhatia, Mithun Paul Saint-Germain, H Aswath Babu

entry.summary: This paper automates pregroup grammar supertagging for Hindi quantum natural language processing, casting type assignment as token-level classification over a 380-sentence annotated corpus. It compares lexical, contextual, prompting, and morphology-aware methods, finding simple contextual backoff models surprisingly strong in this low-resource setting. The work matters because it removes a manual bottleneck in scaling compositional QNLP to non-English languages.

entry.title: A Corpus-Aligned Uthmani-to-Standard Quranic Word Mapping and a Deterministic Recitation Validator

author.name: Yahya Mohamed Elnawasany

entry.summary: The paper releases a 2,290-pair corpus-aligned mapping between the Uthmani and Standard (Imla'i) orthographic forms of the Quran, built by aligning all 6,236 verses, plus a normalization pipeline centering on the frequently mishandled U+0670 superscript alef character. Normalizing both forms yields identical strings, enabling a deterministic recitation validator. This fixes a systematic gap in Arabic NLP tooling for Quranic text.

entry.title: Parameter-Efficient Quantum NLP for Paraphrase Detection: Performance, Robustness, and Entanglement

author.name: Farha Nausheen, Khandakar Ahmed, Farina Riaz

entry.summary: The authors evaluate a 10-qubit hybrid quantum-classical variational circuit with only 2,148 parameters on paraphrase detection across MRPC, QQP, and adversarial PAWS. The circuit statistically outperforms parameter-matched classical baselines on QQP and reaches 92% of BERT-base accuracy on MRPC with 54,000 fewer parameters. The paper also analyzes circuit depth scaling and entanglement, addressing the scarcity of rigorous empirical validation for quantum NLP.

entry.title: ArtSociety: Multi-Agent Multimodal Collaboration for Art Emotion Understanding

author.name: Jian Li, Fanfan Ji, Jinxiang Lai, Ying Tai, Jian Yang, Xiao-Tong Yuan, Chengjie Wang, Yabiao Wang

entry.summary: ArtSociety is a multi-agent framework for the AffectiveArt art emotion task that assembles heterogeneous multimodal experts (a DINOv2-Giant vision agent, a fine-tuned CoT MLLM, and closed-source reasoning agents) coordinated by training-free controllers, including a rare-class-aware voting arbiter for the 1549:1 class imbalance. The design explicitly handles empirical trade-offs between sub-tasks that prevent single models from jointly optimizing all outputs. It addresses fine-grained art emotion prediction with extreme class imbalance.

entry.title: The MODA General Attribute Suite: A Four-Track Evaluation Benchmark for Fashion Attribute Extraction

author.name: Arkid Mitra (Hopit AI)

entry.summary: The MODA suite is a four-track benchmark for fashion attribute extraction that separates localized crops, catalogue images, applicability-aware full-body photos, and product text, each with its own test set, metric, and leakage unit. It addresses inconsistent evaluation practices such as averaging incomparable image types and scoring invisible fields as ordinary negatives. Committed, label-blind prediction with hashing suggests a rigorous evaluation protocol.

entry.title: YOLO12-MambaScan: An Efficient Object Detector with High-Frequency Enhancement and State-Space Modeling

author.name: Hao Wang

entry.summary: YOLO12-MambaScan augments the YOLO12 detector for aerial imagery with a triple-path high-frequency enhancement convolution, receptive-field coordinate attention, and a Mamba-based global-context module to better detect small objects in cluttered UAV scenes. The combination targets retention of edge and texture cues plus efficient long-range context modeling. It is aimed at applications like traffic monitoring and disaster response.

entry.title: Event-Level Emotion Recognition in the Wild Using Deep Facial Expression Analysis

author.name: Aleksandr Semerikov, Pakizar Shamoi

entry.summary: An end-to-end pipeline for event-level emotion recognition that detects faces in event photographs, classifies expressions with a CNN, and aggregates face-level probabilities into an overall emotional distribution for a public event. It benchmarks several CNN architectures on FER-2013 and related in-the-wild data.

entry.title: EECTracker: Swarm Motion Prior-Guided Feature Compensation for Airborne Optical UAV Swarm Tracking

author.name: Zhaochen Chu, Tao Song, Ren Jin, Mingdong Jia, Defu Lin

entry.summary: EECTracker is a joint detection-and-tracking framework for airborne optical tracking of UAV swarms, using swarm motion priors to compensate for unreliable detector responses caused by tiny targets, viewpoint changes, and clutter. It aims to reduce fragmented trajectories and identity switches when target-specific detector responses are intermittent.

entry.title: Seeing What the Vehicle Sees: Video-Augmented Virtual Reality for Physical Autonomous Vehicles

author.name: Md Tanjemul Islam, Mohammad Shafin, Md Rafiul Kabir

entry.summary: The paper presents a video-augmented VR framework coupling a physical ROS 2 autonomous robot vehicle to a Unity 6 application on a Meta Quest 3S headset, streaming vehicle state and live camera feed over two independent channels. It aims to improve passenger trust and transparency compared to fully simulated or pre-scripted VR studies.

entry.title: Distributed Safe Cooperative Vector Field for Trajectory Curvature Constrained Multi-Robot Systems

author.name: Zhouru Xiao, Tao Teng, Weijia Yao, Hui Zhang, Xiangke Wang, Yaonan Wang

entry.summary: The paper proposes a distributed cooperative vector field approach for multi-robot path following under trajectory curvature constraints, combining a cooperative motion field with an adaptively adjustable safety-oriented collision avoidance field. It addresses turning limitations that can cause task failure or path divergence. Guarantees and scalability of the distributed design are the key claims.

entry.title: RSI will not continue indefinitely

author.name: dominicq

entry.summary: The author argues that recursive self-improvement may self-terminate or slow because each sufficiently capable agent has instrumental reasons to avoid creating a misaligned successor, potentially solving alignment for its own sake or halting the loop — implying humans would then restart the process with a fresh agent. The post sketches this loop and its implications for takeoff dynamics.

entry.title: MIT spinout turns plastic waste into resilient building materials

author.name: Zach Winn | MIT News

entry.summary: Atlas Building Composites, an MIT mechanical engineering spinout from the HAUS research group, uses an AI-powered robotic manufacturing platform with waterless plastic recycling and large-scale composite additive manufacturing to convert single-use plastics into construction components like foundations and trusses. The company aims to address plastic pollution and housing shortages simultaneously, with a stated goal of building one billion homes. The piece is a technology-commercialization story with an applied AI component.

entry.title: Planning or Learning: Reliability and Cost in Multi-Asset Maintenance

author.name: Xian Yeow Lee, Chandrasekar Venkatraman, Ahmed Farahat

entry.summary: Empirically compares planning and reinforcement learning for multi-asset bearing maintenance using run-to-failure data, across failure penalty scenarios. It finds a consistent behavioral difference driven by objective formulation: planning enforces reliability as a hard constraint while RL balances it against cost, with implications for reliability-cost trade-offs.

entry.title: ViperQ: Order Flow Pattern Recognition via Auction Market Theory for Reinforcement Learning Trading

author.name: Asser Moustafa, Rares-Mihail Neagu, Jugal Kalita

entry.summary: Presents ViperQ, an RL trading system whose state representation is built from Auction Market Theory and Market Profile primitives—Volume Point of Control, Value Area, Low Volume Nodes, cumulative volume delta divergence, and tape velocity—forming a 20-dimensional normalized vector, with PPO agents trained under prospective framing. Gives a peer-reviewed computational instantiation of practitioner microstructure theories absent from academic RL trading literature. Niche but distinctive.

entry.title: Design of a Deep Learning Credit Risk Early Warning System Integrating Multi-source Heterogeneous Data

author.name: LiYang Wang (Washington University in St. Louis), Zhen Zhong (Georgetown University), Zhen Tian (University of Glasgow), Keyu Chen (Wuyi University), Keyu Chen (Wuyi University)

entry.summary: The paper proposes a credit risk early warning system that fuses heterogeneous data such as transaction behaviors and social networks using deep neural networks with attention mechanisms to identify corporate and individual credit risk early. Reported system tests show improvements in accuracy and timeliness over existing approaches.

entry.title: GEAR: From Dynamic Encoding to Dynamic Activation in Social Trajectory Prediction

author.name: Jiaheng Chen, Jiaxing Li, Leixia Wang, Jianan Ju, Tinghe Zhang

entry.summary: GEAR argues that dynamic social encoding of pedestrian context does not imply dynamic activation during trajectory generation, proposing to modulate how strongly social cues influence predictions across future horizons and scene densities. This targets human trajectory prediction where interaction effects should vary with time and crowding. A modest architectural contribution to a crowded subfield.

entry.title: Finite-Time Node Separation in Recurrent Graph Neural Networks with Persistent Gaussian Perturbations

author.name: Mostafa Haghir Chehreghani

entry.summary: Provides a finite-time theoretical analysis showing that persistent Gaussian perturbations keep individual GNN node representations separated, complementing prior asymptotic oversmoothing results. The paper derives an exact second-moment decomposition and a universal lower bound of 2*sigma^2*d on expected squared distance between node representations at every positive time step.

entry.title: Bi-Level Routing and Sparse Spatial Attention based Multi-View BEV 3D Object Detection for Autonomous Driving

author.name: Jing Zhang, Jiaqi Liu, Zibo Wang

entry.summary: Proposes Sparse-BEVNet for multi-view BEV 3D detection, adding Bi-Level Routing Attention to the image backbone, Cascaded Group Attention to feature fusion, and a Sparse Spatial Cross-Attention mechanism to reduce the cost of dense 2D-to-BEV view transformation. The design targets computational complexity and multi-scale feature extraction challenges.

entry.title: PU classification under Non-SCAR: clustering-assisted logistic model with oversampling enhancement

author.name: Konrad Furma\'nczyk, Kacper Paczutkowski

entry.summary: This study tackles positive-unlabeled classification when the standard SCAR assumption is violated, combining the cluster method, Lasso-regularized logistic regression, and SMOTE oversampling with 2-means-derived cleaning labels. It systematically assesses how oversampling affects these PU algorithms. The work offers a practical recipe rather than new theory.

entry.title: A Machine Learning API for Earth Observation Data Cubes Based on openEO

author.name: Brian Pondi, Jonas Hurst, Rolf Simoes, Jonas Starke, Marius Appel, Edzer Pebesma

entry.summary: The authors propose a process-level machine learning specification for openEO, structured into model initialization, model actions (training, tuning, inference, validation), and model management, to bridge the mismatch between EO data cubes and ML workflows across cloud backends. It supports classical algorithms and deep learning, aiming for reproducible, platform-independent EO analytics. This is infrastructure work for the geospatial ML community.

entry.title: ReH-FUSE: Reliability-Aware Hierarchical Fusion of Experts for Multimodal Emotion Recognition in Conversation

author.name: Guan-Hua Wen, Hou-Chiang Tseng, Kuan-Yu Chen

entry.summary: ReH-FUSE is a reliability-aware fusion framework for multimodal emotion recognition with dialogue-aware text, audio, and cross-modal experts, where a router first models text-audio preference and then balances the unimodal mixture against the cross-modal expert. It achieves strong results on IEMOCAP across three independent runs.

entry.title: Machine Learning in Fish Farming

author.name: Fearghal O'Donncha, Nikos Papandroulakis, Jennie Korus, Abigail Langbridge, Alexander Timms, Konstantinos Topouzelis, Abdul Baseer Khan, Shree Rama Kamal Kumar Vegu, Mahtab Sarvmaili, Ryan Mowat, Rhanna Turberville, Tyler Sclodnick, Christopher Whidden

entry.summary: A book chapter reviewing how machine learning transforms aquaculture, covering techniques from Random Forests and CNNs to emerging GNNs and LLMs, with applications like biomass estimation and species recognition, plus case studies and future directions. It emphasizes real-world operational decision support.

entry.title: Cloud Workflow Scheduling Based on Graph Attention-Driven Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Zongjin Li, Shaohan Feng, Chunxi Yang, Wenbo Wang

entry.summary: The paper presents GA-HRL, a hierarchical reinforcement learning framework for dynamic cloud workflow scheduling that balances deadline satisfaction, container utilization, and energy consumption. It uses multi-head graph attention networks to extract dependency structure from evolving task DAGs with predicted sub-deadlines. It matters for improving resource efficiency in cloud datacenters under stochastic conditions.

entry.title: Online local learning for generative thermodynamic computing

author.name: Huilin Wang, Weibing Deng

entry.summary: The authors train generative thermodynamic computers with a local update at each Langevin integration step, deriving the coupling gradient from a reverse-path Onsager-Machlup objective. In MNIST simulations, online training matches trajectory-batch validation losses while releasing less heat, a relevant property for physical thermodynamic hardware.

entry.title: Inter-Rater Reliability of LLM and Rule-Based Annotation for Inferential Narrative Features: Three Studies on a Turkish Corpus

author.name: Levent Bulut

entry.summary: This report assesses whether humans agree with automatically generated annotations on a Turkish narrative corpus, running three studies that score a rule-based detector, plus Gemini 2.5 Flash and Grok as judges, against blind human labels. It focuses on six craft features such as emotion labelling and materialized metaphor. The work probes a rarely examined question about the trustworthiness of shipped auto-annotations.

entry.title: Personalized and Explainable Blood Pressure Estimation from PPG via Hybrid CNN--Morphological Features

author.name: Myung-Kyu Yi, Jongshill Lee, Jeyeon Lee, In Young Kim

entry.summary: This paper presents a physiology-guided hybrid framework for cuffless blood pressure estimation from photoplethysmography, coupling a CNN capturing waveform dynamics with a morphology-prior branch encoding person-specific vascular characteristics. The design aims to combine deep learning accuracy with physiological interpretability, addressing limitations of both handcrafted-feature and black-box approaches. The work targets personalized continuous health monitoring.

entry.title: Floquet Fibre Geometry and Higher-Order Reduced Coordinates for Off-Manifold Transients near Nonlinear Aeroelastic Flutter

author.name: Puxue Tan

entry.summary: This paper analyzes invariant-fibre geometry for assigning reduced coordinates to states near attracting limit cycles, proving that charts satisfying linearised semiconjugacy leave only second-order invariance residuals while non-invariant projections leave first-order errors. It demonstrates large discrepancies (48.5 to 71.7 degrees) between metric-normal and strong-stable directions for a nonlinear aeroelastic limit cycle.

entry.title: Tracking the Ground: Online Lidar Identification of Robot-Induced Soil Deformation in Agricultural Environments

author.name: Tom Montagnon, Johann Laconte, Benoit Thuilot, Wonjae Cho, Roland Lenain

entry.summary: The paper proposes a framework to quantify vehicle-induced soil deformation and estimate its evolution online from lidar observations, using a reduced-order parametric model with physically meaningful parameters. This is a step toward soil-aware agricultural robotics that explicitly accounts for ground degradation from traffic. The method supports more sustainable field operations.

entry.title: RA-CoA: Training-free Fashion Image Captioning via Retrieval-Augmented Chain-of-Attributes

author.name: Abhirama Subramanyam Penamakuri, Shreya Shukla, Anand Mishra

entry.summary: Proposes a training-free fashion image captioning method that combines retrieval augmentation with a chain-of-attributes reasoning process so instruction-tuned vision-language models can capture fine-grained domain terminology like necklines, closures, and silhouettes. The training-free design supports scalability as fashion vocabularies and styles evolve rapidly.

entry.title: HiGFRL: Hierarchical Graph Fusion-Driven Reinforcement Learning for Dependency-Aware Task Scheduling in Heterogeneous Cloud

author.name: Tiangang Li, Shi Ying, Xiangbo Tian

entry.summary: HiGFRL is a hierarchical reinforcement learning framework for scheduling dependency-aware tasks in heterogeneous cloud clusters, using a three-level state representation combining a static hypergraph, dynamic global graph, and local bipartite graph to model DAG topology alongside multi-dimensional resource constraints. It aims to overcome myopic decisions in prior GNN-based DRL schedulers. It matters for efficient utilization of heterogeneous compute resources.

entry.title: Preserving Subject-Clarity in Image Outpainting with Multiscale Wavelet Supervision

author.name: Abhilash Neog, Taewan Kim, Yi Wu, Xu Chen, Jian Jiao

entry.summary: The authors propose an outpainting framework combining VLM-guided semantic conditioning with multiscale wavelet supervision to preserve subject fidelity when extending image boundaries, targeting commercial and advertising use cases with cropped subjects or truncated text. Existing diffusion outpainting methods often produce plausible completions that degrade the primary subject through structural inconsistency or semantic drift. The framework addresses this subject-clarity problem directly.

entry.title: A Hybrid Agentic AI Framework for Intelligent Supply Chain Analytics

author.name: Xian Yeow Lee, Teppei Inoue, Haiyan Wang, Chetan Gupta

entry.summary: Proposes an agentic system for supply chain analytics in which a coordinator agent interprets user intent and delegates sub-tasks like database querying, KPI analysis, demand forecasting, and performance diagnosis to specialized agents. The system supports both exploratory analysis and deterministic workflows, bridging business decision-making and technical expertise.

entry.title: FedV-KGQA in Practice: Design Lessons and an Interactive Prototype

author.name: Md Saikat Islam Khan Bappy, Oshani Seneviratne

entry.summary: A poster-style paper presenting empirical lessons from FedV-KGQA, a system for multi-hop question answering over vertically partitioned knowledge graphs where each organization trains embeddings on its own triples and a server ranks candidates without raw triples leaving the silo. Includes an interactive prototype demonstrating the privacy-preserving federated reasoning pipeline. Useful for practitioners in federated knowledge management.

entry.title: OptoAgent: A Trustworthy Multi-Agent Framework for Opportunistic Vision Micro-Screening in Classroom Environments

author.name: Toqeer Ali Syed, Ali Akarma, Adeel Ahmad, Hammad Muneer

entry.summary: SightSentinel embeds short calibrated vision-screening probes into ordinary classroom wall-display content, using eight specialized agents to detect reduced distance vision in children without anyone initiating a test. The idea is opportunistic, recurring screening at the moment and place where difficulties appear. Companion paper to the same group's accessibility work with a similar eight-agent architecture.

entry.title: New Conditions for Philosophers to Catch the Wave of Citizen Deliberation in the Age of Artificial Intelligence in advance

author.name: Bernard Reber (CEVIPOF)

entry.summary: This position-style paper from a political philosopher examines how LLMs could support citizen deliberation processes such as citizens' assemblies through moderation, translation, facilitation, and summarization. It describes the Democratic Commons project, an interdisciplinary effort to evaluate LLMs against five proposed democratic principles.

entry.title: Feasibility and Memory Mechanisms of Chern-Simons Context Reservoir Computation

author.name: Jyotiranjan Beuria, Venkatesh H. Chembrolu

entry.summary: This paper investigates whether a Chern-Simons gauge-theory-inspired reservoir is a viable computational substrate, comparing four matched models to isolate gauge-specific effects from generic reservoir behavior. The fully coupled conserved-current dynamics propagates Gauss law to numerical precision and converges under refinement, but the key question is whether the evolving gauge connection provides benefits over simpler mechanisms.

entry.title: Leakage-Safe and Scheduler-Aware Machine Learning for Grid Job Runtime Prediction

author.name: Ashfaq Ali Shafin, Khandaker Mamun Ahmed

entry.summary: This paper reformulates CPU burst time prediction on the AuverGrid workload trace as a leakage-safe, pre-execution runtime prediction task, using only submission-time features and evaluating under temporal and cold-start settings. It compares standard regressors, historical baselines, categorical encodings, and CatBoost, highlighting how random cross-validation overstates real deployment performance. A solid methodological critique of common evaluation practice in scheduling research.

entry.title: A Voxel-Spacing-Aware Extension of PyRadiomics for Anisotropic Texture Analysis

author.name: David Corral Fontecha, Juan Miranda Bautista, Pablo Menendez Fern\'andez-Miranda, Andrea Trapote Fernandez, Lara Lloret Iglesias, Jose A. Vega

entry.summary: Implements and validates a voxel-spacing-aware extension of the widely used PyRadiomics library so that radiomic texture features (GLCM, NGTDM, GLRLM, GLDM, GLSZM) correctly account for anisotropic CT and MRI voxel geometry without interpolated gray levels. Validation uses synthetic 3D phantoms across the Python frontend, C wrapper, and computational backend.

entry.title: Cross-Block Conditioning in Deep Boltzmann Machines for Statistical Data Fusion

author.name: Junichiro Niimi

entry.summary: The paper proposes observed-block multi-prediction training for Deep Boltzmann Machines in statistical data fusion settings where two panels share covariates but observe disjoint outcomes, making standard multi-prediction training infeasible. The restricted objective works for any missingness pattern and reduces to the standard criterion on complete data, enabling evaluation of whether joint modeling actually helps. This is a niche methodological contribution for data fusion.

entry.title: Interpreting hierarchical organisation of speaker embeddings

author.name: Yanze Xu, Wenwu Wang, Mark D. Plumbley

entry.summary: This work applies Single-Linkage Clustering to analyze whether speaker embeddings learned by recognition networks form hierarchically related clusters, framing the analysis within explainable AI. It offers interpretability insights into the latent organization of speaker representations.

entry.title: On the Potential of Multi-Task Learning in Predictive Process Monitoring

author.name: Lukas Kirchdorfer, Keyvan Amiri Elyasi, Heiner Stuckenschmidt

entry.summary: This paper systematically explores multi-task learning for predictive process monitoring, asking whether and under which settings joint learning of multiple prediction targets beats single-task models, which tasks benefit most, and which combinations work. Given that most PPM approaches train a separate model per task, the study clarifies where MTL synergies exist. It is a useful empirical mapping for the business process management community.

entry.title: PPDL: A Real-world Industrial User Retention Ratio Forecasting Framework Integrating Physical Priors with Deep Learning

author.name: Zibo Zhao, Zhengxiong Guan, Chaoli Zhang, Linyuan Geng, Xuanbing Zhu, Zhonglong Zheng, Fan Wu

entry.summary: PPDL forecasts channel-level user retention for paid acquisition on a large short-video platform by embedding physical priors (churn-then-stabilization dynamics, seasonality, autocorrelation) into a deep learning framework. It targets early prediction to optimize budget allocation across channels.
