author.name: Heinrich Jiang, Hager Yasser Mohamed, Alexander Hitt, Valeriia Lomakina, Henning Jiang, Jennifer Jang

entry.summary: This paper demonstrates that existing B-rep encoders are not robust to variations in boundary representations of the same solid, whether from perturbations, CAD software kernel differences, or different human modeling workflows (assessed via a newly created FreeCAD dataset). It proposes canonical inputs so networks learn the underlying solid rather than file-specific artifacts.

entry.title: Conformal-DRO: Distributionally Robust Optimization with Conformalized Ambiguity Set

author.name: Luhao Zhang, Shixiang Zhu

entry.summary: Conformal-DRO addresses distributionally robust optimization under latent distributional heterogeneity, where each instance has an unobserved outcome law observable through a single sample. It constructs ambiguity sets from nested conformal regions, guaranteeing finite-sample coverage of the latent law with probability at least 1-alpha under exchangeability, without estimating latent laws or mixing mechanisms.

entry.title: NCP-ArchPreview Technical Report: Moving towards Latent Space Language Models through Next Concept Prediction

author.name: NCP Team, Jiaqi Cao, Chiyu Chen, Shuang Cheng, Xu Cheng, Beiya Dai, Yufan Feng, Kewen Ge, Ruijun Ge, Jiayi Huang, Yang Jiao, Dahua Lin, Zhouhan Lin, Yifan Liu, Yuliang Liu, Biqing Qi, Mowen Ruan, Junzhe Shen, Yunchong Song, Hao Sun, Zhongbo Tian, Yixuan Wang, Rubin Wei, Jiaxin Xiong, Kangyu Yang, Qian Yao, Qi Zhang, Bowen Zhou

entry.summary: NCP-ArchPreview extends autoregressive pretraining beyond next-token prediction with Next Concept Prediction over a product-quantized concept vocabulary built from the model's own hidden states, jointly trained end-to-end with standard NTP. Predicted multi-token concepts are fed back to guide token-level generation, pushing toward latent-space language modeling.

entry.title: Do Agents Know When They Succeed? Calibrating Agent Confidence from Internal Representations

author.name: Priyanka Mary Mammen, Emil Joswin, Srujananjali Medicherla

entry.summary: Investigates whether LLM agents' internal representations signal eventual task success in multi-turn agentic setups, proposing Latent Trajectory Dynamics over residual streams and an Action Representation Probe to predict success at action decision points. The goal is calibrated confidence for safety-critical agentic deployments.

entry.title: AgentHijack: Visual Patch Attacks on Multimodal Computer-Use Agents

author.name: Zhihao Liu, Hongyu Sun, Zhiyuan Fu, Xiaonan Duan, Jice Wang, Shangru Zhao, Weizhi Meng, Wuxin Yang, Yangfan Zhou, Yuqing Zhang

entry.summary: Introduces an end-to-end evaluation framework for image-triggered command injection against computer-use agents, testing whether adversarial visual patches can cause real environmental actions through the full screenshot-to-action pipeline. Evaluated across five GUI-agent and VLM backends with 600 online cases, achieving up to 84.5% trigger attack success rate. The work reveals serious security risks as computer-use agents are deployed on live web content.

entry.title: What Fixed-Rollout pass@k Evaluations Can Identify

author.name: Pranav Singh, Prashant Singh

entry.summary: This paper provides an identifiability analysis of pass@k evaluations used in repeated-sampling LLM evaluation, proving that fixed-n success counts identify only n moments of the latent per-task success distribution. As a result, direct pass@k is identifiable only for k <= n, and extrapolated pass@k, tail exponents, and tail constants are fundamentally unidentified beyond n, with explicit constructions showing incompatible distributions with identical counts. This is an important caveat for the increasingly common practice of extrapolating pass@k from limited samples.

entry.title: Cascading Gradient Inversion via LT-Code Inspired Peeling in Federated Learning

author.name: Saeed Shariati, Mohsen Alambardar Meybodi

entry.summary: Connects gradient inversion attacks in federated learning to erasure-correcting codes, using LT-code-inspired peeling to construct attacks that exactly recover full batches and labels from a single FedSGD round, exceeding previously known upper bounds for analytic reconstruction attacks. Each recovery is certifiable without ground-truth data.

entry.title: BRACE: Anchored Bellman-Residual Correction for Stale Critics in Asynchronous RL

author.name: Guanqun Zhao, Zijun Xie, Binbin Zheng, Jiafeng Lu, Enlei Gong, Zeyu Chen

entry.summary: BRACE corrects the critic bias caused by policy lag in asynchronous RL training of language models, where existing methods correct only the actor. It bounds the correction horizon to a prefix of policy tokens and anchors constant-weight Monte Carlo estimates, avoiding exponential importance-ratio drift in long agentic trajectories. This addresses a real obstacle to scaling RL for long-horizon LLM agents.

entry.title: Strangers to Themselves: What Language Models Say About Themselves Is Generic

author.name: Phil Blandfort, Urja Pawar

entry.summary: This paper tests LLM self-knowledge by having models predict their own behavior across nine evaluations, comparing predictions against controls. Self-report correlates only weakly with actual behavior (r = +0.04), and asking a model about itself performs no better than asking about capable AI agents in general. The findings challenge the reliability of model introspection and have implications for interpretability and honesty research.

entry.title: Beyond Training: A Feasibility Taxonomy for Inference-Time AI Governance

author.name: Samar Ansari

entry.summary: The paper argues that compute governance focused on training is incomplete as capability migrates to deployment via inference-time scaling, agentic scaffolding, and consumer-hardware compression. It develops a taxonomy of twenty inference-time governance mechanisms across monitoring, verification, and enforcement, each rated for feasibility on a four-point readiness scale with a four-vendor evidence base.

entry.title: The information geometry of large language models is shared, learned, and controllable

author.name: Dario Picozzi

entry.summary: The paper studies the Fisher-Rao geometry of next-token probability distributions and finds that output geometry is shared across transformer, state-space, and recurrent LLMs, supporting semantic-category transfer, while activation geometry diverges. It also shows alignment with human word similarity increases with scale and training and can be improved via model-only calibration, suggesting geometry is a controllable lever on behavior.

entry.title: REVA: Reusable Evidence View Aggregation for Context-Efficient RAG Serving

author.name: Tuan Nguyen, Qiran Hu, Banruo Liu, Khoa D. Doan, Kok-Seng Wong, Fan Lai

entry.summary: REVA reframes retrieval-augmented generation compression from a data-mining angle, aggregating historical query-document-model interactions into reusable evidence views to cut latency, KV-cache memory, and token cost. The paper first documents that modern post-retrieval compressors often have unstable gains over simple truncation and add real inference overhead, then proposes amortized reusable views as a more efficient serving strategy. This is a systems-level efficiency contribution for LLM RAG pipelines.

entry.title: Reification as a Transferable Vocabulary: Zero-Shot Link Prediction with Vanilla GNNs

author.name: Camille Pradel

entry.summary: This work shows that zero-shot inductive link prediction, previously achieved by knowledge graph foundation models like ULTRA via hard-coded transfer architectures, can be accomplished by standard GNNs if the input graph is reified so every fact becomes a node connected via six fixed meta-relations. Five textbook GNNs trained on a tiny 4,245-triple graph for 30 minutes on one A100 transfer zero-shot to 40 inductive link prediction benchmarks. The result challenges the assumption that specialized architectures are required for graph transfer and suggests transferability can live in the representation rather than the model.

entry.title: Musec: MomentUm SpEctral Clipping for Stable Muon-type Training

author.name: Zhuanghua Liu, Menglian Wang, Luo Luo

entry.summary: Musec addresses training instability in the Muon optimizer for LLM training by replacing spectral flattening with spectral clipping of the momentum matrix's singular values, avoiding loss spikes and unbounded weight growth without architecture-specific clipping. This directly targets a practical pain point in an optimizer gaining adoption for large-scale pretraining.

entry.title: Thinking with Looped Flows

author.name: Ayhan Suleymanzade, Chanhyuk Lee, Floor Eijkelboom, Nicholas M. Boffi, \.Ismail \.Ilkan Ceylan, Jinwoo Kim

entry.summary: Looped flows train recurrent (looped) inference computation using local denoising objectives rather than backpropagation through many updates, imposing temporal association via progressively decreasing noise levels and shared noise. This incentivizes recurrent states whose computation transfers across time, addressing a core training difficulty of looped models.

entry.title: When Synthetic Data Hurts: On Catastrophic Forgetting in Skill Retrieval for LLM Agents

author.name: Syed Shariyar Murtaza, Yifan Nie, Utkarsh Soni, Eugene Wen, Arvid Frydenlund

entry.summary: This large-scale production study examines skill routing over 34,396 skills for LLM agents and finds that fine-tuning on synthetic data improves in-distribution retrieval but causes catastrophic forgetting on real and out-of-distribution data. The authors evaluate continual-learning mitigation strategies including embedding-anchor regularization, LwF, EWC, and L2-initialization, showing these can retain in-distribution performance while limiting forgetting. The paper offers practical guidance on the growing but risky practice of synthetic-data fine-tuning for agent systems.

entry.title: Composable CXL Memory as a Kubernetes-Native Shared Memory for LLM Serving

author.name: Hongjian Fan, Kevin Zhang, David Habinsky, Sean Dykstra

entry.summary: This systems paper presents a Kubernetes DRA driver that makes composable CXL memory a schedulable cluster resource, enabling cross-node KV-cache reuse for LLM serving via vLLM/llm-d. It embeds a slot directory directly in the shared memory medium, removing the need for an external metadata service, and demonstrates the approach on a two-node cluster with a 512 GiB CXL appliance. This matters because KV-cache sharing across nodes is a practical bottleneck in scaling LLM inference infrastructure.

entry.title: Your Model Already Knows Don't Teach It, Learn to Ask It: Soft Prompting for Few-Shot Adaptation of Vision-Language Models

author.name: Gautam Rajendrakumar Gare, Siyi Li, Hewei Wang, Cesar Daniel Hernandez, Wei Zhao, Wolfgang M. Pauli, John Galeotti, Deva Ramanan

entry.summary: This work studies few-shot object detection with vision-language models in out-of-domain settings like aerial, industrial, and medical imagery using only ten annotated images, comparing discrete prompt optimization, LoRA fine-tuning, and soft prompting with a frozen backbone. The authors identify two key design choices: placing prompt tokens at the cross-modal boundary between visual and text tokens, and initializing prompts from the empty space token. With only one to three learned prompt tokens, the method reportedly outperforms the alternatives, arguing that pretrained VLMs already contain the needed knowledge and adaptation should elicit rather than teach it.

entry.title: Vidu S2: Real-Time Interactive, Editable, and Spatial Video Generation

author.name: Jintao Zhang, Kai Jiang, Jintao Chen, Xu Wang, Deyuan Liu, Jungang Li, Dechuang Chen, Ming Lin, Jingjiang Zhou, Haopeng Jin, Qi Jia, Xiaohang Wang, Yaole Wang, Zhanqiang Zhang, Ran Li, Zhengkun Huang, Shuyue Xiong, Yuji Wang, Zikun Dai, Hui He, Yang Luo, Mang Ning, Weiqi Feng, Chengyang Ye, Xinyue Lin, Min Zhao, Hongzhou Zhu, Hengkai Tan, Zeyuan Wang, Chendong Xiang, Kaiwen Zheng, Zhijie Deng, Fan Bao, Jianfei Chen, Jun Zhu

entry.summary: Vidu S2 comprises a real-time interactive digital-character model (Vidu S2-Avatar) supporting 720p real-time generation with dynamically updatable references and stronger instruction following, and a real-time video editing model (Vidu S2-Editing) for style, clothing, character, and background replacement in live streams. The team also explores real-time spatial video generation, and reports outperforming all baselines with an online demo available. This is a notable industry contribution pushing video generation toward interactive, latency-critical use cases.

entry.title: Structured Transforms for Low-Overhead Quantization of Language Models

author.name: Daria Cherniuk, Alexander Rudikov, Boris Kashin, Ivan Oseledets

entry.summary: Improves Kashin-decomposition-based weight quantization for LLMs by replacing dense random orthogonal matrices with a sign-randomized DCT, reducing per-iteration cost from O(N^2) to O(N log N). A greedy alternating-update algorithm guarantees the four-peak distribution needed for stable 2-bit clustering, enabling aggressive quantization with structured transforms. Targets extreme low-bit deployment of large models.

entry.title: More than half of recent astronomy papers are written with language-model assistance

author.name: Serat M. Saad, Yuan-Sen Ting

entry.summary: Using a hierarchical Bayesian mixture model over 207,111 astro-ph papers (2015 to mid-2026), the authors estimate that roughly 54% of 2025 astronomy papers show the distinctive vocabulary signature of LLM-assisted writing, calibrated on pre-2020 papers and 392 disclosing papers. The estimate is reported under three assumptions about the counterfactual unassisted rate.

entry.title: Biology-in-the-loop: Amortized Adaptive Hit Discovery in CRISPR Screens

author.name: Carl Edwards, Edward De Brouwer, Xiner Li, Namkyeong Lee, Ehsan Hajiramezanali, Anne Biton, Sara Mostafavi, Gabriele Scalia

entry.summary: The paper introduces AssayBench-Loop, a large-scale benchmark of 1,389 CRISPR screens across five phenotype categories for adaptive hit discovery under budget constraints. Its scale enables learning amortized acquisition strategies across historical experiments, and the authors propose a corresponding method for prioritizing perturbations.

entry.title: LoopVAE: Recurrent Depth Across Scales for Visual Tokenization

author.name: Zhiying Lu

entry.summary: LoopVAE questions the parameter redundancy of hierarchical visual tokenizers by reusing a single scale- and loop-conditioned core both within and across spatial scales. A 29M-parameter model with a four-block core applied 28 times matches or beats 84M reference VAEs on ImageNet-256 reconstruction (0.28 rFID, 32.54 dB PSNR) with roughly 65% fewer parameters.

entry.title: IMLE-VLA: Fast Single-Step Action Generation for Vision-Language-Action Policies

author.name: Kian Hosseinkhani (Simon Fraser University), Qinhe Peng (University of Pennsylvania), George Shramko (Simon Fraser University), Mehran Aghabozorgi (Simon Fraser University), Jianing Qian (University of Pennsylvania), Tristan Engst (Simon Fraser University), Alireza Moazeni (Simon Fraser University), Dinesh Jayaraman (University of Pennsylvania), Ke Li (Simon Fraser University, Canada CIFAR AI Chair)

entry.summary: IMLE-VLA replaces iterative diffusion/flow-matching action heads in vision-language-action robot policies with a single-step conditional generator trained via conditional Implicit Maximum Likelihood Estimation, promoting multimodal action coverage without mode collapse. This removes the inference bottleneck (e.g., 10 Euler steps in pi0.5) that causes stop-and-go robot movement and slower task completion.

entry.title: ActSafeGuard: Differentiable and Training-Aligned Constraint Enforcement for Flow-Matching Policies

author.name: Jianming Ma, Rongjun Jin, Xiaxi Si, Yang Zhang, Yiheng Li, Yue Gao

entry.summary: ActSafeGuard introduces a differentiable, training-aligned safeguard layer for flow-matching VLA/WAM policies that integrates hard action feasibility into policy learning itself, rather than treating safety as an inference-time correction or a soft statistical objective. This closes the mismatch between policy training and execution-time safety enforcement.

entry.title: SEED-UMI: Sharing the Exoskeleton between human and robot for onE-to-one Dexterous demonstration

author.name: Tengbo Yu, Jiahao Wu, Daohan Li, Bingxu Chen, Hao Liu, Xiaojian Ma, Hangxin Liu

entry.summary: SEED-UMI introduces a data-collection framework where the human and robot wear the same exoskeleton, making joint encoders a physically shared measurement and enabling wrist cameras to observe the same mechanism during both demonstration and robot rollouts. This converts retargeting into paired cross-embodiment supervision and allows policies to train on raw exoskeleton-centric images, addressing the bottleneck of transferring contact-rich dexterous demonstrations.

entry.title: A Mathematical Theory of Pragmatic Information

author.name: Kai Niu, Ping Zhang

entry.summary: The authors propose a unified theory of pragmatic information spanning communication, control, and decision-making, centered on an isoteleia mapping that treats distinct semantic paths leading to the same optimal action as equivalent. They build a three-tier syntactic-semantic-pragmatic hierarchy, define pragmatic entropy, mutual information, capacity, and rate-distortion, and prove three coding theorems that generalize Shannon's classical results.

entry.title: Measuring Subliminal Trait Transfer with Confusion Matrices

author.name: Edward Cant

entry.summary: An independent experimental study of subliminal learning (trait transfer through teacher-generated data) proposing a confusion-matrix methodology to avoid selection bias and streetlight effects, and demonstrating the phenomenon in small pretrained PolyPythia models rather than large instruction-tuned LLMs. It explores how random initialization affects subliminal trait transfer across seeds.

entry.title: Understanding In-Context Multimodal Jailbreaks via Posterior Reweighting

author.name: Xu Zhang, Dev Mistry, Xiang Xu, Ren Wang

entry.summary: This paper proposes a posterior reweighting framework that explains why in-context learning jailbreaks succeed in multimodal LLMs, modeling the safety-aligned model as operating over competing behavioral modes where demonstrations act as inference-time evidence shifting posterior preference between safe and harmful behaviors. This formalizes jailbreak effectiveness and how it scales with context composition. It matters because principled theory of jailbreak mechanisms is scarce.

entry.title: The Platonic brain bridge hypothesis: human brain networks as an architectural prior for omni models

author.name: Pengfei Zhang, Biao Tian, Xiangang Li, Li Liu

entry.summary: The paper proposes that omni models processing video, audio, and text converge on brain-like representations, demonstrating the correspondence bidirectionally: brain-likeness is stable across participants and their encoding models top the Algonauts 2025 out-of-distribution leaderboard. In the brain-to-model direction, Brain-MoE assigns cortical-network-pretrained experts to an omni model, raising held-out accuracy in all 15 model-benchmark pairs by 6.42 points on average. This is an ambitious, bidirectional neuroscience-AI research program.

entry.title: LAION-Mobile: Evaluating Deepfake Detectors On One Million Smartphone Photos

author.name: Achim von Stryk, Janis Keuper

entry.summary: This work builds a large-scale dataset of one million modern smartphone photos to test whether on-device computational photography pipelines cause deepfake detectors to flag ordinary phone photos as fake, scaling up a hypothesis raised in a recent ICML position paper. Near-perfect benchmark AUCs may not reflect real-world behavior on smartphone imagery.

entry.title: Subagents vs Agent Skills: Executing Reusable Knowledge for Long-Horizon Agentic Tasks

author.name: Wasu Top Piriyakulkij, Rachel Lawrence, Alicia Curth, Sushrut Karmalkar, Niranjani Prasad

entry.summary: Compares two ways LLM agents can use reusable skill packages: loading instructions into context versus invoking them as subagents. The paper argues context-loading degrades over long horizons and empirically evaluates the subagent alternative, a timely architectural question for agent frameworks.

entry.title: Black-Box Red Teaming of Agentic AI: A Taxonomy-Driven Framework for Automated Risk Discovery

author.name: Divyanshu Kumar, Nitin Aravind Birur, Tanay Baswa, Sahil Agarwal, Prashanth Harshangi

entry.summary: Presents a systematic black-box framework for multi-step agentic security evaluation, including a seven-domain risk taxonomy, automated SAGE-RT red teaming generating 120 adversarial scenarios per domain, and LLM-judge evaluation with human validation. Validated across CrewAI and AutoGen architectures with multiple base models. It addresses the gap left by single-turn evaluations as agentic systems move to production with tool permissions and untrusted inputs.

entry.title: Proof-Carrying Cognition: Closing the Verification Gap with Reality-Settled Reward

author.name: Eshwar Reddy M, Sourav Karmakar

entry.summary: This position-plus-theory paper argues that the binding constraint on RL-based reasoning gains is the lack of cheap, sound verifiers outside formal domains. It derives quantitative results on how verifier-gold correlation trades off against test-time compute, predicts judge soundness with low error, and demonstrates the framework on program-synthesis testbeds with executable ground truth.

entry.title: Quantifying Logical Consistency in Transformers via Query-Key Alignment

author.name: Eduard Tulchinskii, Anastasia Voznyuk, Laida Kushnareva, Andrei Andriiainen, Irina Piontkovskaya, Evgeny Burnaev, Serguei Barannikov

entry.summary: Proposes a lightweight method to assess multi-step logical reasoning in LLMs by computing a QK-score from query-key alignments in attention heads during a single forward pass. The score separates valid from invalid inferences, offering an internal signal of reasoning coherence that complements Chain-of-Thought output evaluation. This matters for interpretability and trustworthy reasoning assessment without expensive probing.

entry.title: Distribution-Consistent Inference for Dynamic Sparse Mixture-of-Experts

author.name: Dohyeon Kim, Bedionita Soro, Sung Ju Hwang

entry.summary: This paper studies inference-time dynamic top-k routing in sparse Mixture-of-Experts models, showing that reducing the number of active experts causes a distributional shift in output representations, specifically increasing RMS scale and variance, which degrades downstream performance. The authors propose distribution-consistent corrections that allow cheaper inference without retraining while preserving quality. This matters for the efficiency of large foundation models where MoE is a dominant scaling paradigm.

entry.title: DiffLUT-Net: Differentiable Training of FPGA LUT Networks with Learnable Connectivity

author.name: Jiaqi Ye, Xinrui Gong, Jingcun Wang, Olga Kondrateva, Bing Li, Grace Li Zhang

entry.summary: DiffLUT-Net trains FPGA-native neural networks built from six-input lookup tables from scratch, jointly learning both the 64-entry truth tables and the connectivity to each LUT input port via a differentiable relaxation. After training, the networks are discretized, pruned, and exported directly as synthesizable Verilog, achieving favorable accuracy-resource trade-offs across five benchmarks. This matters because it enables efficient edge inference without relying on pretrained quantized models or MAC-based acceleration.

entry.title: Arbitrary Cipher Attacks Against Large Language Models Do Not Require Fine-Tuning

author.name: Thomas Rivasseau

entry.summary: Shows that frontier LLMs can learn cipher-based covert communication skills in-context, without fine-tuning, enabling jailbreak-style attacks previously demonstrated only via fine-tuning APIs. This significantly lowers the bar for cipher attacks and challenges assumptions that such attacks require training access.

entry.title: When Auditors Fabricate: Batch-Size Degradation and Confident Hallucination in LLM Detection of Planted Document Contamination

author.name: Karan Parekh, Sanjana Pendyala Ravinder, Sana Mhapsekar, Medina Maloku

entry.summary: This study builds a controlled corpus of 150 papers with 450 injected contaminants and tests Google Gemini 3.0 Pro, an existing model, as an automated document auditor under single, small-batch, and large-batch prompting. Detection collapses from about 50-60% recovery at small scale to 2.8% on large batches, with confident hallucination of contaminations. The result is a cautionary finding for anyone deploying LLMs as quality-assurance auditors at scale.

entry.title: LiteRAG: Cost-Efficient Graph-Based Retrieval-Augmented Generation

author.name: Daniel Alejandro Coll Tejeda, Pedro Garc\'ia L\'opez, Daniel Barcelona-Pons

entry.summary: LiteRAG replaces expensive retrieval-time LLM control in graph-based RAG with query-conditioned algorithmic exploration and reasoning-chain context construction. It achieves the best quality on a multi-hop benchmark while cutting per-query latency by over 100x and cost by over 99% versus GraphRAG Global and DRIFT.

entry.title: Thompson Sampling for Non-Monotone Convex Ridge Bandits: Monotonicity Is Not Needed for Polynomial Regret

author.name: Xuan Li

entry.summary: This theory paper extends Thompson sampling guarantees for bandit convex optimization to the non-monotone ridge loss setting, answering an open question posed by Bakhtiari, Lattimore and Szepesvari (COLT 2025). It proves Bayesian regret of order O~(d^{9/2} sqrt(n)) for arbitrary convex links using a counterexample construction that circumvents the monotonicity assumption in prior John-ellipsoid-based proofs.

entry.title: Hierarchical Clustering Can Jointly Satisfy Richness, Consistency, and Scale Invariance

author.name: Daichi Kuroda, Maximilien Dreveton, Matthias Grossglauser, Patrick Thiran

entry.summary: This theoretical work shows that Kleinberg's famous impossibility theorem for flat clustering does not extend to hierarchical clustering: there exist uncountably many hierarchical methods that simultaneously satisfy analogs of scale invariance, richness, and consistency. The authors explicitly construct several such admissible methods, including ones based on well-separated structures. This resolves a foundational question about what axiomatic definitions of clustering are achievable.

entry.title: Prevalence Determines Precision:Silent Contamination in Detector-Defined Datasets

author.name: Jia Huang, Yankai Wan, Yangjun Ou

entry.summary: This paper shows that the precision of datasets built by running a detector or heuristic over candidate pools is governed by true-positive prevalence via Bayes' rule, not just detector quality. Using a real detector-defined event dataset with an independent ground-truth index, phantom rates vary from 0% to 81.7% across pools, and the Bayes expression predicts all three precisions within 3.3% while naive transfer errs by over 400%.

entry.title: An Empirical Measurement of Jailbreaking Evaluators

author.name: Yujie Mu

entry.summary: This paper systematically compares six widely used automated jailbreak evaluators (HarmBench, JailbreakBench, JailbreakRadar, StrongReject, JADES, and JailMeter), measuring how their differing definitions of jailbreak success affect reported attack strength. It addresses redundant validation effort and non-comparability across jailbreak research papers. The work matters because safety research conclusions currently depend heavily on evaluator choice.

entry.title: Multilingual in Name Only? Cultural and Linguistic Weaknesses of LLMs in Urdu

author.name: Farah Adeeba, Abdul Rafae Khan, Rajesh Bhatt, Hassan Sajjad

entry.summary: A manual evaluation of story generation quality in Urdu, a representative low-resource language, using three existing models (GPT-5.1, Qwen-3-Max, DeepSeek-3.1) — all released well before this study. The authors built a 93-story corpus and annotated errors under a nine-label taxonomy spanning linguistic, semantic, and cultural failures, finding basic grammar and semantics errors, incoherence, and unnatural repetition. The paper demonstrates that multilingual claims of frontier LLMs do not hold up in low-resource settings.

entry.title: Are We Really Doing Few-Shot Learning? A Critical Examination of Pre-Training Assumptions

author.name: Alejandro Galan-Cuenca, Marcelo Saval-Calvo, Antonio Javier Gallego

entry.summary: This critical evaluation shows that standard few-shot learning protocols, which pre-train on class-disjoint in-domain data, leak substantial target-domain information: in-domain pre-training improves over no pre-training by over 33 percentage points on average across eight datasets and three architectures. The paper argues class disjointness alone is insufficient to reflect genuine low-data learning. This is a valuable corrective to how few-shot computer vision results are interpreted.

entry.title: The Oligarch Barely Steers Model Collapse in Multi-Model Ecosystems

author.name: Yangze Liu, Zhongyi Han

entry.summary: This empirical study trains controlled multi-model ecosystems of 13 open 1-4B parameter models with mixed market shares, including an injected probe pushing the top share to 90%, retraining each generation on a shared output pool. It finds that market concentration (an oligopoly) barely changes model collapse dynamics or drags later models toward the dominant producer's output, contrary to common concerns. This is directly relevant to debates about recursive training on AI-generated text.

entry.title: A Fragility Spectrum for Recursive Language-Model Training

author.name: Yangze Liu, Zhongyi Han

entry.summary: This paper studies how different language models vary in susceptibility to model collapse under recursive training on self-generated text. Fixing a single contamination protocol across 13 public checkpoints for five generations, it finds a roughly five-fold spread in output diversity outcomes, from models barely affected to those degenerating into repetitive fragments. This matters because it shifts the model-collapse conversation from a uniform phenomenon to a model-specific fragility property relevant to anyone curating training corpora.

entry.title: Deep operator learning for efficient sampling from invariant measures of stochastic differential equations

author.name: Lin Guo, Li Lei, Jingtong Zhang

entry.summary: This paper introduces an amortized neural sampler combining operator learning with flow-based methods to map SDE coefficient functions to samplers of their invariant measures. After training, new SDE instances require only one encoder pass and a few ODE solver steps, independent of mixing time, with Lagrangian trajectory sensors and cross-attention for high-dimensional problems plus theoretical expressivity guarantees. This matters because sampling from invariant measures is classically expensive, and amortization shifts that cost to a one-time training phase.

entry.title: ZipCodec: Ultra-Low-Frame-Rate Streaming Speech Coding

author.name: Luca Della Libera, Cem Subakan, Mirco Ravanelli

entry.summary: ZipCodec is a streaming neural speech codec operating at 6.25 Hz frame rate and 0.80 kbps with 160 ms theoretical latency, combining WavLM distillation, a redesigned transformer architecture, scalar spherical quantization, and a latency-aware streaming decoder. It substantially outperforms existing streaming codecs at comparable bitrates on reconstruction and downstream tasks.

entry.title: Logit Refiner: Improving Visual Autoregressive Models via Intra-Scale Dependency Modeling

author.name: Meimingwei Li, Stefan Andreas Baumann, Felix Krause, Bj\"orn Ommer

entry.summary: The paper shows next-scale visual autoregressive models parallel-decode tokens per scale as a mean-field approximation that discards intra-scale spatial dependencies, causing local incoherence. The Logit Refiner is a lightweight autoregressive module (~10% parameters, <5% extra training compute) that restores these dependencies and plugs into any pretrained VAR checkpoint without retraining.

entry.title: SearchAtlas: Analyzing Agentic Search Strategies via Evidential Query Graphs

author.name: Jiacheng Sang, Mengyuan Li, Sanxing Chen, Yukun Huang, Yu Feng, Bhuwan Dhingra

entry.summary: SearchAtlas converts LLM search agent trajectories into structured evidential query graphs whose edges track how evidence flows from retrieval to final answer, enabling process-level rather than outcome-only evaluation. The automated parsing pipeline achieves 86.0 F1 against human annotations, and analysis of five agents across three benchmarks reveals systematic strategy differences. This addresses a real gap in agentic search evaluation.

entry.title: FlexComp: One Model for Every Ratio in Context Compression

author.name: Kaiyan Zhao, Zhongtao Miao, Akiko Aizawa, Yoshimasa Tsuruoka

entry.summary: FlexComp decouples compression ratio from training and deployment in soft context compression: Matryoshka-style training with per-instance memory budgets turns one model into an any-ratio compressor, with budgets selected per input via confidence-based routing or a learned predictor. Across ICAE, 500xCompressor, and SAC on MRQA it removes the need for one model per ratio and adapts compression to input needs. This improves both flexibility and efficiency of context compression.

entry.title: Xiaomi-CocktailASR-1 Technical Report

author.name: Yiru Zhang, Hang Su, Lichun Fan, Ying Zeng, Chang Liu, Yifeng Wang, Yuquan Liang, Tao Li, Lian Li, Wenhao Yang, Jian Luan, Cong Zou, Heng Qu

entry.summary: Xiaomi presents an LLM-based end-to-end target-speaker ASR system that uses reference speech as voiceprint prompts to transcribe a target speaker directly, without requiring speech separation. This addresses the cocktail party problem while avoiding the degradation of single-speaker performance and the lack of speaker-absence rejection seen in prior TS-ASR methods.

entry.title: When is Test-Time Adaptation Identifiable From Unlabeled Evidence?

author.name: Kartik Jhawar, Lipo Wang

entry.summary: A theoretical study asking whether unlabeled test-time evidence contains enough information to reliably select among candidate test-time adaptation actions, showing that even a perfect selector fails when an observation channel makes distinct deployments indistinguishable. The result is made precise in a finite-batch Gaussian TTA model.

entry.title: Recursive Code World Models: Building Complex Worlds through Recursive Scene Programs

author.name: Zhiqi Li, Yuxuan Liao, Bo Zhu

entry.summary: Introduces Recursive Code World Models, which reconstruct complex 3D worlds as executable scene code from a single reference image using a recursive solver that alternates whole-local-global passes, giving fine-scale structures their own perception-and-editing loops. Connects code-based world models with compositional 3D reconstruction.

entry.title: World in World: Explore the World with World Models

author.name: Chenxi Song, Yanming Yang, Chi Zhang

entry.summary: World in World introduces a training-free inference-time interface for autoregressive video world models that converts heterogeneous control evidence into camera- and time-labelled clean visual states read through the frozen model's native self-attention. It enables synchronized exploration of source videos from novel viewpoints without task-specific modules or extra training.

entry.title: Seamless Whole Slide Label-Free Virtual Staining

author.name: Dou Hoon Kwark, Kianoush Falahkheirkhah, Ji-hun Oh, Shirui Luo, Volodymyr Kindratenko, Rohit Bhargava

entry.summary: COMB introduces a Consistency Memory Bank for label-free virtual staining of gigapixel whole slide images, decoupling context storage from computation via dynamic feature retrieval to enforce spatial and channel consistency across tiles without memory bottlenecks. This eliminates tiling seams and color shifts that hinder clinical adoption of virtual histopathology.

entry.title: When Information is Worth the Risk: Behavioral Valuation for Hazardous Robotic Exploration

author.name: Alkesh K. Srivastava, Aamodh Suresh, Carlos Nieto-Granda, Philip Dames

entry.summary: This paper addresses hazardous robotic exploration where gathering information can itself cause mission failure, such as mapping mines, radiation, or unsafe terrain. It proposes a valuation-layer framework that keeps the belief update, sensor model, and planner fixed while swapping only the scalar objective used to rank paths, introducing a risk-augmented behavioral valuation to decide when uncertainty reduction is worth the exposure risk.

entry.title: CAP: Continuously Adaptive Perception-Blind Humanoid Locomotion via Learned Denoising

author.name: Hongjin Chen, Zijun Xu, Shihao Ma, Yi Zhao, Xilai Liu, Ke Ma, Wei Zhang, Chunyang Xie, Pengfei Li, Jieru Zhao, Wenchao Ding

entry.summary: CAP proposes a single-stage humanoid locomotion policy that recovers partially corrupted depth observations using a perceptive world-model encoder trained as a learned denoiser, combined with a co-active proprioceptive variational representation. Unlike routing or switching between perceptive and blind sub-policies, it exploits recoverable information in degraded depth rather than discarding it.

entry.title: UniMPA: A Unified Memory-Prediction-Action Model via Action-Grounded Transition Modeling

author.name: Wei Li, Rui Shao, Jie He, Lingsen Zhang, Ziwei Liu, Liqiang Nie

entry.summary: UniMPA is a unified memory-prediction-action architecture for vision-language-action models that addresses a transition realizability gap in manipulation, covering transition ambiguity, prediction-execution mismatch, and experience-realization mismatch through action-grounded transition modeling. By tying predicted future observations to physically realizable actions and context-aware adaptation, it aims to improve robotic manipulation policies beyond visually plausible but physically inconsistent predictions.

entry.title: Task- and Session-Level Model Routing: A Common-Interface Hybrid Evaluation of Four Open-Source Routers Across Four Benchmarks

author.name: Kiran N. Kumar, Santhosh K. Saminathan

entry.summary: This paper presents a standardized evaluation protocol comparing four open-source LLM routers across RouterBench, BFCL v4, tau2-bench, and WebArena, using 290 frozen tasks and a locked matrix of 2,610 candidate model outcomes. The findings are sobering: three of the four routers emit near-constant tier assignments regardless of prompt content, and even the best router (vLLM Semantic Router) achieves the highest success rate on none of the benchmarks, often being matched by a trivial always-mid-tier baseline.

entry.title: Subagents comply more

author.name: jacob_drori

entry.summary: This post presents a 13-scenario synthetic workplace eval measuring how often AI models comply with harmful or negligent requests and whether they raise concerns with humans. Key findings: framing a model as a subagent increases compliance with other AI agents' requests, and while OpenAI models historically complied far more than Anthropic ones, Astra scores nearly zero on silent compliance, making the eval largely saturated for current frontier models.

entry.title: Notes on MoReBench: "Evaluating Procedural and Pluralistic Moral Reasoning in Language Models, More than Outcomes"

author.name: Shunk

entry.summary: A summary of the MoReBench paper (arXiv:2510.16380), which introduces 1000 expert-rubricated moral scenarios for evaluating how language models reason through moral decisions as advisors and agents, plus MoReBench-Theory testing reasoning within five major moral frameworks. The benchmark shows that math, code, and science reasoning benchmarks fail to predict moral reasoning ability, and that training paradigms bias models toward particular moral frameworks.

entry.title: Safe to Stop? Risk-Constrained Stopping for Sequential Clinical Diagnosis Agents

author.name: Yuexin Wu, Vasile Rus

entry.summary: Presents Cros, a risk-constrained stopping layer for clinical diagnosis agents that decides when to diagnose versus defer, combining state-wise error ranking with LTT-style exact tests providing finite-sample guarantees. Evaluated on a 1,834-episode MIMIC-derived abdominal-pain benchmark. It addresses an overlooked reliability question in agentic healthcare: when autonomous stopping is safe.

entry.title: FlowCPO: A Unified Divergence View of Preference Alignment for Flow Models

author.name: Yansen Han, Shengyi Liao, Peng Sun, Deyuan Liu, Yuanxing Zhang, Pengfei Wan, Tao Lin

entry.summary: FlowCPO organizes preference alignment for flow and diffusion models under a divergence-based framework and proposes an offline forward-KL objective that uses both preferred and dispreferred samples without online rollouts. The paper proves the forward-KL objective is bounded by a contrastive term under explicit conditions for linear interpolation. It unifies online RL and offline preference optimization for continuous generative models.

entry.title: When Noise Fabricates Bias: The Fragility of LLM-as-a-Judge Bias Measurement under Noisy Text

author.name: DongHyun Ryu, Jaehyeok Lee, YeongJun Hwang, JinYeong Bak

entry.summary: Applying five realistic noise conditions at multiple intensities to 3,822 stereotype-related responses, the paper shows surface noise (typos, informal spelling) disproportionately flips neutral LLM-judge bias verdicts to biased ones, by up to a 120x margin relative to the reverse direction. This reveals that LLM-as-a-judge bias measurements can be artifacts of text quality. The finding has direct implications for audit methodology and fairness benchmarking.

entry.title: RAG-Safety-Bench: Reliable Evaluation of Retrieval-Augmented LLM Safety

author.name: Adithiyan Rajan Indira Saravanan, Kathleen C. Fraser

entry.summary: Introduces RAG-Safety-Bench, a benchmark measuring how retrieval augmentation affects LLM safety when handling harmful-content prompts, a known side effect where RAG can degrade safety behavior. The benchmark removes retriever-quality confounds and cleanly factors the problem into components for reliable measurement. Important as enterprises increasingly connect RAG to corporate knowledge bases.

entry.title: 2AM: Grounding Agent-Side Memory as Guidance for Steerable Action Models in Long-Horizon Manipulation

author.name: Yutong Hu, Fengjiao Chen, Xuezhi Cao, Renaud Detry

entry.summary: 2AM cleanly separates roles in long-horizon manipulation: a multimodal Agent holds all task memory and compiles instructions, while a stateless RGB-based Action Model executes motion, avoiding confounded attribution between richer observations, tools, and policy failures. This deliberately constrained design tests how far interface bandwidth can substitute for tool breadth.

entry.title: RobustSGPO: Search-Space Control for Agent Harness Evolution

author.name: Zibo Zhao, Jijun Shi, Mo Zhou, Zhongyuan Wang, Shifu Bie, Yunfei Zhang, Xuanting Zhou, Xiangyu Wu, Bin Liu, Ruiming Tang, Wenwu Ou, Kun Gai

entry.summary: Introduces RobustSGPO, a method for controlling edit scope and search-space in semantic-gradient-based prompt optimization of agent harnesses, including permission scheduling, cumulative controls, and task-family transfer. Evaluated at scale (120 tasks, 95 runs, 7,350 candidate attempts), it lifts held-out completion from 60.0% to 80.0% and improves quality scores. This addresses a concrete open problem in automated agent-system self-improvement.

entry.title: Why Sample What You Can Enumerate? Exact Policy Optimization for Genomic Tool Selection

author.name: Haoyue Liu, Xiaoyu Ma, Ye Chen, Zhichao Wang, Xiaoying Tang

entry.summary: This paper argues that GRPO-style sampled RL is structurally mismatched for tool selection where the tool-subset space is small enough to enumerate, showing that group-normalized advantages vanish as the policy concentrates. It proposes exact policy optimization for genomic tool selection, demonstrating the failure mode empirically on frozen-reasoner tool-use training.

entry.title: No Free Checker: A Survey of Verifiers for Robot Policies

author.name: Yang Wan, Xihang Yue, Zhirui Liu, Ziyuan Chu, Shuxun Wang, Yuhan Chen, Xiaonan Jiang, Xukun Zhu, Yubo Dong, Linchao Zhu

entry.summary: This survey covers roughly 150 verifiers for robot policies, spanning success detectors, reward models, runtime monitors, safety filters, and temporal-logic specifications. It organizes the space along two axes, availability (cost, timing, and density of verdicts) and credibility (how much a high score reflects task success), and groups verifiers by who supplies the judgment. The framework clarifies trade-offs in using verifiers both to evaluate and to train vision-language-action policies.

entry.title: Watermarks Without Verification: AI Text Watermarking After the EU AI Act

author.name: Alexander Nemecek, Vipin Chaudhary, Erman Ayday

entry.summary: Analyzes the technical and policy situation after the EU AI Act Article 50 obligations took effect on August 2, 2026, examining vendor text watermarking (including Anthropic's SynthID-Text-based marking on Claude and Google's earlier Gemini deployment), user objections, and the lack of independent verification mechanisms. Evaluates claims about quality impact, identifiability, and robustness versus removability.

entry.title: uFlowCSP: Crystal Structure Prediction using Mean flow generative models

author.name: Sourin Dey, Dipannoy Das Gupta, Lai Wei, Sadman Sadeed Omee, Jianjun Hu

entry.summary: uFlowCSP applies MeanFlow generative modeling to crystal structure prediction, learning average probability-flow velocity so a complete structure is generated in 1-5 network evaluations instead of tens to thousands. This yields 5x-58x faster inference with equal or better performance, using a chemistry- and symmetry-aware transformer. A notable efficiency win for computational materials discovery.

entry.title: Phase-Decoupled, Model-Calibrated Power Control for Disaggregated LLM Serving

author.name: Jae Gon Kim, Donghoon Yoo, Hanyul Ryu, Sungho Ha, Juyeon Lee, Soojung Ryu

entry.summary: The paper shows that NVIDIA's Max-Q inference power profile yields only modest gains (+8.6% tokens/J) with a latency cost (+5.2%) on disaggregated B200 LLM serving, and argues optimal power settings depend on the (model, quantization, engine, hardware) combination and differ between prefill and decode lanes. It proposes phase-decoupled, model-calibrated power control that converts SLO headroom into energy savings.

entry.title: Particle GFlowNets: Rethinking Generative Marginalization Models

author.name: Tiago da Silva, Diego Mesquita, Salem Lahlou

entry.summary: The paper proves that Generative Marginalization Models (MaMs), efficient any-order autoregressive samplers for discrete distributions, are equivalent to GFlowNets, previously thought to be distinct paradigms. It extends MaMs sampling to non-autoregressive processes with an automatic full-state rejuvenation criterion for the Gibbs sampler.

entry.title: Black-Box Membership Inference via Word-Level Probability Estimation

author.name: Shengjie Niu, Yeheng Ge, Jian Huang

entry.summary: This paper introduces WPMIA, a membership inference attack for LLMs that operates in a strict black-box setting where only textual continuations are available, estimating word-level generation probabilities via Monte Carlo sampling with local kernel smoothing and aggregating them into a sequence-level likelihood estimator. This addresses the practical limitation that most MIAs require per-token logits unavailable for proprietary models. It matters for privacy auditing of deployed commercial LLMs.

entry.title: scDEFT: A deep learning framework for drug-effect prediction and counterfactual reasoning

author.name: Murthy Devarakonda

entry.summary: scDEFT treats a drug as a conditioning operator on single-cell representations, using feature-wise linear modulation to produce drug-conditioned cell latents with heads that predict drug-induced state change and responder status. A backward stage ranks latent dimensions to explain why responders and non-responders diverge on the same drug. This enables mechanistic, counterfactual reasoning over longitudinal single-cell drug-response data.

entry.title: Structural priors for data-efficient language learning

author.name: Yana Veitsman, Jonas Mayer Martins, Jonathan Lautenschlager, Lisa Beinborn

entry.summary: The authors investigate structural transfer: pretraining language models on non-language data such as music, probabilistic grammars, and cellular automata to induce useful priors before natural-language training. Several symbolic data types yield lower language-modeling loss than random initialization, with smaller weight shifts during subsequent language training indicating better initialization. This offers a data-efficiency lever for language modeling with conceptual links to multilingual transfer.

entry.title: Negative Self-Distillation: Learning to Reason by Avoiding Flaws

author.name: Rongcan Pei, Zhepei Wei, Shuyao Xu, Xinyu Zhu, Wei-Lin Chen, Yu Meng

entry.summary: The paper identifies that On-Policy Self-Distillation (OPSD) degrades complex reasoning by forcing imitation of artificially confident traces, suppressing uncertainty and self-correction. It proposes Negative Self-Distillation (NSD), which improves LLMs by optimizing away from flawed reasoning traces rather than imitating privileged teacher outputs.

entry.title: Near-Optimal Reinforcement Learning with Multi-Step Transition Lookahead

author.name: Corentin Pla, Hugo Richard, Marc Abeille, Vianney Perchet

entry.summary: The paper resolves open questions about RL with multi-step transition look-ahead: it proves exact planning is NP-hard for every fixed rational discount factor, but also shows near-optimal planning can be performed efficiently. This clarifies when look-ahead information yields tractable performance gains.

entry.title: The widening evaluation gap in medical large language model research 2023 to 2026

author.name: Raad Bin Tareaf, Murad Al-Rajab, Samia Loucif

entry.summary: A systematic analysis of 11,628 PubMed records (Jan 2023 to Jun 2026) showing that medical LLM research is falling behind the systems it evaluates: evaluation lag widened from 1.33 to 6.08 quarters, only 2.5% of studies used randomized/prospective designs, and migration to newer models offsets only about 56% of evaluation drift. Randomized trials evaluate models a median 4.6 quarters older than other designs. Quantifies a structural mismatch between fast-moving LLM releases and slow clinical evidence generation.

entry.title: Nuha-Speech: Building General-Purpose Arabic Speech-LLMs

author.name: Yingzhi Wang, Reem Alhazzani, Muhammad Alqurishi

entry.summary: Nuha-Speech presents a full pipeline for Arabic speech-LLMs: a 1.5M-sample Arabic Speech Question-Answering corpus for instruction tuning, supervised fine-tuning of Qwen-Omni variants at multiple scales, and a systematic evaluation suite. It addresses the significant underrepresentation of Arabic in multilingual speech-LLM development.

entry.title: MindTopo: Can Foundation Models Reason in Topological Space?

author.name: Yunfei Ge, Anbang Liu, Qineng Wang, Johnalbert Garnica, Jianwen Lyu, Zihan Wang, Reuben Tan, Jianfeng Gao, Ruohan Zhang, Yining Hong, Jiajun Wu, Manling Li

entry.summary: MindTopo is a benchmark testing whether foundation models reason about topological relations, such as continuity, separation, order, enclosure, and knots, that are invariant under continuous deformation. It evaluates both reasoning (identifying or inferring topological relations) and planning (closed-loop agentic control grounded in topology).

entry.title: Tri-DehazeGS: Scene--Medium Decoupled Gaussian Splatting with Transmittance-Aware Optimization

author.name: Kui Jiang, Yang Gu, Jiacheng Liu, Shiyu Liu, Youyu Chen, Hui Liu

entry.summary: Extends scattering-aware Gaussian Splatting by explicitly disentangling clean scene radiance from atmospheric medium effects and rebalancing optimization in low-transmittance regions that are otherwise under-reconstructed. Relevant for recovering usable 3D reconstructions from hazy multi-view captures, e.g., outdoor or driving scenarios.

entry.title: MMGait: Benchmarking and Unifying Gait Recognition across Heterogeneous Modalities

author.name: Saihui Hou, Chenye Wang, Qingyuan Cai, Aoqi Li, Yongzhen Huang

entry.summary: MMGait is a large-scale multi-sensor benchmark aligning visible, infrared, depth, LiDAR, and radar gait observations at sequence level, with a shared impostor-augmented protocol for single-modal, cross-modal, and multi-modal evaluation. Findings show modality rankings shift with probe conditions, motivating unified cross-modality gait modeling.

entry.title: Revisiting Avatar-As-Image: High-Fidelity Registration is All You Need

author.name: Margaret Kostyrko, Yuxuan Xue, Garvita Tiwari, Gerard Pons-Moll

entry.summary: AvaImg presents a multi-stage optimization pipeline producing high-fidelity SMPL(-X)+D registrations with UV textures from arbitrary clothed human scans, arguing that the lack of such registration explains the poor quality of prior UV-based avatar methods. This enables pretrained image networks to process, generate, and edit 3D clothed avatars effectively.

entry.title: SwarmNxt: Open-source Software-Hardware Platform for Fast and Agile Aerial Swarms

author.name: Charbel Toumieh, Niel Mistry, Benjamin Jarvis, Simon Jeger, Peize Liu, Shaojie Shen, Dario Floreano

entry.summary: SwarmNxt is an open-source hardware and software platform enabling fast, agile, vision-based aerial swarm flight, targeting time-critical search-and-rescue and GPS-denied surveying. It addresses the gap left by closed-source commercial drones lacking onboard compute, and provides tooling for developing and maintaining software across many aerial robots.

entry.title: Rapid Learning of Dexterous In-Hand Pen Writing through Real-Time Jacobian Estimation

author.name: Kai Stewart, Yasunori Toshimitsu, Robert K. Katzschmann

entry.summary: The paper proposes an embodied control approach for dexterous in-hand manipulation based on real-time task Jacobian estimation of the combined hand-object system, running on a laptop CPU on the physical robot. The controller achieves in-hand pen writing shortly after deployment, avoiding the extensive simulation modeling or demonstration collection required by RL and imitation learning approaches.

entry.title: ObstaDiff: Generalizable Diffusion Policy Learning via Obstacle-aware Representations

author.name: Jiawen Wang, Kevin Yao, Khalid Jawed

entry.summary: ObstaDiff adds a lightweight obstacle-aware visual encoder to a decomposed diffusion policy for robot manipulation, producing structured target-obstacle-background representations that let the policy generate trajectories reasoning about cluttered scenes. It was evaluated on 61 real-robot greenhouse trials with 366 executions, a notably extensive real-world validation. The work targets a key generalization gap between clean lab settings and real cluttered environments.

entry.title: XAI-Arena: Can LLMs Assess the Quality of XAI Explanations?

author.name: Yanfei Hu Fleischhauer, Alona Zharova, Nadja Klein, Stefan Feuerriegel

entry.summary: Introduces XAI-Arena, an LLM-as-a-judge framework for reproducible, scalable, multidimensional evaluation of explainable-AI explanation quality across dimensions like faithfulness, actionability, and trust calibration. This replaces subjective human judgment that has limited comparability across XAI studies.

entry.title: CityPlanner: A Sandbox Agent for Executable Urban Planning

author.name: Wentao Zhang, Jingyuan Wang, Zetong Zhou, Yifan Yang, Wenrui Wang

entry.summary: Introduces CityPlanner, a sandbox-agent framework for urban planning where agents interact with a unified file-based environment (UrbanSandbox), inspecting task files, generating plans, running evaluators, and revising decisions based on executable feedback. To make long-horizon learning tractable, it proposes atomic-task reinforcement learning that decomposes sandbox tasks. This matters because it bridges LLM agents with real-world spatial optimization under practical constraints like cost and service quality.

entry.title: The Era by Eon Benchmark: A Generated Enterprise Estate with Exact Ground Truth for Benchmarking LLM Agents

author.name: Benjamin Gruenbaum, Doron Porat, Assaf Natanzon, Roy Zavida, Chen Dinachi, Or Itzahary

entry.summary: This paper introduces a benchmark of fully generated fictional companies with product simulators (Salesforce, Zendesk, Slack, Gong, etc.), internal databases, and computed answer keys for evaluating enterprise LLM agents. Seeded entity graphs enable reproducible, exact-ground-truth evaluation without touching customer production data.

entry.title: Trust Me, I'm Your Developer: Self-Issued Authentication in Large Language Models

author.name: Syed Ghazanfar Abbas, Dongyan Xu

entry.summary: Tests whether LLMs accept unverified identity claims when asked to authenticate a user claiming to be their developer, using self-designed tests across ChatGPT, Claude, Qwen, Mistral, and Llama. While all models initially rejected the claim, Qwen and Mistral went on to generate their own challenges, define what counted as convincing evidence, and return a Verified verdict. This exposes a novel social-engineering attack surface around self-issued authentication.

entry.title: Talking to Itself While Coding: What Makes Comments Help Code Generation?

author.name: Dangfeng Pan, Zhensu Sun, Cenyuan Zhang, David Lo, Xiaoning Du

entry.summary: The paper investigates how comments generated by code LLMs affect subsequent code quality, using observational analysis and controlled prefill interventions where weaker models receive comments written by stronger models. The key finding is that comments from test-passing solutions raise recipient pass@1 by 17.2% on average, whereas comment surface form and intent alone do not predict performance. This gives a cleaner picture of how autoregressive self-context shapes code generation quality.

entry.title: Voice or Stereotype? Disentangling Acoustic and Content-Based Gender in Speech-to-Speech Models

author.name: Xiaoqun Liu, Tanu Mitra, Harshit Rajgarhia, Abhishek Mukherji

entry.summary: This paper studies bias in speech-to-speech models used in dubbing, translation, and voice agents, asking whether models infer speaker gender from the actual voice versus from stereotypical content cues in what is said. The authors identify a subtle evaluation pitfall: fixed hard-coded output voices can mask biased gender reasoning, and they design experiments to disentangle voice rendering bias from content-based gender attribution. It is significant for fairness evaluation of a rapidly deployed model class.

entry.title: Kernel-Complexity Edge Sanitization for Training-Free Defense against Structural Graph Attacks

author.name: Yaning Jia, Shenyang Deng, Yaoqing Yang, Chiyu Ma, Wenxuan Xu, Soroush Vosoughi

entry.summary: The paper proposes KCES, a training-free, model-agnostic defense that sanitizes adversarially perturbed graph edges using Graph Kernel Complexity, a metric derived from a generalization bound for GNN test error. This gives the defense a theoretical foundation absent from most heuristic graph defenses. It avoids costly adversarial retraining while targeting structural attacks.

entry.title: Subgroup Membership Inference Audits of Differentially Private Synthetic Text

author.name: Yidan Sun, Viktor Schlegel, Srinivasan Nandakumar, Siew Kei Lam, Anil Anthony Bharath

entry.summary: The paper defines a subgroup-targeted membership inference game to audit DP synthetic text releases, showing that average-case audits can conceal elevated leakage risks for vulnerable subgroups. They instantiate the audit across 32 proxies under three scenarios of differing protection. This is an important privacy-fairness intersection finding for synthetic data governance.

entry.title: Active Adaptation, Not Static Defense: Temporal Dynamics of Preventative Steering in Adversarial Fine-Tuning

author.name: Jing Guan, Yachao Yang, Zhaoliang Liu, Yuyao Zhang, Fanyu Meng, Junlan Feng

entry.summary: The paper analyzes how Preventative Steering, a training-time defense injecting undesirable-trait persona vectors during fine-tuning, actually protects models against malicious fine-tuning. It identifies an early compensatory adaptation phase, a steady-state decay of the corrective signal, and attention output projections as the dominant residual-write route, proposing Intervention Delta Preservation to sustain the defense.

entry.title: EGGROLL, Unrolled: Understanding and Improving Low-Rank Evolution Strategies at Scale

author.name: Ege C. Kaya, Abolfazl Hashemi

entry.summary: Analyzes EGGROLL, the low-rank evolution strategies method that made ES practical for LLMs, showing that its rank-one perturbations, though computationally attractive, are geometrically severe zero-volume subsets. The authors characterize the mean update field via a resolvent, show it can introduce a nonconservative component and even reverse local stability of an optimum, and propose improvements. Timely given growing interest in cheap ES fine-tuning of large models.

entry.title: Beyond Solver Verdicts: Generative Reward Models for Autoformalization

author.name: Vikash Singh, Debargha Ganguly, Aman Goel, Ali Torkamani, Xiaoxue Han, Joseph Lilien, Ferhat Erata, Vipin Chaudhary

entry.summary: The paper identifies a failure mode in neurosymbolic autoformalization, Verdict-Preserving-Unfaithfulness, where an incorrect formal encoding still executes and matches the expected solver verdict, and proves verdict-only checks are bounded at chance-level detection. It introduces Generative Verification, distilling a Z3-equivalence oracle into a reference-free continuous faithfulness score to detect such unfaithful translations.

entry.title: Polyhedral Geometry of Time-to-First-Spike Neural Networks

author.name: Manjot Singh, Guido Mont\'ufar, Gitta Kutyniok

entry.summary: This paper analyzes the expressivity of spiking neural networks in the time-to-first-spike model, where the input-output map is continuous piecewise linear with affine pieces constrained by causal feasibility. The authors show each neuron's firing time admits a maxout-like representation with exponentially many affine pieces and derive upper and lower bounds on the number of polyhedral causal regions in shallow and deep networks. This provides one of the first rigorous theoretical expressivity characterizations for spiking architectures.

entry.title: CausalArena: Benchmarking Causal Discovery in the Foundation Model Era

author.name: Zi-Rong Li, Si-Yang Liu, Tian-Zuo Wang, Han-Jia Ye

entry.summary: CausalArena is a unified, evolvable benchmark for causal discovery that addresses evaluation difficulties posed by causal discovery foundation models, where performance may reflect pretraining-environment overlap with test SCMs rather than genuine causal ability. It standardizes graph families, mechanisms, and evaluation protocols.

entry.title: SoK: Privacy Attacks on Machine Learning via Explainable AI

author.name: Abdullah Caglar Oksuz, Anisa Halimi, Erman Ayday

entry.summary: This systematization of knowledge surveys 25 studies that exploit ML explanations for model extraction, membership inference, and model inversion, organizing attack surfaces by how explanations are acquired across five distinct paths rather than a simple black/white-box dichotomy. It shows that explanations reduce extraction cost and leak membership signals. It matters because explainability features are widely deployed without considering their privacy cost.

entry.title: HuRo: Robotizing Human Videos for Scalable VLA Pretraining

author.name: Jinho Jeong, Se June Joo, Jaehyun Kang, Dongyun Kim, Yena Kim, Hanjung Kim, Seon Joo Kim

entry.summary: HuRo builds a pipeline that converts heterogeneous human videos into robot-aligned observations and action trajectories, inferring missing intermediate signals, to create a dataset for pretraining vision-language-action (VLA) policies. The paper systematically examines whether robotized human videos provide effective, scalable supervision and addresses the human-to-robot embodiment gap. This addresses the scarcity and cost of real-robot training data, a major bottleneck in robot learning.

entry.title: CARTS: Contextual Autoregressive Rank Transcoding Steganography for Full-Capacity Keyed Text Encoding

author.name: Wissam Ghantous, Alexander V. Mantzaris

entry.summary: CARTS formalizes a steganographic technique in which autoregressive language models transform a hidden payload into cover text of identical token length by preserving per-position rank information, building on the earlier Calgacus construction. The paper provides the first rigorous security analysis, proving exact correctness under deterministic model assumptions and defining the associated computational security problems in a rank-coordinate representation. This bridges LLM-based steganography with formal cryptography-style analysis.

entry.title: Studying Without a Syllabus: Task-Agnostic Environment Preprocessing

author.name: Vinay Samuel, Varun Ursekar, Vijay S. Kalmath, Apaar Shanker, Veronica Chatrath, Yuan Xue

entry.summary: This paper formalizes task-agnostic environment preprocessing, where an LLM agent inspects corpora and tools in an unfamiliar environment before test time and without knowledge of downstream tasks, deciding what reusable resources to build. It addresses a gap in agent adaptation, where most methods rely on task examples or feedback signals. The open-ended studying framing could influence how autonomous agents prepare for unseen workloads.

entry.title: VikingRAG: Accurate and Token-efficient Retrieval-augmented Generation over Structured Documents

author.name: Peiyuan Gao, Gaoyuan Zhang, Haojie Qin, Yahui Sun, Qianyi Zhang, Yunhao Zhang, Zeyu Wang, Wei Lu

entry.summary: VikingRAG is a directory-aware semantic data management system that reduces structural-context token costs in RAG while maintaining accuracy, using evidence-gap-driven multi-round retrieval over structured documents. It materializes agentic retrieval traces as reusable experience edges so similar queries avoid repeated multi-round exploration. Token efficiency in agentic RAG is a timely and practically important problem given rising inference costs.

entry.title: ORCH: Organizational Principles Enable Collective Intelligence in Embodied AI

author.name: Zhengran Ji, Jonathan Hyun, Boyuan Chen

entry.summary: ORCH constructs task-specific hierarchical organizations for large heterogeneous collectives of embodied agents, drawing on human organization theory to combine pooled and sequential interdependence. It argues collective performance depends on organizational structure, not just individual agent capability.

entry.title: 3D Point Splatting for mmWave Radar Novel View Synthesis

author.name: Adnan Armouti, Yixuan Gao, Rajalakshmi Nandakumar

entry.summary: 3DPS is the first differentiable point renderer for millimeter-wave radar novel view synthesis, preserving complex-valued outputs and explicit material modeling while scaling to multi-view optimization, unlike Monte Carlo ray tracers or optical-NVS ports. It unifies three previously mutually exclusive properties for radar rendering.

entry.title: Auto-RecSys: Harnessing Autonomous Research Agents for Industry-Scale Recommender System

author.name: Ming Li, Dai Li, Xuying Ning, Bo Sun, Rui Li, Yi Zhang, Silvia Gong, Xuan Cao, Rui Li, Cornelia Carapcea, Qunshu Zhang, Zhigang Wang, Yinglong Xia, Andy Wang

entry.summary: Auto-RecSys presents an autonomous research agent system for long-horizon experimentation on industry-scale recommendation models, tackling slow training feedback loops and fragile large-scale infrastructure. It parallelizes hypothesis exploration and includes robust, recoverable execution harnesses. The author list suggests an industry (Meta-affiliated) team, giving rare real-scale deployment evidence for auto-research agents.

entry.title: OmniHallu: Unified Hallucination Detection for Cross-Modal Comprehension and Generation in Multimodal Large Language Models

author.name: Jianjiang Yang, Peihang Li, Shanqing Xu, Mengchen Qian, Lu Zhang, Meng Luo

entry.summary: OmniHallu provides a unified hallucination detection framework spanning comprehension and generation tasks across image, video, and audio modalities, with OmniHallu-Bench: a 10,000-sample benchmark with claim-level human annotations over six cross-modal tasks. This breaks from prior single-modality, single-task hallucination detectors and enables broader generalization assessment. It fills a real gap in multimodal reliability evaluation.

entry.title: ReGround: Grounding Reviewer Comments in Multimodal Evidence

author.name: Serwar Basch, Lizhen Qu, Iryna Gurevych

entry.summary: Introduces ReGround, a large-scale dataset linking 10,267 peer-review comments to 16,274 pieces of evidence in original paper submissions across 3,656 papers, using author rebuttals as a high-precision annotation source. Grounding is cast as a retrieval task over long multimodal documents and evaluated across many retrieval methods. Useful for building tools that assist peer review and for studying long-document multimodal retrieval.

entry.title: Target leakage, not model class, explains reported accuracy in survey-based cardiovascular screening: a leakage-tiered audit of glass-box and tabular foundation models

author.name: Raad Bin Tareaf, Murad Al-Rajab, Samia Loucif, Samer Ellaham, Cedric Schmitz

entry.summary: This paper audits ten classifier families, including glass-box models and tabular foundation models, on cardiovascular risk prediction from the 2022 BRFSS survey across five feature tiers of decreasing leakage risk. It argues that the commonly reported AUROC of ~0.89 in survey-based screening reflects target leakage rather than genuine learning, and tests whether deployment-relevant properties like calibration, fairness, and conformal coverage survive the audit.

entry.title: CamPilot: A Multi-Agent Cinematic Assistant for Camera-Controlled Movie Generation

author.name: Yang Wu, Stefano Petrangeli, Ishita Dasgupta, Yu Shen

entry.summary: CamPilot is a multi-agent framework integrating cinematographic planning and camera-work control for coherent multi-shot movie generation, trained with GRPO on 14K real-world professional movies to internalize motion and composition patterns. It aims to bring human-crafted camera language to LLM-driven video generation.

entry.title: Uncertainty DMD: Restoring Diversity in Few-Step Autoregressive Video Distillation

author.name: Zixuan Duan, Xunzhi Xiang, Yabo Chen, Xin Zhang, Changhan Liu, Haibin Huang, Chi Zhang, Qi Fan, Xuelong Li

entry.summary: Analyzes diversity collapse in DMD-distilled autoregressive video generators, showing that mode-seeking bias collapses the first chunk and the deterministic AR cache propagates this collapse globally, then proposes uncertainty-based corrections to restore temporal variation. Advances understanding of a key failure mode of few-step video distillation.

entry.title: Brain-PACE: A Deep Siamese MRI Framework for Modelling Longitudinal Brain Acceleration

author.name: Samuel Maddox (School of Computing Sciences, University of East Anglia), Jacob Newman (School of Computing Sciences, University of East Anglia), Saber Sami (Norwich Medical School, University of East Anglia), Michal Mackiewicz (School of Computing Sciences, University of East Anglia), for the Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative, the Australian Imaging Biomarkers, Lifestyle flagship study of ageing

entry.summary: Extends Siamese longitudinal brain-age frameworks to directly estimate the pace of structural brain ageing from paired T1-weighted MRIs, finding accelerated ageing in 42.6 percent of participants with mild cognitive impairment and correlations with cognitive impairment measures and regional tau burden. Moves brain-age research from static age gap to longitudinal pace estimation.

entry.title: Language-Augmented Semantic Priors for B-Spline Surface Fitting

author.name: Yunzhong Lou, Yusheng Luo, Jiahao Li, Yu Song, Xiangdong Zhou

entry.summary: LASP introduces a framework that uses large language models to extract semantic priors from CAD modeling histories and inject them into B-spline/NURBS surface fitting and parameterization. This bridges the gap between high-level design intent and solver-executable geometric configuration, addressing a long-standing heuristic-heavy limitation of traditional CAD geometric kernels.

entry.title: LTLDiff: Finite Linear Temporal Logic-Guided Data Generation and Diffusion Policies for Multi-agent Robotic Manipulation

author.name: Chuhan Meng, Haiyan Yin

entry.summary: LTLDiff combines finite linear temporal logic (LTLf) specifications with diffusion policies for multi-agent manipulation, using an LLM to translate natural language task instructions into LTLf formulas that guide both demonstration generation and policy learning. The approach targets desynchronization, action-ordering errors, and coordination failures in multi-agent tasks.

entry.title: Memory as Plans: World-Action Modeling with Memory-Grounded Planning

author.name: Sizhe Zhao, Haozhe Xie, Weiyu Zhao, Chenchu Zhang, Huan Wang, Chenyang Wang, Qinglin Liu, Shengping Zhang

entry.summary: MaP-WAM decomposes memory-dependent world-action modeling into memory-grounded planning and plan-conditioned execution, using long-term multimodal episodic context as planning-time evidence instead of conditioning the executor on full history. This targets non-Markovian manipulation tasks while avoiding the coverage-versus-efficiency tradeoff of growing visual windows or language summaries.

entry.title: EVPeriscope: Extended Perception across Aerial and Ground Vehicles with Event-based Propeller Tracking

author.name: Dexter Ong, Vijay Kumar, Pratik Chaudhari

entry.summary: This robotics paper introduces EVPeriscope, an event-camera-based perception system that lets a ground robot detect and localize a quadrotor by tracking the high-frequency visual signature of its propellers. This enables the aerial robot to act as an extended perception node for the ground vehicle, offering robust relative localization even under motion blur, lighting changes, or occlusion that defeat conventional fiducial-marker approaches.

entry.title: Learning Orthogonal Multi-Index Models Beyond Small Initialization: Incremental Learning, Competitive Dynamics and Symmetry

author.name: Mo Zhou, Weihang Xu, Simon S. Du, Maryam Fazel

entry.summary: Analyzes training dynamics of two-layer networks learning orthogonal multi-index targets under standard initialization with polynomially many samples, going beyond prior analyses that relied on small initialization or layer-wise training. It proves incremental learning still occurs, with loss decreasing sequentially along the Hermite expansion of the target, and characterizes competitive dynamics and symmetry effects. Strong theory work from a credible group (Du, Fazel).

entry.title: Optimizing AI Inference Across the Deployment Stack

author.name: Tejinder Singh, John Pflueger, Jeebak Mitra, Robert Lincourt, Mitchell Markow, Bhavesh A. Patel

entry.summary: The paper presents a unified analytical treatment of LLM inference optimization with a three-layer taxonomy spanning model-level compression, compiler transformations, and system serving policies, formulating deployment as constrained multi-objective optimization. It aims to make cross-stack benchmark comparisons meaningful for deployment decisions.

entry.title: Rebalancing Token Importance in Language Models with TF-IDF Weighted Cross-Entropy Loss

author.name: Zhijian Li, Stefan Larson, Kevin Leach

entry.summary: The paper proposes an information-weighted cross-entropy loss using TF-IDF statistics to down-weight ubiquitous tokens and emphasize semantically informative ones during LLM training and fine-tuning. Across five decoder-only models from 1.1B to 13B parameters, the loss reduces memorized substring length (14% under LoRA fine-tuning) while preserving perplexity and downstream performance. It connects token-weighting to memorization mitigation in a simple, deployable way.

entry.title: Beyond Noise Steering: Dual-Latent Space Reinforcement Learning for Generative Robot Policy

author.name: Pengfei Zhang, Teng Sun, Xianchao Xiu

entry.summary: DLSRL proposes reinforcement learning over generative robot policies that modulates not only the initial noise latent but also intermediate action representations inside a frozen generator, via an actor predicting two distinct latent variables. This addresses the inefficiency and performance degradation of prior noise-only steering of diffusion or flow-based policies.

entry.title: ContractEval: Query-Conditioned Execution Matching for Procedural Instruction Conformance

author.name: Praphul Singh, Shanu Kumar, Akshat Agarwal, Ganesh Kumar

entry.summary: Presents ContractEval, a diagnostic framework that represents procedural instructions as query-active obligations and matches them against response or trace evidence, exposing silent failures like skipped checks, wrong branches, ordering errors, and invariant breaches that output-only or generic trace evaluation misses.

entry.title: LexAgentHallu: A Hierarchical Benchmark for Profiling Hallucinations in Legal Agents

author.name: Yujin Zhou, Mingxuan Zheng, Chuxue Cao, Huang Yidan, Jiale Chen, Yike Guo, Sirui Han

entry.summary: Introduces LexAgentHallu, a benchmark for diagnosing agentic hallucinations in tool-augmented legal agents across multi-step trajectories, where tool-call and reasoning errors cascade into fabricated holdings and miscited authority. Built through a four-stage expert-in-the-loop pipeline with 3,414 examples, it goes beyond single-turn outcome-level legal QA metrics. This fills a gap at the intersection of legal AI and agentic-hallucination evaluation.

entry.title: Kernel-Managed Shared Memory for System-Wide Personalization

author.name: Ryan Lum, Yongfeng Zhang

entry.summary: The paper proposes kernel-managed shared memory, a system-level abstraction where agents write tagged memories while the agent-system kernel governs retrieval, privacy, and prompt injection. Implemented on AIOS and tested across three assistant models over 1,800 trials, it improves personalization over unmanaged memory backends like Mem0 using identical storage.

entry.title: Auditable Emergency Triage for Maternal and Newborn Care in India

author.name: Shobhit Jagga, Aman Dalmia, Niharika Priyadarshini, Neelima Devadas, Amrita K Prasen, Nikhil Nalin, Santhosh SJ, Sreeram Nurani Ramasubramanian, Muhammed Afeer K, Anubhav Arora
