entry.summary: Noora Health describes an LLM-based emergency triage system for a WhatsApp service answering over 50,000 caregiver medical queries per month, classifying which messages need immediate in-person care with interpretability rationales. The paper addresses operational challenges of opacity and regression testing at scale, aligning the LLM system with clinician decision trees for auditability. It is a concrete, high-impact deployment of AI safety practices in a low-resource healthcare setting.

entry.title: Direct Diversity Optimization for Diverse Successful Trajectories in Preference Post-Training

author.name: Junwon Ko, Dong-Jae Lee, Minchan Kwon, Sunghyun Baek, Junmo Kim

entry.summary: DDO is an offline post-training method that improves successful strategy coverage of LLM agents by combining Divergence-Tree Collection, which builds state-aligned branch sets from shared decision states, with a Reference-Relative Target-Odds Objective. It achieves stronger task success and diversity than alternatives under a fixed rollout budget. Addresses a real weakness of scalar outcome-label post-training.

entry.title: Semigroup-JEPA: Latent Dynamics Consistency for Zero-Shot Physics Generalization

author.name: Andy Zeyi Liu, Haoran Sun, Lucas Baker, Randall Balestriero, John Sous

entry.summary: SG-JEPA extends JEPA world models with action-conditioned physics parameters and joint autoregressive latent rollout training, testing whether such models learn physically consistent dynamics. Evaluation uses out-of-distribution gravitational-field tasks that obey the same physical law but differ qualitatively in dynamics, probing zero-shot physics generalization.

entry.title: A Bellman Optimality Equation for Plasticity

author.name: Jeremy Lucas, Doina Precup

entry.summary: Builds on the Abel et al. (2025) information-theoretic definition of plasticity in continual reinforcement learning, presenting preliminary work toward optimizing plasticity in Markov settings via a Bellman-style optimality equation. This complements the extensive empowerment-optimization literature by targeting the rarely addressed plasticity side of the empowerment-plasticity tradeoff. Early-stage but theoretically notable from a strong research group (Precup).

entry.title: Topological Necessities: Mechanism-Invariant Strategic Subgoals for Cross-Embodiment Goal-Conditioned Control

author.name: Hao Shi, Xi Li

entry.summary: This work proposes extracting topologically unavoidable subgoals (separating sets and route choices recovered via homology) from offline trajectories, giving subgoals that are invariant to the executor and thus transferable across robot embodiments. This formalizes a novel notion of strategic subgoals for long-horizon goal-conditioned RL grounded in computational topology.

entry.title: Legible Failures: Detecting and Repairing In-Context Binding Errors

author.name: Manas Venkata Sai Ravulapalli, Samrath Singh Chadha, Abhinav M. Hari

entry.summary: The paper studies in-context binding errors in language models, showing that when a model emits an incorrect prompt-supplied entity binding, a linear probe can often recover the correct binding from its frozen hidden states across 16 public checkpoints. Using train/validation/test folds with careful controls, including a query-entity counterfactual that rules out token presence and recency effects, probe accuracy on wrong trials exceeds the 1/K chance baseline by a statistically significant margin. This suggests many model failures reflect failed information use rather than missing information, with implications for interpretability and error repair.

entry.title: DeFiFlowBench: Benchmarking and Improving Safe Executability in Natural-Language DeFi Workflow Synthesis

author.name: Abhinav Rajeev Kumar, Harshit Arora, Varun Singh, Manikandan Nanjappan

entry.summary: DeFiFlowBench is a 207-prompt benchmark measuring whether LLM-generated DeFi workflows are not just structurally valid but safe to execute, testing them on a local EVM against a 5% price-impact cap. The authors find 14-19 unsafe executions per configuration from standard prompting and propose Koan-Safe, combining intent parsing, structural repair, and default safety parameters to improve held-out safety.

entry.title: General Quantification of Covariate and Concept Shifts

author.name: Hongbo Chen, Li Charlie Xia

entry.summary: Using entropic optimal transport, the paper introduces gamma*-concept shifts that remain well-defined when source and target supports mismatch, deriving a general error bound unifying covariate and concept shifts across broad losses and label spaces. It provides estimators with concentration guarantees and a DataShifts algorithm, bridging generalization theory and practice.

entry.title: Numbat: Building and Verifying a Self-Contained Machine-Learning Stack

author.name: Thang Tran (CloudKites AI Lab, New South Wales, Australia), Lan Dang (Monash Business School, Monash University, Victoria, Australia)

entry.summary: Numbat is a machine-learning stack written entirely in Zig with no third-party runtime dependencies, spanning tensor computation, autodiff, neural-network modules, mixed precision, multi-GPU training, and data loading, exposed via a stable C ABI of over 1,400 entry points. The paper reports on its construction and verification, addressing the engineering fragility of Python-orchestrated ML frameworks. It matters as an existence proof for a radically simplified, self-contained ML infrastructure.

entry.title: New Evidence, Same Choice: Testing Physical Experiment Selection in Vision Language Models

author.name: Sourajit Saha, Shubhashis Roy Dipta, Nobin Sarwar, Shaswati Saha, Yuxuan Jiang, Siyuan Li, Qiheng Wang

entry.summary: The paper introduces a controlled evaluation testing whether vision-language models can decide when an existing physical measurement suffices to answer a question or when to gather new evidence, and which experiment to choose. Current physical reasoning benchmarks only score final answers and miss this decision-making ability. This probes an important component of scientific reasoning that is largely unmeasured in VLMs.

entry.title: A Hilbert-Valued Functional Decomposition Framework for Explaining Time-Dependent Outputs

author.name: Sophie Hanna Langbein, Niklas Koenen, Marvin N. Wright, Julia Herbinger

entry.summary: This paper generalizes feature-based explanation methods (functional decomposition) to Hilbert-valued, i.e., functional or multivariate, prediction functions, enabling coherent explanations of time-dependent outputs such as demand forecasting trajectories. Existing approaches explain each output location independently, ignoring cross-component dependencies; the proposed framework uses kernel-based output representations to handle them jointly. This fills a real gap in explainable AI for structured, non-scalar outputs.

entry.title: Can LLMs Normalize Databases? A Benchmark and Multi-Agent Framework for Schema Normalization

author.name: Dong-Jae Koh, Huisu Kim, SeongHwan Yoon, Lasse M. Jantsch, Chun-Hee Lee, Seonghyeon Lee, Young-Kyoon Suh

entry.summary: DNBENCH is a 3,275-sample benchmark evaluating LLM-driven database normalization from 1NF to BCNF with a three-axis protocol covering semantic equivalence, structural accuracy, and logical validity. It uncovers recurring failures in dependency inference, schema decomposition, and inter-table constraints, and proposes a multi-agent framework. It tests structured-output reliability under database-level constraints.

entry.title: Same Day, Same Story; One Day Ahead, a Different Signal: The Dual Validity of Financial Sentiment

author.name: AS Aravinthkakshan, Laven Srivastava, Harsh Nandwani

entry.summary: The paper tests whether human agreement (construct validity) and market predictive validity coincide for financial sentiment tools, using a corpus of securities class actions linking 70,500 X messages to abnormal stock returns. Across five sentiment instruments run through one pipeline, the relationship between the two validity types depends on sampling convention and score representation, challenging the standard financial NLP workflow.

entry.title: AcFlow: Controlling Text-to-Image Diffusion Transformers via Learned Conditional Activation Flow

author.name: Junran Wang, Zehao Jin, Tianyu Luan, Xinjie Shen

entry.summary: AcFlow is an inference-time controller for text-to-image diffusion transformers that transports intermediate image-token activations through a learned concept-conditioned velocity field while keeping the base DiT frozen. It enables continuous control over style intensity and suppression of unwanted concepts via a textual concept description and an integration horizon parameter.

entry.title: SAMV-DUSt3R: Instance-Centric 3D Scene Decoupling from Sparse Multi-Views

author.name: Langxu Zhao, Zuan Gu, Yingdan Zhang, Pengfei Zhao, Tianhan Gao

entry.summary: Injects SAM2 masks into MV-DUSt3R reconstruction via a cross-flow mask block, achieving object-level disentanglement and improved shape accuracy in a single end-to-end model, plus a lightweight RankGNN reference-view selector. Reports about 11 percent average precision gains over state-of-the-art baselines on sparse multi-view inputs.

entry.title: FreeFlow: A Bias-free Hierarchical Transformer for Optical Flow Estimation

author.name: Vladislav Bargatin, Alexander Yakovenko, Khaled Abud, Dmitriy Vatolin

entry.summary: Builds an optical flow model without flow-specific inductive biases (no correlation volumes, warping, or iterative refinement), using a single feed-forward hierarchical encoder-decoder combining window, shifted-window, and reduced-resolution global attention. Questions the necessity of task-specific heuristics in flow estimation.

entry.title: Self-Supervised Cardiac Phase Detection via Single-Parameter Latent Orbits

author.name: John Bonnici, Matthew Baugh, Aleksandra Kulbaka, Sarah Cechnicka, Bernhard Kainz, Alberto Gomez

entry.summary: This paper proposes a self-supervised method for detecting end-diastole and end-systole frames in echocardiography by encoding the physiological insight that cardiac phase is one-dimensional, using single-parameter latent orbits that balance interpretability with flexibility. This avoids both restrictive periodic assumptions and post-hoc geometric recovery.

entry.title: Guided Super-Resolution of Digital Elevation Models with Diffusion-Based Image Generators

author.name: Armand Mihai Nicolicioiu, Dominik Narnhofer, Nando Metzger, Daniel Panangian, Ksenia Bittner, Konrad Schindler

entry.summary: The paper proposes a diffusion-based guided super-resolution method that enhances coarse 5 m digital surface models to 0.5 m resolution using high-resolution spectral imagery as guidance, transferring image-visible details like building outlines into the elevation model. This addresses the cost mismatch between expensive high-resolution DSMs and widely available coarse satellite products for urban analysis.

entry.title: Expressive Robotic Pianist: Mastering Complex Piano Repertoire with Graph-Mimic and Musical Dynamics

author.name: Yanhong Liang, Xianwei Liu, Chaojie Fu, Shaowen Cheng, Yanyan Yuan, Chengwei Zhuo, Xi Chen, Yongbin Jin, Wei Yang, Hongtao Wang

entry.summary: This work demonstrates a reinforcement learning control framework enabling a dexterous robotic hand to perform diverse, complex piano repertoire with expressive dynamics. A graph-based optimization strategy generates human-like pre-press and key-press fingering transitions, targeting the gap between mechanical precision and artistic interpretation.

entry.title: Contact-Aware Incremental Model Predictive Control for an Underactuated Aerial Manipulator

author.name: Darwin Liu, Tamas Keviczky, Sihao Sun

entry.summary: This work presents a robust contact-aware control framework for aerial writing on an underactuated quadrotor-based manipulator, combining NMPC for end-effector position and normal-force tracking with whole-body incremental nonlinear dynamic inversion for disturbance robustness. It is validated in simulation and real-world experiments across surfaces, forces, and friction conditions.

entry.title: The Menu Is an Execution Prior: State-Path Tool Menus for Online Agents

author.name: Bo Yan, Weikai Lin, Song Wang

entry.summary: Addresses tool selection for LLM agents facing thousands of available interfaces by introducing the tool menu as a learned execution prior. The State-Path Tool Menu framework plans pre-execution routes from request state to outcome, surfacing prerequisite producer tools that relevance-ranking constructors typically miss.

entry.title: Which Tokens Should SFT Actually Learn? A Token-Trimming Perspective on Mathematical Reasoning

author.name: Yaning Jia, Chunhui Zhang, Wenxuan Xu, Xingjian Diao, Xiaoyuan Wang, Soroush Vosoughi

entry.summary: Proposes TrimSFT, a token-level reweighting method for supervised fine-tuning that scales loss by the logit gap between the gold token and its strongest competitor, trimming supervision from both mastered and poorly supported tokens. This concentrates learning on an informative middle band, correcting over-sharpening and amplified pressure from uniform cross-entropy. Targets improved mathematical reasoning training dynamics.

entry.title: TRACE: Training Reasoning Agents for Causal Exploration with Synthesized Rewards

author.name: Rui Sun, Zhan Shi, Bing He

entry.summary: TRACE engineers oracle rewards for diagnostic reasoning by sampling hidden interventions in a controlled simulator and scoring agents against the resulting observations, sidestepping the costly verification of true causes. The agent must still investigate noisy, confounded, distributed evidence, enabling RL training for causal diagnostic exploration.

entry.title: VANTAGE-Bench: Evaluating the Infrastructure AI Gap in Vision-Language Models

author.name: Zaid Pervaiz Bhat, Nimra Nayyar, Arihant Jain, Lap Fung Chan, John Suchanek, Yu Wang, Varun Praveen, Tomasz Kornuta, Vidya Nariyambut Murali

entry.summary: VANTAGE-Bench targets a neglected class of physical AI: infrastructure applications using fixed cameras for safety monitoring and operational logging, rather than embodied agents with consumer video. The benchmark spans logistics, transportation, and smart spaces across semantic, spatial, temporal, and spatio-temporal capabilities, using eight task formulations including dense captioning and spatio-temporal grounding with single-pass trajectory evaluation. It quantifies the gap between current VLMs and infrastructure deployment needs.

entry.title: Pairit: A Platform for Live Experiments on Human-AI Collaboration

author.name: Harang Ju, Sinan Aral

entry.summary: Pairit is an open platform where researchers declare executable human-AI experiments (pages, routing, randomization, matchmaking, chat, shared workspaces) in a single YAML configuration. It enables live experiments on how human-AI groups coordinate, delegate, and decide, with AI participants both communicating and acting on shared work. This fills a methodological gap for empirical organizational research involving AI.

entry.title: Show-Harness: Just a VLM Agent Can Play Robots

author.name: Yanzhe Chen, Zechen Bai, Zhijun Cao, Wenzheng Zeng, Kevin Qinghong Lin, Yiqi Lin, Guoqiang Liang, Kevin Yuchen Ma, Qiming Huang, Mike Zheng Shou

entry.summary: Show-Harness is an embodied harness enabling vision-language models to control robots through a compact semantic interface of discrete action units, with deterministic interpreters grounding them into robot actions. It demonstrates zero-shot control with closed-source frontier VLMs and adaptation of small open-source models via the same interface.

entry.title: A Dataset and Model for Imputing Water Surface Elevation on a Large and Extremely Sparse Spatiotemporal Graph

author.name: Ruben Cartuyvels, Karim Douch, Gabriele Bertoli, Mounia El Baz, Artemis Vrettou, S\'ebastien Lef\`evre, Diego Fernandez Prieto

entry.summary: The authors introduce AmazonSWE, a dataset for spatiotemporal graph imputation of river water surface elevation covering over 19,000 river sections across 10 years, integrating satellite altimetry including wide-swath SWOT. The resource targets flood forecasting and water resource management where in situ gauges are scarce globally.

entry.title: Improving the Sensitivity of Gravitational Wave Detection with Weighted Conformal Prediction

author.name: Ann-Kristin Malz, Gregory Ashton, Nicolo Colombo

entry.summary: The paper combines outputs from multiple gravitational-wave detection pipelines using a conformal prediction framework that yields statistically rigorous confidence estimates for candidate events, instead of selecting the single most significant pipeline output. This improves detection sensitivity and ranking robustness while remaining valid as data properties evolve across observing runs. It demonstrates conformal methods delivering real scientific value in a high-stakes domain.

entry.title: Geospatial Foundation Models Capture Health-Relevant Dimensions of Place Beyond Conventional Social Risk Indices

author.name: Nathaniel Hendrix, Carl Y. Zhang, Chris Heitzig, Andrew Bazemore, David H. Rehkopf

entry.summary: The authors test whether embeddings from four geospatial foundation model families on 2022 satellite data explain health-outcome variance left unexplained by standard social deprivation indices, using LightGBM across 82,646 US census tracts and 40 CDC PLACES outcomes. This demonstrates that foundation-model representations of physical place carry health-relevant signal beyond socioeconomic survey variables.

entry.title: Building py-kvcache: A Performance Characterization of External KV Caching for vLLM with NVMe SSDs

author.name: Joseph Kanichai, Tiziano De Matteis, Animesh Trivedi

entry.summary: The paper characterizes when recomputing KV states beats loading them from external NVMe caches in vLLM, showing performance depends on transfer granularity, staging memory, and scheduling timing rather than device bandwidth alone. It introduces py-kvcache, a KV offload connector with asynchronous direct I/O and scheduler-aware preloading.

entry.title: INDRA: A New AI Tool for Exploring Tobacco, Fossil Fuel, and Chemical Industry Archives

author.name: Daniel Akselrad, Robert N. Proctor

entry.summary: INDRA is a research platform making hundreds of millions of pages of litigation-disclosed industry documents (tobacco, fossil fuel, chemical, drug, food, firearms) usable by LLM-based research, by encoding archival historiography conventions into a system-level protocol to prevent hallucination. It addresses the fact that these archives were never compiled into LLM-readable corpora.

entry.title: GRADE: Single-Frame Generative Radar Depth Estimation Under Visual Degradation

author.name: Bin Zhao, Patrick Chiou, Nakul Garg

entry.summary: GRADE combines a pretrained latent diffusion prior with raw 4D mmWave radar spectra to produce high-fidelity metric depth from a single frame in smoke, fog, and darkness where optical sensors fail. A pixel-space adapter optionally fuses residual camera cues and training spans clear and degraded conditions.

entry.title: Beyond Visual Quality: Evaluating Physical Consistency under Ego-Motion with EgoGenEval

author.name: Yilin Long, Chenming Zhu, Zitang Gou, Jingli Lin, Tai Wang

entry.summary: EgoGenEval is a geometry-grounded, pose-free benchmark evaluating whether visual generators maintain physical consistency under ego-motion, with 1,400 cases spanning single-step and multi-step motion and metrics for camera motion grounding and scene state preservation. The study evaluates 16 generators and validates metrics against human judgments.

entry.title: Multi-Modal Controlled Coherent Motion Generation

author.name: Yifei Liu, Qiong Cao, Hongwei Yi, Huaiguang Jiang, Changxing Ding

entry.summary: Proposes MOCO, a diffusion-based framework that generates coherent 3D avatar motion from simultaneous multimodal conditioning (speech audio, text, trajectory), avoiding the mismatched sequential or weighted-sum combinations of prior work. Tackles the scarcity of aligned multimodal motion data.

entry.title: Structural Process Supervision for Latent Chain-of-Thought Reasoning

author.name: Yiqi Li, Xu Chen, Chen Ju, Jiangchao Yao, Zhaoyang Li, Jinsong Lan, Xiaoyong Zhu, Bo Zheng, Yu Wang

entry.summary: The paper proposes Prototype-Mediated Process Supervision (PMPS) for latent chain-of-thought reasoning, using learnable reasoning prototypes as semantic anchors to supervise latent embeddings and prevent representation collapse. It achieves many-to-many soft alignment between latent and explicit CoT representations of unequal length via prototype assignment.

entry.title: ConvMem: Convolutional Memory for Long-Context Reasoning

author.name: Hongming Zhang, Zhaozhen Gu, Fengshuo Bai, Ming Hao, Qingyang Zhang, Yuanyuan Wang, Shiyang Tang, Yanna Wang, Bo Xu

entry.summary: ConvMem reformulates long-context reasoning as a hierarchical convolution, treating the LLM prompted with a query as a convolutional kernel over text, inspired by CNNs. Unlike sequential approaches such as MemAgent, it is training-free, highly parallelizable, and avoids RL-related overfitting while extending effective context beyond fixed limits.

entry.title: AgenticGen: Reward-Guided Agentic Video Generation for Advertising

author.name: Xingyuan Bu, Chengru Song, Hao Zhou, Tao Zhou, Dong Li, Wei Li, Shilong Li, Hao Shi, Yongxin Guo, Donghao Zhou, Qiangpeng Yang, Shilei Wen

entry.summary: Proposes AgenticGen, a framework that decomposes advertising video generation into strategy selection and draft generation stages, supervised by a performance-based reward learned from online business metrics. This closes the loop between video foundation models and real-world ad effectiveness rather than optimizing only visual realism. It demonstrates applied reinforcement learning from business feedback in generative media.

entry.title: Learning with Synthetic Data via SGD in High-Dimensional Linear Regression

author.name: Jichu li, Difan Zou

entry.summary: Establishes finite-sample risk bounds for one-pass SGD in high-dimensional linear regression trained on mixed synthetic and real data with model shift, disentangling bias, variance, fluctuation, and persistent drift effects. Reveals a sharp contrast between mixed and two-stage training regimes regarding the model-collapse risk floor.

entry.title: Teacher Geometry Shapes Learnability in Teacher-Student Networks

author.name: Kai J. Sandbrink, Flavio Martinelli, Alexander van Meegen, Wulfram Gerstner, Johanni Brea

entry.summary: Formalizes learnability in teacher-student setups as convergence success rate as a function of teacher geometry, overparameterization, algorithm, and initialization, identifying easy and hard teacher distributions via node dissimilarity. Shows that the common assumption of random Gaussian teachers hides substantial variation in learnability.

entry.title: What Makes Adversarial Examples Transfer Across Deepfake Detectors?

author.name: Rafael M. Mamede, Pedro C. Neto, Ana F. Sequeira

entry.summary: This controlled study evaluates transfer-based black-box adversarial attacks across 60 deepfake detectors, six backbones, two pretraining regimes, and five data configurations using AutoAttack and CW-EOT. Matched comparisons disentangle architectural from training factors that drive higher transfer success. It provides actionable insight into why deepfake defenses fail under attack.

entry.title: Relatively Smart II: Tractable or Semi-Supervised Instance-Optimal Learning

author.name: Shaddin Dughmi, Alireza F. Pour

entry.summary: Advances the relatively smart learning program of Dughmi and Pour (2026), where a learner competes with every distribution-fixed error guarantee certifiable from unlabeled data. This sequel shows that ERM, and any proper consistent learner, is relatively smart for binary classification in the distribution-free setting, addressing open questions about tractable learners and whether the sample-complexity blowup can be restricted to unlabeled data. Substantial learning-theory progress.

entry.title: Model-Aware Schedules Improve Generation via Fiberwise Optimal Transport

author.name: Luyi Jia, Boyan Zhang, Yilun Liu, Steffen Rulands

entry.summary: The paper introduces model-aware schedule construction for diffusion and flow matching using fiberwise optimal transport, defining a fiberwise prediction risk between true and predictor-induced signal/noise decompositions and combining it with a kinetic action on coefficient paths. This moves beyond model-agnostic schedule design by incorporating prediction error.

entry.title: Adaptive Diffusion Freezing: Privacy-preserving Diffusion Models Against Membership Inference Attacks

author.name: Jialu Guo, Xiao Han, Junjie Wu

entry.summary: The authors propose Adaptive Diffusion Freezing (ADF), a framework that defends diffusion models against membership inference attacks by using cross-timestep adaptive freezing to control which data subsets participate at different diffusion timesteps via a mask matrix. This reduces over-memorization of training data while aiming for a better privacy-utility-efficiency trade-off than prior defenses. It matters because memorization in generative models is a pressing privacy concern.

entry.title: Symmetry-aware super-resolution of crystal orientation maps via invariant latent-space learning

author.name: Umang Garg, Warren Zamudio, McLean P. Echlin, Samantha H. Daly, Tresa M. Pollock, B. S. Manjunath

entry.summary: SG-SRAN performs super-resolution of electron backscatter diffraction crystal-orientation maps by exploiting the quotient-space geometry SO(3)/G, mapping symmetry-equivalent orientations to a common latent representation with a frozen locally isometric encoder. This prevents the symmetry-mixing artifacts and grain-boundary blurring that standard Euclidean methods cause. The work demonstrates principled group-theoretic design for scientific imaging.

entry.title: DINO-Med: A Unified Patch-Based Adaptation Framework for Multi-Modal Medical Image Analysis Applied to Liver Fibrosis Staging

author.name: Boya Wang, Ruizhe Li, Chao Chen, Xin Chen

entry.summary: Presents a unified pipeline for adapting natural-image foundation models like DINOv3 to multi-modal medical imaging via training-free registration, automated localization, mask-filtered patch extraction, and hierarchical patch-to-subject aggregation, evaluated on liver fibrosis staging against radiomics, ResNet, and SAM-Med2D features. A general recipe for foundation-model transfer to medical scans.

entry.title: Harnessing Intrinsic Subject-Aware Attention for Controllable Multi-Subject Video Generation

author.name: Niange Yu, Ye Tian, Biaolong Chen, Miao Lu, Aixi Zhang, Hao Jiang, Yunhai Tong, Pipei Huang

entry.summary: Finds that certain DiT attention blocks naturally form an intrinsic spatial grounding map that locates reference subjects, and leverages these internal signals at both training and inference to control fidelity strength without retraining and to auto-build preference pairs at high-noise stages. Improves multi-subject video generation control and reduces semantic drift.

entry.title: Spectral Adapters for Segment Anything Model-based Segmentation of Colorectal Liver Metastases in Computed Tomography

author.name: Ramtin Mojtahedi, Mohammad Hamghalam, Jacob J. Peoples, Natalie Gangai, Mithat Gonen, Yun Shin Chun, HyunSeon Christine Kang, Richard K. G. Do, Amber L. Simpson

entry.summary: The authors propose DiSECT and SiGA, parameter-efficient spectral adapters for adapting SAM to colorectal liver metastasis segmentation in contrast-enhanced CT, constraining residual updates to leading singular value directions and adding input-conditioned gating. Evaluated on 446 CT volumes, they compare favorably against LoRA, QLoRA, convolutional adapters, and a 3D nnU-Net baseline.

entry.title: Caption-once, Frames-on-Demand: Visual-Need Routing for Budget-Aware Agentic Long Video Understanding

author.name: Weitong Cai, Hang Zhang, Yukai Huang, Yiqiao Xie, Shan Gao, Jiankang Deng, Songcen Xu, Jifei Song, Zhensong Zhang

entry.summary: CFD is a budget-aware edge-cloud agentic framework for long-video understanding that performs a single offline captioning pass building a dual-track narrative index (event-level story plus clip-level micro-log), then routes queries to either text memories or on-demand frames depending on visual need. This balances temporal structure from language against attribute-level perception from pixels under tight edge compute budgets.

entry.title: Why don’t machine learning research agents overfit?

author.name: Unknown

entry.summary: An Amazon Science post examining why autonomous ML research agents, which repeatedly consult validation data while iterating on models, do not appear to overfit in the classical sense. It walks through the train/validation/test distinction and why held-out performance remains a meaningful proxy even when an agent adaptively queries validation sets.

entry.title: PRAGMA: Evaluating Personalized Guidance with Memory Alignment in Lifelong Conversations

author.name: Hyojeong Yu, Hyukhun Koh, Minsung Kim, Yunah Jang, Kyomin Jung

entry.summary: Proposes PRAGMA, a benchmark evaluating whether memory systems in long-running personalized LLM assistants can integrate user-specific information into practical guidance such as recommendations, planning, and decision support. It highlights that long-context reliance is computationally costly and unreliable, motivating structured memory retrieval. The benchmark distinguishes personalized guidance from simple factual recall.

entry.title: AgentAudit: An Open, Extensible Framework for Full-Lifecycle Trust Evaluation of AI Agents

author.name: Shrey Nag, Sachita, Abhishek Kumar Singh, Lipi Goel, Rajeshwar Singh Janwar

entry.summary: AgentAudit evaluates the complete execution trace of AI agents across ten dimensions spanning capability, grounding, security, and behavior, with failure attribution to the exact pipeline stage. Unlike benchmarks that score only task completion or robustness, it aims to pinpoint where in planning, tool use, memory, or reasoning a failure arose.

entry.title: Reference-Based Bias Detection in LLMs via Relative Representations of Hidden States

author.name: Marek Jeli\'nski, Jan Dubi\'nski, Maciej Chrabaszcz, Sebastian Cygert

entry.summary: The paper proposes auditing bias in hidden-state representations across related model variants by encoding sentences as similarities to fixed anchors, yielding relative representations comparable before and after fine-tuning. It measures Representational Bias Shift, capturing internal shifts that output-based benchmarks might miss without costly judge models.

entry.title: In RAG We Trust? Measuring Robustness of Retrieval-Augmented Generation Under Document Poisoning

author.name: Iliano Fasolino

entry.summary: This work quantifies how a small quantized model (Llama 3.1 8B) degrades when retrieved RAG context is poisoned, testing entity swap, number swap, and negation corruptions across a factorial sweep of 588 runs on a FEVER-based fact-checking task. Accuracy drops from 77.9% on clean context to 43.5% with all three passages corrupted, with entity swaps causing the most damage. It highlights a concrete and underexplored security vulnerability of retrieval-augmented systems.

entry.title: LogiScope-VQA: Benchmarking Vision-Language Models for Logistics Hazard Identification in Industrial Scenarios

author.name: Hanjing Zhou, Mingze Yin, Ying Lian, Jun Ma, Chang-Yu Hsieh, Yanbing Zhou

entry.summary: LogiScope-VQA is a new benchmark of 2,476 images, 2,918 videos from real logistics parks, and 10,274 human-validated VQAs spanning 39 subtasks on 18 objects and 20 risk types. It tests whether mainstream large multimodal models can perceive, understand, and reason about industrial hazards at human-expert level. It exposes a poorly covered vertical where scarce proprietary data has stalled progress.

entry.title: Beyond One-Size-Fits-All: Sample-Adaptive Strategy Routing for Vision Token Pruning in MLLMs

author.name: Haiji Liang, Pengfei Zhou, Zhenglin Wan, Wei Wang, Yang You, Wangbo Zhao

entry.summary: The paper shows that a single fixed vision token pruning strategy underperforms on many individual samples in multimodal LLMs despite good average accuracy. It proposes VIP-Router, a lightweight router that adaptively selects the best pruning strategy per sample to reduce inference costs while preserving accuracy.

entry.title: Counterfactual Marginalisation: Framework for Evaluating Robustness to Nuisance Variables

author.name: Yasin Ibrahim, Hermione Warr, Robin J. Evans, Konstantinos Kamnitsas

entry.summary: Proposes counterfactual marginalisation as a test-time evaluation procedure for assessing whether classification models rely on demographic or acquisition shortcuts. Given a counterfactual image generator, it intervenes on nuisance variables like age or sex, generates CF versions of test images, and averages predictions over an intervention distribution, yielding metrics for CF risk, calibration, stability, and worst-case sensitivity. A rigorous evaluation framework for clinical robustness to spurious factors.

entry.title: MUtE: A Dual Framework for Concept Erasure and Counterfactual Interventions

author.name: Antoine Saillenfest

entry.summary: MUtE revisits optimal bounds on concept erasure to derive a class of erasure functions that also induce a deterministic dual counterfactual mapping, transforming representations so a target concept becomes unpredictable while preserving unrelated information. The implementation imposes a translational bias on counterfactual trajectories, aligning with how concepts manifest geometrically in modern language models. This unifies two important interpretability tools: removing biased information and generating counterfactual explanations.

entry.title: Dynamic language model representations for multi-objective reaction optimisation

author.name: Joshua W. Sin, David Ming Segura, Bojana Rankovi\'c, Siu Lun Chau, Marius D. R. Lutz, Andrea Anelli, Ryan P. Burwood, Kurt P\"untener, Maximilian J. Notheis, Raphael Bigler, Philippe Schwaller

entry.summary: This work learns reaction representations dynamically from text using language models, bypassing hand-crafted featurizations for chemically diverse components in multi-objective reaction optimization (yield, selectivity, safety). The approach applies across chemically distinct components where one-hot encodings and molecular descriptors fall short.

entry.title: A variational physics-informed graph neural network for heterogeneous solid mechanics

author.name: Aashay Rajan Yadav, Amiya Prakash Das, Ratna Kumar Annabattula

entry.summary: The paper presents a variational, label-free physics-informed graph neural network for stress analysis in heterogeneous solids, carrying heterogeneity through the conforming adaptive mesh graph rather than the trial field. This naturally represents C0-continuous displacements with jumping stresses across bimaterial interfaces, avoiding the sensitivity of coordinate-based PINNs to interface regularization choices. It minimizes discrete total potential energy directly.

entry.title: LLM-Anchored Paralinguistic Enrichment for Alzheimer's Disease Detection

author.name: Xiao Wei, Yuqin Lin, Yaru Cao, Jinyu Li, Bin Wen, Kai Li, Yueying Chen, Longbiao Wang, Jianwu Dang

entry.summary: LAPE enriches LLM-derived linguistic representations with paralinguistic cues like pauses and word elongations for non-invasive speech-based Alzheimer's detection. It introduces prosodic event textualization so the LLM models prosody jointly with lexical content. The work has clear healthcare relevance for scalable early cognitive screening.

entry.title: Component-Aware Differential Privacy for Federated Multilingual Speech-LLMs

author.name: Jordi Luque, Fernando L\'opez, Aleix Sant

entry.summary: Shows that per-layer differential privacy clipping, which works well for standard LMs, fails for federated speech-LLMs due to large norm imbalance between acoustic encoders and language decoders, causing cross-component budget collapse. The paper diagnoses the root cause across six per-layer methods and develops component-aware DP clipping that allocates budgets across heterogeneous modules. Relevant to privacy-preserving federated training of multimodal models.

entry.title: BridgeMatch: Conditional Transport Bridges in Matching Matrix Space for 3D Deformable Registration

author.name: Qianliang Wu, Haobo Jiang, Guangwei Gao, Shuo Chen, Jin Xie, Jian Yang, Yaqing Ding

entry.summary: A two-stage generative solver for non-rigid point cloud correspondences that uses diffusion to estimate a global coarse matching matrix, then lifts it to high resolution while preserving completeness of the search space rather than pruning with top-K selection. Targets deformable anatomical registration and dynamic 3D tasks.

entry.title: LangStreet: Persistent Language Fields for Anchor-Decoded Street Gaussians

author.name: Runyi Yang, Deheng Zhang, Xiaoye Wang, Mengjiao Ma, Lei Sun, Kanzhi Wu, Ajad Chhatkuli, Luc Van Gool, Danda Pani Paudel

entry.summary: LangStreet addresses the breakdown of language-grounded Gaussian fields in scalable anchor-decoded representations, where view-conditioned child Gaussians make semantics unstable across views. It introduces semantic ownership so persistent anchors own the language field, using alpha-compositing responsibilities and anchor-aligned evidence completion.

entry.title: RIDE: Relocalization-Informed Depth Estimation with 3D Gaussian Splatting

author.name: Jiarong Lian, Zhe Xiao, Zhaoyang Zhang, Wei Li, Ruizhi Chen

entry.summary: RIDE estimates dense metric depth from a robot's RGB stream by combining sparse metric depth from PnP-RANSAC relocalization correspondences with geometric priors from a pretrained video-depth model, anchored to a metrically scaled 3D Gaussian Splatting map. Global and local depth correction with temporal memory sustains estimation through observation gaps.

entry.title: Stress-Testing Dynamical and Generative Downscaling Using Subseasonal Extreme Precipitation Forecasts

author.name: Mauricio Lima, Marika Koukoula, Romain Pilon, Monika Feldmann, Erwan Koch, Daniela I. V. Domeisen, Tom Beucler

entry.summary: This climate-ML study compares dynamical downscaling via the WRF model against a diffusion-based generative model for resolving extreme precipitation from subseasonal forecasts, across two physically distinct events with lead times up to three weeks. The generative model is trained unpaired for fairness with WRF, and both approaches improve spatial resolution, though performance varies with atmospheric regime and lead time.

entry.title: Can you hear the shape of a Lean soundness bug? A wager.

author.name: Max von Hippel

entry.summary: The author argues that Lean's growing role as a verifiable RL environment and as load-bearing infrastructure for AI safety proposals makes its own soundness a critical, underexamined dependency, framing the detection of Lean soundness bugs as an open problem worth a wager. The post situates formal methods within the current wave of venture capital and big-lab investment in secure-by-construction software.

entry.title: A Function-Space Approach to the Statistical Mechanics of Learning Dynamics

author.name: Yizhou Zhang, Weichen Wu, Lun Du, Zhengjie Miao

entry.summary: Develops a statistical-mechanical theory of neural network learning directly in function space, treating parameter configurations as microscopic states and functions as macroscopic variables. For mean-squared loss, exact error dynamics are governed by a learning operator, and the authors derive a fluctuation functional combining dynamical Boltzmann weights with parameter-space density of states. This provides a theoretically grounded account of why deep networks exhibit regular macroscopic learning behavior.

entry.title: UnitBoost: Managing Compound LLM Systems with a Merge Operator, Not a Model

author.name: Xing Zhang, Guanghui Wang, Yanwei Cui, Mengdie Flora Wang, Peiyang He

entry.summary: UnitBoost replaces the LLM meta-agent that coordinates compound systems with a deterministic merge operator that maps worker outputs to slot-value proposals and exposes an explicit residual for unresolved slots. This makes coordination order-free, provenance-aware, and easier to guarantee, in contrast to opaque model-based managers.

entry.title: OntologyAligner: Ontology-Aligned Retrieval and Hierarchy-Guided Large Language Model Reranking for Biomedical Ontology Normalization

author.name: Jie Song, Zhichuan Xu, Ziyu Lu, Meng Xiao, Cheng Bi, Yuxin Zhang, Xin Zheng, Xiaoran Li, Qiongfang Cao, Hao Yang, Bairong Shen

entry.summary: OntologyAligner is a three-stage framework for biomedical ontology normalization combining ontology-aligned retrieval, LLM reranking, and hierarchy-guided refinement, accompanied by PhenoNormBench with 13,390 samples from seven HPO datasets. It achieves state-of-the-art HPO normalization accuracy (88.78% Macro Top-1), beating existing baselines.

entry.title: From Plausible to Actionable: A Position on LLM Self-Explanations

author.name: Elize Herrewijnen, Benedetta Muscato, Gizem Gezici, Fosca Giannotti

entry.summary: A position paper arguing that LLM self-explanations can be plausible yet unfaithful to the model's actual computation, while still being highly actionable for users. It critiques traditional XAI evaluation protocols when applied to LLM-generated explanations and proposes practical alternatives. The reframing matters because faithfulness may be the wrong sole criterion for judging explanations in practice.

entry.title: Support Discovery With Iteratively Reweighted Least Squares for Fixed-Charge Network Flow

author.name: Sindura Saraswathi, Christian K\"ummerle

entry.summary: The authors propose a scalable continuous-optimization algorithm for large-scale fixed-charge network flow problems, replacing discontinuous fixed-charge objectives with a smooth nonconvex Lasry-Lions surrogate solved via iteratively reweighted least squares. The sequence of weighted quadratic flow subproblems helps discover supports (active arc sets) where exact mixed-integer programming struggles on large networks. This bridges classical optimization and modern smooth-optimization techniques for combinatorial problems.

entry.title: High-probability guarantees for linear accessibility in feature superposition

author.name: Enrico Vompa

entry.summary: Frames linear accessibility of superposed features as a compressed sensing problem and derives high-probability bounds showing sufficient dimension scales as O(k log m) rather than prior worst-case quadratic limits, validated with Gaussian-tail approximations. Provides theoretical tools for evaluating sparse autoencoders and the linear representation hypothesis.

entry.title: Distilling Image Prototypes for Guided Test-Time Adaptation

author.name: Liwen Wang, Xingbo Dong, Iman Yi Liao, Deyin Liu, Massimo Tistarelli, Lin Yuanbo Wu, Zhe Jin

entry.summary: DIPTTA introduces Distilled Image Prototypes, compact synthetic representations, to guide test-time adaptation of vision models under distribution shift. The approach addresses error accumulation from noisy pseudo-labels and catastrophic forgetting, outperforming uncertainty-based filtering and static prototype replay. It matters for deploying vision models on shifting real-world data.

entry.title: A-JIT: Agentic Just-In-Time Software Construction

author.name: Mark Marron, Earl T. Barr

entry.summary: A-JIT proposes replacing static software binaries with applications that include an embedded AI agent continuously observing usage and execution traces to specialize code, workflows, and tool interfaces just in time. The paradigm aims to make software perpetually adaptive, analogous to JIT compilation but at the application-logic level.

entry.title: Halo: Improving forecast accuracy through heteroscedastic estimation

author.name: Adam Cataldo

entry.summary: Shows that heteroscedastic forecasting, usually motivated by uncertainty quantification, also improves point estimates, contradicting previously reported negative results. Halo is a minimal modification that adds a scale output to an existing forecaster and trains under a matching negative log likelihood, demonstrated by adapting three state-of-the-art architectures under Gaussian and Laplacian losses. This offers a cheap, architecture-agnostic accuracy gain for time series practitioners.

entry.title: Generalized Score Matching for Parameter Estimation on Convex Domains

author.name: Nishanth Shetty, Saisuchith Mahajan, Chandra Sekhar Seelamantula

entry.summary: This paper derives a generalized score matching objective on convex subsets of R^d, constructed from Minimum Probability Flow learning, and shows classical score matching and domain-adapted variants for non-negative data arise naturally in the framework. It enables parameter estimation for unnormalized models without tractable partition functions on constrained domains.

entry.title: The Last AI Built by Humans: Toward Genuine Recursive Self-Improvement

author.name: Yi Duan, Ying Liu, Zirui Tang, Haodong Chen, Jun Zhou, Yumou Liu, Bangrui Xu, Yukai Wu, Sidi Chen, Yuhan Zhou, Haoyu Wang, Xiaoyou Yu, Shaokun Han, Xuzhou Zhu, Le Zhou, Bolin Lu, Wei Zhou, Jiachen Liu, Nuozhou Fang, Jiaxin Tian, Ruoyu Chen, Yuxuan Li, Kai Zuo, Kaiyan Zhang, Jiantao Qiu, Conghui He, Guoliang Li, Bowen Zhou, Zhiyuan Liu, Zhoufutu Wen, Jihua Kang, Xuanhe Zhou, Fan Wu

entry.summary: A large-author-group position paper on recursive self-improvement (RSI), introducing a Headroom-Closed Index to diagnose current LLM limitations and a roadmap spanning improvement-execution, strategy, experience-acquisition, and environment-adaptation autonomy through recursive meta-improvement. It surveys RSI across scientific discovery, embodied intelligence, and software engineering.

entry.title: Sequence-Informed Geometric Evaluation of RNA 3D Structures

author.name: Andrea Zerio, Yighua Yao, Alessandro Micheli, Roland G. Huber, Mile Sikic, Samir Bhatt, Andres R. Masegosa, Yuangang Pan

entry.summary: This paper introduces SIRGE, an evaluator for RNA 3D structure candidates that conditions geometric representations on nucleotide embeddings from a pretrained RNA language model. It outperforms established evaluators on Kendall-tau alignment, Top-1 selection, and Top-3 ranking, and controlled comparisons show that sequence conditioning corrects errors made by an otherwise matched purely geometric model. This matters because reliable candidate scoring is a bottleneck in computational RNA structure pipelines with implications for drug design and RNA biology.

entry.title: SynCo: Synthetic Community-Aware Attributed Graph Generator for Graph Neural Network Benchmarking

author.name: Guilherme Henrique Messias, Mariana Caravanti de Souza, Sylvia Iasulaitis, Alan Dem\'etrius Baria Valejo

entry.summary: This paper introduces SynCo, a synthetic attributed graph generator that creates graphs with community structure beyond the typical power-law assumptions, designed to enable better benchmarking of GNNs on community detection tasks. It addresses the scarcity of ground-truth community labels that has stalled progress in GNN-based community detection evaluation. Better synthetic generators allow more rigorous and varied stress-testing of graph learning models.

entry.title: Scale-Aware 3D Deep Learning for Robust Brain Metastasis Detection in Multimodal MRI

author.name: Sylvain Jaume, Hongming Wang, Simon K. Warfield

entry.summary: The authors present a scale-aware 3D framework combining independently trained 96-cubed and 64-cubed U-Nets with weighted late fusion to improve brain metastasis detection in multimodal MRI. Cross-FOV fusion improved lesion-level precision and F1 on a 97-patient cohort. The work addresses the clinically important problem of detecting very small lesions that occupy a minute fraction of 3D volumes.

entry.title: Generative Replay Mitigates Sample Starvation in Quantum Architecture Search

author.name: Akash Kundu, Amit Kumar Jaiswal, Sebastian Feld, Prayag Tiwari

entry.summary: GenQAS is a tensor network-guided reinforcement learning framework for quantum architecture search that combines a matrix product state warm-start with prioritized generative replay. A learned local transition model synthesizes plausible circuit transitions on demand to counter sample starvation as the search space expands. This addresses a real scalability bottleneck at the intersection of RL, generative modeling, and quantum computing.

entry.title: Bio-inspired Learning and Decision-Making with Probabilistic In-Memory Computing Hardware: Part 1

author.name: Thomas Dalgaty, Eiji Kawasaki, Miguel de Prado, Devendra Vyas, Tommaso Salvatori

entry.summary: This work proposes a biologically grounded framework where noisy neural and synaptic dynamics perform Bayesian inference and learning via stochastic sampling from an internal energy function, with neural variability capturing uncertainty over latent states and synaptic variability over model parameters. It links predictive coding and MCMC-style sampling to probabilistic in-memory computing hardware, suggesting how brain-like uncertainty handling could be physically implemented. The paper bridges neuroscience-inspired computation with novel hardware co-design.

entry.title: LOCUS: Task-Aware Low-Rank Post-Training for Token-Efficient Language Generation

author.name: Dongfang Zhao

entry.summary: LOCUS selects a task-aware low-rank adaptation subspace so preference post-training reduces output verbosity without changing the alignment objective or backbone. Experiments on Anthropic HH-RLHF with Pythia-2.8B and Qwen2.5-3B show low-rank updates can trade off token cost against utility.

entry.title: Data-Efficient Language Modeling: From Frontier Advancement to Principle-Guided Model Improvement

author.name: Shuxing Yang, Kaihao Zhu, Junjie Yang, Rui Zhao, Junyao Wu, Yize Wang, Wenhao Li, Fujia Chen, Taowen Deng, Shenzhan Hong, Yaqi Li, Zichen Li, Jincheng Mi, Yuang Pan, Hongsheng Chen, Yihao Yang

entry.summary: The Qiushi Engine team ran a long-horizon autonomous research program on the BabyLM 2026 Strict-Small track (under 10M corpus words), in three stages: building a frontier data-efficient model, discovering principles about repetition versus restatement in context use, and applying those principles to improve the model. It exemplifies automated, principle-driven LM research under extreme data budgets.

entry.title: Larger Context Window, Fewer Overcorrections: Optimizing Prompts and Batching for Minimal-Edit Grammatical Error Correction

author.name: Kateryna Karpo, Artem Chernodub

entry.summary: This work introduces taxonomy-based prompting and batching strategies to reduce systematic overcorrection in zero- and few-shot LLM-based grammatical error correction, closing much of the gap to fine-tuned models without training infrastructure. It frames minimal-edit constraints as a metric-aligned instruction problem tied to F0.5. The approach is practical and model-dependent, benefiting strongest models most.

entry.title: ProMediConv: Benchmarking Proactive Conversational Agents in Legal Dispute Mediation

author.name: Zesheng Wei, Mengfan Li, Wenhao Liu, Yixin Zhang, Zilei Wang, Yang Deng

entry.summary: ProMediConv is a benchmark modeling legal dispute mediation as proactive, multi-stage, party-aware dialogue with 11 mediation strategies and four party behavior pattern states, built from 972 real-world cases with utterance-level annotations. It enables turn-by-turn evaluation of conversational agents in a socially important task. This raises the fidelity bar for LLM-based mediation research.

entry.title: The Illusion of Balanced Multimodal Sentiment Analysis: Beyond the Limits of Optimization-Based Methods

author.name: Ioanna Kaffeza, Efthymios Georgiou, Alexandros Potamianos

entry.summary: This paper provides a unified controlled evaluation of gradient- and loss-based balancing strategies for modality imbalance in multimodal sentiment analysis, plus a theoretical diagnosis explaining why they fail by conflating fitting speed with discriminative contribution. Experiments on CMU-MOSI and CMU-MOSEI show no strategy reliably beats Late Concatenation, and it proposes a research agenda for held-out modality valuation. A strong corrective to overpromised methods.

entry.title: On the Impact of Anonymization on the Performance of Large Language Models

author.name: Tobias Deu{\ss}er, Max Hahnb\"uck, Lorenz Sparrenberg, Tobias Uelwer, Christian Bauckhage, Rafet Sifa

entry.summary: This systematic study measures the privacy-utility trade-off of pseudonymizing LLM inputs, evaluating five models across eleven benchmarks. Anonymization generally degrades performance, and the effect is nuanced: more capable models like Qwen2.5-72B and GPT-4o mini suffer the largest drops, suggesting greater reliance on identifying information. Results inform deployment practice in sensitive domains.

entry.title: SWRouter: Similarity-Contractive Window Routing for Multi-Turn Large Language Model Conversations

author.name: Yu Wang, Yuchen Li, Rui Kong, Xinran Chen, Jiamin Chen, Hengyi Cai, Shuaiqiang Wang, Jiashu Zhao, Yulun Zhang, Zhonghao Lyu, Haoyi Xiong, Linghe Kong, Jimmy Xiangji Huang, Dawei Yin

entry.summary: Proposes SWRouter, a routing method that dispatches queries in multi-turn LLM conversations to the most suitable model by addressing how historical context is segmented and incorporated. It tackles information loss/confusion in context construction and decouples model-selection quality from prompt-construction quality. This extends LLM routing from single-turn to dialogue settings, relevant to cost-efficient multi-model serving.

entry.title: Epistemic orientation predicts legislative effectiveness among members of the US Congress

author.name: Segun Aroyehun, Stephan Lewandowsky, David Garcia

entry.summary: Using Evidence-Minus-Intuition (EMI) scores computed from congressional floor speeches, this study shows that individual legislators' epistemic orientation varies systematically and predicts legislative effectiveness. It extends prior session-level analyses of declining evidence-oriented language to member-level analysis with behavioral outcomes.

entry.title: KuaiRP Series Role-playing Models Technical Report

author.name: Yipeng Wang, Ziwei Zhang, Jiahui Zhang, Qi Gan, Kai Sheng

entry.summary: A technical report on the KuaiRP role-playing model series, proposing a multi-stage training pipeline that combines standardized character templates, SFT from simulated user behavior with reverse profile filtering, and rule-based composite rewards to inject domain knowledge while avoiding catastrophic forgetting of general agent capabilities. It targets small, efficient deployment with stable outputs and built-in world knowledge.

entry.title: Shedding Light: A Benchmark for Evaluating Lighting Understanding in Generative Image Models

author.name: Justine Giroux, Jack Oliver Hilliard, Yannick Hold-Geoffroy, Javier Vazquez-Corral, Jean-Fran\c{c}ois Lalonde

entry.summary: This benchmark assesses whether generative image models genuinely understand lighting by testing how well they insert novel objects into real photographs with consistent illumination. It probes physical plausibility of illumination rather than just visual quality.

entry.title: Overpainting: Localized Context-aware Diffusion Image Editing

author.name: Sam Sartor, Iliyan Georgiev, Michael Fischer, Valentin Deschaintre, Pieter Peers

entry.summary: Overpainting is an image editing operation using a trimap to specify pixels that must, may, or must not be edited, giving both precise and loose spatial control with awareness of previous content. It adapts a pretrained editing diffusion model via joint attention and low-rank adaptation, with an automated training data generation pipeline.

entry.title: CEM-TUDASR: Computationally efficient multi-modality transformer based unsupervised domain adaptive super-resolution approach

author.name: Anjali Sarvaiya, Jay Kadel, Kishor Upla, Kiran Raja

entry.summary: Proposes a Transformer-based unsupervised super-resolution framework for wireless capsule endoscopy images that avoids paired low/high-resolution training data by using a domain-adaptive degradation network to synthesize realistic WCE-like degradations from conventional endoscopy images. It matters because low-resolution endoscopic imagery limits diagnosis, and paired data does not exist in this modality.

entry.title: GRIPNet: Gaussian Radial Intensity Prior Guided Architecture for Pulmonary Nodule Detection in CT

author.name: Haojie Yang, Ran Su

entry.summary: Shows that pulmonary nodule intensity follows a highly regular Gaussian radial profile (validated on 18,218 lesions across three benchmarks) and designs an architecture with radial priors to improve detection of sub-6mm nodules. Grounds the network design in imaging physics rather than treating nodules as generic objects.

entry.title: MC-DeTra: Motion-Consistent Joint Object Detection and Socially-Aware Trajectory Forecasting in Bird's-Eye-View Images

author.name: Vladislav Diuzhev, Dmitry Yudin

entry.summary: This work releases an open reimplementation of DeTra, the strongest unified detection-plus-trajectory-forecasting model for autonomous driving, and adds MC-DeTra motion-consistency mechanisms using annotation-derived auxiliary supervision on past motion and social traffic context. The open release fills a reproducibility gap since the original DeTra had no public implementation.

entry.title: Freehand Sketching for End-User Programming of Robot Swarms

author.name: Riwa Karam, Ian Kuo, Magnus Egerstedt

entry.summary: The paper introduces a sketch-to-swarm framework where non-expert users draw freehand geometries to specify robot swarm formations; the system extracts target points, builds a rigid formation graph, assigns robots, and runs distributed formation control with a guarantee against reflected formations. A 20-participant human study over 42 shapes evaluated usability.

entry.title: Aerodynamic Prior-Free Coordinated Trajectory Generation and Tracking Control for a Tail-Sitter UAV

author.name: Erchao Rong, Zihao Liu, Junning Liang, Jianguo Wang, Xiao Jie, Haoran Fu, Ziliang Chen, Ximin Lyu

entry.summary: This paper presents a trajectory generation and tracking control framework for tail-sitter UAVs that avoids requiring airframe-specific aerodynamic priors, using phase-specific modeling such as phi-theory-based differential flatness mapping for coordinated flight and simplified local models for predictive control. This matters because tail-sitters face highly nonlinear aerodynamics across hover and forward flight, and removing the need for per-airframe system identification makes the approach more generalizable and practical for new vehicles.

entry.title: What the Pro-Democracy Movement Knows About Quitting in Protest

author.name: Maxwell Love

entry.summary: Drawing on 15 years of pro-democracy organizing experience, the author applies empirical findings (Pinckney and Trilling, 2024) on defections during democratic backsliding to AI lab employees considering resignation. Key data points: insider noncooperation succeeded roughly twice as often as public speaking out, and quiet outreach moved insiders far more often than public protest.

entry.title: Categorical taboos are much better than threshold taboos: neuralese edition

author.name: Linch

entry.summary: A conceptual analysis of the ongoing debate about whether models communicate in neuralese, arguing that the definitional choice between a categorical standard (whether recurrence occurs outside natural language) and a threshold standard (a fixed count of opaque serial steps) drives much of the disagreement. The author argues the categorical definition is preferable for policy and monitoring purposes, while acknowledging that many technical experts favor threshold definitions as more causally relevant.

entry.title: Belief-State Engine: Augmenting LLMs for Principled Planning Under Partial Observability

author.name: Arnab Chattopadhayay, Debdipta Halder

entry.summary: The paper diagnoses characteristic LLM agent failures under partial observability as stemming from the absence of an explicit belief over hidden state, and proposes a Belief-State Engine that maintains a Bayesian posterior over a POMDP's latent states outside the LLM. This architectural add-on aims to prevent premature commitment, wrong-hypothesis collapse, and policy drift.

entry.title: From Symbolic Perception to Logical Deduction: A Framework for Guiding Language Models in Geometric Reasoning

author.name: Weichen Dai, Rafael Medeiros Cabral, Ziyi Shou, Yan Cao, Xin Shen, Dongcai Lu, Yi Zhou

entry.summary: The paper shows a pure LLM equipped with a Geometric Vision Parser (translating diagrams to symbolic form) and a Symbolic Solver can rival state-of-the-art multimodal models on complex plane geometry, with reduced hallucination and more interpretable reasoning. It also curates a challenging benchmark from 2025 Chinese Zhongkao problems.

entry.title: Can AI Agents Detect and Repair Artifact Drift in Network Experiments?

author.name: Tianzhu Zhang, Weichen Tao, Changgang Zheng, Yusheng Zheng, Long Chen, Xiaoyi Fan, Meikang Qiu

entry.summary: The paper introduces artifact integrity, the property that an AI agent's modifications to an experiment record remain evidence-supported, in-scope, and traceable, and releases NetArtifactBench to test whether agents can detect and repair drift in network experiment records. It reframes agent evaluation beyond task completion toward trustworthiness of the records agents touch. Timely as agentic systems enter operational research settings.

entry.title: Can Foundation Models Moderate Online Content? Evaluating Instruction- vs. Example-Driven Policy Operationalization

author.name: Ayan Majumdar, Shounak Paul, Pushpdeep Singh, Ines Abdelaziz, Sayeh Jarollahi, Seungeon Lee, Krishna P. Gummadi, Ingmar Weber, Abhisek Dash

entry.summary: The paper systematically compares instruction-driven versus example-driven operationalization of content moderation policies in vision-language models, using ModerationBench of 4,000 manually annotated Bluesky posts. It finds foundation models can substantially moderate content reliably, clarifying which guidance paradigm suits policy consistency.

entry.title: Conformal Calibration Transfer

author.name: Achref Doula

entry.summary: Studies conformal prediction when labeled calibration data exists only in a source space while prediction sets are needed in a linked target space, such as under sensor or modality changes. The proposed Transported Conformal Calibration transports labeled source calibration via paired unlabeled data and corrects residual mismatch using unlabeled target inputs, with two instantiations (TCC-KS and another variant). Extends coverage guarantees to a practically common transfer setting.

entry.title: Importance Weighting for Unlabeled-unlabeled Learning under Distribution Shift

author.name: Atsutoshi Kumagai, Tomoharu Iwata, Hiroshi Takahashi, Taishi Nishiyama, Kazuki Adachi, Yasuhiro Fujiwara

entry.summary: The paper proposes an importance-weighting method for unlabeled-unlabeled (UU) learning that adapts to distribution shift between training and test distributions using only unlabeled data plus a small amount of test-distribution UU data. Since UU learning subsumes positive-unlabeled and noisy-label learning, the method broadly improves robustness of weakly supervised binary classification under covariate/prior shift.

entry.title: A Station-Based Evaluation of Machine Learning-based Weather Forecasting Models in Northern Norway

author.name: Siyan Chen, Lars Uebbing, Eirik Mikal Samuelsen, Georgios Leontidis, Arnt-B{\o}rre Salberg, S\'ebastien Lef\`evre, Robert Jenssen, Kristoffer Wickstr{\o}m

entry.summary: This case study evaluates machine learning weather prediction models (FourCastNet3 and GraphCast) against the operational ECMWF HRES baseline for wind speed forecasting in Northern Norway, using multi-year station observations in a challenging fjord environment. The finding that HRES still slightly outperforms the ML models, particularly under high-wind conditions, provides an important reality check on MLWP generalization claims. This matters because rigorous localized evaluations are rare relative to global reanalysis-based benchmarks.

entry.title: Testing Between the Test Cases: Proving End-to-End Steering in Conditions You Never Drove

author.name: Menuka Ghalan, Charles Rodgers, Zachary D. Asher

entry.summary: Using bound propagation on trained end-to-end steering networks, the authors formally verify lane-keeping behavior across continuous ranges of disturbance strength between test images, covering 133 poses on an arterial road without further driving. This bridges the gap between passing discrete test conditions and guaranteed real-world robustness in autonomous driving. One verification run spans more conditions than an empirical testing campaign could cover.

entry.title: BodyCam-VQA: Enhanced Body-Worn Camera Video Captioning via Multimodal Reasoning and Probe Question Generation

author.name: Karish Gupta, Matthew Alex, Alex Li, Yang Wu, Yun-Wei Chu, Kashif Munir, Xiaotian Zhou, Zhengping Ji, Xiaozhong Liu

entry.summary: BodyCam-VQA targets body-worn camera video understanding, where chaotic scenes, low visual quality, and noisy audio defeat current VLMs and cause missed forensic details. The approach combines multimodal reasoning with generated probe questions to improve captioning and evidence surfacing for legal transparency and accountability.

entry.title: ReconPlusGen: Injecting Reconstruction Prior into Multi-view 3D Generation through Noise Inversion and Modulation

author.name: Jiarui Liu, Heng Li, Weiyu Li, Keng Deng, Junyuan Deng, Zheng Zhongxing, Junyu Huang, Jiahao Chang, Xiaoguang Han, Ping Tan

entry.summary: ReconPlusGen predicts a point cloud from multiple input images and deterministically injects the predicted geometry into the diffusion process via noise inversion, then modulates the noise to preserve generative flexibility for completing unobserved regions. It fuses reconstruction priors with multi-view 3D generation.

entry.title: CARLAverse: A Highly Modular, Distributed, and Multimodal Framework for Human-in-the-Loop Simulation

author.name: Patrick Rebling, Philipp Nenninger, Reiner Kriesten

entry.summary: CARLAverse is an open-source multimodal human-in-the-loop simulation ecosystem integrating driving, cycling, and pedestrian simulators into a shared CARLA-based virtual environment, designed to handle network latency and synchronization constraints for high-fidelity haptic feedback in mixed-traffic studies. It enables safe investigation of authentic human social negotiation with autonomous vehicles.

entry.title: Valerant: An Automatic Navigable Game Map Generator via Action-Conditioned World Model Exploration

author.name: Yiran Qiao, Feng Wang, Jing Ma

entry.summary: Extends World Action Models to 3D games, where the environment persists independently of the model, and builds Valerant, a system that automatically generates navigable game maps through action-conditioned world model exploration. This bridges world-model advances from robotics and driving into general game content generation.

entry.title: RESCUE-BENCH: Towards Relation-Aware Multi-Party Emotional Support Conversation Systems

author.name: Haichuan Hu, Yang Xiao, Mingni Tang, Jiawen Duan, Quanjun Zhang, Congqing He, Hao Zhang, Jiashuo Wang, Johan F. Hoorn, Wenjie Li

entry.summary: Introduces relation-aware emotional support conversation as a new task and builds RESCUE, a benchmark from real couple and family interview conversations with 191 samples, 7,079 annotated turns, and over 1,000 minutes of video. It tests whether LLMs can leverage evolving interpersonal relationship dynamics for effective emotional support. This extends emotional support research beyond one-on-one interactions.

entry.title: Grounded Evaluation and Repair for NL-to-PDDL Problem Generation

author.name: Joana Rosa, Pedro Santos, Valdemar Oliveira, Rom\~ao Silva, L. Miguel Silveira, Bruno Martins

entry.summary: The paper shows that standard metrics for LLM-generated PDDL problem instances (parseability, planner success) overestimate faithfulness to the described task, and builds an end-to-end pipeline combining parsing, planning, validation, domain-conformance checking, an LLM critic, and iterative repair. Fine-grained repair feedback improves the semantic correctness of generated planning problems.

entry.title: RAP: Research Attention Prediction Reveals Target-Conditioned Evidence Acquisition Biases

author.name: Yingqian Wu, Jingcong Liang, Siyuan Wang, Zhenfei Yin, Philip Torr, Junchi Yu, Zhongyu Wei

entry.summary: RAP is a rolling benchmark (278 AI/ML fields, 1,390 episodes) where LLM agents search a temporally restricted arXiv corpus to predict future paper shares across research directions. All diagnostic models underperform a simple EWMA count baseline, and the authors trace failures to state carry-over and evidence acquisition biases tied to target conditions.

entry.title: Fine-Tuning a KV Cache Concatenation-Aware Model or Recomputing KV Caches? Why Not Both?

author.name: Fumihiko Tachibana, Daisuke Miyashita, Jun Deguchi

entry.summary: The authors combine fine-tuning a model to be aware of KV cache concatenation with selective recomputation of a subset of cached keys to speed up RAG prefill for very long contexts. Precomputed KV cache reuse reduces time-to-first-token, and this hybrid approach aims to preserve response quality where naive reuse degrades it. Relevant to latency-critical retrieval-augmented serving.

entry.title: GANDR: Claim Auditing for Verifiable Legal Answer Generation

author.name: Chen Qian, Yimeng Wang, Yu Chen, Lingfei Wu, Andreas Stathopoulos

entry.summary: GANDR is a two-agent grounded-generation system where a Drafter writes structured legal answers and a Critic audits each claim against its cited source, emitting a per-claim audit trace. It is paired with an evaluation measuring per-claim verifiability, addressing cases where a correct conclusion rests on fabricated citations.

entry.title: GEOSTEER: Geodesic Optimization for Activation Steering in Large Language Models

author.name: Xuan Cuong Ngo, Hao Vo, Ngan Le

entry.summary: Reframes norm-preserving activation steering in LLMs as a Riemannian optimization problem, replacing predefined one-step steering trajectories with sequences of small geodesic updates that better respect the geometry of activation distributions. This provides a principled, lightweight inference-time control method for LLM behavior. Relevant to model control and interpretability without retraining.

entry.title: Certifying Lower Bounds for Risk-Sensitive Reinforcement Learning under Adversarial State Perturbations

author.name: Tong Li, Saunak Kumar Panda, Yisha Xiang

entry.summary: Extends certified robustness for RL from risk-neutral to risk-sensitive objectives, establishing lower bounds on the exponential utility of cumulative rewards under lp-norm-bounded adversarial state perturbations. A phi-divergence relaxation of the perturbation set enables a tractable risk-sensitive certification formulation. Important for deploying RL agents in safety-critical, adversarial environments.

entry.title: LILA: Calibration-Free Structured Pruning of Large Language Models via Latent Spectral Geometry

author.name: Sankar Behera, Dhruv Singh, Anshika Agnihotri, Raj Kumar Choudhary, Satyadev Ahlawat, Yamuna Prasad

entry.summary: LILA scores FFN neuron importance via Kolmogorov-Smirnov distance between singular value distributions of full and ablated weight matrices, enabling closed-form structured pruning without calibration data, gradients, or auxiliary networks. Without fine-tuning it beats PruneNet and calibrated SliceGPT on LLaMA-2-7B at 25% sparsity.

entry.title: Predicting Privacy Leakage from Weight Spectral Density

author.name: Richard J. Preen, Jim Smith

entry.summary: The authors test whether cheap WeightWatcher spectral metrics from the heavy-tailed self-regularisation framework can proxy membership inference attack vulnerability, avoiding costly shadow-model training. Stable rank correlates strongly with overall MIA success across image and tabular tasks, suggesting fast privacy auditing.

entry.title: A Quantum-Inspired Dequantization Method for Diagonally Weighted Matrix Functions: Application to Learning with Optimized Random Features

author.name: Natsuto Isogai, Mio Murao, Hayata Yamasaki

entry.summary: The authors develop a classical algorithm that dequantizes a QSVT-based sampler for learning with optimized random features, a case not covered by existing dequantization frameworks because the relevant matrix is not accessible via sampling. Their approach samples heavy indices, reduces the problem to a small principal block, and outputs a sparse representation with operator-norm guarantees. This removes a claimed quantum advantage for a concrete quantum machine learning candidate.

entry.title: Temporal and Multimodal Deep Learning for Cyberattack Detection in LEO Satellite Systems

author.name: Kyle Stein, Guillermo Francia III, Eman El-Sheikh, Hossain Shahriar

entry.summary: A systematic study of deep-learning cyberattack detection for Low-Earth Orbit satellite systems using the satellite-specific UNSW-IoT dataset, combining temporal and multimodal signals across RF links, onboard hardware, and orbital operations. The work shows that modeling temporal attack behavior and heterogeneous modalities improves detection over approaches that treat observations independently or rely on terrestrial intrusion datasets. It matters because space systems are an increasingly critical and under-defended infrastructure.

entry.title: Risk-Averse Decision Making with Multi-Level Reliability Guarantees

author.name: Amirmohammad Farzaneh, Osvaldo Simeone

entry.summary: The paper studies maximizing weighted performance certificates at multiple target outage levels under state uncertainty, showing the problem is equivalent to optimization over nested prediction sets and connecting it to conformal prediction. It extends single-level risk-averse decision making to multi-level guarantees and derives a dual formulation that decouples optimization across inputs, illustrated on a wireless transmission system. This bridges conformal prediction theory and engineering decision-making under uncertainty.

entry.title: SIRF: A Spec-Internalized Risk Foundation Model for Industrial Content Risk Control

author.name: Suwan Wu, Yumeng Lin, Pengcheng Yuan, Xiaolong Jiang

entry.summary: SIRF internalizes platform content-risk policies via continued pretraining using synthetic data from EntiGraph, MAGA rewriting, and account-level chain-of-thought, enabling verdict-only, low-latency risk classification without extra human annotation. A controlled comparison against Qwen3-8B-SFT attributes gains to policy internalization rather than output format.

entry.title: Think Before You Link: Rarity, Reasoning, and Retrieval in Multilingual Entity Linking

author.name: Parinthapat Pengpun, Simran Khanuja, Graham Neubig

entry.summary: The paper shows knowledge-graph structural rarity metrics surface rare entities that popularity-based metrics miss, with SOTA multimodal entity linking accuracy dropping 15.4-39.9% on these slices. It introduces a training-free framework where a reasoning-capable vision-language model iteratively searches Wikipedia to improve rare-entity linking.

entry.title: Distribution-aware Language Neuron Identification in Multilingual Large Language Models

author.name: Minjun Kim, Inho Won, Junghun Yuk, Dongyeon Kim, Jihyo Kim, KyungTae Lim

entry.summary: This work improves identification of language-specific neurons in multilingual LLMs by replacing entropy-based activation statistics with distribution-aware comparisons of per-language activation distributions over the full activation range, including negative values. It argues prior methods miss the distributional, mutually related nature of multilingual representations. This advances mechanistic understanding of how mLLMs encode language.

entry.title: Rethinking Verbalized Confidence for LLM-as-a-Judge: A Compatibility Shift on Post-2025 Proprietary Models

author.name: Yu-Chung Hsiao

entry.summary: This single-author study shows that verbalized confidence has overtaken log-probability-based scoring as the better soft-signal for LLM-as-a-Judge evaluation on post-2025 proprietary models, calling this a compatibility shift. Across SummEval, AggreFact, and HelpSteer2 with up to 18 LLMs, added techniques like an overconfidence advisory and self-debate improve calibration. It challenges standard advice on confidence extraction methods.

entry.title: Overview of the NLPCC 2026 Shared Task 11: Agent-Based Experiment Reproduction from Scientific Papers

author.name: Hanhua Hong, Yizhi Li, Luu Gia Huy, Jian Yang, Ming Zhou, Chenghua Lin

entry.summary: This shared-task overview introduces AgentActionBench, a process-oriented benchmark evaluating LLM agents on reproducing experiments from scientific papers across ML and AI4Science, using an MCP-based Action Recorder and paper-specific rubrics over 150 papers. Unlike prior work focused on final repositories, it evaluates the entire agent behavior trace. It advances reproducibility infrastructure through agent evaluation.

entry.title: Recognizing Is Not Reversing: A Controlled Inversion Test of Fact-Preserving News Framing

author.name: Yi Liu

entry.summary: Introduces a controlled inversion test measuring whether LLMs can undo a known news-framing transformation while preserving atomic facts, spanning evaluative lexis, agency realization, and information salence across 540 paired variants. Testing Qwen, DeepSeek, and Kimi models, it finds factual preservation near 0.84 but intervention reversal only 0.044-0.068, showing models recognize framing yet cannot reverse it. This has implications for media-analysis and debiasing applications.

entry.title: Augustinian BabyLM: What Ostensive Definition Can and Cannot Teach a Small Language Model

author.name: Lisa Bylinina

entry.summary: The paper implements Augustine's ostensive definition in a small masked LM (DeBERTa, 10M words) by initializing embeddings for visually grounded tokens from image-region representations before training. Visual initialization leaves a lasting trace and improves zero-shot object-property knowledge (e.g., COMPS) but has no effect on most BabyLM grammatical benchmarks.

entry.title: MHE-Former: Multi-Hypothesis Transformers via Entropy Maximization for 3D Mesh Recovery

author.name: Boshu Jia, Rongyu Chen, Linlin Yang, Zihao Liu, Yingjie Chen, Zhongqun Zhang, Zhulin Tao, Shaohui Lin, Xiaoyu Wu, Libiao Jin, Baochang Zhang, Angela Yao
